records.title: INT 0148 (CALGB 9344)
records.subtitle: General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · Randomised clinical trial (3 × 2 factorial design) · 2003
records.body:
Operable primary breast cancer with axillary node involvement and clear surgical margins; postoperative adjuvant setting; surgery mastectomy or lumpectomy with axillary node sampling; radiotherapy required after breast-conserving surgery; systemic therapy started within 84 days of last surgery Ⓐ CA: cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² IV + doxorubicin 60, 75 or 90 mg/m² IV (randomised dose) every 3 weeks × 4 cycles, then no further chemotherapy
Ⓑ CA as Ⓐ (randomised doxorubicin dose) → paclitaxel 175 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks × 4 cycles
・Doxorubicin: Day 1 for 60 mg/m², days 1–2 for 75 and 90 mg/m²; routine G-CSF + ciprofloxacin at 90 mg/m²
・Design: 3 × 2 factorial randomisation; tamoxifen 20 mg/d for 5 years if receptor positive; radiotherapy after chemotherapy if lumpectomy Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, toxicity, first local recurrence, first distant recurrence, second malignancy, delayed cardiotoxicity Adding four cycles of sequential paclitaxel after adjuvant CA improved disease-free and overall survival in node-positive early breast cancer
・DFS: Ⓐ 65% vs Ⓑ 70% at 5 yr; HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.73–0.91) at ~10-yr follow-up, Ⓑ v Ⓐ
・OS: Ⓐ 77% vs Ⓑ 80% at 5 yr; HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.72–0.92) at ~10-yr follow-up, Ⓑ v Ⓐ
・Doxorubicin dose: No dose effect; 60 v 90 mg/m² HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.86–1.13) recurrence, 1.03 (95% CI 0.89–1.23) death at ~10 yr
・HER2 × paclitaxel: Interaction HR 0.59 (P=0.01) recurrence, 0.57 (P=0.01) death (CB11 IHC); consistent across both IHC assays and FISH; no HER2 × doxorubicin-dose interaction
・HER2 subgroups: Ⓑ v Ⓐ benefit in HER2-positive tumours regardless of ER status; none in HER2-negative/ER-positive disease (>50% of patients)
・Subgroups (ER): Unplanned; ER-negative HR 0.72 (0.59–0.86) vs ER-positive 0.91 (0.78–1.07); not significant after adjustment
・Toxicity: 3 on-treatment deaths (2 on paclitaxel, incl. 1 anaphylaxis); hypersensitivity 6%; posttreatment cardiotoxicity 11/13/16% (60/75/90 mg/m²)
・Limitations: Ⓑ confounds added drug with 3 v 6 months therapy; HER2 findings exploratory in correlative subset (1322/3121), require validation; unadjusted multiple comparisons
records.keywords: Henderson et al. J Clin Oncol 2003;21:976-983  12637460 Hayes et al. N Engl J Med 2007;357:1496-1506

records.title: INT C9741 (CALGB 9741)
records.subtitle: General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · Randomised clinical trial · 2003
records.body:
Women with primary adenocarcinoma of the breast (including metaplastic and bilateral lesions) and no metastases other than histologically involved axillary lymph nodes (T0 to T3, N1/2, M0); postoperative adjuvant chemotherapy after segmental mastectomy plus axillary dissection or modified radical mastectomy with tumor-free margins; chemotherapy within 84 days of primary surgery Ⓐ Sequential doxorubicin → paclitaxel → cyclophosphamide, four cycles each, every 3 weeks
Ⓑ Sequential doxorubicin → paclitaxel → cyclophosphamide, four cycles each, every 2 weeks with filgrastim
Ⓒ Doxorubicin plus cyclophosphamide four cycles → paclitaxel four cycles, every 3 weeks
Ⓓ Doxorubicin plus cyclophosphamide four cycles → paclitaxel four cycles, every 2 weeks with filgrastim
・Doses: Doxorubicin 60 mg/m², paclitaxel 175 mg/m², cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² IV
・Filgrastim (Ⓑ, Ⓓ): 5 μg/kg days 3–10 of each cycle
・Tamoxifen: Recommended (not required) 20 mg/d for 5 years after chemotherapy per hormone-receptor/menopausal status
・Design: 2×2 factorial of dose density (q2 v q3) and sequence (concurrent v sequential) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, toxicity Dose-dense (every-2-week) scheduling improved DFS and OS versus every-3-week; sequential was as effective as concurrent (protocol-specified analysis, median follow-up 36 months)
・DFS: Ⓑ+Ⓓ vs Ⓐ+Ⓒ RR 0.74 (95% CI 0.59 to 0.93); 4-yr DFS 82% vs 75%
・OS: Ⓑ+Ⓓ vs Ⓐ+Ⓒ RR 0.69 (95% CI 0.50 to 0.93); 3-yr OS 92% vs 90%
・Sequence: Ⓒ+Ⓓ vs Ⓐ+Ⓑ no difference in DFS or OS; DFS RR 0.93 (95% CI 0.75 to 1.18), OS RR 0.89 (95% CI 0.66 to 1.20)
・Contralateral BC: Reduced with dose density, 0.3% vs 1.5%
・Toxicity: G4 granulocytopenia Ⓑ+Ⓓ 6% vs Ⓐ+Ⓒ 33%; no treatment-related deaths during therapy; six treatment-related deaths at 23–41 months (four AML, one MDS, one cardiomyopathy)
・Limitations: Relapses fewer than anticipated; OS benefit beyond 2 years subject to change; radiation rates across arms not yet collated
records.keywords: Citron et al. J Clin Oncol 2003;21:1431-1439  12668651

records.title: NSABP B-28
records.subtitle: General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · Randomised clinical trial · 2005
records.body:
Resected operable invasive adenocarcinoma of the breast (cT1-3, cN0-1, cM0) with at least one positive axillary node; adjuvant setting after lumpectomy with free margins plus axillary dissection or modified radical mastectomy, randomised within 63 days of diagnosis; prior invasive breast cancer/DCIS and any prior radiation, chemotherapy, immunotherapy or hormonal therapy excluded Ⓐ Doxorubicin 60 mg/m² IV plus cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² IV every 21 days × 4 cycles
Ⓑ Doxorubicin 60 mg/m² IV plus cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² IV every 21 days × 4 cycles → paclitaxel 225 mg/m² IV every 21 days × 4 cycles
・Tamoxifen: 20 mg/day for 5 years from day 1 of first AC cycle if ER- or PR-positive or age ≥50 at surgery
・Radiotherapy: Whole-breast irradiation mandated after lumpectomy; postmastectomy or regional nodal irradiation not permitted Primary: disease-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: recurrence-free interval, site of first event, safety Adding paclitaxel after AC improved disease-free survival but not overall survival versus AC alone in resected node-positive breast cancer
・DFS: 5-yr Ⓐ 72% vs Ⓑ 76%; RR 0.83 (95% CI 0.72–0.95)
・OS: 5-yr Ⓐ 85% vs Ⓑ 85% at 64.6-mo median follow-up; RR 0.93 (95% CI 0.78–1.12)
・First events: 5-yr cumulative incidence Ⓐ 28.3% vs Ⓑ 24.4%; fewer contralateral breast cancers with Ⓑ (P = .039)
・Subgroups: No interaction by HR status (DFS P = .30, OS P = .82) or tamoxifen (DFS P = .44); DFS RR 0.77 HR-positive vs 0.90 HR-negative
・Toxicity: Ⓑ PTX grade ≥3 neurosensory/neuromotor 18%, arthralgia/myalgia 12%, febrile neutropenia 3%; seven possible treatment-related deaths; AML/MDS eight (six Ⓑ, two Ⓐ)
・Limitations: OS immature beyond year 6 (few at risk); Ⓑ 8.8% never started PTX, 75.9% completed all protocol cycles; tamoxifen concurrent with chemotherapy
records.keywords: Mamounas et al. J Clin Oncol 2005;23:3686-3696  15897552

records.title: ECOG E1199
records.subtitle: General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · Randomised clinical trial · 2008
records.body:
Women with operable, histologically confirmed adenocarcinoma of the breast; adjuvant postoperative setting; histologically involved lymph nodes (tumor stage T1, T2 or T3 and nodal stage N1 or N2) or high-risk axillary node-negative disease (T2 or T3, N0) without distant metastases; further eligibility criteria in supplementary appendix Ⓐ Paclitaxel 175 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks for 4 doses (standard)
Ⓑ Paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV weekly for 12 doses
Ⓒ Docetaxel 100 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks for 4 doses
Ⓓ Docetaxel 35 mg/m² IV weekly for 12 doses
・AC backbone: Doxorubicin 60 mg/m² plus cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks for 4 cycles before taxane, all arms
・Endocrine/RT: Tamoxifen 20 mg daily for 5 years if hormone receptor–positive; radiotherapy after completion of chemotherapy Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, toxic effects AC followed by weekly paclitaxel improved disease-free and overall survival vs paclitaxel every 3 weeks; docetaxel every 3 weeks improved disease-free survival only
・5-yr DFS: Ⓐ 76.9% vs Ⓑ 81.5% vs Ⓒ 81.2% vs Ⓓ 77.6%; HR vs Ⓐ Ⓑ 1.27 (98.3% CI 1.03–1.57), Ⓒ 1.23 (1.00–1.52), Ⓓ 1.09 (0.89–1.34)
・DFS factorial: Paclitaxel vs docetaxel HR 1.03 (95% CI 0.91–1.17); weekly vs every-3-wk HR 1.06 (0.94–1.20); neither significant
・5-yr OS: Ⓐ 86.5% vs Ⓑ 89.7% vs Ⓒ 87.3% vs Ⓓ 86.2%; HR vs Ⓐ Ⓑ 1.32 (98.3% CI 1.02–1.72), Ⓒ 1.13 (0.88–1.46), Ⓓ 1.02 (0.80–1.32)
・Subgroups: Ⓑ improved DFS and OS in HER2-negative disease regardless of hormone-receptor status, not seen in HER2-positive; exploratory post hoc
・Toxicity: G3/4 any Ⓐ 30% vs Ⓑ 28% vs Ⓒ 71% vs Ⓓ 45%; Ⓒ neutropenia 46%, febrile neutropenia 16%, infection 13%; Ⓑ G2–4 neuropathy 27% vs Ⓐ 20%
・Limitations: Unanticipated taxane–schedule interaction complicates interpretation; subgroup analyses exploratory post hoc; Ⓓ poorer adherence (40% dose-modified)
records.keywords: Sparano et al. N Engl J Med 2008;358:1663-1671  18420499

records.title: US Oncology 9735
records.subtitle: General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2006
records.body:
Operable stage I to III invasive breast cancer after complete surgical excision of the primary tumor, adjuvant setting; primary tumor ≥1.0 cm and less than 7.0 cm; age 18–75 years, Karnofsky performance status ≥80%, no evidence of metastatic disease; no prior chemotherapy or hormonal therapy, no neoadjuvant chemotherapy; pregnant and lactating females excluded Ⓐ Doxorubicin 60 mg/m² IV day 1 + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² IV day 1, every 21 days × 4 cycles
Ⓑ Docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV day 1 + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² IV day 1, every 21 days × 4 cycles
・Duration: Four 21-day cycles; off treatment for disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
・After chemotherapy: Radiation therapy as indicated; tamoxifen for 5 years in hormone receptor–positive disease Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, safety With 7-year follow-up, four cycles of TC improved both disease-free and overall survival versus AC as adjuvant therapy for operable breast cancer
・7-yr DFS: Ⓐ 75% vs Ⓑ 81%; HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.56 to 0.98)
・7-yr OS: Ⓐ 82% vs Ⓑ 87%; HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.50 to 0.97), now significant
・Subgroups: Exploratory DFS analyses favoured Ⓑ in older and younger patients; no interaction with hormone receptor or HER2 status
・Toxicity: G4 neutropenia Ⓑ 51% vs Ⓐ 43%; febrile neutropenia Ⓑ 5% vs Ⓐ 2.5%, doubled in older patients (Ⓑ 8% vs Ⓐ 4%); late Ⓐ deaths from CHF, myelodysplasia, myelofibrosis, plus acute leukemia 10 yr after Ⓐ; Ⓑ more edema, myalgia, arthralgia; Ⓐ more nausea/vomiting
・Limitations: Unplanned substudies with small subgroups; HER2 status available for 170 patients only; not generalizable to four or more positive nodes
records.keywords: Jones et al. J Clin Oncol 2006;24:5381-5387  17135639 Jones et al. J Clin Oncol 2009;27:1177-1183  19204201

records.title: ABC trials (USOR 06-090, NSABP B-46-I/USOR 07132, NSABP B-49; NRG Oncology)
records.subtitle: General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · Prospectively planned joint efficacy analysis of three randomised clinical trials (phase III) · 2017
records.body:
HER2-negative invasive breast cancer after excision and axillary node evaluation; adjuvant chemotherapy; node-positive (pT1-3, including pN1mi) or high-risk node-negative (ER/PgR negative, tumor >2.0 cm, or T1c ER/PgR-positive with grade 3 or Oncotype DX recurrence score ≥25; ≥31 in USOR 06-090); excluded metastatic disease, T4 tumors, supraclavicular nodes, prior ipsilateral invasive cancer or DCIS, nonbreast malignancy within 5 years Ⓐ TC6: docetaxel 75 mg/m² and cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² every 21 days for six cycles
Ⓑ TaxAC: TAC6 (docetaxel, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide 75/50/500 mg/m² every 21 days for six cycles) or AC every 3 weeks for four cycles → paclitaxel 80 mg/m² weekly for 12 doses or DD AC every 2 weeks for four cycles → paclitaxel 80 mg/m² weekly for 12 doses or paclitaxel 175 mg/m² every 2 weeks for four cycles
・Design: Open-label; prospectively planned joint analysis of three sequential trials (USOR 06-090, NSABP B-46-I/USOR 07132, NSABP B-49) Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: recurrence-free interval, disease-free survival–DCIS, overall survival, toxicity Final analysis (median follow-up 6.9 years): noninferiority of TC6 to TaxAC for IDFS could not be declared; RFI favored TaxAC and OS did not differ
・IDFS: 5-yr Ⓐ 85.1% vs Ⓑ 86.7%; HR 1.14 (95% CI 0.99 to 1.32); 80% CI upper bound 1.25 does not exclude 1.18
・RFI: 5-yr Ⓐ 88.2% vs Ⓑ 91.0%; HR 1.38 (95% CI 1.16 to 1.65), favoring Ⓑ TaxAC
・OS: 5-yr Ⓐ 91.8% vs Ⓑ 92.4%; HR 1.05 (95% CI 0.87 to 1.26); no significant difference
・Subgroups: RFI treatment-by-hormone-receptor interaction (P=.02); receptor-negative disease: RFI HR 1.90 (95% CI 1.39 to 2.61), IDFS HR 1.30 (95% CI 1.02 to 1.67), favoring Ⓑ
・Toxicity (B-49 only): G3 febrile neutropenia Ⓐ 7% vs Ⓑ 3%; G3 oral mucositis Ⓐ <1% vs Ⓑ 4%; no grade 5 events
・Toxicity (late events): Leukemias (P=.03) and non-breast-cancer deaths (P=.003) increased with Ⓑ; deaths without recurrence Ⓐ 34 vs Ⓑ 62; cardiac deaths Ⓐ 3 vs Ⓑ 8
・Limitations: Open-label; cause-of-death data not available for USOR 06-090; P values not controlled for multiple comparisons
records.keywords: Blum et al. J Clin Oncol 2017;35:2647-2655  28398846 Geyer et al. J Clin Oncol 2024;42:1344-1349  38335467

records.title: EBCTCG chemohormonal therapy 15-year overview
records.subtitle: General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · Individual patient data meta-analysis · 2005
records.body:
Women with early breast cancer (disease in the breast, or breast and locoregional nodes) in unconfounded randomised adjuvant trials begun by 1995; comparisons of CMF-based or anthracycline-based (FAC/FEC) chemotherapy, tamoxifen, or ovarian ablation/suppression (women younger than 50); none involved taxanes, trastuzumab, raloxifene or modern aromatase inhibitors; short chemotherapy (<1 month) trials excluded ・Anthracycline-based vs no chemotherapy (8000 women)
・CMF-based vs no chemotherapy (14 000 women)
・Anthracycline-based vs CMF-based chemotherapy (14 000 women)
・About 5 years of tamoxifen vs none (15 000 women)
・About 1–2 years of tamoxifen vs none (33 000 women)
・About 5 vs 1–2 years of tamoxifen (18 000 women)
・Ovarian ablation or suppression vs not (8000 women)
・Regimens: Anthracycline-based FAC or FEC (doxorubicin or epirubicin) about 6 months; CMF-based about 6 months (mean 6·5); tamoxifen 20 or 30–40 mg/day; ovarian ablation by surgery or irradiation, or LHRHI suppression, women younger than 50 years Primary: first recurrence (any site), breast cancer mortality, overall mortality, cause-specific mortality before recurrence, incidence of other cancers before breast cancer recurrence Anthracycline-based chemotherapy and 5 years of tamoxifen in ER-positive disease each substantially reduce 15-year breast cancer mortality; combined, they approximately halve the annual death rate
・Polychemotherapy vs none: Recurrence rate ratio 0.77 (SE 0.02); breast cancer death rate ratio 0.83 (SE 0.02), both 2p<0·00001
・Anthracycline vs none, breast cancer mortality: Rate ratio 0·62 (SE 0·05) younger than 50 years; 0·80 (SE 0·04) at age 50–69 years (direct plus indirect evidence)
・Anthracycline vs CMF: Recurrence rate ratio 0·89 (SE 0·03), 2p=0·001; breast cancer death rate ratio 0·84 (SE 0·03), 2p<0·00001
・Tamoxifen about 5 years vs none, ER-positive: Recurrence rate ratio 0·59 (SE 0·03); breast cancer death rate ratio 0·66 (SE 0·04); 15-year gains 11·8% recurrence, 9·2% breast cancer mortality
・Tamoxifen about 5 vs 1–2 years: Recurrence rate ratio 0·82 (SE 0·03); breast cancer death rate ratio 0·91 (SE 0·04), 2p=0·01
・Ovarian ablation/suppression vs not: Recurrence rate ratio 0·830 (SE 0·038); breast cancer death rate ratio 0·870 (SE 0·045), 2p=0·004; benefit apparent only without other systemic treatment
・Chemoendocrine, ER-positive: Anthracycline plus tamoxifen death rate ratios about 0·43 (younger than 50 years) and 0·55 (50–69 years)
・Subgroups: Chemotherapy proportional reductions larger at younger ages, independent of ER and nodal status; tamoxifen benefit confined to ER-positive disease
・Toxicity: Anthracyclines excess heart/haemopoietic deaths only a few per 1000 per decade; tamoxifen uterine cancer about 3-fold (1·9 vs 0·6 per 1000/year) outweighed by contralateral breast cancer reduction (4·0 vs 6·0)
・Limitations: Trials begun by 1995, none with taxanes, trastuzumab or modern aromatase inhibitors; about 9% of randomised women unavailable; few women age 70 or older in chemotherapy trials
records.keywords: Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group. Lancet 2005;365:1687-1717  15894097

records.title: EBCTCG polychemotherapy meta-analysis
records.subtitle: General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · Individual patient data meta-analysis · 2012
records.body:
Early breast cancer; adjuvant polychemotherapy randomised trials begun 1973–2003 (individual patient data sought 2005–10): taxane vs non-taxane (begun 1994–2003), anthracycline-based vs CMF (1978–97), anthracycline dose comparisons (1985–94), polychemotherapy vs none (1973–96); stem-cell rescue and dose-density-only trials excluded ・Taxane+anthracycline-based vs same, or more, non-taxane chemotherapy (44 000 women)
・Anthracycline-based vs another anthracycline-based regimen (7000 women)
・Anthracycline-based vs CMF (18 000 women)
・Polychemotherapy vs no chemotherapy (32 000 women)
・Regimens: standard CMF 6 cycles C100×14 M40×2 F500×2 4-weekly; standard 4AC 4 cycles A60 C600 IV 3-weekly; CAF 6 cycles C100×14 A30×2 F500×2 4-weekly; CEF 6 cycles C75×14 E60×2 F500×2 4-weekly (doses mg/m²) Primary: distant recurrence, any recurrence, breast cancer mortality, other mortality, overall mortality Taxane-plus-anthracycline or higher-cumulative-dose anthracycline regimens reduced breast cancer mortality by about one-third on average, largely independent of age, nodal status or ER status
・Breast cancer mortality (BCM), taxane+anthracycline vs same or more non-taxane control (44 000 women): RR 0·87 (SE 0·03, 2p<0·00001)
・BCM, taxane vs same non-taxane control, unconfounded (11 167 women): 8-yr 21·1% vs 23·9%; RR 0·86 (95% CI 0·79–0·93)
・Recurrence, taxane vs same control: 8-yr gain 4·6%; RR 0·84 (95% CI 0·78–0·91)
・Overall mortality, taxane vs same control: 8-yr gain 3·2%; RR 0·86 (95% CI 0·79–0·93)
・BCM, taxane vs roughly doubled non-taxane control (10 000 women): No significant difference; RR 0·94 (SE 0·06, 2p=0·33)
・BCM, any anthracycline-based vs CMF (18 000 women): RR 0·89 (SE 0·03, 2p=0·0006)
・BCM, standard 4AC vs standard CMF (5122 women): Equivalent; RR 0·98 (95% CI 0·89–1·08)
・BCM, higher-dose anthracycline (CAF/CEF) vs CMF (9527 women): RR 0·80 (95% CI 0·72–0·88); 10-yr gain 4·1%
・BCM, any anthracycline-based vs none (8575 women): RR 0·79 (95% CI 0·72–0·85); 10-yr gain 6·5%
・BCM, CMF vs none (5253 women): RR 0·76 (95% CI 0·68–0·84); 10-yr gain 6·2%
・BCM vs none, by regimen: CAF RR 0·64 (2p<0·0001); standard 4AC RR 0·78 (2p=0·01); standard CMF RR 0·76 (2p<0·0001)
・Subgroups: Proportional risk reductions little affected by age, nodal status, tumour diameter, differentiation, ER status or tamoxifen use
・Toxicity: 1-yr mortality without recurrence 0·3% (taxane-based) vs 0·2% (control), 2p=0·06; AML deaths 11 vs 1; cardiac mortality RR 1·56 (2p=0·02)
・Limitations: Indirect between-regimen comparisons; taxane follow-up short beyond year 8; no gene-expression or quantitative IHC predictor data
records.keywords: Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group. Lancet 2012;379:432-444  22152853

records.title: WSG PlanB
records.subtitle: General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body:
HER2-negative primary invasive breast cancer (pT1–pT4c) after adequate surgery, no metastases; adjuvant setting; pN+ or pN0 with one or more risk factors (pT >2, grade 2/3, high uPA/PAI-1, age <35 years, or HR negative); after amendment, HR-positive tumors RS-tested with chemotherapy omitted if RS ≤11 in pN0–pN1; women aged 18–75 Ⓐ Docetaxel 75 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² every 3 weeks for 6 cycles
Ⓑ Epirubicin 90 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² every 3 weeks for 4 cycles → docetaxel 100 mg/m² every 3 weeks for 4 cycles
・Design: Noninferiority of Ⓐ vs Ⓑ for DFS Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: distant recurrence-free interval, overall survival, safety Six cycles of TC was non-inferior to EC-T for 5-year DFS in HER2-negative early breast cancer
・5-yr DFS: Ⓐ 89.6% vs Ⓑ 89.8%; HR 1.004 (95% CI 0.776–1.299); noninferiority met, 90% upper limit 1.246 below 1.467
・5-yr dRFI: Ⓐ 94.1% vs Ⓑ 93.4%; HR 0.875 (95% CI 0.625–1.225)
・5-yr OS: Ⓐ 94.7% vs Ⓑ 94.5%; HR 0.937 (95% CI 0.654–1.342)
・Subgroups: No predictive interaction for TN, luminal A/B-like, pN, RS or age; TC comparable to EC-T in all subgroups
・No-chemo cohort (RS ≤11, pN0–pN1): 5-yr DFS 94.6%, dRFI 97.8%
・Toxicity: Grade 3–4 leukopenia Ⓐ 50.8% vs Ⓑ 57.5%; febrile neutropenia 5.3% vs 3.9%; treatment-related deaths 5 vs 1
・Limitations: Underpowered to exclude small DFS differences (5-yr DFS approximately 90% vs assumed 71.1%); limited conclusions for pN2–pN3; evidence strongest for pN0–pN1
records.keywords: Nitz et al. J Clin Oncol 2019;37:799-808  30785826

records.title: NSABP B-18 and NSABP B-27
records.subtitle: General Principles · Neoadjuvant therapy — timing & pathological response · Randomised clinical trial · 2008
records.body:
Operable palpable breast cancer (B-18: T1-3, N0-1, M0; B-27: T1c-3, N0-1, M0) diagnosed by core needle biopsy or fine-needle aspirate; primary chemotherapy given pre- or postoperatively; no biomarker selection; hormone receptor status not required at random assignment Ⓐ Surgery → postoperative AC (B-18)
Ⓑ Preoperative AC → surgery (B-18; B-27 group 1)
Ⓒ Preoperative AC → preoperative docetaxel → surgery (B-27 group 2)
Ⓓ Preoperative AC → surgery → postoperative docetaxel (B-27 group 3)
・Surgery: Lumpectomy and axillary lymph node dissection or modified radical mastectomy
・AC: Doxorubicin 60 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² every 21 days, four cycles
・Docetaxel: 100 mg/m² every 21 days, four cycles
・B-18 endocrine: Tamoxifen 10 mg orally twice daily for 5 years after chemotherapy if age ≥50 years; none if younger than 50
・B-27 endocrine: Tamoxifen 20 mg/d for 5 years from first day of chemotherapy, regardless of age or receptor status
・Radiotherapy: To breast after lumpectomy; regional and post-mastectomy chest-wall radiotherapy prohibited in B-27 Primary: overall survival, disease-free survival, relapse-free interval. Secondary: clinical and pathologic tumor response, axillary nodal downstaging, breast-conserving surgery, ipsilateral breast tumor recurrence, site-specific failure rates Preoperative AC did not improve DFS or OS versus postoperative AC (B-18); adding docetaxel raised pCR but not DFS or OS (B-27)
・OS (B-18, 16 y): Ⓐ 55% vs Ⓑ 55%; HR 0.99 (95% CI 0.85–1.16)
・DFS (B-18, 16 y): Ⓐ 39% vs Ⓑ 42%; HR 0.93 (95% CI 0.81–1.06)
・RFI (B-18): HR 0.98 (95% CI 0.83–1.15), no significant difference
・Response (B-18): Ⓑ cCR 36%, pCR 13%; node-negative Ⓑ 58% vs Ⓐ 42%; breast-conserving surgery Ⓑ 68% vs Ⓐ 60%
・IBTR (B-18): Ⓑ 13% vs Ⓐ 10% among lumpectomy patients, not significant (P=.21)
・OS (B-27, 8 y): Ⓑ 74% vs Ⓒ 75% vs Ⓓ 75%; no significant difference across arms (P=.76)
・DFS (B-27, 8 y): Ⓑ 59% vs Ⓒ 62% vs Ⓓ 62%; HR 0.92 (95% CI 0.78–1.08) for both Ⓒ and Ⓓ vs Ⓑ
・RFI (B-27): Ⓒ vs Ⓑ HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.69–0.99), P=.04; Ⓓ vs Ⓑ HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.73–1.04)
・pCR (B-27): Ⓒ 26% vs Ⓑ/Ⓓ 13%; cCR Ⓒ 63% vs Ⓑ/Ⓓ 40%
・Local recurrence (B-27): Lower as first event with Ⓒ/Ⓓ vs Ⓑ; HR 0.67, P=.02
・Subgroups (B-18): Age–treatment interaction for OS (P=.01); <50 y favored Ⓑ (OS HR 0.81), trend to Ⓐ at ≥50 y (HR 1.23)
・5-y landmark DFS (B-18, post hoc): Ⓑ favored; HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.66–1.00), P=.053
・pCR prognostic: DFS HR 0.47 (B-18), 0.49 (B-27); OS HR 0.32 (B-18), 0.36 (B-27); all P<.0001
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: No safety data in this update; age-subgroup and 5-y landmark analyses post hoc; pCR a weak surrogate for treatment effect
records.keywords: Rastogi et al. J Clin Oncol 2008;26:778-785  18258986

records.title: EBCTCG neoadjuvant meta-analysis
records.subtitle: General Principles · Neoadjuvant therapy — timing & pathological response · Individual patient data meta-analysis · 2018
records.body:
Early (operable) breast cancer; randomised trials begun before 2005 comparing neoadjuvant chemotherapy with the same regimen postoperatively (patient entry 1983–2002); mostly anthracycline-based chemotherapy (81%), one trial added a taxane; no trastuzumab; trials such as NSABP B-27 ineligible Ⓐ Neoadjuvant chemotherapy: same regimen as Ⓑ, begun before surgery
Ⓑ Adjuvant chemotherapy: same regimen, all chemotherapy postoperative
・Regimens: Trial-specific; anthracycline-based for 3838 (81%) of 4756 women; one trial (902 women) added a taxane; four trials (918 women) used CMF or MMM Primary: tumour response, extent of local therapy, local recurrence, distant recurrence, breast cancer mortality, overall mortality NACT was associated with more breast-conserving therapy and higher local recurrence than the same chemotherapy given postoperatively, without excess distant recurrence or mortality
・Tumour response: Ⓐ complete response 28%, partial 41%, stable or progressive 31% of 1947 assessed
・BCT: Ⓐ 65% vs Ⓑ 49%; rate ratio 1·28 (95% CI 1·22–1·34)
・Local recurrence: Ⓐ 21·4% vs Ⓑ 15·9% at 15 yr; RR 1·37 (95% CI 1·17–1·61)
・Distant recurrence: Ⓐ 38·2% vs Ⓑ 38·0% at 15 yr; RR 1·02 (95% CI 0·92–1·14)
・Breast cancer mortality: Ⓐ 34·4% vs Ⓑ 33·7%; RR 1·06 (95% CI 0·95–1·18)
・All-cause mortality: Ⓐ 40·9% vs Ⓑ 41·2%; RR 1·04 (95% CI 0·94–1·15)
・Subgroups: 10-yr local recurrence excess largest in two surgery-omission trials (RR 1·62) vs eight others (RR 1·28); heterogeneity p=0·19
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: Surgery extent differed between arms (confounding); trials pre-2005, no trastuzumab; patient-level radiotherapy data unavailable

records.title: CTNeoBC
records.subtitle: General Principles · Neoadjuvant therapy — timing & pathological response · Pooled analysis · 2014
records.body:
HER2-positive early breast cancer treated with neoadjuvant anti-HER2 therapy followed by surgery; individual-patient data from randomised trials enrolling at least 100 patients, with pCR, EFS and OS data and median follow-up of at least 3 years; patients without pCR information excluded, those without surgery counted as nonresponders Ⓐ Pathological complete response (ypT0/is ypN0)
Ⓑ No pathological complete response (residual invasive cancer)
・Chemotherapy: Neoadjuvant anti-HER2 therapy (trastuzumab, lapatinib or pertuzumab) with anthracycline- and taxane-based backbones across 11 randomised trials
・Design: Pooled individual-patient-data responder analysis; EFS and OS compared between Ⓐ and Ⓑ irrespective of treatment assignment
・Trial-level: Randomised contrasts of treatment effect on pCR vs EFS/OS Primary: patient-level association of pathological complete response (ypT0/is ypN0) with event-free survival and overall survival, and trial-level association between treatment effects on pathological complete response and on event-free survival and overall survival. Secondary: correlations by group of clinical question, in hormone receptor–negative disease, and using the more stringent pCR definition (ypT0 ypN0) pCR was associated with better EFS and OS in all subtypes and in HER2-positive disease, but weak trial-level associations precluded validation as a surrogate endpoint
・EFS (all subtypes), Ⓐ vs Ⓑ: ypT0/is ypN0 HR 0.48 (95% CI 0.43–0.54); ypT0 ypN0 0.44 (0.39–0.51); breast-only ypT0/is 0.60 (0.55–0.66)
・OS (all subtypes), Ⓐ vs Ⓑ: ypT0/is ypN0 HR 0.36 (95% CI 0.31–0.42); ypT0 ypN0 0.36 (0.30–0.44); breast-only ypT0/is 0.51 (0.45–0.58)
・EFS (HER2-positive), Ⓐ vs Ⓑ: HR 0.42 (95% CI 0.36–0.49); OR 2.64 (2.20–3.07)
・OS (HER2-positive), Ⓐ vs Ⓑ: HR 0.34 (95% CI 0.27–0.43); OR 3.15 (2.38–3.91)
・Trial-level (all subtypes): pCR gain vs EFS R² 0.03 (95% CI 0.00–0.25); vs OS R² 0.24 (0.00–0.70); ten randomised comparisons
・Trial-level (HER2-positive): Vs EFS R² 0.23 (0 to 0.66); vs OS R² 0.02 (0 to 0.17), paradoxically negative
・Subgroups: Triple-negative EFS 0.24 (0.18–0.33), OS 0.16 (0.11–0.25); HER2-positive/HR-negative with trastuzumab EFS 0.15 (0.09–0.27), OS 0.08 (0.03–0.22); HR-positive/HER2-negative EFS 0.49 (0.33–0.71), OS 0.43 (0.23–0.71)
・Sensitivities (HER2-positive): Stringent ypT0 ypN0 and HR-negative disease qualitatively similar; moderate EFS R² 0.74 and 0.42 in two question groups viewed with extreme caution
・pCR rate: ypT0/is 22%, ypT0/is ypN0 18%, ypT0 ypN0 13%
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: Responder analysis independent of treatment assignment; heterogeneous subtypes and regimens across trials; only two trials significant for pCR

records.title: MDACC-LAB98-240
records.subtitle: General Principles · Neoadjuvant therapy — timing & pathological response · Cohort study with prospective follow-up (five institutional cohorts) · 2017
records.body:
Breast cancer of HR-positive/HER2-negative, HER2-positive or triple-negative phenotype; neoadjuvant chemotherapy (± trastuzumab) then surgery at one institution; HR-positive if ≥10% of nuclei stained, HER2-positive if 3+ in ≥30% of cells or FISH ratio >2.2; excluded previous invasive breast cancer, pre-treatment surgical biopsy of primary or positive node, <75% of prescribed cycles, inflammatory or stage IV disease, adjuvant systemic therapy other than hormonal/HER2-targeted Ⓐ T/FAC: paclitaxel → fluorouracil, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide (cohorts T/FAC-1, -2, -3)
Ⓑ FAC: fluorouracil, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide (validation cohort)
Ⓒ H+T/FEC: trastuzumab concurrent with paclitaxel → fluorouracil, epirubicin, cyclophosphamide, then adjuvant trastuzumab (HER2-positive cohort)
・Design: Non-randomised treatment cohorts; RCB index/class scored by pathology review of the surgical specimen Primary: relapse-free survival, distant relapse-free survival, overall survival, c-index RCB after neoadjuvant chemotherapy was prognostic for long-term RFS in all three breast cancer phenotypic subsets
・RCB index: Adjusted RFS HR per unit significant in all 5 cohorts; combined T/FAC 1.86 (95% CI 1.68–2.05)
・10-yr RFS TNBC (Ⓐ): pCR 86%, RCB-I 81%, RCB-II 55%, RCB-III 23%
・10-yr RFS HR+/HER2− (Ⓐ): pCR 83%, RCB-I 97%, RCB-II 74%, RCB-III 52%
・10-yr RFS HER2+ (Ⓒ): pCR 95%, RCB-I 77%, RCB-II 47%, RCB-III 21%
・10-yr RFS HER2+ without trastuzumab (Ⓐ): pCR 88%, RCB-I 63%, RCB-II 44%, RCB-III 47%
・yp-Stage: RCB classes prognostic within yp-stage II and III, not significantly in yp-stage I
・Subgroups: TNBC residual risk ended before 7 yr; HR+/HER2− RCB-II/III hazard still elevated a decade later
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: Single institution; development cohort included; too small for modest differences (pCR vs RCB-I, yp-stage I)
records.keywords: Symmans et al. J Clin Oncol 2017;35:1049-1060  28135148

records.title: SUPREMO (BIG 2-04)
records.subtitle: General Principles · Adjuvant radiation therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Women with unilateral intermediate-risk stage II breast cancer without distant metastases after mastectomy, axillary surgery and systemic therapy; pT1N1, pT2N1, pT3N0 or pT2N0 with grade 3, lymphovascular invasion or both (T1 ≤2 cm, T2 >2 to 5 cm, T3 >5 cm); minimum clear margin 1 mm; level II axillary clearance mandatory for N1 disease; immediate reconstruction and post-neoadjuvant patients eligible (2010 amendment) Ⓐ Chest-wall irradiation 40 Gy in 15 fractions to 50 Gy in 25 fractions
Ⓑ No chest-wall irradiation
・Systemic therapy: Anthracycline-based chemotherapy ± taxanes recommended; ≥5 years endocrine therapy for ER-positive disease; trastuzumab per local policy
・Design: Axillary irradiation not permitted; elective supraclavicular fossa or internal mammary chain irradiation allowed irrespective of assigned group Primary: overall survival. Secondary: chest-wall recurrence, regional recurrence, disease-free survival, distant metastasis–free survival, cause of death, short-term and long-term radiation-related adverse events, quality of life, cost-effectiveness Chest-wall irradiation did not improve 10-year overall survival over no irradiation after mastectomy for intermediate-risk breast cancer
・OS (10-yr): Ⓐ 81.4% vs Ⓑ 81.9%; HR for death 1.04 (95% CI 0.82–1.30)
・Chest-wall recurrence: Ⓐ 1.1% vs Ⓑ 2.5%; HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.20–0.99); absolute difference <2 percentage points
・Locoregional recurrence: Ⓐ 2.7% vs Ⓑ 4.5%; HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.36–1.03)
・DFS (10-yr): Ⓐ 76.2% vs Ⓑ 75.5%; HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.79–1.18)
・DMFS (10-yr): Ⓐ 78.2% vs Ⓑ 79.2%; HR 1.06 (95% CI 0.86–1.31)
・QoL (5-yr, UK-only substudy): Chest wall symptoms worse with Ⓐ, effect estimate 1.99 (95% CI 0.36–3.62); no difference in global QOL or other domains
・Chest wall symptom worsening (5-yr responder): Ⓐ 13% vs Ⓑ 9%
・Social function (5-yr): Larger improvement with Ⓐ, effect estimate 2.89 (95% CI 0.11–5.67); nominal, multiple testing
・Subgroups: Triple-negative OS appeared lower with irradiation, HR 1.91 (95% CI 1.06–3.46); no differential effect by age or nodal status; QoL: SLNB plus axillary clearance had worse chest wall symptoms with Ⓐ, difference −5.29 (95% CI −8.53 to −2.05)
・Toxicity: Grade ≥2 lung-related events Ⓐ 13 vs Ⓑ 5 (OR 2.59, 95% CI 0.97–8.12); cardiac deaths Ⓐ 0.7% vs Ⓑ 1.0%
・Limitations: 10-yr survival ~81% both arms vs 56% design assumption; CI allows up to 3.8-point OS difference; neoadjuvant exposure very limited

records.title: EBCTCG regional node radiotherapy individual patient data meta-analysis
records.subtitle: General Principles · Adjuvant radiation therapy · Individual patient data meta-analysis · 2023
records.body:
Early breast cancer in women, adjuvant postoperative setting; individual patient data from randomised trials of regional node radiotherapy (internal mammary chain, supraclavicular fossa, or axilla, alone or combined) versus no regional node radiotherapy, started before 2009, with surgery, breast/chest wall radiotherapy and systemic therapy the same in both groups; one DBCG study allocated by tumour laterality; one trial of 165 women with unavailable data excluded Ⓐ Regional node radiotherapy — internal mammary chain, supraclavicular fossa, axilla or combinations (site per trial)
Ⓑ No regional node radiotherapy
・Shared: Within each trial, surgery, breast/chest wall radiotherapy and systemic therapy the same in both groups
・Newer trials (1989–2008): Addition to breast or chest wall radiotherapy; older trials (1961–78): usually nodal radiotherapy vs none
・Design: Individual patient data meta-analysis of 16 trials; one DBCG study allocated by tumour laterality Primary: recurrence at any site, breast cancer mortality, non-breast-cancer mortality, all-cause mortality. Secondary: locoregional recurrence, distant recurrence, heart disease mortality, contralateral breast cancer incidence, second cancer incidence, lymphoedema Regional node radiotherapy significantly reduced breast cancer mortality and all-cause mortality in trials done after the 1980s, but not in older trials
・Any recurrence (newer trials): Ⓐ vs Ⓑ RR 0.88 (95% CI 0.81–0.95); 15-yr absolute gain 2.6% (0.6–4.6)
・Breast cancer mortality (newer trials): Ⓐ vs Ⓑ RR 0.87 (95% CI 0.80–0.94); 15-yr gain 3.0% (1.1–4.9)
・Non-breast-cancer mortality (newer trials): Ⓐ vs Ⓑ RR 0.97 (95% CI 0.84–1.11); no increase seen with 15 years of follow-up
・All-cause mortality (newer trials): Ⓐ vs Ⓑ RR 0.90 (95% CI 0.84–0.96); 15-yr gain 3.0% (1.0–5.0)
・Distant recurrence (newer trials): Ⓐ vs Ⓑ RR 0.86 (95% CI 0.80–0.93)
・Older trials (1961–78): Ⓐ vs Ⓑ breast cancer mortality RR 1.04 (0.91–1.20); all-cause mortality RR 1.17 (1.04–1.31)
・Non-breast-cancer mortality (older trials): Ⓐ vs Ⓑ RR 1.42 (1.18–1.71); excess mainly after year 20
・Subgroups: Illustrative 15-yr breast cancer mortality gains with Ⓐ — pN0 1.6%, pN1–3 2.7%, pN4+ 4.5%; greater proportional effect for medial/central tumours (any recurrence p=0.021)
・Toxicity: Lymphoedema (MA.20) Ⓐ 8.3% vs Ⓑ 4.5%
・Limitations: One 165-woman trial unavailable; DBCG study allocated by laterality, not randomisation; few non-fatal side-effect endpoints
records.keywords: Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group. Lancet 2023;402:1991-2003  37931633

records.title: EBCTCG radiotherapy and extent of surgery for early breast cancer meta-analysis
records.subtitle: General Principles · Adjuvant radiation therapy · Individual patient data meta-analysis · 2005
records.body:
Early breast cancer (node-negative and node-positive); adjuvant local treatment after surgery; women in unconfounded randomised trials begun by 1995 comparing radiotherapy vs no radiotherapy with the same surgery, more vs less surgery, or more surgery vs radiotherapy, with systemic therapy identical between arms Ⓐ Radiotherapy after breast-conserving surgery (generally to the conserved breast) or after mastectomy and axillary clearance (chest wall and regional lymph nodes)
Ⓑ Same surgery without radiotherapy
・Also pooled: More vs less surgery; more surgery vs less surgery plus radiotherapy
・Design: Individual patient data meta-analysis of 78 unconfounded randomised comparisons; systemic therapy identical between trial arms Primary: 5-year isolated local recurrence risk, 15-year breast cancer mortality risk, overall mortality. Secondary: contralateral breast cancer incidence, other second primary cancers, non-breast-cancer mortality Local treatment differences that substantially reduced 5-year local recurrence moderately reduced 15-year breast cancer and overall mortality, avoiding about one breast cancer death per four local recurrences avoided
・5-yr local recurrence: Ⓐ 7% vs Ⓑ 26%; absolute reduction 19% (aggregate of >10%-difference comparisons, 25 000 women)
・15-yr breast cancer mortality: Ⓐ 44.6% vs Ⓑ 49.5%; absolute reduction 5.0% (SE 0.8), 2p<0.00001
・Post-BCS RT: 15-yr breast cancer mortality Ⓐ 30.5% vs Ⓑ 35.9%; absolute reduction 5.4% (SE 1.7); rate ratio 0.83 (95% CI 0.75–0.91); overall mortality reduction 5.3% (SE 1.8)
・Post-mastectomy RT (node-positive): 15-yr breast cancer mortality Ⓐ 54.7% vs Ⓑ 60.1%; absolute reduction 5.4% (SE 1.3); overall mortality reduction 4.4% (SE 1.2)
・Post-mastectomy RT (node-negative): No significant 15-yr breast cancer mortality reduction; 5-yr local recurrence 6% without RT vs 2% with RT
・Four-to-one: 20% absolute 5-yr local recurrence reduction → about 5% absolute 15-yr breast cancer mortality reduction (hypothetical absence of other causes)
・Beyond 15 yr: Breast cancer death rate ratio 1.03; continuing excess non-breast-cancer mortality (rate ratio 1.17)
・Subgroups: Proportional local recurrence reductions similar irrespective of age, grade, tumour size, ER status, nodal involvement; absolute benefit tracks control risk
・Toxicity: Excess contralateral breast cancer (rate ratio Ⓐ 1.18) and non-breast-cancer mortality (rate ratio Ⓐ 1.12), mainly heart disease (Ⓐ 1.27) and lung cancer (Ⓐ 1.78); 15-yr non-breast-cancer mortality Ⓐ 15.9% vs Ⓑ 14.6%
・Limitations: Older RT regimens, late hazards likely lower with modern RT; absolute risks not generalisable due to practice changes; little post-BCS follow-up beyond 15 years

records.title: NSABP B-51 (RTOG 1304)
records.subtitle: General Principles · Adjuvant radiation therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Breast cancer, clinical stage T1–T3 (tumour ≤2 cm to >5 cm), N1 (biopsy-proven movable ipsilateral level I–II axillary nodes), M0, operable; ypN0 at surgery after ≥8 weeks anthracycline- and/or taxane-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy (HER2-positive also required neoadjuvant anti-HER2 therapy unless contraindicated); axillary staging by SLNB (≥2 nodes) or ALND Ⓐ Regional nodal irradiation 50 Gy in 25 fractions (retained level I–III axillary nodes, supraclavicular nodes, internal mammary nodes in first three to four intercostal spaces) with chest wall after mastectomy or whole breast after lumpectomy
Ⓑ No regional nodal irradiation: no radiotherapy after mastectomy or whole-breast irradiation 50 Gy in 25 fractions after lumpectomy
・Whole-breast boost: 12–14 Gy in 6–7 fractions to the surgery site, required after whole-breast irradiation
・Design: Three-dimensional conformal or intensity-modulated radiotherapy; bolus not permitted Primary: invasive breast cancer recurrence–free interval. Secondary: locoregional recurrence–free interval, distant recurrence–free interval, disease-free survival, overall survival, safety, quality-of-life measures Adjuvant regional nodal irradiation did not decrease invasive breast cancer recurrence or death from breast cancer at 5 years in ypN0 disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy
・IBC recurrence–free interval: Ⓐ 92.7% vs Ⓑ 91.8% at 5 years; HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.60–1.28); P=0.51
・Locoregional recurrence–free interval: Ⓐ 98.9% vs Ⓑ 98.4% at 5 years; HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.21–1.54)
・Distant recurrence–free interval: Ⓐ 93.4% vs Ⓑ 93.4% at 5 years; HR 1.00 (95% CI 0.67–1.51)
・DFS: Ⓐ 88.3% vs Ⓑ 88.5% at 5 years; HR 1.06 (95% CI 0.79–1.44)
・OS: Ⓐ 93.6% vs Ⓑ 94.0% at 5 years; HR 1.12 (95% CI 0.75–1.68)
・Subgroups: Exploratory by subtype — triple negative HR 2.30 (95% CI 1.00–5.25) vs HR+/HER2− HR 0.41 (95% CI 0.17–0.99)
・Toxicity: G3 Ⓐ 10.0% vs Ⓑ 6.5%; G4 Ⓐ 0.5% vs Ⓑ 0.1%; G3 radiation dermatitis Ⓐ 5.7% vs Ⓑ 3.3%; no protocol-related deaths
・Limitations: Final analysis time-driven with 109 of planned 172 events; exploratory subtype subgroups small with wide CIs; HR+/HER2− needs longer follow-up
records.keywords: Mamounas et al. N Engl J Med 2025;392:2113-2124  40466065

records.title: EBCTCG adjuvant bisphosphonate meta-analysis
records.subtitle: General Principles · Bone-targeted adjuvant therapy (bisphosphonates) · Individual patient data meta-analysis · 2015
records.body:
Women with early breast cancer in unconfounded randomised trials begun before 2008 of adjuvant bisphosphonate (any type, dose, schedule) versus control (open label or placebo, no bisphosphonate), all other treatments similar; 97% in trials of 2–5 years of treatment; median follow-up 5·6 woman-years Ⓐ Adjuvant bisphosphonate of any type, dose and schedule: clodronate or aminobisphosphonate (zoledronic acid, ibandronate, pamidronate, risedronate); mean scheduled duration 3·4 years, 2–5 years in 97% of women
Ⓑ Control (open label or placebo) with no bisphosphonate; all other treatments similar in both groups Primary: any recurrence, distant recurrence, breast cancer mortality. Secondary: all-cause mortality, death without recurrence, bone recurrence as the first distant recurrence, other first (extraskeletal) distant recurrence, locoregional recurrence as first event, contralateral new primary breast cancer as first event, any bone fractures Adjuvant bisphosphonates reduced bone recurrence and improved breast cancer survival, with definite benefit only in postmenopausal women
・Recurrence: Ⓐ 24·9% vs Ⓑ 25·9% at 10 years; RR 0·94 (95% CI 0·87–1·01)
・Distant recurrence: Ⓐ 20·4% vs Ⓑ 21·8% at 10 years; RR 0·92 (0·85–0·99)
・Breast cancer mortality: Ⓐ 16·6% vs Ⓑ 18·4% at 10 years; RR 0·91 (0·83–0·99)
・Bone recurrence: Ⓐ 7·8% vs Ⓑ 9·0% at 10 years; RR 0·83 (0·73–0·94)
・All-cause mortality: Ⓐ 20·8% vs Ⓑ 22·3% at 10 years; RR 0·92 (0·85–1·00)
・Fractures: Ⓐ 6·3% vs Ⓑ 7·3%; RR 0·85 (0·75–0·97)
・Extraskeletal: No significant effect on extraskeletal distant, locoregional or contralateral recurrence, overall or postmenopausal
・Subgroups: Postmenopausal (n=11 767) recurrence RR 0·86 (0·78–0·94), bone recurrence RR 0·72 (0·60–0·86), breast cancer mortality RR 0·82 (0·73–0·93); premenopausal no apparent effect
・Postmenopausal 10-yr gains: Bone recurrence 2·2% (0·6–3·8; Ⓐ 6·6% vs Ⓑ 8·8%); breast cancer mortality 3·3% (0·8–5·7; Ⓐ 14·7% vs Ⓑ 18·0%)
・Toxicity: Not systematically collected; ONJ incidence not assessable; major adverse events uncommon (impaired renal function, osteonecrosis of the jaw)
・Limitations: Menopausal-status heterogeneity borderline (trend 2p=0·06); fracture data only 71% of women; limited follow-up beyond 5 years

records.title: SUBITO
records.subtitle: General Principles · High-dose chemotherapy & autologous stem-cell transplant · Randomised, open-label, controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Newly diagnosed stage IIIA–C HER2-negative breast cancer without distant metastasis; pathogenic germline BRCA1/2 mutation or HRD tumour on BRCA1-like MLPA testing (done if TNBC or grade 3 with ER and PgR expression <50%); aged 18–66 years; neoadjuvant systemic treatment setting Ⓐ IACT: ddAC four cycles → two mCTC cycles (cyclophosphamide 3000 mg/m² day 1, thiotepa 250 mg/m² day 2, carboplatin 400 mg/m² days 1 and 2, 3 weeks apart) each followed by autologous stem cell transplantation
Ⓑ ddAC four cycles → carboplatin AUC 6 IV every 3 weeks for four cycles + paclitaxel 80 mg/m² weekly for 12 weeks → olaparib 300 mg orally twice daily for 52 weeks
・ddAC: Doxorubicin 60 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² IV every 2 weeks with pegfilgrastim 6 mg SC every 2 weeks
・All: Surgery and radiotherapy per local practice; endocrine therapy if hormone receptor-positive; capecitabine 1000–1250 mg/m² twice daily (14 days on, 1 week rest) for 6–8 cycles if no pCR after Oct 4, 2019 amendment
・Design: Open-label; stratified by centre, age, stage and ER status Primary: overall survival. Secondary: overall survival in the gBRCAwt–HRD group, recurrence-free survival, pathological complete response rate, toxicity, health-related quality of life, cost-effectiveness IACT did not improve 4-year overall survival over standard chemotherapy followed by 1 year of olaparib in stage III HER2-negative HRD breast cancer
・4-yr OS: Ⓐ 77·0% vs Ⓑ 76·4%; HR 1·11 (95% CI 0·57–2·17); median follow-up 41 mo
・4-yr OS (gBRCAwt–HRD, key secondary): Ⓐ 73·8% vs Ⓑ 71·5%; HR 0·97 (95% CI 0·46–2·05)
・4-yr RFS: Ⓐ 76·8% vs Ⓑ 70·0%; HR 0·91 (95% CI 0·48–1·71)
・pCR: Ⓐ 40% vs Ⓑ 44%
・4-yr OS by pCR (post-hoc): With pCR Ⓐ 96·7% vs Ⓑ 97·0%; without pCR Ⓐ 64·3% vs Ⓑ 58·2%
・QoL: No statistically significant or clinically meaningful QLQ-C30 global health status differences over time
・Toxicity: G3–4 febrile neutropenia Ⓐ 44% vs Ⓑ 12%; platelet count decreased Ⓐ 99% vs Ⓑ 19%; no treatment-related deaths
・Limitations: Open-label; powered for a large effect (assumed HR 0·353), possibly underpowered; pembrolizumab not in regimens

records.title: SENOMAC
records.subtitle: General Principles · Axillary management — surgical de-escalation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body:
Female or male breast cancer, cN0 T1–T3 (T1 ≤20 mm; T2 21–50 mm; T3 >50 mm) treated with breast-conserving surgery or mastectomy; one or two sentinel-node macrometastases (>2 mm), with additional micrometastases and extracapsular extension allowed; primary systemic treatment allowed (2016 amendment) if sentinel-node biopsy came before it; excluded extra-axillary regional or distant metastases, prior invasive breast cancer Ⓐ Sentinel-node biopsy only (no further axillary surgery)
Ⓑ Completion axillary-lymph-node dissection (same session or second surgery)
・Adjuvant therapy: Systemic treatment and radiation therapy per national guidelines; whole-breast radiation therapy mandatory after breast-conserving surgery
・Design: Non-inferiority Primary: overall survival. Secondary: recurrence-free survival, breast cancer–specific survival, patient-reported outcomes Omitting completion axillary dissection was non-inferior to dissection for overall survival, the primary endpoint, and reduced patient-reported arm morbidity
・5-yr OS (primary analysis, median follow-up 60.1 mo): Ⓐ 94.4% vs Ⓑ 93.4%; HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.64–1.12); below 1.44 non-inferiority margin
・5-yr RFS: Ⓐ 89.7% vs Ⓑ 88.7%; HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.66–1.19); below the 1.44 non-inferiority margin (P<0.001)
・mITT RFS: HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.67–1.19); consistent with per-protocol result
・5-yr BCSS (median follow-up 60.1 mo): Ⓐ 97.8% vs Ⓑ 97.3%; HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.55–1.34); below non-inferiority margin
・Arm function (Lymph-ICF): Better with Ⓐ; mean difference 6.14 at 3 yr (95% CI 5.00–7.43), 5.71 at 5 yr (95% CI 4.46–7.25)
・Arm symptoms (QLQ-BR23): Worse with Ⓑ; Ⓐ 10.83 vs Ⓑ 20.80 at 3 yr; Ⓐ 9.31 vs Ⓑ 19.40 at 5 yr
・QoL: No significant difference in global health-related quality of life at 3 or 5 yr
・Subgroups: ER-positive/HER2-positive HR 0.26 (95% CI 0.07–0.96); not prespecified, no formal testing
・Toxicity: Not reported; arm morbidity reported only as patient-reported outcomes
・Limitations: Most patients received nodal radiotherapy; short follow-up for late-recurring luminal disease; questionnaire response 74.6% at 5 yr

records.title: ACOSOG Z0011 (Alliance)
records.subtitle: General Principles · Axillary management — surgical de-escalation · Randomised non-inferiority clinical trial (phase III) · 2011
records.body:
Women with clinical T1-T2 invasive breast cancer (5 cm or less), no palpable adenopathy, and 1-2 sentinel nodes containing metastases on frozen section, touch preparation, or hematoxylin-eosin staining; lumpectomy to negative margins required; ineligible if 3 or more positive SLNs, matted nodes, gross extranodal disease, IHC-only metastases, or prior neoadjuvant therapy Ⓐ Axillary lymph node dissection (levels I and II, at least 10 nodes)
Ⓑ SLND alone; no further axillary treatment, no third-field nodal irradiation
・Shared: Lumpectomy and tangential whole-breast irradiation
・Adjuvant systemic therapy: At treating physician's discretion, not protocol-specified Primary: overall survival. Secondary: disease-free survival, locoregional recurrence, surgical morbidities SLND alone was non-inferior to ALND for 10-year overall survival in women with 1-2 sentinel node metastases treated with breast conservation
・10-yr OS: Ⓐ 83.6 vs Ⓑ 86.3%; HR 0.85 (1-sided 95% CI 0-1.16), non-inferiority P=.02; median follow-up 9.3 yr
・10-yr DFS: Ⓐ 78.2 vs Ⓑ 80.2%; HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.62-1.17)
・5-yr local recurrence: Ⓐ 3.1 vs Ⓑ 1.6% (P=.11); total locoregional recurrence Ⓐ 3.6 vs Ⓑ 2.5%
・Regional recurrence yr 5-10: Ⓑ 1 vs Ⓐ none; 10-yr regional recurrence did not differ significantly
・Toxicity: Wound infection, seroma and paresthesias Ⓐ 70% vs Ⓑ 25% (P<.001); lymphedema more common with Ⓐ (P<.001)
・Limitations: Closed early, Ⓐ+Ⓑ 891 of 1900 target and Ⓐ+Ⓑ 110 vs 500 planned deaths; 10-yr OS analysis not prespecified; Ⓐ+Ⓑ 18.9% protocol-prohibited nodal irradiation, similarly distributed

records.title: AMAROS
records.subtitle: General Principles · Axillary management — surgical de-escalation · Randomised, multicentre, open-label, non-inferiority clinical trial (phase III) · 2014
records.body:
Invasive T1–2 primary breast cancer, initially unifocal up to 3 cm, broadened from a Feb 22, 2008 amendment to tumours up to 5 cm or multifocal disease; no palpable lymphadenopathy with positive sentinel node; fit for any protocol axillary procedure; excluded previous malignancy, neoadjuvant systemic treatment, prior axillary surgery or radiotherapy Ⓐ Axillary lymph node dissection: dissection of at least anatomical levels I and II including at least ten nodes; adjuvant axillary radiotherapy allowed when at least four positive nodes were found
Ⓑ Axillary radiotherapy: all three levels of the axilla and medial part of the supraclavicular fossa; prescribed dose 25 fractions of 2 Gy
・Timing: Axillary treatment within 12 weeks after sentinel node biopsy; systemic treatment, if indicated, after completing axillary treatment
・Breast treatment: Breast-conserving treatment with whole-breast radiotherapy or mastectomy with or without chest-wall irradiation; adjuvant systemic treatment at the multidisciplinary team's discretion
・Design: Open-label; randomisation before sentinel node biopsy Primary: 5-year axillary recurrence. Secondary: axillary recurrence-free survival, disease-free survival, overall survival, shoulder mobility, lymphoedema, QoL Axillary radiotherapy gave axillary control comparable to axillary lymph node dissection with significantly less lymphoedema; the planned non-inferiority test was underpowered
・5-yr axillary recurrence: Ⓐ 0·43% vs Ⓑ 1·19%; underpowered non-inferiority test, one-sided 95% CI 0·00–5·27 (margin 2)
・5-yr DFS: Ⓐ 86·9% vs Ⓑ 82·7%; HR 1·18 (95% CI 0·93–1·51)
・5-yr OS: Ⓐ 93·3% vs Ⓑ 92·5%; HR 1·17 (95% CI 0·85–1·62)
・QoL: No significant or clinically relevant differences in arm symptoms, pain, or body image; shoulder range of motion did not differ
・Toxicity: Clinical lymphoedema signs 1 yr Ⓐ 28% vs Ⓑ 15%, 5 yr Ⓐ 23% vs Ⓑ 11% (p<0·0001); arm-circumference increase ≥10% at 5 yr Ⓐ 13% vs Ⓑ 6%
・Limitations: Underpowered primary test (few events); imbalance of sentinel-node-positive patients across arms; open-label

records.title: CALOR (IBCSG 27-02, BIG 1-02, NSABP B-37)
records.subtitle: General Principles · ISOLATED locoregional recurrence · Randomised, open-label, pragmatic clinical trial · 2014
records.body:
Breast cancer with histologically proven, completely excised first isolated locoregional recurrence (ILRR) with clear margins; adjuvant post-resection setting; women of any age suitable for 3–6 months of chemotherapy with available hormone receptor status; ILRR without distant metastasis; previous malignancy other than the original breast cancer excluded Ⓐ Chemotherapy, investigator-selected, mainly anthracycline-based; at least two cytotoxic drugs for 3–6 months recommended
Ⓑ No chemotherapy
・Endocrine therapy: Recommended for all patients with oestrogen-receptor-positive or progesterone-receptor-positive ILRR
・Radiotherapy: Recommended for all patients; required for microscopically involved surgical margins
・Anti-HER2 therapy: Optional
・Design: Open-label, pragmatic Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, sites of first recurrence, incidence of second non-breast malignancies, causes of death without relapse of breast cancer, safety Adjuvant chemotherapy after complete resection of breast cancer ILRR improved disease-free and overall survival, particularly with oestrogen-receptor-negative recurrence
・5-yr DFS: Ⓐ 69% vs Ⓑ 57%; HR 0.59 (95% CI 0.35–0.99)
・5-yr OS: Ⓐ 88% vs Ⓑ 76%; HR 0.41 (95% CI 0.19–0.89)
・DFS, ER-negative ILRR: Ⓐ 67% vs Ⓑ 35% at 5 yr; HR 0.32 (0.14–0.73); pinteraction=0.046
・DFS, ER-positive ILRR: HR 0.94 (0.47–1.89); benefit cannot be excluded
・Toxicity: SAEs in 12 (15%) of 81 chemotherapy recipients; neutropenia, febrile neutropenia, intestinal infection most common
・Limitations: Closed early at 162 patients (planned 265); open-label; wide CIs in small ER subgroups

records.title: MINDACT (EORTC 10041/BIG 3-04)
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body:
Women aged 18–70 with histologically confirmed primary invasive breast cancer (T1, T2 or operable T3); postsurgical decision on adjuvant chemotherapy guided by genomic risk (70-gene signature) versus clinical risk (Adjuvant! Online); node-negative by initial design, amended from August 2009 to allow up to three positive axillary nodes Ⓐ Adjuvant chemotherapy, use directed by clinical-risk result in patients at high clinical and low genomic risk or by genomic-risk result in those at low clinical and high genomic risk
Ⓑ No adjuvant chemotherapy, use directed by genomic-risk result in patients at high clinical and low genomic risk or by clinical-risk result in those at low clinical and high genomic risk
・Risk tools: Genomic risk by 70-gene signature (MammaPrint); clinical risk by Adjuvant! Online (version 8.0 with HER2 status)
・Concordant risk: Low clinical and low genomic risk advised no chemotherapy; high clinical and high genomic risk advised chemotherapy Primary: survival without distant metastasis at 5 years. Secondary: proportion of patients who received chemotherapy by clinical-risk versus genomic-risk strategy, overall survival, disease-free survival Forgoing chemotherapy guided by the low genomic-risk result met the noninferiority boundary for 5-year survival without distant metastasis, at a cost of 1.5 percentage points
・DMFS (primary test): Ⓑ 94.7% (95% CI 92.5 to 96.2); lower boundary above 92% noninferiority margin
・DMFS (randomized ITT): Ⓐ 95.9% vs Ⓑ 94.4% at 5 years; adjusted HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.50 to 1.21)
・DFS and OS: 5-year rates 2.8 and 1.4 percentage points higher with Ⓐ (ITT); study not powered for significance
・Chemotherapy use: Genomic-risk guidance would spare adjuvant chemotherapy in 1550 of 3356 high-clinical-risk patients (46.2%)
・Strategies: 5-year DMFS 95.0% clinical-risk vs 94.7% genomic-risk strategy; similar outcomes, much lower chemotherapy use genomically
・Low clinical, high genomic risk: Ⓐ 95.8% vs Ⓑ 95.0% at 5 years; HR 1.17 (95% CI 0.59 to 2.28)
・Subgroups: Similar DMFS in ER-positive, HER2-negative disease and across node-negative and one-to-three-node subgroups
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: Not powered for chemotherapy-comparison significance; 5-year median follow-up only; adherence 86%
records.keywords: Cardoso et al. N Engl J Med 2016;375:717-729  27557300

records.title: TAILORx
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation · Randomised clinical trial (non-inferiority design) · 2018
records.body:
Hormone-receptor–positive, HER2-negative, axillary node–negative early breast cancer (adjuvant setting); women 18–75 years of age; 21-gene (Oncotype DX) recurrence score 11–25 on central assay; met NCCN guidelines for recommendation or consideration of adjuvant chemotherapy; full inclusion and exclusion criteria in Supplementary Appendix (not supplied) Ⓐ Endocrine therapy alone (physician-choice endocrine regimen)
Ⓑ Chemoendocrine therapy (physician-choice adjuvant chemotherapy plus endocrine therapy)
・Endocrine therapy: Median duration 5.4 years; approximately 35% treated beyond 5 years; aromatase inhibitor in 91% of postmenopausal women, tamoxifen alone or followed by aromatase inhibitor in 78% of premenopausal women, ovarian function suppression in 13% of premenopausal women
・Chemotherapy (Ⓑ): Most common docetaxel–cyclophosphamide (56%) and anthracycline-containing regimens (36%)
・Design: Non-inferiority of Ⓐ endocrine therapy alone vs Ⓑ chemoendocrine therapy for invasive disease–free survival Primary: Invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: Freedom from recurrence of breast cancer at a distant site, Freedom from recurrence of breast cancer at a distant or local-regional site, Overall survival Endocrine therapy alone was noninferior to chemoendocrine therapy for invasive disease–free survival; exploratory analyses suggested some chemotherapy benefit in women ≤50 years
・iDFS (9 yr, final analysis): Ⓐ 83.3% vs Ⓑ 84.3%; HR 1.08 (95% CI 0.94–1.24), P=0.26
・Freedom from distant recurrence (9 yr): Ⓐ 94.5% vs Ⓑ 95.0%; HR 1.10, P=0.48
・Freedom from distant or local–regional recurrence (9 yr): Ⓐ 92.2% vs Ⓑ 92.9%; HR 1.11, P=0.33
・OS (9 yr): Ⓐ 93.9% vs Ⓑ 93.8%; HR 0.99, P=0.89
・Other cohorts: 9-yr iDFS 84.0% (RS ≤10, endocrine) and 75.7% (RS ≥26, chemoendocrine); 9-yr distant recurrence ~3% (RS ≤10)
・Subgroups: Age × recurrence-score interaction P=0.004; women ≤50 yr with RS 21–25, chemotherapy associated with 6.5 percentage-point lower distant recurrence at 9 yr
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: Nonadherence 12% overall (as-treated iDFS HR 1.14, 95% CI 0.99–1.31); subgroup analyses exploratory; distant recurrences only 24% of first events
records.keywords: Sparano et al. N Engl J Med 2018;379:111-121  29860917

records.title: RxPONDER
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation · Randomised clinical trial · 2021
records.body:
Hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer with one to three positive axillary nodes (N1), non-inflammatory, without distant metastasis; 21-gene recurrence score 25 or lower (range 0–100); adjuvant setting after primary surgery with sentinel-node biopsy or axillary lymph-node dissection; eligible for taxane, anthracycline, or both Ⓐ Endocrine therapy only
Ⓑ Chemotherapy followed by endocrine (chemoendocrine) therapy
・Chemotherapy: Approved protocol options; preferred anthracycline plus taxane for premenopausal women (54%), taxane plus cyclophosphamide for postmenopausal women (57%)
・Follow-up: Planned 15 years after randomization Primary: invasive disease–free survival. Secondary: distant relapse–free survival, overall survival Adjuvant chemotherapy improved invasive disease–free and distant relapse–free survival in premenopausal women but not postmenopausal women with recurrence score 25 or lower
・iDFS overall (third interim): Ⓑ 92.2% vs Ⓐ 91.0% at 5 yr; HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.72–1.03)
・Predictive effect: Recurrence score did not predict relative chemotherapy benefit (P=0.35)
・iDFS premenopausal: Ⓑ 93.9% vs Ⓐ 89.0% at 5 yr; HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.43–0.83)
・iDFS postmenopausal: Ⓑ 91.3% vs Ⓐ 91.9% at 5 yr; HR 1.02 (95% CI 0.82–1.26)
・DRFS overall: Ⓑ 94.9% vs Ⓐ 93.9% at 5 yr; HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.71–1.09)
・DRFS premenopausal: HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.39–0.87); absolute gain 3.3 percentage points at 5 yr
・DRFS postmenopausal: HR 1.05 (95% CI 0.81–1.37)
・Subgroups: Menopausal-status interaction P=0.008; benefit across all premenopausal subgroups, none postmenopausal
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: Third interim analysis with 58% of expected events; 16.2% declined chemoendocrine vs 5.8% endocrine-only assignments; overall survival immature
records.keywords: Kalinsky et al. N Engl J Med 2021;385:2336-2347  34914339

records.title: Paik et al. (NSABP B-20 21-gene recurrence score chemotherapy-benefit analysis)
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation · Randomised clinical trial · 2006
records.body:
Primary invasive breast cancer, axillary node-negative, ER-positive; adjuvant NSABP B20 (tamoxifen ± chemotherapy); retrospective 21-gene recurrence-score assay on archived tumor blocks; tumor block available in NSABP Tumor Bank required; excluded insufficient tumor (≤5% tissue), insufficient RNA (≤0.5 μg), weak RT-PCR signal (reference-gene cycle threshold >35) Ⓐ Tamoxifen alone
Ⓑ Tamoxifen plus CMF or MF chemotherapy
・Tamoxifen: 5 years
・Chemo: Cyclophosphamide, methotrexate and fluorouracil (CMF) or methotrexate and fluorouracil (MF)
・Design: Retrospective recurrence-score assay on randomly assigned NSABP B20 patients; two chemotherapy arms combined for primary analysis Primary: freedom from distant recurrence. Secondary: freedom from any relapse (locoregional or distant), overall survival Recurrence score predicted the magnitude of chemotherapy benefit (tamoxifen ± CMF/MF vs tamoxifen alone) in node-negative, ER-positive breast cancer
・Interaction: Chemotherapy × RS interaction P = .038; RS was the strongest predictor of chemotherapy benefit
・10-yr DRF: Ⓐ 87.8% vs Ⓑ 92.2%
・High RS (≥31): Ⓐ 60.5% vs Ⓑ 88.1% 10-yr DRF; RR 0.26 (95% CI 0.13–0.53); absolute decrease 27.6%
・Low RS (≤18): Ⓐ 96.8% vs Ⓑ 95.6% 10-yr DRF; RR 1.31 (95% CI 0.46–3.78); absolute change −1.1%
・Intermediate RS (18–30): RR 0.61 (95% CI 0.24–1.59); clinically important benefit not excluded
・10-yr OS: Ⓐ 86.4% vs Ⓑ 89.5%
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: Retrospective analysis (651 of 2,299 eligible); tamoxifen-arm tissue used in assay development; no clear RS cutoff for no benefit
records.keywords: Paik et al. J Clin Oncol 2006;24:3726-3734  16720680

records.title: OPTIMA
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation · Randomised non-inferiority clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
ER-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer of high clinical risk recommended to receive adjuvant chemotherapy; mostly node-positive, 0-9 involved axillary nodes with tumour size >30 mm if node negative; women and men aged >40 Ⓐ Standard chemotherapy followed by endocrine therapy (CET)
Ⓑ Prosigna (PAM50) test-directed decision: ROR score >60 → CET; low ROR score (≤60) → endocrine therapy (ET) alone
・Premenopausal ET: Includes ovarian function suppression (OFS) absent chemotherapy-induced ovarian insufficiency
・Design: Open-label in test-directed arm; ROR scores undisclosed; CET patients blinded to randomisation Primary: 5-year invasive breast cancer free survival Prosigna test-directed chemotherapy was non-inferior to standard chemotherapy for 5-year IBCFS, meeting the pre-defined margin
・5-yr IBCFS: Ⓐ 91.5% vs Ⓑ 90.4%; HR 0.99 (90% CI 0.81-1.20); NI p=0.013
・5-yr IBCFS, low ROR (≤60): Ⓐ 94.9% vs Ⓑ 93.7%; HR 1.06 (90% CI 0.78-1.46); NI p=0.0051
・Chemo omission: Low ROR score (≤60) tumors received ET alone if test-directed; 68% of PP population had low ROR score
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: First results; median follow-up 3.9 years; NI tested in per-protocol population
records.keywords: Stein et al. ASCO Oral Abstract Session 2026, abstract 500

records.title: ASTER 70s
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Women aged 70 years and older with oestrogen receptor-positive (≥10% by immunohistochemistry) HER2-negative primary breast cancer or isolated local relapse after complete surgery and before systemic treatment; genomic grade index (GGI) high-risk (threshold –0·277 or higher) required for randomisation; any tumour size, nodal status or medical history; chemotherapy discussable and patient agreement to GGI-guided decision; neoadjuvant treatment not permitted Ⓐ Doxorubicin 60 mg/m² or non-pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 60 mg/m² or docetaxel 75 mg/m², each with cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m², IV every 3 weeks for 4 cycles → hormonotherapy
Ⓑ Hormonotherapy alone
・Hormonotherapy: Tamoxifen, an aromatase inhibitor, or a sequence of the two, for 5 years with possible extension
・Design: No blinded procedure; 84 clinical sites in France and Belgium Primary: overall survival. Secondary: invasive disease-free survival, breast cancer-specific survival, safety, quality of life, acceptability of chemotherapy, cost-effectiveness Adjuvant chemotherapy added to hormonotherapy did not improve overall survival in women aged 70 years and older with GGI high-risk ER-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer
・OS: Ⓐ 90.5% vs Ⓑ 89.3% at 4 years; Ⓐ 72.7% vs Ⓑ 68.3% at 8 years; HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.63–1.11)
・IDFS: Ⓐ 82.7% vs Ⓑ 79.9% at 4 years; Ⓐ 62.4% vs Ⓑ 59.4% at 8 years; HR 0.90 (95% CI 0.71–1.15)
・BCSS: Ⓐ 96.8% vs Ⓑ 95.3% at 4 years; Ⓐ 89.6% vs Ⓑ 86.7% at 8 years; HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.51–1.23)
・Subgroups: No significant differential treatment effect (age, G8, Lee score, pN, pT, GGI subcategory); per-protocol analysis consistent
・QoL: Time to definitive deterioration of quality of life shorter with Ⓐ chemotherapy in several dimensions
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 AEs Ⓐ 34% vs Ⓑ 9%; deaths Ⓐ 3 (1 treatment-related) vs Ⓑ 1 (not treatment-related)
・Limitations: No blinded procedure; 111 (21%) of Ⓐ did not start chemotherapy; null hypothesis set indirectly, control better than expected

records.title: NCIC CTG MA.27
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2013
records.body:
Postmenopausal women with histologically confirmed, adequately excised, hormone receptor–positive invasive breast cancer; initial adjuvant therapy; postmenopausal defined as age ≥60 years, age 45–59 with spontaneous cessation of menses >12 months (or <12 months with postmenopausal-range FSH), or bilateral oophorectomy; excluded receptor-negative tumors, prior tamoxifen, metachronous contralateral primaries, other prior cancer except nonmelanoma skin cancer or cervical carcinoma in situ Ⓐ Exemestane 25 mg orally once daily
Ⓑ Anastrozole 1 mg orally once daily
・Duration: Up to 5 years or until unacceptable toxicity
・Design: Open-label; original celecoxib factorial discontinued early, patients retained and stratified Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, distant disease-free survival, incidence of contralateral new primary breast cancer, disease-specific survival, safety Neither exemestane nor anastrozole was superior for event-free survival or other breast cancer outcomes as 5-year initial adjuvant therapy
・EFS: Ⓐ 91.0% vs Ⓑ 91.2% at 4 years; HR 1.02 (95% CI 0.87 to 1.18); final analysis, median follow-up 4.1 years
・OS: Deaths Ⓐ 5.5% vs Ⓑ 5.9%; HR 0.93 (95% CI 0.77 to 1.13)
・DDFS: Ⓐ 4.1% vs Ⓑ 4.3% events; HR 0.95 (95% CI 0.76 to 1.18)
・DSS: Ⓐ 2.4% vs Ⓑ 2.6% events; HR 0.93 (95% CI 0.70 to 1.24)
・Contralateral new primaries: Ⓐ 46 vs Ⓑ 33 patients
・Subgroups: Exploratory race/ethnicity by treatment interaction significant (HR 0.38; 95% CI 0.17 to 0.83); minority women on exemestane fewer deaths
・Toxicity: No treatment-related deaths; osteoporosis Ⓐ 31% vs Ⓑ 35%; fragility fractures 4% each; atrial fibrillation Ⓐ 72 vs Ⓑ 46 patients
・Discontinuation: Ⓐ 33.8% vs Ⓑ 29.4% for adverse effects, concomitant disease or study refusal
・Limitations: Open-label may have influenced adverse-event reporting; exploratory race findings need confirmation; median follow-up 4.1 years
records.keywords: Goss et al. J Clin Oncol 2013;31:1398-1404  23358971

records.title: BIG 1-98
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · Randomised, double-blind clinical trial (phase III) · 2005
records.body:
Postmenopausal women with operable invasive breast cancer positive for estrogen receptors, progesterone receptors, or both, after primary surgery with clear margins (adjuvant endocrine therapy setting); excluded metastatic disease, previous or concurrent cancer within 5 years, and prior adjuvant antiestrogen therapy for at least 1 month Ⓐ Letrozole 2.5 mg daily for five years (or two years → tamoxifen for three years)
Ⓑ Tamoxifen 20 mg daily for five years (or two years → letrozole for three years)
・Design: Double-blind; primary core analysis compares initial treatments, including sequential-arm events up to 30 days after switch Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, systemic disease-free survival, safety, disease-free survival excluding second nonbreast cancers, time to recurrence, time to distant recurrence, breast cancer mortality, time to contralateral breast cancer, second nonbreast primary cancers Initial letrozole significantly improved disease-free survival versus tamoxifen, but by 12.6 years' follow-up only modest, nonsignificant trends favoring letrozole remained
・5-yr DFS: Ⓐ 84.0% vs Ⓑ 81.4%; HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.70–0.93); median follow-up 25.8 mo
・DFS (12.6-yr LTFU): HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.81–1.01), nonsignificant 9% hazard reduction with letrozole
・Distant recurrence (25.8-mo analysis): HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.60–0.88)
・DRFI (12.6-yr LTFU): HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.72–1.005; P=.057)
・OS (25.8-mo analysis): Deaths Ⓐ 4.1% vs Ⓑ 4.8%; HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.70–1.06), not significant
・OS (12.6-yr LTFU): HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.77–1.02; P=.087)
・Systemic DFS: HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.72–0.97), favored letrozole
・BCFI (12.6-yr LTFU): HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.77–1.02; P=.10)
・Breast cancer mortality (12.6-yr LTFU): HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.74–1.07), nonsignificant 11% reduction
・Death without prior cancer event: Ⓐ 1.4% vs Ⓑ 0.9%, not significantly different
・Contralateral BC (LTFU): HR 0.62 (0–5 yr), 0.47 (95% CI 0.23–0.97; 5–10 yr), 1.35 (>10 yr); treatment-by-time P=.005, reverses beyond 10 yr
・Second nonbreast primaries: 18% increase with Ⓑ, largely endometrial cancer excess during original study
・Let→Tam sequence: DFS cumulative incidence Ⓐ 12.3% vs sequence 12.6% at 5 yr; Ⓐ 35.5% vs 36.2% at 14 yr
・Subgroups: Node-positive 5-yr DFS Ⓐ 77.9% vs Ⓑ 71.4%; node-negative 88.7% both; greater letrozole effect with prior chemotherapy; 12.6-yr HRs similar across nodal groups
・Toxicity (treatment period): Fractures Ⓐ 5.7% vs Ⓑ 4.0%; grade 3–5 cardiac events Ⓐ 2.1% vs Ⓑ 1.1%; thromboembolism Ⓐ 1.5% vs Ⓑ 3.5%; vaginal bleeding Ⓐ 3.3% vs Ⓑ 6.6%
・Toxicity (LTFU, per 1,000 pt-yr): Other cardiac Ⓐ 8.4 vs Ⓑ 3.0; thromboembolic Ⓐ 4.1 vs Ⓑ 2.0; fracture Ⓐ 14.9 vs Ⓑ 15.6; MI Ⓐ 3.9 vs Ⓑ 3.4
・Limitations: 12.6-yr ITT diluted by Ⓑ crossover to letrozole (25.2%); 167/247 centers closed, ~30% without LTFU, weighted analysis; 25.8-mo core analysis counted sequential-arm follow-up to 30 days after switch
records.keywords: Thürlimann et al. N Engl J Med 2005;353:2747-2757  16382061 Ruhstaller et al. J Clin Oncol 2019;37:105-114  30475668

records.title: ATAC
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · Randomised clinical trial · 2002
records.body:
Postmenopausal women with histologically proven operable invasive breast cancer after primary surgery and chemotherapy (if given), candidates for adjuvant hormonal therapy; postmenopausal defined by bilateral oophorectomy, age >60 years, or age 45–59 with amenorrhoea ≥12 months; hormone-receptor status not required for entry; excluded metastatic disease, previous invasive malignancy, prior hormonal therapy, unwillingness to stop HRT, severe concomitant disease Ⓐ Anastrozole 1 mg orally daily (+ tamoxifen placebo)
Ⓑ Tamoxifen 20 mg orally daily (+ anastrozole placebo)
Ⓒ Anastrozole 1 mg + tamoxifen 20 mg orally daily (discontinued after the initial analysis)
・Duration: Planned 5 years; stopped on refusal, confirmed recurrence, or investigator recommendation
・Design: Double-dummy placebo-controlled Primary: disease-free survival, occurrence of adverse events. Secondary: time to recurrence, incidence of new contralateral primary breast tumours, distant recurrence, overall survival, death after recurrence, death without recurrence Anastrozole maintained improved disease-free survival versus tamoxifen in postmenopausal early breast cancer at the 10-year analysis (median follow-up 120 months)
・DFS (first analysis, median 33.3 mo): Ⓐ 89.4% vs Ⓑ 87.4% at 3 years; HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.71–0.96)
・DFS (10-yr analysis): Ⓐ vs Ⓑ HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.83–0.99); HR-positive HR 0.86 (0.78–0.95)
・Combination: Ⓒ 87.2% at 3 years; not different from Ⓑ (HR 1.02, 95% CI 0.89–1.18) and worse than Ⓐ (HR 0.81, 0.70–0.94); arm discontinued after first analysis
・Time to recurrence (10-yr): Ⓐ vs Ⓑ HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.75–0.93); HR-positive HR 0.79 (0.70–0.89), absolute difference 2.7% at 5 and 4.3% at 10 years
・Post-treatment recurrence: HR-positive Ⓐ vs Ⓑ HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.67–0.98); carryover benefit smaller after 8 years
・Time to distant recurrence (10-yr): Ⓐ vs Ⓑ HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.77–0.99); HR-positive HR 0.85 (0.73–0.98), absolute difference 2.6% at 10 years
・Contralateral breast cancer: First analysis OR 0.42 (95% CI 0.22–0.79); 10-yr Ⓐ vs Ⓑ HR 0.68 (0.50–0.91), HR-positive HR 0.62 (0.45–0.85)
・OS (10-yr): No difference; Ⓐ vs Ⓑ HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.88–1.08); HR-positive HR 0.95 (0.84–1.06)
・Death after recurrence: HR-positive Ⓐ vs Ⓑ HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.74–1.02); not significant
・Subgroups: First analysis HR-positive DFS HR 0.78 (0.65–0.93), receptor-negative HR 1.13 (0.79–1.61); 10-yr post-hoc: no effect in receptor-negative or unknown
・Toxicity (first analysis): Fractures Ⓐ 5.9% vs Ⓑ 3.7%; musculoskeletal disorders Ⓐ 27.8% vs Ⓑ 21.3%; endometrial cancer Ⓐ 0.1% vs Ⓑ 0.5%; venous thromboembolism Ⓐ 2.1% vs Ⓑ 3.5%
・Toxicity (10-yr): Fractures on treatment Ⓐ vs Ⓑ OR 1.33 (95% CI 1.15–1.55), similar after treatment (OR 0.98); treatment-related SAEs OR 0.57 (0.48–0.69); endometrial cancer OR 0.25 (0.08–0.63); colorectal cancer OR 1.51 (1.01–2.27)
・Limitations: Recurrence benefit smaller after about 8 years; no OS difference at 10 years; no benefit in receptor-negative disease
records.keywords: ATAC Trialists' Group. Lancet 2002;359:2131-2139  12090977 Cuzick et al. Lancet Oncol 2010;11:1135-1141  21087898

records.title: EBCTCG meta-analysis: adjuvant tamoxifen
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · Individual patient data meta-analysis of randomised trials · 2011
records.body:
Early breast cancer, adjuvant setting; women in 20 unconfounded randomised trials of about 5 years of tamoxifen versus no tamoxifen (most exactly 5 years, four of 3 years); ER-positive disease n=10 645 with ER-poor and ER-unknown also analysed; ER positivity defined as ≥10 fmol/mg cytosol protein; ductal carcinoma in situ trials excluded Ⓐ Adjuvant tamoxifen about 5 years
Ⓑ No adjuvant tamoxifen (control)
・Duration: Most trials exactly 5 years; four trials of only 3 years; some re-randomised at year 2 or year 5 to stop or continue
・Dose: 20, 30 or 40 mg per day across trials
・Chemotherapy: Present or absent; when present, concurrent or sequential
・Design: Individual patient data meta-analysis of 20 unconfounded randomised trials; about 80% compliance with tamoxifen allocation Primary: recurrence, breast cancer mortality, overall mortality, mortality without recurrence by cause, contralateral breast cancer incidence, second primary cancer incidence About 5 years of adjuvant tamoxifen reduced 15-year recurrence and breast cancer mortality in ER-positive disease, with little or no effect in ER-negative disease
・15-yr recurrence: Ⓐ 33.0% vs Ⓑ 46.2%; RR 0.61 (95% CI 0.57–0.65)
・15-yr breast cancer mortality: Ⓐ 23.9% vs Ⓑ 33.1%; RR 0.70 (95% CI 0.64–0.75)
・Recurrence RR by period: 0.53 years 0–4, 0.68 years 5–9, 0.97 years 10–14 (no further gain or loss after year 10)
・All-cause mortality: RR 0.78 (SE 0.03; p<0.00001)
・Contralateral breast cancer: 15-yr incidence Ⓐ 6.5% vs Ⓑ 9.8% (absolute reduction 3.2%)
・Subgroups: ER-poor no recurrence reduction (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.88–1.07); ER 10–19 fmol/mg still benefits (RR 0.67); RR independent of PR, age, nodal status, chemotherapy
・Toxicity: Uterine cancer incidence RR 2.40 (p=0.00002), 15-yr Ⓐ 3.8% vs Ⓑ 1.1% at entry age 55–69; six vs no pulmonary embolus deaths in years 0–4
・Limitations: About 80% compliance; a sixth allocated only 2–3 years; some controls may have started hormonal therapy
