records.title: EBCTCG meta-analysis: aromatase inhibitor vs tamoxifen in postmenopausal women
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · Individual patient data meta-analysis · 2015
records.body:
Postmenopausal women with ER-positive early breast cancer in trials of about 5 years of adjuvant endocrine therapy; eligible trials began by 2005 and randomised aromatase inhibitor versus tamoxifen schedules (five comparisons A–E); trials in premenopausal women with ovarian suppression not included ・5 years of aromatase inhibitor vs 5 years of tamoxifen (9885 women)
・5 years of aromatase inhibitor vs 2–3 years of tamoxifen then aromatase inhibitor to year 5 (12 779 women)
・2–3 years of tamoxifen then aromatase inhibitor to year 5 vs 5 years of tamoxifen (11 798 women)
・5 years of aromatase inhibitor vs 2 years of aromatase inhibitor then tamoxifen to year 5 (2558 women)
・2 years of aromatase inhibitor then tamoxifen to year 5 vs 5 years of tamoxifen (3060 women)
・Duration: About 5 years of adjuvant endocrine therapy Primary: any recurrence of breast cancer, breast cancer mortality, death without recurrence, all-cause mortality. Secondary: incidence of second primary cancers, site of second primary cancers, bone fracture Aromatase inhibitors reduced recurrence rates by about 30% versus tamoxifen while treatments differed, but not thereafter; 5 years of AI reduced 10-year breast cancer mortality by about 15%
・Recurrence, AI vs tamoxifen while treatments differed (five comparisons): RR 0.70 (95% CI 0.64–0.77); thereafter RR 0.93 (0.86–1.01; 2p=0.08)
・Breast cancer mortality, aggregated: RR 0.86 (95% CI 0.80–0.94) all periods; 0.79 (0.67–0.92) while differed, 0.89 (0.81–0.99) after
・All-cause mortality, five comparisons aggregated: RR 0.90 (95% CI 0.84–0.95)
・Comparison A (AI vs tamoxifen, 5 yr each), recurrence: RR 0.80 (0.73–0.88); 10-yr risk 19.1% vs 22.7%
・Comparison A, breast cancer mortality: 12.1% vs 14.2% at 10 yr; RR 0.85 (0.75–0.96)
・Comparison B (AI 5 yr vs tamoxifen 2–3 yr then AI): Recurrence RR 0.90 (0.81–0.99), benefit only years 0–1 (RR 0.74, 0.62–0.89); breast cancer mortality not significant (RR 0.89, 0.78–1.03)
・Comparison C (tamoxifen 2–3 yr then AI vs tamoxifen 5 yr): Recurrence RR 0.56 (0.46–0.67) years 2–4; 10-yr breast cancer mortality 8.7% vs 10.1% (2p=0.015)
・Comparison D (AI 5 yr vs AI 2 yr then tamoxifen; 2558 women): No apparent gain from continuing AI, CIs wide
・Comparison E (AI 2 yr then tamoxifen vs tamoxifen 5 yr; 3060 women): Early recurrence reduction similar to other comparisons; appendix
・Subgroups: RRs differed little by age, BMI, stage, grade, PR, HER2; absolute 5-yr recurrence reduction rose with nodes (N0 1.2%, N1–3 3.7%, N4+ 6.4%)
・Toxicity: Fewer endometrial cancers with AI (10-yr 0.4% vs 1.2%; RR 0.33, 0.21–0.51); more fractures (5-yr 8.2% vs 5.5%; RR 1.42, 1.28–1.57); non-breast-cancer mortality similar
・Limitations: ITT ignores crossover and dropout, understating AI benefit; little follow-up beyond year 10; comparisons D and E from one trial with few events

records.title: TEXT & SOFT
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III), preplanned combined analysis of two trials · 2014
records.body:
Premenopausal women with hormone-receptor–positive (ER or PR in at least 10% of cells) operable early breast cancer confined to the breast and ipsilateral axilla; adjuvant setting after total mastectomy with optional radiotherapy or breast-conserving surgery with radiotherapy; adjuvant chemotherapy optional, trastuzumab allowed; bisphosphonates not permitted unless T score −1.5 or lower Ⓐ Exemestane 25 mg orally daily plus ovarian suppression
Ⓑ Tamoxifen 20 mg orally daily plus ovarian suppression
・Ovarian suppression: Triptorelin 3.75 mg intramuscularly every 28 days, or bilateral oophorectomy or ovarian irradiation
・Duration: Protocol-assigned endocrine therapy for 5 years from randomization
・Chemotherapy: Optional; concurrent with triptorelin in TEXT, before randomization in SOFT
・Design: Open-label Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: freedom from breast cancer, freedom from distant recurrence, overall survival, safety, quality of life At final 16-year follow-up exemestane plus OFS sustained DFS, BCFI and distant-recurrence reductions over tamoxifen plus OFS; ITT overall survival did not improve, meaningful benefit limited to HER2-negative high-risk subgroups
・15-yr DFS, final: Ⓐ 74.9% vs Ⓑ 71.3%; HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.73–0.92)
・15-yr BCFI, final: HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.70–0.90)
・15-yr DRFI, final: Ⓐ 86.5% vs Ⓑ 83.9%; HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.71–0.97)
・15-yr OS, final: Ⓐ 87.8% vs Ⓑ 87.0%; HR 0.94 (95% CI 0.80–1.11)
・SOFT, OFS vs tamoxifen alone: 15-yr BCFI 78.6% (E+OFS) and 75.7% (T+OFS) vs 72.1% (T); T+OFS vs T HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.69–0.98)
・Subgroups, HER2-negative (n=4035): DRFI Ⓐ 87.6% vs Ⓑ 83.7%, HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.63–0.90); OS 88.5% vs 86.9%, HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.74–1.06); chemo-cohort absolute OS gain 3.9% SOFT, 2.5% TEXT
・Subgroups, high-risk HER2-negative: Grade 3 absolute 15-yr gains 12.1% BCFI, 9.7% DRFI, 5.8% OS; under 40 gains ∼7.5% DRFI, ∼3.7% OS
・Subgroups: No significant heterogeneity by trial or chemotherapy use; treatment-effect heterogeneity between HER2-negative and HER2-positive subgroups
・QoL: Overall quality of life did not favor either treatment; exemestane more bone/joint pain and vaginal dryness, tamoxifen more hot flushes
・Toxicity: G3/4 targeted AEs 30.6% vs 29.4%; osteoporosis (T score <−2.5) 13.2% vs 6.4%; early treatment cessation 16.1% vs 11.2%; no grade 5 events; deaths without breast/second cancer rare, not higher with Ⓐ (13-yr MFU)
・Late events, SOFT yrs 6–15: Fractures Ⓐ 6.8% vs Ⓑ 6.6% vs tamoxifen-alone 4.2%; late cardiovascular/cerebrovascular Ⓐ 2.6% vs Ⓑ 2.7% vs tamoxifen-alone 1.8%; no excess deaths without breast cancer event with OFS
・Limitations: Open-label; ITT OS not improved at final analysis, survival benefit confined to HER2-negative subgroups (HRs and CIs only); combined analysis designated primary by 2011 amendment

records.title: SOFT
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2015
records.body:
Premenopausal women with operable, hormone-receptor–positive early breast cancer (estrogen or progesterone receptor in at least 10% of cells) after definitive surgery with axillary staging; adjuvant endocrine therapy; women remaining premenopausal after (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy (confirmed estradiol) or suitable for tamoxifen alone Ⓐ Tamoxifen 20 mg orally daily
Ⓑ Tamoxifen 20 mg orally daily plus ovarian suppression
Ⓒ Exemestane 25 mg orally daily plus ovarian suppression
・Ovarian suppression: Triptorelin 3.75 mg IM every 28 days, bilateral oophorectomy, or bilateral ovarian irradiation
・Duration: 5 years from randomization Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: interval without breast cancer, interval to recurrence of breast cancer at a distant site, overall survival, safety At 12 years, adding OFS to adjuvant tamoxifen still improved DFS, exemestane plus OFS further reduced recurrence, and absolute OS gains were largest in higher-risk disease
・DFS: 12-yr Ⓐ 71.9% vs Ⓑ 76.1% vs Ⓒ 79.0%; HR Ⓑ 0.82 (95% CI 0.69–0.98), Ⓒ 0.69 (95% CI 0.57–0.83) vs Ⓐ
・OS: 12-yr Ⓐ 86.8% vs Ⓑ 89.0% vs Ⓒ 89.4%; HR Ⓑ 0.78 (95% CI 0.60–1.01), Ⓒ 0.80 (0.62–1.04); Ⓒ benefit emerged after 5 yr
・DRFI: 12-yr Ⓐ 84.8% vs Ⓑ 86.2% vs Ⓒ 87.8%; HR Ⓑ 0.90 (0.71–1.14), Ⓒ 0.75 (0.59–0.97) vs Ⓐ
・Freedom from breast cancer: 5-yr Ⓐ 86.4% vs Ⓑ 88.4%; HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.63–1.03)
・Combined SOFT+TEXT, Ⓒ vs Ⓑ: 8-yr DFS 86.8% vs 82.8%, HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.67–0.90); OS HR 0.98 (95% CI 0.79–1.22)
・Prior-chemo cohort: 8-yr DFS Ⓐ 71.4%, Ⓑ 76.7%, Ⓒ 80.4%; OS Ⓐ 85.1% vs Ⓑ 89.4%, HR 0.59 (95% CI 0.42–0.84), Ⓒ 87.2%
・Prior-chemo cohort, 12-yr: DRFI Ⓐ 75.1% vs Ⓑ 77.7% vs Ⓒ 79.6%; HER2-negative OS Ⓐ 78.8% vs Ⓑ 81.1% vs Ⓒ 84.4%
・No-chemo cohort: 12-yr OS exceeded 95% in all arms; DRFI Ⓐ 95.8% vs Ⓑ 95.9% vs Ⓒ 97.7%
・HER2-negative tumors: 12-yr OS Ⓐ 87.7% vs Ⓑ 88.8% vs Ⓒ 90.9%
・Grade 3 tumors: 12-yr OS Ⓐ 76.4% vs Ⓑ 80.8% vs Ⓒ 84.0%
・HER2 interaction: Ⓑ vs Ⓐ benefit larger in HER2-positive (HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.22–0.75) than HER2-negative (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.67–1.04; P=0.04); persisted at 12 yr
・<35 yr: 8-yr freedom from distant recurrence Ⓐ 73.8%, Ⓑ 77.5%, Ⓒ 82.4%; 12-yr BCFI Ⓐ 57.0% vs Ⓑ 71.6%
・Toxicity: G≥3 targeted AEs Ⓐ 24.6% vs Ⓑ 31.0% vs Ⓒ 32.3% (Ⓑ/Ⓒ pooled SOFT/TEXT); osteoporosis (T score <−2.5) Ⓒ 14.8% vs Ⓑ 7.2% vs Ⓐ 3.9%; one G5 cardiac ischemia (Ⓐ); no excess noncancer deaths with OFS evident
・Limitations: No updated adverse-event data in this 12-yr report; only 60.2% (221/367) of HER2-positive patients received HER2-targeted therapy; small absolute benefit without chemotherapy

records.title: lidERA (BC)
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
ER-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer (stage I–III); adjuvant endocrine therapy after breast cancer surgery and (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy if indicated; this report presents results by menopausal status (40.7% premenopausal, 59.3% postmenopausal) Ⓐ Giredestrant 30 mg orally once daily
Ⓑ SOC endocrine therapy: anastrozole, letrozole or exemestane (aromatase inhibitors), or tamoxifen
・Duration: 5 years of treatment
・LHRH agonist: Added for premenopausal patients on Ⓐ giredestrant and on aromatase inhibitors Primary: invasive disease-free survival, distant recurrence-free interval, safety Adjuvant giredestrant improved IDFS and DRFI vs SOC endocrine therapy, with benefit consistent irrespective of menopausal status
・IDFS: 3-yr Ⓐ 94.0 vs Ⓑ 91.5% (premenopausal; HR 0.65) and Ⓐ 91.3 vs Ⓑ 88.3% (postmenopausal; HR 0.74)
・DRFI: 3-yr Ⓐ 95.5 vs Ⓑ 92.6% (premenopausal; HR 0.58) and Ⓐ 93.6 vs Ⓑ 91.6% (postmenopausal; HR 0.76)
・Toxicity: G3–4 AEs Ⓐ 18.2 vs Ⓑ 17.3% (premenopausal) and Ⓐ 20.7 vs Ⓑ 18.4% (postmenopausal); AE discontinuation Ⓐ 4.9–5.7% vs AI 7.5–8.2%; musculoskeletal-pain discontinuation 1.6% Ⓐ vs 4.5% AI
・Limitations: Menopausal-status subgroup report; unstratified HRs; congress abstract without full endpoint hierarchy or ITT analyses

records.title: POSITIVE
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · Single-arm clinical trial with external control cohort comparison · 2023
records.body:
Women ≤42 years with stage I–III hormone receptor–positive (≥1% cutoff) early breast cancer who had received adjuvant endocrine therapy for 18–30 months, wished to temporarily discontinue it to attempt pregnancy, and had no clinical evidence of recurrence; previous chemotherapy allowed (single-arm) Temporary interruption of adjuvant endocrine therapy to attempt pregnancy
・Washout: 3 months off endocrine therapy before attempting pregnancy
・Duration: Interruption of up to 2 years for attempting pregnancy, delivery and breast-feeding
・After: Resumption of endocrine therapy to complete planned 5 to 10 years strongly recommended Primary: number of breast cancer events during follow-up. Secondary: freedom from a breast cancer event, freedom from distant recurrence, ability to become pregnant, pregnancy outcomes, birth outcomes, breast-feeding, use of assisted reproductive technology, resumption of endocrine therapy Temporary interruption of endocrine therapy to attempt pregnancy did not confer greater short-term breast cancer event risk than the external control cohort
・Breast cancer events: 44 events in 1638 patient-years, within prespecified safety threshold of 46; median follow-up 41 mo
・3-yr BC events: 8.9% (95% CI 6.3–11.6) vs 9.2% (95% CI 7.6–10.8) external control; HR 0.81 (0.57–1.15)
・3-yr distant recurrence: 4.5% (95% CI 2.7–6.4) vs 5.8% (95% CI 4.5–7.2) external control; HR 0.70 (0.44–1.12)
・Pregnancy: 74.0% of 497 followed had ≥1 pregnancy; ≥1 live birth 63.8%; assisted reproductive technology 43.3%
・Resumption: 73.3% of 415 disease-free ≥2 yr resumed endocrine therapy; 15.4% not resumed by 48 mo
・Toxicity: Pregnancy complications 11.1% of 368; low birth weight 7.9%; birth defects 2.2%
・Limitations: Median follow-up 3.4 yr only; single-arm with external control, possible healthy-mother bias; population not broadly representative

records.title: EBCTCG meta-analysis: aromatase inhibitors vs tamoxifen with ovarian suppression in early breast cancer
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · Individual patient data meta-analysis · 2022
records.body:
Premenopausal women with ER-positive operable breast cancer; adjuvant endocrine therapy for 3 or 5 years plus ovarian function suppression (goserelin or triptorelin) or ablation; ER positivity at least 1% of tumour cells by immunohistochemistry (Reiner score ≥3 in ABCSG XII); ER-negative PR-positive tumours excluded Ⓐ Aromatase inhibitor plus ovarian function suppression or ablation (triptorelin in SOFT, TEXT, HOBOE; goserelin in ABCSG XII; oophorectomy or ovarian irradiation allowed in SOFT and TEXT)
Ⓑ Tamoxifen plus ovarian function suppression
・AI agent: Anastrozole in ABCSG XII, exemestane in SOFT and TEXT, letrozole in HOBOE
・Duration: 5 years in SOFT, TEXT and HOBOE; 3 years in ABCSG XII with or without zoledronic acid Primary: any recurrence of invasive breast cancer, breast cancer mortality, death without recurrence, all-cause mortality. Secondary: second primary cancers (incidence and site, including endometrial cancer), bone fracture Aromatase inhibitor rather than tamoxifen with ovarian suppression reduced breast cancer recurrence in premenopausal ER-positive early breast cancer; longer follow-up needed for mortality
・Any recurrence: Ⓐ RR 0·79 (95% CI 0·69–0·90; p=0·0005); 5-year risk Ⓐ 6·9% vs Ⓑ 10·1%, absolute reduction 3·2% (95% CI 1·8–4·5)
・Time course: Benefit in years 0–4 (RR 0·68, 99% CI 0·55–0·85); no further benefit or loss in years 5–9 (RR 0·98, 99% CI 0·73–1·33)
・Distant recurrence: RR 0·83 (95% CI 0·71–0·97; p=0·018)
・Mortality: Breast cancer RR 1·01 (95% CI 0·82–1·24); all-cause RR 1·04 (0·86–1·27); death without recurrence RR 1·30 (0·75–2·25)
・Subgroups: No apparent benefit in N4+ disease (RR 1·03, 95% CI 0·79–1·34); HER2 interaction weak (p=0·021), below prespecified subgroup threshold
・Toxicity: Bone fractures Ⓐ 6·4% vs Ⓑ 5·1% (RR 1·27, 95% CI 1·04–1·54); endometrial cancer Ⓐ 0·2% vs Ⓑ 0·3% (RR 0·52, 0·22–1·23)
・Limitations: Median follow-up 8·0 years, breast cancer mortality immature; individual-trial results inconsistent (ABCSG XII); quality-of-life data unavailable

records.title: ABCSG-16 / SALSA
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body:
Postmenopausal women aged 80 years or younger with histologically verified invasive hormone-receptor–positive breast cancer at an early stage (stage I, II, or III) without evidence of recurrence; all had completed 5 years (±12 months) of adjuvant endocrine therapy with tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitors, or both sequentially up until 12 months before randomization Ⓐ Extended anastrozole for 2 additional years (total 7 years of endocrine therapy)
Ⓑ Extended anastrozole for 5 additional years (total 10 years of endocrine therapy)
・Anastrozole: 1 mg orally daily Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, contralateral breast cancer, second primary cancer, clinical bone fracture, serious adverse events Five additional years of anastrozole did not improve disease-free survival over two additional years and increased clinical bone fracture risk
・DFS: Ⓐ 73.6% vs Ⓑ 73.9% at 8 yr (10 yr since randomization); HR 0.99 (95% CI 0.85–1.15)
・OS: Ⓐ 87.5% vs Ⓑ 87.3% at 8 yr; HR 1.02 (95% CI 0.83–1.25)
・Contralateral BC: HR 1.15 (95% CI 0.75–1.77); second primary cancer HR 1.06 (95% CI 0.81–1.38)
・Fracture: Ⓐ 4.7% vs Ⓑ 6.3% at 5 yr; HR 1.35 (95% CI 1.00–1.84); NNH 63
・Toxicity: Any SAE Ⓐ 26.5% vs Ⓑ 40.2%; anastrozole-related SAE 2.3% vs 4.0%; osteoarthritis 1.7% vs 4.3%
・Limitations: Analysis starts 2 yr after randomization; average-risk population; adherence fell to approximately 33% by 5 yr

records.title: EBCTCG meta-analysis: ovarian function suppression (OFS) in early breast cancer
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · Individual patient data meta-analysis · 2026
records.body:
Premenopausal women with ER-positive or ER-unknown early breast cancer, younger than 55 years at randomisation; adjuvant OFS vs no OFS trials recruited 1948–2014 with other treatments the same in both arms; trials ineligible if additional systemic therapy (other than prednisone) in only one arm or only non-oncological outcomes; women aged 55 or older, postmenopausal or ER-negative excluded ・OFS vs no OFS (confirmed premenopausal, no tamoxifen; 2593 women)
・OFS plus tamoxifen vs tamoxifen (confirmed premenopausal; 4849 women)
・OFS vs no OFS (premenopausal status unconfirmed after chemotherapy; 7633 women)
・OFS: Ovarian ablation (oophorectomy or ovarian irradiation) or GnRHa; GnRHa mostly 2–5 years
・Tamoxifen: 2–5 years, mean about 4 years where given
・Chemotherapy: Same in both arms when given, mostly cyclophosphamide, methotrexate and fluorouracil
・Design: Unconfounded randomised trials with other treatments the same in both arms Primary: invasive breast cancer recurrence, breast cancer mortality, other mortality, all-cause mortality. Secondary: distant recurrence, locoregional recurrence, contralateral recurrence, death without recurrence, second primary cancers, safety Ovarian function suppression reduced 15-year recurrence and death in premenopausal ER-positive early breast cancer, even when chemotherapy or tamoxifen given
・Recurrence, OFS vs no OFS (all trials): RR 0.82 (95% CI 0.77–0.87); 15-yr risk 36.5% vs 41.9%
・Breast cancer mortality, all trials: RR 0.86 (0.80–0.93); 15-yr risk 31.3% vs 34.4%
・Confirmed premenopausal, no tamoxifen: Recurrence RR 0.61 (0.52–0.71), 15-yr 39.1% vs 56.5%; breast cancer mortality RR 0.65 (0.56–0.76)
・Confirmed premenopausal, OFS plus tamoxifen vs tamoxifen: Recurrence RR 0.79 (0.70–0.91), 15-yr 24.8% vs 30.7%; breast cancer mortality RR 0.84 (0.69–1.02), p=0.080
・Unconfirmed premenopausal: Recurrence RR 0.91 (0.84–1.00); breast cancer mortality RR 0.96 (0.88–1.05), little apparent effect
・Other mortality: Non-breast cancer death RR 1.10 (0.86–1.41); no increase in deaths without recurrence
・Heterogeneity: Recurrence reduction differed by menopausal-status confirmation (p=0.0004) and by tamoxifen among confirmed (p=0.0080)
・Subgroups: With tamoxifen, larger recurrence reduction under 45 years, RR 0.73 (0.63–0.86) vs 0.95 (0.75–1.21) at 45–54; interaction p=0.072
・Aged under 45 years, OFS plus tamoxifen: Distant recurrence RR 0.77 (0.64–0.93); breast cancer mortality RR 0.74 (0.58–0.94); all-cause mortality RR 0.72 (0.57–0.90), 10-yr 9.4% vs 12.2%
・Toxicity: Patient-level toxicity not sought; more higher-grade hot flushes with OFS; two trials more glucose intolerance and grade 3 hypertension
・Limitations: Many trials before the 1980s with less sensitive recurrence ascertainment and incomplete ER status; menopausal status unconfirmed after chemotherapy in 13 trials; QOL from only four trials

records.title: FATA-GIM3
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body:
Postmenopausal women (if <60 years: amenorrhoea >1 year or postmenopausal FSH) with completely resected invasive ER- or PR-positive early breast cancer (≥10% of cells on immunohistochemistry or ≥10 fmol/mg), any tumour size and nodal status, any HER2 status (HER2-positive required trastuzumab); excluded hormone-replacement therapy, recurrent or metastatic disease, previous tamoxifen, other malignancy in previous 10 years Ⓐ Upfront strategy: assigned aromatase inhibitor orally once daily for 5 years
Ⓑ Switch strategy: tamoxifen 20 mg orally once daily for 2 years, then assigned aromatase inhibitor orally once daily for 3 years
・Aromatase inhibitor options: Anastrozole 1 mg, exemestane 25 mg or letrozole 2·5 mg once daily
・Duration: 5 years of endocrine treatment in both strategies
・Design: Open-label 2×3 factorial (schedule × aromatase inhibitor) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, toxicity, invasive-disease-free survival, distant-disease-free survival, distant-recurrence-free survival, relapse-free survival, recurrence-free interval, breast-cancer-free interval, distant-recurrence-free interval, lipid profile Upfront 5-year aromatase inhibitor did not improve disease-free survival over 2 years of tamoxifen then 3 years of an aromatase inhibitor; the three inhibitors did not differ
・5-yr DFS: Ⓐ 89·8% vs Ⓑ 88·5%; HR 0·89 (95% CI 0·73–1·08); p=0·23
・5-yr OS: Ⓐ 96·8% vs Ⓑ 95·3%; HR 0·72 (95% CI 0·51–1·00); p=0·052
・5-yr DFS, AI comparison: Anastrozole 90·0%, exemestane 88·0%, letrozole 89·4%; p=0·24
・Toxicity: G3–4 musculoskeletal Ⓐ 7% vs Ⓑ 7%; grade 1 musculoskeletal more with Ⓐ (52% vs 42%); no treatment-related deaths
・Limitations: Underpowered schedule comparison (power 0·59); open-label; too few deaths for conclusions beyond DFS

records.title: FACE
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase IIIb) · 2017
records.body:
Postmenopausal women with HR-positive, node-positive early breast cancer (stage IIA to IIIC invasive); adjuvant, within 12 weeks after breast surgery or completion of adjuvant chemotherapy; neoadjuvant chemotherapy or trastuzumab allowed; excluded metastatic or inflammatory, contralateral or metachronous bilateral breast cancer, prior neoadjuvant endocrine therapy or adjuvant antiestrogen >1 month after surgery, Child-Pugh C cirrhosis Ⓐ Letrozole 2.5 mg once per day
Ⓑ Anastrozole 1 mg once per day
・Duration: Until disease recurrence/relapse or for a maximum of 5 years
・Design: Open-label Primary: 5-year disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, time to development of distant metastases, distant disease-free survival, safety Adjuvant letrozole did not demonstrate significantly superior efficacy or safety versus anastrozole in postmenopausal, HR-positive, node-positive early breast cancer
・5-yr DFS: Ⓐ 84.9% vs Ⓑ 82.9%; HR 0.93 (95% CI 0.80 to 1.07; P = .3150); final analysis, 709 events
・5-yr OS: Ⓐ 89.9% vs Ⓑ 89.2%; HR 0.98 (95% CI 0.82 to 1.17)
・TDM: HR 0.99 (95% CI 0.82 to 1.19)
・DDFS: HR 0.96 (95% CI 0.82 to 1.12)
・Subgroups: Exploratory; nonsignificant letrozole trend with ≥4 nodes (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.69 to 1.06); obese no advantage (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.54 to 1.37)
・Toxicity: G3/4 AEs Ⓐ 30.6% vs Ⓑ 28.7%; arthralgia Ⓐ 3.9% vs Ⓑ 3.3%; on-treatment deaths Ⓐ 2.0% vs Ⓑ 2.2%
・Limitations: Open-label; terminated early at 709 of 959 planned DFS events; median follow-up 65 months

records.title: ELPh (Exemestane and Letrozole Pharmacogenetics) trial
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · Randomised, open-label clinical trial · 2012
records.body:
Postmenopausal women with stage 0 to III hormone receptor-positive breast cancer initiating adjuvant AI therapy; prior tamoxifen permitted but no prior AI; all indicated surgery, chemotherapy and radiotherapy completed before enrollment Ⓐ Exemestane 25 mg daily
Ⓑ Letrozole 2.5 mg daily
・Duration: 2 years Primary: persistence with the second AI medication after discontinuation of the initial AI because of toxicity. Secondary: time to treatment discontinuation because of any treatment-emergent symptom, time to treatment discontinuation because of musculoskeletal symptoms, predictors of treatment discontinuation, change in HAQ and pain VAS scores Exemestane was associated with shorter time to symptom-driven AI discontinuation than letrozole; more than one third of switchers tolerated the alternate AI
・2nd AI persistence: 38.6% of 83 switchers continued (median 13.7 mo); 61.4% stopped second AI, median 3.5 mo
・Discontinuation, any symptom: Overall 32.6%; Ⓐ 36.7% vs Ⓑ 28.6%; P = .02
・Time to discontinuation: Ⓐ 5.8 vs Ⓑ 8.1 mo; HR 1.5 (95% CI 1.1 to 2.1)
・MSK time to discontinuation: HR 1.4 (95% CI 0.95 to 2.0); log-rank P = .08, trend only
・Predictors (multivariate): Exemestane HR 1.4 (1.02 to 1.9); age <55 years HR 1.4 (1.0 to 1.9); taxane HR 1.9 (0.99 to 3.6); baseline pain HR 1.1 (1.00 to 1.2)
・Toxicity: Musculoskeletal symptoms caused 24.4% of discontinuations overall; same symptoms recurred on second AI in seventy-eight percent
・Limitations: Exploratory ELPh objective; optional crossover may select motivated patients; exemestane–letrozole difference requires replication

records.title: EBCTCG meta-analysis: extended adjuvant aromatase inhibitor therapy
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy - duration · Individual patient data meta-analysis · 2025
records.body:
Postmenopausal women with ER-positive early breast cancer, recurrence-free after completing at least 5 years of endocrine therapy (tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitor treatment [AIT], or tamoxifen then AIT); randomly assigned to further AIT vs no further adjuvant treatment; ER-negative and unknown-ER tumours excluded ・Further AIT vs no further adjuvant treatment (22 031 women, 12 trials)
・2–3 further years of AIT vs no further AIT, some previous AIT (6893 women)
・5 further years of AIT vs no further AIT, some previous AIT (7511 women)
・5 further years vs no further AIT after 5 years previous AIT, 10 vs 5 years total (5710 women)
・Agents: Letrozole six trials, anastrozole four, exemestane two
・Design: Patient-level meta-analysis, intention-to-treat; four trials placebo-controlled, eight open control Primary: Recurrence of invasive breast cancer (local, distant, or new contralateral), Breast cancer mortality, Mortality from other causes, All-cause mortality. Secondary: Time to first distant recurrence, Bone fractures, Cardiovascular deaths, Site-specific second primary cancers Allocation to further AIT reduced recurrence rates by about a quarter overall, and 5 further years reduced distant recurrence by about a quarter despite substantial non-adherence
・Recurrence, further AIT vs none (22 031 women, 12 trials): RR 0.73 (95% CI 0.67–0.80), p<0.0001
・Recurrence, 5 further vs none after some previous AIT (7511 women): Risk year 5 to year 15 11.6% vs 15.2%; RR 0.71 (95% CI 0.61–0.81), p<0.0001
・Distant recurrence, 5 further vs none: 6.6% vs 8.6%; RR 0.73 (95% CI 0.61–0.88), p=0.0010
・Breast cancer mortality, 5 further vs none: 4.4% vs 5.0%; RR 0.90 (95% CI 0.70–1.15), p=0.40
・All-cause mortality, 5 further vs none: RR 0.99 (95% CI 0.86–1.14), p=0.89
・Recurrence, 2–3 further vs none (6893 women): RR 0.87 (95% CI 0.76–0.99), p=0.040; distant recurrence RR 0.91 (95% CI 0.77–1.07), p=0.23
・10 vs 5 years total AIT (5710 women): Recurrence 12.2% vs 15.4%, RR 0.74 (0.63–0.88); distant recurrence 6.9% vs 8.8%, RR 0.75 (0.60–0.93); breast cancer mortality 4.3% vs 4.7%
・Subgroups: Proportional reductions unaffected by tumour characteristics; absolute recurrence reduction larger node-positive (16.3% vs 20.1%) than node-negative (9.1% vs 11.8%)
・Toxicity: 5-year fracture risk 4.6% vs 3.4%; RR 1.35 (95% CI 1.13–1.61), p=0.0009; endometrial cancer 0.3% vs 0.5%; no cardiovascular mortality excess (68 vs 70 deaths)
・Limitations: Widespread non-adherence (39.0% further AIT vs 37.6% placebo); 5-year trials under-powered for mortality; placebo crossover after tamoxifen-only limited long-term evidence

records.title: NSABP B-33
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy - duration · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2008
records.body:
Postmenopausal women with ER and/or PgR-positive invasive breast cancer, clinical stage T1-3 N0-1 M0, disease-free after 57 to 66 months of adjuvant tamoxifen; randomization less than 180 days after tamoxifen completion; prior adjuvant or neoadjuvant chemotherapy allowed; postlumpectomy breast radiotherapy required Ⓐ Exemestane 25 mg orally daily
Ⓑ Placebo orally daily
・Duration: 5 years (amended from planned 2 years before any patient completed therapy)
・Design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, relapse-free survival, bone mineral density, blood lipid profile, quality of life Despite premature closure and placebo-group crossover, exemestane significantly improved 4-year RFS but only non-significantly improved DFS
・DFS: Ⓐ 91% vs Ⓑ 89% at 4 years; RR 0.68, P = .07; 32% event reduction (ITT, 30-mo median follow-up)
・RFS: Ⓐ 96% vs Ⓑ 94% at 4 years; RR 0.44, P = .004; 56% reduction in breast cancer recurrence
・OS: Not significantly different; too few deaths for definitive conclusions
・Distant recurrence: 31% non-significant reduction, P = .13 (not a prespecified end point)
・QoL: No significant exemestane effect on MENQOL vasomotor, psychosocial, physical or sexual scales; scores numerically higher
・Subgroups (exploratory DFS): Node-positive HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.30–0.86); tumor >2 cm HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.24–0.98); age <60 HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.27–1.03)
・Toxicity: G3 Ⓐ 9% vs Ⓑ 6% (P = .03); G4 1% each; no treatment-related deaths; fractures Ⓐ 28 vs Ⓑ 20 (P = .33)
・Limitations: Accrual stopped at 1,598 of planned 3,000; 44% placebo crossover to exemestane; toxicity assessed only to unblinding

records.title: MA.17 (NCIC CTG)
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy - duration · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2003
records.body:
Postmenopausal women with histologically confirmed primary breast cancer after 4.5–6 years of adjuvant tamoxifen, stopped <3 months before enrollment; ER- or PR-positive tumors (10 fmol/mg protein or positive immunohistochemistry/immunocytochemistry); excluded prior other cancer except skin or cervical carcinoma in situ, and concomitant hormone-replacement therapy or SERM Ⓐ Letrozole 2.5 mg orally daily
Ⓑ Placebo orally daily
・Duration: Planned five years; trial terminated early after first interim analysis
・Stopping: Serious intercurrent illness, unacceptable toxic effects, recurrence, or patient request
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, quality of life, long-term safety Letrozole after completion of standard tamoxifen significantly improved disease-free survival versus placebo in postmenopausal early breast cancer
・4-yr DFS: Ⓐ 93% vs Ⓑ 87%; HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.43–0.75); first interim analysis, median follow-up 2.4 yr
・4-yr OS: Ⓐ 96% vs Ⓑ 94%; HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.48–1.21)

records.title: ATLAS
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy - duration · Randomised clinical trial · 2013
records.body:
Early breast cancer after ~5 years of adjuvant tamoxifen (median 5.0 years, IQR 4.8–5.2), clinically free of disease at entry; main recurrence and breast cancer mortality analyses restricted to ER-positive disease (6846 of 12 894); no restrictions on age, histology, nodal status or other treatments; contraindications to tamoxifen continuation precluded entry Ⓐ Continue tamoxifen (Nolvadex) 20 mg per day for another 5 years, to 10 years total
Ⓑ Stop tamoxifen at 5 years
・Design: Open control, no placebo; other management at clinician discretion
・Prior therapy: Adjuvant tamoxifen ~5 years (median 5.0, IQR 4.8–5.2) Primary: recurrence, breast cancer mortality, overall mortality. Secondary: mortality without recurrence, endometrial cancer, pulmonary embolus, stroke, ischaemic heart disease Continuing tamoxifen to 10 years reduced recurrence, breast cancer mortality and overall mortality versus stopping at 5 years in ER-positive disease, particularly after year 10
・Recurrence, yrs 5–14: Ⓐ 21.4% vs Ⓑ 25.1%; RR 0.84 (95% CI 0.76–0.94), p=0.002; ≥10 yrs RR 0.75 (0.62–0.90)
・Breast cancer mortality, yrs 5–14: Ⓐ 12.2% vs Ⓑ 15.0% (absolute reduction 2.8%); ≥10 yrs RR 0.71 (0.58–0.88)
・Overall mortality: Ⓐ 639 vs Ⓑ 722 deaths; RR 0.87 (95% CI 0.78–0.97), p=0.01
・Overall mortality, all women (protocol-defined): RR 0.93 (95% CI 0.86–1.00), p=0.04
・Mortality without recurrence: RR 0.99 (95% CI 0.89–1.10), p=0.78, all 12 894 women
・Subgroups (ER): No effect in ER-negative disease (1248 women); intermediate effect in ER-unknown (4800)
・Toxicity: Endometrial cancer yrs 5–14 Ⓐ 3.1% vs Ⓑ 1.6%, RR 1.74 (1.30–2.34); pulmonary embolus RR 1.87 (1.13–3.07); ischaemic heart disease RR 0.75 (0.60–0.95)
・Limitations: Open-label, no placebo; ER status unknown in 37%; ER-positive emphasis proposed by statistician knowing results

records.title: MA.17R
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy - duration · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body:
Postmenopausal women with hormone-receptor–positive primary breast cancer, disease-free after 4.5 to 6 years of adjuvant aromatase-inhibitor therapy (preceded in most by tamoxifen) and randomized within 2 years of completing it; ECOG performance status <3; unknown receptor status allowed only for prior MA.17 participants; minimum life expectancy of at least 5 years Ⓐ Letrozole 2.5 mg orally once daily
Ⓑ Placebo orally once daily
・Duration: Another 5 years; stopped for serious intercurrent illness, unacceptable toxic effects, disease recurrence, or patient request
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, incidence of contralateral breast cancer, quality of life, long-term safety Extending adjuvant aromatase-inhibitor therapy to 10 years improved disease-free survival and reduced contralateral breast cancer vs placebo, without an overall-survival benefit
・5-yr DFS: Ⓐ 95% vs Ⓑ 91%; HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.48–0.91)
・5-yr OS: Ⓐ 93% vs Ⓑ 94%; HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.73–1.28)
・Contralateral BC: Ⓐ 0.21% vs Ⓑ 0.49% annual incidence; HR 0.42 (95% CI 0.22–0.81)
・Post hoc DFS incl. all deaths: Ⓐ 90% vs Ⓑ 88% at 5 yr; HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.63–1.01)
・Subgroups: Letrozole superior across all prespecified subgroups; no significant interactions
・QoL: No significant differences on most SF-36/MENQOL subscales; role–physical worse with letrozole (3.2 points, below MCID of 5)
・Toxicity: Fractures Ⓐ 14% vs Ⓑ 9%; new-onset osteoporosis Ⓐ 11% vs Ⓑ 6%; bone pain Ⓐ 18% vs Ⓑ 14%; discontinuation for toxic effects 5.4% vs 3.7%
・Limitations: Primary analysis amended to time-based before target events; adherence Ⓐ 62.5% vs Ⓑ 62.3% by self-report; no multiplicity adjustment

Postmenopausal women with early-stage hormone receptor–positive breast cancer (ER and/or PR positive in ≥10% of nuclei) who had completed five years of any adjuvant endocrine therapy; no evidence of recurrence at random assignment; initial endocrine therapy completed no longer than two years before randomization; WHO performance status 0 or 1 Ⓐ Letrozole 2.5 mg daily for 2.5 years

・Design: Open-label; multicentre (73 hospitals in the Netherlands) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, distant metastasis–free interval, new primary breast malignancies, safety Extending letrozole to five years was not superior to 2.5 years for disease-free survival after five years of any adjuvant endocrine therapy; only second primary breast cancers were reduced

・DMFi: HR 1.06 (95% CI 0.78 to 1.45), Ⓑ vs Ⓐ

records.title: NRG Oncology/NSABP B-42
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy - duration · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body:
Postmenopausal women with ER- or PR-positive invasive ductal carcinoma, stage I–IIIA, disease-free after about 5 years of endocrine therapy (aromatase inhibitor, or tamoxifen ≤3 years then aromatase inhibitor); randomised within 6 months of completing 57–63 months of therapy and total cholesterol CTCAE grade ≤1; excluded history of non-traumatic osteoporotic fracture, bilateral breast cancer, other malignancies unless disease-free ≥5 years, sex hormone or hormonal osteoporosis therapy Ⓐ Letrozole 2·5 mg orally once daily
Ⓑ Placebo orally once daily
・Duration: 5 years from first dose, beginning within 30 days after randomisation
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled; study drug suspended for grade 3–4 high cholesterol until grade ≤1 Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, breast-cancer-free interval, distant recurrence, incidence of osteoporotic fractures, incidence of arterial thrombotic events, adverse events, recurrence-free interval At 10 years, extended letrozole significantly improved disease-free survival, breast cancer-free interval and distant recurrence without improving overall survival
・DFS: 10-yr Ⓐ 75.9% vs Ⓑ 72.6%; HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.74–0.96); absolute benefit 3.3%
・OS: 10-yr Ⓐ 86.1% vs Ⓑ 86.2%; HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.82–1.15); no difference
・BCFI: 10-yr cumulative incidence Ⓐ 10.5% vs Ⓑ 13.2%; HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.62–0.91)
・Distant recurrence: 10-yr Ⓐ 5.6% vs Ⓑ 7.4%; HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.55–0.92); benefit only between 4.0 and 7.4 yr
・RFI: 10-yr cumulative incidence Ⓐ 7.8% vs Ⓑ 9.3%; HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.64–0.99); post hoc, not prespecified
・Osteoporotic fractures: 10-yr Ⓐ 6.6% vs Ⓑ 6.1%; HR 1.12 (95% CI 0.86–1.45)
・Arterial thrombotic events: 10-yr Ⓐ 4.7% vs Ⓑ 4.1%; HR 1.11 (95% CI 0.82–1.51); no increase
・Subgroups: Larger DFS effect with T-score no more than -2.0 (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.52–0.86) vs more than -2.0 (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.79–1.06); interaction p=.04
・Toxicity: No notable differences between groups and no new signals with longer follow-up; grade 3 arthralgia Ⓐ 3% vs Ⓑ 2%; one grade 5 LV systolic dysfunction with letrozole
・Limitations: 10-yr update not prespecified in protocol; DR benefit absent before 4.0 yr; post-7.4-yr estimates unreliable from heavy censoring

records.body:
HR+, HER2−, node-positive high-risk early breast cancer, adjuvant setting after definitive surgery; high risk = ≥4 positive axillary nodes, or 1–3 nodes plus tumour ≥5 cm, histologic grade 3 or central Ki-67 ≥20%; randomization within 16 months of surgery, ≤12 weeks prior ET allowed; occult, metastatic, node-negative or inflammatory breast cancer, prior CDK4/6 inhibitor and VTE history excluded Ⓐ Abemaciclib 150 mg orally twice daily (continuous) + standard adjuvant endocrine therapy

・Design: Open-label Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: invasive disease-free survival in patients with high Ki-67 index (≥20%), distant relapse-free survival, overall survival, safety, pharmacokinetics, patient-reported outcomes Abemaciclib plus endocrine therapy sustained IDFS benefit and significantly improved overall survival versus endocrine therapy alone at median follow-up 6.3 years

records.title: NATALEE
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body:
HR-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer, anatomical stage II or III (AJCC 8th ed.); adjuvant setting; stage III/IIB eligible irrespective of nodal status; node-negative stage IIA only if grade 3, grade 2 with Ki-67 ≥20%, or high genomic risk; prior endocrine therapy up to 12 months allowed; excluded prior CDK4/6 inhibitor, uncontrolled heart disease or repolarization abnormality Ⓐ Ribociclib 400 mg orally once daily, 21 days on/7 days off, for 36 months + NSAI

・Design: International, open-label Primary: invasive disease-free survival. records.title: PENELOPE-B

Secondary: invasive disease-free survival excluding second primary invasive nonbreast cancers, distant disease-free survival, overall survival, locoregional relapse-free interval, safety, compliance Palbociclib for 1 year added to endocrine therapy did not improve iDFS in high-risk HR-positive, HER2-negative residual breast cancer after NACT

ER-positive/HER2-negative unresectable locoregional recurrent or metastatic breast cancer after one line of CDK4/6 inhibitor plus endocrine therapy (one CDK4/6 inhibitor only; up to one additional endocrine line; most recent endocrine therapy given for ≥6 months; adjuvant counted if progression within 12 months); measurable RECIST v1.1 disease or nonmeasurable bone-only disease; no prior chemotherapy for advanced disease, fulvestrant, elacestrant or PI3K/AKT/mTOR inhibitors Ⓐ Vepdegestrant 200 mg orally once every day of each 28-day cycle
Ⓑ Fulvestrant 500 mg intramuscularly on day 1 and day 15 of cycle 1, then day 1 of subsequent cycles
・Design: Open-label; stratified by ESR1-mutation status and visceral disease Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response, safety Vepdegestrant significantly improved progression-free survival vs fulvestrant in ESR1-mutated, ER-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer but not in the overall population
・PFS, ESR1-mutant: Ⓐ 5.0 vs Ⓑ 2.1 mo; HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.43–0.78)
・PFS, all patients: Ⓐ 3.8 vs Ⓑ 3.6 mo; HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.69–1.01); P=0.07
・OS (key secondary): Immature; median not reached in either group
・ORR, ESR1-mutant: Ⓐ 18.6% vs Ⓑ 4.0% (nominal; no multiplicity correction)
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 23.4% vs Ⓑ 17.6%; AE discontinuation Ⓐ 2.9% vs Ⓑ 0.7%
・QT: Any grade Ⓐ 9.9% vs Ⓑ 1.3%, grade 3 Ⓐ 1.6% vs Ⓑ 0.3%; no torsades de pointes or ventricular arrhythmias
・Limitations: Short follow-up (OS and duration of response not analysable); Black patients underrepresented

records.title: SERENA-6
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · ESR1-mutant disease & next-generation oral SERDs · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer (locoregionally recurrent or metastatic) on first-line aromatase inhibitor plus CDK4/6 inhibitor for at least 6 months; no evidence of progression; emerging ESR1 mutation detected on ctDNA surveillance (every 2–3 months) before randomization Ⓐ Switch to oral camizestrant 75 mg once daily with continued CDK4/6 inhibitor, plus placebo in place of aromatase inhibitor
Ⓑ Continue aromatase inhibitor plus CDK4/6 inhibitor (same type and dose), plus placebo in place of camizestrant
・CDK4/6 inhibitor: Palbociclib, ribociclib or abemaciclib continued at pre-randomization type and dose
・Duration: Until RECIST v1.1 progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent or death
・Ovarian suppression: LHRH agonist continued in premenopausal or perimenopausal women and men Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: second progression-free survival, overall survival, objective response, safety, quality of life, patient-reported visual effects, progression-free survival by blinded independent central review, chemotherapy-free or ADC-free survival, clinical benefit at 24 weeks, time to first subsequent therapy or death, time to second subsequent therapy or death, time to deterioration in breast and arm symptoms, pain and physical functioning, camizestrant plasma concentration Switching to camizestrant plus continued CDK4/6 inhibitor at ESR1 mutation emergence sustained PFS benefit and significantly improved second PFS vs continuing aromatase inhibitor
・PFS: Ⓐ 16.8 vs Ⓑ 9.2 mo; HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.34–0.59); updated at 23.5-mo median follow-up, descriptive
・PFS2: Ⓐ 25.7 vs Ⓑ 19.1 mo; HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.46–0.86); p=0.0037; final analysis
・OS: Ⓐ 41.2 vs Ⓑ 40.2 mo; HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.57–1.30); immature, 58% information fraction
・Chemo/ADC-free survival: Ⓐ 22.6 vs Ⓑ 18.7 mo; HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.47–0.87)
・BICR PFS: Ⓐ 19.3 vs Ⓑ 11.5 mo; HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.29–0.63)
・QoL (exploratory): Time to deterioration in GHS-QoL HR 0.48 (95% CI 0.31–0.76); interim medians Ⓐ 21.0 vs Ⓑ 6.4 mo
・Subgroups: Benefit consistent irrespective of PIK3CA or TP53 mutation status; PFS2 broadly consistent across clinically relevant subgroups
・ESR1 ctDNA: Allele frequency fell by week 4 with camizestrant and rose on continued aromatase inhibitor (exploratory)
・Toxicity: G3–4 neutropenia Ⓐ 27% vs Ⓑ 17%; photopsia Ⓐ 21% vs Ⓑ 8%, mostly grade 1–2; discontinuation 1% vs 3%; three possibly related deaths (Ⓐ sudden death; Ⓑ sepsis, ileus)
・Limitations: PFS updated descriptively at this cutoff; OS immature; few Black patients randomised

records.title: evERA Breast Cancer
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · ESR1-mutant disease & next-generation oral SERDs · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
ER-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced/metastatic breast cancer not amenable to curative intent; progression after ≥6 months of CDK4/6 inhibitor plus endocrine therapy for advanced disease, or recurrence during or within 12 months after adjuvant CDK4/6i plus endocrine therapy (≥12 months endocrine therapy, 6 months with CDK4/6i); measurable disease or evaluable bone metastases; excluded: progression on >2 endocrine lines, previous chemotherapy for advanced disease, previous oral SERD Ⓐ Giredestrant 30 mg orally once daily
Ⓑ Standard endocrine therapy (exemestane initially; fulvestrant or tamoxifen options after protocol amendment)
・Everolimus: 10 mg orally once daily in both arms
・LHRH agonist: For premenopausal or perimenopausal women and men
・Duration: Until disease progression or unacceptable toxic effects
・Design: Open-label Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response, duration of response, progression-free survival by blinded independent central review, safety Giredestrant–everolimus significantly prolonged progression-free survival vs standard endocrine therapy–everolimus after a CDK4/6 inhibitor, mainly in ESR1-mutated tumors
・PFS, ESR1-mutated: Ⓐ 10.0 vs Ⓑ 5.5 mo; HR 0.38 (95% CI 0.27–0.54)
・PFS, overall: Ⓐ 8.8 vs Ⓑ 5.5 mo; HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.44–0.71)
・OS, ESR1-mutated: Interim; 18-mo Ⓐ 71.5% vs Ⓑ 50.9%; HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.38–1.02); boundary not crossed
・OS, overall: Interim; 18-mo Ⓐ 75.1% vs Ⓑ 62.0%; HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.47–1.00); boundary not crossed
・ORR (measurable disease): ESR1-mutated Ⓐ 26.6% vs Ⓑ 13.8%; overall Ⓐ 23.8% vs Ⓑ 11.7%
・DoR (measurable disease): ESR1-mutated Ⓐ 14.9 vs Ⓑ 7.3 mo; overall Ⓐ 12.7 vs Ⓑ 7.7 mo
・Subgroups: ESR1 not detected — PFS Ⓐ 5.7 vs Ⓑ 5.5 mo; HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.59–1.18), exploratory
・Toxicity: Stomatitis Ⓐ 47.3% vs Ⓑ 48.9%; serious AEs Ⓐ 29.1% vs Ⓑ 23.1%; fatal AEs Ⓐ 2.7% vs Ⓑ 2.7%
・Limitations: Open-label; overall population enriched for ESR1-mutated tumors (55.5%); interim OS immature

records.title: DESTINY-Breast04
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · Antibody-drug conjugates & later-line therapy · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body:
HER2-low (IHC 1+ or IHC 2+/ISH-negative) unresectable or metastatic breast cancer after one or two previous chemotherapy lines for metastatic disease (or recurrence during or within 6 months of adjuvant chemotherapy); HR-positive (ER/PR in ≥1% of nuclei) required at least one endocrine therapy line; treated stable brain metastases eligible; excluded glucocorticoid-treated noninfectious interstitial lung disease or suspected interstitial lung disease at screening Ⓐ Trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks
Ⓑ Physician's choice of chemotherapy: capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel, given per local label or NCCN guidelines
・Design: Randomized, open-label Primary: progression-free survival in the hormone receptor–positive cohort. Secondary: progression-free survival among all patients, overall survival in the hormone receptor–positive cohort, overall survival among all patients, investigator-assessed progression-free survival, confirmed objective response, duration of response, efficacy in the hormone receptor–negative cohort, safety Trastuzumab deruxtecan significantly prolonged progression-free and overall survival versus physician's choice chemotherapy in HER2-low metastatic breast cancer
・PFS (HR-positive): Ⓐ 10.1 vs Ⓑ 5.4 mo; HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.40–0.64)
・PFS (all patients): Ⓐ 9.9 vs Ⓑ 5.1 mo; HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.40–0.63)
・OS (HR-positive): Ⓐ 23.9 vs Ⓑ 17.5 mo; HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.48–0.86)
・OS (all patients): Ⓐ 23.4 vs Ⓑ 16.8 mo; HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.49–0.84)
・ORR: Ⓐ 52.6% vs Ⓑ 16.3% (HR-positive); DoR Ⓐ 10.7 vs Ⓑ 6.8 mo
・HR-negative cohort: PFS Ⓐ 8.5 vs Ⓑ 2.9 mo (HR 0.46); OS Ⓐ 18.2 vs Ⓑ 8.3 mo (HR 0.48)
・Subgroups: PFS benefit consistent; Ⓐ 10.3 mo (IHC 1+), 10.1 mo (IHC 2+/ISH-negative); 10.0 with vs 11.7 mo without prior CDK4/6
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 52.6% vs Ⓑ 67.4%; G≥3 neutropenia Ⓐ 13.7% vs Ⓑ 40.7%; drug-related ILD/pneumonitis Ⓐ 12.1% (grade 5 0.8%); drug-related deaths Ⓐ only (pneumonitis 0.5%)
・Limitations: Open-label; OS interim (crossed 0.0075 boundary); small HR-negative cohort (63)

records.title: TROPiCS-02
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · Antibody-drug conjugates & later-line therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body:
HR+/HER2− endocrine-resistant, chemotherapy-treated locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic breast cancer; 2-4 prior chemotherapy regimens for metastatic disease, including a taxane; at least one prior hormonal treatment and at least one CDK4/6 inhibitor; (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy counted if relapse within 12 months Ⓐ Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV once weekly on days 1 and 8 every 21 days
Ⓑ Physician's choice single-agent chemotherapy: eribulin 1.4 mg/m² (North America) or 1.23 mg/m² (Europe) IV days 1 and 8 every 21 days; vinorelbine 25 mg/m² IV once weekly; gemcitabine 800-1,200 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days; capecitabine 1,000-1,250 mg/m² orally twice daily, 2 weeks on then 1 week rest, every 21 days
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent, or investigator's decision
・Design: Open-label; physician's choice chemotherapy selected before random assignment Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, clinical benefit rate, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, safety Sacituzumab govitecan improved both progression-free and overall survival versus physician's choice chemotherapy in heavily pretreated, endocrine-resistant HR+/HER2− metastatic breast cancer
・PFS (final): Ⓐ 5.5 vs Ⓑ 4.0 mo; HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.53 to 0.83)
・PFS rate: 6 mo Ⓐ 46% vs Ⓑ 30%; 12 mo Ⓐ 21% vs Ⓑ 7%
・OS (final analysis): Ⓐ 14.4 vs Ⓑ 11.2 mo; HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.65 to 0.96), p=0.020; 390 deaths, median follow-up 12.5 mo
・OS rate: 12 mo Ⓐ 61% vs Ⓑ 47%; 18 mo Ⓐ 39% vs Ⓑ 32%; 24 mo Ⓐ 25% vs Ⓑ 21%
・ORR: Ⓐ 21% vs Ⓑ 14%; OR 1.63 (95% CI 1.03 to 2.56), p=0.035; now formally tested given significant OS
・CBR: Ⓐ 34% vs Ⓑ 22%; DOR Ⓐ 8.1 vs Ⓑ 5.6 mo
・QoL: Time to deterioration longer with Ⓐ for global health status/QoL (Ⓐ 4.3 vs Ⓑ 3.0 mo; HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.61 to 0.92) and fatigue (Ⓐ 2.2 vs Ⓑ 1.4 mo; HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.60 to 0.89), now formally tested
・Subgroups (PFS): Benefit maintained across most prespecified subgroups, including visceral metastases, age 65 years or older and ≥3 prior metastatic chemotherapy regimens
・Subgroups (OS): Consistent regardless of Trop-2 expression (H-score <100 Ⓐ 14.6 vs Ⓑ 11.3 mo; ≥100 Ⓐ 14.4 vs Ⓑ 11.2 mo); larger with CDK4/6 inhibitor ≤12 mo (15.2 vs 10.5 mo) than >12 mo (13.9 vs 12.6 mo)
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 treatment-emergent neutropenia Ⓐ 51% vs Ⓑ 39%, diarrhea Ⓐ 10% vs Ⓑ 1%; discontinuations Ⓐ 6% vs Ⓑ 4%; 1 treatment-related death with Ⓐ (septic shock from neutropenic colitis), none with Ⓑ; no pneumonitis with Ⓐ
・Limitations: Open-label; 22 patients (8%) assigned to chemotherapy untreated; central review of progression not real-time, possibly increasing censoring

records.title: TROPION-Breast01
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · Antibody-drug conjugates & later-line therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body:
Inoperable or metastatic HR+/HER2– breast cancer (HER2– IHC 0, IHC 1+ or IHC 2+ FISH/ISH-negative); one or two previous lines of chemotherapy in the inoperable/metastatic setting; progression on endocrine therapy with further endocrine therapy unsuitable (original protocol also allowed endocrine-naïve patients); previous CDK4/6 inhibitor not required (capped); previous topoisomerase I agent (including ADCs) or TROP2-targeted therapy excluded; stable brain metastases allowed Ⓐ Datopotamab deruxtecan 6 mg/kg IV once every 3 weeks
Ⓑ Investigator's choice single-agent chemotherapy: eribulin 1.4 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8; capecitabine 1,000 or 1,250 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1-14; vinorelbine 25 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8; or gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8; each every 3 weeks
・Duration: Until investigator-assessed radiologic progression (RECIST v1.1), unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal of consent
・Design: Open-label Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate at 12 weeks, duration of response, time to first subsequent therapy or death, time to second subsequent therapy or death, PFS2, safety and tolerability Dato-DXd significantly improved PFS vs ICC, with fewer grade ≥3 TRAEs; OS immature at this analysis
・PFS: Ⓐ 6.9 vs Ⓑ 4.9 mo; HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.52–0.76)
・OS: Interim, immature (maturity 23.4%); HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.62–1.14)
・ORR: Ⓐ 36.4% vs Ⓑ 22.9%; OR 1.95 (95% CI 1.41–2.71)
・DoR: Ⓐ 6.7 vs Ⓑ 5.7 mo
・TFST: Ⓐ 8.2 vs Ⓑ 5 mo; HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.45–0.64)
・Subgroups: PFS benefit consistent across prespecified subgroups
・Toxicity: G≥3 TRAEs Ⓐ 20.8% vs Ⓑ 44.7%; stomatitis Ⓐ 50% vs Ⓑ 13.1%; ocular surface events Ⓐ 40% vs Ⓑ 11.7%; G≥3 neutropenia Ⓐ 1.1% vs Ⓑ 30.8%; adjudicated drug-related ILD Ⓐ 3.3% (one grade 5); one fatal TRAE Ⓑ (febrile neutropenia)
・Limitations: Open-label; OS immature; treatment landscape changed during study; more ICC than Dato-DXd patients not treated

records.body:
Hormone receptor–positive, HER2-low (IHC 1+ or 2+/ISH-negative) or HER2-ultralow (IHC 0 with membrane staining) metastatic breast cancer after endocrine-based therapy; progression after at least two endocrine lines for metastatic disease, or one line with recurrence within 24 months of starting adjuvant endocrine therapy or progression within 6 months on first-line endocrine therapy plus CDK4/6 inhibitor; no previous chemotherapy for metastatic disease; clinically active CNS metastases excluded Ⓐ Trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks
Ⓑ Physician's choice of single-agent chemotherapy: capecitabine 1250 or 1000 mg/m² orally twice daily for 2 weeks, then 1-week rest, in 3-week cycles; nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m² IV weekly for 3 weeks, then 1-week rest, in 4-week cycles; or paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV weekly in 3-week cycles
・Duration: Until disease progression (RECIST v1.1) or unacceptable toxic effects Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall survival, objective response, duration of response, safety Trastuzumab deruxtecan improved progression-free survival vs physician's-choice chemotherapy in endocrine-pretreated, HR-positive, HER2-low/ultralow metastatic breast cancer

records.title: NSABP B-31 / NCCTG N9831 (joint analysis)
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant trastuzumab — foundational trials · Joint analysis of two randomised clinical trials · 2005
records.body:
Women with adenocarcinoma of the breast, surgically removed, adjuvant setting after complete resection and axillary-node dissection; HER2-positive by immunohistochemistry 3+ or FISH amplification; node-positive (N9831 from May 2003 also high-risk node-negative: >2 cm ER/PR-positive or >1 cm ER/PR-negative); LVEF at or below lower limit of normal; excluded metastatic disease and cardiac history (myocardial infarction, heart failure, arrhythmia requiring medication) Ⓐ Doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by paclitaxel (control)
Ⓑ Doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide followed by paclitaxel plus concurrent trastuzumab
・Doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide: 60 mg/m² and 600 mg/m² every 21 days for four cycles
・Paclitaxel: B-31 175 mg/m² every 3 weeks for four cycles; N9831 80 mg/m² weekly for 12 weeks
・Trastuzumab (Ⓑ): 4 mg/kg loading dose with first paclitaxel dose, then 2 mg/kg weekly for 51 weeks
・Hormonal therapy: Tamoxifen 20 mg daily for five years in ER/PgR-positive tumours
・Design: Joint analysis of NSABP B-31 and NCCTG N9831; group B of N9831 (trastuzumab after completion of chemotherapy) excluded Primary: overall survival. Secondary: disease-free survival, time to recurrence, time to distant recurrence, death from breast cancer, contralateral breast cancer, other second primary cancers, safety Adding trastuzumab to paclitaxel after doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide produced a substantial and durable OS and DFS improvement in early-stage HER2-positive breast cancer, similar in HR-positive and HR-negative disease
・OS: Definitive analysis, median follow-up 8.4 yr; Ⓐ 75.2% vs Ⓑ 84% 10-yr OS; HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.54–0.73)
・DFS: Ⓐ 62.2% vs Ⓑ 73.7% 10-yr DFS; HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.53–0.68)
・10-yr RFS (2019 combined analysis): HR+ disease Ⓐ 65.17% vs Ⓑ 81.39%; HR 0.46 (95% CI 0.37–0.57); HR− disease Ⓐ 59.27% vs Ⓑ 77.78%; HR 0.47 (95% CI 0.38–0.58); interaction P .87
・RFS by period (Ⓑ vs Ⓐ): Years 0–5 HR 0.42 (95% CI 0.35–0.49); years 5–10 HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.49–0.97)
・Late relapse (years 5–10): More than 90% of 5-year recurrence-free survivors survived without additional recurrence; Ⓑ HR+ disease RoR 3.23% (N0) and 6.39% (N1)
・HR+ vs HR− pattern: Years 0–5 HR+ lower risk (HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.56–0.77); years 5–10 HR 1.32 (95% CI 0.93–1.88), adjusted HR 1.7 (95% CI 1.01–2.85)
・Time to distant recurrence (2005 interim): Ⓐ 81.5% vs Ⓑ 90.4% recurrence-free at 3 yr; HR 0.47 (95% CI 0.37–0.61)
・First events: Distant recurrence Ⓐ 20.6% vs Ⓑ 11.9%; brain involvement Ⓐ 2.0% vs Ⓑ 3.1%
・Subgroups: All subgroups benefited; DFS HR 0.62 (ER/PgR-negative) vs 0.61 (ER/PgR-positive); node-negative too small (191 women, 3 events; 2005 interim)
・Toxicity: 8-yr cardiac deaths Ⓑ 0.2% vs Ⓐ 0.1%; 3-yr CHF/cardiac death B-31 Ⓐ 0.8% vs Ⓑ 4.1%, N9831 Ⓐ 0% vs Ⓑ 2.9% (2005); two fatal pneumonitis (2005)
・Limitations: Control-arm contamination (20% of Ⓐ received trastuzumab after 2005 release; 5% of Ⓑ never did); no joint cardiac-safety analysis; 2019 nodal subsets small (N0 43, N3 69) with multiple comparisons

records.title: HERA (BIG 01-01)
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant trastuzumab — foundational trials · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2005
records.body:
Women with HER2-positive (central IHC 3+ or FISH-positive) early-stage invasive breast cancer, completely excised, after locoregional therapy plus four or more courses of neoadjuvant/adjuvant chemotherapy; node-positive, or node-negative with tumour >1 cm; LVEF ≥55 percent; excluded distant metastases, T4/inflammatory or supraclavicular disease, previous breast cancer, doxorubicin >360 or epirubicin >720 mg per square meter, cardiac history Ⓐ Trastuzumab initial dose 8 mg/kg IV, then 6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks for 1 year
Ⓑ Observation alone
・Design: Open-label, three-group randomised trial (observation, 1-yr and 2-yr trastuzumab); this final analysis reports both durations vs observation (row compares 1-yr trastuzumab vs observation) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: cardiac safety, overall survival, site of first disease-free-survival event, time to distant recurrence, competing-risk cumulative incidence of breast cancer and non-breast cancer DFS events, efficacy by hormone receptor status 1 year of trastuzumab after adjuvant chemotherapy improved long-term disease-free survival and overall survival versus observation in HER2-positive early breast cancer at 11 years’ median follow-up
・DFS (final analysis, median 11 years): 10-yr Ⓐ 69% vs Ⓑ 63%; HR 0·76 (95% CI 0·68–0·86); absolute benefit 6·8%
・OS (final analysis): 12-yr Ⓐ 79% vs Ⓑ 73%; HR 0·74 (95% CI 0·64–0·86); absolute benefit 6·5%
・TTDR (2005 interim): 2-yr Ⓐ 90.6% vs Ⓑ 82.8%; HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.38–0.63)
・2-yr trastuzumab: Vs observation DFS HR 0·77 (0·69–0·87); vs 1 yr (landmark) DFS HR 1·02 (0·89–1·17), no additional benefit
・Subgroups: DFS benefit in HR-positive (HR 0·80, 0·68–0·96) and HR-negative disease (0·73, 0·62–0·85), difference not significant; benefit irrespective of nodal status
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 18% vs Ⓑ 9%; primary cardiac endpoints Ⓐ 1% vs Ⓑ 0·1%; secondary cardiac endpoints Ⓐ 4·4% vs Ⓑ 0·9%, 2-yr arm 7·3%; no late cardiac emergence to 10 years
・Limitations: Open-label; selective crossover of 884 (52%) observation patients to trastuzumab attenuates ITT estimates, true benefit probably underestimated

records.title: FinHer
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant trastuzumab — foundational trials · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2006
records.body:
Early breast cancer, adjuvant after breast surgery; axillary-node–positive, or node-negative tumour ≥20 mm with progesterone-receptor–negative disease (<10% cell staining); women <66 years; HER2 by immunohistochemistry, CISH-confirmed when 2+/3+; excluded distant metastases, pregnancy, severe hypertension, cardiac disease Ⓐ Docetaxel 100 mg/m² IV day 1 per 21-day cycle, three cycles → FEC three cycles (docetaxel starting dose cut to 80 mg/m² during study)
Ⓑ Vinorelbine 25 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 per 21-day cycle, three cycles (day-15 dose omitted in third cycle) → FEC three cycles
Ⓒ Trastuzumab 4 mg/kg IV loading dose then 2 mg/kg weekly, nine infusions (nested randomisation for HER2/neu-amplified tumours, given during docetaxel/vinorelbine only)
Ⓓ No trastuzumab (nested randomisation for HER2/neu-amplified tumours)
・FEC: Fluorouracil 600 mg/m², epirubicin 60 mg/m², cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² IV day 1 per 21-day cycle, three cycles
・Duration: Chemotherapy 18 weeks; trastuzumab nine weeks; tamoxifen 20 mg daily for five years if hormone-receptor–positive
・Design: Open-label, multicentre; radiotherapy after chemotherapy Primary: distant disease–free survival. Secondary: adverse effects, left ventricular ejection fraction, overall survival, recurrence-free survival Adjuvant docetaxel improved distant disease–free survival versus vinorelbine in early breast cancer; 9-week trastuzumab did not significantly improve outcome in HER2-positive disease
・DDFS: Ⓐ better than Ⓑ; HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.49 to 0.91); P = .010; final analysis, median follow-up 62 mo
・OS: Ⓐ vs Ⓑ HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.46 to 1.05); P = .086; not significantly different
・DDFS, HER2+ (Ⓒ vs Ⓓ): HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.38 to 1.12); P = .12; nodal-status-adjusted HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.33 to 0.99), P = .047, above the P ≤ .029 limit
・OS, HER2+ (Ⓒ vs Ⓓ): HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.27 to 1.11); P = .094
・Exploratory DDFS, HER2+: Docetaxel + trastuzumab + FEC superior to docetaxel/FEC (HR 0.32; 95% CI 0.12 to 0.89) and vinorelbine + trastuzumab + FEC (HR 0.31; P = .020)
・Toxicity: Ⓐ more neutropenic fever (36.9% of women), stomatitis, alopecia, edema; Ⓑ more phlebitis, AST elevation
・Cardiac: Heart failure Ⓒ 0.9% vs Ⓓ 1.7%; median LVEF 65% (Ⓒ) vs 62% (Ⓓ) at 60 mo; ANCOVA difference 2.0 (95% CI 0.6 to 3.4; P = .006)
・Limitations: Open-label; small HER2+ trastuzumab subgroup (232), limited power; four-group comparisons exploratory

records.title: BCIRG 006
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant trastuzumab — foundational trials · Randomised clinical trial · 2011
records.body:
Women with HER2-positive, invasive, high-risk, node-negative or node-positive breast adenocarcinoma (stage T1, T2 or T3) in the adjuvant setting; HER2 status confirmed by fluorescence in situ hybridization before randomisation; enrolled from 41 countries Ⓐ Doxorubicin 60 mg/m² plus cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² every 3 weeks for four cycles → docetaxel 100 mg/m² every 3 weeks for four doses (AC-T)
Ⓑ AC-T plus trastuzumab, trastuzumab starting with the first docetaxel dose and continuing for 52 weeks
Ⓒ Docetaxel 75 mg/m² plus carboplatin AUC 6 every 3 weeks for six cycles concurrently with trastuzumab, then trastuzumab for 34 weeks (TCH)
・Trastuzumab dosing: 4 mg/kg initially, then 2 mg/kg weekly during chemotherapy, then 6 mg/kg every 3 weeks to complete 1 year Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, global safety, cardiac safety Both trastuzumab-containing regimens significantly improved disease-free and overall survival vs AC-T; no significant efficacy difference between them, with less cardiotoxicity favouring TCH
・5-yr DFS: Ⓐ 75% vs Ⓑ 84% vs Ⓒ 81%; HR 0.64 (Ⓑ) and 0.75 (Ⓒ) vs Ⓐ; third protocol-specified analysis, median follow-up 65 mo
・5-yr OS: Ⓐ 87% vs Ⓑ 92% vs Ⓒ 91%; HR 0.63 (Ⓑ) and 0.77 (Ⓒ) vs Ⓐ; P<0.001 and P=0.04
・Ⓑ vs Ⓒ: No significant DFS or OS difference; study not powered to detect equivalence
・TOP2A (prespecified): With coamplification (35% of cancers) trastuzumab-regimen DFS virtually indistinguishable from AC-T; benefit greater without coamplification
・Toxicity: CHF Ⓑ 2.0% vs Ⓒ 0.4% vs Ⓐ 0.7%; >10% LVEF fall Ⓑ 18.6% vs Ⓒ 9.4% vs Ⓐ 11.2%; acute leukemia seven anthracycline-arm vs one TCH case
・Limitations: Ⓑ vs Ⓒ comparison not powered for equivalence; subclinical LVEF loss persisted at least 4 yr in 33% of affected Ⓑ patients

records.title: EBCTCG trastuzumab meta-analysis
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant trastuzumab — foundational trials · Individual patient data meta-analysis · 2021
records.body:
Early-stage, HER2-positive operable breast cancer (node-negative or node-positive); adjuvant or neoadjuvant chemotherapy setting; most trials required node-positive or high-risk node-negative disease (generally grade 3, tumour >1 cm if ER-negative or >2 cm if ER-positive); HER2 by local IHC or FISH, some central confirmation; trials of trastuzumab plus other biological therapies excluded Ⓐ Chemotherapy plus trastuzumab
Ⓑ Same chemotherapy alone
・Chemotherapy: Anthracycline and/or taxane based; adjuvant except NOAH (neoadjuvant); endocrine therapy recommended in hormone receptor-positive disease
・Schedule: Concurrent with taxane (or vinorelbine) in most trials; sequential after all chemotherapy in HERA, PACS-04 and one NCCTG N9831 group
・Duration: Trastuzumab 12 months in all trials except FinHER (9 weeks); HERA also had 24-month group; mean scheduled duration 14·4 months Primary: breast cancer recurrence, breast cancer mortality, death without recurrence, all-cause mortality. Secondary: distant recurrence, local recurrence, contralateral breast cancer incidence, brain metastases as first site of distant recurrence, cardiovascular mortality, deaths from new cancers at sites other than the breast Adding trastuzumab to chemotherapy reduced breast cancer recurrence and mortality by a third in early-stage, HER2-positive disease, irrespective of recorded patient and tumour characteristics
・Recurrence: RR 0·66 (95% CI 0·62–0·71); 10-year absolute reduction 9·0% (7·4–10·7)
・Breast cancer mortality: RR 0·67 (0·61–0·73); 10-year absolute reduction 6·4% (4·9–7·8)
・All-cause mortality: RR 0·69 (0·64–0·75); 10-year absolute reduction 6·5% (5·0–8·0)
・Death without recurrence: Not increased; RR 0·90 (0·72–1·12)
・Recurrence timing: Largest reduction years 0–1 (RR 0·53, 99% CI 0·46–0·61), persisting years 2–4 (0·73) and 5–9 (0·80); little follow-up beyond 10 years
・Site of first recurrence: Distant RR 0·63 and local RR 0·72 reduced; contralateral breast cancer (0·93) and brain as first site (0·91) not reduced
・Subgroups: Proportional reductions similar by ER status, nodal status, age and HER2:CEP17 ratio; 5-year absolute gain rose from 5·7% (N0) to 10·7% (N4+)
・Concurrent vs sequential: No significant difference (RR 0·61 vs 0·69; heterogeneity p=0·083); NCCTG N9831 direct comparison favoured concurrent (RR 0·78, 0·63–0·97)
・Toxicity: No cardiovascular mortality increase (RR 1·23, 0·73–2·06); more year-1 deaths without recurrence Ⓐ 0·37% vs Ⓑ 0·16% (RR 2·15)
・Limitations: Control-group crossover in HERA (52·1%) and NSABP B-31 (36·0%); patient-level cardiac toxicity data from one trial only

records.title: PHARE
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Duration of adjuvant trastuzumab · Randomised, open-label, non-inferiority clinical trial (phase III) · 2013
records.body:
Women with HER2-positive invasive early breast cancer (local IHC or FISH); positive axillary nodes, or negative axillary nodes with tumour at least 10 mm; adjuvant setting after at least four cycles of chemotherapy and breast-axillary surgery; up to 6 months of trastuzumab before randomisation, LVEF assessed after at least 2 months and suitable to continue trastuzumab; patients who did not complete adjuvant chemotherapy or recurred early before randomisation excluded Ⓐ Trastuzumab continued for another 6 months (12 months total; control)
Ⓑ Trastuzumab discontinued at 6 months (6 months total; experimental)
・Trastuzumab: 8 mg/kg IV loading dose, then 6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks
・Chemotherapy, hormone therapy, radiotherapy: Investigator choice; trastuzumab concomitant with or sequential to chemotherapy
・Design: Open-label; randomised after up to 6 months of trastuzumab Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: cardiac safety, overall survival, metastasis-free survival, safety At final analysis, 6 months of adjuvant trastuzumab was not shown to be non-inferior to 12 months for DFS; cardiac events were fewer with 6 months
・DFS (final, median follow-up 7.5 yr): 7-yr Ⓐ 82.3% vs Ⓑ 80.6%; HR 1.08 (95% CI 0.93–1.25); margin 1.15 included, non-inferiority not shown
・DFS first 2 yr: HR 1.43 (95% CI 1.12–1.84) favouring Ⓐ; proportional hazards rejected
・OS (final): Deaths Ⓐ 10.1% vs Ⓑ 11.0%; HR 1.13 (95% CI 0.92–1.39)
・MFS (final): Distant recurrence as first event Ⓐ 13.3% vs Ⓑ 14.7%; HR 1.15 (95% CI 0.96–1.37)
・Subgroups: Consistent treatment effect; interim ER-negative/sequential heterogeneity disappeared
・Toxicity: Cardiac events Ⓐ 5.7% vs Ⓑ 1.9%; LVEF <50% Ⓐ 6.3% vs Ⓑ 4.7%; no trastuzumab-related deaths; final: no new heart failure, 3 further LVEF <50% cases in Ⓐ
・Limitations: Open-label; non-inferiority would have been claimed with a 1.29 margin (as in PERSEPHONE); only patients able to continue trastuzumab randomised, lower-risk population

records.title: ShortHER
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Duration of adjuvant trastuzumab · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body:
HER2-positive early breast cancer after surgery, adjuvant setting; women aged 18–75 suitable for adjuvant chemotherapy; node positive, or node negative with at least one risk factor (tumour >2 cm, grade 3, lympho-vascular invasion, Ki-67 >20%, age ≤35 years, or ER and PgR <10%); LVEF within institutional normal range; stage IIIB/IV excluded Ⓐ AC (doxorubicin 60 mg/sqm + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/sqm) or EC (epidoxorubicin 90 mg/sqm + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/sqm) every 3 weeks ×4 → paclitaxel 175 mg/sqm or docetaxel 100 mg/sqm every 3 weeks ×4 with trastuzumab 8 mg/kg loading dose then 6 mg/kg every 3 weeks for 18 doses (1 year)
Ⓑ Docetaxel 100 mg/sqm every 3 weeks ×3 with weekly trastuzumab for 9 weeks (4 mg/kg loading dose, then 2 mg/kg) → FEC (5-fluorouracil 600 mg/sqm, epidoxorubicin 60 mg/sqm, cyclophosphamide 600 mg/sqm) every 3 weeks ×3
・Amendment: Docetaxel 80 mg/sqm for patients aged ≥65 in both arms
・After chemotherapy: Radiotherapy and hormonal therapy when indicated, per local standard Primary: disease-free survival, overall survival (coprimary). Secondary: 2-year failure rate, cardiac safety At 10 years, 9 weeks of trastuzumab still could not be claimed non-inferior to 1 year; N0/N1-3 differences negligible, N4+ clearly favoured 1 year
・10-yr DFS: Ⓐ 77% vs Ⓑ 78%; HR 1.06 (90% CI 0.86–1.31); event-driven primary missed non-inferiority, HR 1.13 (90% CI 0.89–1.42) vs margin 1.29
・10-yr OS (final coprimary): Ⓐ 89% vs Ⓑ 88%; HR 1.15 (90% CI 0.85–1.56)
・Bayesian DFS, 10-yr: Posterior probability short arm non-inferior 93.2%; no pre-defined positive cut-off
・2-yr failure rate: Ⓐ 9.4% vs Ⓑ 8.6%; risk ratio 0.92 (95% CI 0.64–1.30)
・Subgroups: N4+ 10-yr DFS Ⓐ 63% vs Ⓑ 53%, OS Ⓐ 84% vs Ⓑ 64%; N0 and N1-3 differences negligible
・Toxicity: Grade ≥2 cardiac events Ⓐ 13.1% vs Ⓑ 4.3%, risk ratio 0.33 (95% CI 0.22–0.50); trastuzumab discontinued Ⓐ 8.5% vs Ⓑ 3.4%
・Limitations: Underpowered (power 0.56 after sample-size reduction); arms differ in chemotherapy and epidoxorubicin dose; subgroup findings exploratory

records.title: PERSEPHONE
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Duration of adjuvant trastuzumab · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body:
HER2-positive invasive early breast cancer (overexpression defined by UK Royal College of Pathologists guidelines); adjuvant or neoadjuvant trastuzumab with chemotherapy, any regimen allowed; clear indication for chemotherapy required; randomisation before trastuzumab start, amended July 2009 to allow up to the ninth trastuzumab cycle Ⓐ Trastuzumab 12 months (18 cycles)
Ⓑ Trastuzumab 6 months (9 cycles)
・Trastuzumab: Every 3 weeks; IV 8 mg/kg loading then 6 mg/kg maintenance, or subcutaneous 600 mg
・Chemotherapy: Adjuvant or neoadjuvant, concurrent or sequential; all regimens allowed Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, cardiac function (LVEF), predictive factors for cardiac damage, expected incremental cost-effectiveness, quality of life (EQ-5D-3L), safety, disease-free interval, distant disease-free interval, distant disease-free survival, invasive disease-free survival, breast-cancer specific survival 6-month trastuzumab was non-inferior to 12-month trastuzumab for 4-year disease-free survival, with fewer severe adverse events and less cardiotoxicity
・4-yr DFS (6.1-yr median follow-up): Ⓐ 90.3% vs Ⓑ 89.5%; HR 1.10 (90% CI 0.96–1.26); non-inferior, p=0.01
・4-yr OS (6.1-yr median follow-up): Ⓐ 94.9% vs Ⓑ 94.2%; HR 1.14 (90% CI 0.96–1.34); non-inferior, p=0.0003
・Landmark 4-yr DFS (from 6 mo after trastuzumab start, exploratory): Ⓐ 88.7% vs Ⓑ 88.4%; HR 1.09 (90% CI 0.95–1.26); non-inferior, p=0.03
・Landmark 4-yr OS (exploratory): Ⓐ 93.2% vs Ⓑ 92.6%; HR 1.12 (90% CI 0.95–1.34); non-inferior, p=0.006
・iDFS, DDFS, BCSS: Survival curves comparable with the protocol-specified end points
・PERSEPHONE + PHARE trial-level meta-analysis: Pooled DFS HR 1.08 (90% CI 0.98–1.18); non-inferior at 2% margin, p=0.04
・QoL: EQ-5D VAS steady to 3 months then slowly rising in both arms; fatigue and aches/pains most reported
・Cost-effectiveness: Lifetime saving £9316 with 0.01 fewer QALYs per patient; 73% probability cost-effective at £20,000/QALY
・Subgroups: DFS interaction by trastuzumab timing p<0.001: concurrent HR 1.54 (95% CI 1.19–1.99), sequential HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.70–1.07); OS timing interaction p=0.006
・Toxicity: Severe AEs Ⓐ 24% vs Ⓑ 19%; stopped for cardiotoxicity Ⓐ 8% vs Ⓑ 3%; clinical cardiac dysfunction Ⓐ 11% vs Ⓑ 8%; no trastuzumab-related deaths
・Limitations: Open-label; lower-risk population than original registration trials; concurrent vs sequential timing chosen by investigators, not randomised

records.title: NeoSphere
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase II) · 2012
records.body:
Women with centrally confirmed HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or 2+ with in-situ hybridisation positivity) operable (T2–3, N0–1, M0), locally advanced (T2–3, N2–3, M0 or T4a–c, any N, M0), or inflammatory (T4d, any N, M0) breast cancer with primary tumours larger than 2 cm; no previous cancer therapy; neoadjuvant setting; excluded stage IV, bilateral breast cancer, impaired cardiac function Ⓐ Trastuzumab plus docetaxel
Ⓑ Pertuzumab, trastuzumab, plus docetaxel
Ⓒ Pertuzumab plus trastuzumab (chemotherapy-free)
Ⓓ Pertuzumab plus docetaxel
・Trastuzumab: 8 mg/kg IV loading dose, then 6 mg/kg every 3 weeks
・Pertuzumab: 840 mg IV loading dose, then 420 mg every 3 weeks
・Docetaxel: 75 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks, escalating if tolerated to 100 mg/m²
・Duration: Four neoadjuvant cycles, then surgery; investigators could discontinue for insufficient benefit
・Adjuvant: FEC three cycles plus trastuzumab every 3 weeks to 1 year; Ⓒ had four docetaxel cycles before FEC
・Design: Open-label; Ⓓ added after 29 patients by amendment Primary: pathological complete response in the breast. Secondary: clinical response rate, time to clinical response, breast-conserving surgery rate, progression-free survival, disease-free survival, safety Adding pertuzumab to neoadjuvant trastuzumab plus docetaxel improved breast pathological complete response versus trastuzumab plus docetaxel; 5-year PFS and DFS descriptively support the benefit
・pCR breast: Ⓑ 45·8% vs Ⓐ 29·0%; p=0·0141 (ITT)
・pCR Ⓐ vs Ⓒ: Ⓒ 16·8% vs Ⓐ 29·0%; p=0·0198
・pCR Ⓑ vs Ⓓ: Ⓓ 24·0% vs Ⓑ 45·8%; p=0·003
・Clinical response: Ⓐ 79·8%, Ⓑ 88·1%, Ⓒ 67·6%, Ⓓ 71·4% (primary tumour)
・5-yr PFS: Ⓐ 81%, Ⓑ 86%, Ⓒ 73%, Ⓓ 73%; HR Ⓑ vs Ⓐ 0·69 (95% CI 0·34–1·40), Ⓓ vs Ⓑ 2·05 (1·07–3·93); descriptive
・5-yr DFS: Ⓐ 81%, Ⓑ 84%, Ⓒ 80%, Ⓓ 75%; consistent with PFS
・tpCR vs no tpCR: 5-yr PFS 85% vs 76%; HR 0·54 (95% CI 0·29–1·00); exploratory, all groups combined
・Subgroups: pCR ER/PR-negative Ⓑ 63·2% vs Ⓐ 36·8%; ER/PR-positive Ⓑ 26·0% vs Ⓐ 20·0%
・PFS subgroups: Pertuzumab benefit consistent irrespective of tpCR and hormone receptor status; few events
・Toxicity (neoadjuvant): G≥3 neutropenia Ⓐ 57%, Ⓑ 45%, Ⓒ 1%, Ⓓ 55%; febrile neutropenia 7–8%, none in Ⓒ; one death (Ⓑ fulminant hepatitis, possibly related)
・Toxicity (overall, 5-yr follow-up): G≥3 neutropenia Ⓐ 66%, Ⓑ 55%, Ⓒ 37%, Ⓓ 64%; febrile neutropenia Ⓓ 16% vs Ⓒ 5%; cardiac events 22 (5%) of 416; no new long-term safety concerns
・Limitations: Phase 2 proof-of-concept, α=0·2, open-label; PFS/DFS not powered, descriptive with wide CIs; 25 of 417 (6%) no planned surgery, mostly Ⓒ
