records.title: TRYPHAENA
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2013
records.body:
Female patients with HER2-positive primary breast cancer; neoadjuvant, no prior anticancer therapy: operable (T2-3, N0-1, M0), locally advanced (T2-3, N2 or N3, M0; T4a-c, any N, M0) or inflammatory (T4d, any N, M0), primary tumour >2 cm; HER2 IHC 3+ or FISH-positive, centrally confirmed; baseline LVEF ≥55%; excluded metastatic or bilateral disease, MI within 6 months Ⓐ FEC + trastuzumab + pertuzumab ×3 → docetaxel + trastuzumab + pertuzumab ×3
Ⓑ FEC ×3 → docetaxel + trastuzumab + pertuzumab ×3
Ⓒ Docetaxel 75 mg/m² (no escalation) + carboplatin AUC6 + trastuzumab + pertuzumab ×6
・Anti-HER2: Trastuzumab 8 mg/kg then 6 mg/kg IV; pertuzumab 840 mg then 420 mg IV; every 3 weeks
・FEC (Ⓐ, Ⓑ): 5-fluorouracil 500 mg/m², epirubicin 100 mg/m², cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m²; docetaxel 75 mg/m², escalating to 100 mg/m² if no dose-limiting toxicity in cycle 4
・Duration: Six neoadjuvant cycles every 3 weeks → surgery; trastuzumab continued to complete 1 year
・Design: Open-label; adjuvant radiotherapy, chemotherapy, hormonal treatment per local guidelines Primary: symptomatic left ventricular systolic dysfunction, LVEF decline ≥10% points from baseline to <50%. Secondary: pathological complete response (ypT0/is), clinical response rate, time to clinical response, rate of breast-conserving surgery, disease-free survival, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety during neoadjuvant and adjuvant treatment, pathological complete response (ypT0 ypN0), clinical complete response rate Pertuzumab plus trastuzumab with anthracycline-containing or carboplatin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy resulted in low rates of symptomatic LVSD in all three arms; long-term DFS and PFS were similar
・Symptomatic LVSD (neoadjuvant): Ⓐ 0.0% vs Ⓑ 2.7% vs Ⓒ 0.0%; one Ⓑ event during FEC alone
・LVEF decline ≥10% points to <50% (neoadjuvant): Ⓐ 5.6% vs Ⓑ 5.3% vs Ⓒ 3.9%; all recovered to ≥50%
・Adjuvant cardiac (final data): LVEF decline Ⓐ 7.4% vs Ⓑ 12.3% vs Ⓒ 4.5%; symptomatic LVSD 1.5% in Ⓒ only
・Cardiac, overall study period (5-yr follow-up): Symptomatic LVSD Ⓐ 0% vs Ⓑ 2.7% vs Ⓒ 1.3%; LVEF decline ≥10% to <50% Ⓐ 11.1% vs Ⓑ 16.0% vs Ⓒ 11.8%
・pCR (ypT0/is): Ⓐ 61.6% vs Ⓑ 57.3% vs Ⓒ 66.2%; descriptive, no between-arm testing
・ypT0 ypN0: Ⓐ 50.7% vs Ⓑ 45.3% vs Ⓒ 51.9%
・3-yr DFS: Ⓐ 87% vs Ⓑ 88% vs Ⓒ 90%; descriptive
・3-yr PFS: Ⓐ 89% vs Ⓑ 89% vs Ⓒ 87%
・3-yr OS: Ⓐ 94% vs Ⓑ 94% vs Ⓒ 93%; post-treatment deaths Ⓐ 5.6% vs Ⓑ 9.3% vs Ⓒ 13.2%, mostly from progression
・DFS by tpCR: tpCR vs no tpCR HR 0.27 (95% CI 0.11–0.64), all arms pooled; exploratory, not powered
・Subgroups: pCR higher in hormone receptor-negative than hormone receptor-positive tumours
・Toxicity: G≥3 neutropenia Ⓐ 47.2% vs Ⓑ 42.7% vs Ⓒ 46.1%; G≥3 febrile neutropenia Ⓐ 18.1% vs Ⓑ 9.3% vs Ⓒ 17.1%; SAEs Ⓐ 27.8% vs Ⓑ 20.0% vs Ⓒ 35.5%; no neoadjuvant deaths; no new safety signals at long-term follow-up
・Limitations: All arms experimental, no control arm; no formal hypothesis testing; survival reported at 3 years because 5-year follow-up was incomplete

records.title: TRAIN-2
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body:
HER2-positive stage II–III breast cancer, treatment-naive, neoadjuvant setting; HER2 defined as immunohistochemistry 3+ or 2+ with positive in-situ hybridisation; left ventricular ejection fraction of at least 50%; excluded pregnancy or breastfeeding, second primary breast cancer or other malignancy unless treated at least 5 years ago with curative intent without chemotherapy or radiotherapy Ⓐ 5-Fluorouracil 500 mg/m², epirubicin 90 mg/m² and cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks for three cycles → paclitaxel + carboplatin for six cycles
Ⓑ Paclitaxel + carboplatin for nine cycles
・Paclitaxel/carboplatin: Paclitaxel 80 mg/m² days 1 and 8; carboplatin AUC 6 mg/mL per min day 1 or AUC 3 mg/mL per min days 1 and 8, every 3 weeks
・Dual HER2 blockade: Trastuzumab 6 mg/kg (loading 8 mg/kg) and pertuzumab 420 mg (loading 840 mg) day 1 of each 3-week cycle with all chemotherapy cycles; trastuzumab continued to complete 1 year
・Design: Open-label Primary: pathological complete response (ypT0/is ypN0). Secondary: grade 3–5 adverse events, grade 2 or worse peripheral neuropathy, breast-conserving surgery, event-free survival, recurrence-free survival, distant metastasis-free survival, breast cancer-specific survival, overall survival Adding anthracyclines did not improve pCR; 3-year EFS and OS were similar with dual HER2 blockade, with more febrile neutropenia and cardiotoxicity
・pCR: Ⓐ 67% vs Ⓑ 68%; difference –1·5% (95% CI –11 to 8)
・3-yr EFS: Ⓐ 92.7% vs Ⓑ 93.6%; HR 0.90 (95% CI 0.50–1.63)
・3-yr OS: Ⓐ 97.7% vs Ⓑ 98.2%; HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.35–2.36)
・Breast-conserving surgery: Ⓐ 56% vs Ⓑ 60%; p=0·33
・DFS by pCR: pCR associated with fewer DFS events, HR 0.42 (95% CI 0.23–0.78); exploratory
・Subgroups: Similar EFS risk with vs without anthracyclines across hormone receptor, nodal, stage and grade subgroups
・Subgroups: Post-hoc by hormone receptor, pCR Ⓐ 89% vs Ⓑ 84% (receptor-negative) and Ⓐ 51% vs Ⓑ 55% (receptor-positive); interaction p=0·32
・Toxicity: Febrile neutropenia Ⓐ 10% vs Ⓑ 1% (p<0·0001); grade ≥2 LVEF decline (whole-study update) Ⓐ 36.4% vs Ⓑ 22.5%; two Ⓐ acute leukemias; one Ⓐ death from pulmonary embolism
・Limitations: Superiority design only, non-inferiority cannot be claimed; EFS/OS descriptive, not powered, follow-up short in hormone receptor–positive; quality-of-life endpoints not collected

records.title: TRAIN-3
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2026
records.body:
Newly diagnosed, pathologically confirmed stage II–III HER2-positive breast cancer in the neoadjuvant setting; LVEF of 50% or higher required; hormone receptor negativity defined as ER and PR expression on less than 10% of tumour cells; excluded pregnancy, bilateral breast cancer, and previous treatment for this invasive breast cancer (single-arm) Neoadjuvant paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8, trastuzumab 6 mg/kg IV day 1 (loading 8 mg/kg), carboplatin AUC 6 IV day 1, pertuzumab 420 mg IV day 1 (loading 840 mg), per 21-day cycle, up to nine cycles
・MRI: Breast MRI repeated every three cycles; surgery at complete radiological response or after maximum nine cycles
・pCR: 1 full year of adjuvant trastuzumab and pertuzumab
・Residual invasive disease: Total nine cycles of the same regimen, then 14 cycles trastuzumab emtansine 3.6 mg/kg IV day 1 per 21-day cycle Primary: 3-year event-free survival. Secondary: radiological complete response, pathological complete response, number of neoadjuvant chemotherapy cycles administered, number of radical resections, 3-year overall survival, health-related quality of life, safety MRI-guided shortening of neoadjuvant chemotherapy duration was associated with favourable 3-year event-free survival, meeting the primary endpoint in both hormone receptor subgroups
・3-yr EFS: 92.2% (95% CI 88.7–95.9) hormone receptor-negative; 92.0% (88.5–95.6) hormone receptor-positive; primary outcome met in both subgroups
・3-yr OS: 97.8% (96.0–99.7) hormone receptor-negative; 98.7% (97.2–100) hormone receptor-positive
・EFS by cycles (receptor-neg/receptor-pos): 1–3 cycles 96.1%/98.6%; 4–6 89.2%/94.2%; 7–9 90.6%/85.4%
・EFS by pCR: 87.5% (95% CI 82.6–92.7) without vs 94.8% (92.2–97.5) with pCR; HR 0.40 (0.21–0.75)
・QoL: Clinically significant deterioration at 6 months in 36%, 54%, 72% after 1–3, 4–6, 7–9 cycles
・Toxicity: G3–4 neutropenia 40%, anaemia 18%, diarrhoea 13%; treatment-related serious AEs 12%; no treatment-related deaths; rose with more cycles
・Limitations: Single-arm; follow-up short, late recurrences possible beyond 3 years; no central pathology or radiology review

records.title: KRISTINE (TRIO-021)
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body:
HER2-positive early breast cancer; operable clinical stage II–III (cT2–cT4/cN0–cN3/cM0, >2 cm), neoadjuvant, no previous systemic therapy; central HER2 confirmation (IHC 3+ or ISH-positive), known hormone receptor status; LVEF ≥55%; excluded bilateral or multicentric (>1 quadrant) disease, prior invasive breast cancer, incisional/excisional biopsy of tumour or node, positive baseline sentinel node, grade ≥2 neuropathy Ⓐ Trastuzumab emtansine 3·6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks × 6 cycles
Ⓑ Docetaxel 75 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 6 mg/mL × min + trastuzumab 8 mg/kg loading, 6 mg/kg maintenance IV every 3 weeks × 6 cycles
・Pertuzumab (both arms): 840 mg loading, 420 mg maintenance IV every 3 weeks
・Surgery: 14 days to 6 weeks after neoadjuvant therapy
・Adjuvant: Assigned HER2-targeted regimen (Ⓐ trastuzumab emtansine plus pertuzumab; Ⓑ trastuzumab plus pertuzumab) for 12 cycles, 18 cycles in total; anthracycline-based chemotherapy (≥4 cycles) recommended in Ⓐ for non-pCR with residual tumour >1 cm or >ypN0
・Design: Open-label Primary: pathological complete response (ypT0/is, ypN0). ・OS, 3-yr: Ⓐ 97·0% vs Ⓑ 97·6% event-free; HR 1·21 (95% CI 0·37 to 3·96); 6 vs 5 deaths, too few for conclusions
・IDFS by pCR (post hoc): pCR vs residual disease HR 0·24 (95% CI 0·09 to 0·60), regardless of arm
・BCS: Ⓐ 42% vs Ⓑ 53% (no inflammatory cancer); difference −10·8 points (95% CI −20·2 to −1·5)
・QoL: Median time to HRQOL deterioration Ⓐ 4·6 vs Ⓑ 3·0 mo; physical function Ⓐ 4·9 vs Ⓑ 2·8 mo; descriptive
・QoL, 3-yr PROs: Fewer neoadjuvant impairments with Ⓐ (global health, physical and cognitive functioning, diarrhea); similar during adjuvant treatment

records.title: PHERGain-2
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2026
records.body:
Previously untreated, invasive, centrally confirmed HER2-positive (IHC 3+) operable early breast cancer; node-negative, tumor size 5-30 mm by central MRI; ECOG PS 0/1, LVEF ≥55%; lymph node involvement, bilateral breast cancer and metastatic disease excluded (single-arm) Subcutaneous trastuzumab–pertuzumab 600 mg + 1200 mg loading, then 600 mg + 600 mg maintenance, every 3 weeks × 8 cycles, then surgery
・Cohort A (pCR, ypT0/is ypN0): trastuzumab–pertuzumab maintenance × 10 cycles q3w
・Cohort B (residual invasive tumor and/or ypN0(i+), ypN0(mol+), ypN1mi): T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV q3w × 10 cycles
・Cohort C (ypN1-N3): optional chemotherapy, then T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV q3w × 10 cycles
・ET: Endocrine therapy for HR-positive tumors
・Duration: Adjuvant treatment continued until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal, or investigator decision Primary: 1-year global health status decline (≥10%, EORTC QLQ-C30), 3-year recurrence-free interval. Secondary: pathologic complete response rate, pCR rate by hormone receptor status, pCR rate by tumor stage, objective response rate, breast-conserving surgery rate, safety, 5-year recurrence-free interval, 3- and 5-year event-free survival, relapse-free survival, disease-free survival, invasive disease-free survival, overall survival Chemotherapy-free neoadjuvant trastuzumab–pertuzumab with pCR-guided adjuvant HP or T-DM1 achieved a 59.6% pCR rate and 42.8% ≥10% HRQoL decline at 1 year
・HRQoL: 42.8% ≥10% global health status decline at 1 year; 37.3% with pCR vs 51.9% with residual disease
・pCR: 59.6%; 63.0% HR− vs 58.3% HR+
・Subgroups: HRQoL decline 45.2% HR+ vs 36.1% HR−
・ORR: 78.3%, complete response 62.1%
・BCS: 83.9% among 391 undergoing surgery
・Toxicity: TRAEs 86.6% (grade ≥3 5.6%); SAEs 6.1%; one death (0.3%) from T-DM1-related pneumonitis
・Limitations: Single-arm without control; 3-year RFI co-primary pending (median follow-up 15.1 months); pCR not centrally assessed

records.title: WSG-ADAPT-TP
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2023
records.body:
Centrally reviewed HR+/HER2+ early breast cancer (clinical stage I-III); neoadjuvant de-escalated, systemic chemotherapy-free setting; HER2 positivity per ASCO-CAP criteria on central pathology; adjuvant chemotherapy optional after pCR, standard chemotherapy mandatory after non-pCR Ⓐ T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg once every 3 weeks
Ⓑ T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg once every 3 weeks + endocrine therapy
Ⓒ Trastuzumab 8 mg/kg loading dose, then 6 mg/kg once every 3 weeks + endocrine therapy
・ET: Tamoxifen in premenopausal women; aromatase inhibitor in postmenopausal women
・Duration: 12 weeks neoadjuvant; adjuvant chemotherapy optional after pCR, standard chemotherapy after non-pCR Primary: pathologic complete response (ypT0/is, ypN0). Secondary: invasive disease-free survival, distant disease-free survival, overall survival, biomarker analysis De-escalated neoadjuvant T-DM1 ± ET and trastuzumab + ET showed similar 5-year iDFS, DDFS and OS; pCR predicted excellent survival without adjuvant chemotherapy
・pCR (primary, previously reported): Ⓐ 41% vs Ⓑ 41.5% vs Ⓒ 15.1%
・5-yr iDFS: Ⓐ 88.9% vs Ⓑ 85.3% vs Ⓒ 84.6%; stratified log-rank P = .448
・5-yr DDFS: Ⓐ 91.6% vs Ⓑ 92.3% vs Ⓒ 88.9%; P = .567
・5-yr OS: Ⓐ 97.2% vs Ⓑ 96.4% vs Ⓒ 96.3%; P = .671
・iDFS by response: 5-yr iDFS 92.7% pCR vs 82.7% non-pCR; HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.18 to 0.85)
・ACT after pCR: 5-yr iDFS 93.0% with vs 92.1% without ACT; HR 1.15 (95% CI 0.27 to 4.81)
・Biomarkers (exploratory): PIK3CA mutation worse iDFS on T-DM1 (HR 3.65; 95% CI 1.33 to 10.06), interaction not significant; luminal-A, high CD8/PD-L1 better
・Subgroups: Node-positive iDFS risk HR 2.36 (95% CI 1.28 to 4.34) vs node-negative; early Ki67 response not prognostic
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: Not powered for survival endpoints; ACT at investigator discretion; too small for subgroup analyses

records.title: Villacampa et al.
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · Network meta-analysis · 2023
records.body:
HER2-positive breast cancer treated preoperatively; pooled randomised trials with at least one anti-HER2 arm and any available efficacy endpoint; single-arm/non-randomised trials, trials without any anti-HER2 arm and ongoing unpublished trials excluded ・Dual anti-HER2 + CT vs single anti-HER2 + CT (11,049 patients, 46 RCTs)
・Dual anti-HER2 + CT vs T-DM1 without CT
・Dual anti-HER2 + CT vs dual anti-HER2 without CT
・Anthracycline vs non-anthracycline CT (trastuzumab, lapatinib, pertuzumab + trastuzumab, lapatinib + trastuzumab)
・TCHP vs THP (addition of carboplatin)
・Trastuzumab biosimilar vs trastuzumab
・Regimens: 32 evaluated; TKIs = lapatinib, neratinib, pyrotinib; PI3K/AKT inhibitors = buparlisib, MK-2206; EFS network 4,919 patients Primary: pathologic complete response. Secondary: event-free survival, overall survival, cardiac toxicity, neutropenia grade ≥3, diarrhoea grade ≥3, LVEF decline Dual anti-HER2 blockade plus chemotherapy improved pCR, EFS and OS versus single anti-HER2 plus chemotherapy, with no efficacy gain from anthracyclines
・pCR, dual vs single anti-HER2 + CT: OR 2.09 (95% CI 1.81–2.40)
・EFS (network 4,919): HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.45–0.69)
・OS: HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.44–0.84)
・vs T-DM1 (no CT): pCR OR 1.38 (95% CI 1.00–1.94); EFS HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.29–0.91)
・Anthracycline vs non-anthracycline: No significant efficacy difference; EFS with pertuzumab + trastuzumab + CT HR 1.00 (95% CI 0.63–1.59)
・TCHP vs THP: pCR OR 1.45 (95% CI 0.73–2.88); EFS HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.22–2.35); thrombocytopenia grade ≥3 12.9% vs 0%
・pCR surrogacy: Weak trial-level correlation with EFS (R2 = 0.34) and OS (R2 = 0.12)
・Toxicity: Dual anti-HER2 + CT worst cardiac toxicity (P-score 0.21) and LVEF drop (P-score 0.18); TKIs and T-DM1 highest diarrhoea grade ≥3
・Limitations: Treatment duration and adjuvant therapy not accounted for; immature OS data; safety restricted to neoadjuvant period

records.title: APHINITY

records.body:
Invasive HER2-positive breast cancer, nonmetastatic, adequately excised, adjuvant setting; centrally confirmed HER2 (IHC 3+ in >10% of cells or ERBB2 amplification); node-positive or node-negative tumor >1.0 cm (0.5–1.0 cm if grade 3, ER/PR-negative, or age <35; node-negative entry closed after 3655 randomized); baseline LVEF ≥55%; excluded prior invasive breast cancer, nonbreast cancer within 5 years, any prior chemotherapy/radiotherapy, prior anti-HER2 therapy, serious cardiac disease Ⓐ Pertuzumab 840 mg IV loading dose, then 420 mg IV every 3 weeks
Ⓑ Placebo IV 840 mg loading dose, then 420 mg every 3 weeks
・Trastuzumab: 8 mg/kg IV loading dose, then 6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks, from first taxane cycle to maximum 18 cycles within 1 year
・Chemotherapy: Anthracycline-based regimen followed by docetaxel or weekly paclitaxel, or docetaxel plus carboplatin
・Endocrine therapy: For hormone-receptor-positive disease, from end of chemotherapy, at least 5 years
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled Primary: invasive-disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, disease-free survival, invasive-disease-free survival including second primary nonbreast cancer (STEEP definition), relapse-free interval, distant-relapse-free interval, safety, health-related quality of life Adjuvant pertuzumab sustained the invasive-disease-free survival benefit at 8.4 years' median follow-up, driven by node-positive disease, without a significant overall survival improvement at the third interim analysis
・IDFS: 8-year Ⓐ 88.4% vs Ⓑ 85.8%; HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.66–0.91); absolute benefit 2.7% (95% CI 0.7–4.6); descriptive update, median FU 8.4 years
・OS: Third interim, 8-year Ⓐ 92.7% vs Ⓑ 92.0%; HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.68–1.02); P .078, required <.0060 not reached; follow-up continuing to final analysis
・Subgroups (node-positive): 8-year iDFS Ⓐ 86.1% vs Ⓑ 81.2%; HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.60–0.87), absolute benefit 4.9%; OS HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.63–1.00)
・Subgroups (node-negative): No iDFS benefit, HR 1.01 (95% CI 0.72–1.42); 8-year OS Ⓑ 96.4%; only meaningful interaction nodal status, nominal P .088
・Subgroups (HR status): Benefit in both; HR-positive HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.61–0.92), absolute benefit 2.8%; HR-negative HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.64–1.06), 2.4%
・Toxicity: G≥3 diarrhea Ⓐ 9.8% vs Ⓑ 3.7%; febrile neutropenia Ⓐ 12.1% vs Ⓑ 11.1%; primary cardiac events Ⓐ 0.8% vs Ⓑ 0.4%; fatal cardiac disorder Ⓐ 0.1% vs Ⓑ 0.2%; no late cardiac toxicity
・Limitations: OS not significant at third interim, final analysis event-driven; no iDFS benefit in node-negative disease; only 1 year of pertuzumab tested

records.title: KATHERINE
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant dual blockade & post-neoadjuvant escalation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body:
Centrally confirmed HER2-positive, nonmetastatic invasive breast cancer (clinical stage T1–T4, N0–N3, M0, excluding T1aN0/T1bN0) with pathological residual invasive disease in breast or axillary nodes after neoadjuvant taxane plus trastuzumab (≥6 cycles/16 weeks, ≥9 weeks taxane, ≥9 weeks trastuzumab); excluded gross residual disease or positive margins, progression during neoadjuvant therapy, NYHA class II+ heart failure or prior LVEF <40% Ⓐ T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks
Ⓑ Trastuzumab 6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks (8 mg/kg loading dose if >6 weeks since preceding dose)
・Duration: 14 cycles
・Design: Open-label
・SOC: Radiotherapy and endocrine therapy per institutional standards Primary: invasive disease–free survival. Secondary: invasive disease–free survival including second primary nonbreast cancer, disease-free survival (including noninvasive breast cancers), overall survival, distant recurrence–free survival, safety Adjuvant T-DM1 improved overall survival with sustained invasive disease–free survival benefit vs trastuzumab after residual invasive disease following neoadjuvant therapy
・IDFS (final analysis, median follow-up 8.4 yr): Ⓐ 80.8% vs Ⓑ 67.1% at 7 yr; HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.44–0.66); absolute difference 13.7 percentage points
・OS (second interim): Ⓐ 89.1% vs Ⓑ 84.4% at 7 yr; HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.51–0.87); P=0.003 crossed the prespecified O'Brien–Fleming boundary
・Distant recurrence: First event Ⓐ 14.7% vs Ⓑ 21.5%; 7-yr distant recurrence–free interval Ⓐ 84.5% vs Ⓑ 76.2%, HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.47–0.76)
・Other secondary: IDFS incl. second primary nonbreast cancers HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.46–0.68); DFS HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.47–0.70)
・CNS: No reduced CNS recurrence risk with T-DM1; first-event CNS numerically higher on Ⓐ, cumulative CNS similar in both arms
・Subgroups: iDFS benefit smaller in IHC 2+/ISH-amplified (HR 0.84, 0.56–1.25) than IHC 3+ (HR 0.47, 0.37–0.60); exploratory interaction HR 0.55 (0.35–0.88)
・Residual ≤1 cm, node-negative: iDFS HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.37–1.03); 7-yr Ⓐ 85.7% vs Ⓑ 76.7%
・Consistency: iDFS and OS benefit irrespective of extent at presentation, hormone-receptor status, nodal status, age, race
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs (entire trial) Ⓐ 26.1% vs Ⓑ 15.7%; SAEs Ⓐ 12.7% vs Ⓑ 8.1%; discontinuations Ⓐ 18.0% vs Ⓑ 2.1%; G≥3 thrombocytopenia Ⓐ 5.7% vs Ⓑ 0.3%; 1 fatal intracranial hemorrhage on Ⓐ; delayed toxicities rare
・Limitations: Open-label; final iDFS analysis descriptive, formal testing only for OS; OS at second interim analysis

records.title: ExteNET

records.body:
Women with locally confirmed invasive HER2-positive breast cancer; early stage, extended adjuvant after neoadjuvant/adjuvant trastuzumab and chemotherapy; stage 1–3 node-positive or node-negative (≥T1c), trastuzumab completed up to 2 years before randomisation, amended Feb 25, 2010 to stage 2–3 node-positive with trastuzumab completed up to 1 year previously, no recurrence; excluded clinically significant cardiac, gastrointestinal or psychiatric comorbidities Ⓐ Neratinib 240 mg orally once daily continuously

Secondary: disease-free survival including ductal carcinoma in situ, time to distant recurrence, distant disease-free survival, cumulative incidence of CNS recurrences, overall survival, safety, health-related quality of life Neratinib for 12 months after trastuzumab-based adjuvant therapy improved 2-year invasive disease-free survival vs placebo; benefit maintained at 5-year follow-up
・2-yr iDFS: Ⓐ 93.9% vs Ⓑ 91.6%; HR 0.67 (95% CI 0.50–0.91)
・5-yr iDFS: Ⓐ 90.2% vs Ⓑ 87.7%; HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.57–0.92); prespecified sensitivity analysis
・5-yr DFS incl. DCIS: Ⓐ 89.7% vs Ⓑ 86.8%; HR 0.71 (95% CI 0.56–0.89)
・5-yr DDFS/TTDR: Not significantly different; HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.60–1.01) and 0.79 (95% CI 0.60–1.03)
・CNS recurrence: 5-yr cumulative incidence Ⓐ 1.3% vs Ⓑ 1.8%; p=0.333
・QoL: FACT-B and EQ-5D worse with Ⓐ at month 1, not clinically important; recovered thereafter (exploratory)
・Subgroups: At 5 yr, hormone receptor-positive HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.43–0.83); receptor-negative HR 0.95 (95% CI 0.66–1.35); p-interaction 0.063; not powered
・Toxicity: G3 diarrhoea Ⓐ 40% vs Ⓑ 2%, no prophylaxis; diarrhoea caused Ⓐ dose reduction 26%, discontinuation 17%; serious TEAEs Ⓐ 7% vs Ⓑ 6%; no treatment-related deaths; no evidence of increased long-term toxicity
・Limitations: 5-yr analysis is a sensitivity analysis after 2-yr truncation, 75% re-consented; OS immature; more early censoring with Ⓐ

records.title: APT (Adjuvant Paclitaxel + Trastuzumab)
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · De-escalation for low-risk / node-negative disease · Single-arm clinical trial · 2015
records.body:
Adenocarcinoma of the breast, HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or FISH HER2:CEP17 ratio ≥2.0), adjuvant setting; invasive tumour ≤3 cm greatest dimension with no lower size limit, node-negative (amended to allow one nodal micrometastasis if axillary dissection showed no further involvement), predominantly stage I; LVEF ≥50% (single-arm) Paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV weekly for 12 weeks + trastuzumab 4 mg/kg IV loading dose then 2 mg/kg weekly (12 doses) → trastuzumab monotherapy to complete a full year
・Trastuzumab continuation: weekly dosing, or 6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks for 40 weeks Primary: survival free from invasive disease. Secondary: recurrence-free interval, recurrence-free survival, breast cancer–specific survival, overall survival, adverse events including cardiac toxicity and neurotoxicity At final 10-year analysis, adjuvant paclitaxel plus trastuzumab remained associated with very good long-term outcomes and few recurrences in small, node-negative, HER2-positive breast cancer
・DFS: 3-yr 98.7% at primary cut (Poisson vs 9.2% null, P<0.001); 10-yr 91.3% (95% CI 88.3–94.4), median follow-up 10.8 years
・RFI: 10-yr 96.3% (95% CI 94.3–98.3); excludes non-breast-cancer deaths
・10-yr BCSS: 98.8% (95% CI 97.6–100); 98.8% (97.7–100) accounting for competing risks
・10-yr OS: 94.3% (95% CI 91.8–96.8)
・Subgroups: 10-yr DFS 91.6% HR-positive vs 90.6% HR-negative; HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.40–1.72); outcomes similar regardless of HR status or tumour size
・PAM50 (exploratory, n=278): HER2-enriched 66%, luminal B 14%, luminal A 13%, basal-like 8%; distribution similar to larger tumours
・PAM50 10-yr (exploratory): Luminal B DFS 85.2% (95% CI 74.0–98.1) vs 90.6–94.4% other subtypes; luminal B RFI 88.0% (77.6–99.8)
・HER2DX (exploratory, n=284): Per 10-unit score HR 1.24 (95% CI 1.00–1.52) DFS, 1.45 (1.09–1.93) RFI; score <32 vs ≥32: 10-yr recurrence 1.4% vs 13.3%; not significant in multivariable analysis
・TIPN genotype (exploratory): rs3012437 associated with grade ≥2 TIPN (10.4%); OR 2.1, P=.024
・Toxicity: Grade 3 neuropathy 3.2%; grade ≥2 TIPN 10.4% (genotyped subgroup), no grade 4 neurotoxicity; symptomatic CHF 0.5% with LVEF recovery; asymptomatic LVEF decline 3.2%; 6% withdrew for protocol-specified toxic effects
・Limitations: Single-arm design; post-hoc HER2DX in subset (284/406) needs validation before treatment escalation or omission; low event rate limits biomarker analyses

records.title: ATEMPT
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · De-escalation for low-risk / node-negative disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2021
records.body:
Stage I HER2-positive invasive breast cancer, centrally confirmed (ASCO/CAP 2013), tumour ≤2 cm, node-negative or ≤1 node with micrometastasis (N1mi), AJCC 7th edition; adjuvant setting within 90 days of surgery; no prior breast cancer Ⓐ T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV on day 1 of each 21-day cycle × 17 cycles (1 year)
Ⓑ Paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV weekly × 12 weeks with trastuzumab (4 mg/kg load → 2 mg/kg weekly) → trastuzumab 6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks × 13 cycles
・Radiotherapy/endocrine therapy: Could start after 12 weeks of Ⓐ or after paclitaxel in Ⓑ
・Design: Randomised to compare toxicity; efficacy assessed one-sample in the Ⓐ arm Primary: incidence of clinically relevant toxicities, invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: recurrence-free interval, quality of life (FACT-B), symptom distress (Rotterdam Symptom Checklist), neuropathy (Patient Neurotoxicity Questionnaire), work productivity and activity (WPAI:SHP), alopecia, safety Adjuvant T-DM1 maintained 5-year iDFS of 97.0% with clinically relevant toxicities similar to TH; high HER2DX risk predicted recurrence
・CRT: Ⓐ 46% vs Ⓑ 47%; P=.83 (median follow-up 3.9 years)
・5-yr iDFS: Ⓐ 97.0% (95% CI 95.2–98.7); final preplanned analysis, median follow-up 5.8 years
・5-yr RFI: Ⓐ 98.3% (95% CI 97.0–99.7)
・5-yr OS: Ⓐ 97.8% (95% CI 96.3–99.3); BCSS 99.4% (95% CI 98.6–100)
・5-yr outcomes, Ⓑ descriptive: iDFS 91.1% (95% CI 85.7–96.8), RFI 93.2% (95% CI 88.5–98.2); arm not powered for efficacy
・HER2DX (post hoc, n=187): High-risk 6.4% had worse 5-yr RFI 81.8% vs 98.1%; HR 0.10 (95% CI 0.02–0.57), P=.01; iDFS HR 0.20 (0.04–0.98), P=.047
・Correlatives: No germline variant predicted T-DM1 thrombocytopenia/bleeding; HER2 heterogeneity (approximately 8%) had no significant impact on survival
・QoL: Ⓑ larger FACT-B decline to week 12 (approx 6 points); Ⓐ less neuropathy, alopecia and work impairment
・Toxicity: G≥2 neuropathy Ⓐ 11% vs Ⓑ 23%, alopecia Ⓐ 0% vs Ⓑ 41%, thrombocytopenia Ⓐ 11% vs Ⓑ 1%; AE discontinuation Ⓐ 17% vs Ⓑ 6%
・Limitations: Not designed to compare efficacy between arms; HER2DX post hoc, tested in 37.6% of patients; mostly HR-positive disease

records.title: H0648g (pivotal trastuzumab)
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · First-line metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2001
records.body:
Women with progressive metastatic breast cancer overexpressing HER2 (immunohistochemistry 2+ or 3+ in more than 10 percent of tumor cells, central laboratory), no prior chemotherapy for metastatic disease; excluded untreated brain metastases, bilateral breast cancer, osteoblastic bone metastases, pleural effusion or ascites as only evidence of disease, second primary cancer, Karnofsky score <60 Ⓐ Chemotherapy plus trastuzumab — trastuzumab IV 4 mg/kg loading dose, then 2 mg/kg weekly, until disease progression
Ⓑ Chemotherapy alone
・Chemotherapy: Doxorubicin 60 mg/m² (or epirubicin 75 mg/m²) plus cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m², or paclitaxel 175 mg/m², every three weeks for six cycles; additional cycles at investigator's discretion
・Backbone choice: Anthracycline plus cyclophosphamide if anthracycline-naive; paclitaxel if prior adjuvant anthracycline Primary: time to disease progression. Secondary: rate of objective response, duration of response, time to treatment failure, overall survival, adverse events Adding trastuzumab to first-line chemotherapy improved time to disease progression, response rate and overall survival in HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer
・TTP: Ⓐ 7.4 vs Ⓑ 4.6 mo; RR 0.51 (95% CI 0.41–0.63)
・ORR: Ⓐ 50% vs Ⓑ 32%
・DoR: Ⓐ 9.1 vs Ⓑ 6.1 mo
・TTF: Ⓐ 6.9 vs Ⓑ 4.5 mo; RR 0.58 (95% CI 0.47–0.70)
・OS: Ⓐ 25.1 vs Ⓑ 20.3 mo; RR 0.80 (95% CI 0.64–1.00); 1-yr death Ⓐ 22% vs Ⓑ 33%
・Subgroups: TTP improved in both strata — anthracycline/cyclophosphamide+trastuzumab 7.8 vs 6.1 mo, paclitaxel+trastuzumab 6.9 vs 3.0 mo; HER2 3+ benefited more than 2+
・Toxicity: Cardiac dysfunction with anthracycline+cyclophosphamide+trastuzumab Ⓐ 27% vs Ⓑ 8%, paclitaxel+trastuzumab Ⓐ 13% vs Ⓑ 1%; NYHA III/IV Ⓐ 16%; 1 cardiac death per anthracycline arm; trastuzumab stopped in Ⓐ 8% overall
・Limitations: Two thirds of Ⓑ crossed to open-label trastuzumab after progression, reducing the survival difference expected; cardiotoxicity from retrospective review

records.title: CLEOPATRA
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · First-line metastatic disease · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2012
records.body:
HER2-positive locally recurrent, unresectable or metastatic breast cancer; first-line, no prior chemotherapy or biologic therapy for metastatic disease (one prior hormonal treatment allowed); HER2 centrally confirmed by IHC 3+ or FISH amplification ratio ≥2.0; prior (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy ± trastuzumab allowed if ≥12 months before metastatic diagnosis; LVEF ≥50%; excluded CNS metastases, prior doxorubicin >360 mg/m² or LVEF decline to <50% on prior trastuzumab Ⓐ Placebo IV every 3 weeks
Ⓑ Pertuzumab 840 mg IV loading dose, then 420 mg IV every 3 weeks
・Trastuzumab: 8 mg/kg IV loading dose, then 6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks
・Docetaxel: 75 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks (increase to 100 mg/m² permitted); at least six cycles recommended
・Duration: Until disease progression or toxicity that could not be effectively managed; antibodies continued if docetaxel stopped for toxicity
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, investigator-assessed progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, safety, cardiac safety, time to symptom progression, biomarker associations with clinical outcomes Adding pertuzumab to trastuzumab plus docetaxel improved independently assessed PFS and overall survival, with the gain maintained after more than 8 years' median follow-up, in first-line HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer
・PFS: Ⓐ 12.4 vs Ⓑ 18.5 mo; HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.51–0.75)
・OS (end-of-study, descriptive): Ⓐ 40.8 vs Ⓑ 57.1 mo; HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.58–0.82); significance established at earlier analyses
・8-yr OS: Ⓑ 37% vs Ⓐ 23%
・OS sensitivity (final analysis, crossover): Censoring crossovers HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.52–0.78); excluding them Ⓐ 34.7 mo, HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.45–0.67)
・Investigator-assessed PFS (end-of-study): Ⓐ 12.4 vs Ⓑ 18.7 mo; HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.59–0.81); 8-yr landmark Ⓑ 16% vs Ⓐ 10%
・ORR: Ⓐ 69.3% vs Ⓑ 80.2%; difference 10.8 points (95% CI 4.2–17.5); now judged significant under testing hierarchy
・DoR (independent review): Ⓐ 12.5 vs Ⓑ 20.2 mo; extended by 7.7 mo
・Subgroups: OS generally consistent across subgroups; non-visceral disease HR 1.08 (95% CI 0.72–1.62); benefit consistent in PIK3CA wild-type and mutant tumours
・Prior (neo)adjuvant trastuzumab: PFS HR 0.75; OS Ⓑ 53.8 vs Ⓐ 46.6 mo, HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.51–1.43); post-hoc, small subgroup
・Long-term responders (post-hoc): Ⓑ 99 vs Ⓐ 53 on treatment and progression-free ≥35 mo; more with non-visceral, PIK3CA-wild-type disease
・Toxicity: G3-4 neutropenia (end-of-study) Ⓑ 49% vs Ⓐ 46%; G3 diarrhoea (end-of-study) Ⓑ 10% vs Ⓐ 5%; febrile neutropenia (primary cut) Ⓐ 7% vs Ⓑ 13%, Asia Ⓐ 12% vs Ⓑ 26%; AE deaths during treatment Ⓐ 3% vs Ⓑ 2%
・Cardiac safety: LV dysfunction (final analysis) Ⓐ 8.6% vs Ⓑ 6.6%; LVEF decline ≥10% to <50% Ⓐ 7.4% vs Ⓑ 6.1%, mostly reversible; since previous analysis one new CHF-suggestive SAE, one new symptomatic LVSD
・Limitations: Descriptive analyses with no formal statistical comparisons; crossover to pertuzumab unadjusted, likely conservative; CNS metastases excluded

records.title: HER2CLIMB-05
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · First-line metastatic disease · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Centrally confirmed HER2+ (2018 ASCO-CAP) unresectable locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer; first-line maintenance after 4-8 cycles of trastuzumab, pertuzumab and a taxane without progression; any known hormone receptor status; if recurrent, ≥6-month treatment-free interval from early-setting trastuzumab/pertuzumab; no or asymptomatic brain metastases on MRI; excludes prior HER2/EGFR TKI (extended adjuvant neratinib allowed if ≥12 months earlier), leptomeningeal disease Ⓐ Tucatinib 300 mg twice daily + trastuzumab + pertuzumab
Ⓑ Placebo twice daily + trastuzumab + pertuzumab
・Trastuzumab/pertuzumab: Trastuzumab 6 mg/kg IV or 600 mg SC + pertuzumab 420 mg IV, or SC fixed-dose trastuzumab 600 mg/pertuzumab 600 mg/hyaluronidase, every 21 days
・Endocrine therapy: Permitted for hormone receptor–positive disease
・Duration: Until unacceptable toxicity, disease progression, withdrawal of consent or study closure
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled; no crossover from placebo to tucatinib Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, progression-free survival by BICR, CNS-PFS, safety Adding tucatinib to trastuzumab–pertuzumab maintenance improved PFS vs placebo, with more grade ≥3 and hepatic toxicity
・PFS: Ⓐ 24.9 vs Ⓑ 16.3 mo; HR 0.641 (95% CI 0.514–0.799)
・PFS by BICR: Ⓐ 28.9 vs Ⓑ 16.0 mo; HR 0.654 (95% CI 0.517–0.828)
・OS: Immature at primary analysis; median not reached in either arm; HR 0.539 (95% CI 0.303–0.957)
・CNS-PFS: All patients HR 0.846 (95% CI 0.616–1.162); baseline BM Ⓐ 8.5 vs Ⓑ 4.3 mo, HR 0.719 (95% CI 0.406–1.273); preliminary
・Subgroups: Consistent benefit; hormone receptor–negative HR 0.554 (95% CI 0.403–0.761); positive HR 0.725 (95% CI 0.535–0.983)
・Toxicity: G≥3 TEAEs Ⓐ 42.3% vs Ⓑ 24.4%; G≥3 ALT rise Ⓐ 13.5% vs Ⓑ 0.6%; diarrhea Ⓐ 72.7% vs Ⓑ 51.2%; one grade 5 DILI with tucatinib
・Limitations: OS immature; excludes progression during induction; under half of hormone receptor–positive patients received ET

records.title: DESTINY-Breast09
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · First-line metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
HER2-positive advanced or metastatic breast cancer (centrally confirmed), first-line; no previous chemotherapy or HER2-directed therapy for metastatic disease; adjuvant or neoadjuvant chemotherapy allowed if disease-free interval more than 6 months (183 days); one previous line of endocrine monotherapy permitted in metastatic disease; clinically active CNS metastasis excluded Ⓐ Trastuzumab deruxtecan plus pertuzumab
Ⓑ Trastuzumab deruxtecan plus placebo
Ⓒ THP: paclitaxel or docetaxel (per physician choice) plus trastuzumab and pertuzumab
・Duration: Planned to continue until disease progression; in Ⓒ taxane for a minimum of six cycles or until unacceptable toxic effects, then trastuzumab plus pertuzumab
・HR-positive disease: Concurrent endocrine therapy (aromatase inhibitor or tamoxifen) after taxane discontinuation or six cycles of trastuzumab deruxtecan
・Design: Pertuzumab vs placebo blinded in the experimental arms; THP open-label, administered according to local institutional standards Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response, duration of response, safety Trastuzumab deruxtecan plus pertuzumab significantly lowered the risk of progression or death vs THP as first-line treatment of HER2-positive advanced or metastatic breast cancer
・PFS: Ⓐ 40.7 vs Ⓒ 26.9 mo; HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.44–0.71); prespecified interim analysis crossed the superiority boundary
・PFS, 24 mo: Ⓐ 70.1% vs Ⓒ 52.1%
・PFS, investigator: Ⓐ 40.7 vs Ⓒ 20.7 mo; HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.39–0.61)
・ORR: Ⓐ 85.1% vs Ⓒ 78.6% (OR 1.59, 95% CI 1.09–2.32); complete response Ⓐ 15.1% vs Ⓒ 8.5%
・DoR: Ⓐ 39.2 vs Ⓒ 26.4 mo
・Subgroups: Benefit across most subgroups; consistent regardless of hormone-receptor status and brain metastases (few such patients enrolled)
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 AEs Ⓐ 63.5% vs Ⓒ 62.3%; drug-related ILD/pneumonitis Ⓐ 12.1% (grade 5 in 2 patients) vs Ⓒ 1.0%; grade 5 AEs Ⓐ 3.4% vs Ⓒ 0.8%
・Limitations: Prespecified interim analysis (37.7% maturity), medians may evolve; partial open-label; Black patients underrepresented

records.title: PERUSE
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · First-line metastatic disease · Single-arm clinical trial (phase IIIb) · 2019
records.body:
HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or ISH-positive) locally recurrent/metastatic breast cancer not amenable to curative resection; first-line (no prior systemic therapy for LR/MBC except ≤2 lines of endocrine therapy); ECOG PS ≤2, LVEF ≥50%; CNS metastases eligible if stable ≥3 months after local therapy; excluded prior anti-HER2 beyond (neo)adjuvant trastuzumab/lapatinib, progression during such therapy, recurrence within 6 months of (neo)adjuvant non-hormonal therapy, grade ≥3 peripheral neuropathy (single-arm) Pertuzumab + trastuzumab + investigator-selected taxane (docetaxel, paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel; weekly or q3w per local prescribing information and/or recognised guidelines)
・Pertuzumab: 840 mg loading dose, then 420 mg q3w
・Trastuzumab: 8 mg/kg loading dose, then 6 mg/kg q3w
・Taxane switching: alternative taxane allowed during treatment
・Endocrine maintenance: approved endocrine maintenance therapy permitted after chemotherapy discontinuation
・Duration: until unacceptable toxicity, disease progression, withdrawal of consent or death Primary: safety. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall survival, overall response rate, clinical benefit rate, duration of response, time to response, patient-reported outcomes First-line pertuzumab plus trastuzumab and an investigator-chosen taxane showed safety and efficacy consistent with CLEOPATRA, median OS exceeding 5 years; single-arm, descriptive
・PFS: Median 20.7 mo (95% CI 18.9–23.1); final analysis, 5.7 years' median follow-up
・OS: Median 65.3 mo (95% CI 60.9–70.9); final analysis
・ORR: 79% (95% CI 77–82%) in measurable disease, final; confirmed complete response 15% (preliminary cut)
・DoR: Median 20.0 mo; clinical benefit rate 86%
・QoL: FACT-B almost unchanged from baseline; mean changes did not exceed meaningful thresholds
・Subgroups (initial taxane, final): PFS docetaxel 19.4, paclitaxel 23.2, nab-paclitaxel 19.2 mo; OS 66.5, 64.0, 70.9 mo; ORR 79%, 83%, 77% (preliminary cut)
・Subgroups: OS HR-positive 66.7 vs HR-negative 60.2 mo, PFS similar; post hoc, visceral disease plus prior trastuzumab PFS 13.1, OS 46.3 mo
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs 61%; G≥3 neutropenia 10% (docetaxel 15%, paclitaxel 5%, nab-paclitaxel 2%), diarrhoea 8%; G≥3 febrile neutropenia docetaxel 11%, paclitaxel 1%, nab-paclitaxel 0%; LVEF decline 6%; fatal AEs 2%; all-grade neuropathy paclitaxel 31% vs docetaxel 16% (preliminary cut)
・Limitations: Single-arm, open-label, all analyses descriptive; taxane and risk-factor subgroups exploratory, not randomised; progression criteria tightened before final analysis

records.title: JBCRG-M06/EMERALD
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · First-line metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
HER2-positive (histological diagnosis) locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer; first-line chemotherapy with dual HER2 blockade; age 20-70 years; no prior cytotoxic chemotherapy for LABC/MBC other than T-DM1; prior hormonal or anti-HER2 therapy for recurrent disease allowed Ⓐ Eribulin 1.4 mg/m² on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle
Ⓑ Physician-choice taxane: docetaxel 75 mg/m² on day 1 or paclitaxel 80 mg/m² on days 1, 8 and 15, per 21-day cycle
・Dual HER2 blockade: Trastuzumab plus pertuzumab in both arms
・Duration: Until disease progression, unmanageable toxicity, or consent withdrawal; recommended minimum six cycles Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, OS and PFS by ctDNA PIK3CA mutation status, OS and PFS by ctDNA HER2 amplification status Eribulin did not differ significantly from taxane in final overall survival with dual HER2 blockade; median OS exceeded 6 years in both arms
・PFS: Ⓐ 14.0 vs Ⓑ 12.9 mo; HR 0.95 (primary analysis; noninferiority confirmed)
・OS, final (≥5-yr follow-up): Ⓐ 78.5 vs Ⓑ NR mo; HR 1.25 (95% CI 0.92-1.71); 60-mo OS 59.7% vs 65.2%
・OS by ctDNA PIK3CAm+ vs −: 43.2 mo vs NR; 60-mo 38.5% vs 67.4%; no treatment interaction
・OS by ctDNA HER2 amp+ vs −: NR vs 65.3 mo; 60-mo 64.7% vs 54.9%; no treatment interaction

records.title: HEALER

records.body:
HER2-positive recurrent or metastatic breast cancer (IHC 3+ or IHC 2+ with in situ hybridization–positive status by central laboratory); first line, no previous chemotherapy or HER2-targeted therapy for advanced disease (one endocrine monotherapy line permitted); prior (neo)adjuvant chemo or HER2-targeted therapy only if progression >12 months after completion; LVEF ≥50% Ⓐ Anbenitamab 30 mg/kg IV + HB1801 (albumin-bound docetaxel) 100 mg/m² IV, day 1 of every 3-week cycle
Ⓑ Trastuzumab 8 mg/kg loading then 6 mg/kg maintenance + pertuzumab 840 mg loading then 420 mg maintenance + docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV, day 1 of every 3-week cycle
・Duration: Taxane for minimum of six cycles unless unacceptable side effects or progression; treatment until loss of clinical benefit, unacceptable side effects, withdrawal, or death
・Design: Open-label; hormone-receptor-positive patients received no endocrine therapy or CDK4/6 inhibitors Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival, overall survival, objective response, duration of response, safety, disease control Anbenitamab plus HB1801 significantly improved progression-free survival versus THP as first-line therapy in HER2-positive advanced breast cancer
・PFS (BICR, interim): Ⓐ 24-mo 58.5% vs Ⓑ 34.4%; HR 0.46 (95% CI 0.37–0.56); P<0.001; Ⓑ median 14.3 mo, follow-up 21.0 mo

・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 45.9% vs Ⓑ 34.4%; G≥3 neutropenia 13.1% vs 8.4%; fatal AEs 2 in each group (Ⓐ 1 sudden cardiac death)

records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · HR-positive / HER2-positive — endocrine-containing maintenance · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Hormone-receptor–positive (≥1% staining), HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or ISH-amplified) advanced breast cancer; first-line maintenance after four to eight cycles of trastuzumab-based induction (trastuzumab and pertuzumab plus taxane) without progression; no previous systemic therapy for metastatic disease beyond induction; disease-free interval ≥6 months after prior (neo)adjuvant anti-HER2 therapy; asymptomatic CNS metastases eligible; progression during induction excluded Ⓐ Palbociclib 125 mg orally once daily, 21 days on / 7 days off per 28-day cycle, added to anti-HER2 and endocrine therapy
Ⓑ Anti-HER2 and endocrine therapy alone (standard maintenance)
・Anti-HER2: Trastuzumab with or without pertuzumab, per standard guidelines
・Endocrine therapy: Aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant; ovarian suppression required if premenopausal
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxic effects, withdrawal of consent, or death
・Design: Open-label; randomised after four to eight cycles of induction therapy Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response, clinical benefit, overall survival, duration of confirmed response, safety Adding palbociclib to maintenance anti-HER2 and endocrine therapy improved progression-free survival over standard therapy, with increased toxicity mainly neutropenia
・PFS: Ⓐ 44.3 vs Ⓑ 29.1 mo; HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.59 to 0.96); final analysis at median follow-up 53.5 mo
・ORR: Ⓐ 32.9% vs Ⓑ 24.8%
・Clinical benefit: Ⓐ 88.9% vs Ⓑ 80.9%
・DoR: Ⓐ 44.9 vs Ⓑ 30.8 mo
・OS: Immature; HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.61 to 1.23); final analysis planned after 247 deaths
・Toxicity: G3 AEs Ⓐ 79.7% vs Ⓑ 30.6%; G3 neutropenia Ⓐ 55.9% vs Ⓑ 2.0%; G4 Ⓐ 10.0% vs Ⓑ 3.6%; no treatment-related deaths
・Limitations: Open-label; OS immature; excluded progression during induction (favorable-biology enrichment)

records.title: GeparSixto (GBG 66)
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin-based regimens) · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2014
records.body:
Women with previously untreated non-metastatic stage II–III triple-negative (oestrogen/progesterone receptor <1%, HER2-negative) or HER2-positive primary invasive breast cancer; neoadjuvant; Karnofsky 80 or greater with clinical T2–T4a-d tumours or T1c with clinical or histological N+; no previous chemotherapy or breast radiotherapy; excludes grade 2 or greater neuropathy, prior thromboembolic event Ⓐ Backbone + carboplatin AUC 1.5 weekly (AUC 2.0 for the first 329 patients)
Ⓑ Backbone alone, no carboplatin
・Backbone: Paclitaxel 80 mg/m² weekly + non-pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 20 mg/m² weekly for 18 weeks
・TNBC: + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks
・HER2-positive: + trastuzumab 8 mg/kg load then 6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks and lapatinib 750 mg orally daily
・Design: Open-label Primary: pathological complete response rate (ypT0 ypN0). Secondary: tolerability, treatment adherence, clinical response rate, pathological complete response rate (ypT0/is ypN0), pathological complete response rate (ypT0/is ypN0/+), ypN0 rate, regression grade, breast conservation rate, axillary conservation rate, disease-free survival, overall survival Adding carboplatin to neoadjuvant anthracycline–taxane plus targeted therapy increased pCR and, at final analysis, improved disease-free survival in triple-negative but not HER2-positive disease
・pCR (ypT0 ypN0): Ⓐ 43.7% vs Ⓑ 36.9%; OR 1.33 (95% CI 0.96–1.85); p=0.107, significant at prespecified α 0.2
・DFS (TNBC, final analysis, median follow-up 47.3 mo): 3-yr Ⓐ 86.1% vs Ⓑ 75.8%; HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.34–0.93)
・OS (TNBC, final analysis): 3-yr Ⓐ 91.9% vs Ⓑ 86.0%; HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.32–1.12), not significant
・HER2-positive survival: No DFS or OS benefit; Ⓐ vs Ⓑ HR 1.34 (95% CI 0.77–2.34) and 1.13 (95% CI 0.44–2.93)
・Secondary efficacy: No between-group differences; overall response Ⓐ 89.8% vs Ⓑ 89.4%
・Subgroups: TNBC pCR Ⓐ 53.2% vs Ⓑ 36.9% (p=0.005); HER2-positive Ⓐ 32.8% vs Ⓑ 36.8% (p=0.581); interaction p=0.015
・HRD (TNBC, exploratory, 193/315 measurable): HR deficiency predicted pCR (OR 2.60, 95% CI 1.26–5.37) and OS (HR 0.320, 95% CI 0.158–0.649)
・pCR by HRD status: HR-deficient Ⓐ 63.5% vs Ⓑ 33.9% (p=0.001); non-deficient Ⓐ 29.6% vs Ⓑ 20.0% (p=0.540); no interaction, p=0.327
・Germline BRCA pCR (TNBC, ypT0/is ypN0): Non-carriers Ⓐ 55% vs Ⓑ 36.4%, OR 2.14 (95% CI 1.28–3.58); carriers Ⓐ 65.4% vs Ⓑ 66.7%; interaction p=0.58
・Germline BRCA DFS (TNBC): Non-carriers Ⓐ 85.3% vs Ⓑ 73.5%, HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.29–0.96); carriers Ⓐ 86.3% vs Ⓑ 82.5%, not significant
・MGMT (TNBC, exploratory, 174/315 evaluable): 21.8% methylated; pCR 42.1% methylated vs 45.6% unmethylated, p=0.717
・MGMT, 3-yr survival: DFS 81.1% methylated vs 78.4% unmethylated, p=0.674; OS 88.6% both, p=1.000; no predictive value for carboplatin
・Toxicity: G3/4 neutropenia Ⓐ 65% vs Ⓑ 27%, anaemia 15% vs <1%, thrombocytopenia 14% vs <1%; discontinuations 48% vs 39%
・Fatal events: Ⓑ 4 (2 cardiac, 2 neutropenic) vs Ⓐ 1 (port-related sepsis)
・Limitations: Open-label; phase 2, not confirmatory, survival not powered a priori; HRD retrospective (193/315 measurable) and BRCA subgroups small (50 carriers)

records.title: CALGB 40603
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin-based regimens) · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2015
records.body:
Operable, biopsy-confirmed, previously untreated clinical stage II to III non-inflammatory invasive triple-negative breast cancer; neoadjuvant chemotherapy; ER and PgR expression <10% and HER2 IHC 0 to 1+ or FISH ratio <2.0; excluded grade ≥2 neuropathy and bevacizumab contraindications including uncontrolled hypertension Ⓐ wP → ddAC
Ⓑ wP → ddAC + bevacizumab
Ⓒ wP + carboplatin → ddAC
Ⓓ wP + carboplatin → ddAC + bevacizumab
・wP: Paclitaxel 80 mg/m² once per week × 12
・ddAC: Doxorubicin 60 mg/m² plus cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² once every 2 weeks × 4 with myeloid growth factor support
・Carboplatin (Ⓒ, Ⓓ): AUC 6 once every 3 weeks × 4, concurrent with wP
・Bevacizumab (Ⓑ, Ⓓ): 10 mg/kg once every 2 weeks × 9, during wP and first three ddAC cycles
・Design: 2 × 2 factorial, open-label; surgery after NACT, radiotherapy and any adjuvant therapy at physician discretion Primary: pCR breast (ypT0/is), pCR in genomically defined basal-like tumors (coprimary). Secondary: pCR breast/axilla (ypT0/isN0), treatment delivery, treatment-related toxicities, residual cancer burden (RCB), conversion from clinically node-positive to pathologically node-negative status, conversion from BCS-ineligible to BCS-eligible status, relapse-free survival, time to first failure, overall survival, event-free survival, distant recurrence-free interval Adding carboplatin or bevacizumab to neoadjuvant wP→ddAC significantly increased pCR breast, but neither appeared to improve long-term outcomes at 7.9-year median follow-up
・pCR breast, +carbo: Ⓒ+Ⓓ 60% vs Ⓐ+Ⓑ 46%; OR 1.76, one-sided P = .0018
・pCR breast, +bev: Ⓑ+Ⓓ 59% vs Ⓐ+Ⓒ 48%; OR 1.58, one-sided P = .0089
・pCR breast/axilla, +carbo: Ⓒ+Ⓓ 54% vs Ⓐ+Ⓑ 41%; OR 1.71, one-sided P = .0029
・pCR breast/axilla, +bev: Ⓑ+Ⓓ 52% vs Ⓐ+Ⓒ 44%; OR 1.36, one-sided P = .057
・pCR, basal-like (coprimary): Significantly increased by either agent; EFS not improved
・Interaction: No more-than-additive carbo–bev effect on pCR breast (P = .52) or pCR breast/axilla (P = .43)
・5-yr EFS, +carbo: Ⓒ+Ⓓ 70.4% vs Ⓐ+Ⓑ 70.1%; HR 0.94 (95% CI 0.67–1.32)
・5-yr EFS, +bev: Ⓑ+Ⓓ 70.9% vs Ⓐ+Ⓒ 69.6%; HR 0.92 (95% CI 0.66–1.29)
・OS: Not improved with either agent (+carbo HR 1.12, 95% CI 0.77–1.61; +bev HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.67–1.40)
・pCR vs RD: 5-yr EFS 85.5% vs 56.6%; HR 0.29 (95% CI 0.19–0.42); 5-yr OS 87.9% vs 63.4%
・Residual disease: Any RD, even RCB-I, worse EFS than pCR (RCB-I HR 2.49, 95% CI 1.46–4.25)
・Delivery: All four carbo doses in 80% (Ⓒ+Ⓓ); ≥8 of 9 bev doses in 66% (Ⓑ+Ⓓ); wP/ddAC dose reductions more frequent with either agent; multiple wP doses missed 35% vs 15% with carbo
・Subgroups: No patient subset showed improved EFS or OS with either agent
・Exploratory, ≥11 wP doses: +carbo pCR Ⓒ+Ⓓ 61% vs Ⓐ+Ⓑ 41%; 5-yr EFS Ⓒ+Ⓓ 78.5% vs Ⓐ+Ⓑ 72%; HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.44–1.06)
・Immune correlates, exploratory: TILs and immune gene signatures associated with higher pCR and improved EFS; only multigene signatures independently prognostic
・Toxicity: Carbo raised G3–4 neutropenia (Ⓒ 56%, Ⓓ 67% vs Ⓐ 22%, Ⓑ 27%) and thrombocytopenia; bev grade 3 hypertension 10–12% vs 0–2%, only on-study death, more postoperative complications (9% vs 5%)
・Limitations: Underpowered for LTOs (135 events vs 1,381 needed); postsurgery systemic therapy not collected; open-label

records.title: BrighTNess
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin-based regimens) · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body:
Invasive triple-negative breast cancer (oestrogen/progesterone receptor <1%, HER2 0–1+ or no amplification); clinical stage II–III (T1N1–2 or T2–4N0–2); previously untreated neoadjuvant candidates for potentially curative surgery; documented gBRCA mutation testing required, any BRCA status eligible; excluded previous anti-cancer treatment, pre-existing neuropathy, previous or concurrent cancer Ⓐ Paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV weekly for 12 doses + carboplatin AUC 6 mg/mL per min IV every 3 weeks for four cycles + veliparib 50 mg orally twice daily
Ⓑ Paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV weekly for 12 doses + carboplatin AUC 6 mg/mL per min IV every 3 weeks for four cycles + veliparib placebo twice daily
Ⓒ Paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV weekly for 12 doses + carboplatin placebo IV every 3 weeks for four cycles + veliparib placebo twice daily
・AC (all patients, segment 2): Doxorubicin 60 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² IV every 2 or 3 weeks for four cycles
・Duration: Segment 1 maximum 16 weeks; stop for progression, alternative anti-cancer agents, surgery or radiotherapy, pregnancy, or investigator discretion
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled Primary: pathological complete response. Secondary: event-free survival, overall survival, suitability for breast-conservation surgery, clinical breast tumour response, minimal residual disease, ECOG performance status, quality of life, safety, second malignancies, MDS/AML Adding carboplatin improved pCR and was associated with long-term EFS benefit without increasing second malignancies; veliparib added no pCR or EFS benefit
・pCR, Ⓐ vs Ⓒ (co-primary): 53% vs 31%; risk difference 22·2 (95% CI 13·1 to 31·2), p<0·0001
・pCR, Ⓐ vs Ⓑ (co-primary): 53% vs 58%; risk difference –4·3 (95% CI –13·8 to 5·1), p=0·36
・pCR, Ⓑ vs Ⓒ: 58% vs 31%; risk difference 26·5 (95% CI 16·0 to 37·0), post-hoc exploratory
・EFS (final, median 4.5-yr follow-up): Ⓐ vs Ⓒ HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.43-0.92), nominal p=0.02; Ⓐ vs Ⓑ HR 1.12 (0.72-1.72)
・EFS, Ⓑ vs Ⓒ (post hoc): HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.36-0.91); 4-yr EFS Ⓐ 78% vs Ⓑ 79% vs Ⓒ 69%
・OS: No significant differences; Ⓐ vs Ⓒ HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.48-1.38), Ⓐ vs Ⓑ 1.25 (0.70-2.24), Ⓑ vs Ⓒ 0.63 (0.33-1.21); events few
・RCB 0/1: Ⓐ 68% vs Ⓑ 70% vs Ⓒ 47%
・Breast-conservation eligibility: Ⓐ 62% vs Ⓑ 44% vs Ⓒ 44% (baseline-unsuitable subset)
・pCR–EFS: pCR vs non-pCR HR 0.26 (95% CI 0.18-0.38); gBRCA mutant 0.14, wildtype 0.29
・Subgroups: No subgroup attained higher pCR with Ⓐ than Ⓑ (interactions not tested); no subgroup gained EFS from veliparib
・Toxicity: Grade 3/4 TEAEs Ⓐ 71% vs Ⓑ 68% vs Ⓒ 15%; febrile neutropenia during AC Ⓐ 18% vs Ⓑ 17% vs Ⓒ 5%; one fatal sudden death (Ⓐ)
・Second malignancies (≥4-yr): MDS Ⓐ 2% vs Ⓑ 2% vs Ⓒ 1%; non-breast cancers Ⓐ 2% vs Ⓑ 4% vs Ⓒ 3%; not increased by carboplatin or veliparib
・Limitations: EFS/OS descriptive with nominal p values after missed Ⓐ vs Ⓑ co-primary, not powered for EFS/OS (OS follow-up inadequate); Ⓑ vs Ⓒ post hoc; QoL not analysed

records.title: Gupta et al. (TMC)
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin-based regimens) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Previously untreated triple-negative (ER-, PR-, HER2-negative) invasive breast cancer; large operable (clinical T3 and N1) or locally advanced (any T4 or any N2-3) nonmetastatic disease; neoadjuvant chemotherapy; age 18-70 years; adequate renal, hepatic and cardiac function, fit for anthracycline-taxane chemotherapy Ⓐ Carboplatin AUC-2 IV once per week plus paclitaxel for 8 weeks → anthracycline-cyclophosphamide for four cycles
Ⓑ Paclitaxel alone for 8 weeks → anthracycline-cyclophosphamide for four cycles
・Chemotherapy: Paclitaxel 100 mg/m² IV once per week for 8 weeks; doxorubicin 60 mg/m² or epirubicin 90 mg/m² plus cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² IV once every 3 weeks for four cycles
・Design: Open-label; surgery within 6 weeks of last cycle, then adjuvant radiotherapy Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, pathologic complete response, toxicity, distant disease-free survival Adding weekly carboplatin did not significantly improve EFS but improved OS and pCR, with benefit confined to premenopausal patients
・EFS: Ⓐ 5-yr 70.7% vs Ⓑ 64.1%; HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.62–1.03)
・OS: Ⓐ 5-yr 74.4% vs Ⓑ 66.8%; HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.57–0.97), nominal
・pCR: Ⓐ 54.5% vs Ⓑ 40.3%, nominal P<.001
・DDFS: Ⓐ 5-yr 72.2% vs Ⓑ 65.4%; HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.600–1.015)
・Subgroups: Premenopausal EFS HR 0.61 (0.43–0.84) and OS HR 0.57 (0.40–0.82); postmenopausal no benefit; significant menopausal interaction
・Toxicity: G≥3 neutropenia Ⓐ 8.6% vs Ⓑ 2.0%; febrile neutropenia 4.4% vs 2.8%; nonhematologic toxicities not different
・Limitations: Open-label, single centre; primary analysis conducted early, before planned events; capecitabine and pembrolizumab not used

records.title: KEYNOTE-522
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body:
Triple-negative breast cancer, centrally confirmed in all foci; previously untreated, nonmetastatic stage II or III (T1c N1-2 or T2-4 N0-2, AJCC 7th edition), neoadjuvant setting; enrolled regardless of PD-L1 status; ECOG 0 or 1; bilateral, multifocal and inflammatory cancers eligible; excluded active autoimmune disease treated systemically within 2 years, immunodeficiency, HIV, prior pneumonitis requiring glucocorticoids Ⓐ Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks: 4 cycles with paclitaxel–carboplatin → 4 cycles with AC/EC → after surgery, adjuvant pembrolizumab every 3 weeks for up to 9 cycles
Ⓑ Placebo every 3 weeks: 4 cycles with paclitaxel–carboplatin → 4 cycles with AC/EC → after surgery, adjuvant placebo every 3 weeks for up to 9 cycles
・Chemotherapy: Paclitaxel 80 mg/m² weekly + carboplatin AUC 5 every 3 weeks or AUC 1.5 weekly (12 weeks) → doxorubicin 60 mg/m² or epirubicin 90 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² every 3 weeks (12 weeks)
・Surgery: Definitive surgery 3 to 6 weeks after the neoadjuvant phase; adjuvant radiotherapy as indicated; adjuvant capecitabine not allowed
・Duration: Until progression, recurrence or unacceptable toxicity, within the fixed cycles
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled Primary: pathological complete response (ypT0/Tis ypN0), event-free survival. Secondary: pathological complete response (ypT0 ypN0), pathological complete response (ypT0/Tis), pathological complete response by all definitions in PD-L1–positive tumours, event-free survival in PD-L1–positive tumours, overall survival, overall survival in PD-L1–positive tumours, distant progression–free or distant recurrence–free survival, residual cancer burden, safety Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy followed by adjuvant pembrolizumab significantly improved overall survival and event-free survival vs neoadjuvant chemotherapy alone in early triple-negative breast cancer
・EFS, 5-yr (seventh interim, descriptive): Ⓐ 81.2% vs Ⓑ 72.2%; HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.51–0.83); median follow-up 75.1 mo
・EFS, fourth interim (formal test): 36-mo Ⓐ 84.5% vs Ⓑ 76.8%; HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.48–0.82); P<0.001; median follow-up 39.1 mo; medians not reached
・pCR (ypT0/Tis ypN0): Ⓐ 64.8% vs Ⓑ 51.2%; difference 13.6 percentage points (95% CI 5.4–21.8); first interim, first 602 patients
・pCR, other definitions: Consistent results with ypT0 ypN0 and ypT0/Tis
・OS, final: 5-yr Ⓐ 86.6% vs Ⓑ 81.7% (95% CI 84.0–88.8 vs 77.5–85.2); difference 4.9 percentage points (95% CI 0.3–9.4); P=0.002; median follow-up 75.1 mo
・OS, piecewise HR: 0.87 (95% CI 0.57–1.32) before 2-yr follow-up, 0.51 (95% CI 0.35–0.75) afterwards
・Distant DFS (exploratory): HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.46–0.82), pembrolizumab vs placebo
・Distant recurrence, first EFS event: Ⓐ 9.8% vs Ⓑ 14.4%
・EFS by pCR status (exploratory, nonrandomized): Ⓐ lower event risk regardless of pCR; without pCR events 33.1% vs 44.5%, HR 0.70 (0.52–0.95)
・OS by pCR status (exploratory, nonrandomized): Ⓐ lower death risk regardless of pCR; without pCR deaths 30.4% vs 39.3%, 5-yr difference 6.1 percentage points (95% CI −2.7 to 14.9)
・RCB distribution (exploratory, 39.1-mo cut): Ⓐ shifted patients into lower RCB categories vs Ⓑ; RCB-0 (pCR) 63.4% vs 56.2%
・EFS by RCB category (exploratory, nonrandomized): Benefit in RCB-0/1/2, greatest in RCB-2; 36-mo Ⓐ 75.7% vs Ⓑ 55.9%, HR 0.52 (95% CI 0.32–0.82); RCB-3 no benefit, HR 1.24 (0.69–2.23)
・First EFS events by RCB: Distant recurrence most common, fewer with Ⓐ across all categories; RCB-0/1 distant recurrences mostly CNS (55.3%); RCB-3 local recurrence Ⓐ 25.0% vs Ⓑ 7.7%
・EFS by chemo exposure (post hoc): Ⓐ EFS benefit with full chemotherapy, HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.47–0.89), and less-than-full chemotherapy, HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.32–0.89)
・Subgroups, pCR: Benefit generally consistent; PD-L1–positive Ⓐ 68.9% vs Ⓑ 54.9%; PD-L1–negative Ⓐ 45.3% vs Ⓑ 30.3%
・Subgroups, EFS: Benefit consistent across all prespecified subgroups, including PD-L1 expression and nodal involvement
・Subgroups, OS: Benefit regardless of PD-L1 expression, across nodal-status and tumor-size subgroups; exploratory, underpowered
・Toxicity, combined phases: G≥3 TRAEs Ⓐ 77.1% vs Ⓑ 73.3%; serious TRAEs Ⓐ 34.1% vs Ⓑ 20.1%; G≥3 immune-mediated AEs Ⓐ 13.0% vs Ⓑ 1.5%; discontinuation for TRAEs Ⓐ 27.7% vs Ⓑ 14.1%; TRAE deaths Ⓐ 4 (0.5%) vs Ⓑ 1 (0.3%), immune-mediated deaths Ⓐ 2 (0.3%) vs Ⓑ 0
・Limitations: Neoadjuvant vs adjuvant phase contributions not separable; adjuvant capecitabine not allowed; subgroup and RCB analyses exploratory, nonrandomized, no alpha assigned (descriptive only)

records.title: NeoPACT
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2024
records.body:
Stage I (tumor >1 cm), II or III TNBC (ER and PR staining 10% or less, HER2-negative per 2018 ASCO/CAP guideline); neoadjuvant, no prior systemic chemotherapy or immunotherapy and no breast surgery; women aged 18-70, ECOG 0-1; suspicious axillary nodes required histologic confirmation; excluded inflammatory breast cancer, ejection fraction <50%, grade >2 neuropathy, autoimmune disease needing systemic treatment within 2 years, active hepatitis B/C, HIV (single-arm) Pembrolizumab 200 mg plus carboplatin AUC 6 and docetaxel 75 mg/m² every 21 days for 6 cycles
・Design: Open-label single-group at 2 sites; breast surgery after neoadjuvant therapy, adjuvant chemotherapy/immunotherapy at physician discretion Primary: pathologic complete response. Secondary: residual cancer burden, event-free survival, toxicity, immune biomarkers, overall survival Anthracycline-free neoadjuvant pembrolizumab, carboplatin and docetaxel showed activity in stage I-III TNBC, with pCR 58% and 3-year EFS 86%
・pCR: 58%; RCB 0+1: 69% (among 111 pathologic-evaluable)
・3-yr EFS: 86% overall; 98% with pCR vs 68% with residual disease; median follow-up 27.4 mo
・3-yr OS: 89%
・Biomarkers: sTILs, PD-L1, DDIR and TIM each independently predictive of pCR; pCR exceeded 70% in biomarker-positive subgroups
・Subgroups: pCR 69% stage I, 58% stage II, 43% stage III
・Toxicity: G≥3 TRAEs 26.9%; G≥3 iAEs 3.5%; 1 study-related death (myocardial infarction); any-drug discontinuation 12%
・Limitations: Single-group historical-control design; pCR gain 8% missed 15% target; stage I and low ER/PR (1%-10%) patients included

records.title: GeparNuevo
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase II) · 2019
records.body:
Previously untreated uni- or bilateral primary non-metastatic invasive triple-negative breast cancer (ER <1%, PR <10%, HER2 IHC 0/1 or 2+ with ISH ratio <2.0 or <6 copies), cT1b-cT4a-d with centrally confirmed TNBC and sTILs on core biopsy; excluded autoimmune disease, inflammatory bowel disease, hepatitis B/C, HIV, thyroid dysfunction; LVEF ≥55% required Ⓐ Durvalumab 0.75 g IV once 2 weeks before chemotherapy (window phase), then durvalumab 1.5 g IV every 4 weeks with nab-paclitaxel and with EC
Ⓑ Placebo on the same schedule
・Nab-paclitaxel: 125 mg/m² weekly for 12 weeks
・EC: Dose-dense epirubicin/cyclophosphamide every 2 weeks for 4 cycles
・Design: Double-blind; window phase stopped after 117 patients by amendment, subsequent patients started durvalumab/placebo plus chemotherapy on day 1 Primary: pathological complete response rate (ypT0 ypN0). Secondary: pCR by other definitions (ypT0/is ypN0, ypT0/is ypN0/+, ypN0), clinical and imaging response, breast-conserving surgery rate, axillary lymph node dissection rate, subgroup efficacy (sTILs, PD-L1 status, window vs no window, BC stage, grading, age), tolerability, treatment adherence, invasive disease-free survival, distant disease-free survival, overall survival Adding durvalumab to nab-paclitaxel-EC did not significantly increase pCR but improved long-term iDFS, DDFS and OS irrespective of pCR, without adjuvant checkpoint-inhibition continuation
・pCR (ypT0 ypN0): Ⓐ 53.4% vs Ⓑ 44.2%; OR 1.45 (95% CI 0.80–2.63)
・iDFS: Ⓐ 7-yr 73.7% vs Ⓑ 60.7%; HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.32–0.99); median follow-up 86.4 mo
・DDFS: Ⓐ 7-yr 81.6% vs Ⓑ 62.9%; HR 0.41 (95% CI 0.21–0.80)
・OS: Ⓐ 7-yr 91.6% vs Ⓑ 74.7%; HR 0.33 (95% CI 0.14–0.79)
・Secondary pCR/surgery: Other pCR definitions consistent; no significant difference in breast-conserving surgery, axillary dissection or clinical response
・Subgroups: Window cohort pCR Ⓐ 61.0% vs Ⓑ 41.4%, OR 2.22 (95% CI 1.06–4.64; interaction P 0.048); non-window Ⓐ 37.9% vs Ⓑ 50.0%; nodal involvement iDFS HR 0.33 (95% CI 0.144–0.771), interaction P 0.045
・Biomarkers: sTILs predicted pCR in both arms; iTILs increase over window predicted durvalumab pCR (OR 5.15, 95% CI 1.10–24.05)
・sTILs in residual disease: Post hoc 7-yr iDFS 92.3% (high >10%) vs 51.4% (low ≤10%), assessable in 39/71 without pCR
・Toxicity: Thyroid dysfunction any grade Ⓐ 50.0% vs Ⓑ 43.9%; hyperthyroidism Ⓐ 9.8% vs Ⓑ 1.2%; SAEs Ⓐ 30 vs Ⓑ 29; no deaths
・Limitations: Phase II hypothesis-generating (update two-sided α .05, no multiple-comparison adjustment); iDFS gain not significant after pCR adjustment; window vs non-window cohorts small

records.title: CREATE-X (JBCRG-04)

records.body:

records.title: IMpassion130
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — first-line chemoimmunotherapy (PD-L1-positive) · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body:
Metastatic or unresectable locally advanced triple-negative (hormone-receptor–negative, HER2-negative) breast cancer; first-line, no prior chemotherapy or targeted therapy for metastatic disease; tumour specimen for central PD-L1 (SP142) testing; (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy (incl. taxanes) allowed if completed ≥12 months before randomization; excluded untreated CNS disease (treated asymptomatic CNS metastases permitted), autoimmune disease, prior checkpoint therapy and systemic glucocorticoids Ⓐ Atezolizumab 840 mg IV days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle
Ⓑ Placebo IV days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle
・Nab-paclitaxel: 100 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle, both arms
・Duration: Until progression or unacceptable toxic effects; nab-paclitaxel six cycles or more absent toxic effects
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, time to deterioration in global health status (EORTC QLQ-C30), safety Atezolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel prolonged progression-free survival; final overall survival did not significantly improve in the ITT population, with clinically meaningful exploratory OS benefit in PD-L1 IC-positive disease

・PFS, PD-L1+ (second-interim update): Ⓐ 7.5 vs Ⓑ 5.3 mo; HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.50–0.80)
・OS, final analysis: Ⓐ 21.0 vs Ⓑ 18.7 mo; HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.75–1.02); P=0.077
・OS, PD-L1+ (exploratory, not formally tested), final: Ⓐ 25.4 vs Ⓑ 17.9 mo; HR 0.67 (95% CI 0.53–0.86)
・36-mo OS, PD-L1+, final: Ⓐ 35.8% vs Ⓑ 22.2%
・ORR: Ⓐ 56.0% vs Ⓑ 45.9%; CR Ⓐ 7.1% vs Ⓑ 1.6%

records.title: KEYNOTE-355
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — first-line chemoimmunotherapy (PD-L1-positive) · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body:
Previously untreated locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, centrally confirmed; first-line; eligible regardless of PD-L1 status, with tumour sample required for central CPS testing; prior early-stage disease allowed if ≥6 months from curative treatment to recurrence, or ≥12 months if same chemotherapy class reused; excluded prior anti–PD-1/PD-L1 therapy, active autoimmune disease, active CNS metastases or carcinomatous meningitis Ⓐ Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks plus investigator's-choice chemotherapy
Ⓑ Saline placebo IV every 3 weeks plus the same chemotherapy options
・Chemotherapy: Nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m² days 1, 8, 15 every 28 days; paclitaxel 90 mg/m² days 1, 8, 15 every 28 days; or gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² plus carboplatin AUC 2 days 1, 8 every 21 days
・Duration: Pembrolizumab or placebo up to 35 administrations (chemotherapy continued at investigator's discretion), until confirmed progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent, or physician decision
・Design: Double-blind for pembrolizumab vs saline placebo; chemotherapy open-label Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival (dual primary, each assessed in PD-L1 CPS ≥10, CPS ≥1 and intention-to-treat populations). Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, disease control rate, safety Pembrolizumab–chemotherapy improved progression-free and overall survival versus placebo–chemotherapy in PD-L1 CPS ≥10 advanced triple-negative breast cancer (PFS at interim, OS at final analysis)
・PFS, CPS≥10: Ⓐ 9.7 vs Ⓑ 5.6 mo; HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.50–0.88), 44.1-mo descriptive update; interim criterion met
・PFS, CPS≥1: Ⓐ 7.6 vs Ⓑ 5.6 mo; HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.62–0.91), 44.1-mo descriptive update; interim boundary not met
・PFS, ITT: Ⓐ 7.5 vs Ⓑ 5.6 mo; HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.70–0.98), 44.1-mo descriptive update
・OS, CPS≥10: Ⓐ 23.0 vs Ⓑ 16.1 mo; HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.55–0.95); two-sided p=0.0185 met final criterion
・OS, CPS≥1: Ⓐ 17.6 vs Ⓑ 16.0 mo; HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.72–1.04); two-sided p=0.1125, criterion not met
・OS, ITT: Ⓐ 17.2 vs Ⓑ 15.5 mo; HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.76–1.05); not tested per multiplicity strategy
・ORR/DoR, CPS≥10: Ⓐ 52.7% vs Ⓑ 40.8%; median DoR 12.8 vs 7.3 mo
・Subgroups: OS effect rose with PD-L1 (CPS<1 HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.72–1.32; CPS 1–9 HR 1.09, 0.85–1.40; CPS≥20 HR 0.72, 0.51–1.01)
・Toxicity: Grade 3–5 regimen-related AEs Ⓐ 68.1% vs Ⓑ 66.9%; immune-mediated AEs 26.5% vs 6.4% (grade 3/4 5.3% vs 0); related deaths 0.4% vs 0
・Limitations: Benefit established only in CPS≥10; CPS≥10 endpoints amended after enrolment; exploratory subgroups underpowered

・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxic effects, withdrawal from the trial, or death, whichever occurred first
・Design: Open-label Primary: progression-free survival (blinded independent central review). Secondary: overall survival, progression-free survival (investigator assessment), objective response, duration of response, time to response, safety Sacituzumab govitecan improved progression-free and overall survival versus single-agent chemotherapy in relapsed or refractory metastatic triple-negative breast cancer

・DoR: Ⓐ 6.3 vs Ⓑ 3.6 mo

・QoL: Global health status did not decline over 12 months on either arm; differences not clinically significant
・Subgroups: IDFS, DDFS, OS benefit consistent across BRCA1 vs BRCA2, hormone-receptor status, prior platinum, NACT vs ACT; no heterogeneity; high-risk HR-positive included
・New primaries: Ⓐ 4.9% vs Ⓑ 7.5%; fewer new breast and ovarian/fallopian tube cancers on Ⓐ; CIBC HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.52–1.32); pancreatic cancers not fewer (three vs one)
・Toxicity: On-treatment AEs unchanged since IA2 (G≥3 Ⓐ 24.5% vs Ⓑ 11.3%; G≥3 anemia Ⓐ 8.7%; discontinuations Ⓐ 10.8% vs Ⓑ 4.6%); to IA3 MDS/AML Ⓐ 0.4% vs Ⓑ 0.7%, pneumonitis Ⓐ 1.0% vs Ⓑ 1.4%, fatal AEs Ⓐ 0.5% vs Ⓑ 1.1%; no AESI more frequent on Ⓐ
・Limitations: IA3 estimates descriptive, no formal testing (boundaries crossed at IA1/IA2); no direct comparison with adjuvant capecitabine; blinded follow-up planned to 2029

records.title: TNT (CRUK/07/012)
records.subtitle: BRCA · Advanced disease · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body:
Advanced breast cancer (metastatic or recurrent locally advanced), measurable and unsuitable for local therapy; triple-negative (ER and PgR Allred <3 or H-score <10; HER2 IHC 0 or 1+ or no amplification) or any ER/PgR/HER2 status with known germline BRCA1/2 mutation; fit to receive carboplatin or docetaxel Ⓐ Carboplatin AUC 6 day 1 every 3 weeks
Ⓑ Docetaxel 100 mg/m² day 1 every 3 weeks
・Duration: Six cycles; a further two cycles allowed for responders tolerating treatment, per local policy
・Design: Open-label Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall survival, response to crossover treatment, tolerability, safety, objective response rate in prespecified biomarker subgroups Carboplatin was not more active than docetaxel in unselected advanced TNBC; germline BRCA1/2 carriers had double the ORR with carboplatin (prespecified subgroup)
・ORR: Ⓐ 31.4% vs Ⓑ 34.0%; difference −2.6% (95% CI −12.1 to 6.9)
・PFS: Median Ⓐ 3.1 vs Ⓑ 4.4 mo; restricted mean difference −0.30 mo (95% CI −1.00 to 0.40)
・OS: Median Ⓐ 12.8 vs Ⓑ 12.0 mo; restricted mean difference −0.03 mo; P = 0.96
・Subgroups: Germline BRCA1/2 ORR Ⓐ 68% vs Ⓑ 33.3% (interaction P = 0.01); PAM50 non-basal ORR Ⓐ 16.7% vs Ⓑ 72.2% (interaction P = 0.003); no carboplatin advantage with BRCA1 methylation, BRCA1 mRNA-low or high HRD score
・Toxicity: More grade 3 and 4 AEs with docetaxel; SAEs Ⓐ 102 vs Ⓑ 174; one death possibly carboplatin-related (pulmonary embolism)
・Limitations: Open-label; fixed-duration chemotherapy, not to progression; OS confounded by crossover at progression; small biomarker subgroups

records.title: EMBRACA
records.subtitle: BRCA · Advanced disease · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body:
Advanced breast cancer (locally advanced not amenable to curative therapy or metastatic) with a deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA1/2 mutation (central BRACAnalysis); no more than three prior cytotoxic regimens for advanced disease and prior taxane and/or anthracycline unless contraindicated; HER2-positive excluded; platinum only if no RECIST progression within ~8 weeks of last dose and ≥6-month disease-free interval after (neo)adjuvant platinum Ⓐ Talazoparib 1 mg orally once daily continuously
Ⓑ Physician's-choice single-agent chemotherapy: capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, or vinorelbine in continuous 21-day cycles per institutional dose guidelines
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxic effects, withdrawal of consent, or physician decision to end treatment
・Design: Open-label; standard-therapy drug chosen before randomization Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, clinical benefit rate at 24 weeks, duration of response, safety, EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC QLQ-BR23 Talazoparib improved progression-free survival over physician's-choice single-agent chemotherapy in advanced breast cancer with a germline BRCA1/2 mutation; final overall survival was not significantly improved
・PFS: Ⓐ 8.6 vs Ⓑ 5.6 mo; HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.41–0.71)
・OS, final: Ⓐ 19.3 vs Ⓑ 19.5 mo; HR 0.848 (95% CI 0.670–1.073); not significant
・OS, RPSFTM-adjusted for subsequent PARP inhibitor/platinum: Ⓐ 19.3 vs Ⓑ 17.4 mo; HR 0.756 (95% bootstrap CI 0.503–1.029)
・ORR: Ⓐ 62.6% vs Ⓑ 27.2%; OR 5.0 (95% CI 2.9–8.8)
・CBR at 24 wk: Ⓐ 68.6% vs Ⓑ 36.1%; OR 4.3 (95% CI 2.7–6.8)
・DoR: Ⓐ 5.4 vs Ⓑ 3.1 mo
・QoL, extended follow-up: GHS/QoL change Ⓐ 2.1 vs Ⓑ −5.7 (P=0.001); breast symptoms Ⓐ −4.9 vs Ⓑ 0.1 (P=0.009); not adjusted for multiplicity
・TTD: Delayed with Ⓐ for GHS/QoL (HR 0.385, 95% CI 0.264–0.563) and breast symptoms (HR 0.347, 95% CI 0.177–0.680)
・Subgroups: PFS favored Ⓐ in all clinically relevant subgroups; prior platinum the only 95% CI crossing 1.0; final OS generally consistent across subgroups
・Toxicity: G3–4 AEs Ⓐ 69.6% vs Ⓑ 64.3%; G3–4 hematologic Ⓐ 56.6% vs Ⓑ 38.9%; G3–4 anemia Ⓐ 40.2% vs Ⓑ 4.8%; transfusion Ⓐ 39.2% vs Ⓑ 5.6%; AML one case each; primary report: G3 nonhematologic 32% vs 38%, one drug-related death each (veno-occlusive disease vs sepsis)
・Limitations: Open-label; platinum not available in the standard-therapy arm; OS possibly confounded by subsequent PARP inhibitor (Ⓐ 4.5% vs Ⓑ 32.6%) and platinum
