records.title: OlympiAD
records.subtitle: BRCA · Advanced disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body:
HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer (hormone-receptor-positive or triple-negative) with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutation; no more than two chemotherapy regimens for metastatic disease; prior anthracycline unless contraindicated and taxane; hormone-receptor-positive disease required prior endocrine therapy with progression; platinum allowed only if at least 12 months since last adjuvant/neoadjuvant dose or no progression on metastatic platinum Ⓐ Olaparib 300 mg orally twice daily
Ⓑ Standard therapy: single-agent chemotherapy of physician's choice — capecitabine 2500 mg per square meter orally daily (divided into two doses) for 14 days every 21 days, eribulin mesylate 1.4 mg per square meter IV on days 1 and 8 every 21 days, or vinorelbine 30 mg per square meter IV on days 1 and 8 every 21 days
・Duration: Until disease progression or unacceptable toxic effects
・Design: Open-label; multicenter, international Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, time to a second progression event or death, objective response rate, health-related quality of life (QLQ-C30), safety, complete response rate, duration of response Olaparib significantly prolonged progression-free survival versus standard single-agent chemotherapy in HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer with a germline BRCA mutation; final analysis showed no significant overall survival improvement; exploratory biomarker analysis showed olaparib activity regardless of HRD score or gsLOH status
・PFS: Ⓐ 7.0 vs Ⓑ 4.2 mo; HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.43 to 0.80)
・Time to second progression or death: Ⓐ 13.2 vs Ⓑ 9.3 mo; HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.40 to 0.83)
・OS, final analysis (64% maturity): Ⓐ 19.3 vs Ⓑ 17.1 mo; HR 0.90 (95% CI 0.66 to 1.23); no significant difference
・ORR: Ⓐ 59.9% vs Ⓑ 28.8%
・DoR, final cut-off (investigator-assessed): Ⓐ 6.9 vs Ⓑ 4.5 mo
・QoL: QLQ-C30 adjusted mean change Ⓐ 3.9 vs Ⓑ −3.6 points (difference 7.5; 95% CI 2.5 to 12.4); ≥10-point decrease not reached Ⓐ vs 15.3 mo Ⓑ
・Subgroups (PFS): HR 0.43 (0.29 to 0.63) triple negative vs 0.82 (0.55 to 1.26) hormone-receptor positive; hypothesis-generating
・Subgroups (OS, final): First-line Ⓐ 22.6 vs Ⓑ 14.7 mo, HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.29 to 0.90); second/third-line HR 1.13 (0.79 to 1.64); small subsets, hypothesis-generating
・Biomarkers (tumor testing): gBRCAm–tBRCAm concordance 99% (141/142); gsLOH 118/125 (94%); no clear benefit of added tumor HRD/gsLOH testing in confirmed gBRCAm
・Biomarkers (HRD spectrum): HRD-negative (<42) 21/129 (16%), commoner with BRCA2m (27% vs 9%) and HR+ (22% vs 11%) disease
・Biomarkers (ORR by HRD, exploratory): Ⓐ 60% (HRD <42) vs 57% (HRD ≥42); Ⓑ no responses with HRD <42 (seven patients) vs 29.4% (HRD ≥42)
・Biomarkers (PFS by HRD, exploratory): Ⓐ 8.2 vs Ⓑ 4.3 mo (HRD <42); Ⓐ 8.0 vs Ⓑ 2.6 mo (HRD ≥42); low HRD or absent gsLOH did not preclude olaparib response
・Toxicity (longer follow-up): G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 38.0% vs Ⓑ 49.5%; G≥3 anemia Ⓐ 16.1% vs Ⓑ 4.4%; AE discontinuation Ⓐ 4.9% vs Ⓑ 7.7%; Ⓐ sepsis death (unrelated), Ⓑ dyspnea death re-assigned to progression; no cumulative toxicity
・Limitations: Open-label; final OS not powered and confounded by post-progression PARP/platinum in Ⓑ; biomarker population non-randomly selected (161/302), small HRD-negative and gsLOH-negative subsets

records.title: PLUS trial (van Tinteren et al.)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Staging · Randomised clinical trial · 2002
records.body: Suspected operable NSCLC undergoing preoperative staging Conventional workup vs conventional workup + whole-body FDG-PET Futile thoracotomy (surgery not resulting in cure) Adding PET to conventional staging reduced futile thoracotomies from 41% to 21% (relative reduction ~51%) by detecting unsuspected advanced/metastatic disease; established PET in preoperative NSCLC staging.

records.title: Fischer et al. (PET-CT staging)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Staging · Randomised clinical trial · 2009
records.body:
Newly diagnosed or highly suspected NSCLC referred for preoperative staging and deemed operable after conventional work-up (history, examination, blood tests, contrast-enhanced CT of chest and upper abdomen, bronchoscopy); age 18–80; exclusions: type 1 diabetes, another malignant condition, confirmed distant metastases, known claustrophobia, estimated post-surgery FEV1 <30% Ⓐ Conventional staging plus PET–CT (400 MBq 18F-FDG IV), followed by further invasive diagnostic procedures
Ⓑ Conventional staging plus invasive diagnostic procedures alone
・Invasive procedures: Mediastinoscopy (mandatory), endoscopic or endobronchial ultrasonography
・Follow-up: Until death or for at least 12 months
・Design: Central permuted-block randomisation stratified by sex and recruiting centre Primary: number of futile thoracotomies. Secondary: total number of thoracotomies, number of justified thoracotomies, overall survival, relapse, diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity Adding PET–CT to conventional staging reduced total and futile thoracotomies in NSCLC without affecting overall survival
・Futile thoracotomies: Ⓐ 21/98 (21%) vs Ⓑ 38/91 (42%); among thoracotomies Ⓐ 35% vs Ⓑ 52%, P=0.05
・Futile thoracotomies, per-protocol: Ⓐ 13/52 (25%) vs Ⓑ 38/73 (52%), P=0.002
・Total thoracotomies: Ⓐ 60/98 (61%) vs Ⓑ 73/91 (80%), P=0.004
・OS: Median Ⓐ 31 vs Ⓑ 49 mo, P=0.29 (mean follow-up 27 mo)
・Staging accuracy: Ⓐ 79% vs Ⓑ 60%; sensitivity Ⓐ 64% vs Ⓑ 32%
・Toxicity: Not reported; one death in each group attributable to complications after primary surgery
・Limitations: Stopped early for slow accrual (189 randomized vs 215 per group planned); 14 in Ⓐ never underwent PET–CT; futile-thoracotomy definition debated
records.keywords: Fischer et al. N Engl J Med 2009;361:32-39  19571281

records.title: Maziak et al. (PET-CT staging)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Staging · Randomised clinical trial · 2009
records.body: Clinical stage I-IIIA NSCLC considered resectable Conventional staging vs conventional + PET-CT Correct upstaging / disease stage PET-CT more often correctly upstaged disease and identified patients who would not benefit from surgery, refining selection for thoracotomy.

records.title: ASTER
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Staging · Randomised clinical trial · 2010
records.body:
Resectable (suspected) NSCLC with an indication for mediastinal nodal sampling (mediastinal nodes short axis ≥10 mm, PET-positive mediastinal or hilar nodes, or centrally located tumour); excluded proven distant metastasis, irresectable disease, small peripheral tumours without enlarged or PET-positive nodes, concurrent malignancy, prior lung cancer therapy, or contraindication to EUS, EBUS or surgical staging Ⓐ Surgical staging alone: mediastinoscopy, with parasternal mediastinotomy or video-assisted thoracoscopy if deemed necessary
Ⓑ Endosonography (EUS-FNA plus EBUS-TBNA) followed by surgical staging if no nodal metastases found
・Thoracotomy: With complete lymph node dissection when staging showed no mediastinal tumour spread
・Design: Randomised multicentre (Leiden, Ghent, Leuven, Papworth) Primary: sensitivity for mediastinal nodal (N2/N3) metastases. Secondary: rate of unnecessary thoracotomy, rate of complications due to preoperative staging procedures, detection rate of locally advanced disease, rate of avoided mediastinoscopies, detection rate of nodal metastases by endosonography alone vs surgical staging, interobserver agreement of EUS/EBUS cytology, negative predictive value Endosonography followed by surgical staging improved sensitivity for mediastinal nodal (N2/N3) metastases and reduced unnecessary thoracotomies vs surgical staging alone
・Sensitivity (N2/N3): Ⓐ 79% (95% CI 66-88) vs Ⓑ 94% (85-98); P=.02, ITT
・Unnecessary thoracotomies: Ⓐ 18% (95% CI 12-26) vs Ⓑ 7% (4-13); P=.02
・NPV: Ⓐ 86% (95% CI 76-92) vs Ⓑ 93% (84-97); P=.18
・Locally advanced disease: Ⓐ 36% vs Ⓑ 52%; P=.01
・Avoided mediastinoscopies: Ⓑ 47% (58/123)
・Toxicity: Staging complications Ⓐ 6% vs Ⓑ 5% (P=.78); 1 pneumothorax after endosonography, 12 events related to surgical staging; most common persistent hoarseness
・Limitations: Tertiary referral centres only; no accepted definition of unnecessary thoracotomy; nodal status unverified in 11 patients

records.title: MEDIASTrial
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Staging · Randomised controlled noninferiority clinical trial · 2023
records.body:
Suspected or proven resectable NSCLC without distant metastasis and an indication for invasive mediastinal staging (cN1-3, or central, FDG-non-avid or >3 cm peripheral tumor); mandatory tumor-negative systematic endosonography of stations 4R-7-4L plus CT-enlarged (>10 mm)/FDG-avid (SUV >2.5) stations; excluded neoadjuvant treatment, unresectable/bulky cN2-3 disease, mediastinoscopy or resection contraindications, highly suspicious (SUV >5, three malignant criteria) nodes out of reach Ⓐ Immediate lung tumor resection with mediastinal lymph node dissection
Ⓑ Confirmatory cervical videomediastinoscopy (sampling stations 4R-7-4L, plus 2R for right-sided tumors) followed by lung tumor resection if node-negative
・Prior staging: Systematic endosonography (EBUS in all, EUS(B) added in 20%) with tumor-negative N2-3 cytology
・Resection: Anatomic resection with dissection of at least three mediastinal stations including subcarinal Primary: unforeseen N2 disease after tumor resection with lymph node dissection. Secondary: 30-day major morbidity, 30-day mortality Omitting confirmatory mediastinoscopy after negative systematic endosonography was noninferior for the rate of unforeseen N2 in resectable NSCLC
・uN2 (ITT): Ⓐ 8.8% vs Ⓑ 7.7%; difference 1.03%, 95% CI upper limit 7.2%, below the 8% margin
・uN2 (PP): Ⓐ 9.0% vs Ⓑ 8.2%; difference 0.83%, 95% CI upper limit 7.3%
・Mediastinoscopy yield: Ⓑ detected N2-3 in 8.0%; number needed to test 12.5
・Delay: Interval to resection Ⓐ 28 vs Ⓑ 38 days
・Subgroups: cN1 uN2 Ⓐ 13.6% vs Ⓑ 7.0%; authors advise special consideration for cN1
・Toxicity: Major morbidity/30-day mortality Ⓐ 12.9% vs Ⓑ 15.4% (P = .4940); mediastinoscopy minor complications 4.6%, major 1.7%, one sudden death at 10 days
・Limitations: Open-label; 8% noninferiority margin; EUSⒷ added in only 20%
records.keywords: Bousema et al. J Clin Oncol 2023;41:3805-3815  37018653

records.title: IALT (International Adjuvant Lung Cancer Trial)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant chemotherapy - HISTORIC evidence · Randomised clinical trial · 2004
records.body:
Completely resected pathological stage I, II or III (1986 AJCC) non–small-cell lung cancer, adjuvant setting after complete surgery; age 18–75; no previous chemotherapy or radiotherapy and no contraindication to chemotherapy; no previous cancer other than nonmelanoma skin cancer or carcinoma in situ of the cervix; randomization within 60 days after surgery Ⓐ Cisplatin 80–120 mg/m² per cycle for three or four cycles, with center-chosen etoposide 100 mg/m², vinorelbine 30 mg/m², vinblastine 4 mg/m² or vindesine 3 mg/m²
Ⓑ Observation (no adjuvant chemotherapy)
・Timing: Chemotherapy to start within 60 days after surgery and within 14 days after randomization
・RT: Postoperative radiotherapy ≤60 Gy to mediastinal nodes per pre-set center policy (never, pathological stage N2 only, or N1 and N2), after chemotherapy in Ⓐ and after randomization in Ⓑ
・Design: Open-choice; each center fixed cisplatin dose, partner drug and radiotherapy policy before the study began Primary: overall survival. Secondary: disease-free survival, second primary cancers, adverse effects With 7.5 years' follow-up, adjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy no longer significantly improved overall survival vs observation; benefit was confined to the first 5 years
・OS: 7.5-yr cut HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.81–1.02; P=.10); median Ⓐ 54 vs Ⓑ 45 mo; absolute gain 3.9% at 5 yr
・OS by period: First 5 yr HR 0.86 (0.76–0.97; P=.01), after 5 yr HR 1.45 (1.02–2.07; P=.04); interaction P=.006
・DFS: 7.5-yr cut HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.78–0.98; P=.02), gain 4.3% at 5 yr; first 5 yr HR 0.85 (0.75–0.95), after 1.33 (0.89–2.0), interaction P=.04
・Non-lung cancer deaths: HR 1.34 (95% CI 0.99–1.81; P=.06); after 5 yr HR 2.46 (1.15–5.28)
・Subgroups: Less benefit suggested at age ≥70 (trend P=.08) and WHO PS 2 (trend P=.05)
・Toxicity: 0.8% died of chemotherapy toxic effects; grade 4 toxic effects 22.6%, mainly neutropenia 17.5%; lethal toxicity 2.4% after cisplatin 120 mg/m² vs 0.6% after 100 mg/m² or less
・Limitations: Open-choice dose, partner drug and radiotherapy per center; 7.8% of Ⓐ never received chemotherapy and 2.1% of Ⓑ did; postoperative radiotherapy 27.7% (Ⓑ) vs 22.9% (Ⓐ)

records.title: JBR.10 (NCIC CTG)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant chemotherapy - HISTORIC evidence · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2005
records.body:
Completely resected stage IB or II NSCLC (T2N0, T1N1, T2N1), adjuvant setting; ECOG PS 0–1; intraoperative mediastinal lymph-node resection or biopsy of nodes 1.5 cm or larger mandatory; wedge or segmental resection, T3 tumors, station 10 or more central nodes, mixed histology, bronchioalveolar carcinoma, prior cancers within five years, significant cardiac dysfunction, active infection or neurologic/psychiatric disorders excluded Ⓐ Vinorelbine 25 mg/m² weekly for 16 weeks plus cisplatin 50 mg/m² on days 1 and 8 every 4 weeks for four cycles
Ⓑ Observation
・Dose amendment: Vinorelbine originally 30 mg/m² weekly, reduced to 25 mg/m² in August 1995 for hematologic toxicity; 18 patients received 30 mg/m² Primary: overall survival. Secondary: recurrence-free survival, safety, toxicity, quality of life Adjuvant vinorelbine plus cisplatin improved overall and recurrence-free survival vs observation after complete resection of stage IB or II NSCLC
・OS: Ⓐ 94 vs Ⓑ 73 mo median; HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.52–0.91)
・5-yr OS: Ⓐ 69% vs Ⓑ 54%; absolute gain 15 percentage points (P=0.03)
・RFS: Ⓐ median not reached vs Ⓑ 46.7 mo; HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.45–0.79)
・Subgroups: Stage II median OS Ⓐ 80 vs Ⓑ 41 mo (HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.42–0.85); stage IB not significant (P=0.79); stage–treatment interaction P=0.13
・ras: OS benefit in wild-type (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.49–0.98), none with mutation (HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.53–1.71); interaction P=0.29
・Toxicity: G3/4 neutropenia 73%, febrile neutropenia 7%; treatment-related deaths 2 (0.8%); dose reduction or omission in 77%
・Limitations: Stage IB subgroup small, non-significant interaction; ras finding exploratory; QoL results beyond article scope
records.keywords: Winton et al. N Engl J Med 2005;352:2589-2597  15972865

records.title: ANITA
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant chemotherapy - HISTORIC evidence · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2006
records.body:
Completely resected (R0, margins free) stage IB (T2N0 only)–IIIA NSCLC by 1986 TNM, adjuvant setting after surgery; histologically proven primary NSCLC apart from bronchoalveolar carcinoma; age 18–75 years, WHO performance status 2 or less; history of concurrent malignant disease or other previous primary tumours excluded Ⓐ Vinorelbine 30 mg/m² IV days 1, 8, 15 and 22 (cycles every 4 weeks, maximum 16 doses) plus cisplatin 100 mg/m² IV days 1, 29, 57 and 85
Ⓑ Observation
・Duration: Planned four cycles
・Radiotherapy: Postoperative, optional, per centre policy
・Design: Open-label Primary: Overall survival Secondary: Disease-free survival; Safety Adjuvant vinorelbine plus cisplatin improved overall survival versus observation in resected stage IB–IIIA NSCLC, mainly in stages II–IIIA
・OS: Ⓐ 65.7 vs Ⓑ 43.7 mo; HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.66–0.96); median follow-up 76 mo
・5-yr OS: Absolute benefit 8.6% at 5 years, maintained 8.4% at 7 years
・DFS: Ⓐ 36.3 vs Ⓑ 20.7 mo; HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.64–0.91)
・Subgroups: Exploratory, unplanned; no benefit stage IB (HR 1.10), stage II 0.71, IIIA 0.69 (0.53–0.90); nodal interaction p=0.004
・Toxicity: Ⓐ grade 3–4 neutropenia 85%, febrile neutropenia 9%; seven (2%) toxic deaths
・Limitations: Open-label; unplanned exploratory subgroups; non-randomised postoperative radiotherapy more frequent in Ⓑ (33% vs 22%)

records.title: LACE (Lung Adjuvant Cisplatin Evaluation) meta-analysis
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant chemotherapy - HISTORIC evidence · Pooled analysis of randomised trials · 2008
records.body:
Completely resected stage I–III NSCLC after surgery; individual patient data pooled from the five largest post-1995 randomised trials (each >300 patients) of postoperative cisplatin-based chemotherapy; trials of preoperative chemotherapy, concurrent radiochemotherapy or carboplatin excluded, as were 74 Big Lung Trial patients with incomplete resection or neoadjuvant chemotherapy Ⓐ Postoperative cisplatin-based chemotherapy, 3–4 cycles planned, with vinorelbine, vindesine, vinblastine, etoposide or mitomycin-based combinations
Ⓑ No postoperative chemotherapy (control)
・RT: Thoracic radiotherapy planned per trial, after chemotherapy in Ⓐ
・Design: Pooled individual patient data from five randomised trials Primary: overall survival. Secondary: disease-free survival, lung cancer–related death, non–lung cancer–related death, treatment delivery, toxicity Postoperative cisplatin-based chemotherapy improved overall and disease-free survival in completely resected NSCLC across five pooled randomised trials
・OS: HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.82 to 0.96); 5-yr absolute benefit 5.4%; median follow-up 5.2 years; no significant heterogeneity (I² 6%)
・DFS: HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.78 to 0.91); 5-yr absolute benefit 5.8%
・Lung cancer death: HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.76 to 0.90); 5-yr absolute benefit 6.9%
・Non–lung cancer death: HR 1.36 (95% CI 1.10 to 1.69), 5-yr increase 1.4%; early excess mainly first 6 months, HR 2.41 (95% CI 1.64 to 3.55)
・Subgroups: Effect varied by stage — stage II HR 0.83 (0.73 to 0.95), stage III 0.83 (0.72 to 0.94), stage IA 1.40 (0.95 to 2.06); greater benefit with better PS, possibly detrimental at PS 2
・Toxicity: Grade 3–4 toxicity 66% and grade 4 32% (chemotherapy arm); neutropenia most frequent (28% grade 4); 19 chemotherapy-related deaths (0.9%)
・Limitations: Subgroup/interaction analyses exploratory; carboplatin, preoperative and concurrent radiochemotherapy trials excluded; toxicity collection varied across trials
records.keywords: Pignon et al. J Clin Oncol 2008;26:3552-3559  18506026

records.title: CALGB 9633
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant chemotherapy - HISTORIC evidence · Randomised clinical trial · 2008
records.body:
Resected stage IB (pathologically confirmed T2N0) NSCLC after lobectomy or pneumonectomy; adjuvant setting, randomised within 4 to 8 weeks of resection; required histologically proven NSCLC, T2 tumour and pathologically negative lymph nodes at mediastinoscopy and/or surgery Ⓐ Paclitaxel 200 mg/m² IV + carboplatin AUC 6 mg/mL per minute IV every 3 weeks for four cycles
Ⓑ Observation
・Timing: Random assignment within 4 to 8 weeks of resection Primary: overall survival. Secondary: disease-free survival, death from lung cancer versus other causes (competing risk), toxicity Adjuvant paclitaxel/carboplatin did not significantly improve overall survival versus observation in resected stage IB NSCLC; exploratory analysis favoured chemotherapy for tumours ≥4 cm
・OS (mature): Ⓐ 95 vs Ⓑ 78 mo; HR 0.83 (90% CI 0.64 to 1.08)
・DFS: Ⓐ 89 vs Ⓑ 56 mo; HR 0.80 (90% CI 0.62 to 1.02)
・Lung-cancer mortality: HR 0.72 (90% CI 0.50 to 1.02), 28% reduction, not significant
・Subgroups, tumour ≥4 cm (exploratory): OS Ⓐ 99 vs Ⓑ 77 mo, HR 0.69 (90% CI 0.48 to 0.99); DFS Ⓐ 96 vs Ⓑ 63 mo, HR 0.69 (90% CI 0.49 to 0.97)
・Subgroups, tumour <4 cm: OS trend against Ⓐ; HR 1.12 (90% CI 0.75 to 1.67)
・Toxicity: G3–4 neutropenia Ⓐ 35%; no treatment-related deaths
・Limitations: Tumour-size subgroup unplanned; underpowered (31% power at HR 0.83); 344 patients with low event rates
records.keywords: Strauss et al. J Clin Oncol 2008;26:5043-5051  18809614

records.title: NSCLC Meta-analysis Collaborative Group
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant chemotherapy - HISTORIC evidence · Individual patient data meta-analysis · 2014
records.body:
Resectable NSCLC, predominantly squamous cell carcinoma (50%) or adenocarcinoma (29%), mostly clinical stage IB–IIIA (93%); pooled individual participant data from randomised trials of chemotherapy-naive patients suitable for surgery, without any previous malignancy, comparing chemotherapy plus surgery vs surgery alone Ⓐ Preoperative chemotherapy followed by surgery
Ⓑ Surgery alone
・Chemotherapy: Platinum-based in all trials except one (docetaxel alone); ten trials gave chemotherapy preoperatively only, five also postoperatively to responders
・Design: Pooled individual participant data from 15 randomised trials; eight trials used postoperative radiotherapy in both arms Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Recurrence-free survival, Time to locoregional recurrence, Time to distant recurrence, Cause-specific survival, Complete resection rate, Overall resection rate, Postoperative mortality Preoperative chemotherapy improved overall survival, recurrence-free survival and time to distant recurrence in resectable, mainly stage IB–IIIA NSCLC
・OS: HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.78–0.96), p=0.007; 5-year survival Ⓐ 45% vs Ⓑ 40%, 5% absolute gain
・RFS: HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.76–0.94), p=0.002; 5-year RFS Ⓐ 36% vs Ⓑ 30%, 6% absolute gain
・Time to distant recurrence: HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.58–0.82), p<0.001; 5-year distant-recurrence-free Ⓐ 70% vs Ⓑ 60%, 10% absolute gain
・Time to locoregional recurrence: HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.73–1.07), p=0.20, not significant
・Complete resection: OR 0.88 (95% CI 0.68–1.14), p=0.33
・Postoperative mortality: 30-day OR 1.48 (95% CI 0.85–2.58), p=0.17
・Subgroups: No survival-effect difference by age, sex, performance status, histology or stage; distant-recurrence benefit modified by scheduling (interaction p=0.05)
・Toxicity: Could not be assessed at the patient level
・Limitations: Toxicity not assessable; four eligible trials (198 patients) excluded, 92% of randomised included; results most reliable for stage IB–IIIA

records.title: IMpower010
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA negative) · Randomised, multicentre, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body:
Completely resected stage IB (tumours ≥4 cm) to IIIA NSCLC (UICC/AJCC 7th edition); adjuvant after one to four cycles of cisplatin-based chemotherapy, randomised only if free of disease recurrence; complete resection with negative margins and mediastinal nodal dissection or sampling 28–84 days before enrolment; EGFR or ALK altered tumours allowed Ⓐ Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV on day 1 of each 21-day cycle for up to 16 cycles (or 1 year)
Ⓑ Best supportive care (observation and regular scans for disease recurrence)
・Chemotherapy: Investigator's-choice cisplatin doublet (vinorelbine, docetaxel, gemcitabine, or pemetrexed in non-squamous) for one to four 21-day cycles before randomisation
・Design: Open-label; 227 sites in 22 countries and regions Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, disease-free survival in PD-L1 TC ≥50% population, 3-year disease-free survival rate, 5-year disease-free survival rate, safety Adjuvant atezolizumab improved DFS vs BSC in resected stage II–IIIA PD-L1 TC ≥1% NSCLC; ITT DFS did not reach significance at 5-year final analysis
・DFS, PD-L1 TC ≥1% (stage II–IIIA), final analysis: Ⓐ 68.5 vs Ⓑ 37.3 mo; HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.55–0.91); significant at interim, not retested
・DFS, all stage II–IIIA, final analysis: Ⓐ 57.4 vs Ⓑ 40.8 mo; HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.69–1.00); significant at interim, not retested
・DFS, ITT (stage IB–IIIA), final analysis: Ⓐ 65.6 vs Ⓑ 47.8 mo; HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.71–1.01), p=0.07; significance boundary not crossed
・OS, second interim: Not formally tested, immature; HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.56–1.06) TC ≥1%; 0.94 (0.75–1.19) stage II–IIIA; 0.97 (0.78–1.22) ITT
・DFS, PD-L1 TC ≥50% (stage II–IIIA), final analysis: HR 0.48 (95% CI 0.32–0.72); excluding EGFR/ALK HR 0.49 (0.32–0.75); unstratified, secondary
・OS, PD-L1 TC ≥50% (stage II–IIIA): HR 0.47 (95% CI 0.28–0.77); excluding EGFR/ALK HR 0.44 (0.26–0.74); unstratified, not formally tested
・3-yr DFS, final analysis: Ⓐ 62.7% vs Ⓑ 52.1% (TC ≥1% stage II–IIIA); Ⓐ 59.3% vs Ⓑ 52.6% (all stage II–IIIA); Ⓐ 61.4% vs Ⓑ 55.5% (ITT)
・5-yr DFS: Ⓐ 53.2% vs Ⓑ 42.7% (TC ≥1% stage II–IIIA); Ⓐ 49.3% vs Ⓑ 44.4% (all stage II–IIIA); Ⓐ 52.0% vs Ⓑ 46.5% (ITT)
・Subgroups: PD-L1 TC 1-49% DFS HR 0.91 (0.65–1.27), OS HR 1.09 (0.71–1.68) at final cut; PD-L1 <1% HR 0·97 (0·72–1·31) at interim, post-hoc exploratory
・Toxicity: G3–4 AEs Ⓐ 22% vs Ⓑ 12%; atezolizumab-related grade 5 in four (1%); AESIs Ⓐ 52.1% vs Ⓑ 9.7%, grade 3/4 Ⓐ 7.9% vs Ⓑ 0.8%
・Limitations: Open-label, no placebo; OS immature (event-to-patient ratio approximately 31%) and not formally tested; PD-L1 subgroup results not alpha-controlled

records.title: PEARLS/KEYNOTE-091
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA negative) · Randomised, triple-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body:
Completely resected stage IB (tumours of ≥4 cm in diameter), II, or IIIA NSCLC per AJCC 7th edition, any histology or PD-L1 expression, after R0 resection; adjuvant setting with chemotherapy strongly recommended for stage II and IIIA but not mandatory; known PD-L1 expression status required for randomisation; previous neoadjuvant or adjuvant radiotherapy not permitted; history of HIV, active hepatitis B or C, or autoimmune disease requiring treatment within past 2 years excluded Ⓐ Pembrolizumab 200 mg intravenously every 3 weeks
Ⓑ Saline placebo intravenously every 3 weeks
・Duration: Until recurrence, new malignancy, unacceptable toxicity, investigator decision, consent withdrawal, or completion of 18 administrations (approximately 1 year)
・Design: Triple-blind, placebo-controlled Primary: disease-free survival in the overall population, disease-free survival in the PD-L1 TPS of 50% or greater population. Secondary: disease-free survival in the PD-L1 TPS of 1% or greater population, overall survival in the overall population, overall survival in the PD-L1 TPS of 50% or greater population, overall survival in the PD-L1 TPS of 1% or greater population, lung cancer-specific survival in the overall population, safety Adjuvant pembrolizumab improved disease-free survival versus placebo in the overall population; the PD-L1 TPS of 50% or greater dual primary was not met at this interim analysis
・DFS (overall): Ⓐ 53·6 vs Ⓑ 42·0 mo; HR 0·76 (95% CI 0·63–0·91); p=0·0014 at second interim analysis
・DFS (PD-L1 TPS ≥50%): Not reached in either arm; HR 0·82 (95% CI 0·57–1·18); p=0·14
・OS: Medians not reached; HR 0·87 (95% CI 0·67–1·15); immature at interim
・Subgroups: Generally similar DFS benefit across PD-L1 expression subgroups; exploratory, no definitive conclusions
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 34% vs Ⓑ 26%; AE discontinuation Ⓐ 20% vs Ⓑ 6%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ four (1%; two myocarditis) vs Ⓑ none
・Limitations: Second interim analysis with immature OS; EGFR/ALK testing not required; no independent central review of baseline imaging

records.title: ANVIL (ALCHEMIST)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA negative) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Resected NSCLC (adenocarcinoma without sensitizing EGFR/ALK variants or squamous cell carcinoma); tumors ≥4 cm and/or N1/N2 lymph node positive; adjuvant setting after completion of planned chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy, enrolled ≥4 weeks and within 3, 8 or 10 months post-operation by regimen; ECOG PS 0–1; no recurrence on chest CT within 1 month Ⓐ Nivolumab 480 mg IV every 4 weeks (240 mg IV every 2 weeks before a protocol amendment)
Ⓑ Standard care observation
・Duration: Up to 1 year or until disease progression or unacceptable adverse events
・Design: Open-label Primary: disease-free survival (overall population), disease-free survival (PD-L1 ≥50% population), overall survival. Secondary: safety, DFS by PD-L1 expression subset, stage, tumor mutation burden, strata Adjuvant nivolumab did not improve disease-free survival vs observation in resected NSCLC after planned adjuvant chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy
・DFS, ITT: Ⓐ 71.3 vs Ⓑ 68.8 mo; HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.81-1.17); 1-sided P = .39
・DFS, PD-L1 ≥50%: Ⓐ 89.8 vs Ⓑ 78.5 mo; HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.59-1.25); 1-sided P = .22
・OS (exploratory): Ⓐ 96 vs Ⓑ not reached mo; HR 1.02 (95% CI 0.82-1.26); PD-L1 ≥50% HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.53-1.28)
・Subgroups: No DFS difference in any subgroup examined; results consistent including PD-L1 ≥50%
・Toxicity: Ⓐ treatment-related grade 3–5 events 116 (25%), grade 5 in 2 (<1%), both respiratory
・Limitations: Open-label; stopped for futility at 75% information; postoperative enrollment timing excluded early relapses

records.title: CheckMate 816
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA negative) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body:
Resectable stage IB (≥4 cm) to IIIA NSCLC (AJCC 7th edition); treatment-naive adults, ECOG PS 0–1, neoadjuvant therapy before definitive surgery; measurable disease by RECIST v1.1 and pretreatment tumour tissue for PD-L1 required; known ALK translocations or EGFR mutations excluded Ⓐ Nivolumab 360 mg plus platinum-doublet chemotherapy every 3 weeks for three cycles, then definitive surgery
Ⓑ Platinum-doublet chemotherapy alone every 3 weeks for three cycles, then definitive surgery
・Surgery: Planned within 6 weeks after completion of neoadjuvant treatment
・Post-surgery: Up to four cycles of adjuvant chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or both allowed in both groups
・Design: International, open-label
・Closed arm: Nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks for three cycles plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg (cycle 1 only) closed to enrollment early on external data Primary: event-free survival, pathological complete response. Secondary: major pathological response, time to death or distant metastases, overall survival, EFS2, safety Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus chemotherapy significantly improved overall survival vs chemotherapy alone at final analysis, with event-free survival benefit maintained at 5 years
・EFS: Ⓐ 31.6 vs Ⓑ 20.8 mo; HR 0.63 (97.38% CI 0.43–0.91); interim analysis 1, minimum follow-up 21 mo
・EFS, 5-yr update: Ⓐ 49.2% vs Ⓑ 34.4%; HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.51–0.91)
・pCR: Ⓐ 24.0% vs Ⓑ 2.2%; OR 13.94 (99% CI 3.49–55.75); final pCR analysis
・OS, final analysis: 5-yr Ⓐ 65.4% vs Ⓑ 55.0%; HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.523–0.998); P=0.048; median follow-up 68.4 mo
・MPR: Ⓐ 36.9% vs Ⓑ 8.9%; OR 5.70 (95% CI 3.16–10.26)
・TTDM: HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.36–0.77), favored nivolumab plus chemotherapy
・Recurrence, 5 yr: Postsurgery Ⓐ 31.5% vs Ⓑ 48.1%; distant metastases Ⓐ 11.4% vs Ⓑ 20.7%
・EFS2 (exploratory): HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.37–0.80)
・Surgery: Ⓐ 83.2% vs Ⓑ 75.4% underwent definitive surgery; R0 resection Ⓐ 83.2% vs Ⓑ 77.8%
・Lung-cancer–specific survival (exploratory): 5-yr Ⓐ 74.9% vs Ⓑ 65.1%; HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.44–0.96)
・OS by pCR (exploratory, within Ⓐ): 5-yr 95.3% with vs 55.7% without pCR; HR 0.11 (95% CI 0.04–0.36)
・ctDNA clearance (post hoc): 5-yr OS 75.0% with vs 52.6% without presurgery clearance
・Closed arm, nivolumab plus ipilimumab vs chemotherapy (exploratory; median follow-up 49.2 mo): EFS 54.8 vs 20.9 mo, HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.51–1.15), curves crossed at 9 mo; pCR 20.4% vs 4.6%; 3-yr OS 73% vs 61%, HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.47–1.14); G3/4 TRAEs 14% vs 36%; no treatment-related death with nivolumab plus ipilimumab vs one with chemotherapy
・Subgroups: OS benefit across stage and histology, greater with PD-L1 ≥1%; EFS benefit greater in stage IIIA, PD-L1 ≥1%, nonsquamous; exploratory
・Toxicity: G3/4 TRAEs Ⓐ 33.5% vs Ⓑ 36.9%; three treatment-related deaths, all Ⓑ (primary analysis); no new safety signals at final analysis
・Limitations: Open-label; OS significance at slight margin (P=0.048); pCR, ctDNA and subgroup analyses exploratory

records.title: KEYNOTE-671
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA negative) · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body:
Previously untreated, pathologically confirmed, resectable stage II, IIIA or IIIB (N2: ≥1 ipsilateral mediastinal or subcarinal lymph node) NSCLC per AJCC 8th edition, deemed resectable after surgical consultation; ECOG PS 0–1; tumor sample for central PD-L1 assessment (PD-L1-unselected); EGFR/ALK testing not mandated Ⓐ Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks + cisplatin-based chemotherapy for 4 cycles (neoadjuvant) → surgery → adjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks for up to 13 cycles
Ⓑ Placebo IV every 3 weeks + cisplatin-based chemotherapy for 4 cycles (neoadjuvant) → surgery → adjuvant placebo IV every 3 weeks for up to 13 cycles
・Chemotherapy: Cisplatin + gemcitabine (squamous) or cisplatin + pemetrexed (nonsquamous)
・Duration: Until maximum administrations, progression or recurrence, unacceptable toxic effects, investigator decision, withdrawal of consent or other reasons
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled; surgery within 20 weeks of first neoadjuvant dose Primary: event-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: major pathological response, pathological complete response, change from baseline in GHS/QoL (neoadjuvant and adjuvant phases), safety At 5 years, perioperative pembrolizumab plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy nearly doubled EFS and continued to improve OS vs neoadjuvant chemotherapy and surgery alone
・EFS, 5-yr analysis: Ⓐ 49.9% vs Ⓑ 26.5%; median Ⓐ 57.1 vs Ⓑ 18.4 mo; HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.48–0.69)
・OS, 5-yr analysis: Ⓐ 64.6% vs Ⓑ 53.6%; HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.59–0.92); median Ⓐ NR vs Ⓑ 70.7 mo
・mPR: Ⓐ 30.2% vs Ⓑ 11.0%; difference 19.2 pp (95% CI 13.9–24.7)
・pCR: Ⓐ 18.1% vs Ⓑ 4.0%; difference 14.2 pp (95% CI 10.1–18.7)
・QoL: No long-term GHS/QoL detriment; improved or stable Ⓐ 59.7% vs Ⓑ 53.0%, difference 6.8% (95% CI −0.1–13.6)
・Landmark (post hoc, nonrandomized): EFS from surgery improved even without pCR (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.50–0.78); OS from surgery improved only with adjuvant therapy (HR 0.69, 0.50–0.95)
・Subgroups: EFS benefit maintained with PD-L1 TPS <1% (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.55–0.98) and N2 (HR 0.64, 0.49–0.83); relative benefit greater with PD-L1 ≥1%; OS less clear age ≥65, never smokers
・Toxicity: G3–5 TRAEs Ⓐ 45.2% vs Ⓑ 37.8%; fatal TRAEs Ⓐ 4 (1.0%) vs Ⓑ 3 (0.8%); immune-mediated AEs Ⓐ 26% vs Ⓑ 9% any grade (prior report), G3–5 6.3% vs 1.8% with 1 Ⓐ death (0.3%); discontinuation Ⓐ 13.9% vs Ⓑ 5.3%; no late-term toxicities
・Limitations: No alpha assigned to this analysis (all spent on previous preplanned analyses); surgical-landmark analyses post hoc and nonrandomized; design cannot separate neoadjuvant vs adjuvant contributions

records.title: AEGEAN
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA negative) · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body:
Resectable NSCLC (stage IIA to IIIB [N2 node stage], eighth-edition AJCC), newly diagnosed and previously untreated; documented tumour PD-L1 status (central SP263 assay) required; candidates for planned lobectomy, sleeve resection or bilobectomy; excluded prior anti–PD-1/PD-L1/CTLA-4 exposure and, after amendment, EGFR-mutant or ALK-positive disease, T4 other than by size >7 cm, and planned pneumonectomy Ⓐ Durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 3 weeks for 4 cycles with platinum-based chemotherapy, then 1500 mg IV every 4 weeks for up to 12 cycles after surgery
Ⓑ Placebo IV every 3 weeks for 4 cycles with platinum-based chemotherapy, then IV every 4 weeks for up to 12 cycles after surgery
・Chemotherapy: Platinum-based doublet per NCCN guidance, selected by histology at investigator discretion
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled; surgery after neoadjuvant phase; adjuvant phase required R0 or R1 resection Primary: event-free survival, pathological complete response. Secondary: major pathological response, disease-free survival, overall survival, pharmacokinetics, immunogenicity, patient-reported outcomes, safety, objective response rate before surgery, lung cancer–specific survival Perioperative durvalumab plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy significantly improved EFS and pCR versus neoadjuvant chemotherapy alone in resectable NSCLC; EFS benefit maintained at second interim with no new safety signals
・EFS: Ⓐ NR vs Ⓑ 30.0 mo; HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.55–0.88) at second planned interim (39.1% maturity; median follow-up 25.9 mo)
・pCR: Ⓐ 17.2% vs Ⓑ 4.3% (final analysis); difference 13.0 percentage points (95% CI 8.7–17.6)
・MPR: Ⓐ 33.3% vs Ⓑ 12.3%; difference 21.0 percentage points (95% CI 15.1–26.9); P<0.001 at interim
・DFS: HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.47–0.92) at interim, resected subpopulation; P=.0137 did not cross MTP boundary .0123; final analysis pending
・OS: Ⓐ NR vs Ⓑ 53.2 mo; HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.70–1.14); not formally tested at interim (35.3% maturity)
・LCSS: Exploratory, investigator-assessed, not formally tested; HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.52–0.93)
・Surgery: Ⓐ 80.6% vs Ⓑ 80.7% underwent surgery; Ⓐ 77.6% vs Ⓑ 76.7% completed; delayed surgery Ⓐ 17.3% vs Ⓑ 22.2% (first-interim DCO)
・R0 resection: Ⓐ 94.7% vs Ⓑ 91.3% among completed surgery (numerical, no formal testing)
・Nodal downstaging: Exploratory; N2→N0 Ⓐ 47.3% vs Ⓑ 40.2%; N1→N0 Ⓐ 53.6% vs Ⓑ 46.2%
・Biomarker: Exploratory presurgery radiologic CR/PR associated with higher pCR and MPR; no radiologic progression patient had pCR or MPR
・Subgroups: EFS benefit maintained across predefined subgroups at second interim (including N2 single/multi-station); larger with PD-L1 ≥50%; no clear EGFR-mutant benefit
・Toxicity: G3/4 AEs Ⓐ 42.4% vs Ⓑ 43.2%; immune-mediated AEs Ⓐ 23.7% vs Ⓑ 9.3%; possibly treatment-related deaths 1.7% vs 0.5%; adjuvant-phase max G3/4 AEs Ⓐ 15.4% vs Ⓑ 10.6% at update, no new safety signals
・Surgical safety: Complications Ⓐ 59.1% vs Ⓑ 60.1% (mostly grade 1/2); Clavien-Dindo grade ≥3 Ⓐ 6.1% vs Ⓑ 8.3%; deaths possibly surgery-related Ⓐ 2.0% vs Ⓑ 1.3%
・Limitations: DFS did not cross MTP boundary at interim; OS immature (35.3% maturity) and not formally tested; EGFR/ALK-positive disease excluded from efficacy

records.title: ALINA
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA positive) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body:
Completely resected stage IB (tumors ≥4 cm), II or IIIA NSCLC (AJCC–UICC 7th edition) with documented ALK positivity by FDA-approved or CE-marked test; adjuvant setting after complete resection, before any systemic therapy; chemotherapy-eligible, ECOG performance status 0–1; no previous systemic anticancer therapy Ⓐ Alectinib 600 mg orally twice daily for 24 months or until disease recurrence, unacceptable toxic effects or withdrawal
Ⓑ Platinum-based chemotherapy IV in four 21-day cycles: cisplatin 75 mg/m² day 1 plus vinorelbine 25 mg/m² days 1 and 8, gemcitabine 1250 mg/m² days 1 and 8 or pemetrexed 500 mg/m² day 1; carboplatin AUC 5 or 6 if cisplatin intolerance
・Design: Open-label Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, safety, CNS disease-free survival, quality of life Adjuvant alectinib significantly improved disease-free survival vs platinum-based chemotherapy in resected stage IB, II or IIIA ALK-positive NSCLC, consistently across AJCC 8th edition stage, nodal status and tumor size
・DFS, ITT: Ⓐ 93.6 vs Ⓑ 63.7% at 2 yr; HR 0.24 (95% CI 0.13–0.43)
・DFS, stage II/IIIA (AJCC 7th ed): Ⓐ 93.8 vs Ⓑ 63.0% at 2 yr; HR 0.24 (95% CI 0.13–0.45)
・DFS, stage II (AJCC 8th ed): Ⓐ 84.7 vs Ⓑ 57.5% at 3 yr; HR 0.28 (95% CI 0.11–0.70)
・DFS, stage IIIA (AJCC 8th ed): Ⓐ 92.3 vs Ⓑ 50.2% at 3 yr; HR 0.22 (95% CI 0.10–0.51)
・DFS by nodal status: N0 HR 0.19 (95% CI 0.04–0.88), N1 0.34 (0.13–0.89), N2 0.21 (0.09–0.47)
・DFS by tumor size: ≤3 cm HR 0.30 (95% CI 0.13–0.67); >3 cm HR 0.19 (95% CI 0.08–0.43)
・OS: Immature at this interim cut; 2.3% event–patient ratio
・CNS DFS, exploratory: HR 0.22 (95% CI 0.08–0.58); brain recurrences Ⓐ 4 (3.1%) vs Ⓑ 14 (11.0%)
・QoL, wk 12 (post-hoc, not tested): Clinically meaningful MCS and domain gains with Ⓐ vs Ⓑ, except physical functioning; PCS stable in both
・QoL, wk 96: Ⓐ MCS 49.9, PCS 48.8, near population norm 50; Ⓑ HRQoL recovered only after chemotherapy ended
・Toxicity: G3–4 TRAEs Ⓐ 18.0% vs Ⓑ 27.5%; no grade 5 events; AE discontinuation Ⓐ 5.5% vs Ⓑ 12.5%
・Toxicity, update: Serious TRAEs Ⓐ 2% vs Ⓑ 7%; AE dose reduction Ⓐ 26% vs Ⓑ 10%; Ⓐ G3–4 CPK increase 6%

records.title: NeoADAURA
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA positive) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Nonsquamous NSCLC (histologically or cytologically documented) considered completely resectable by a multidisciplinary team (stage II-IIIB, AJCC eighth edition); neoadjuvant setting before surgical resection; sensitizing EGFR mutation (Ex19del or L858R) confirmed by sponsor-preapproved local or central tissue testing Ⓐ Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily for ≥9 weeks plus platinum-based chemotherapy
Ⓑ Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily for ≥9 weeks as monotherapy
Ⓒ Placebo orally once daily for ≥9 weeks plus platinum-based chemotherapy
・Chemotherapy: Intravenous pemetrexed 500 mg/m² plus investigators’ choice of carboplatin (AUC 5) or cisplatin (75 mg/m²), once every 3 weeks for three cycles, per local practice
・Sequence: Neoadjuvant treatment → surgery scheduled within 12 weeks of neoadjuvant start → adjuvant osimertinib offered to eligible patients after surgery
・Design: Osimertinib v placebo double-blind within the chemotherapy combination groups; monotherapy open-label, sponsor-blinded Primary: major pathologic response. Secondary: event-free survival, pathologic complete response, nodal downstaging at surgery, safety Neoadjuvant osimertinib with or without chemotherapy significantly improved MPR rate versus placebo plus chemotherapy in resectable, EGFR-mutated, stage II-IIIB NSCLC
・MPR: Ⓐ 26% vs Ⓑ 25% vs Ⓒ 2%; ORs 19.82 (95.002% CI, 4.60 to 85.33) and 19.28 (99.9% CI, 1.71 to 217.39), both P < .0001
・EFS at 12 mo (interim, 15% maturity): Ⓐ 93% vs Ⓑ 95% vs Ⓒ 83%; HR Ⓐ 0.50 (99.8% CI, 0.17 to 1.41; P = .04), not significant at prespecified 0.002; Ⓑ HR 0.73 (95% CI, 0.40 to 1.35), not formally tested
・pCR: Ⓐ 4% vs Ⓑ 9% vs Ⓒ 0%
・Nodal downstaging (baseline N2): Ⓐ 53% vs Ⓑ 53% vs Ⓒ 21%; ORs 4.77 (95% CI, 1.62 to 14.00) and 4.18 (95% CI, 1.44 to 12.14)
・Surgery: Ⓐ 92% vs Ⓑ 97% vs Ⓒ 89% underwent curative-intent surgery; no surgery due to PD Ⓐ/Ⓑ 1% vs Ⓒ 6%
・Toxicity: Neoadjuvant grade ≥3 AEs of any cause Ⓐ 36% vs Ⓑ 13% vs Ⓒ 33%; serious AEs 20%/11%/20%; no fatal AEs
・Limitations: MPR surrogate primary end point; EFS interim at 15% maturity, not significant; >90% started adjuvant osimertinib after surgery across arms

records.title: LORIN
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA positive) · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2026
records.body:
Stage III ALK-fusion NSCLC judged potentially resectable or unresectable, local-regional setting; neoadjuvant lorlatinib before optional local therapy; ALK fusion required; abstract prints no further entry criteria or material exclusions (single-arm) Neoadjuvant lorlatinib up to 3 cycles → optional local treatment (surgery or radiotherapy) → consolidation lorlatinib up to 2 years
・Design: Open-label, multicentre, Simon two-stage Primary: pathological complete response. Secondary: major pathological response, event-free survival, overall survival, objective response rate, R0 resection rate, conversion surgery, safety Neoadjuvant lorlatinib met its pCR primary endpoint in stage III ALK-fusion NSCLC and enabled conversion surgery in initially unresectable disease
・pCR: 46.9% (15/32 operated); primary endpoint reached
・MPR: 81.3% (26/32 operated)
・Nodal downstaging: 90.6% (29/32 operated)
・EFS: 1-yr 97.1% (95% CI 91.5-100) at median follow-up 13 mo; no OS events
・ORR: 83.7% (36/43); no progressive disease
・R0 resection: 96.9% (31/32 operated)
・Conversion surgery: 75.0% (18/24) of initially unresectable disease
・Relapse: 3 local relapses without distant metastasis; all baseline N3, none had adjuvant lorlatinib
・Toxicity: Most common TRAEs hypertriglyceridemia, hypercholesterolemia, edema; grades not reported
・Limitations: Single-arm phase 2; median follow-up 13 mo; pathological endpoints in 32 of 43 operated only

records.body:
Histologically confirmed, completely resected stage IB to IIIB NSCLC (eighth-edition AJCC/UICC staging); ALK-positive on central VENTANA D5F3 immunohistochemistry; stage IIB–IIIB required prior adjuvant chemotherapy unless unacceptable side effects or patient declined, stage IB/IIA chemotherapy at physician discretion; no preoperative or postoperative radiotherapy Ⓐ Ensartinib 225 mg orally once daily

Secondary: disease-free survival in the overall stage IB to IIIB population, overall survival, 3-year disease-free survival, 5-year disease-free survival, safety, CNS disease-free survival Adjuvant ensartinib improved 24-month disease-free survival over placebo in resected stage IB–IIIB ALK-positive NSCLC (prespecified interim analysis)
・DFS (stage II–IIIB): Ⓐ 86.4% vs Ⓑ 53.5% alive and disease-free at 24 mo; HR 0.20 (95% CI 0.11–0.38); median follow-up 24 mo

records.title: ADAURA
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA positive) · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body:
Completely resected primary nonsquamous NSCLC, postsurgical pathological stage IB to IIIA (AJCC seventh edition); centrally confirmed EGFR mutation (Ex19del or L858R, alone or with other EGFR mutations); adjuvant chemotherapy before randomization allowed but not mandatory; no preoperative, postoperative or planned radiotherapy allowed Ⓐ Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily
Ⓑ Placebo
・Duration: 3 years or until disease recurrence or discontinuation criterion met
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled; randomized after surgery and any chemotherapy Primary: disease-free survival in stage II to IIIA disease. Secondary: disease-free survival in the overall stage IB to IIIA population, overall survival, health-related quality of life, safety, time to CNS disease recurrence or death, sites of recurrence Adjuvant osimertinib significantly prolonged disease-free survival and, at final analysis, overall survival vs placebo in completely resected stage IB to IIIA EGFR mutation–positive NSCLC
・DFS, stage II to IIIA (primary): Ⓐ 90% vs Ⓑ 44% disease-free at 24 mo; HR 0.17 (99.06% CI 0.11–0.26); median NR vs 19.6 mo
・DFS, overall stage IB to IIIA: Ⓐ 89% vs Ⓑ 52% disease-free at 24 mo; HR 0.20 (99.12% CI 0.14–0.30); median NR vs 27.5 mo
・DFS update (after 2 additional yr follow-up): Benefit sustained; HR 0.23 (stage II to IIIA), 0.27 (stage IB to IIIA)
・OS (final analysis): 5-yr OS Ⓐ 85% vs Ⓑ 73% in stage II to IIIA; HR 0.49 (95.03% CI 0.33–0.73); overall stage IB to IIIA Ⓐ 88% vs Ⓑ 78%; HR 0.49 (95.03% CI 0.34–0.70)
・CNS DFS (exploratory): Ⓐ 98% vs Ⓑ 85% alive without CNS disease at 24 mo; HR 0.18 (95% CI 0.10–0.33); updated analysis HR 0.36
・Subgroups: DFS benefit consistent across all predefined subgroups, including stages IB, II and IIIA and adjuvant-chemotherapy use
・OS subgroups (exploratory): Benefit consistent by stage; HR 0.44 (IB), 0.63 (II), 0.37 (IIIA)
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 AEs Ⓐ 20% vs Ⓑ 13%; ILD Ⓐ 3% vs Ⓑ none, all mild or moderate; no fatal AEs with Ⓐ, one pulmonary embolism with Ⓑ
・Update (final OS cutoff): No new adverse events of special interest; one new serious AE, COVID-19-related pneumonia, unrelated to regimen; safety consistent with primary analysis
・Limitations: DFS from unplanned interim analysis after early unblinding; subsequent osimertinib may have reduced the OS difference; OS subgroup analyses exploratory, some CIs crossed 1

records.title: Lung ART
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Adjuvant radiotherapy · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body:
Completely resected stage IIIAN2 NSCLC with proven mediastinal N2 involvement, documented at surgery (or pre-chemotherapy if downstaged); lobectomy, bilobectomy or pneumonectomy with mediastinal nodal exploration; perioperative chemotherapy allowed but not concomitant with radiotherapy; required postoperative FEV1 >1 L or >35% of theoretical value; excluded prior chest radiotherapy, synchronous contralateral lung cancer, past/current neoplasm, severe cardiopulmonary disease within 6 months Ⓐ Mediastinal PORT 54 Gy in 27 fractions of 2·0 Gy or 30 fractions of 1·8 Gy, five consecutive days a week for 5·5 weeks
Ⓑ No PORT (control)
・Technique: 3D conformal radiotherapy mandatory; IMRT permitted in centres with expertise
・Chemo: Preoperative or postoperative adjuvant chemotherapy (or both) allowed, not concomitant with radiotherapy
・Timing: Randomised after surgery or adjuvant chemotherapy; PORT initiated after surgery per protocol
・Design: Open-label Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, adverse events, local control, patterns of recurrence, secondary cancers, prognostic and predictive factors for disease-free survival and overall survival 3D conformal PORT did not improve disease-free survival versus no PORT after complete resection of stage IIIAN2 NSCLC, with excess cardiopulmonary toxicity
・3-yr DFS: Ⓐ 47% vs Ⓑ 44%; adjusted HR 0·86 (95% CI 0·68–1·08)
・Median DFS: Ⓐ 30·5 vs Ⓑ 22·8 mo; median follow-up 4·8 years
・Mediastinal relapse: Ⓐ 25% vs Ⓑ 46% of DFS events; death as first event Ⓐ 15% vs Ⓑ 5%
・3-yr OS: Ⓐ 67% vs Ⓑ 69%; adjusted HR 0·97 (95% CI 0·73–1·28), early analysis
・Toxicity: Late grade 3–4 cardiopulmonary events Ⓐ 11% vs Ⓑ 5%; grade 3–4 pneumonitis Ⓐ 6% vs Ⓑ <1%; two pneumonitis deaths in Ⓐ
・Limitations: Open-label; investigator-assessed DFS events; slight non-proportionality of risks

records.title: PACIFIC
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Unresectable stage III NSCLC — chemoradiation & consolidation · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body:
Unresectable, stage III locally advanced NSCLC (any histology) without progression after two or more cycles of platinum-based concurrent chemoradiotherapy (54–66 Gy; mean lung dose <20 Gy, V20 <35%, or both); no PD-L1 expression threshold for enrollment; key exclusions: prior anti–PD-1/PD-L1 antibodies, autoimmune disease within 2 years, unresolved grade ≥2 toxicity, grade ≥2 pneumonitis after chemoradiotherapy Ⓐ Durvalumab 10 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks
Ⓑ Matching placebo IV every 2 weeks
・Duration: Up to 12 months; stopped for confirmed progression, alternative anticancer therapy, unacceptable toxic effects, or withdrawal of consent
・Prior therapy: Platinum-based concurrent chemoradiotherapy (two or more cycles; 54–66 Gy), completed 1–42 days before randomization
・Design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; stratified by age, sex, smoking history Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: 12-month progression-free survival, 18-month progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, time to death or distant metastasis, time to second progression, overall survival at 24 months, safety, health-related quality of life, pharmacokinetics, immunogenicity Updated 5-year analyses showed sustained overall and durable progression-free survival benefit with durvalumab versus placebo after chemoradiotherapy; 42.9% of durvalumab patients alive at 5 years
・OS: Ⓐ 47.5 vs Ⓑ 29.1 mo; HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.59–0.89); 5-yr OS 42.9% vs 33.4% (5-yr update, Jan 2021 DCO)
・PFS: Ⓐ 16.9 vs Ⓑ 5.6 mo; HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.45–0.68); 5-yr PFS 33.1% vs 19.0% (5-yr update)
・12-mo PFS: Ⓐ 55.9% vs Ⓑ 35.3%; 18-mo PFS 44.2% vs 27.0% (2018 update)
・ORR: Ⓐ 29.8% vs Ⓑ 18.3% (5-yr update; BICR, measurable disease)
・DoR: Ⓐ median NR vs Ⓑ 18.4 mo; ongoing response at 5 yr Ⓐ 51.1%, Ⓑ not estimable
・TTDM: Ⓐ 36.5 vs Ⓑ 17.7 mo; HR 0.59 (95% CI 0.47–0.74) (5-yr update)
・PFS2: Ⓐ 28.3 vs Ⓑ 17.1 mo; HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.46–0.73)
・TFST/TSST: Ⓐ 21.2 vs Ⓑ 10.4 mo and Ⓐ 30.3 vs Ⓑ 17.8 mo; both HR 0.65; subsequent immunotherapy Ⓐ 12.6% vs Ⓑ 29.1%
・New lesions: Ⓐ 24.2% vs Ⓑ 33.3%; brain metastases Ⓐ 6.5% vs Ⓑ 11.8%
・Subgroups: OS and PFS benefit across all prespecified subgroups; exception OS PD-L1 TC <1% HR 1.15 (95% CI 0.75–1.75), PFS HR 0.80 (0.53–1.20)
・Toxicity: G3/4 AEs Ⓐ 30.5% vs Ⓑ 26.1%; G3/4 pneumonitis/radiation pneumonitis 3.4% vs 2.6%; AE discontinuation 15.4% vs 9.8%; deaths due to AEs 4.4% vs 6.4%
・Limitations: Updated analyses exploratory; subgroup HRs unstratified, no adjustment for multiple comparisons; PD-L1 unknown in 37%

records.body:

records.title: FLAURA
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · Randomised, double-blind clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body:
Locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC, previously untreated and eligible for first-line gefitinib or erlotinib; EGFR exon 19 deletion (Ex19del) or L858R confirmed by local or central test, alone or co-occurring with other EGFR mutations; neurologically stable CNS metastases allowed Ⓐ Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily
Ⓑ Standard EGFR-TKI: gefitinib 250 mg orally once daily or erlotinib 150 mg orally once daily
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable side effects, or withdrawal of consent
・Design: Double-blind Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, disease-control rate, depth of response, safety First-line osimertinib improved progression-free survival and, at final analysis, overall survival over standard EGFR-TKIs in EGFR mutation–positive advanced NSCLC
・PFS: Ⓐ 18.9 vs Ⓑ 10.2 mo; HR 0.46 (95% CI 0.37–0.57)
・OS (final analysis, 58% maturity): Ⓐ 38.6 vs Ⓑ 31.8 mo; HR 0.80 (95.05% CI 0.64–1.00); P=0.046; 3-yr Ⓐ 54% vs Ⓑ 44%
・ORR: Ⓐ 80% vs Ⓑ 76%; OR 1.27 (95% CI 0.85–1.90)
・DoR: Ⓐ 17.2 vs Ⓑ 8.5 mo
・Subgroups (PFS): Consistent benefit across all predefined subgroups; known/treated CNS metastases HR 0.47 (95% CI 0.30–0.74)
・Subgroups (OS): Benefit across most subgroups; HRs near 1.00 in Asian 1.00 (0.75–1.32) and L858R 1.00 (0.71–1.40)
・Resistance Ⓐ (plasma ctDNA, exploratory): MET amplification 16% (11 of 15 shortest treatment durations); EGFR C797S 6%; no acquired T790M; 65% none detected
・Resistance Ⓑ (plasma ctDNA, exploratory): Acquired T790M 44%; MET amplification 6%; 49% any detectable mechanism; 51% none detected
・Baseline tissue (exploratory): TP53 missense, RBM10, HER2, MET, SMARCA4 or RICTOR alterations enriched in suboptimal response, 87% vs 22%; P<0.001
・Toxicity (final analysis): G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 42% vs Ⓑ 47%; ILD Ⓐ 2% vs Ⓑ 1%; QT prolongation Ⓐ 10% vs Ⓑ 4%; fatal AEs Ⓐ 3% vs Ⓑ 4%
・Limitations: 31% of Ⓑ crossed over to osimertinib, probably aiding Ⓑ OS; afatinib excluded from comparator; brain MRI not mandated
・Limitations (resistance analysis): Exploratory post-baseline subset excluding patients without detectable baseline plasma EGFRm; plasma ctDNA may underestimate MET amplification; histological transformation not assessed

records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · Multicentre single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2025
records.body:
Advanced EGFR-mutant (exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R) NSCLC, AJCC 8th edition stage IV, previously untreated, not restricted by number, site or size of metastases; ECOG 0–2; prior palliative RT allowed with at least one non-radiated baseline lesion; asymptomatic or previously treated brain metastases eligible; no prior EGFR or immune checkpoint inhibitors (single-arm) Osimertinib 80 mg orally daily → re-staging at 8–10 weeks → consolidative RT to persisting lesions (24 Gy in 1 fraction, 27–30 Gy in 3 or 35 Gy in 5 stereotactic fractions, or 15-fraction hypofractionated; up to six sites/organs)
・Duration: Osimertinib continued until progression or intolerance; held 3 days before until 3 days after thoracic RT
・Cranial RT: Discouraged for responding brain metastases; no patients received consolidative RT to the brain Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: duration of response, objective response rate, overall survival, time to subsequent RT or death, time to osimertinib discontinuation or death, safety, tolerability Osimertinib plus consolidative RT met the primary PFS endpoint against a 19-month historical control in advanced EGFR-mutant NSCLC
・PFS: Median 32.3 mo (95% CI 21.9–51.7) vs 19-mo historical control; median follow-up 35.7 mo
・OS: Median 45 mo (95% CI 39.3–56.4)
・Duration on osimertinib: Median 32.4 mo (95% CI 17.6–44.6)
・Consolidative RT: 32 (76%) received; insufficient residual disease the most common reason for omission
・Toxicity: Pneumonitis 2 (5%), one grade 4; intracranial hemorrhage grade ≥3 1 (2%); osimertinib-related events almost all grade 1–2
・Limitations: Single-arm, non-randomised; cross-trial comparison with FLAURA not appropriate; no correlative endpoints

records.title: ACHILLES
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · Randomised, open-label clinical trial · 2025
records.body:
Nonsquamous NSCLC with sensitizing uncommon EGFR mutations (excluding exon 20 insertions and T790M); clinical stage IIIB/C or IVA/B (TNM eighth edition) or postoperative recurrence; treatment-naive with no previous chemotherapy or targeted therapies; asymptomatic brain metastases allowed Ⓐ Afatinib 40 mg or 30 mg orally once daily, starting dose chosen before random assignment (escalation to 40 mg not allowed)
Ⓑ Cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 6 (AUC 5 if age ≥75 years) plus pemetrexed 500 mg/m² every 3 weeks for four cycles → pemetrexed 500 mg/m² every 3 weeks
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, death, or consent withdrawal
・Design: Open-label Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, disease control rate, time to treatment failure, overall survival, duration of response, safety Afatinib improved PFS versus platinum doublet chemotherapy as initial therapy in nonsquamous NSCLC with uncommon EGFR mutations; DSMB stopped the trial early at interim
・PFS: Ⓐ 10.6 vs Ⓑ 5.7 mo; HR 0.421 (95% CI 0.251–0.706); interim analysis
・ORR: Ⓐ 61.4% vs Ⓑ 47.1%, similar; DCR Ⓐ 82.9% vs Ⓑ 82.4%, similar
・TTF: HR 0.514 (95% CI 0.317–0.836), favored afatinib
・OS: Immature, 29 events; 22 patients (61%) crossed from Ⓑ to EGFR-TKI
・DoR (exploratory): Ⓐ 10.6 vs Ⓑ 5.6 mo; HR 0.348 (95% CI 0.160–0.758)
・PFS by afatinib dose: 40 mg start HR 0.128 vs 30 mg start HR 0.704; 30-mg group selected frailer patients
・ORR by mutation (Ⓐ): G719X 66.7%, L861Q 46.2%, S768I single 0%, compound 72.7%
・PFS by mutation (Ⓐ): Major uncommon 9.5, compound 21.0, other uncommon 8.0 mo
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 44% vs Ⓑ 37%; Ⓐ grade 3/4 diarrhea 22%; one Ⓐ treatment-related death (pneumonia)
・Limitations: Open-label; small sample with early interim termination; OS immature
records.keywords: Miura et al. J Clin Oncol 2025;43:2049-2058  40239133

records.title: Robichaux et al.
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · Retrospective cohort study with preclinical validation (EGFR-mutant NSCLC databases, Ba/F3 drug screening, PDX models) · 2021
records.body:
EGFR-mutant NSCLC (classical and atypical mutations, kinase-domain exons 18–21) from five genomic databases; atypical defined as non-classical, non-synonymous; TTF for first EGFR TKI (80% stage IV; prior chemotherapy allowed); afatinib outcomes from Uncommon EGFR Database; cBioPortal OS/PFI; unknown mutation sequence excluded ・Structure–function groups vs exon-based groups (prediction of EGFR TKI sensitivity and patient outcomes)
・2nd-gen vs 3rd-gen vs 1st-gen EGFR TKI (retrospective TTF on first EGFR TKI received; PACC-mutant and atypical NSCLC)
・Regimens: 18 EGFR TKIs screened — first-, second-, third-generation and Ex20ins-active; clinical outcomes by TKI class and for afatinib (Uncommon EGFR Database) Primary: EGFR mutation frequency, in vitro EGFR TKI sensitivity, time to treatment failure, overall response rate, duration of treatment, progression-free interval, overall survival Structure–function-based EGFR mutation groups predicted drug sensitivity and patient outcomes better than exon-based groups, identifying PACC mutations as sensitive to second-generation TKIs
・Prediction: Structure–function groups more predictive of drug sensitivity than exon-based groups (P < 0.0001; CART variable importance 66–94%)
・TTF: Atypical shorter than classical EGFR mutations (HR 1.8, P < 0.0001; excluding Ex20ins HR 1.6)
・TTF, PACC by TKI class: 2nd-gen 21.7 vs 1st-gen 10.0 vs 3rd-gen 4.1 mo; 2nd vs 3rd HR 0.23 (P < 0.0001)
・TTF, 2nd-gen: PACC 21.7 vs non-PACC 10.0 mo; HR 2.6 (P = 0.0068)
・Afatinib: DOT 17.1 mo in PACC (n = 156) vs exon 18 (n = 87) 17.4 mo; ORR 63% sensitive vs 20% resistant groups
・Preclinical: G719A PDX resistant to osimertinib, most sensitive to poziotinib; 2nd-gen TKIs most selective for PACC in vitro
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: Retrospective, non-randomised TKI-class comparisons; datasets enriched for North American patients; small TKI-class subgroups (3rd-gen PACC n = 11)

records.title: LUX-Lung 2, LUX-Lung 3, and LUX-Lung 6
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · Pooled analysis (combined post-hoc analysis of one single-group phase 2 trial and two randomised phase 3 trials) · 2015
records.body:
Advanced (stage IIIb–IV) lung adenocarcinoma with uncommon EGFR mutations (any mutation other than del19 or Leu858Arg): exon 18–21 point mutations/duplications, de-novo Thr790Met, or exon 20 insertions; TKI-naive, first-line (LL3/LL6) or untreated/after one prior chemotherapy regimen (LL2); excluded active brain metastases, interstitial lung disease, LVEF <50%, significant GI disorders with diarrhoea Ⓐ Afatinib 40 mg orally once daily (LL2 originally 50 mg starting dose)
Ⓑ Chemotherapy (randomised LL3/LL6 only), up to six cycles: pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV every 21 days (LL3) or gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² days 1 and 8 + cisplatin 75 mg/m² day 1 IV every 21 days (LL6)
・Duration (Ⓐ): Until disease progression, intolerable adverse events, or withdrawal of consent; escalation to 50 mg permitted after first course if tolerated (LL3/LL6)
・Design: LL2 single-group afatinib; LL3 and LL6 randomly assigned afatinib or chemotherapy; post-hoc pooled analysis without formal between-treatment comparison Primary: objective response, disease control, duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, tumour shrinkage Afatinib showed activity against frequent uncommon EGFR mutations (Gly719Xaa, Leu861Gln, Ser768Ile) but poor activity against de-novo Thr790Met and exon 20 insertions
・ORR: Ⓐ group 1 (exon 18–21 point mutations/duplications) 71.1%, group 2 (de-novo Thr790Met) 14.3%, group 3 (exon 20 insertions) 8.7%
・PFS: Ⓐ group 1 10.7 mo, group 2 2.9 mo, group 3 2.7 mo
・OS: Ⓐ group 1 19.4 mo, group 2 14.9 mo, group 3 9.2 mo
・DoR: Ⓐ group 1 11.1 mo, group 2 8.2 mo, group 3 7.1 mo
・ORR, Gly719Xaa/Leu861Gln/Ser768Ile: Ⓐ 77.8%, 56.3%, 100.0%
・Chemotherapy (Ⓑ): ORR 24.0%, median PFS 8.2 mo, median OS 30.2 mo; no formal comparison
・Subgroups: Ⓐ Thr790Met+Leu858Arg PFS 7.5 mo vs Thr790Met+del19 1.2 mo
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: Post-hoc pooled analysis; small heterogeneous subgroups, no formal comparisons; 84% Asian population

records.title: KCSG-LU15-09
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2019
records.body:
Metastatic or recurrent NSCLC, 97% adenocarcinoma, harboring EGFR mutations other than exon 19 deletion, L858R, T790M or exon 20 insertion; mixed lines (61% first-line, 31% second-line, 8% third-line); excluded prior EGFR-TKI, radiotherapy or chemotherapy within 2 weeks, interstitial lung disease, active infection, uncontrolled symptomatic brain metastasis (single-arm) Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily
・Duration: Until RECIST v1.1-defined progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal of consent Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall survival, duration of response, safety Osimertinib showed activity in metastatic or recurrent NSCLC harboring uncommon EGFR mutations, with ORR 50% and median PFS 8.2 months
・ORR: 50%; disease control rate 89%
・PFS: 8.2 mo (95% CI 5.9–10.5); median follow-up 20.6 mo
・OS: Median not reached; 12-mo survival rate 86%
・DoR: 11.2 mo (95% CI 7.7–14.7)
・Subgroups: L861Q ORR 78%, PFS 15.2 mo; G719X ORR 53%, PFS 8.2 mo; S768I ORR 38%, PFS 12.3 mo
・CNS: Intracranial ORR 40% among five evaluable patients
・Toxicity: Grade 3–4 AEs in 6% (grade 3 dyspnea, headache); no pneumonitis or QT prolongation; any-grade rash 31%, pruritus 25%
・Limitations: Single-arm; mixed first- to third-line therapy; small numbers per mutation subtype with local EGFR testing

records.title: UNICORN
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · Single-arm, non-randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2024
records.body:
Metastatic NSCLC (histologically or cytologically confirmed) with uncommon EGFR mutations other than exon 20 insertions, previously untreated; mutations identified by PCR-based or next-generation sequencing-based testing; ECOG PS 0-2 and at least 1 measurable lesion per RECIST version 1.1; symptomatic brain metastases at screening excluded (single-arm) Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily
・Duration: Until disease progression or unacceptable toxic effects Primary: overall response rate. Secondary: disease control rate, progression-free survival, time to treatment failure, overall survival, duration of response, safety First-line osimertinib showed clinical activity in previously untreated metastatic NSCLC with uncommon EGFR mutations, meeting its primary endpoint
・ORR: 55.0% (90% CI 40.9%-68.5)
・DCR: 90.0%
・PFS: Median 9.4 mo (95% CI 3.7-15.2)
・OS: Median NR (95% CI 19.3 mo-NR); 1-yr 81.3%, 2-yr 62.1%
・DoR: Median 22.7 mo (95% CI 9.5 mo-NR)
・Subgroups: Solitary vs compound mutations ORR 45.5% vs 66.7%; median PFS 5.4 vs 9.8 mo (exploratory)
・Subgroups: Solitary G719X ORR 30.0%, median PFS 3.6 mo; brain metastases median PFS 4.5 vs 9.8 mo
・Toxicity: Grade 3-4 AEs 27.5%; interstitial lung disease 12.5%; cardiac events 2.5%; no treatment-related deaths
・Limitations: Single-arm, non-randomised, small (40 eligible); single-ethnicity cohort with heterogeneous uncommon-mutation subtypes; OS immature

records.title: CHRYSALIS-2 Cohort C
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · Single-arm clinical trial (phase I/Ib) · 2025
records.body:
Advanced or metastatic NSCLC with atypical activating EGFR mutations (including S768I, L861Q, G719X); treatment-naive or ≤2 prior lines of chemotherapy and/or first-/second-generation EGFR-TKIs as most recent therapy; stable treated CNS metastases eligible; excluded solitary Ex20ins, coexisting Ex20ins or Ex19del/L858R, and prior third-generation EGFR-TKI receipt (single-arm) Amivantamab 1,050 mg (1,400 mg if ≥80 kg) IV weekly for the first 4 weeks, then every 2 weeks, plus lazertinib 240 mg orally once daily
・Duration: 28-day cycles until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, noncompliance, withdrawal of consent, or discontinuation at investigator discretion Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: duration of response, clinical benefit rate, progression-free survival, overall survival, time to treatment discontinuation, adverse events Amivantamab-lazertinib showed durable antitumor activity in atypical EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC in this single-arm cohort; comparative benefit unestablished
・ORR: 52%; all responses were partial (interim analysis; median follow-up 16.1 mo)
・DoR: Median 14.1 mo
・CBR: 79%
・PFS: Median 11.1 mo
・OS: Median not estimable; 24-month rate 58%
・Subgroups: First-line ORR 57%, mPFS 19.5 mo, 24-mo OS 77%; previously treated ORR 48%, mPFS 7.8 mo, mOS 22.8 mo
・Exploratory: ORR 45% with PACC mutations, 64% classical-like, 67% T790M-like; TP53 mutation not associated with lower ORR
・Toxicity: G≥3 TEAEs 70%; G≥3 treatment-related AEs 48% (rash 13%, hypoalbuminemia 8%); VTE 30%, no grade 4-5; treatment-related death 1%
・Limitations: Single-arm phase I proof-of-concept cohort; no blinded independent central review of ORR; interim analysis with OS not estimable

records.title: Marcoux et al.
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · Retrospective cohort study · 2018
records.body:
EGFR-mutant small-cell lung cancer or other high-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma, transformed from EGFR-mutant NSCLC after at least one EGFR TKI (58 patients, predominantly adenocarcinoma) or de novo/mixed at diagnosis (nine); retrospective multicentre cohort treated 2006-2018 at eight North American cancer centers (retrospective cohort; post-transformation systemic therapy at treating physicians' discretion, not assigned)
・Platinum-etoposide: most commonly used post-transformation regimen (n = 53)
・Taxanes: administered to 21 patients, generally late line; 14 of 21 single agent
・Checkpoint inhibitors: 17 patients (PD-1 or PD-L1 monotherapy n = 9; ipilimumab-nivolumab n = 8)
・EGFR TKI: 34 patients after transformation
・Pre-transformation: at least one EGFR TKI in all 58 transformed cases Primary: time to SCLC transformation, clinical response rate to post-transformation systemic therapy, progression-free survival on platinum-etoposide, progression-free survival on taxanes, overall survival since initial diagnosis, overall survival since SCLC transformation, CNS progression frequency, founder EGFR mutation retention and recurrent tumour mutations In this retrospective multicentre cohort, transformed EGFR-mutant SCLC showed frequent responses to platinum-etoposide and taxanes but no responses to checkpoint inhibitors
・Time to transformation: Median 17.8 mo (95% CI 14.3 to 26.2)
・ORR, platinum-etoposide: 54% among 46 patients with estimable response; PFS 3.4 mo (95% CI 2.4 to 5.4)
・ORR, taxanes: 50% among 20 patients with estimable response; PFS 2.7 mo (95% CI 1.3 to 3.4)
・Taxane type: Paclitaxel and nab-paclitaxel five responses each among seven treated (71%); docetaxel none among six
・Checkpoint inhibitors: No responses among 17 patients; longest time to progression 9 weeks
・OS: 31.5 mo since diagnosis (95% CI 24.8 to 41.3); 10.9 mo since transformation (95% CI 8.0 to 13.7); median follow-up after transformation 8.1 mo
・Genotype: Founder EGFR mutation retained; T790M lost in 15 (79%) of 19 with prior T790M; TP53 38 (79%) of 48, Rb1 18 (58%) of 31, PIK3CA 14 (27%) of 52
・CNS progression: 38 (64%) of 59 patients with follow-up imaging
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: Retrospective with non-standardised treatments and response assessment; no formal RECIST confirmation; no central pathology or radiology review
records.keywords: Marcoux et al. J Clin Oncol 2018;37:278-285  30550363

records.title: Zhou et al; osimertinib with or without chemotherapy in EGFR/TP53 co-mutated advanced NSCLC
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Stage IV or recurrent nonsquamous NSCLC with concurrent TP53 and EGFR-sensitizing mutations (Ex19del or L858R); first-line, no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease; at least one measurable lesion; asymptomatic stable brain metastases allowed; symptomatic brain metastases excluded Ⓐ Osimertinib 80 mg once daily + pemetrexed 500 mg/m² and carboplatin AUC 5 mg/mL/min IV every 3 weeks for 4 cycles, then maintenance osimertinib + pemetrexed
Ⓑ Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily continuously
・Duration: Until RECIST version 1.1 progression, consent withdrawal, intolerable toxic effects, or symptomatic progression requiring urgent intervention
・Design: Open-label Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, disease control rate, safety, quality of life First-line osimertinib plus pemetrexed-carboplatin significantly improved PFS vs osimertinib monotherapy in EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC with concurrent TP53 mutations
・PFS: Ⓐ 34.0 vs Ⓑ 15.6 mo; HR 0.44 (95% CI 0.32-0.60)
・OS interim: Ⓐ 48.4 vs Ⓑ 36.5 mo; HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.38-0.88); nominal P=.01; 30.6% maturity
・ORR: Ⓐ 82.9% vs Ⓑ 71.6%
・DoR: Ⓐ 32.7 vs Ⓑ 15.3 mo
・QoL: Global health status time to deterioration favoured Ⓑ (RMST difference −7.8; 95% CI −15.6 to 0), faster Ⓐ decline during induction
・Subgroups: Benefit consistent across prespecified subgroups; brain metastases HR 0.39 (0.25-0.60), L858R HR 0.43 (0.28-0.67)
・Toxicity: G≥3 TRAEs Ⓐ 62.4% vs Ⓑ 14.9%; serious TRAEs 10.6% vs 1.4%; one Ⓐ treatment-related death (severe thrombocytopenia, pulmonary hemorrhage)
・Limitations: Open-label, investigator-assessed PFS; OS immature at interim; conducted in one region (China)

records.title: PROFILE 1014
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · ALK-positive · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2014
records.body:
Locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic ALK-rearranged nonsquamous NSCLC (ALK positive on central Vysis break-apart FISH); first-line, no previous systemic therapy for advanced disease; treated brain metastases eligible if neurologically stable for at least 2 weeks without ongoing glucocorticoids Ⓐ Crizotinib 250 mg orally twice daily
Ⓑ Pemetrexed 500 mg/m² IV plus cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5–6, every 3 weeks for up to six cycles
・Duration: Until RECIST-defined disease progression, unacceptable toxic effects, death, or withdrawal of consent
・Design: Open-label; platinum agent at investigator's choice Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, overall survival, safety, patient-reported outcomes First-line crizotinib improved progression-free survival, objective response and quality of life versus pemetrexed-platinum; final overall survival did not significantly differ, favoring crizotinib after crossover adjustment
・PFS: Ⓐ 10.9 vs Ⓑ 7.0 mo; HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.35–0.60)
・ORR: Ⓐ 74% vs Ⓑ 45%; P<0.001
・DoR: Ⓐ 11.3 vs Ⓑ 5.3 mo
・OS (final analysis, median follow-up ~46 mo): Ⓐ not reached vs Ⓑ 47.5 mo; HR 0.760 (95% CI 0.548–1.053); crossover-adjusted HR 0.346 (95% bootstrap CI 0.081–0.718)
・QoL: Greater improvement in global quality of life and lung-cancer symptoms with crizotinib; symptom worsening HR 0.59 (95% CI 0.45–0.77)
・Subgroups (OS, final): Without baseline brain metastases HR 0.672 (95% CI 0.457–0.987); with brain metastases HR 1.285 (95% CI 0.716–2.306), not significant
・Subsequent ALK TKI (exploratory): Longest OS with crizotinib then any ALK TKI (median not reached); chemotherapy then any ALK TKI 49.5 mo
・Toxicity (final): Any-grade vision disorder Ⓐ 73.1% vs Ⓑ 8.9%; grade 3–4 transaminase elevation Ⓐ 14.0% vs Ⓑ 2.4%; one fatal crizotinib-related pneumonitis after crossover; no new safety signals
・Limitations: Open-label; 84.2% chemotherapy-arm crossover to crizotinib with assumption-dependent RPSFTM adjustment; no maintenance pemetrexed in control arm

records.title: ALEX
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · ALK-positive · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body:
Advanced ALK-positive NSCLC (mostly adenocarcinoma), ALK-positive by central VENTANA ALK (D5F3) IHC assay; first-line, no previous systemic treatment; ECOG PS 0–2; measurable disease per RECIST version 1.1; asymptomatic brain or leptomeningeal metastases eligible, prior CNS radiotherapy allowed if completed at least 14 days before enrollment Ⓐ Alectinib 600 mg orally twice daily
Ⓑ Crizotinib 250 mg orally twice daily
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxic effects, withdrawal of consent, or death
・Design: Open-label Primary: progression-free survival (investigator-assessed). Secondary: independent review committee–assessed progression-free survival, time to CNS progression, objective response rate, overall survival, duration of response, CNS response rate, duration of CNS response, safety Alectinib improved investigator-assessed PFS versus crizotinib in first-line advanced ALK-positive NSCLC; final analysis showed longer median OS (81.1 vs 54.2 mo; HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.56–1.08)
・PFS: Ⓐ median not reached vs Ⓑ 11.1 mo; HR 0.47 (95% CI 0.34–0.65); 12-mo event-free rate 68.4% vs 48.7%
・PFS (final analysis, 2020): Ⓐ 34.8 vs Ⓑ 10.9 mo
・IRC-PFS: Ⓐ 25.7 vs Ⓑ 10.4 mo; HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.36–0.70)
・CNS progression: Ⓐ 12% vs Ⓑ 45% with events; cause-specific HR 0.16 (95% CI 0.10–0.28); 12-mo cumulative incidence 9.4% vs 41.4%
・ORR: Ⓐ 82.9% vs Ⓑ 75.5% (P = 0.09)
・DoR (final analysis): Ⓐ 42.3 vs Ⓑ 11.1 mo; HR 0.41 (95% CI 0.30–0.56)
・OS (final analysis, cut-off 28 Apr 2025): Ⓐ 81.1 vs Ⓑ 54.2 mo; HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.56–1.08)
・5-yr/7-yr OS: Ⓐ 59.5%/48.6% vs Ⓑ 48.1%/38.2%
・OS (RPSFT, crossover-adjusted): Ⓑ crizotinib median 42.0 mo (95% CI 30.0–61.1)
・CNS ORR (measurable lesions): Ⓐ 81% vs Ⓑ 50%; complete CNS response Ⓐ 38% vs Ⓑ 5%
・Subgroups: PFS effect generally consistent; smaller in active smokers and ECOG PS 2 (small numbers)
・Subgroups (final OS): Ⓐ 63.4 vs Ⓑ 30.9 mo with baseline CNS metastases (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.40–1.15); Ⓐ 94.0 vs Ⓑ 69.8 mo without (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.58–1.32)
・Toxicity (final analysis): Grade 3–5 AEs Ⓐ 57.9% vs Ⓑ 57.6% (Ⓐ treatment 28.1 vs Ⓑ 10.8 mo); SAEs Ⓐ 46.1% vs Ⓑ 31.8%; fatal AEs Ⓐ 10 vs Ⓑ 7; gr 3–5 anaemia Ⓐ 7.2% vs ALT rise Ⓑ 16.6%
・Limitations: Open-label; not powered for OS (formal testing stopped at non-significant ORR); subsequent alectinib after Ⓑ progression (25.2%; RPSFT-adjusted Ⓑ median OS 42.0 mo)
