records.title: ALTA-1L
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · ALK-positive · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body:
Locally advanced or metastatic ALK-positive NSCLC, no previous ALK-targeted therapy; locally determined ALK status; at least one measurable lesion per RECIST v1.1; asymptomatic untreated CNS metastases allowed (symptomatic excluded); more than one prior systemic anticancer regimen for advanced disease excluded Ⓐ Brigatinib 180 mg orally once daily (after 7-day lead-in at 90 mg once daily)
Ⓑ Crizotinib 250 mg orally twice daily
・Duration: Until blinded-independent-review-assessed progression, unacceptable toxic effects, or another discontinuation criterion
・Design: Open-label Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, intracranial response, intracranial PFS, duration of response, overall survival, safety, quality of life Final ALTA-1L analysis (median follow-up 40.4 mo): brigatinib continued to exhibit superior progression-free survival versus crizotinib; overall survival remained immature
・PFS (final): Median Ⓐ 24.0 vs Ⓑ 11.1 mo; HR 0.48 (95% CI 0.35–0.66); 3-yr Ⓐ 43% vs Ⓑ 19%
・ORR: Ⓐ 71% vs Ⓑ 60%; OR 1.59 (95% CI 0.96–2.62)
・DoR (final, confirmed responders): Median Ⓐ 33.2 vs Ⓑ 13.8 mo
・Intracranial ORR (measurable brain metastases): Ⓐ 78% vs Ⓑ 29%
・Intracranial DoR (final, measurable brain metastases): Median Ⓐ 27.9 vs Ⓑ 9.2 mo
・Intracranial PFS (final, baseline brain mets): Median Ⓐ 24.0 vs Ⓑ 5.5 mo; HR 0.29 (95% CI 0.17–0.51)
・Intracranial PFS (final, ITT): 3-yr Ⓐ 57% vs Ⓑ 38%; HR 0.44 (95% CI 0.30–0.65)
・OS (final): Medians not reached; HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.53–1.22); 3-yr Ⓐ 71% vs Ⓑ 68%
・OS (crossover-adjusted sensitivity): HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.31–0.92) MSM; 0.50 (95% CI 0.28–0.87) IPCW
・QoL: Time to GHS/QoL worsening median Ⓐ 26.7 vs Ⓑ 8.3 mo; HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.49–0.98)
・Subgroups (PFS): Baseline brain mets HR 0.25 (0.14–0.46); no brain mets HR 0.62 (0.43–0.91)
・Subgroups (OS, posthoc): Baseline brain mets HR 0.43 (0.21–0.89); 3-yr Ⓐ 74% vs Ⓑ 55%
・Biomarkers (exploratory): PFS benefit consistent across EML4-ALK variants and TP53 status; V3 vs V1 worse PFS in both arms (HR 2.45, 3.42)
・Crossover brigatinib (after crizotinib PD, n 65): Median PFS 16.8 mo; confirmed ORR 57%
・Toxicity (final): G3–5 TEAEs Ⓐ 78% vs Ⓑ 64%; grade ≥3 CPK increased Ⓐ 26% vs Ⓑ 1%; grade ≥3 ILD/pneumonitis Ⓐ 3% vs Ⓑ <1%; fatal AEs 8% both arms, none treatment-related
・Limitations: OS immature with 47% crizotinib-to-brigatinib crossover; open-label; brain-mets OS posthoc in small subgroup

records.title: CROWN
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · ALK-positive · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body:
Locally advanced or metastatic ALK-positive NSCLC (Ventana ALK D5F3 CDx assay); no previous systemic treatment for metastatic disease; prior adjuvant/neoadjuvant therapy allowed if completed >12 months before randomization; asymptomatic treated or untreated CNS metastases eligible; at least one non-irradiated extracranial measurable lesion (RECIST v1.1) Ⓐ Lorlatinib 100 mg orally once daily
Ⓑ Crizotinib 250 mg orally twice daily
・Duration: Until independently assessed RECIST-defined progression, death, withdrawal of consent, or unacceptable toxic effects Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival, overall survival, objective response, objective intracranial response, intracranial time to progression, duration of response, intracranial duration of response, safety, quality of life, biomarker analyses After 7 years' follow-up, first-line lorlatinib continued to show long-term PFS benefit and durable intracranial protection versus crizotinib, with median PFS still not reached
・PFS (7-yr cut): Ⓐ median NR vs Ⓑ 9.1 mo; HR 0.19 (95% CI 0.13–0.26); 7-yr PFS Ⓐ 55% vs Ⓑ 3%
・Conditional PFS: Ⓐ event-free at 24 mo → 79% alive and progression-free at year 7

records.body:
Advanced or metastatic EGFR-mutated NSCLC (any histology) progressed on first-line osimertinib after objective clinical benefit; MET amplification by tissue biopsy FISH (GCN ≥5 or MET-to-CEP7 ratio ≥2) or liquid biopsy NGS (plasma GCN ≥2·3); ECOG performance status of 0 or 1; measurable disease; asymptomatic brain metastases not needing steroids, radiotherapy, or surgery within 2 weeks eligible Ⓐ Tepotinib 500 mg orally once daily plus osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily
Ⓑ Tepotinib 500 mg orally once daily (monotherapy)
・Duration: Until disease progression, death, adverse event leading to discontinuation, or study or consent withdrawal
・Design: Open-label, non-comparative; tissue-FISH-positive patients initially randomly assigned to Ⓐ or Ⓑ, thereafter all to Ⓐ Primary: confirmed objective response. Secondary: duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, health-related quality of life (NSCLC-SAQ), safety, resistance mechanisms (cell-free DNA NGS), intracranial response, intracranial progression-free survival Tepotinib plus osimertinib showed antitumour activity after progression on first-line osimertinib in EGFR-mutated, MET-amplified NSCLC; tepotinib monotherapy showed limited activity
・ORR: Ⓐ 50·0% (95% CI 39·7–60·3) in the primary activity population; Ⓑ 8·3% (95% CI 0·2–38·5)
・ORR, liquid-biopsy cohort: Ⓐ 54·8% (95% CI 36·0–72·7)
・DoR: Ⓐ median 8·5 months (95% CI 6·1–NE)
・PFS: Ⓐ median 5·6 months (95% CI 4·2–8·1)
・OS: Ⓐ median 17·8 months (95% CI 11·1–NE)
・Intracranial (exploratory): Ⓐ ORR 29·2% (95% CI 12·6–51·1); median intracranial PFS 7·8 months
・QoL: Ⓐ cough (d=−0·37) and pain (d=−0·24) improved, dyspnoea stable (week 12)
・Subgroups: Ⓐ ORR 56·6% with MET GCN ≥10 vs 42·2% with GCN <10
・Toxicity: Ⓐ grade ≥3 TRAEs in 44 (34%); oedema, QT prolongation, pneumonitis; 4 (3%) potentially related deaths; Ⓑ grade 1–2 only
・Limitations: Non-comparative, open-label design without a control group; monotherapy cohort n=12; intracranial, QoL and subgroup findings exploratory or descriptive

records.title: VISION
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Other actionable drivers (KRAS G12C, BRAF, MET, RET, NTRK) · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2020
records.body:
Locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with confirmed MET exon 14 skipping mutation; up to two previous courses of treatment; mutation detected centrally by liquid biopsy (Guardant360) or tissue biopsy (Oncomine Focus Assay); EGFR-mutation and ALK-rearrangement negative; stable brain metastases and untreated asymptomatic lesions 1 cm or less allowed (single-arm) Tepotinib 500 mg orally once daily
・Duration: Until disease progression, consent withdrawal, or adverse events leading to discontinuation Primary: objective response. Secondary: objective response, duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC QLQ-LC13, EQ-5D-5L), molecular cfDNA response, safety Tepotinib showed durable antitumor activity in advanced NSCLC with MET exon 14 skipping mutations, with responses in about half of patients
・ORR: 46% (95% CI 36–57) by independent review; all responses partial
・ORR by biopsy: Liquid 48% (95% CI 36–61); tissue 50% (95% CI 37–63)
・ORR, investigator: 56% (95% CI 45–66); similar regardless of previous therapy
・DoR: 11.1 mo (95% CI 7.2 to could not be estimated)
・PFS: 8.5 mo (95% CI 6.7–11.0) by independent review
・OS: 17.1 mo (95% CI 12.0–26.8); data not mature
・QoL: Global functioning stable; cough improved beyond minimally important difference; dyspnoea stable
・cfDNA: Molecular response 67% (34 of 51) with matched samples; exploratory
・Subgroups: Brain metastases (nontarget) ORR 55% (95% CI 23–83), median PFS 10.9 mo
・Toxicity: Treatment-related G≥3 AEs 28%; peripheral edema G3 7% (any grade 63%); discontinuation 11%; one fatal ILD
・Limitations: Single-arm, open-label, phase 2; descriptive analysis, no statistical comparisons; OS not mature

records.title: LIBRETTO-431
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Other actionable drivers (KRAS G12C, BRAF, MET, RET, NTRK) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body:
Unresectable stage IIIB, IIIC or IV nonsquamous NSCLC, first-line (no previous systemic therapy for advanced disease), RET fusion–positive by validated NGS or PCR testing; known brain metastases eligible if asymptomatic or neurologically stable ≥2 weeks; excluded other validated oncogenic drivers, active cardiovascular disease, uncontrolled infections or effusions Ⓐ Selpercatinib 160 mg twice daily in continuous 21-day cycles
Ⓑ Pemetrexed 500 mg per square meter plus investigator's choice of platinum (carboplatin AUC 5, maximum 750 mg, or cisplatin 75 mg per square meter) with or without pembrolizumab 200 mg, every 21 days
・Control continuation: After four cycles without progressive disease, pemetrexed with or without pembrolizumab; pembrolizumab for a maximum of 35 cycles
・Design: Open-label Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, intracranial response, time to CNS progression, time to confirmed worsening of pulmonary symptoms, safety First-line selpercatinib significantly prolonged progression-free survival versus platinum-based chemotherapy with or without pembrolizumab in advanced RET fusion–positive NSCLC
・PFS (ITT-pembro, interim): Ⓐ 24.8 vs Ⓑ 11.2 mo; HR 0.46 (95% CI 0.31–0.70)
・PFS (overall ITT): Ⓐ 24.8 vs Ⓑ 11.2 mo; HR 0.48 (95% CI 0.33–0.70)
・OS: Immature at interim (information fraction 28.6%); HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.58–1.87)
・ORR: Ⓐ 84% vs Ⓑ 65%
・DoR: Ⓐ 24.2 vs Ⓑ 11.5 mo
・CNS: Time to CNS progression HR 0.28 (95% CI 0.12–0.68); intracranial response Ⓐ 82% vs Ⓑ 58%
・CNS protection (update; no baseline mets, n=150): 12-mo cumulative incidence of CNS progression Ⓐ 1.1% vs Ⓑ 14.7%; cause-specific HR 0.17 (95% CI 0.04–0.69)
・Intracranial PFS (update; no baseline mets): 12-mo Ⓐ 91.8% vs Ⓑ 74.7%; HR 0.46 (95% CI 0.18–1.18)
・Baseline CNS mets (update; n=42): 12-mo cumulative incidence of CNS progression Ⓐ 25.7% vs Ⓑ 33.3%, cause-specific HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.19–1.92); intracranial PFS HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.28–1.97)
・Intracranial response (update, no prior CNS radiotherapy): Ⓐ 93.3% vs Ⓑ 64.3%
・Pulmonary symptoms: Ⓐ median worsening not reached vs Ⓑ 1.9 mo; HR 0.34 (95% CI 0.20–0.55)
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 70% vs Ⓑ 57%; Ⓐ grade ≥3 ALT 22%, hypertension 20%, QTc 9%; fatal AEs Ⓐ 4.4% vs Ⓑ none
・Limitations: Open-label; preplanned interim analysis; OS confounded by crossover
・Limitations (CNS update): Short follow-up, few events; serial CNS imaging added by protocol amendment

records.title: AcceleRET Lung
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Other actionable drivers (KRAS G12C, BRAF, MET, RET, NTRK) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Adults with RET fusion–positive advanced or metastatic NSCLC; first-line systemic treatment; multicentre enrolment at 74 sites in 22 countries; detailed entry criteria and material exclusions not printed in this abstract Ⓐ Pralsetinib 400 mg/d orally
Ⓑ Platinum-based SOC therapy
・Design: Randomised, open-label, phase 3 Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall response rate, overall survival, duration of response, safety Pralsetinib improved PFS and ORR vs platinum-based SOC in first-line RET fusion–positive NSCLC, with higher infection rates
・PFS: Ⓐ 18.7 vs Ⓑ 9.0 mo; HR 0.59 (95% CI 0.42–0.84)
・ORR: Ⓐ 65.5% vs Ⓑ 41.6%; OR 2.81 (95% CI 1.61–4.93)
・OS: Ⓐ NR vs Ⓑ 39.8 mo; HR 1.09 (95% CI 0.65–1.85)
・DOR: Ⓐ 20.6 vs Ⓑ 9.7 mo; HR 0.48 (95% CI 0.28–0.80)
・Toxicity: Infections Ⓐ 71.3% vs Ⓑ 51.9%, incl pneumonia 19.4% vs 5.8%; infection deaths Ⓐ 7.4% vs Ⓑ 0; grade ≥3 hypertension 11.1% vs 0
・Limitations: Terminated early per sponsor decision; open-label design; optional crossover from SOC to pralsetinib upon progression

records.title: PHAROS
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Other actionable drivers (KRAS G12C, BRAF, MET, RET, NTRK) · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2023
records.body:
Stage IV or recurrent NSCLC with BRAF V600 class I mutation by local NGS/PCR; treatment-naive or previously treated with prior first-line platinum-based chemotherapy ± anti–PD-1/PD-L1 (two cohorts); excluded more than one prior advanced-setting line, prior BRAF/MEK inhibitor, EGFR/ALK/ROS1 alterations, untreated symptomatic brain metastases, leptomeningeal disease; untreated brain metastases <5 mm or treated ones stable ≥28 days eligible if asymptomatic (single-arm) Encorafenib 450 mg orally once daily plus binimetinib 45 mg orally twice daily in 28-day cycles
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent, initiation of subsequent anticancer therapy, or death Primary: confirmed objective response rate. Secondary: duration of response, disease control rate, progression-free survival, overall survival, time to response, safety Encorafenib plus binimetinib showed sustained long-term survival in treatment-naive and previously treated BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic NSCLC, meeting the confirmed ORR primary endpoint in both cohorts
・ORR: 75% (95% CI, 62 to 85) treatment-naive; 49% (95% CI, 32 to 65) previously treated (March 2025 cut)
・DOR: Median 40.0 months (95% CI, 23.2 to NE) treatment-naive; 16.7 months (95% CI, 7.4 to NE) previously treated; ≥12-month responses 64% and 42%
・DCR at 24 weeks: 64% (95% CI, 51 to 76) treatment-naive; 41% (95% CI, 26 to 58) previously treated
・PFS: Median 30.4 months (95% CI, 15.7 to NE) treatment-naive; 9.3 months (95% CI, 6.2 to 24.8) previously treated
・OS (March 2025 cut): Median 47.6 months (95% CI, 31.3 to NE) treatment-naive; 22.7 months (95% CI, 14.1 to 32.6) previously treated
・4-yr OS: 49% (95% CI, 35 to 62) treatment-naive; 31% (95% CI, 16 to 47) previously treated
・Time to response: Median 1.9 months treatment-naive; 1.7 months previously treated
・Subgroups (brain metastases): All four treatment-naive patients responded, none of four previously treated
・Subgroups (prior immunotherapy): ORR 58% with vs 33% without prior IO; mOS 26.6 vs 20.7 months (previously treated)
・Subgroups (smoking): Treatment-naive never-smokers had longer mPFS (41.8 vs 24.8 months) and mOS (61.4 vs 35.7 months)
・Toxicity: Grade 3/4 TRAEs 46%; nausea 52%, diarrhea 44%, fatigue 33%; dose reduction 33%, permanent discontinuation 20%; one grade 5 intracranial hemorrhage
・Limitations: Single-arm, open-label design; treatment-naive OS upper CI NE; longest-mOS claim rests on cautioned cross-trial comparison

records.title: Krascendo 1
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Other actionable drivers (KRAS G12C, BRAF, MET, RET, NTRK) · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Histologically or cytologically confirmed KRAS G12C–mutated locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC; progression during or after at least one prior systemic therapy including platinum-based doublet chemotherapy and a PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor, no more than three prior lines; excluded known concomitant actionable oncogenic drivers, any prior KRAS G12C, pan-KRAS or pan-RAS inhibitor, and untreated or active CNS metastases Ⓐ Divarasib 400 mg orally once daily
Ⓑ Control: sotorasib 960 mg orally once daily or adagrasib 600 mg orally twice daily
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable adverse events, loss of clinical benefit, withdrawal of consent, death, or trial termination
・Design: Open-label Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, confirmed overall response, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, safety Divarasib improved progression-free and overall survival versus sotorasib or adagrasib in previously treated KRAS G12C–mutated advanced NSCLC
・PFS: Ⓐ 9.8 vs Ⓑ 5.7 mo; HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.44–0.76)
・OS: Ⓐ 17.7 vs Ⓑ 12.0 mo; HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.41–0.78)
・ORR: Ⓐ 58.4% vs Ⓑ 32.3%; difference 25.8 percentage points (95% CI 15.6–36.0)
・DoR: Ⓐ 11.9 vs Ⓑ 6.9 mo
・QoL: Time to confirmed deterioration (cough) did not meet significance; further PROs untested per hierarchy
・Subgroups: PFS and OS benefit with divarasib in KEAP1-mutated tumors; benefit regardless of PD-L1 status
・Toxicity: G3/4 TRAEs Ⓐ 24.6% vs Ⓑ 34.5%; any-grade GI toxicity higher with Ⓐ (91.0% vs 68.4%, mainly grade 1), hepatotoxicity lower (26.9% vs 39.2%); no treatment-related deaths
・Limitations: Open-label; control predominantly sotorasib (15 patients received adagrasib); Black patients underrepresented

records.title: KEYNOTE-024
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body:
Stage IV NSCLC, first-line systemic therapy for metastatic disease; PD-L1 tumor proportion score 50% or greater, no sensitizing EGFR mutations or ALK translocations; ECOG performance status 0 or 1 and measurable RECIST v1.1 disease; untreated brain metastases, systemic glucocorticoids or immunosuppression, active autoimmune disease treated within 2 years, interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis history excluded Ⓐ Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks for 35 cycles
Ⓑ Investigator's choice of platinum-based chemotherapy for 4 to 6 cycles: carboplatin plus pemetrexed, cisplatin plus pemetrexed, carboplatin plus gemcitabine, cisplatin plus gemcitabine, or carboplatin plus paclitaxel
・Maintenance: Pemetrexed continuation permitted after combination chemotherapy in nonsquamous tumors
・Duration: Until radiologic progression, treatment-related adverse events of unacceptable severity, or withdrawal
・Design: Open-label Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, PFS2, safety Pembrolizumab improved long-term overall survival versus platinum chemotherapy as first-line therapy in PD-L1 TPS 50% or greater metastatic NSCLC (5-year update)
・PFS: Ⓐ 7.7 vs Ⓑ 5.5 mo; HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.39–0.65); 5-yr update
・OS: Ⓐ 26.3 vs Ⓑ 13.4 mo; HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.48–0.81); 5-yr rate Ⓐ 31.9% vs Ⓑ 16.3%; 5-yr update
・ORR: Ⓐ 46.1% vs Ⓑ 31.1%; 5-yr update
・DoR: Ⓐ 29.1 vs Ⓑ 6.3 mo; 5-yr update
・PFS2: Ⓐ 24.1 vs Ⓑ 8.5 mo; HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.39–0.67); exploratory
・35-cycle completers: 39 patients; 82.1% alive at ~5 yr; exploratory
・Toxicity: Grade 3–5 treatment-related AEs Ⓐ 31.2% vs Ⓑ 53.3%; immune-mediated AEs and infusion reactions Ⓐ 34.4% vs Ⓑ 5.3%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 2 vs Ⓑ 3
・Limitations: Open-label; 66.0% effective crossover to anti–PD-(L)1 therapy after Ⓑ; no alpha assigned to this analysis

records.title: KEYNOTE-042
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · Randomised, open-label, controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body:
Locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC (squamous or non-squamous), first-line; PD-L1 tumour proportion score ≥1% on central 22C3 IHC; no sensitising EGFR mutation or ALK translocation; ECOG 0–1 with at least one measurable RECIST 1.1 lesion; excluded unstable or untreated CNS metastases, active autoimmune disease, pneumonitis requiring systemic glucocorticoids, systemic immunosuppression, active hepatitis B or C Ⓐ Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks
Ⓑ Investigator's-choice platinum doublet IV every 3 weeks: carboplatin AUC 5–6 mg/mL per min plus paclitaxel 200 mg/m² or pemetrexed 500 mg/m²
・Duration: Until confirmed complete response, radiographic progression, intolerable toxicity, investigator decision or withdrawal; Ⓐ up to 35 cycles, Ⓑ four to six cycles
・Maintenance: Pemetrexed 500 mg/m² every 3 weeks optional, encouraged in non-squamous Ⓑ Primary: overall survival in PD-L1 TPS ≥50%, ≥20% and ≥1% populations. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response, safety, duration of response Pembrolizumab first-line monotherapy maintained overall survival benefit versus platinum chemotherapy at 5 years (median follow-up 61.1 months) in every PD-L1 TPS population tested (≥50%, ≥20%, ≥1%), with durable responses
・OS, TPS ≥50%: Ⓐ 20.0 vs Ⓑ 12.2 mo; HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.57–0.81); 5-yr rate Ⓐ 21.9% vs Ⓑ 9.8%
・OS, TPS ≥20%: Ⓐ 18.0 vs Ⓑ 13.0 mo; HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.64–0.87); 5-yr rate Ⓐ 19.4% vs Ⓑ 10.1%
・OS, TPS ≥1%: Ⓐ 16.4 vs Ⓑ 12.1 mo; HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.70–0.89); 5-yr rate Ⓐ 16.6% vs Ⓑ 8.5%
・PFS: Ⓐ 6.5 vs Ⓑ 6.5 mo, HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.72–1.02) (TPS ≥50%); Ⓐ 6.2 vs Ⓑ 6.9 mo, HR 0.94 (95% CI 0.81–1.09) (TPS ≥20%); Ⓐ 5.6 vs Ⓑ 6.8 mo, HR 1.03 (95% CI 0.91–1.16) (TPS ≥1%); superiority boundary missed in primary analysis
・ORR: Ⓐ 39.1% vs Ⓑ 32.3% (TPS ≥50%); Ⓐ 33.2% vs Ⓑ 29.1% (TPS ≥20%); Ⓐ 27.3% vs Ⓑ 26.7% (TPS ≥1%)
・DoR: Ⓐ 28.1 vs Ⓑ 10.8 mo (TPS ≥50%); Ⓐ 26.5 vs Ⓑ 8.4 mo (TPS ≥1%); ≥60 mo in Ⓐ 28.4% vs Ⓑ 16.0% (TPS ≥50%)
・PFS2 (exploratory): HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.54–0.76) (TPS ≥50%); 0.67 (0.58–0.78) (TPS ≥20%); 0.74 (0.65–0.83) (TPS ≥1%)
・Subgroups: TPS 1–49% (exploratory) OS HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.75–1.04), 5-yr OS Ⓐ 11.9% vs Ⓑ 7.4%; never-smoker OS HRs 1.00 or greater (primary analysis)
・Completed 35 cycles (n=102): ORR 84.3%; median DoR 31.9 mo; 4-yr OS after completion 61.8%; grade 3–5 TRAEs 11.8%
・Second-course pembrolizumab (n=33): ORR 15.2%; disease control 75.8%; 6.1% alive without PD at cutoff
・Toxicity: TRAEs Ⓐ 63.8% vs Ⓑ 90.2% (as-treated); G≥3 TRAEs Ⓐ 18% vs Ⓑ 41%; TRAE deaths Ⓐ 13 (2%) vs Ⓑ 14 (2%), none new at 5 yr; pneumonitis Ⓐ any grade 8%, one death
・Limitations: Open-label; 5-yr analysis descriptive (no alpha assigned, no multiplicity adjustment); off-study anti–PD-(L)1 in 23.1% of Ⓑ may have influenced Ⓑ efficacy

records.title: IMpower110
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body:
Metastatic (stage IV) nonsquamous or squamous NSCLC, first line with no previous chemotherapy; PD-L1 expression on ≥1% of tumor cells or tumor-infiltrating immune cells covering ≥1% of tumor area (SP142 assay); EGFR-sensitizing mutation or ALK translocation excluded from analysis by amendment (initially eligible after prior targeted therapy), primary analysis in EGFR/ALK wild-type tumors; active or untreated CNS metastases excluded Ⓐ Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV every 3 weeks; continuation beyond progression allowed with continued clinical benefit
Ⓑ Platinum-based chemotherapy IV every 3 weeks for 4 or 6 cycles; nonsquamous: cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 6 plus pemetrexed 500 mg/m²; squamous: cisplatin 75 mg/m² plus gemcitabine 1250 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5 plus gemcitabine 1000 mg/m²
・Design: Open-label Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, response, duration of response, overall survival and progression-free survival in PD-L1 (SP263) subgroups, overall survival and progression-free survival in blood-based tumor mutational burden subgroups, overall survival and progression-free survival in PD-L1 (22C3) subgroups, safety Atezolizumab prolonged overall survival versus platinum-based chemotherapy in first-line metastatic NSCLC with high PD-L1 expression (interim analysis)
・OS, high PD-L1: Ⓐ 20.2 vs Ⓑ 13.1 mo; HR 0.59 (95% CI 0.40–0.89)
・OS, high/intermediate PD-L1: Ⓐ 18.2 vs Ⓑ 14.9 mo; HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.52–0.99); missed alpha boundary (P=0.04)
・OS, any PD-L1: Ⓐ 17.5 vs Ⓑ 14.1 mo; HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.65–1.07); not formally tested
・PFS, high PD-L1: Ⓐ 8.1 vs Ⓑ 5.0 mo; HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.45–0.88)
・Confirmed response, high PD-L1: Ⓐ 38.3% vs Ⓑ 28.6%; ongoing Ⓐ 68.3% vs Ⓑ 35.7%
・bTMB ≥16: PFS Ⓐ 6.8 vs Ⓑ 4.4 mo; HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.33–0.92); OS Ⓐ 13.9 vs Ⓑ 8.5 mo, HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.41–1.35)
・Toxicity: G3/4 Ⓐ 30.1% vs Ⓑ 52.5%; grade 5 Ⓐ 3.8% vs Ⓑ 4.2%; immune-mediated Ⓐ 40.2% vs Ⓑ 16.7% (G3/4 6.6% vs 1.5%, no grade 5)
・Limitations: Interim analysis, final OS ongoing; open-label; hierarchical testing stopped after high/intermediate PD-L1 boundary missed

records.title: KEYNOTE-189
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body:
Metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC without sensitizing EGFR or ALK mutations; first-line, no previous systemic therapy for metastatic disease; any PD-L1 tumor proportion score (tumor sample required); excluded symptomatic CNS metastases, active autoimmune disease, noninfectious pneumonitis requiring glucocorticoids, systemic immunosuppressive treatment, or more than 30 Gy lung radiotherapy in previous 6 months Ⓐ Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks
Ⓑ Saline placebo IV every 3 weeks
・Chemotherapy: Investigator's choice cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5 plus pemetrexed 500 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks for 4 cycles, then pemetrexed 500 mg/m² every 3 weeks
・Duration: Pembrolizumab or placebo up to 35 cycles; treatment continued until radiographic progression, unacceptable toxic effects, investigator decision, or withdrawal of consent Primary: overall survival, progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, safety, disease control rate, effect of PD-L1 expression on efficacy, patient-reported outcomes, progression-free survival-2 Pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed–platinum continued to prolong overall and progression-free survival versus placebo plus the same chemotherapy after 5 years of follow-up (64.6 months' median follow-up)
・OS: Ⓐ 22.0 vs Ⓑ 10.6 mo; HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.50–0.72); 5-yr rates 19.4% vs 11.3%
・PFS: Ⓐ 9.0 vs Ⓑ 4.9 mo; HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.42–0.60); 5-yr rates 7.5% vs 0.6%
・ORR: Ⓐ 48.3% vs Ⓑ 19.9%
・DoR: Ⓐ 12.7 vs Ⓑ 7.1 mo
・PFS2 (exploratory): Ⓐ 17.0 vs Ⓑ 9.1 mo; HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.45–0.65)
・35-cycle completers (Ⓐ): 57 patients; ORR 86.0%; median DOR 57.7 mo; 3-yr OS after completion 71.9%; grade 3/4 AEs 66.7%, none grade 5
・Crossover (Ⓑ→pembrolizumab): 84 on-study; effective anti-PD-(L)1 crossover 57.3%; ORR 17.9% and median OS 6.9 mo from crossover start (final analysis)
・Subgroups: Benefit across PD-L1 strata incl. TPS <1% (5-yr OS HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.39–0.76; PFS HR 0.67, 0.49–0.92); TPS ≥50% 5-yr OS 29.6% vs 21.4%; brain mets OS HR 0.43 (0.27–0.71) and liver mets OS HR 0.64 (0.42–1.00) (final analysis)
・Toxicity: Grade 3-5 AEs (all cause) Ⓐ 72.8% vs Ⓑ 67.3%; immune-mediated AEs/infusion reactions Ⓐ 27.9% vs Ⓑ 13.4%; AKI 6.2% vs 0.5% (interim), no new cases
・Fatal AEs: Ⓐ 29 (7.2%) vs Ⓑ 14 (6.9%); treatment-attributed deaths Ⓐ 8 (2.0%) vs Ⓑ 2 (1.0%), all previously reported; pneumonitis Ⓐ 2 (final analysis)
・Limitations: Exploratory 5-year analysis, no alpha assigned; effective crossover to anti-PD-(L)1 57.3% in Ⓑ; few patients at risk at 5 years in some subgroups

records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body:
Stage IV or recurrent squamous or nonsquamous NSCLC, first-line (no previous systemic therapy for advanced disease); coprimary analysis in TMB ≥10 mutations per megabase by FoundationOne CDx assay, irrespective of PD-L1; excluded known sensitizing EGFR or ALK mutations, autoimmune disease, untreated CNS metastases (treated CNS metastases eligible if neurologically stable ≥2 weeks) Ⓐ Nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg every 6 weeks
Ⓑ Platinum doublet chemotherapy based on tumor histologic type every 3 weeks for up to four cycles
・Chemo: Nonsquamous — pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5 or 6, optional pemetrexed maintenance; squamous — gemcitabine 1000 or 1250 mg/m² + cisplatin 75 mg/m² or gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 5
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable adverse effects, or completion per protocol (≤2 years for immunotherapy)
・Design: Open-label; further randomised arms nivolumab 240 mg every 2 weeks (PD-L1 ≥1%) and nivolumab 360 mg every 3 weeks plus chemotherapy (PD-L1 <1%) Primary: progression-free survival (population selected on TMB ≥10 mutations per megabase), overall survival (population selected on PD-L1 expression). Secondary: progression-free survival with nivolumab versus chemotherapy (TMB ≥13 mutations per megabase, PD-L1 ≥1%), overall survival with nivolumab plus ipilimumab (TMB ≥10 mutations per megabase), progression-free survival with nivolumab plus ipilimumab versus chemotherapy (PD-L1 ≥1%), overall survival with nivolumab plus chemotherapy versus chemotherapy alone (PD-L1 <1%), overall survival with nivolumab monotherapy versus chemotherapy (PD-L1 ≥50%), objective response rate, duration of response, safety First-line nivolumab plus ipilimumab maintained long-term overall survival benefit versus chemotherapy at 5 years, regardless of PD-L1 expression
・PFS (TMB ≥10, coprimary): Ⓐ 7.2 vs Ⓑ 5.5 mo; HR 0.58 (97.5% CI 0.41–0.81); 1-yr PFS Ⓐ 42.6% vs Ⓑ 13.2%
・OS (PD-L1 ≥1%, coprimary; 5-yr cut, min follow-up 61.3 mo): Ⓐ 17.1 vs Ⓑ 14.9 mo; HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.66–0.91); 5-yr OS Ⓐ 24% vs Ⓑ 14%
・OS (PD-L1 <1%, descriptive; 5-yr cut): Ⓐ 17.4 vs Ⓑ 12.2 mo; HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.52–0.81); 5-yr OS Ⓐ 19% vs Ⓑ 7%
・OS (all patients, descriptive): Ⓐ 17.1 vs Ⓑ 13.9 mo; HR 0.73 (0.64–0.84); 2-yr OS Ⓐ 40.1% vs Ⓑ 29.7%; 5-yr survival Ⓐ 23%
・PFS (PD-L1 ≥1%; 5-yr cut): Ⓐ 5.1 vs Ⓑ 5.6 mo; HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.67–0.94)
・PFS2 (5-yr cut, exploratory): HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.62–0.85) PD-L1 ≥1%; 0.61 (0.49–0.76) PD-L1 <1%
・ORR/DoR (PD-L1 ≥1%; 5-yr cut): Ⓐ 36% vs Ⓑ 30%; median DoR Ⓐ 24.5 vs Ⓑ 6.7 mo; response ≥5 yr Ⓐ 28% vs Ⓑ 3%
・ORR/DoR (PD-L1 <1%; 5-yr cut): Ⓐ 27% vs Ⓑ 23%; median DoR Ⓐ 19.4 vs Ⓑ 4.8 mo; response ≥5 yr Ⓐ 21%, none Ⓑ
・ORR/DoR (exploratory, TMB ≥10): Ⓐ 45.3% vs Ⓑ 26.9%; median DoR Ⓐ NR vs Ⓑ 5.4 mo; ongoing at 1 yr Ⓐ 68% vs Ⓑ 25%
・Low TMB (<10 mutations per megabase): PFS Ⓐ 3.2 vs Ⓑ 5.5 mo; HR 1.07 (95% CI 0.84–1.35)
・OS by TMB (exploratory): Similar benefit regardless of TMB; low TMB HR 0.75 (0.59–0.94), high TMB HR 0.68 (0.51–0.91)
・Subgroups (PFS, TMB ≥10): Benefit at PD-L1 ≥1% (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.44–0.88) and <1% (HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.27–0.85)
・Subgroups (OS, PD-L1 ≥1%): Most favoured Ⓐ; exceptions liver metastases and never-smokers
・Subgroups (OS, 5-yr cut): Lower effect at PD-L1 1%–49% (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.72–1.12) vs ≥50% (0.69, 0.54–0.86); not powered
・Nivolumab vs chemotherapy (secondary; TMB ≥13, PD-L1 ≥1%): PFS 4.2 vs 5.6 mo; HR 0.95 (97.5% CI 0.61–1.48)
・Other comparisons: Nivo+chemo vs chemo (PD-L1 <1%) 2-yr PFS 10.5% vs 4.6%, HR 0.73 (97.72% CI 0.56–0.95, P=0.007); OS HR 0.78 (97.72% CI 0.60–1.02) missed nominal 0.023 (P=0.035); nivo mono vs chemo OS not formally tested
・Other comparisons (5-yr cut, descriptive): Nivo+chemo vs chemo (PD-L1 <1%) OS HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.64–1.00); nivo vs chemo (PD-L1 ≥1%) OS HR 0.92 (0.79–1.07)
・OS after TRAE discontinuation (5-yr cut): Discontinuation Ⓐ 17% vs Ⓑ 8%; 5-yr OS Ⓐ 39% vs Ⓑ 20%
・2-yr immunotherapy completers: 12% (133); 5-yr OS Ⓐ 72% (PD-L1 ≥1%) and 56% (PD-L1 <1%)
・QoL (5-yr survivors): EQ-5D VAS Ⓐ improved then at or above US general-population norm
・Toxicity: Grade 3/4 TRAEs Ⓐ 32.8% vs Ⓑ 36.0%; serious TRAEs Ⓐ 24.5% vs Ⓑ 13.9%; discontinuation Ⓐ 18.1% vs Ⓑ 9.1%; deaths Ⓐ 1.4% vs Ⓑ 1.1%, pneumonitis in 4 Ⓐ deaths
・Toxicity (5-yr cut): No new safety signals; no new treatment-related deaths
・Limitations: Open-label; proportional-hazards assumption not met for OS; TMB evaluated in 58.2%

Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, overall survival by PD-L1 expression level, progression-free survival by PD-L1 expression level, objective response rate by PD-L1 expression level, time to response, duration of response, efficacy by tumour mutational burden, safety Nivolumab plus ipilimumab with two chemotherapy cycles maintained durable overall-survival, PFS and response benefit versus four chemotherapy cycles alone at final 6-year analysis in first-line metastatic/recurrent NSCLC

・PFS, final 6-yr cut: HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.59-0.82); 6-yr PFS Ⓐ 9% vs Ⓑ 3%
・ORR, final 6-yr cut: Ⓐ 38% vs Ⓑ 25%; complete response Ⓐ 4% vs Ⓑ 1% (4-yr cut, not re-reported)
・DoR, final 6-yr cut: Ⓐ 13.0 vs Ⓑ 5.6 mo; ongoing response at 6 yr Ⓐ 19% vs Ⓑ not available
・OS, switching-adjusted (IPCW), exploratory, 4-yr cut: Adjusted HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.55-0.80) vs unadjusted 0.74; Ⓑ median OS 10.9→9.7 mo; 37% of Ⓑ received subsequent immunotherapy (6-yr cut)
・Stopped for TRAEs, exploratory: Ⓐ all-drug discontinuation (n=61): median OS 27.5 mo; 6-yr OS 34%
・Brain mets, post hoc, 3-yr cut: OS Ⓐ 19.3 vs Ⓑ 6.8 mo; HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.29-0.70); 3-yr OS Ⓐ 28% vs Ⓑ 12%
・Brain-mets PFS, post hoc, 3-yr cut: Systemic Ⓐ 9.7 vs Ⓑ 4.1 mo, HR 0.44 (95% CI 0.28-0.69); intracranial Ⓐ 11.4 vs Ⓑ 4.6 mo, HR 0.42 (95% CI 0.26-0.68)

・Toxicity: No new TRAEs, treatment-related deaths or IMAEs at 6 years, detail in unsupplied supplement; 3-yr cut G3-4 TRAEs Ⓐ 48% vs Ⓑ 38%, TR deaths Ⓐ 2% vs Ⓑ 2%
・Limitations: Open-label; treatment-switching, TRAE-discontinuation, brain-metastasis and mutation analyses exploratory/post hoc, small mutation subgroups; chemotherapy control no longer standard of care

records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body:
Locally advanced (stage IIIB) or metastatic (stage IV) nonsquamous NSCLC, histologically confirmed per AJCC seventh edition; first-line, treatment naive, not amenable to curative surgery or radiotherapy; without known sensitizing EGFR mutations or ALK rearrangements by tissue-based analyses; adults aged 18–75 y Ⓐ Tislelizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks + carboplatin AUC 5 or cisplatin 75 mg/m² with pemetrexed 500 mg/m², four to six induction cycles, then maintenance tislelizumab plus pemetrexed
Ⓑ Carboplatin AUC 5 or cisplatin 75 mg/m² with pemetrexed 500 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks, four to six induction cycles, then maintenance pemetrexed
・Duration: Until radiographic or clinical progression, unacceptable toxic effects, investigator decision or consent withdrawal
・Design: Open-label, multicenter Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: PFS by investigator assessment, PFS by PD-L1 expression, objective response rate, duration of response, time to response, overall survival, safety First-line tislelizumab plus platinum-pemetrexed continued to prolong PFS versus chemotherapy alone at final analysis; overall survival did not differ
・PFS (final analysis): Ⓐ 9.8 vs Ⓑ 7.6 mo; HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.47–0.86)
・ORR: Ⓐ 57.8% vs Ⓑ 36.0%
・DoR: Ⓐ 10.6 vs Ⓑ 6.9 mo
・OS (final analysis): Ⓐ 21.4 vs Ⓑ 21.3 mo; HR 0.90 (95% CI 0.63–1.28)
・OS update: Ad hoc DCO (median follow-up 19.3 mo) HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.63–1.14); post hoc two-stage crossover-adjusted HR 0.71 (0.47–1.07, final) and 0.68 (0.48–0.96, ad hoc)
・Subgroups: PFS benefit greater at TC PD-L1 ≥50% (HR 0.29) than <1% (HR 0.83); exploratory
・Toxicity: Serious TEAEs Ⓐ 39.2% vs Ⓑ 22.7%; fatal pneumonitis Ⓐ 1.4% vs Ⓑ 0.9%, fatal myocarditis Ⓐ 0.5%; interim G≥3 neutropenia 44.6% vs 35.5%, leukopenia 21.6% vs 14.5%, serious pneumonitis Ⓐ 5.9% vs Ⓑ 0.9%
・Limitations: Open-label, China-only enrollment; OS confounded by Ⓑ-arm crossover to tislelizumab; not powered for OS superiority

records.title: RATIONALE-307
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body:
Treatment-naive, histologically confirmed locally advanced (stage IIIB) or metastatic (stage IV) squamous NSCLC not amenable to curative surgery or radiotherapy; unselected for PD-L1 expression but tumor tissue required for PD-L1 assessment; age 18-75 years, mixed histology eligible if squamous component predominated; excluded EGFR-sensitizing sequence variants, ALK fusions, interstitial lung disease, noninfectious pneumonitis Ⓐ Tislelizumab 200 mg IV day 1 + paclitaxel 175 mg/m² day 1 + carboplatin AUC 5 day 1, every 3 weeks
Ⓑ Tislelizumab 200 mg IV day 1 + nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m² days 1, 8, and 15 + carboplatin AUC 5 day 1, every 3 weeks
Ⓒ Paclitaxel 175 mg/m² day 1 + carboplatin AUC 5 day 1, every 3 weeks
・Duration: Tislelizumab until lack of clinical benefit or intolerable toxicity; doublet chemotherapy 4–6 cycles or until progression or intolerable toxicity
・Design: Open-label Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, investigator-assessed PFS, objective response rate, duration of response, disease control rate, health-related quality of life, PD-L1 expression as a predictive biomarker, adverse events Tislelizumab plus paclitaxel–carboplatin or nab-paclitaxel–carboplatin maintained superior PFS and higher ORR vs chemotherapy alone in first-line advanced squamous NSCLC (final analysis)
・PFS, Ⓐ vs Ⓒ (final; P descriptive): 7.7 vs 5.5 mo; HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.33-0.62)
・PFS, Ⓑ vs Ⓒ (final; P descriptive): 9.6 vs 5.5 mo; HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.31-0.60)
・OS, Ⓐ vs Ⓒ: Final 22.8 vs 20.2 mo, HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.46-1.01); updated cut HR 0.69 (0.50-0.95)
・OS, Ⓑ vs Ⓒ: Final NE vs 20.2 mo, HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.50-1.12); updated cut HR 0.84 (0.61-1.14)
・OS, two-stage crossover-adjusted (post hoc, updated cut): Ⓐ HR 0.57 (0.37-0.87); Ⓑ HR 0.65 (0.40-1.05)
・ORR: Ⓐ 74.2% vs Ⓑ 73.9% vs Ⓒ 47.9% (final)
・DoR: Ⓐ 8.4 vs Ⓑ 8.6 vs Ⓒ 4.3 mo (final)
・Subgroups: PFS benefit consistent across PD-L1 expression, disease stage, age, sex, smoking and liver-metastasis subgroups (final)
・Toxicity: ≥G3 treatment-related AEs Ⓐ 86.7% vs Ⓑ 83.9% vs Ⓒ 80.3%; fatal TEAEs Ⓐ 4, Ⓑ 7, Ⓒ 5, none solely tislelizumab; no new safety signals
・Limitations: Open-label (blinded IRC); OS not powered for superiority with 58.7% arm Ⓒ crossover; China-only population

records.title: HARMONi-6
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · Randomised, double-blind clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Advanced unresectable stage IIIB, IIIC or IV squamous NSCLC; first-line, no previous systemic therapy; aged 18–75, ECOG 0–1, ≥1 measurable RECIST 1.1 lesion; excluded EGFR mutation or ALK translocation, active or ≥1·5 cm CNS metastases, tumour necrosis/cavitation with high bleeding risk or major blood vessel invasion, autoimmune disease, steroid-requiring pneumonitis/ILD Ⓐ Ivonescimab 20 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks
Ⓑ Tislelizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks
・Backbone: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m² and carboplatin AUC 5 mg/mL per min IV every 3 weeks for up to four cycles, then assigned-antibody monotherapy maintenance
・Duration: Until no more clinical benefit, unacceptable toxicity, new antitumour treatment, or 24 months total Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, duration of response, time to response, safety, pharmacokinetic profiles, immunogenicity, correlation between PD-L1 status and treatment efficacy, health-related quality of life Ivonescimab plus chemotherapy improved progression-free and overall survival versus tislelizumab plus chemotherapy as first-line treatment of advanced squamous NSCLC, regardless of PD-L1 status
・PFS (primary, interim): Ⓐ 11·1 vs Ⓑ 6·9 mo; HR 0·60 (95% CI 0·46–0·78), one-sided p<0·0001; median follow-up 10·3 mo
・OS (interim, median follow-up 21·4 mo): Ⓐ 27·9 vs Ⓑ 23·7 mo; HR 0·66 (95% CI 0·50–0·87), one-sided p=0·0017, met prespecified boundary (p<0·0049)
・24-mo OS: Ⓐ 64·7% vs Ⓑ 48·6%
・ORR: Ⓐ 76% vs Ⓑ 67%
・DoR: Ⓐ 11·2 vs Ⓑ 8·4 mo
・QoL: Time to deterioration not reached Ⓐ vs 12·4 mo Ⓑ; HR 0·94 (95% CI 0·71–1·25)
・PFS subgroups: Benefit across PD-L1 TPS <1% (HR 0·55), 1–49% (0·63), ≥50% (0·71); not powered for subgroups
・OS subgroups: PD-L1 TPS <1% HR 0·64 (95% CI 0·43–0·96), 1–49% 0·67 (0·42–1·05), ≥50% 0·64 (0·32–1·31); descriptive, not powered
・Toxicity (interim OS cut): G≥3 TRAEs Ⓐ 69% vs Ⓑ 59%; G≥3 haemorrhage Ⓐ 3% vs Ⓑ 1%; G≥3 irAEs 14% vs 14%; fatal TRAEs 4% vs 4%
・Anti-VEGF AEs: Any Ⓐ 60% vs Ⓑ 26%, mostly grade 1–2; G≥3 renal injury/proteinuria Ⓐ 7% vs Ⓑ 0
・Limitations: Interim analyses (final OS after 322 events); median OS reached on last single event; all-Chinese population, few women, none aged >75

records.title: CAMPASS
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · Randomised, blinded, controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Stage IIIB–IV squamous or non-squamous NSCLC, first-line (no previous systemic treatment for advanced, recurrent or metastatic disease); PD-L1 TPS 1% or greater; age 18–75 years, ECOG 0–1, at least one measurable lesion; excluded EGFR, ALK or ROS1 alterations (not mandatory for squamous), centrally located squamous carcinoma with cavity, haemorrhage risk, untreated or symptomatic CNS metastases Ⓐ Benmelstobart 1200 mg IV on day 1 plus anlotinib 12 mg orally once daily on days 1–14, every 3 weeks
Ⓑ Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV on day 1 plus placebo orally on days 1–14, every 3 weeks
・Duration: Until confirmed disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or other protocol-prespecified conditions; benmelstobart/pembrolizumab exposure capped at 2 years
・Design: Masked to patients and statisticians; open-label for investigators Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, progression-free survival (investigator-assessed), objective response rate, disease control rate, duration of response, 6-month progression-free survival rate, 12-month progression-free survival rate, 12-month overall survival rate, safety, quality of life, immunogenicity Benmelstobart plus anlotinib improved progression-free survival versus pembrolizumab monotherapy in first-line, driver gene-negative, PD-L1-positive advanced NSCLC
・PFS (final analysis): Ⓐ 11.0 vs Ⓑ 7.1 mo; HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.54–0.90)
・ORR: Ⓐ 57% vs Ⓑ 40%; nominal p=0.0001
・DCR: Ⓐ 86% vs Ⓑ 79%; nominal p=0.047
・DoR: Ⓐ 12.3 mo vs Ⓑ not reached
・OS: Immature; 12-month OS Ⓐ 74% vs Ⓑ 71%
・Subgroups: No PFS benefit at PD-L1 TPS 1–49% (HR 0.79, 0.57–1.11), non-squamous histology (0.83, 0.54–1.27) or bone metastases (1.21, 0.66–2.22); benefit at TPS ≥50% (0.60, 0.41–0.88)
・Toxicity: G≥3 TRAEs Ⓐ 59% vs Ⓑ 29%; hypertension 26% vs 3%; serious TRAEs 25% vs 21%; fatal TRAEs 1% vs 2%, two haemoptysis deaths in Ⓐ
・Limitations: OS immature; pembrolizumab-alone control despite preferred chemo-immunotherapy at TPS 1–49%; all-Chinese population, short follow-up

records.title: POD1UM-304
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Stage IV squamous or non-squamous NSCLC (AJCC v8), first-line (no previous systemic therapy for metastatic disease); prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant therapy allowed if completed ≥12 months before metastatic disease and without PD-1 or PD-L1 therapy; non-squamous tumours with EGFR, ALK, BRAF or ROS1 driver mutations or rearrangements excluded Ⓐ Retifanlimab 375 mg IV on day 1 of each 21-day cycle
Ⓑ Placebo IV on day 1 of each 21-day cycle
・Non-squamous NSCLC chemotherapy: Pemetrexed 500 mg/m² plus cisplatin 75 mg/m², or carboplatin AUC 5, day 1 for four cycles, then pemetrexed 500 mg/m² every 21 days
・Squamous NSCLC chemotherapy: Carboplatin AUC 6 plus paclitaxel 200 mg/m² day 1 for four cycles, or nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m² on days 1, 8 and 15 for four cycles
・Duration: Retifanlimab or placebo up to 35 cycles (~2 years) unless progression, unacceptable toxicity or consent withdrawal; pemetrexed maintenance until progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, safety and tolerability, retifanlimab pharmacokinetics Adding retifanlimab to first-line platinum-based chemotherapy improved overall survival versus placebo plus chemotherapy in metastatic squamous or non-squamous NSCLC
・OS (final analysis): Ⓐ 18.1 vs Ⓑ 13.4 mo; HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.60–0.93)
・OS, crossover-adjusted (RPSFTM): HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.56–0.86); 59 (31%) of Ⓑ crossed over
・PFS: Ⓐ 7.7 vs Ⓑ 5.5 mo; HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.52–0.79)
・ORR: Ⓐ 52% vs Ⓑ 39%
・DoR: Ⓐ 12.7 vs Ⓑ 6.1 mo
・Subgroups: OS benefit consistent regardless of squamous vs non-squamous histology; no clear OS benefit at PD-L1 TPS <1% (HR 1.02, 95% CI 0.69–1.48)
・Toxicity: G≥3 TEAEs Ⓐ 61% vs Ⓑ 54%; serious 41% vs 30%; fatal 10% vs 11%; fatal COVID-19 1% vs 3%
・Limitations: Crossover to retifanlimab at progression in Ⓑ; replication design; PD-L1 TPS <1% estimate imprecise

records.title: IMpower132
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body:
Stage IV nonsquamous NSCLC (AJCC seventh edition), first-line (no previous treatment for metastatic disease), measurable disease per RECIST 1.1, ECOG PS 0 or 1; no sensitizing EGFR mutation or ALK alteration; treatment-free interval ≥6 months if prior curative-intent chemotherapy/radiotherapy; excluded untreated CNS metastases, autoimmune disease, prior immunotherapy Ⓐ Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV every 21 days + pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 6 mg/mL/min or cisplatin 75 mg/m² → maintenance atezolizumab + pemetrexed every 21 days
Ⓑ Pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 6 mg/mL/min or cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV → maintenance pemetrexed every 21 days
・Induction: Four to six 21-day cycles, number at investigator discretion
・Duration: Maintenance until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or death
・Design: Open-label Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, safety Adding atezolizumab to carboplatin/cisplatin plus pemetrexed improved PFS but did not meet the co-primary OS end point versus chemotherapy alone
・PFS: Ⓐ 7.6 vs Ⓑ 5.2 mo; stratified HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.49–0.72), p < 0.0001
・PFS, final cut: Ⓐ 7.7 vs Ⓑ 5.2 mo; HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.47–0.67)
・OS, final cut: Ⓐ 17.5 vs Ⓑ 13.6 mo; stratified HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.71–1.06), p = 0.1546
・OS, interim cut: Ⓐ 18.1 vs Ⓑ 13.6 mo; stratified HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.64–1.03), p = 0.0797
・ORR: Ⓐ 47% vs Ⓑ 32%; median DOR 10.1 vs 7.2 mo
・Subgroups: Asian PFS Ⓐ 10.2 vs Ⓑ 5.3 mo, HR 0.42 (95% CI 0.28–0.63); exploratory PD-L1-high PFS Ⓐ 10.8 vs Ⓑ 6.5 mo, HR 0.46 (95% CI 0.22–0.96)
・Toxicity: G3/4 TRAEs Ⓐ 54.6% vs Ⓑ 40.1%; grade 5 TRAEs Ⓐ 3.8% vs Ⓑ 2.9%; G3/4 immune-mediated AEs Ⓐ 15.1% vs Ⓑ 6.9%
・Limitations: Open-label; exploratory PD-L1 subgroups (59.5% biomarker-assessable); more subsequent immunotherapy in Ⓑ (45.8%) than Ⓐ (5.5%)

records.title: Di Federico et al.
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · Individual patient data meta-analysis · 2026
records.body:
Advanced/metastatic NSCLC with high PD-L1 expression (TPS 50% or higher; IMpower trials: 50% or higher in tumor cells or 10% or higher in immune cells), treatment-naive, first-line; pooled phase 3 RCTs of PD-(L)1 inhibitor monotherapy or chemoimmunotherapy vs platinum-based chemotherapy; ECOG PS 0 to 1; treated/controlled asymptomatic brain metastases allowed; trials with only CTLA-4 inhibitor-containing experimental arms excluded Ⓐ PD-(L)1 inhibitor plus platinum-based chemotherapy (chemoimmunotherapy)
Ⓑ PD-(L)1 inhibitor monotherapy
・Benchmark: Platinum-based chemotherapy alone, shared control of all pooled trials
・Regimens: Specific PD-(L)1 inhibitors and platinum doublets varied across the 24 included phase 3 RCTs
・Design: Indirect comparison, no head-to-head trial; IPD reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, treatment-related adverse events, discontinuation due to treatment-related adverse events Chemoimmunotherapy was associated with improved OS and PFS vs PD-(L)1 inhibitor monotherapy in PD-L1-high advanced NSCLC (indirect comparison of phase 3 RCTs)
・OS: Ⓐ 29.2 vs Ⓑ 19.8 mo (reconstructed IPD; median follow-up 51.4 mo); HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.66-0.82)
・PFS: Ⓐ 11.3 vs Ⓑ 6.8 mo; HR 0.67 (95% CI 0.60-0.75)
・OS vs chemo: Ⓐ HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.56-0.72) vs Ⓑ HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.69-0.80)
・PFS vs chemo: Ⓐ HR 0.44 (95% CI 0.39-0.49) vs Ⓑ HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.65-0.76)
・Indirect (meta-regression, NMA): OS HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.73-0.99); PFS HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.50-0.75)
・Sensitivity, 5-yr follow-up trials: OS HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.70-0.97); PFS HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.65-0.89)
・Toxicity: Any-grade TRAEs vs chemo RR Ⓐ 1.01 (95% CI 1.00-1.02) vs Ⓑ 0.76 (95% CI 0.72-0.80); Ⓐ also more grade 3 or higher TRAEs and discontinuations (overall trial populations)
・Limitations: Indirect comparison, no head-to-head RCT; IPD reconstructed, not original datasets; safety from overall trial populations

records.title: Aguilar et al.
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · Retrospective cohort study · 2019
records.body:
Advanced NSCLC without EGFR mutations or ALK rearrangements and PD-L1 expression ≥50%; first-line commercial pembrolizumab monotherapy at four academic centres; prior chemo/radiotherapy for early-stage NSCLC eligible if completed ≥6 months before pembrolizumab start (single-arm) Pembrolizumab monotherapy (commercial, first-line) Primary: overall response rate, progression-free survival, overall survival In a retrospective first-line pembrolizumab cohort, PD-L1 90–100% was associated with higher ORR and longer PFS and OS than PD-L1 50–89%
・ORR: 44.4% overall (95% CI 37.1–51.8); 60.0% PD-L1 90–100% vs 32.7% 50–89%, P < 0.001
・PFS: 14.5 vs 4.1 mo (PD-L1 90–100% vs 50–89%); HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.33–0.74)
・OS: Not reached vs 15.9 mo (PD-L1 90–100% vs 50–89%); HR 0.39 (95% CI 0.21–0.70)
・Cohort: mPFS 6.5 mo (95% CI 4.5–8.5); mOS not reached; median follow-up 12.6 mo
・PD-L1 75–100% vs 50–74%: ORR 53.6% vs 30.7%; PFS 7.8 vs 4.3 mo (HR 0.63); OS not significantly different
・TMB: Not associated with PFS [HR 0.98 (95% CI 0.95–1.02)] or OS [HR 0.96 (95% CI 0.91–1.01)]
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: Retrospective; mixed PD-L1 immunohistochemical assays; non-trial population (18.2% ECOG PS ≥2)

records.title: OptiTROP-Lung06
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Locally advanced (stage IIIB or IIIC) or metastatic (stage IV) nonsquamous NSCLC not amenable to curative surgery or chemoradiotherapy; no previous systemic therapy; PD-L1 tumor proportion score <1% by central 22C3 assay; without targetable genomic alterations (no sensitizing EGFR mutations or ALK rearrangements); meningeal, brain-stem, spinal-cord metastases or compression and active or untreated CNS metastases excluded Ⓐ Sacituzumab tirumotecan 4 mg/kg IV on days 1, 15 and 29 of each 6-week cycle
Ⓑ Pemetrexed 500 mg/m² IV plus investigator's-choice carboplatin AUC 5 or cisplatin 75 mg/m² on days 1 and 22 of each 6-week cycle; platinum for maximum 2 cycles, then pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed maintenance
・Pembrolizumab: 400 mg IV on day 1 of each 6-week cycle (both arms), up to 18 cycles
・Duration: Until BICR-determined progression, unacceptable toxic effects, withdrawal of consent, or another protocol-specified discontinuation criterion Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, progression-free survival (investigator), objective response, duration of response, time to response, safety, patient-reported outcomes (global health status and quality of life), pharmacokinetics, immunogenicity First-line sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab significantly prolonged progression-free survival versus chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab in PD-L1–negative advanced nonsquamous NSCLC
・PFS (interim): Ⓐ 15.0 vs Ⓑ 5.7 mo; HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.36–0.65)
・OS: Immature at interim; HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.38–0.88); 12-mo OS Ⓐ 77.6% vs Ⓑ 66.4%
・ORR: Ⓐ 50.2% vs Ⓑ 47.3%
・DoR: Ⓐ 13.6 vs Ⓑ 6.8 mo; HR for loss of response 0.47 (95% CI 0.29–0.77)
・QoL: Time to deterioration Ⓐ 6.9 vs Ⓑ 5.1 mo; HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.66–1.13)
・Subgroups: Consistent PFS benefit across Trop-2 expression; high (H score >200) HR 0.59 (95% CI 0.37–0.92), low (≤200) HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.30–0.80)
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 47.6% vs Ⓑ 60.6%; stomatitis Ⓐ 51.1% any grade (G≥3 2.2%); AEs resulting in death Ⓐ 2.2% vs Ⓑ 6.2%
・Limitations: Prespecified interim (median follow-up 9.7 mo), OS immature; conducted exclusively in China; active or untreated CNS metastases excluded
records.keywords: Zhou et al. N Engl J Med 2026 (online ahead of print)

records.title: PARAMOUNT
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Chemotherapy & maintenance · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2012
records.body:
Advanced non-squamous NSCLC (stage IIIB or IV); continuation maintenance after four induction cycles of pemetrexed plus cisplatin without progression (complete or partial response or stable disease), ECOG PS 0–1; no previous systemic chemotherapy including adjuvant; excluded predominantly squamous-cell or mixed small-cell histology; treated stable CNS metastases allowed off corticosteroids ≥4 weeks Ⓐ Pemetrexed 500 mg/m² IV day 1 of a 21-day cycle + best supportive care
Ⓑ Placebo (0·9% sodium chloride) IV day 1 of a 21-day cycle + best supportive care
・Induction: Pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV day 1 of a 21-day cycle, four cycles
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable adverse events, or decision of patient or physician
・Design: Double-blind (patients and investigators masked) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: tumour response rate, patient-reported outcomes, resource use, adverse events, overall survival Continuation maintenance with pemetrexed improved progression-free survival and, on final analysis, overall survival versus placebo after pemetrexed–cisplatin induction in advanced non-squamous NSCLC
・PFS: Ⓐ 4·1 vs Ⓑ 2·8 mo; HR 0·62 (95% CI 0·49–0·79)
・PFS, OS-datalock reassessment: Ⓐ 4·4 vs Ⓑ 2·8 mo; HR 0·60 (95% CI 0·50–0·73)
・PFS, independent review: Ⓐ 3·9 vs Ⓑ 2·6 mo; HR 0·64 (95% CI 0·51–0·81)
・ORR: Ⓐ 3% vs Ⓑ 0·6%; p=0·18 (independent review)
・DCR: Ⓐ 72% vs Ⓑ 60%; p=0·009 (independent review)
・OS, final: Ⓐ 13·9 vs Ⓑ 11·0 mo; HR 0·78 (95% CI 0·64–0·96); p=0·0195
・Subgroups, PFS: Induction CR/PR HR 0·48 (0·34–0·67) vs SD 0·74 (0·53–1·04); exploratory
・Subgroups, OS: Consistent across all subgroups; induction CR/PR HR 0·81 (0·59–1·11), SD 0·76 (0·57–1·01), not powered
・QoL: No overall EQ-5D treatment differences during maintenance
・Toxicity: Drug-related G3–4 anaemia Ⓐ 6·4% vs Ⓑ 0·6%, neutropenia Ⓐ 5·8% vs Ⓑ 0, fatigue Ⓐ 4·7% vs Ⓑ 1·1%; drug-related deaths Ⓐ 1 (pneumonia) vs Ⓑ 2
・Limitations: Enrolled only good performance status with disease control after induction

records.title: MARIPOSA-2
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body:
Locally advanced or metastatic EGFR-mutated (Ex19del or L858R) NSCLC with disease progression on or after osimertinib monotherapy as the most recent line of treatment; brain metastases eligible if clinically stable, asymptomatic, on stable steroid doses, without requirement for prior definitive radiation or surgery Ⓐ Amivantamab + carboplatin–pemetrexed chemotherapy
Ⓑ Amivantamab + lazertinib + carboplatin–pemetrexed chemotherapy (lazertinib start deferred until after carboplatin completion by mid-trial amendment)
Ⓒ Carboplatin–pemetrexed chemotherapy alone
・Amivantamab: 1400 mg IV weekly for first 4 weeks (1750 mg if ≥80 kg), then 1750 mg (2100 mg if ≥80 kg) every 3 weeks from cycle 3
・Lazertinib: 240 mg orally daily
・Chemotherapy: Pemetrexed 500 mg/m² IV every 21-day cycle; carboplatin AUC 5 IV for first four cycles
・Duration: Amivantamab, lazertinib and pemetrexed until disease progression or lack of clinical benefit
・Design: Open-label (blinding not possible) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, overall survival, PFS after first subsequent therapy, symptomatic PFS, intracranial PFS, safety Amivantamab-chemotherapy and amivantamab-lazertinib-chemotherapy improved PFS and intracranial PFS versus chemotherapy after progression on osimertinib
・PFS: Ⓐ 6.3 vs Ⓒ 4.2 mo; HR 0.48 (95% CI 0.36-0.64); Ⓑ 8.3 vs Ⓒ 4.2 mo; HR 0.44 (95% CI 0.35-0.56)
・ORR: Ⓐ 64% vs Ⓒ 36%, OR 3.10 (95% CI 2.00-4.80); Ⓑ 63% vs Ⓒ 36%, OR 2.97 (95% CI 2.08-4.24)
・DoR: Ⓐ 6.9 and Ⓑ 9.4 vs Ⓒ 5.6 mo
・Intracranial PFS: Ⓐ 12.5 and Ⓑ 12.8 vs Ⓒ 8.3 mo; HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.38-0.79) and 0.58 (95% CI 0.44-0.78)
・OS: First interim analysis; HR Ⓐ 0.77 (95% CI 0.49-1.21), Ⓑ 0.96 (95% CI 0.67-1.35)
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 72%, Ⓑ 92%, Ⓒ 48%; VTE Ⓐ 10%, Ⓑ 22%, Ⓒ 5%; fatal treatment-related AEs Ⓐ 2%, Ⓑ 2%, Ⓒ 0.4%
・Limitations: Open-label; OS at first interim analysis only; mid-trial lazertinib deferral limits Ⓑ regimen evaluation

records.title: COMPEL
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Locally advanced, metastatic or recurrent EGFR-mutated NSCLC (Ex19del or L858R, alone or with other EGFR mutations); second-line after radiological non-CNS progression on first-line osimertinib, following response or stable disease ≥6 months, with no subsequent treatment; with or without stable CNS metastases; measurable disease per RECIST v1.1 Ⓐ Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily
Ⓑ Placebo once daily
・Chemotherapy: Cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC5 plus pemetrexed 500 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks for four cycles, then maintenance pemetrexed 500 mg/m² q3w (platinum chosen by investigator before randomization)
・Duration: Until RECIST v1.1 or CNS RECIST v1.1 progression or another discontinuation criterion; continuation beyond progression allowed for clinical benefit Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: CNS PFS in patients with and without baseline CNS metastases, non-CNS PFS, overall survival, non-CNS objective response rate, best objective response, duration of response, safety Continuing osimertinib beyond progression, with added chemotherapy, was associated with improved PFS and longer OS vs placebo plus chemotherapy
・PFS: Ⓐ 8.4 vs Ⓑ 4.4 mo; HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.27-0.70)
・CNS PFS, no baseline CNS metastases: Ⓐ 15.9 vs Ⓑ 8.6 mo; HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.27-1.13)
・CNS PFS, baseline CNS metastases: 6-mo rates Ⓐ 82% vs Ⓑ 56%; HR not calculated
・Non-CNS PFS: Ⓐ 8.4 vs Ⓑ 5.2 mo; HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.26-0.71)
・OS: Ⓐ 15.9 vs Ⓑ 9.8 mo; HR 0.71 (95% CI 0.42-1.23)
・Non-CNS ORR, post hoc: Ⓐ 35% vs Ⓑ 29%
・New brain lesions at progression: Ⓐ 10% vs Ⓑ 27%
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 63% vs Ⓑ 46%; G≥3 neutropenia Ⓐ 15%, anemia 13% both arms; fatal AEs one per arm, not treatment-related
・Limitations: Descriptive analysis without hypothesis testing, enrolment cut from ~204 planned; placebo arm could receive open-label osimertinib after CNS progression

records.title: REVEL
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2014
records.body:
Stage IV NSCLC (squamous or non-squamous) progressed during or after one first-line platinum regimen ± maintenance/bevacizumab; ECOG PS 0–1; excluded EGFR-TKI-only prior therapy, untreated CNS metastases, major blood vessel involvement, intratumour cavitation, poorly controlled hypertension, GI perforation/fistulae, arterial thromboembolic event within 6 months, gross haemoptysis within 2 months, grade 3–4 GI bleeding within 3 months Ⓐ Ramucirumab 10 mg/kg IV plus docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV day 1 of a 21-day cycle
Ⓑ Placebo IV plus docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV day 1 of a 21-day cycle
・Duration: Until radiographically confirmed disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal, or death
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled; stratified by sex, region, performance status, previous maintenance therapy Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, quality of life (LCSS), safety Ramucirumab plus docetaxel improved overall survival versus placebo plus docetaxel as second-line treatment of stage IV NSCLC
・OS: Ⓐ 10.5 vs Ⓑ 9.1 mo; HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.75–0.98)
・PFS: Ⓐ 4.5 vs Ⓑ 3.0 mo; HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.68–0.86)
・ORR: Ⓐ 23% vs Ⓑ 14%; OR 1.89 (95% CI 1.41–2.54)
・DCR: Ⓐ 64% vs Ⓑ 53%; OR 1.60 (95% CI 1.28–2.01)
・QoL: Time to deterioration of global quality of life did not differ; HR 1.00 (95% CI 0.84–1.19)
・Subgroups: Non-squamous OS HR 0.83 (0.71–0.97); squamous HR 0.88 (0.69–1.13); not powered for subgroup analysis
・Toxicity: G≥3 neutropenia Ⓐ 49% vs Ⓑ 40%; febrile neutropenia Ⓐ 16% vs Ⓑ 10%; hypertension Ⓐ 6% vs Ⓑ 2%; deaths from AEs 5% vs 6%, not different
・Limitations: ECOG PS ≥2 and anti-angiogenic high-risk patients excluded, limiting generalisability; benefit in elderly uncertain

records.title: EAST-LC
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · Randomised, open-label, non-inferiority clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body:
Locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC, second- or third-line after platinum-based chemotherapy; age ≥20 years, ECOG PS ≤2, ≤2 previous regimens including ≥1 platinum-based (three if prior EGFR-TKI gefitinib/erlotinib); run in Japan, China, Hong Kong, Singapore, Taiwan Ⓐ S-1 80–120 mg/day orally twice daily by body surface area (<1.25 m2: 80 mg; ≥1.25 to <1.5 m2: 100 mg; ≥1.5 m2: 120 mg), days 1–28 of a 6-week cycle
Ⓑ Docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV day 1 of a 3-week cycle (60 mg/m² at Japanese sites)
・Design: Open-label, non-inferiority Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, time to treatment failure, response rate, quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30, QLQ-LC13), safety S-1 was non-inferior to docetaxel in OS as second- or third-line therapy for previously treated advanced NSCLC, with different toxicity and QoL profiles
・OS: Ⓐ 12.75 vs Ⓑ 12.52 mo; HR 0.945 (95% CI 0.833–1.073); non-inferiority confirmed, upper CI limit below 1.2
・PFS: Ⓐ 2.86 vs Ⓑ 2.89 mo; HR 1.033 (95% CI 0.913–1.168)
・TTF: Ⓐ 2.66 vs Ⓑ 2.56 mo; HR 0.886 (95% CI 0.788–0.997)
・ORR: Ⓐ 8.3% vs Ⓑ 9.9%
・QoL: EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status better with Ⓐ to 48 weeks; P=0.0065
・Subgroups: PFS interactions with EGFR mutation (P=0.002) and sex (P=0.0154), Ⓐ favoured in EGFR wild-type and males; no OS interactions
・Toxicity: G3–4 neutropenia Ⓐ 5.4% vs Ⓑ 47.7%; febrile neutropenia Ⓐ 0.9% vs Ⓑ 13.6%; Ⓐ appetite loss and diarrhoea, Ⓑ neutropenia and alopecia; treatment-related deaths in both arms
・Limitations: Open-label; docetaxel control chosen before anti-PD-1/PD-L1 second-line standard; QoL mean differences small

records.title: HARMONi
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Stage IIIB/IIIC or IV non-squamous NSCLC with any EGFR activation mutation; progression after a third-generation EGFR-TKI; age ≥18 years (upper limit 75 years in Asian cohort), ECOG performance status 0–1; excluded history of severe bleeding tendencies, including haemoptysis Ⓐ Ivonescimab 20 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks
Ⓑ Placebo IV every 3 weeks
・Chemotherapy: Pemetrexed 500 mg/m² plus carboplatin AUC 5 mg/mL per min IV every 3 weeks; carboplatin stopped after four cycles
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, completion of 24 months of treatment, withdrawal of consent, or death
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled; stratified by brain metastases status and geographical region Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, safety, pharmacokinetics, immunogenicity, quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30), intracranial progression-free survival, time to response Ivonescimab plus chemotherapy improved progression-free survival but not overall survival versus placebo plus chemotherapy after EGFR-TKI progression
・PFS: Ⓐ 6.8 vs Ⓑ 4.4 mo; HR 0.52 (95% CI 0.41–0.66)
・PFS, extended cut, post-hoc all enrolled: Ⓐ 6.3 vs Ⓑ 4.8 mo; HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.46–0.71)
・OS: Ⓐ 16.8 vs Ⓑ 14.0 mo; HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.62–1.01); primary analysis not significant (p=0.057)
・OS, extended cut, post-hoc: Ⓐ 16.8 vs Ⓑ 14.0 mo; HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.62–0.98); exploratory, alpha spent
・ORR: Ⓐ 45% vs Ⓑ 34%
・DoR: Ⓐ 7.6 vs Ⓑ 4.2 mo
・Intracranial PFS: Ⓐ 13.7 vs Ⓑ 10.3 mo; HR 0.67 (95% CI 0.53–0.85); exploratory
・QoL: No clinically meaningful differences (≥10 points) in EORTC QLQ-C30 symptoms between groups
・Subgroups: PFS benefit consistent across preplanned subgroups, including brain metastases
・Toxicity: G3–5 TRAEs Ⓐ 50% vs Ⓑ 42%; serious TRAEs Ⓐ 28% vs Ⓑ 15%; TRAE deaths 4 vs 5; G3–5 treatment-related haemorrhage <1% (Ⓐ)
・Limitations: Short Western-cohort OS follow-up (median 9.2 mo); sequential cohort enrolment; mostly Asian or White patients

records.title: HARMONi-A
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body:
Non–small cell lung cancer with EGFR variant; locally advanced or metastatic (stage IIIB, IIIC, or IV per AJCC Eighth Edition) with progression after EGFR-TKI therapy — after first-/second-generation TKI with confirmed T790M-negative status, or after third-generation TKI as first- or second-line treatment; adults aged 18–75 years, ECOG 0–1; excluded small cell or squamous histology, prior systemic antitumor therapy except EGFR-TKIs, prior immunotherapy Ⓐ Ivonescimab 20 mg/kg IV + pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 5 mg/mL/min on day 1 every 3 weeks for 4 cycles, then ivonescimab + pemetrexed maintenance
Ⓑ Placebo IV + pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 5 mg/mL/min on day 1 every 3 weeks for 4 cycles, then placebo + pemetrexed maintenance
・Duration: Until disease progression, intolerable toxic effects, investigator decision, withdrawal of consent, or death
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, disease control rate, time to response, PFS, safety, pharmacokinetic profile, immunogenicity, health-related quality of life Ivonescimab plus chemotherapy improved final overall survival and interim progression-free survival vs placebo plus chemotherapy in EGFR-variant NSCLC after EGFR-TKI therapy
・PFS (interim, IRRC): Ⓐ 7.1 vs Ⓑ 4.8 mo; HR 0.46 (95% CI 0.34-0.62)
・OS (final analysis, median follow-up 32.5 mo): Ⓐ 16.8 vs Ⓑ 14.1 mo; HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.58-0.95)
・30-mo OS: Ⓐ 29.1% vs Ⓑ 18.4% (10.7-point difference)
・ORR: Ⓐ 50.6% vs Ⓑ 35.4%; difference 15.6% (95% CI 5.3-26.0)
・DoR: Ⓐ 6.6 vs Ⓑ 4.2 mo
・QoL (exploratory, EORTC QLQ-C30): Time to deterioration Ⓐ 9.5 vs Ⓑ 7.3 mo; HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.61-1.22)
・Subgroups (PFS, interim): Third-generation EGFR-TKI HR 0.48 (95% CI 0.35-0.66); brain metastases HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.22-0.73)
・Subgroups (OS, final): Leu858Arg HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.41-0.89); third-generation EGFR-TKI HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.58-0.98); brain metastases HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.37-1.03)
・Toxicity (final analysis): G≥3 TEAEs Ⓐ 67.1% vs Ⓑ 54.7%; G≥3 TRAEs Ⓐ 59.6% vs Ⓑ 44.7%; irAEs Ⓐ 29.2% vs Ⓑ 8.1%, no irAE-related deaths; exposure longer with Ⓐ (10.5 vs 8.2 cycles)
・Limitations: Conducted exclusively in China; postprogression therapies nonrandomized, may confound OS; benefit after intensified first-line regimens unproven

records.title: RATIONALE-303
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body:
Locally advanced or metastatic squamous or nonsquamous NSCLC with progressive disease during or after at least one platinum doublet (no more than two previous lines); any PD-L1 expression; ECOG PS 0–1; treated stable brain metastases allowed; excluded prior docetaxel for metastatic disease, prior PD-1/PD-L1/CTLA-4 inhibitors, known EGFR mutation or ALK translocation Ⓐ Tislelizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks
Ⓑ Docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks
・Duration: Until disease progression per RECIST v1.1, intolerable toxicity, or withdrawal of consent
・Design: Open-label, multicentre Primary: overall survival (ITT population), overall survival (PD-L1 ≥ 25% population). Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, health-related quality of life, safety Tislelizumab improved OS versus docetaxel in pretreated advanced NSCLC, meeting both co-primary OS endpoints (ITT and PD-L1 ≥25% populations)
・OS, ITT (final): Ⓐ 16.9 vs Ⓑ 11.9 mo; HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.56–0.79)
・OS, PD-L1 ≥25% (final): Ⓐ 19.3 vs Ⓑ 11.5 mo; HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.40–0.70)
・OS, ITT (interim): Ⓐ 17.2 vs Ⓑ 11.9 mo; HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.53–0.78)
・PFS: HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.53–0.75) ITT; HR 0.37 (95% CI 0.28–0.49) PD-L1 ≥25%
・ORR (ITT): Ⓐ 22.6% vs Ⓑ 7.1%; DoR Ⓐ 13.5 vs Ⓑ 6.0 mo
・Subgroups: Consistent OS benefit across PD-L1 levels, histologies, liver metastases; similar in Asian and White patients
・Biomarkers (exploratory): NOTCH1–4 mutation OS Ⓐ 24.7 vs Ⓑ 7.7 mo, HR 0.22 (95% CI 0.10–0.49); tissue TMB correlated with PFS, not OS
・Toxicity: G≥3 TEAEs Ⓐ 42.1% vs Ⓑ 74.8%; febrile neutropenia Ⓐ 0 vs Ⓑ 12.8%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 1.5% vs Ⓑ 1.6%
・Limitations: Open-label design; poststudy immunotherapy in Ⓑ 20.4%; tissue TMB available for 45% only, small NOTCH-mutant numbers

records.title: TROPION-Lung01
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Advanced/metastatic NSCLC (stage IIIB/C or IV) previously treated; without actionable genomic alterations (AGAs): only platinum-based chemotherapy and anti–PD-1/PD-L1; with AGAs (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, NTRK, BRAF, MET exon 14 skipping, RET): one to two targeted-therapy lines and platinum-based chemotherapy, with or without anti–PD-1/PD-L1; no previous docetaxel; clinically inactive or treated asymptomatic brain metastases eligible; excluded for current/suspected or historic ILD requiring steroids Ⓐ Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) 6 mg/kg IV once every 3 weeks
Ⓑ Docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV once every 3 weeks
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or other reasons
・Design: Open-label Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, disease control rate, duration of response, time to response, safety Dato-DXd significantly improved PFS but not OS versus docetaxel in previously treated advanced/metastatic NSCLC, with benefit driven by nonsquamous histology
・PFS: Ⓐ 4.4 vs Ⓑ 3.7 mo; HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.62–0.91); P = .004
・OS, final analysis: Ⓐ 12.9 vs Ⓑ 11.8 mo; HR 0.94 (95% CI 0.78–1.14); P = .530
・ORR: Ⓐ 26.4% vs Ⓑ 12.8%
・DoR: Ⓐ 7.1 vs Ⓑ 5.6 mo
・Subgroups, nonsquamous: PFS Ⓐ 5.5 vs Ⓑ 3.6 mo, HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.51–0.79); OS Ⓐ 14.6 vs Ⓑ 12.3 mo, HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.68–1.05)
・Subgroups, squamous: PFS Ⓐ 2.8 vs Ⓑ 3.9 mo, HR 1.41 (95% CI 0.95–2.08); OS Ⓐ 7.6 vs Ⓑ 9.4 mo, HR 1.32 (95% CI 0.91–1.92)
・Subgroups, interaction: Treatment-by-histology P = .0006 for PFS, P = .0312 for OS
・Toxicity: G≥3 TRAEs Ⓐ 25.6% vs Ⓑ 42.1%; any-grade stomatitis Ⓐ 47.5% vs Ⓑ 15.5%; adjudicated drug-related ILD/pneumonitis Ⓐ 8.8% (fatal 2.4%) vs Ⓑ 4.1% (fatal 0.3%)
・Limitations: Open-label design; histology subgroup analyses not powered for statistical significance

records.title: TROPION-Lung05
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2025
records.body:
Advanced/metastatic NSCLC with actionable genomic alterations (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, NTRK, BRAF, MET exon 14 skipping, or RET) progressing on or after targeted therapy and platinum chemotherapy; required 1-2 cytotoxic therapies (including 1 platinum regimen) and 1-2 alteration-specific targeted therapies with radiographic progression, measurable disease (RECIST v1.1), ECOG PS 0-1; excluded prior topoisomerase I or TROP2-directed therapy, active CNS metastases, ILD/pneumonitis, KRAS mutations (single-arm) Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) 6.0 mg/kg IV once every 3 weeks
・Duration: Until investigator-assessed radiographic or clinical disease progression, death, withdrawal of consent, loss to follow-up, unacceptable toxicity, or study termination
・Design: Global, open-label Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: duration of response, disease control rate, clinical benefit rate, progression-free survival, time to response, overall survival, safety, tolerability Dato-DXd showed durable antitumor activity in heavily pretreated advanced/metastatic NSCLC with actionable genomic alterations
・ORR: Confirmed 35.8%, including 2.9% complete responses
・DOR: 7.0 mo (95% CI 4.2 to 9.8)
・DCR: 78.8%
・PFS: 5.4 mo (95% CI 4.7 to 7.0)
・OS: 13.6 mo (95% CI 9.9 to NE)
・Subgroups: EGFR-mutant ORR 43.6%, PFS 5.8 mo, OS 18.3 mo; ALK-rearranged ORR 23.5%, PFS 4.3 mo, OS 9.3 mo
・EGFR post-osimertinib: ORR 49.1% in sensitizing/T790M-mutant disease
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 TRAEs 28.5%; stomatitis any grade 56.2%, grade ≥3 9.5%; ocular surface events 26.3%; ILD/pneumonitis 3.6%, 1 grade 5
・Limitations: Single-arm, open-label; OS immature (upper CI NE)

records.title: BR.21
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2005
records.body:
Stage IIIB or IV NSCLC after failure of first- or second-line chemotherapy; one or two prior combination regimens and not eligible for further chemotherapy (single agents allowed if 70 years or older); ECOG performance status 0 to 3; excluded symptomatic brain metastases, prior breast cancer, melanoma or hypernephroma, other malignancy within five years Ⓐ Erlotinib 150 mg orally daily
Ⓑ Placebo orally daily
・Design: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall response rate, duration of response, toxic effects, quality of life Erlotinib prolonged survival and delayed symptom deterioration vs placebo after prior chemotherapy in advanced NSCLC
・OS: Ⓐ 6.7 vs Ⓑ 4.7 mo; adjusted HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.58–0.85); one-year survival 31% vs 22%
・PFS: Ⓐ 2.2 vs Ⓑ 1.8 mo; adjusted HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.51–0.74)
・ORR: Ⓐ 8.9% vs Ⓑ <1%; median duration of response 7.9 vs 3.7 mo
・QoL: Time to deterioration longer with Ⓐ for cough (4.9 vs 3.7 mo), dyspnea and pain
・Subgroups: Significant treatment-by-smoking interaction only; never-smoker response 24.7% vs 3.9% in current/ever smokers
・Toxicity: Rash Ⓐ 76% vs Ⓑ 17% (grade 3–5: 9% vs 0); diarrhea 55% vs 19%; dose reductions 19% vs 2%; pneumonitis death 1 patient per group
・Limitations: Subgroup analyses exploratory with possibly inadequate sample sizes; EGFR mutations not predictive of survival benefit

records.title: SACHI
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · Randomised, active-controlled, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Unresectable locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC with EGFR-sensitive mutations, progressed on first-line EGFR TKI (any generation); MET amplification by central FISH (copy number ≥5 or MET/CEP7 ratio ≥2 after 1st/2nd-generation TKI; copy number ≥10 after 3rd-generation TKI); T790M negative after 1st/2nd-generation TKI; age 18–75 years; excluded meningeal metastases, spinal cord compression, active brain metastases (asymptomatic permitted) Ⓐ Savolitinib 600 mg if ≥50 kg or 400 mg if <50 kg orally once daily + osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily, 21-day cycles
Ⓑ Pemetrexed 500 mg/m² IV + cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5 IV day 1, 21-day cycles, limited to 4–6 cycles then pemetrexed maintenance permitted
・Duration: Until disease progression, intolerable toxicity, or death
・Design: Open-label, active-controlled; 68 centres in China Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: PFS by IRC, objective response rate, disease control rate, time to response, duration of response, 6-month PFS rate, overall survival, safety, diagnostic technology development Savolitinib plus osimertinib improved investigator-assessed PFS versus platinum-based chemotherapy in EGFR mutation-positive, MET-amplified NSCLC after EGFR TKI progression
・PFS: Ⓐ 9·8 vs Ⓑ 5·4 mo (3rd-gen EGFR TKI-naive); HR 0·34 (95% CI 0·21–0·56); prespecified interim, enrolment stopped
・PFS (ITT): Ⓐ 8·2 vs Ⓑ 4·5 mo; HR 0·34 (95% CI 0·23–0·49)
・PFS (IRC, ITT): Ⓐ 7·2 vs Ⓑ 4·2 mo; HR 0·40 (0·28–0·59)
・ORR (INV, ITT): Ⓐ 58% vs Ⓑ 34%; OR 2·74 (95% CI 1·50–4·98)
・DoR (INV, ITT): Ⓐ 8·4 vs Ⓑ 3·2 mo
・OS: Ⓐ 22·9 vs Ⓑ 17·7 mo; HR 0·84 (95% CI 0·55–1·29); immature
・Subgroups: Consistent benefit; 3rd-gen TKI-pretreated PFS Ⓐ 6·9 vs Ⓑ 3·0 mo; HR 0·32 (0·18–0·57); exploratory
・Toxicity: G≥3 TEAEs Ⓐ 57% vs Ⓑ 57%; drug-related deaths Ⓐ 2% vs Ⓑ none; pyrexia, vomiting, oedema more with Ⓐ; haematological events more with Ⓑ
・Limitations: Interim analysis with early stop; open-label; OS immature with Ⓑ crossover

records.title: HERTHENA-Lung02
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Advanced EGFR-mutated (Ex19del or L858R) NSCLC after disease progression on a third-generation EGFR TKI; resistant post-TKI disease; no full eligibility or exclusion criteria printed (congress abstract) Ⓐ Patritumab deruxtecan (HER3-DXd)
Ⓑ Platinum-based chemotherapy (PBC)
・Design: Randomised, open-label Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, intracranial PFS, safety HER3-DXd improved PFS vs platinum-based chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated NSCLC after a third-generation EGFR TKI
・PFS: Ⓐ 5.8 vs Ⓑ 5.4 mo; HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.63-0.94)
・ORR: Ⓐ 35.2% vs Ⓑ 25.3%
・Intracranial PFS (baseline brain mets): Ⓐ 5.4 vs Ⓑ 4.2 mo; HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.53-1.06)
・Toxicity: G≥3 TEAEs Ⓐ 73% vs Ⓑ 57%; G≥3 thrombocytopenia 30% vs 7.9%; drug-related ILD 5%, 2 G5; 1 G≥3 bleed each arm
・Limitations: OS immature at protocol-specified interim; open-label design

records.title: OptiTROP-Lung04
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Locally advanced (stage IIIB or IIIC) or metastatic (stage IV) nonsquamous NSCLC progressing after EGFR-TKI therapy; sensitizing EGFR mutations (exon 19 deletions or L858R); not candidates for curative surgery or definitive chemoradiotherapy; after first- or second-generation TKIs, documented T790M-negative status required, after third-generation TKIs any T790M status; treated, stable brain metastases eligible Ⓐ Sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT) 5 mg/kg IV on days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle
Ⓑ Pemetrexed 500 mg/m² plus carboplatin AUC 5 or cisplatin 75 mg/m² on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, up to four cycles, then pemetrexed maintenance
・Duration: Until progression, unacceptable toxic effects, withdrawal, or other protocol-specified discontinuation criteria
・Design: Open-label, 66 sites in China Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response, disease control, duration of response, safety, patient-reported outcomes Sacituzumab tirumotecan improved progression-free and overall survival vs pemetrexed–platinum chemotherapy after EGFR-TKI progression in EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC
・PFS (final analysis): Ⓐ 8.3 vs Ⓑ 4.3 mo; HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.39–0.62)
・OS (interim analysis): Ⓐ NE vs Ⓑ 17.4 mo; HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.44–0.82); 18-mo rate 65.8% vs 48.0%
・ORR: Ⓐ 60.6% vs Ⓑ 43.1%; difference 17.0 percentage points (95% CI 7.0–27.1)
・DoR: Ⓐ 8.3 vs Ⓑ 4.2 mo; response ≥12 mo 36.3% vs 8.1%
・QoL: Time to deterioration of global health status and lung cancer symptoms appeared longer with Ⓐ than Ⓑ
・Toxicity: G≥3 TRAEs Ⓐ 58.0% vs Ⓑ 53.8%; serious TRAEs 9.0% vs 17.6%; stomatitis any grade 64.4% vs 4.9%; TR deaths Ⓐ 0 vs Ⓑ 1 (0.5%)
・Limitations: Open-label; China-only, all-Asian participants; OS interim analysis (maturity 35.6% vs 53.7%)
