records.title: ATTLAS (KCSG-LU19-04)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body:
Stage IV NSCLC with sensitizing EGFR mutation or ALK translocation; progression on or intolerance to one or more EGFR or ALK TKIs; acquired Thr790Met after first- or second-generation EGFR TKI required prior third-generation EGFR TKI (recruitment capped up to 30%); at least one measurable RECIST v1.1 lesion, ECOG PS 0 or 1, asymptomatic brain metastases allowed Ⓐ Atezolizumab 1,200 mg + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg + paclitaxel 175 mg/body-surface area + carboplatin AUC 5 or 5.5 every 21 days → maintenance atezolizumab + bevacizumab
Ⓑ Pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 5.0 or cisplatin 70 mg/m² every 21 days → maintenance pemetrexed
・Induction: Four or six cycles, investigator-determined before random assignment
・Duration: Maintenance until progression or unacceptable toxicity
・Design: Open-label; atezolizumab beyond progression allowed if clinical benefit anticipated Primary: progression-free survival. records.body:

・Design: Open-label Primary: progression-free survival (up to 12 months). Secondary: overall survival, time to initiation of a new systemic therapy, toxicity of SBRT, quality of life, progression-free survival by disease site, cell-free DNA changes Adding SBRT to standard-of-care systemic therapy improved PFS at a preplanned interim analysis; benefit seen in NSCLC but not breast cancer

records.title: SAVANNAH
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · Multicohort clinical trial (phase II) with a randomized double-blind contribution-of-components sub-study · 2025
records.body:

・Duration: 28-day cycles until objective disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, consent withdrawal or another discontinuation criterion; continuation beyond RECIST progression permitted with clinical benefit
・Other cohorts: Savolitinib 300 mg o.d. or 600 mg o.d. plus osimertinib 80 mg o.d.; protocol version 7 randomized savolitinib 300 mg b.i.d. plus placebo (contribution of components) Primary: confirmed objective response rate. ・ORR: 56.3% (95% CI 44.7 to 67.3); lower bound above ~30% historical platinum-pemetrexed reference
・ORR (BICR): 55.0% (95% CI 43.5 to 66.2)

・PFS: 7.4 months (95% CI 5.5-7.6); BICR 7.5 months (95% CI 6.4-11.3)

records.title: Aupérin et al. (Prophylactic Cranial Irradiation Overview Collaborative Group)
records.subtitle: SCLC · Limited-stage SCLC (LS-SCLC) — prophylactic cranial irradiation (PCI) · Individual patient data meta-analysis · 1999
records.body:
Small-cell lung cancer (histologically proved) in complete remission after induction chemotherapy; seven randomised trials of prophylactic cranial irradiation vs none, enrolment completed January 1965–December 1995, most patients enrolled after 1985; no evidence of brain metastasis before randomisation and no previous cranial irradiation Ⓐ Prophylactic cranial irradiation, pooled across seven trials (recommended 24 to 40 Gy in 8 to 20 fractions)

・Setting: Randomised in complete remission, median five months after start of induction chemotherapy
・Induction: Chemotherapy alone or with thoracic radiotherapy
・Design: Individual patient data meta-analysis, intention-to-treat Primary: overall survival. Secondary: disease-free survival, cumulative incidence of brain metastasis, cumulative incidence of other metastases, cumulative incidence of local or regional recurrence Prophylactic cranial irradiation improved overall and disease-free survival and reduced brain metastases vs no PCI in SCLC complete remission
・OS: Ⓐ 3-yr 20.7% vs Ⓑ 15.3%; RR 0.84 (95% CI 0.73–0.97); absolute benefit +5.4%
・DFS: RR 0.75 (95% CI 0.65–0.86); 3-yr Ⓑ 13.5%, absolute benefit +8.8%

・Toxicity: Neuropsychological sequelae not assessable (only two trials evaluated); tested changes did not differ between groups
・Limitations: Complete-remission criteria heterogeneous across trials; dose and timing analyses indirect; sex difference exploratory

records.body:

・Platinum–etoposide: Etoposide 80–100 mg/m² days 1–3 plus carboplatin AUC 5–6 mg/mL per min or cisplatin 75–80 mg/m² on day 1, per 21-day cycle
・Duration: Until disease progression per investigator assessment, unacceptable toxicity, or other discontinuation criteria

Secondary: progression-free survival, unconfirmed objective response, overall survival at 18 months, progression-free survival at 6 and 12 months, safety, pharmacokinetics, immunogenicity, health-related quality of life, confirmed objective response, duration of response, overall survival at 12 months Updated CASPIAN analysis after more than 2 years' follow-up confirms sustained overall survival improvement with first-line durvalumab plus platinum–etoposide versus platinum–etoposide in ES-SCLC

・PFS: Ⓐ 5.1 vs Ⓑ 5.4 mo; HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.66–0.96); not formally tested within the multiple testing procedure
・18-mo OS: Ⓐ 32.0% vs Ⓑ 24.8%; 24-mo OS Ⓐ 22.2% vs Ⓑ 14.4%; post hoc 12-mo OS Ⓐ 52.8% vs Ⓑ 39.3%
・12-mo PFS: Ⓐ 17.9% vs Ⓑ 5.3%; 24-mo PFS Ⓐ 11.0% vs Ⓑ 2.9%; 6-mo PFS Ⓐ 45.4% vs Ⓑ 45.8%

・Toxicity: Serious AEs Ⓐ 32% vs Ⓑ 36%; AE deaths Ⓐ 5% vs Ⓑ 6% (treatment-related 2% vs 1%); immune-mediated AEs Ⓐ 20% vs Ⓑ 3%, grade 3–4 in 5% vs <1%
・Limitations: Open-label design; PFS could not be formally tested at interim or final analysis; non-proportional hazards for OS and PFS

records.body:
Extensive small-cell lung cancer (disease beyond hemithorax and supraclavicular nodes or pleural effusion with tumor cells) with any response after four to six cycles of initial chemotherapy; age 18–75, WHO performance status 0–2, randomization within 5 weeks of last cycle; excluded brain or leptomeningeal metastases, prior head-and-neck radiotherapy, previous or other current cancer Ⓐ Prophylactic cranial irradiation: 20 Gy in 5 or 8 fractions, 24 Gy in 12 fractions, 25 Gy in 10 fractions, or 30 Gy in 10 or 12 fractions (one centre-fixed schedule), starting 4–6 weeks after chemotherapy

Extensive-stage SCLC (disease beyond hemithorax, hilar, mediastinal and supraclavicular nodes) with any response after four to six cycles of platinum-etoposide; randomisation within 6 weeks of chemotherapy; thoracic volume treatable with acceptable radiation fields; no clinical brain, leptomeningeal or pleural metastases; no previous brain or thoracic radiotherapy Ⓐ Thoracic radiotherapy 30 Gy in ten fractions

・Subgroups: PFS benefit across all subgroups, including brain or liver metastases; analyses underpowered
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 46.8% vs Ⓑ 40.6%; CRS Ⓐ 49.6% (mostly grade 1–2, one grade 3, no fatal); ICANS Ⓐ 1.1%, none grade ≥3
・Limitations: Interim analysis, OS estimate may evolve; open-label; limited second-line tarlatamab exposure in Ⓑ

records.title: von Pawel et al.
records.subtitle: SCLC · Second-line & relapsed/refractory therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 1999
records.body:
Progressive limited or extensive SCLC relapsing at least 60 days after first-line chemotherapy (amended from at least 90 days); second-line; excluded symptomatic brain metastases requiring corticosteroids, prior topotecan or more than one prior chemotherapy regimen, CAV contraindication, doxorubicin over 270 mg/m² or epirubicin over 540 mg/m² Ⓐ Topotecan 1.5 mg/m² IV daily for 5 days every 21 days
Ⓑ Cyclophosphamide 1,000 mg/m², doxorubicin 45 mg/m² and vincristine 2 mg IV on day 1 every 21 days
・Duration: Responders until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity, or for at least six courses past maximal response; progressive disease removed from study Primary: response rate, duration of response. Secondary: time to progression, time to response, survival, improvement of disease-related symptoms, time to symptom worsening, safety Single-agent topotecan showed efficacy similar to CAV in recurrent SCLC and improved several disease-related symptoms
・ORR: Ⓐ 24.3% (95% CI 16.2–32.4) vs Ⓑ 18.3% (95% CI 10.8–25.7); P=.285
・DoR: Ⓐ 14.4 vs Ⓑ 15.3 wk; P=.300
・TTP: Ⓐ 13.3 vs Ⓑ 12.3 wk; P=.552
・OS: Ⓐ 25.0 vs Ⓑ 24.7 wk; P=.795
・Symptoms: Greater improvement with Ⓐ in dyspnea, anorexia, hoarseness, fatigue and interference with daily activity
・Toxicity: Grade 4 neutropenia Ⓐ 37.8% vs Ⓑ 51.4% of courses; grade 4 thrombocytopenia Ⓐ 9.8% vs Ⓑ 1.4%; grade 3/4 anemia Ⓐ 17.7% vs Ⓑ 7.2%; Seven myelosuppression/sepsis deaths (four Ⓐ, three Ⓑ)
・Limitations: Symptom questionnaire not a validated QoL instrument; baseline brain metastases imbalanced (Ⓐ 11.2% vs Ⓑ 24.0%)

records.title: PM1183-B-005-14
records.subtitle: SCLC · Second-line & relapsed/refractory therapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2020
records.body:
Small-cell lung cancer, second line, after failure of only one previous chemotherapy-containing line (platinum-based; immunotherapy allowed); documented progression before study entry; excluded known CNS involvement, prior lurbinectedin or trabectedin, and previous malignancy unless in complete remission >5 years (single-arm) Lurbinectedin 3.2 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks
・Duration: Until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: overall response rate. Secondary: duration of response, disease control, progression-free survival, progression-free survival at 4 and 6 months, overall survival, overall survival at 6 and 12 months, pharmacokinetics, pharmacogenomics, pharmacogenetics, safety, overall response and secondary activity endpoints by independent review committee Lurbinectedin showed activity as second-line therapy in relapsed SCLC, meeting its primary endpoint; single-arm design, so comparative benefit unestablished
・ORR: 35.2%, all partial responses; exceeded the prespecified 23% activity threshold
・DoR: Median 5.3 mo; 43% of responders still responding at 6 mo
・PFS: Median 3.5 mo
・OS: Median 9.3 mo
・ORR, independent review: 32.7%
・Subgroups: Chemotherapy-free interval ≥90 days ORR 45.0%, OS 11.9 mo; <90 days ORR 22.2%, OS 5.0 mo
・Toxicity: Grade 3–4 neutropenia 46%, leucopenia 29%, anaemia 9%, thrombocytopenia 7%, febrile neutropenia 5%; no treatment-related deaths
・Limitations: Single-arm design with no control group; brain metastases excluded; basket study used general, not SCLC-specific, inclusion criteria

records.title: DeLLphi-301
records.subtitle: SCLC · Second-line & relapsed/refractory therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2023
records.body:
Extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer relapsed or refractory to one platinum-based regimen and at least one other line of therapy; DLL3 expression positivity not required for entry; asymptomatic, treated, stable brain metastases eligible Ⓐ Tarlatamab 1 mg IV step dose day 1 of cycle 1 → 10 mg IV days 8 and 15 of cycle 1, then 10 mg IV every 2 weeks
Ⓑ Tarlatamab 1 mg IV step dose day 1 of cycle 1 → 100 mg IV days 8 and 15 of cycle 1, then 100 mg IV every 2 weeks
・Duration: Until disease progression in 28-day cycles; continuation after radiographic progression allowed if judged clinically beneficial
・Design: Open-label; part 1 randomised dose comparison, part 2 expansion at 10 mg, part 3 reduced inpatient monitoring Primary: confirmed objective response. Secondary: duration of objective response, disease control, duration of disease control, progression-free survival, overall survival, adverse events during the treatment period, serum concentration of tarlatamab, formation of antitarlatamab antibody, patient-reported outcomes (EORTC QLQ-C30, QLQ-LC13), DLL3 expression Both tarlatamab doses showed durable antitumor activity exceeding the 15% historical-control benchmark; the 10-mg dose was selected for further trials on benefit-to-risk
・ORR: Ⓐ 40% vs Ⓑ 32% (97.5% CI 29–52 vs 21–44)
・DoR: Median NE in both arms; ≥6 months in 59% and ≥9 months in 29% of responders
・Disease control: Ⓐ 70% vs Ⓑ 63%
・PFS: Ⓐ 4.9 vs Ⓑ 3.9 mo (95% CI 2.9–6.7 vs 2.6–4.4)
・OS: 9-month Ⓐ 68% vs Ⓑ 66%; median Ⓐ 14.3 mo
・QoL: Exploratory; trend toward improved global health status and lung-cancer symptoms to cycle 12
・Subgroups: Responses with DLL3-positive, DLL3-negative and non-evaluable tumour samples
・Toxicity: CRS Ⓐ 51% vs Ⓑ 61% (grade 3: 1% vs 6%); ICANS Ⓐ 8% vs Ⓑ 28%; one treatment-related death (Ⓐ); 3% discontinued for TRAEs
・Limitations: No standard-care comparator; overall survival immature; no multiplicity adjustment for secondary endpoints

records.title: DeLLphi-304
records.subtitle: SCLC · Second-line & relapsed/refractory therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Small-cell lung cancer progressing during or after one previous line of platinum-based first-line therapy, with or without PD-L1/PD-1 inhibitor (second line); DLL3 expression not required; age ≥18 and ECOG PS 0–1; asymptomatic, clinically stable brain metastases permitted regardless of treatment Ⓐ Tarlatamab 1 mg IV step-up dose day 1 of cycle 1, then 10 mg IV days 8 and 15, then 10 mg IV every 2 weeks in 28-day cycles
Ⓑ Chemotherapy (per country): topotecan 1.5 mg/m² IV or 2.3 mg/m² orally days 1–5 every 3 weeks, lurbinectedin 3.2 mg/m² IV day 1 every 3 weeks, or amrubicin 40 mg/m² IV days 1–3 every 3 weeks
・Duration: Until investigator-determined RECIST v1.1 progression, unacceptable toxic effects, withdrawal of consent, or death Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, patient-reported outcomes (EORTC QLQ-C30/LC13: week-19 change in dyspnea, cough, chest pain, physical functioning, global health status), objective response, disease control, duration of response, adverse events, serious adverse events Tarlatamab prolonged overall survival versus chemotherapy in small-cell lung cancer progressing during or after platinum-based first-line therapy
・OS: Ⓐ 13.6 vs Ⓑ 8.3 mo; stratified HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.47–0.77); prespecified interim analysis
・PFS: Ⓐ 4.2 vs Ⓑ 3.7 mo; RMST at 12 mo 5.3 vs 4.3 mo (P=0.002); PH invalid, weighted average HR 0.71 (95% CI 0.59–0.86)
・ORR: Ⓐ 35% vs Ⓑ 20%; risk ratio 1.73 (95% CI 1.29–2.33)
・DoR: Ⓐ 6.9 vs Ⓑ 5.5 mo; 12-mo DoR 41% vs 13%
・QoL: Week-19 dyspnea −9.14 points (P<0.001), cough OR 2.04 (P=0.01) favoured Ⓐ; chest pain NS; physical functioning/global health not formally tested
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 54% vs Ⓑ 80%; CRS 56% (mostly grade 1–2, no grade 4/5); ICANS 6%, one grade-5 death; dysgeusia 24%
・Limitations: Open-label; interim OS analysis (boundary P<0.02); ECOG 0–1 population and few Black patients limit generalizability

records.title: BL-B01D1-101
records.subtitle: SCLC · Second-line & relapsed/refractory therapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase Ib) · 2026
records.body:
Extensive-stage SCLC (histologically or cytologically confirmed at initial diagnosis) with progression after at least one prior platinum-based chemotherapy and a PD-(L)1 inhibitor, second line and beyond; ECOG PS 0-1 with at least one measurable lesion per RECIST v1.1; excluded active brain metastases, uncontrolled comorbidities, ECOG PS >1 (single-arm) Iza-bren (EGFR-HER3 bispecific ADC) 2.5 mg/kg IV on days 1 and 8 of each 3-week cycle
・Duration: Until disease progression, intolerance, or treatment delay >28 days Primary: objective response rate, safety/tolerability. Secondary: duration of response, disease control rate, progression-free survival, overall survival Iza-bren showed antitumor activity in relapsed extensive-stage SCLC, with higher response as second-line therapy; comparative benefit unestablished
・ORR: 48.1% (95% CI 34.0 to 62.4); 72.7% (95% CI 49.8 to 89.3) in second-line patients
・DCR: 80.8% (95% CI 67.5 to 90.4)
・DOR: Median 4.9 months (95% CI 4.2 to 6.7)
・PFS: Median 4.1 months (95% CI 3.0 to 5.5); 6.2 months (95% CI 3.7 to 8.2) second-line
・OS: Median 12.2 months (95% CI 9.1 to 13.2); 15.0 months (95% CI 8.7 to not reached) second-line
・Subgroups: Platinum-sensitive (treatment-free interval >6 months) ORR 69.2%; prior irinotecan ORR 31.6%; HER3-positive ORR 68.8% vs HER3-negative 14.3% (exploratory)
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 TRAEs 75%; anemia 84.6% any grade; dose reduction 46%; grade 5 TRAEs 3.8%; no treatment-related ILD
・Limitations: Single-arm design and limited sample size; biomarker and subgroup findings exploratory

records.title: Groupe Français de Pneumo-Cancérologie 01–13
records.subtitle: SCLC · Second-line & relapsed/refractory therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body:
Histologically or cytologically confirmed small-cell lung cancer, stage IV or localised relapse outside the radiation field; sensitive relapse at least 90 days after RECIST v1.1 response to first-line cisplatin or carboplatin plus etoposide; second-line; ECOG PS 0–2 and weight loss <10% in 3 months; symptomatic brain or meningeal metastases and prior immunotherapy excluded Ⓐ Carboplatin AUC 5 mg/mL per min IV day 1 plus etoposide 100 mg/m² IV days 1–3
Ⓑ Topotecan 2·3 mg/m² orally days 1–5
・Cycle: Every 3 weeks; maximum six cycles, no minimum number planned
・Prophylaxis: Primary prophylactic filgrastim recommended in both groups
・Design: Open-label Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, treatment-related adverse events, quality of life Carboplatin plus etoposide improved progression-free survival and objective response rate versus oral topotecan in sensitive relapsed small-cell lung cancer, without longer overall survival
・PFS: Ⓐ 4·7 vs Ⓑ 2·7 mo; stratified HR 0·57 (90% CI 0·41–0·73); p=0·0041
・OS: Ⓐ 7·5 vs Ⓑ 7·4 mo; HR 1·03 (95% CI 0·87–1·19); p=0·94
・ORR: Ⓐ 49% vs Ⓑ 25%; p=0·0024
・DoR: Ⓐ 5·4 vs Ⓑ 4·1 mo
・Subgroups: PFS benefit of Ⓐ significant when relapse occurred at least 180 days after first-line chemotherapy
・Toxicity: G3–4 neutropenia Ⓐ 14% vs Ⓑ 22%; thrombocytopenia Ⓐ 31% vs Ⓑ 36%; febrile neutropenia Ⓐ 6% vs Ⓑ 11%; two treatment-related deaths with Ⓑ, none with Ⓐ
・Limitations: Open-label; large third-line crossover from Ⓑ (almost 40% received carboplatin plus etoposide) may explain absent OS gain; quality of life not analysable (22 patients)

records.title: TAISHAN-302
records.subtitle: SCLC · Second-line & relapsed/refractory therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Small-cell lung cancer, histologically or cytologically confirmed; progressed or relapsed during or after first-line platinum-based therapy (local disease only if local recurrence within 6 months after platinum-based chemotherapy plus definitive radiotherapy); age 18 to 75 years, ECOG 0 or 1, at least one measurable lesion per RECIST 1.1, asymptomatic stable brain metastases allowed; excluded combined or transformed small-cell lung cancer Ⓐ Tambotatug pelitecan 2.0 mg/kg IV on day 1 every 3 weeks (maximum 200 mg per cycle)
Ⓑ Topotecan 1.2 mg/m² IV on days 1 through 5 every 3 weeks
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable side effects, new anticancer therapy, withdrawal of consent or investigator-assessed loss of clinical benefit
・Design: Open-label Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response, duration of response, time to response, adverse events, serious adverse events, intracranial objective response, intracranial progression-free survival, duration of intracranial response Tambotatug pelitecan improved OS vs topotecan at the prespecified interim analysis, with longer PFS, higher ORR and fewer grade ≥3 AEs
・OS: Ⓐ 13.3 vs Ⓑ 9.4 mo; HR 0.46 (95% CI 0.35–0.62); interim analysis
・PFS: Ⓐ 7.4 vs Ⓑ 2.8 mo; HR 0.29 (95% CI 0.23–0.37)
・ORR: Ⓐ 59.1% vs Ⓑ 9.7%; P<0.001
・DoR: Ⓐ 6.3 vs Ⓑ 7.8 mo; not adjusted for multiplicity
・Intracranial ORR (exploratory, baseline brain lesions): Ⓐ 32% vs Ⓑ 3%
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 55.4% vs Ⓑ 77.9%; G≥3 TR thrombocytopenia Ⓐ 12.5% vs Ⓑ 54.8%; ILD/pneumonitis Ⓐ 4.9% vs Ⓑ 1.4%; fatal AEs Ⓐ 4.0% vs Ⓑ 2.8%, none treatment-related in Ⓐ
・Limitations: Interim analysis, median follow-up 9.2 mo; open-label with investigator-assessed PFS/ORR; enrolment restricted to China

records.title: EMPHACIS
records.subtitle: Mesothelioma · First-line chemotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2003
records.body:
Malignant pleural mesothelioma, histologically proven, not candidates for curative surgery; uni- or bidimensionally measurable disease, Karnofsky performance status ≥70, life expectancy ≥12 weeks; excluded prior chemotherapy, brain metastases, second primary malignancy, inability to interrupt NSAIDs Ⓐ Pemetrexed 500 mg/m² IV + cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV day 1, every 21 days
Ⓑ Cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV day 1, every 21 days
・Supplementation: Folic acid 350 to 1,000 µg orally daily and vitamin B12 1,000 µg IM every 9 weeks, both arms, required from December 2, 1999
・Duration: Discontinued after three dose reductions
・Design: Single-blind; normal saline replaced pemetrexed in Ⓑ Primary: overall survival. Secondary: time to progressive disease, time to treatment failure, tumor response rate, duration of response, safety Pemetrexed plus cisplatin improved survival, time to progression and response rate versus cisplatin alone in malignant pleural mesothelioma
・OS: Ⓐ 12.1 vs Ⓑ 9.3 mo; HR 0.77 (P = .020)
・TTP: Ⓐ 5.7 vs Ⓑ 3.9 mo; HR 0.68 (P = .001)
・ORR: Ⓐ 41.3% vs Ⓑ 16.7% (P < .0001); all partial responses
・Subgroups: Fully supplemented OS Ⓐ 13.3 vs Ⓑ 10.0 mo (P = .051)
・Toxicity: G3/4 neutropenia Ⓐ 27.9% vs Ⓑ 2.3%, leukopenia Ⓐ 17.7% vs Ⓑ 0.9%; three drug-related deaths before vitamin supplementation, none after
・Limitations: Single-blind; second-line therapy uncontrolled (Ⓑ 47.3% vs Ⓐ 37.6%); survival tested at alpha .0476 after interim analysis

records.title: MAPS (IFCT-GFPC-0701)
records.subtitle: Mesothelioma · First-line chemotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body: Untreated non-resectable malignant pleural mesothelioma First-line cisplatin + pemetrexed + bevacizumab vs cisplatin + pemetrexed Overall survival Adding bevacizumab improved OS (18.8 vs 16.1 months, HR 0.77; p=0.017); an option for fit patients without contraindications to anti-VEGF therapy, though not universally adopted.

records.title: CheckMate 743
records.subtitle: Mesothelioma · First-line immunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body:
Unresectable malignant pleural mesothelioma, histologically confirmed and not amenable to curative therapy; previously untreated (first-line); ECOG performance status 0–1; measurable disease per mRECIST with tumour sample available for PD-L1 testing; excluded brain metastases (unless treated and asymptomatic), autoimmune disease, prior checkpoint or T-cell costimulation therapy, and non-pleural mesotheliomas Ⓐ Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV every 6 weeks, up to 2 years
Ⓑ Pemetrexed 500 mg/m² IV plus cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV or carboplatin AUC 5 mg/mL per min IV, every 3 weeks for up to six cycles
・Duration: Until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
・Design: Open-label; stratified by sex and histology Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, time to response, duration of response, disease control rate, overall survival by PD-L1 expression, progression-free survival by PD-L1 expression, objective response rate by PD-L1 expression, safety Nivolumab plus ipilimumab improved overall survival versus platinum plus pemetrexed chemotherapy in first-line unresectable MPM, meeting the primary endpoint at the interim analysis considered final
・OS: Ⓐ 18·1 vs Ⓑ 14·1 mo; HR 0·74 (96·6% CI 0·60–0·91); p=0·0020; interim analysis considered final
・2-yr OS: Ⓐ 41% vs Ⓑ 27%
・PFS: Ⓐ 6·8 vs Ⓑ 7·2 mo; HR 1·00 (95% CI 0·82–1·21), no formal testing; 2-yr PFS Ⓐ 16% vs Ⓑ 7%
・ORR: Ⓐ 40% vs Ⓑ 43%; DoR Ⓐ 11·0 vs Ⓑ 6·7 mo; 2-yr response Ⓐ 32% vs Ⓑ 8%
・Subgroups: OS effect larger non-epithelioid (HR 0·46 [95% CI 0·31–0·68]) than epithelioid (0·86 [0·69–1·08]); PD-L1 exploratory, ≥1% HR 0·69 vs <1% 0·94
・Toxicity: G3–4 TRAEs Ⓐ 30% vs Ⓑ 32%; serious TRAEs 21% vs 8%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 3 (1%; pneumonitis, encephalitis, heart failure) vs Ⓑ 1 (<1%; myelosuppression)
・Limitations: Open-label; interim analysis; secondary endpoints and PD-L1 subgroups exploratory

records.title: KEYNOTE-483 (CCTG IND227)
records.subtitle: Mesothelioma · First-line immunotherapy · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body:
Advanced pleural mesothelioma unsuitable for surgery, previously untreated ([neo]adjuvant chemotherapy allowed >1 year before); ECOG performance status 0 or 1; measurable disease per mRECIST with tumour sample provided; excluded untreated CNS metastases, pneumonitis, glucocorticoids >10 mg/day prednisone equivalent, or concurrent serious illness or cancer Ⓐ Cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV (or carboplatin AUC 5–6 mg/mL per min) plus pemetrexed 500 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks for up to 6 cycles
Ⓑ Same platinum–pemetrexed chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks for up to 2 years
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxic effects, investigator or patient decision, or planned treatment completion
・Design: Open-label Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, response rate, duration of response, quality of life, health economics, safety Adding pembrolizumab to platinum–pemetrexed improved overall survival versus chemotherapy alone in untreated advanced pleural mesothelioma
・OS, final analysis: Ⓐ 16.1 vs Ⓑ 17.3 mo; HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.64–0.98); 3-yr OS 17% vs 25%
・OS, 54-mo RMST: Ⓐ 20 vs Ⓑ 23.4 mo, exploratory
・PFS: Ⓐ 7.16 vs Ⓑ 7.13 mo; HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.65–0.99); 1-yr PFS 17% vs 26%
・ORR: Ⓐ 38% vs Ⓑ 62%; OR 2.70 (95% CI 1.8–4.0); median DoR 5.5 vs 5.8 mo
・QoL: Time to deterioration in cough, dyspnoea or chest pain not different; pain and global health status favoured Ⓑ
・Subgroups: Non-epithelioid OS Ⓐ 8.2 vs Ⓑ 12.3 mo, HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.36–0.89); epithelioid HR 0.89 (0.70–1.13); benefit regardless of PD-L1
・Toxicity: Grade 3–4 related AEs Ⓐ 15% vs Ⓑ 27%; related deaths Ⓐ 1 vs Ⓑ 2; related-drug hospital admissions Ⓐ 6% vs Ⓑ 18%
・Limitations: Open-label; median OS gain slightly over 1 month with delayed effect; subsequent immunotherapy in 28% of Ⓐ vs 8% of Ⓑ

records.title: MARS (Mesothelioma and Radical Surgery)
records.subtitle: Mesothelioma · Surgery in resectable disease · Randomised, open-label feasibility clinical trial · 2011
records.body:
Malignant pleural mesothelioma; after three cycles of platinum-based induction chemotherapy, still operable (T1–3, N0–1, M0); registration required pathologically confirmed mesothelioma, no unresectable disease or distant metastases on preoperative CT staging, and fitness for pneumonectomy (BTS criteria) plus planned postoperative radiotherapy Ⓐ EPP followed by postoperative hemithorax irradiation
Ⓑ No EPP (no radical surgery)
・Induction: Three cycles of platinum-based chemotherapy before randomisation, regimen chosen by the treating centre
・SOC: Continued oncological management per local policy for all randomly assigned patients Primary: feasibility of randomly assigning 50 patients in 1 year, proportion randomised who received treatment, proportion eligible (registered) who proceeded to randomisation, perioperative mortality, quality of life. Secondary: overall survival, relapse-free survival, progression-free survival, serious adverse events EPP within trimodal therapy offered no survival or quality-of-life benefit and possibly harmed patients versus no EPP
・Feasibility: 50 randomised over the entire study period, not the anticipated 1 year; cumulative loss 76·3%
・OS: Ⓐ 14·4 vs Ⓑ 19·5 mo; HR 1·90 (0·92–3·93), adjusted HR 2·75 (1·21–6·26)
・12-mo OS: Ⓐ 52·2% vs Ⓑ 73·1%
・RFS/PFS: Ⓐ median 7·6 mo; Ⓑ median 9·0 mo
・QoL: Median scores lower in Ⓐ, no statistically significant differences between groups
・Toxicity: Perioperative deaths three of 24 Ⓐ (12·5%); postoperative complications 11 of 16 Ⓐ completers; SAEs Ⓐ 10 vs Ⓑ 2
・Limitations: Feasibility-sized trial (50 randomised); open-label; three Ⓑ patients had EPP off trial

records.title: MARS 2
records.subtitle: Mesothelioma · Surgery in resectable disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body:
Pleural mesothelioma (epithelioid, sarcomatoid, or biphasic) confined to one hemithorax on CT and deemed surgically resectable at a MARS 2 surgical site and specialist mesothelioma MDT; randomised after two cycles of first-line chemotherapy with repeat CT confirming ongoing resectability; adequate organ and lung function; severe comorbidities precluding surgery excluded Ⓐ Pleurectomy decortication or extended pleurectomy decortication, followed by two to four further cycles of chemotherapy
Ⓑ Two to four further cycles of chemotherapy
・Chemotherapy: Two cycles (3 weeks per cycle) of standard-of-care chemotherapy (eg, platinum and pemetrexed) before randomisation; further cycles per local treatment policies
・Design: Open-label; parallel two-group, pragmatic Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, serious adverse events, quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30, EQ-5D), health-care resource use, quality-adjusted life years, costs (Extended) pleurectomy decortication plus chemotherapy was associated with worse survival to 2 years and more serious adverse events than chemotherapy alone
・OS: Ⓐ 19·3 vs Ⓑ 24·8 mo median; RMST to 24 mo −1·9 (95% CI −3·4 to −0·3, p=0·019) in favour of chemotherapy alone
・OS 0–42 mo: HR 1·28 (95% CI 1·02–1·60, p=0·032), 28% increase in risk of death with surgery
・PFS: Ⓐ 10·6 vs Ⓑ 11·0 mo; HR 0·90 (95% CI 0·72–1·11, p=0·33); no difference
・QoL: All significant EORTC differences favoured Ⓑ; global health MD −5·51 (95% CI −9·73 to −1·89); EQ-5D MD −0·14 (−0·19 to −0·10)
・QALYs: Ⓐ 1·02 vs Ⓑ 1·21; MD −0·19 (95% CI −0·30 to −0·08); costs £30 436 vs £15 805
・Subgroups: OS effect differed by histology; epithelioid HR 1·12 (0·86–1·47) vs non-epithelioid 2·66 (1·22–5·81); RMST interaction p=0·0020
・Toxicity: Ⓐ 318 vs Ⓑ 169 grade ≥3 SAEs, IRR 3·6 (95% CI 2·3–5·5); post-surgery in-hospital and 30-day mortality both 6 (4%) of 157, 90-day 14 (9%)
・Limitations: Open-label; non-proportional hazards with curves crossing at 42 months; fewer chemotherapy cycles and less immunotherapy in surgery group

records.title: MAPS2 (IFCT-1501)
