records.body: Relapsed malignant pleural mesothelioma after platinum-based chemotherapy Second/third-line nivolumab vs nivolumab + ipilimumab 12-week disease control rate 12-week DCR was 40% (nivolumab) and 52% (combination); median OS 15.9 vs 15.9 months; both regimens showed promising activity in the relapsed setting, supporting the dual checkpoint approach later confirmed in CheckMate 743.

records.title: CONFIRM
records.subtitle: Mesothelioma · Second-line & salvage therapy · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body:
Histologically confirmed pleural or peritoneal mesothelioma of any subtype with radiological progression after at least one platinum-based chemotherapy course; relapsed setting with no limit on previous lines; ECOG 0–1 and measurable disease by modified RECIST or RECIST 1.1; archival tumour biopsy required; excluded prior immune checkpoint inhibitor, uncontrolled CNS metastasis, autoimmune disease Ⓐ Nivolumab 240 mg IV every 2 weeks
Ⓑ Placebo IV every 2 weeks
・Duration: Until disease progression, withdrawal, or a maximum of 12 months
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: overall response rate, stable disease, progressive disease, 12-month overall survival, 12-month progression-free survival, safety, progression-free survival and overall survival by tumour PD-L1 tumour proportion score Nivolumab improved progression-free survival but not overall survival versus placebo at final analysis in relapsed mesothelioma
・PFS (final): Ⓐ 2.89 vs Ⓑ 1.64 mo; HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.51–0.82); co-primary met at α 0.01
・OS (final, 37.2-mo median follow-up): Ⓐ 9.49 vs Ⓑ 6.77 mo; HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.64–1.04); P = .096; boundary 0.04 not met
・OS (preliminary): Ⓐ 10.2 vs Ⓑ 6.9 mo; HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.52–0.91); P = 0.0090; not confirmed at final analysis
・12-mo RMST OS: Ⓐ vs Ⓑ +1.1 mo (95% CI 0.2–2.0); post-hoc
・1-yr OS (preliminary): Ⓐ 43.4% vs Ⓑ 30.1%
・1-yr PFS (preliminary): Ⓐ 14.2% vs Ⓑ 7.2%
・ORR (final, central recomputation): Ⓐ 10.3% vs Ⓑ 0.0%
・DoR: Ⓐ 7.1 mo; post-hoc
・PD-L1 (final): Longer PFS only with TPS >50% (interaction HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.09–0.94); OS and ORR not different; TPS >50% in 5.8%
・Exploratory multi-omics: Responders had CD8+/CD19+ infiltration, TLSs, IL24/CCL19; non-responders EMT, mitosis; TMB, 9p21, BAP1 not different; hypothesis-generating
・Toxicity: G≥3 TRAEs Ⓐ 20.4% vs Ⓑ 7.2% (final); infusion reactions causing discontinuation Ⓐ 13.6% vs Ⓑ 2.7%; preliminary G≥3 diarrhoea Ⓐ 3% vs Ⓑ 2%; no treatment-related deaths
・Limitations: No central radiology review; mostly third-line population; 18.1% of placebo patients received immunotherapy after unblinding
records.keywords: Fennell et al. Lancet Oncol 2021;22:1530-1540  34656227 Fennell et al. Nat Commun 2025;16:6688  40691143

records.title: VIM
records.subtitle: Mesothelioma · Second-line & salvage therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2022
records.body: Relapsed malignant pleural mesothelioma after platinum-based chemotherapy Oral vinorelbine + active symptom control vs active symptom control alone Progression-free survival Vinorelbine improved PFS (4.2 vs 2.8 months, HR 0.60) without significant OS benefit (9.3 vs 9.1 months); provides a chemotherapy option for patients progressing after platinum-pemetrexed in the immunotherapy era.

records.title: KEYNOTE-158 (Meso cohort)
records.subtitle: Mesothelioma · Second-line & salvage therapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2021
records.body: Previously treated advanced malignant pleural mesothelioma Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w (single arm) Objective response rate ORR 8% with median DOR 14.3 months; median OS 10.0 months in an unselected pretreated population; limited single-agent activity but durable responses in a minority support biomarker-selected use.

records.title: ITMIG PORT Analysis (Rimner)
records.subtitle: Thymic Epithelial Tumours · Resectable & locally advanced disease — radiotherapy & combined-modality therapy · Retrospective cohort study · 2016
records.body: Completely resected (R0) Masaoka-Koga stage II-III thymoma Surgery + postoperative radiotherapy vs surgery alone Overall survival Postoperative radiotherapy improved 5- and 10-year OS (95%/86% vs 90%/79% with surgery alone; p=0.002), with benefit retained for stage II and III separately and on multivariable analysis; strongest evidence supporting adjuvant radiotherapy in resected stage II-III thymoma.

records.title: Intergroup PAC + RT (Loehrer)
records.subtitle: Thymic Epithelial Tumours · Resectable & locally advanced disease — radiotherapy & combined-modality therapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 1997
records.body: Limited-stage unresectable thymoma/thymic carcinoma, chemo-naive Induction PAC x2-4 cycles then 54 Gy thoracic radiotherapy Response rate Induction PAC produced a 69.6% response (5 CR, 11 PR); with consolidative radiotherapy, median survival reached 93 months and 5-year OS was 52.5%; established combined-modality therapy as standard for unresectable thymoma.

records.title: ADOC (Fornasiero)
records.subtitle: Thymic Epithelial Tumours · Advanced / metastatic disease — first-line chemotherapy · Retrospective cohort study · 1991
records.body: Stage III-IV invasive (advanced) thymoma ADOC (cisplatin, doxorubicin, vincristine, cyclophosphamide) Response rate ORR 91.8% with 43% complete responses and no life-threatening toxicity; one of the most active first-line regimens for advanced thymoma, though never compared randomly against other platinum doublets.

records.title: Intergroup PAC trial (Loehrer et al.)
records.subtitle: Thymic Epithelial Tumours · Advanced / metastatic disease — first-line chemotherapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 1994
records.body:
Thymoma (n=29) or thymic carcinoma (n=1) with metastatic or locally progressive recurrent disease; extensive stage IV (pleural/pulmonary metastases ± mediastinal disease) or limited stage III (mediastinum and ipsilateral supraclavicular nodes, single radiotherapy portal) progressing after radiotherapy; bidimensionally measurable disease; no prior chemotherapy, prior malignancy within 5 years (except nonmelanomatous skin cancer or stage 0 to IIA cervical) or congestive heart failure (single-arm) PAC: cisplatin 50 mg/m² + doxorubicin 50 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m², all IV, every 3 weeks
・Duration: Maximum eight cycles; response assessed after two cycles, continued for stable or responsive disease unless grade 4 toxicity or progression Primary: toxicity, objective response rate, duration of remission, overall survival, time to treatment failure PAC showed activity in metastatic or recurrent thymoma, achieving a 50% objective response rate and 37.7-month median survival
・ORR: 50% (95% CI 31.3% to 68.7%)
・DoR: Median 11.8 months
・TTF: Median 18.4 months
・OS: Median 37.7 months; 5-year survival 32%
・Toxicity: Primarily hematologic and relatively mild; 12 grade III and four grade IV incidents; one febrile neutropenia hospitalization; no early deaths
・Limitations: Single-arm, no comparator; small sample; indolent thymoma biology may contribute to prolonged survival
records.keywords: Loehrer et al. J Clin Oncol 1994;12:1164-1168  8201378

records.title: Carboplatin-Paclitaxel (Lemma)
records.subtitle: Thymic Epithelial Tumours · Advanced / metastatic disease — first-line chemotherapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2011
records.body:
Histologically confirmed invasive, recurrent or metastatic thymoma or thymic carcinoma not amenable to potentially curative surgery; previously untreated systemic therapy (prior preoperative/adjuvant chemotherapy allowed if disease-free >1 year before recurrence); prior malignancy excluded unless no recurrence within previous 5 years (single-arm) Paclitaxel 225 mg/m² IV + carboplatin AUC 6 IV on day 1, every 3 weeks
・Duration: Two courses, then four additional courses without progression or unacceptable toxicity (maximum six); beyond six at physician discretion Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, toxicity Carboplatin plus paclitaxel showed moderate clinical activity in thymic malignancies, seemingly less than anthracycline-based therapy; thymic carcinoma had poorer PFS and OS than thymoma
・ORR, thymoma: 42.9% (90% CI 24.5–62.8), three CR and six PR; first-stage criterion not met (one response short), stratum closed early
・ORR, thymic carcinoma: 21.7% (90% CI 9.0–40.4), no CRs; not consistent with a true response rate of 45%
・PFS: Thymoma 16.7 mo (95% CI 7.2–19.8); thymic carcinoma 5.0 mo (3.0–8.3)
・OS: Thymoma not reached after 59.4 mo median follow-up; thymic carcinoma 20.0 mo (95% CI 5.0–43.6)
・DoR: Thymoma 16.9 mo (95% CI 3.1–22.0); thymic carcinoma 4.5 mo (3.4–9.9)
・Prognosis: Thymic carcinoma worse OS vs thymoma (log-rank P = .01; adjusted HR 3.0, 95% CI 1.2–7.8); PFS marginal (P = .06)
・Toxicity: Grade 4 neutropenia 24.4%; grade 3 sensory neuropathy 13.3%; one grade 3 and one grade 4 febrile neutropenia; no cardiotoxicity; one acute nonlymphocytic leukemia at 14 months
・Limitations: Single-arm, small strata; thymoma stratum closed early; anthracycline comparison historical
records.keywords: Lemma et al. J Clin Oncol 2011;29:2060-2065  21502559

records.title: Cisplatin-Etoposide (Giaccone)
records.subtitle: Thymic Epithelial Tumours · Advanced / metastatic disease — first-line chemotherapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 1996
records.body:
Biopsy-proven metastatic or recurrent invasive thymoma considered incurable by excision and/or irradiation; all Masaoka stage III or IV; measurable disease required; prior chemotherapy allowed except cisplatin or etoposide; concomitant corticosteroids not allowed (single-arm) Cisplatin 60 mg/m² on day 1 + etoposide 120 mg/m² on days 1, 2 and 3, every 3 weeks
・Duration: Up to a maximum of eight consecutive cycles in patients who tolerated treatment and did not progress Primary: tumor response, toxicity, duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival Cisplatin–etoposide showed activity in recurrent or metastatic malignant thymoma, with a 56% response rate and durable responses
・ORR: 56%; 5 complete and 4 partial responses; 60% among the 15 response-assessable patients
・DoR: Median 3.4 years; range 4 to 78+ months
・PFS: Median 2.2 years; 48%, 38% and 26% progression-free at 3, 5 and 7 years
・OS: Median 4.3 years; 69%, 50% and 42% alive at 3, 5 and 7 years; median follow-up 7 years
・Toxicity: Grade 3-4 leukopenia 51%, nausea/vomiting 81%, alopecia 69%; one cardiac-arrest death after cycle 1; two infection deaths after pure RBC aplasia
・Limitations: Single-arm, 16 patients over 6 years; good prognostic characteristics and limited tumor load in most
records.keywords: Giaccone et al. J Clin Oncol 1996;14:814-820  8622029

records.title: RYTHMIC
records.subtitle: Thymic Epithelial Tumours · Advanced / metastatic disease — first-line chemotherapy · Observational cohort study (retrospective analysis of a prospective nationwide cohort) · 2018
records.body:
Advanced thymic epithelial tumors (thymoma 50%, thymic carcinoma 50%); 96% Masaoka-Koga stage III or IV at diagnosis; systemic therapy as primary chemotherapy for unresectable locally advanced tumors, exclusive therapy with no planned focal treatment, or treatment of first to fourth recurrence; required histologically confirmed TET discussed at the RYTHMIC tumor board with at least one cycle delivered (observational cohort) Systemic therapy regimens chosen per RYTHMIC/ESMO recommendations at the national tumor board
・Primary chemotherapy: PAC (cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, cisplatin) in 70% of 91 patients
・Exclusive therapy: PAC in 67% of 54 patients
・First recurrence: Carboplatin + paclitaxel in 44% of 114 patients
・Second to fourth recurrences: Sunitinib or other VEGFR TKI, platin + paclitaxel, gemcitabine + capecitabine, etoposide, pemetrexed, everolimus Primary: objective response, progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, time to progression, disease control rate Systemic therapy for advanced TETs showed setting-dependent response rates and PFS across primary, exclusive and recurrence settings; objective response was associated with longer PFS
・ORR, primary chemo: Thymoma 83%, thymic carcinoma 75%; median TTP 23.2 mo; OS not reached
・ORR, exclusive: Thymoma 31%, thymic carcinoma 37%; median PFS 6.2 mo; OS not reached
・First recurrence: ORR thymoma 39%, thymic carcinoma 18%; median PFS 7.7 mo; OS 44.0 mo
・Recurrences 2–4: Median PFS 6.2, 5.9, 6.5 mo; OS 32.1, 13.8, 11.4 mo
・Regimens: Exclusive ORR 44% with PAC vs 17% others (p = 0.044); no significant between-regimen differences in later lines
・Predictors, TTP: Thymoma histology (HR 0.36, 95% CI 0.18–0.70) and PAC (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.19–0.74) after primary chemotherapy
・Predictors, PFS: Tumor response predicted longer PFS: exclusive HR 0.39 (95% CI 0.23–0.67), first recurrence HR 0.32 (95% CI 0.18–0.56), later HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.37–0.79)
・Toxicity: Not reported; toxicities not captured in the RYTHMIC database
・Limitations: Retrospective uncontrolled design; individual regimen choice without prespecified algorithm; no blinded radiological review
records.keywords: Merveilleux du Vignaux et al. J Thorac Oncol 2018;13:1762-1770  30138763

records.title: RELEVENT
records.subtitle: Thymic Epithelial Tumours · Advanced thymic carcinoma — first-line chemo-immunotherapy & antiangiogenic combinations · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2024
records.body:
Advanced, recurrent or metastatic thymic carcinoma (centrally confirmed; B3 thymoma with carcinoma areas eligible, none enrolled), not previously treated for metastatic disease, first line; measurable disease per RECIST v1.1 and ECOG PS 0-1; excluded untreated brain metastases and major antiangiogenic contraindications (major vessel invasion/encasement, thromboembolic history, uncontrolled hypertension) (single-arm) Ramucirumab 10 mg/kg IV followed by paclitaxel 200 mg/m² IV and carboplatin AUC 5 IV on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, up to six cycles or until progression or intolerable toxicity
・Maintenance: Ramucirumab monotherapy every 3 weeks until progression, death or unacceptable toxicity after disease control on combination Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall survival, safety, disease control rate, duration of response Ramucirumab plus carboplatin and paclitaxel showed high first-line activity in untreated advanced thymic carcinoma, meeting the single-arm ORR primary endpoint
・ORR: 80.0% (95% CI 63.1% to 91.6%); binomial P < 0.0001
・ORR, central review: 57.6% (95% CI 39.2% to 74.5%) by RECIST v1.1, 60.6% (95% CI 42.1% to 77.1%) by mRECIST
・PFS: Median 18.1 months (95% CI 10.8-52.3); median follow-up 31.6 months
・OS: Median 43.8 months (95% CI 31.9 months to not reached)
・DOR: Median 15.7 months (95% CI 12.5-50.8)
・DCR: 100% (95% CI 89.4% to 100.0%)
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs 48.6%; neutrophil count decreased 20.0%, hypertension 8.6%; ramucirumab-related SAEs included two acute myocardial infarction G3, pulmonary embolism G4, arterial hemorrhage G3
・Limitations: Single-arm without direct comparator; accrual stopped at 35 of 55 planned patients; central-review ORR lower than investigator-assessed (57.6% vs 80.0%)

records.title: MARBLE
records.subtitle: Thymic Epithelial Tumours · Advanced thymic carcinoma — first-line chemo-immunotherapy & antiangiogenic combinations · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2025
records.body:
Advanced or recurrent thymic carcinoma (histologically confirmed Masaoka stage III, IVA or IVB not amenable to definitive treatment, or recurrence after definitive treatment); first-line therapy, no previous systemic drug therapy for thymic carcinoma (>6 months since postoperative adjuvant chemotherapy allowed); excluded symptomatic brain metastases or carcinomatous meningitis, autoimmune disease, or conditions requiring ongoing systemic corticosteroids (single-arm) Atezolizumab 1200 mg + carboplatin AUC 6 mg/mL per min + paclitaxel 200 mg/m² IV day 1 every 3 weeks for up to six cycles → atezolizumab 1200 mg IV every 3 weeks
・Duration: Atezolizumab maintenance up to 2 years (including induction phase), until progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: disease control rate, progression-free survival, duration of response, overall survival, safety Atezolizumab plus carboplatin and paclitaxel showed antitumour activity in previously untreated advanced or recurrent thymic carcinoma; comparative benefit unestablished
・ORR: 56%, primary endpoint met vs 30% threshold; p<0·0001
・DCR: 98%
・PFS: Median 9·6 months (95% CI 7·7–14·8); 12-month 43·3%
・DoR: Median 6·4 months
・OS: Median not reached; 12-month 91·3%
・Subgroups: Post-hoc PFS by PD-L1, TC3 or IC3 17·0 vs TC0 and IC0 7·5 months; log-rank p=0·0048
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 adverse reactions 75%; neutropenia 56%, leukopenia 33%, febrile neutropenia 23%; no treatment-related deaths
・Limitations: Single-arm phase 2 without randomised comparator; OS immature (17% died); no central pathological review

records.title: Octreotide ± Prednisone (Loehrer)
records.subtitle: Thymic Epithelial Tumours · Advanced / recurrent disease — second-line targeted & antiangiogenic therapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2004
records.body: Advanced octreotide-scan-positive thymoma/thymic carcinoma Octreotide, with later addition of prednisone for non-responders Response rate ORR 32% (2 CR, 10 PR; responses confined to pure thymoma) with 2-year OS 75.7%; octreotide with or without prednisone is an option for somatostatin-receptor-positive thymoma.

records.title: Everolimus (Zucali)
records.subtitle: Thymic Epithelial Tumours · Advanced / recurrent disease — second-line targeted & antiangiogenic therapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2018
records.body:
Pathologically confirmed advanced (unresectable or metastatic) thymoma or thymic carcinoma, all progressing at study entry, after failure of at least one previous line of platinum-based chemotherapy; salvage setting (single-arm) Everolimus 10 mg orally once daily
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, death, or discontinuation for any other reason
・Design: Open-label, multicenter Primary: disease control rate. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall survival, duration of response, safety, time to treatment failure, predictive role of intratumoral biomarkers Everolimus showed durable disease control in 88% of platinum-pretreated thymoma and thymic carcinoma patients, but 6% died of pneumonitis
・DCR: 88% (44/50; 95% CI, 75.7% to 95.5%); thymoma 93.8%, thymic carcinoma 77.8%
・PFS: Median 10.1 mo (95% CI, 6.0 to 14.2); thymoma 16.6 mo, thymic carcinoma 5.6 mo
・OS: Median 25.7 mo (95% CI, 16.1 to not evaluable); thymoma not reached, thymic carcinoma 14.7 mo
・DoR: Median 7.1 mo (range, 1.2 to 25.9+); 56% free of PD at 6 months
・Biomarkers: Exploratory; p4E-BP1 (P < .001) and IGF1R (P = .023) positivity associated with shorter survival; no predictive marker
・Toxicity: G3/4 drug-related AEs 28%; pneumonitis 36%, three fatal (6%); stomatitis 66%; 18% discontinued definitively
・Limitations: Single-arm, open-label; no preplanned analysis by histology; biomarker tissue from only 27 patients
records.keywords: Zucali et al. J Clin Oncol 2018;36:342-349  29240542

records.title: Sunitinib (Thomas)
records.subtitle: Thymic Epithelial Tumours · Advanced / recurrent disease — second-line targeted & antiangiogenic therapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2015
records.body: Chemotherapy-refractory thymic carcinoma or thymoma Sunitinib 50 mg/day (4 weeks on, 2 weeks off) Objective response ORR 26% in thymic carcinoma (6/23 PR) versus 6% in thymoma, with stable disease in the majority of both; established sunitinib as an active second-line option for thymic carcinoma.

records.title: REMORA
records.subtitle: Thymic Epithelial Tumours · Advanced / recurrent disease — second-line targeted & antiangiogenic therapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2020
records.body: Advanced/metastatic thymic carcinoma after >=1 platinum regimen Lenvatinib 24 mg/day Objective response rate ORR 38% with disease control rate 95% and median PFS 9.3 months; among the most active second-line agents in thymic carcinoma and a standard salvage option.

records.title: PECATI
records.subtitle: Thymic Epithelial Tumours · Advanced / recurrent disease — second-line targeted & antiangiogenic therapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2025
records.body: Pretreated metastatic B3 thymoma / thymic carcinoma Lenvatinib + pembrolizumab 5-month progression-free survival Met its primary endpoint with 5-month PFS 88.4% and no treatment-related deaths; a chemo-free TKI plus checkpoint-inhibitor combination is a promising platinum-refractory option.

records.title: Pembrolizumab (Giaccone)
records.subtitle: Thymic Epithelial Tumours · Advanced / recurrent disease — immune checkpoint inhibition · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2018
records.body: Recurrent thymic carcinoma after >=1 line of chemotherapy Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w Objective response rate ORR 22.5% (1 CR, 8 PR) with stable disease in 53%; severe autoimmune toxicity occurred in 15% (including myocarditis), so checkpoint blockade requires close monitoring even in thymic carcinoma.

records.title: Pembrolizumab (Cho)
records.subtitle: Thymic Epithelial Tumours · Advanced / recurrent disease — immune checkpoint inhibition · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2019
records.body: Refractory/relapsed thymic epithelial tumor (26 carcinoma, 7 thymoma) Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w Response rate Partial responses in 19.2% of thymic carcinoma and 28.6% of thymoma (median PFS 6.1 months), but grade >=3 immune-related events in 71% of thymoma versus 15% of carcinoma; checkpoint blockade is generally avoided in thymoma.

records.title: CAO/ARO/AIO-94
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Establishing preoperative (chemo)radiation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2004
records.body:
Resectable rectal adenocarcinoma with the inferior margin within 16 cm from the anal verge; clinical stage T3 or T4 or node-positive disease on endorectal ultrasound and CT, with TNM stage I tumors and distant metastases ruled out; no prior chemotherapy or pelvic radiotherapy; excluded age >75 years, prior cancer other than nonmelanoma skin cancer, contraindications to chemoradiotherapy Ⓐ Preoperative chemoradiotherapy: radiotherapy 5040 cGy in 28 fractions of 180 cGy five times weekly, with fluorouracil 1000 mg per square meter per day as a 120-hour continuous intravenous infusion during the first and fifth weeks; surgery six weeks after completion; one month after surgery, four five-day cycles of fluorouracil 500 mg per square meter per day
Ⓑ Postoperative chemoradiotherapy: identical chemoradiotherapy plus a 540-cGy boost to the tumor bed after surgery; four cycles of bolus fluorouracil 500 mg per square meter per day, five times weekly, every four weeks
・Surgery: Total mesorectal excision by standardized technique in all patients Primary: overall survival. Secondary: disease-free survival, local recurrence, distant recurrence, postoperative complications, acute toxic effects, long-term toxic effects, sphincter preservation Preoperative chemoradiotherapy did not improve overall survival vs postoperative chemoradiotherapy, and its 10-year local control benefit persisted (median follow-up 134 months)
・OS (10-yr): Ⓐ 59.6% vs Ⓑ 59.9%; HR 0.98 (95% CI 0.79–1.21)
・DFS (10-yr): Ⓐ 68.1% vs Ⓑ 67.8%; HR 0.94 (95% CI 0.73–1.21)
・Local recurrence (10-yr): Ⓐ 7.1% vs Ⓑ 10.1%; HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.4–1.0); P=.048; competing-risk P=.051
・Distant metastases (10-yr): Ⓐ 29.8% vs Ⓑ 29.6%; HR 0.98 (95% CI 0.76–1.28)
・Postop complications: Ⓐ 36% vs Ⓑ 34%; in-hospital mortality Ⓐ 0.7% vs Ⓑ 1.3%
・Sphincter preservation: In 194 patients deemed to require abdominoperineal resection, Ⓐ 39% vs Ⓑ 19%; P=0.004
・Downstaging: Ⓐ pathological complete response 8%; TNM stage III Ⓐ 25% vs Ⓑ 40%
・Subgroups: Intersphincteric or abdominoperineal resection, local recurrence HR 2.24 (95% CI 1.07–4.71) postop vs preop CRT; exploratory
・Toxicity: G3/4 acute Ⓐ 27% vs Ⓑ 40%; long-term Ⓐ 14% vs Ⓑ 24%; anastomotic strictures Ⓐ 4% vs Ⓑ 12% (2004); 17 of 341 deaths treatment-related (long-term follow-up)
・Limitations: Relapse assessors aware of treatment assignment; Ⓑ 145 of 393 received no postoperative CRT (75 stage 0/I, 19 stage IV); seven of 60 local recurrences beyond 5 years
records.keywords: Sauer et al. N Engl J Med 2004;351:1731-1740  15496622 Sauer et al. J Clin Oncol 2012;30:1926-1933  22529255

records.title: Polish I
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Establishing preoperative (chemo)radiation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2004
records.body:
Rectal adenocarcinoma, resectable T3–4 without sphincter infiltration; preoperative radiotherapy before total mesorectal excision; inferior margin palpable on digital rectal examination, WHO performance score 0–2, age ≤75 years, no distant metastases; fixed tumour, previous malignancy and anal canal involvement excluded Ⓐ 5 × 5 Gy preoperative irradiation in one week with surgery within 7 days
Ⓑ Radiochemotherapy 50.4 Gy (1.8 Gy per fraction over 5.5 weeks) plus leucovorin 20 mg/m²/day IV then 5-FU 325 mg/m²/day IV bolus on 5 consecutive days in weeks 1 and 5, surgery 4–6 weeks later
・Surgery: Total mesorectal excision for low-lying cancers, subtotal mesorectal excision for mid-rectal; sphincter decision based on tumour status at surgery
・RT technique: Simulator-based three- or four-field, identical beams in both arms
・Postoperative chemotherapy: Optional; protocol called for 4 months bolus 5-FU/leucovorin in Ⓑ, 6 months in Ⓐ Primary: sphincter preservation rate. Secondary: acute postirradiation toxicity, postoperative complications, 30-day postoperative mortality, clinical complete response, pathological complete response, positive radial margin, overall survival, disease-free survival, local recurrence, distant metastases, late toxicity, permanent stoma Chemoradiation did not increase sphincter preservation, survival, local control or late toxicity vs short-course radiotherapy despite greater downstaging
・Sphincter preservation: Ⓐ 61.2% vs Ⓑ 58.0%; P = 0.570 (intention-to-treat)
・OS: 4-yr actuarial (median f/u 48 mo) Ⓐ 67.2% vs Ⓑ 66.2%; P = 0.960; HR 1.01 (95% CI 0.69–1.48)
・DFS: 4-yr actuarial Ⓐ 58.4% vs Ⓑ 55.6%; P = 0.820; HR 0.96 (95% CI 0.69–1.35)
・Local recurrence: Crude Ⓐ 9.0% vs Ⓑ 14.2%, P = 0.170; 4-yr actuarial 10.6% vs 15.6%, P = 0.210; HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.32–1.28)
・Distant metastases: Crude Ⓐ 31.4% vs Ⓑ 34.6%; P = 0.540
・Permanent stoma: Ⓐ 56.9% vs Ⓑ 51.6%; P = 0.350; RR 1.10 (95% CI 0.90–1.35)
・Pathology: Tumour 1.9 cm smaller in Ⓑ, P < 0.001; pCR Ⓐ 0.7% vs Ⓑ 16.1%, P < 0.001; positive radial margin Ⓐ 12.9% vs Ⓑ 4.4%, P = 0.017
・Clinical CR: Ⓐ 2% vs Ⓑ 13%, P < 0.001; Ⓑ 5/18 complete responders underwent APR
・Subgroups: No benefit for tumours ≤6 cm from anal verge (Ⓐ 47% vs Ⓑ 42%; P = 0.40) or by intended surgery
・Early toxicity: Any complication Ⓐ 24% vs Ⓑ 85%, P < 0.001; grade III–IV Ⓐ 3.2% vs Ⓑ 18.2%, P < 0.001; two sudden cardiac deaths in Ⓑ
・Late toxicity: Any Ⓐ 28.3% vs Ⓑ 27.0%, P = 0.810; severe Ⓐ 10.1% vs Ⓑ 7.1%, P = 0.360; severe RR 1.43 (95% CI 0.67–3.07)
・Limitations: Surgeons' sphincter decisions partly based on pre-treatment tumour volume (30% declared AR regardless); powered only to detect ≥15% differences; follow-up not long enough for late toxicity
records.keywords: Bujko et al. Radiother Oncol 2004;72:15-24  15236870 Bujko et al. Br J Surg 2006;93:1215-1223  16983741

records.title: TROG 01.04
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Establishing preoperative (chemo)radiation · Randomised clinical trial · 2012
records.body:
Ultrasound- or MRI-staged T3 rectal adenocarcinoma with lower border within 12 cm of anal verge, neoadjuvant radiotherapy setting; no restriction on nodal stage; excluded distant metastases, recurrent rectal cancer, prior radiotherapy, unstable cardiac disease, active infection, other cancers within 5 years Ⓐ SC: pelvic radiotherapy 25 Gy in 5 fractions in 1 week → surgery 3 to 7 days later → six monthly courses FU 425 mg/m² + folinic acid 20 mg/m² daily for 5 days from 4 to 6 weeks post-surgery
Ⓑ LC: pelvic chemoradiotherapy 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions over 5 weeks and 3 days + continuous infusional FU 225 mg/m² per day → surgery 4 to 6 weeks later → four monthly courses of same chemotherapy from 4 to 6 weeks post-surgery Primary: local recurrence rate at 3 years. Secondary: time to local recurrence, time to distant recurrence, recurrence-free survival, overall survival, late toxicity SC and LC did not differ significantly in local recurrence at 3 years; CI consistent with no clinically important difference or a difference favoring LC
・3-yr LR: Ⓐ 7.5% vs Ⓑ 4.4%; difference 3.1% (95% CI −2.1 to 8.3; P = .24)
・Time to LR: HR Ⓑ:Ⓐ 0.75 (95% CI 0.32 to 1.77; P = .66)
・5-yr distant recurrence: Ⓐ 27% vs Ⓑ 30%; HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.69 to 1.56)
・RFS: HR Ⓑ:Ⓐ 1.15 (95% CI 0.80 to 1.62; P = .47)
・5-yr OS: Ⓐ 74% vs Ⓑ 70%; HR 1.12 (95% CI 0.76 to 1.67)
・Downstaging: Ⓑ 45% vs Ⓐ 28% (P = .002); pCR (ypT0) Ⓑ 15% vs Ⓐ 1%
・Subgroups: Distal tumors (≤ 5 cm) LR Ⓐ 12.5% vs Ⓑ 0.0% cumulative incidence; HR 0.26 (95% CI 0.06 to 1.20); exploratory
・Toxicity: Late G3-4 RT toxicity Ⓐ 5.8% vs Ⓑ 8.2% (P = .53); no severe neuropathy reported
・Limitations: Cannot exclude clinically important LR difference favoring LC; distal-tumor LC benefit exploratory; longer follow-up needed for late effects
records.keywords: Ngan et al. J Clin Oncol 2012;30:3827-3833  23008301

records.title: Stockholm III
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Establishing preoperative (chemo)radiation · Randomised, non-blinded, non-inferiority clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body:
Primary rectal adenocarcinoma within 15 cm of the anal verge, planned for open abdominal resection; preoperative radiotherapy setting, no concomitant chemotherapy (18 Swedish hospitals); no signs of non-resectability or distant metastases; no previous abdominal or pelvic radiotherapy, severe ischaemic disease or severe arteriosclerosis; no age restriction Ⓐ Short-course radiotherapy 5 × 5 Gy, surgery within 1 week
Ⓑ Short-course radiotherapy 5 × 5 Gy, surgery after 4–8 weeks
Ⓒ Long-course radiotherapy 25 × 2 Gy (50 Gy total), surgery after 4–8 weeks
・Chemotherapy: None concomitant; resection by total mesorectal excision
・Design: Non-blinded; after May 1999 amendment centres chose three-arm or two-arm (Ⓐ/Ⓑ) randomisation Primary: time to local recurrence. Secondary: overall survival, postoperative mortality, postoperative complications, reoperations, late complications, radiation toxicity, sphincter-preserving surgeries, quality of life, recurrence-free survival, distant metastases-free survival Delayed surgery after short-course radiotherapy was non-inferior to immediate surgery, with fewer postoperative complications but more acute radiation toxicity
・Local recurrence: Ⓑ HR 1.44 (95% CI 0.41–5.11), Ⓒ HR 2.24 (0.71–7.10) vs Ⓐ; both deemed non-inferior (whole trial)
・Postop complications: Pooled Ⓐ 53% vs Ⓑ 41%; OR 0.61 (95% CI 0.45–0.83); three-arm 50% vs 38% vs 39%, p=0.075
・OS: 5-year Ⓐ 73% vs Ⓑ 76% vs Ⓒ 78% (three-arm); pooled Ⓐ 76% vs Ⓑ 77%
・RFS: 5-year post-hoc pooled Ⓐ 65% vs Ⓑ 68%
・LRT-delay: Similar to both short-course regimens but prolongs treatment time substantially
・Toxicity: Acute radiation-toxicity admission pooled Ⓑ 7% vs Ⓐ <1%; Ⓒ 5%; no death from radiation toxicity; 30-day mortality <1%
・Limitations: Original HR 1.7 non-inferiority boundary not excluded (revised HR 3.6); Ⓒ under-enrolled after two-arm amendment; T1–T2 and 25–30% pathological stage I included

records.title: PRODIGE 42 / GERICO 12
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Establishing preoperative (chemo)radiation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body:
Resectable T3–T4 rectal adenocarcinoma with lower margin within 12 cm of the anal verge, or T2 of the very low rectum; aged ≥75 years, PS 0–2, any nodal status; excluded metastatic disease, local recurrence, or significant serious disease preventing treatment Ⓐ Chemoradiotherapy: 50 Gy in 25 fractions of 2 Gy over 5 weeks with capecitabine 800 mg/m² orally twice daily, 5 days per week
Ⓑ Short course radiotherapy: 25 Gy in 5 fractions in one week
・Surgery: Delayed surgery 7 ± 1 weeks after neoadjuvant treatment in both arms Primary: R0 resection rate, autonomy deterioration by IADL score from baseline to 12 months post-operative. Secondary: overall survival, disease-free survival, specific survival, locoregional recurrence-free survival, safety, post-operative ostomy rate at 6 and 12 months Short course radiotherapy missed both co-primary endpoints but showed better tolerance and exploratory overall/specific survival gains versus chemoradiotherapy
・R0: Ⓐ 88 vs Ⓑ 84.3% (mITT), non-inferiority not met (p = 0.28); PP Ⓐ 95.6 vs Ⓑ 88.0% (p = 0.49)
・IADL deterioration to 12 months (co-primary): Ⓐ 28.6% vs Ⓑ 29.2%; no significant difference
・IADL deterioration at 3 months post-operative: Ⓐ 44.8% vs Ⓑ 14.8%; p = 0.032
・OS, 36-month follow-up: Favoured Ⓑ; HR 0.28 (95% CI 0.07–1.00), p = 0.05
・Specific survival: Favoured Ⓑ; HR 0.21 (95% CI 0.04–0.97), p = 0.027
・RFS: No difference; HR 0.99 (95% CI 0.47–2.09); local RFS HR 1.7 (95% CI 0.3–9.1)
・pCR: Ⓐ 17.4% vs Ⓑ 6.1%; p = 0.16
・Ostomy at 12 months: Ⓐ 32.5% vs Ⓑ 39.1%; no significant difference
・Toxicity: Pre-operative serious AEs Ⓐ 22% vs Ⓑ 9.8%; grade 3–5 Ⓐ 32% vs Ⓑ 21.5%; two treatment-related deaths in Ⓐ
・Limitations: Stopped early for poor accrual (105 of 420 planned); underpowered for survival comparisons; open-label
records.keywords: François et al. Eur J Cancer 2023;180:62-70  36535196

records.title: STAR-01
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Intensifying chemoradiation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2011
records.body:
Locally advanced resectable rectal adenocarcinoma within 12 cm of the anal verge (mid-low rectum), cT3-4 and/or cN1-2 (nodes >5 mm positive), no infiltration of pelvic wall, prostate or bladder base, no distant metastases; preoperative chemoradiotherapy; WHO PS 0-2, age ≤75; no prior treatment for this disease, pelvic RT or other tumor history Ⓐ Pelvic radiotherapy 50.4 Gy in 28 daily fractions + infusional fluorouracil 225 mg/m²/d throughout radiotherapy
Ⓑ Ⓐ + oxaliplatin 60 mg/m² IV weekly × 6
・Duration: Radiotherapy over ~6 weeks; surgery 6–8 weeks after chemoradiotherapy, TME advised
・Adjuvant: Fluorouracil-based chemotherapy planned for all achieving curative resection Primary: post-therapy pathologic complete response (this protocol-planned response analysis), overall survival (trial primary end point). Secondary: pathologically positive lymph nodes, tumor infiltration beyond muscularis propria, positive circumferential resection margin, resection status, tumor regression grade, intra-abdominal metastases at surgery, acute toxicity, treatment compliance Adding weekly oxaliplatin to preoperative fluorouracil chemoradiotherapy did not improve primary tumor response and significantly increased acute toxicity
・ypCR: Ⓐ 16% vs Ⓑ 16%; OR 0.98 (95% CI 0.66 to 1.44); P = .904
・ypN+: Ⓐ 26% vs Ⓑ 29%; P = .447
・CRM positive: Ⓐ 7% vs Ⓑ 4%; P = .239; 60.9% of data available
・ypM1 at surgery: Ⓐ 2.9% vs Ⓑ 0.5%; P = .014
・Toxicity: G3–4 Ⓐ 8% vs Ⓑ 24%; P < .001; diarrhea 4.2% vs 15.3%; potentially related deaths 1 vs 2
・Limitations: Overall survival (trial primary end point) awaits longer follow-up; compliance reduced in Ⓑ
records.keywords: Aschele et al. J Clin Oncol 2011;29:2773-2780  21606427

records.title: ACCORD 12/0405-Prodige 2
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Intensifying chemoradiation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2010
records.body:
Histologically confirmed rectal adenocarcinoma, T3 or resectable (R0 or R1 resection deemed achievable) T4, no distant metastases (M0); neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy before planned surgery; T2 tumours of the anterior and lower rectum also eligible; tumour accessible to digital rectal examination; age ≤ 80 years, WHO performance status 0 or 1 Ⓐ Radiotherapy 45 Gy in 25 fractions of 1.8 Gy over 5 weeks with concurrent capecitabine 800 mg/m² orally twice daily 5 days per week (Cap 45)
Ⓑ Radiotherapy 50 Gy in 25 fractions of 2 Gy over 5 weeks with capecitabine 800 mg/m² orally twice daily 5 days per week plus oxaliplatin 50 mg/m² IV once weekly (Capox 50)
・Surgery: Total mesorectal excision planned 6 weeks after chemoradiotherapy Primary: pathologic complete response (ypCR). Secondary: circumferential rectal margin, sphincter preservation, local control, progression-free survival, safety Capox 50 did not significantly improve ypCR versus Cap 45; oxaliplatin benefit was not demonstrated and early toxicity increased
・ypCR: Ⓐ 13.9 vs Ⓑ 19.2%; P = .09
・ypCR + near-complete (Dworak 2/3): Ⓐ 28.9 vs Ⓑ 39.4%; P = .008
・CRM: R1 (≤ 1 mm) Ⓐ 12.7 vs Ⓑ 7.7%, P = .17; exploratory 0–2 mm Ⓐ 19.3 vs Ⓑ 9.9%, P = .022
・Sphincter preservation: No difference; conservative surgery 75% in both groups
・Toxicity: Grade 3–4 Ⓐ 10.9 vs Ⓑ 25.4%, P < .001; diarrhea Ⓐ 3.2 vs Ⓑ 12.6%; 60-day postoperative deaths 0.3% both
・Limitations: Underpowered for primary endpoint; radiotherapy dose and oxaliplatin changed together; median follow-up 12 months, no local control or survival data
records.keywords: Gérard et al. J Clin Oncol 2010;28:1638-1644  20194850

records.title: NSABP R-04
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Intensifying chemoradiation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2015
records.body:
Rectal adenocarcinoma, clinical stage II (T3-4N0) or III (T1-4N1-2, positive node ≥1.0 cm on imaging) by transrectal ultrasound/CT/MRI, distal border <12 cm from anal verge, planned preoperative chemoradiotherapy and curative resection, no metastatic disease; excluded recent myocardial infarction (6 months), active inflammatory bowel disease, preexisting peripheral neuropathy, previous pelvic radiation Ⓐ 5-FU 225 mg/m²/day continuous IV infusion + radiotherapy
Ⓑ 5-FU 225 mg/m²/day continuous IV infusion + oxaliplatin 50 mg/m² IV weekly x 5 during radiotherapy + radiotherapy
Ⓒ Capecitabine 825 mg/m² orally twice daily + radiotherapy
Ⓓ Capecitabine 825 mg/m² orally twice daily + oxaliplatin 50 mg/m² IV weekly x 5 during radiotherapy + radiotherapy
・RT: 180 cGy/day, five days per week, 25 fractions over five weeks; 4500 cGy pelvic field with boost to total 5040–5580 cGy
・Duration: Fluoropyrimidine from first to last day of radiotherapy; surgery within six to eight weeks after radiotherapy completion
・Schedule: Fluoropyrimidine initially seven days a week; amended October 2005 to five days a week (radiation days only)
・Design: 2x2 factorial; oxaliplatin question added by protocol amendment after accrual had begun Primary: local-regional tumor control at three years. Secondary: overall survival, disease-free survival, time to loco-regional recurrence, pathological complete response, sphincter-sparing surgery, surgical downstaging, toxicity Capecitabine produced local-regional control, DFS and OS similar to infusional 5-FU plus radiation; oxaliplatin did not improve local-regional failure, DFS or OS in any risk group but added considerable toxicity
・3-yr LRC: 5-FU (Ⓐ/Ⓑ) 11.2% vs CAPE (Ⓒ/Ⓓ) 11.8%; HR 1.0 (95% CI 0.75–1.32), P = .98; prespecified equivalence criteria met
・3-yr LRC: OX (Ⓑ/Ⓓ) 12.1% vs none (Ⓐ/Ⓒ) 11.2%; HR 0.94, P = .70; no fluoropyrimidine-by-oxaliplatin interaction, P = .46
・5-yr DFS: 5-FU (Ⓐ/Ⓑ) 66.4% vs CAPE (Ⓒ/Ⓓ) 67.7%, HR 0.97, P = .70; no-OX (Ⓐ/Ⓒ) 64.2% vs OX (Ⓑ/Ⓓ) 69.2%, HR 0.91, P = .34
・5-yr OS: 5-FU (Ⓐ/Ⓑ) 79.9% vs CAPE (Ⓒ/Ⓓ) 80.8%, HR 0.94, P = .61; no-OX (Ⓐ/Ⓒ) 79.0% vs OX (Ⓑ/Ⓓ) 81.3%, HR 0.89, P = .38
・3-yr LRR after R0: OX 3.1% vs none 5.1%, HR 0.71, P = .21; 5-FU vs CAPE HR 0.86, P = .53
・QoL: Year-1 FACT-C showed essentially no difference between fluoropyrimidines; five-year data awaited
・Subgroups: Unplanned high-risk analysis (lymph node–positive or T4): OX 3-yr local events 24.1% vs 19.2%, HR 1.27, P = .38
・Toxicity: Grade 3–5 Ⓐ 26.5%, Ⓒ 30.1% vs Ⓑ 40.1%, Ⓓ 41.9%; grade 3–5 diarrhea 6.9% vs 16.5% with OX, P < .0001
・Deaths: On treatment/within 45 days 1.3–1.6% CAPE arms vs 0.3% 5-FU arms; not statistically significant
・Limitations: Type/use of adjuvant therapy incompletely documented; high-risk analyses unplanned; pCR and surgical endpoints published separately
records.keywords: Allegra et al. JNCI J Natl Cancer Inst 2015;107:djv248  26374429

records.title: CAO/ARO/AIO-04
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Intensifying chemoradiation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2015
records.body:
Histopathologically confirmed rectal adenocarcinoma no more than 12 cm from the anal verge; locally advanced, clinically staged cT3–4 (perirectal fat infiltration or invasion of adjacent tissues/organs) or node-positive (cN1–2); preoperative chemoradiotherapy and surgery setting; excluded metastatic disease, prior chemotherapy or pelvic radiotherapy, previous or concurrent malignancies, peripheral neuropathy >grade 2 Ⓐ Radiotherapy 50·4 Gy in 28 fractions + infusional fluorouracil 1000 mg/m² days 1–5 and 29–33 → surgery → bolus fluorouracil 500 mg/m² days 1–5 and 29, four cycles
Ⓑ Radiotherapy 50·4 Gy in 28 fractions + infusional fluorouracil 250 mg/m² days 1–14 and 22–35 + oxaliplatin 50 mg/m² days 1, 8, 22, 29 → surgery → oxaliplatin 100 mg/m² + leucovorin 400 mg/m² + infusional fluorouracil 2400 mg/m² days 1–2 and 15–16, eight cycles
・Surgery: Total mesorectal excision 5–6 weeks after chemoradiotherapy; adjuvant chemotherapy 4 weeks after surgery
・Design: Open-label Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, pathological complete response, R0 resection, sphincter-sparing surgery, cumulative incidence of locoregional recurrence, cumulative incidence of distant recurrence, acute toxicity, late toxicity Adding oxaliplatin to fluorouracil-based preoperative chemoradiotherapy and adjuvant chemotherapy improved disease-free survival versus fluorouracil-based combined modality treatment; overall survival did not differ significantly
・3-yr DFS: Ⓐ 71·2 vs Ⓑ 75·9%; HR 0·79 (95% CI 0·64–0·98); median follow-up 50 months
・3-yr OS: Ⓐ 88·0 vs Ⓑ 88·7%; HR 0·96 (95% CI 0·72–1·26)
・pCR: Ⓐ 13 vs Ⓑ 17%; OR 1·41 (95% CI 1·03–1·94); unplanned exploratory analysis
・3-yr recurrences: Local Ⓐ 4·6 vs Ⓑ 2·9%; distant Ⓐ 22·4 vs Ⓑ 18·5%
・Subgroups: Exploratory DFS benefit in cN0 (HR 0·56, 95% CI 0·36–0·86) vs cN+ (0·91, 0·71–1·16)
・Toxicity: G3–4 with chemoradiotherapy Ⓐ 20 vs Ⓑ 24%; G≥3 sensory neuropathy (adjuvant) Ⓑ 10 vs Ⓐ 1%; treatment-related deaths Ⓑ 8 (1%) vs Ⓐ 3 (<1%)
・Limitations: Open-label; fluorouracil schedules differed between arms; MRI not mandatory for staging

records.title: ARISTOTLE
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Intensifying chemoradiation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma (histologically confirmed), non-metastatic; preoperative chemoradiotherapy; MRI-defined entry: mesorectal fascia involved or breached, threatened (tumour ≤1 mm), low tumour ≤1 mm from levator, muscularis propria involvement at or below puborectalis, or inter-sphincteric plane/external anal sphincter involvement; excludes unequivocal metastases, prior pelvic radiotherapy, malignancy within 5 years, Gilbert's disease Ⓐ Capecitabine 900 mg/m² orally twice daily on radiotherapy days (Mon–Fri)
Ⓑ Capecitabine 650 mg/m² orally twice daily on radiotherapy days (Mon–Fri) + irinotecan 60 mg/m² IV once weekly in weeks 1–4
・RT: Preoperative pelvic radiotherapy 45 Gy in 25 daily fractions over 5 weeks, started within 4 weeks of randomisation
・Surgery: Recommended 8–10 weeks after chemoradiotherapy completion
・Design: Open-label Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, cause-specific survival, time to locoregional failure, time to distant metastasis, time to treatment failure, circumferential resection margin status, histopathological complete response, histopathological tumour cell density, health-related quality of life, functional outcome, frequency and severity of adverse events, compliance to trial treatment Adding concurrent weekly irinotecan to preoperative capecitabine chemoradiotherapy did not improve disease-free survival or pathological complete response and added severe toxicity
・36-mo DFS: Ⓐ 67% vs Ⓑ 68%; stratified HR 0·91 (95% CI 0·68–1·23), p=0·54; median FU 78 mo
・36-mo OS: Ⓐ 83% vs Ⓑ 88%; stratified HR 0·97 (0·69–1·37), p=0·86
・pCR (operated): Ⓐ 17% vs Ⓑ 19%; p=0·56
・36-mo distant metastasis: Ⓐ 25·3% vs Ⓑ 27·7%; sHR 0·90 (0·67–1·20)
・Subgroups: Nominal DFS interactions (ECOG p=0·045; stoma p=0·012), unadjusted for multiplicity; Ⓑ favoured in ambulatory (HR 0·59, 0·36–0·99) and stoma (0·45, 0·23–0·85)
・Toxicity: Grade 3–5 AEs Ⓐ 52% vs Ⓑ 78%; diarrhoea 4% vs 14%; neutrophil decreased 1% vs 10%; 5 treatment-related deaths (3 Ⓑ, 2 Ⓐ)
・Treatment delivery: Full 45 Gy received Ⓐ 89% vs Ⓑ 75%; ≥90% capecitabine dose Ⓐ 89% vs Ⓑ 68%
・QoL: Pain opening bowels and vaginal bleeding more common with Ⓑ at 12–36 months
・Limitations: Open-label; fewer events than assumed, possibly underpowered; UGT1A1 and DPYD status not evaluated

records.title: CAO/ARO/AIO-12
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) · Randomised non-comparative clinical trial (phase II) · 2019
records.body:
Rectal adenocarcinoma ≤12 cm from anal verge on rigid rectoscopy; stage II or III, preoperative (total neoadjuvant) setting; MRI-defined: cT3 <6 cm from anal verge, cT3 in middle third (≥6 to 12 cm) with extramural spread >5 mm (>cT3b), cT4, or lymph node involvement; ECOG 0–1; distant metastases excluded by CT Ⓐ Induction FOLFOX (three cycles) → fluorouracil/oxaliplatin CRT → TME
Ⓑ Fluorouracil/oxaliplatin CRT → consolidation FOLFOX (three cycles) → TME
・CRT: 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions (IMRT) with continuous-infusion fluorouracil 250 mg/m² days 1–14 and 22–35 and oxaliplatin 50 mg/m² days 1, 8, 22 and 29
・FOLFOX: Oxaliplatin 100 mg/m², leucovorin 400 mg/m², fluorouracil 2,400 mg/m² 46-hour continuous infusion, repeated on day 15
・Surgery: TME scheduled on day 123 after start of TNT, irrespective of tumour response; adjuvant chemotherapy not recommended
・Design: Open-label Primary: pathologic complete response (ypT0N0). Secondary: acute toxicity, compliance with TNT, surgical complications, tumor regression grading, Neoadjuvant Rectal Score, R0 resection, sphincter-sparing surgery, long-term oncologic outcomes, combined pCR and cCR rate, circumferential resection margin involvement, TME quality CRT followed by consolidation chemotherapy (Ⓑ) met the pCR hypothesis of 25% vs a 15% historical CRT benchmark; induction chemotherapy first (Ⓐ) did not
・pCR: Ⓐ 17% vs Ⓑ 25%; vs 15% benchmark Ⓐ P = .210, Ⓑ P < .001
・pCR, exploratory Ⓑ vs Ⓐ: OR 1.69 (95% CI 0.96–2.99); P = .071
・pCR + cCR: Ⓐ 21% vs Ⓑ 28%
・Compliance: Full-dose RT Ⓐ 91% vs Ⓑ 97%; all induction/consolidation cycles Ⓐ 92% vs Ⓑ 85%
・TRG 4–3: Ⓐ 41% vs Ⓑ 50%; low NAR score 26% vs 35% (descriptive)
・R0: Ⓐ 92% vs Ⓑ 90%; sphincter-preserving surgery 68% vs 72%
・Toxicity: CRT-related G3–4 Ⓐ 37% vs Ⓑ 27%; chemotherapy-related G3–4 22% vs 22%; one pre-surgery death and one 60-day postoperative death per arm
・Limitations: Each arm tested against historical control, not powered for between-arm comparison; CRT-to-surgery interval Ⓐ 45 vs Ⓑ 90 days; no long-term outcomes yet
records.keywords: Fokas et al. J Clin Oncol 2019;37:3212-3222  31150315

records.title: RAPIDO
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body:
Primary rectal adenocarcinoma, biopsy-proven, newly diagnosed, locally advanced, distal extension <16 cm from anal verge; untreated, preoperative; high risk on pelvic MRI with at least one of cT4a/cT4b, extramural vascular invasion, cN2, involved mesorectal fascia (tumour or node ≤1 mm) or enlarged lateral nodes considered metastatic; fit for chemotherapy, ECOG 0–1; excluded metastatic or recurrent disease, or extensive growth into cranial sacrum/lumbosacral nerve roots Short-course radiotherapy 5 × 5 Gy (over a maximum of 8 days) → 6 cycles CAPOX (capecitabine 1000 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1–14, oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1) or 9 cycles FOLFOX4 (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² IV day 1, leucovorin 200 mg/m² IV days 1–2, bolus fluorouracil 400 mg/m² then 600 mg/m² over 22 h days 1–2), started within 11–18 days (at most 4 weeks) → TME 2–4 weeks after chemotherapy vs chemoradiotherapy 28 × 1.8 Gy to 50.4 Gy or 25 × 2.0 Gy to 50.0 Gy with capecitabine 825 mg/m² orally twice daily → TME 6–10 weeks after last fraction → optional adjuvant 8 cycles CAPOX or 12 cycles FOLFOX4 per hospital policy Primary: 3-year disease-related treatment failure. Secondary: completion rate of neoadjuvant treatment, toxicity, R0 resection rate, pathological complete response rate, surgical complications within 30 days, quality of life, functional outcome, overall survival, local recurrence, distant metastases, locoregional failure, serious adverse events Short-course radiotherapy then preoperative chemotherapy reduced disease-related treatment failure vs chemoradiotherapy, sustained at 5 years, but increased locoregional recurrence
・3-yr DrTF: 23.7% vs 30.4%; HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.60–0.95)
・5-yr DrTF: 27.8% vs 34.0%; HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.63–1.00); P = 0.0480
・5-yr distant metastases: 23.0% vs 30.4%; HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.57–0.93)
・LRF at median 5.6-yr follow-up: 11.7% vs 8.1%; P = 0.07
・LRR after R0/R1 resection: 10.2% vs 6.1%; P = 0.027; multivariable HR 1.87 (95% CI 1.14–3.07)
・pCR: 28% vs 14%; OR 2.37 (95% CI 1.67–3.37)
・5-yr OS: 81.7% vs 80.2%; HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.70–1.19); similar
・Subgroups: LRR excess after 3D-CRT (11.6% vs 6.0%), not after IMRT/VMAT (6.3% vs 6.2%)
・Limitations: open-label; primary endpoint changed from DFS during the trial; LRF analyses unpowered, no central MRI/RT/pathology review
・Toxicity: preoperative G≥3 AEs 48% vs 25% (34% during standard-arm adjuvant chemotherapy); G≥3 diarrhoea 18% vs 9%; 4 vs 4 treatment-related deaths

records.title: PRODIGE 23
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body:
Newly diagnosed, biopsy-proven rectal adenocarcinoma within 15 cm of the anal verge; locally advanced, previously untreated, cT3 (at risk of local recurrence, preoperative chemoradiotherapy recommended by tumour board) or cT4 M0 on MRI; age under 76 years, WHO PS 0-1; excluded distant metastases, non-resectable cancer, prior pelvic radiotherapy or chemotherapy, ischaemic coronary disease, peripheral neuropathy > grade 1, ongoing inflammatory bowel disease FOLFIRINOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², irinotecan 180 mg/m², leucovorin 400 mg/m², fluorouracil 2400 mg/m² continuous IV over 46 hours, every 14 days for 6 cycles) → chemoradiotherapy (50 Gy over 5 weeks, 2 Gy 5 times/week, with capecitabine 800 mg/m² twice daily 5 days/week) → total mesorectal excision 6–8 weeks later → adjuvant mFOLFOX6 (6 cycles) or capecitabine (4 cycles) for 3 months vs the same chemoradiotherapy → total mesorectal excision → adjuvant mFOLFOX6 (12 cycles) or capecitabine 1250 mg/m² twice daily days 1–14 every 21 days (8 cycles) for 6 months; adjuvant regimen by centre choice Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, metastasis-free survival, cancer-specific survival, locoregional recurrence rate, metastatic recurrence rate, pathologic complete response rate (ypT0N0), R0 resection rate, surgical morbidity, safety, quality of life, neoadjuvant rectal score, tumour regression Neoadjuvant mFOLFIRINOX before chemoradiotherapy improved DFS and, at 82.2-mo follow-up, OS vs standard chemoradiotherapy, surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy
・3-yr DFS: 75.7% vs 68.5%; HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.49–0.97)
・7-yr DFS: 67.6% vs 62.5%; RMST difference 5.73 mo (95% CI 0.05–11.41)
・7-yr OS: 81.9% vs 76.1%; RMST difference 4.37 mo (95% CI 0.35–8.38)
・7-yr MFS: 79.2% vs 72.3%; RMST difference 6.1 mo (95% CI 0.93–11.37)
・5-yr CSS: 88.1% vs 82.4%; HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.42–1.05); not significant
・Locoregional relapse: 7-yr 5.3% vs 8.1%; no increase with neoadjuvant chemotherapy
・pCR (ypT0N0): 27.8% vs 12.1%
・DrTF (post hoc): 7-yr 25.0% vs 34.0%; RMST difference 6.3 mo (95% CI 1.03–11.57)
・Limitations: open-label; non-proportional hazards, long-term effects as RMST differences without HR; 7.3% had cT3N0 without high-risk features
・Toxicity: FOLFIRINOX G3/4 46.5%; adjuvant G3/4 45.1% vs 74.1%; G3/4 neuropathy 11.7% vs 20.7%; Clavien-Dindo IV–V 0.9% vs 4.3%; treatment-related deaths one vs 2; second cancers 7-yr 6.1% vs 2.2%

records.title: STELLAR
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body:
Rectal adenocarcinoma of the distal or middle third (0-5 cm and 5.1-10 cm from anal edge); locally advanced cT3-4 and/or regional node-positive without distant metastases, MRI-staged, no previous anticancer treatment; age 18-70 years, ECOG 0-1; excluded recurrent disease, second primary malignancy, contraindication to planned treatment or MRI TNT: short-course RT 5 Gy × 5 (IMRT) → 7-14 days later 4 cycles CAPOX (oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1 + capecitabine 1,000 mg/m² twice daily days 1-14) → TME 6-8 weeks after preoperative therapy → 2 cycles CAPOX vs CRT: 50 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks (IMRT) with concurrent capecitabine 825 mg/m² twice daily → TME 6-8 weeks after → 6 cycles CAPOX; watch-and-wait allowed after cCR Primary: 3-year disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, metastasis-free survival, locoregional recurrence, surgical complications, toxicity, treatment completion rate, radical resection rate, complete response rate (pCR plus sustained cCR), postrecurrence progression-free survival, postrecurrence survival Short-course RT then CAPOX was non-inferior to long-course CRT for 3-year DFS, with higher 5-year OS (exploratory) at the cost of higher acute toxicity
・3-yr DFS: 64.5% vs 62.3%; HR 0.883 (one-sided 95% CI upper bound 1.11; NI margin 1.43); non-inferiority P<.001
・5-yr DFS (exploratory update, median follow-up 68.7 mo): 62.0% vs 58.7%; HR 0.849 (95% CI 0.662–1.089)
・5-yr OS (exploratory update): 78.1% vs 69.7%; HR 0.739 (95% CI 0.550–0.993)
・3-yr MFS: 77.1% vs 75.3%; HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.63–1.24); not significant
・5-yr DM (exploratory update): 26.4% vs 28.8%; HR 0.826 (95% CI 0.609–1.121)
・5-yr LRR (exploratory update): 9.6% vs 11.6%; HR 0.814 (95% CI 0.494–1.340)
・CR (pCR + sustained cCR): 21.8% vs 12.3%; P=.002
・Watch-and-wait: 28 vs 10 cCR patients; 6 vs 2 failures; local regrowth as late as 83 mo
・Postrecurrence (exploratory, after LRR or DM): PFS HR 0.691 (95% CI 0.497–0.961); survival HR 0.698 (95% CI 0.490–0.994)
・Subgroups (exploratory, unadjusted): advanced ESMO risk OS HR 0.663 (95% CI 0.469–0.937); LRR lower in cT4 (HR 0.186) and >5 cm (HR 0.261), interaction P<.05
・Limitations: open-label; 5-yr analyses exploratory, OS gain modest and possibly statistically fragile; wide NI margin (HR 1.43)
・Toxicity: preoperative acute grade III–V 26.5% vs 12.6%; grade 3–4 hematologic 15.8% vs 2.0%; one CRT-arm death (myocardial infarction) after CRT; late-complication deaths 2 vs 2; late toxicity not comprehensively collected

records.title: TNTCRT
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: High-risk locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma within 12 cm of the anal verge; clinical stage II or III on MRI, neoadjuvant setting; at least 1 MRI high-risk feature: resectable cT4a-b, cT3c-d with positive EMVI, cN2, or threatened MRF (≤2 mm); age 18-70 years; excluded metastatic or unresectable disease, lateral lymph node >10 mm or major comorbidities Doublet-LC TNT: 1 cycle induction CAPOX (oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² every 3 weeks; capecitabine 1,000 mg/m² twice daily days 1-14 of each 3-week cycle) → LCRT 50-50.4 Gy in 25-28 fractions with capecitabine 825 mg/m² twice daily 5 days/week plus oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² every 3 weeks for two cycles → three consolidation CAPOX cycles at induction dose → TME 3-4 weeks after consolidation vs nCRT: LCRT 50-50.4 Gy with capecitabine 825 mg/m² twice daily 5 days/week → TME 6-8 weeks after chemoradiotherapy → six cycles adjuvant CAPOX starting 4-8 weeks postoperatively Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: pathologic complete response, overall survival, metastasis-free survival, local recurrence, R0 resection, tumor regression grade, overall complete response, locoregional failure, postoperative complications, safety Doublet-LC TNT improved DFS versus conventional nCRT, with higher MFS and pCR rates and manageable toxicity. At median follow-up 51 months, 3-year DFS was 74.8% vs 66.0% (HR 0.674, 95% CI 0.489-0.929; P=.016). Secondary results are descriptive: 3-year MFS 77.7% vs 67.6% (HR 0.655); pCR among resected patients 26.37% vs 9.80%; 3-year OS 90.2% vs 87.5% (HR 0.727, 95% CI 0.462-1.143; P=.167); locoregional failure 6.03% vs 6.19%. Long-term outcomes remain immature with limited DFS events; patients were younger than 70 years, and the nCRT control reflects an earlier treatment paradigm. Grade ≥3 AEs during neoadjuvant therapy were 27.59% vs 8.56% but comparable across the whole course (28.02% vs 24.32%). Treatment-related deaths: 1 from rectal bleeding during chemoradiotherapy with TNT; two from febrile neutropenia during adjuvant chemotherapy with nCRT.

records.title: Habr-Gama et al. (USP)
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Organ preservation & watch-and-wait · Observational cohort study · 2004
records.body:
Distal rectal adenocarcinoma 0–7 cm from anal verge, considered resectable; neoadjuvant 5-FU/leucovorin CRT (5040 cGy); stage 0 after CRT: complete clinical response at 8 weeks (no residual ulcer or positive biopsy) or incomplete clinical response with pT0N0M0 after radical surgery; synchronous distant metastasis excluded Neoadjuvant CRT (5040 cGy at 180 cGy/d, 5 days/week for 6 weeks, with IV 5-FU 425 mg/m²/d + folinic acid 20 mg/m²/d on the first and last 3 days of RT) → reassessment at 8 weeks: complete clinical response → observation alone (strict follow-up; radical surgery on recurrence) vs incomplete clinical response → radical surgery with TME (APR or LAR ± coloanal anastomosis with loop ileostomy), pT0N0M0; no adjuvant chemotherapy in either group Overall survival, disease-free survival, recurrence (endorectal, pelvic, systemic), post-treatment tumour size, stoma construction, operative morbidity and mortality Observation after complete clinical response was associated with survival no worse than resection of pT0N0M0 disease, which mostly required a stoma
・5-yr OS: 100% vs 88%; P=0.01 (non-randomised groups)
・5-yr DFS: 92% vs 83%; P=0.09
・10-yr OS/DFS: observation 100% and 86%; all stage 0 97.7% and 84%
・Recurrence: systemic 3 per group; endorectal 2 in observation, both salvaged; no pelvic recurrence; cancer deaths 0 vs 2
・Limitations: non-randomised, response-defined groups; small resection group; mean follow-up 57.3 vs 48 mo
・Toxicity: CRT toxicity not reported; resection: stoma in 16 (72.7%), 9 definitive colostomies; no perioperative mortality; 2 parastomal hernias reoperated

records.title: IWWD
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Organ preservation & watch-and-wait · Registry study · 2018
records.body:
Rectal cancer with clinical complete response after neoadjuvant therapy (no signs of residual tumour at reassessment by DRE, endoscopy and imaging per local policy); TME surgery omitted, managed by watch and wait; diagnostic local excision to confirm cCR allowed; excluded clinical near-complete response, refusal of surgery or inoperability without cCR, and distant metastasis at baseline (single-arm) Watch and wait (TME surgery omitted) after neoadjuvant therapy, most commonly chemoradiotherapy (45–60 Gy schedules) with capecitabine or 5-fluorouracil; restaging and follow-up per local protocol Primary: cumulative incidence of local regrowth. Secondary: incidence of distant metastasis, overall survival, disease-specific survival, salvage resection after local regrowth In clinical complete responders managed by watch and wait, local regrowth occurred mostly within 2 years, in the bowel wall; locally unsalvageable disease was rare
・2-yr local regrowth: 25.2%; 88% of regrowths within 2 years; 97% in bowel wall
・Distant metastasis: 3-yr rate 8.1%; 18% with local regrowth vs 5% with sustained cCR
・5-yr OS: 84.7% overall; 87.9% sustained cCR; 75.4% local regrowth
・5-yr DSS: 93.8% overall; 97.3% sustained cCR; 84.0% local regrowth
・Salvage: TME resection in 78% of documented regrowths; R0 in 88%; locally unsalvageable disease estimated at 1% at most
・Limitations: registry without surgical comparator; cCR criteria and protocols varied by centre; high-volume centres, possible selection bias
・Toxicity: not reported

records.title: OPRA
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Organ preservation & watch-and-wait · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2022
records.body:
Biopsy-proven rectal adenocarcinoma; locally advanced, previously untreated, for total neoadjuvant therapy; clinical stage II (T3-4, N0) or stage III (any T, N1-2) staged with rectal MRI, full colonoscopy and CT chest/abdomen/pelvis; excluded recurrent rectal cancer, distant metastasis at diagnosis or prior pelvic irradiation INCT-CRT: induction mFOLFOX6 ×8 (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² IV, leucovorin 400 mg/m² IV, FU 400 mg/m² IV push, FU 2,400 mg/m² over 46-48 h; 14-day cycle) or CAPEOX ×5 (oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² day 1, capecitabine 1,000 mg/m² twice daily days 1-14; 21-day cycle) → CRT (4,500 cGy in 25 fractions to pelvic nodes, 5,000-5,600 cGy to tumour/involved nodes, with capecitabine 825 mg/m² twice daily or continuous-infusion FU 225 mg/m²/d) vs CRT-CNCT: same CRT → consolidation mFOLFOX6 ×8 or CAPEOX ×5; both → restaging: TME for incomplete response, watch-and-wait for complete/near-complete response with TME on regrowth Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: TME-free survival (organ preservation), adverse events, local recurrence, distant recurrence, overall survival, bowel function, urinary function, sexual function, quality of life, time to tumour regrowth Neither TNT sequence improved 3-yr DFS over the historical 75%; CRT-CNCT was associated with higher organ preservation than INCT-CRT
・3-yr DFS: 76% (95% CI 69–84) vs 76% (95% CI 69–83); primary endpoint (improvement over historical controls) not met
・3-yr TME-free survival: 41% (95% CI 33–50) vs 53% (95% CI 45–62); P = .01
・Regrowth on watch-and-wait: 40% vs 27%; log-rank P = .03
・LRFS/DMFS: local recurrence-free survival 94% vs 94%; distant metastasis-free survival 84% vs 82%; OS no difference
・Delayed TME: DFS similar after TME at restaging vs TME after regrowth
・Limitations: arms compared with historical controls, not randomised against standard therapy; between-arm tests additional; open-label; median follow-up 3 yr, OS immature
・Toxicity: grade ≥3 AEs during TNT 41% vs 34%; six deaths during TNT, three per arm, five from treatment-related toxicity

records.title: PROSPECT
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Selective omission of radiation · Randomised clinical trial (phase II/III) · 2023
records.body:
Previously untreated, pathologically confirmed locally advanced rectal adenocarcinoma; neoadjuvant setting, surgeon considering neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy then sphincter-sparing surgery appropriate; clinical stage T2N+, T3N0 or T3N+ (AJCC 7th); excluded T4, ≥4 pelvic nodes with short axis >10 mm, tumour within 3 mm of radial margin on baseline imaging, prior pelvic radiation or chemotherapy within 5 years Neoadjuvant modified FOLFOX6 IV every 2 weeks × 6 cycles → restaging → surgery; chemoradiotherapy (as in control arm) before surgery only if primary tumour decreased <20% or <5 FOLFOX cycles completed; postoperative chemoradiotherapy recommended if not R0; adjuvant FOLFOX × 6 suggested vs pelvic radiotherapy 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions with continuous-infusion fluorouracil 225 mg/m²/day or oral capecitabine 825 mg/m² twice daily, 5 days/week on radiation days → surgery; adjuvant FOLFOX × 8 suggested Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, local recurrence, R0 resection, pathological complete response, toxic effects Neoadjuvant FOLFOX with selective chemoradiotherapy was non-inferior to chemoradiotherapy for disease-free survival in rectal cancer eligible for sphincter-sparing surgery
・DFS: 5-yr 80.8% vs 78.6%; HR 0.92 (90.2% CI 0.74–1.14); non-inferiority P=0.005
・OS: 5-yr 89.5% vs 90.2%; HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.74–1.44)
・Local recurrence: 5-yr 1.8% vs 1.6%; HR 1.18 (95% CI 0.44–3.16)
・pCR: 21.9% vs 24.3% among resected patients
・RT avoidance: 89.6% of FOLFOX-assigned patients avoided chemoradiotherapy
・Limitations: open-label; excluded T4, ≥4 enlarged nodes, threatened radial margin; secondary endpoints not adjusted for multiplicity
・Toxicity: neoadjuvant G≥3 41.0% vs 22.8% (FOLFOX neutropenia 20.3%); postoperative G≥3 25.6% vs 32.6%

records.title: CONVERT
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Selective omission of radiation · Randomised, open-label, non-inferiority clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body:
Locally advanced rectal cancer (cT2N1 or cT3-4aNany) with uninvolved mesorectal fascia, no previous treatment; tumor distal edge 5 to 12 cm from anal verge, amended April 2019 to include tumors within 5 cm; excluded cT4b, tumor adjacent to MRF, symptomatic bowel obstruction, prior pelvic radiation, chemotherapy or invasive malignancy within 5 years Ⓐ Neoadjuvant CAPOX 4 cycles: oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1 + capecitabine 1000 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1-14, every 3 weeks → TME → adjuvant CAPOX 4 cycles
Ⓑ Capecitabine 825 mg/m² orally twice daily with concurrent radiotherapy 50 Gy in 25 fractions to gross tumor volume and 45 Gy in 25 fractions to clinical target volume, 5 days/week for 5 weeks → TME → adjuvant CAPOX 6 cycles
・Surgery: TME 2-4 weeks after chemotherapy in Ⓐ, 6-10 weeks after chemoradiotherapy in Ⓑ
・Design: Open-label, non-inferiority Primary: 3-year local-regional failure-free survival. Secondary: 3-year disease-free survival, pathologic complete response rate, tumor regression grade, pelvic R0 resection rate, overall survival, AE profiles, compliance, rate of receiving preoperative or postoperative chemoradiation, downstaging (ypStage 0 to 1), perioperative distant metastases, sphincter preservation, preventive ileostomy, postoperative morbidity Neoadjuvant CAPOX did not confirm non-inferiority for 3-year LRRFS, but showed comparable 3-year DFS and OS and fewer long-term grade 2-4 AEs vs chemoradiation
・3-yr LRRFS (final results, median follow-up 48 mo): Ⓐ 96.3% vs Ⓑ 97.4%; HR 1.40 (95% CI 0.53 to 3.68); non-inferiority not confirmed (upper CI exceeds margin 1.6)
・3-yr DFS: Ⓐ 89.2% vs Ⓑ 87.9%; HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.54 to 1.44)
・3-yr OS: Ⓐ 95.0% vs Ⓑ 94.1%; HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.42 to 1.76)
・pCR: Ⓐ 11·0% vs Ⓑ 13·8%; RR 1.140 (95% CI 0.8863-1.541)
・Downstaging (ypStage 0 to 1): Ⓐ 40·8% vs Ⓑ 45·6%; RR 1.101 (95% CI 0.9305-1.310)
・TRG 0-1: Ⓐ 23·2% vs Ⓑ 36·8%; P < 0·001
・Perioperative distant metastases: Ⓐ 0·7% vs Ⓑ 3·1%; P = 0·03
・R0 resection: Ⓐ 99·6% vs Ⓑ 99·6%; sphincter preservation 94·9% vs 94·3%
・Diverting ileostomy: Ⓐ 52·2% vs Ⓑ 63·6% (P = 0·008); postoperative morbidity 18·8% vs 25·7% (P = 0·05)
・Subgroups: Tumors within 5 cm of anal verge showed similar short-term outcomes; nCT alone less effective for cCR in very low rectal cancer
・Subgroups (final): Tumors <5 cm on nCT had higher LRRFS risk (HR 3.60, P = .063, NS); cT2N1/cT3N0-1 and cT4a/cN2 subsets similar 3-yr LRRFS, DFS, OS (post hoc)
・Toxicity: Short-term G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 15.3% vs Ⓑ 13.1% (NS); neutropenia lower with Ⓐ (39.3% vs 48.1%), thrombocytopenia higher (28.7% vs 20.1%)
・Long-term toxicity: G2-4 AEs Ⓐ 16.0% vs Ⓑ 26.3% (P = .002); proctitis Ⓐ 33.6% vs Ⓑ 41.7% (P = .049); radiodermatitis Ⓑ 12.5% at 1 year
・Neoadjuvant toxicity (initial report): G3-4 Ⓐ 12·3% vs Ⓑ 8·3%; 2 neoadjuvant deaths in Ⓐ, 1 postoperative death in Ⓑ
・Limitations: Open-label; 11% excluded from mITT; cT4b and MRF-involved tumors not included

records.title: FOWARC
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Selective omission of radiation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body:
Rectal adenocarcinoma, clinically stage II (T3-4N0) or stage III (T1-4N1-2; positive node 1.0 cm or larger on imaging); distal border <12 cm from anal verge; neoadjuvant treatment before curative resection; ages 18-75 years; excluded metastatic disease, prior radiotherapy or chemotherapy, other cancers, clinically significant cardiac disease, known peripheral neuropathy Ⓐ Fluorouracil plus radiotherapy: five cycles of leucovorin 400 mg/m² IV plus fluorouracil 400 mg/m² IV plus fluorouracil 2.4 g/m² by 48-hour infusion, with radiotherapy 46.0 to 50.4 Gy in 23 to 25 fractions during cycles 2 to 4 → surgery → seven cycles of fluorouracil
Ⓑ mFOLFOX6 plus radiotherapy: Ⓐ regimen plus oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² IV on day 1 of each cycle
Ⓒ mFOLFOX6 without radiotherapy: four to six cycles → surgery → six to eight cycles, with radiation before or after surgery at physicians' discretion
・Surgery: Total mesorectal excision, followed by postoperative chemotherapy in keeping with neoadjuvant treatment
・Design: Open-label Primary: 3-year disease-free survival. Secondary: locoregional recurrence, overall survival, relapse-free survival, quality of life, anal function Neither mFOLFOX6 plus radiotherapy (Ⓑ) nor mFOLFOX6 alone (Ⓒ) improved 3-year DFS, locoregional recurrence or OS versus fluorouracil plus radiotherapy (Ⓐ); 10-year results similar
・3-yr DFS: Ⓐ 72.9% vs Ⓑ 77.2% vs Ⓒ 73.5%; HR Ⓑ 0.838 (95% CI 0.547-1.284), Ⓒ 0.942 (0.626-1.418); median follow-up 45.2 mo
・DFS, 10-yr update (median follow-up 122.5 mo): Ⓐ 52.5% vs Ⓑ 62.6% vs Ⓒ 60.5%; HR Ⓑ 0.834 (0.584-1.190), Ⓒ 0.862 (0.606-1.226)
・Locoregional recurrence: 3-yr after R0/1 resection Ⓐ 8.0% vs Ⓑ 7.0% vs Ⓒ 8.3%; HR Ⓑ 0.806 (0.348-1.866), Ⓒ 0.952 (0.428-2.120)
・LR, 10-yr update: Ⓐ 10.8% vs Ⓑ 8.0% vs Ⓒ 9.6%; HR Ⓑ 0.668 (0.310-1.440), Ⓒ 0.911 (0.450-1.843)
・OS: 3-yr Ⓐ 91.3% vs Ⓑ 89.1% vs Ⓒ 90.7%; HR Ⓑ 1.106 (0.542-1.905), Ⓒ 1.057 (0.572-1.955)
・OS, 10-yr update: Ⓐ 65.9% vs Ⓑ 72.3% vs Ⓒ 73.4%; HR Ⓑ 0.930 (0.600-1.442), Ⓒ 0.903 (0.581-1.405)
・pCR (initial report): Ⓐ 14.0% vs Ⓑ 27.5% vs Ⓒ 6.5%
・Anal function: No-stoma subset, better without radiotherapy; Wexner >8 Ⓐ 41% vs Ⓑ 35.7% vs Ⓒ 18%; night incontinence Ⓐ 32.8% vs Ⓑ 27.1% vs Ⓒ 9.0%
・Prognostic: Perineural invasion independently predicted locoregional recurrence and DFS; ypTNM stage II-III and tumor deposits also predicted worse DFS
・Prognostic, 10-yr update: ypTNM stage predicted DFS, LR and OS; pCR 10-yr DFS 84.3%, LR 3.0%, OS 92.4%
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: Open-label, no stratification; ~10% protocol violations; 5-yr loss to follow-up 12.1%, 9.1%, 8.5%; not designed for noninferiority of Ⓒ vs Ⓐ

records.title: Cercek et al. (MSKCC)
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Immunotherapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2022
records.body:
Mismatch repair–deficient rectal adenocarcinoma; stage II or III, locally advanced, untreated, neoadjuvant setting; dMMR by chromogenic IHC loss of MMR protein expression; staged by protocol rectal MRI, CT and colonoscopy, no distant metastases, ECOG 0 or 1; excluded prior immunotherapy, chemotherapy or radiation for the rectal tumour, active autoimmune or infectious disease, immunosuppressive therapy within previous 7 days (single-arm) Dostarlimab 500 mg IV every 3 weeks for 6 months (nine cycles) → clinical complete response: nonoperative follow-up; otherwise standard chemoradiotherapy (5040 cGy in 28 fractions with concurrent capecitabine) → total mesorectal excision, with nonoperative follow-up for clinical complete response after chemoradiotherapy Primary: sustained clinical complete response 12 months after completion of dostarlimab or pathological complete response, overall response. Secondary: clinical complete response rate, progression or recurrence, FDG-PET response, adverse events, immune biomarkers Dostarlimab alone showed activity in dMMR locally advanced rectal cancer: clinical complete response in all 12 patients completing 6 months
・ORR: primary end point criteria for overall response met
・cCR: 100% after 6 months of dostarlimab; no chemoradiotherapy or surgery given
・Sustained 12-mo cCR: not yet reported; 4 patients with 1 year sustained cCR so far, of 13 needed
・Progression: none; no recurrence at median follow-up 12 mo (range 6 to 25); pCR not evaluable
・Limitations: single-arm, single-institution; small early report before full accrual of 30; durability immature
・Toxicity: no grade ≥3 AEs; any grade 75%; rash/dermatitis 31%, pruritus 25%, fatigue 25%; thyroid abnormality 6%

records.title: UNION
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Immunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Untreated cT3–4 or N+ rectal adenocarcinoma within ≤10 cm of the anal verge, planned for surgery after neoadjuvant therapy; aged 18–75 years, ECOG performance status 0 or 1; mismatch repair not restricted (93% pMMR); excluded active or previous autoimmune disease, congenital or acquired immunodeficiency, active hepatitis B or C Ⓐ Short-course radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions) → two 21-day cycles of camrelizumab 200 mg IV day 1 + CAPOX → surgery → six adjuvant CAPOX + camrelizumab cycles → camrelizumab monotherapy up to 17 cycles from neoadjuvant start
Ⓑ Long-course chemoradiotherapy (50.4 Gy in 28 fractions with concurrent capecitabine 825 mg/m² orally twice daily) → two CAPOX cycles → surgery → six adjuvant CAPOX cycles
・CAPOX: Capecitabine 1000 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1–14 + oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1
・Surgery: Total mesorectal excision within 10 weeks after radiotherapy; adjuvant therapy started 4–6 weeks after surgery
・Duration: Until disease progression or recurrence, unacceptable toxicity, or patient or investigator decision
・Design: Open-label, multicentre (nine hospitals in China) Primary: BIRC-assessed pathological complete response rate. Secondary: investigator-assessed event-free survival, overall survival, completion rate of neoadjuvant therapy, R0 resection rate, tumour regression grade, BIRC-assessed event-free survival, investigator-assessed disease-free survival, quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30), safety Short-course radiotherapy plus camrelizumab and CAPOX improved pathological complete response and 3-year event-free survival versus long-course chemoradiotherapy plus CAPOX
・pCR: Ⓐ 39.8% vs Ⓑ 15.3% (primary endpoint, previously reported)
・3-yr EFS (interim): Ⓐ 91.3% vs Ⓑ 77.4%; stratified HR 0.33 (95% CI 0.15–0.71); p=0.0029, boundary 0.0102 met
・3-yr EFS, BIRC: Ⓐ 87.2% vs Ⓑ 73.7%; stratified HR 0.41 (0.21–0.81)
・3-yr OS: Ⓐ 96.3% vs Ⓑ 89.8%; stratified HR 0.35 (0.11–1.10); no formal hypothesis testing
・3-yr DFS (R0 resection): Ⓐ 92.6% vs Ⓑ 81.4%; stratified HR 0.33 (0.14–0.80)
・Subgroups: EFS point estimates favoured Ⓐ across PD-L1 CPS and TPS groups; exploratory, >30% PD-L1 data missing
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 TRAEs Ⓐ 51% vs Ⓑ 48%; TR serious AEs 19% vs 13%; one treatment-related death (Ⓐ) vs none (Ⓑ), chemotherapy-related septic shock
・Limitations: Open-label; interim analysis, OS immature; Chinese patients only, conventional perioperative comparator

records.title: ADORE
records.subtitle: Rectal Cancer · Adjuvant chemotherapy — after preoperative CRT · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2014
records.body:
Rectal adenocarcinoma <12 cm from anal verge or below peritoneal reflection; adjuvant setting after preoperative fluoropyrimidine-monotherapy chemoradiotherapy and total mesorectal excision; pathological stage II (ypT3–4N0) or III (ypTanyN1–2) with R0 resection, no prior chemotherapy apart from preoperative chemoradiotherapy; excluded R1/R2 resection (circumferential margin ≤1 mm counted as R1), non-fluoropyrimidine-alone chemoradiotherapy, prior peripheral neuropathy Adjuvant FOLFOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + leucovorin 200 mg/m² 2-h infusion, fluorouracil bolus 400 mg/m² day 1, then fluorouracil 2400 mg/m² continuous infusion over 46 h) every 2 weeks for eight cycles vs fluorouracil 380 mg/m² + leucovorin 20 mg/m² bolus days 1–5 every 4 weeks for four cycles; stopped on recurrence, unacceptable toxicity or refusal Primary: 3-year disease-free survival. Secondary: safety, patterns of recurrence, quality of life, overall survival Adjuvant FOLFOX improved DFS vs fluorouracil plus leucovorin after preoperative chemoradiotherapy and TME, sustained at 6 years; OS was not improved
・3-yr DFS: 71.6% vs 62.9%; HR 0.657 (95% CI 0.434–0.994)
・6-yr DFS (final, median follow-up 74.1 mo): 68.2% vs 56.8%; HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.43–0.93)
・6-yr OS (final): 78.1% vs 76.4%; HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.45–1.19); earlier 3-yr OS advantage not retained
・Subgroups (6-yr DFS, post hoc): ypStage III HR 0.59 (95% CI 0.38–0.92); ypStage II HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.30–1.36), not significant; interaction P = .86
・QoL: more than ten-point appetite-loss deterioration with FOLFOX at end of treatment; no difference in global health status
・Limitations: phase 2, one-sided 5% type I error; open-label, recurrence without central review; bolus FL active control (not observation), FU schedules differ between arms
・Toxicity: G≥3 neutropenia 36% vs 26%; any-grade sensory neuropathy 71% vs 5%; no G≥3 difference; no treatment-related deaths

records.title: RTOG 87-04/ECOG 1289
records.subtitle: Anal Cancer · Definitive chemoradiation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 1996
records.body:
Epidermoid carcinoma of the anal canal; definitive nonsurgical chemoradiation, any tumour or nodal stage (1978 UICC staging); measurable primary tumour, Karnofsky performance status ≥60, enlarged inguinal/pelvic nodes staged by fine-needle aspiration or excisional biopsy; distant metastases excluded Ⓐ Pelvic RT 45 Gy at 1.8 Gy/d in 5 weeks (boost to 50.4 Gy for N+ or residual disease) + 5-FU 1,000 mg/m²/d continuous IV infusion for 96 hours from days 1 and 29
Ⓑ Same RT + 5-FU + mitomycin 10 mg/m² IV bolus on day 1 of each 5-FU course (max 20 mg per cycle)
・Salvage: Positive biopsy 4 to 6 weeks after CR → salvage 9 Gy boost + 5-FU + cisplatin 100 mg/m² → APR if postsalvage biopsy positive Negative postinduction biopsy rate, positive salvage biopsy rate, locoregional control, time to colostomy, colostomy-free survival, disease-free survival, overall survival, toxicity Adding mitomycin to 5-FU chemoradiation improved colostomy-free and disease-free survival and lowered colostomy, without OS benefit, at greater toxicity
・Positive postinduction biopsy: Ⓐ 15% vs Ⓑ 7.7%; P = .135 (not significant)
・4-yr local failure: Ⓐ 34% vs Ⓑ 16%; P = .0008
・4-yr colostomy: Ⓐ 22% vs Ⓑ 9%; P = .002
・4-yr CFS: Ⓐ 59% vs Ⓑ 71%; P = .014
・4-yr DFS: Ⓐ 51% vs Ⓑ 73%; P = .0003
・4-yr OS: Ⓐ 67% vs Ⓑ 76%; P = .31 (not significant)
・Salvage CR: Negative postsalvage biopsy in 12 of 22 assessable (non-randomised)
・Subgroups: Colostomy benefit significant in T3/T4 (P = .019), not T1/T2 (P = .141)
・Toxicity: Grade 4 Ⓐ 7% vs Ⓑ 23% (P < .001); fatal Ⓐ 0.7% vs Ⓑ 2.7%, all from neutropenic sepsis
・Limitations: No designated primary endpoint; median follow-up 3.01 yr; salvage efficacy uncertain (small numbers)
