records.title: ACT II
records.subtitle: Anal Cancer · Definitive chemoradiation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2013
records.body:
Histologically confirmed invasive squamous-cell, basaloid or cloacogenic carcinoma of the anal canal or margin; non-metastatic, randomised before initial treatment for primary chemoradiation; no biomarker selection; GFR ≥50 mL/min, fit for trial treatment, T1N0 or clinician-judged unsuitable patients not randomised for maintenance; excluded prior complete local excision, prior pelvic radiotherapy, HIV-positive status or cardiac disease Ⓐ Radiotherapy 50.4 Gy in 28 daily fractions over 5.5 weeks (no planned gap) + fluorouracil 1000 mg/m² per day continuous IV days 1–4 and 29–32 + mitomycin 12 mg/m² IV bolus day 1 only (max 20 mg)
Ⓑ Radiotherapy 50.4 Gy in 28 daily fractions over 5.5 weeks (no planned gap) + fluorouracil 1000 mg/m² per day continuous IV days 1–4 and 29–32 + cisplatin 60 mg/m² IV days 1 and 29
・Second randomisation (factorial, both arms): ± maintenance fluorouracil 1000 mg/m² per day days 71–74 and 92–95 + cisplatin 60 mg/m² days 71 and 92 (2 courses, weeks 11 and 14)
・Design: Open-label Primary: complete response at 26 weeks, grade 3 or 4 acute toxic effects (mitomycin vs cisplatin), progression-free survival (maintenance vs no maintenance). Secondary: colostomy-free survival, in-field recurrence rate, cause-specific survival, overall survival, grade 3–4 adverse events during maintenance Concurrent cisplatin was not more effective than mitomycin for complete response, PFS or OS, with similar overall grade 3–4 toxicity
・CR at 26 wk: 90.5% vs 89.6%; difference –0.9% (95% CI –4.9 to 3.1)
・PFS: No significant difference between mitomycin and cisplatin; HR 0.95 (95% CI 0.75–1.19)
・OS: Cisplatin vs mitomycin HR 1.05 (95% CI 0.80–1.38)
・Maintenance vs none (other comparison): 3-yr PFS 74% vs 73%; HR 0.95 (95% CI 0.75–1.21); OS HR 1.07 (95% CI 0.81–1.41)
・cCR timing (post hoc): 52% at 11 wk, 71% at 18 wk, 78% at 26 wk; 72% of 11-wk non-responders reached cCR by 26 wk; no arm difference
・Outcome by 26-wk cCR (post hoc): 5-yr OS 87% vs 46%, crude HR 0.17 (95% CI 0.12–0.23); 5-yr PFS 80% vs 33%, HR 0.16 (0.12–0.21)
・Subgroups: No significant PFS differences by baseline subgroup; no interaction between factors (p=0.94)
・Toxicity: G3–4 71% vs 72%; haematological G3–4 26% vs 16%; skin 48% vs 47%; 8 treatment-related deaths overall
・Limitations: Open-label; MRI/PET staging not routine; no quality-of-life or late-toxicity data

records.title: RTOG 98-11
records.subtitle: Anal Cancer · Definitive chemoradiation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2008
records.body:
Anal canal carcinoma (squamous, basaloid or cloacogenic); localized disease, primary chemoradiation; T2–T4 (T2 2-5 cm, T3 >5 cm, T4 invading adjacent organs), any N (pelvic or inguinal), Karnofsky ≥60%; excluded T1 or M1, severe comorbidity including AIDS, or other major malignancy unless disease-free ≥5 years Ⓐ Fluorouracil 1000 mg/m²/d continuous infusion days 1-4 and 29-32 + mitomycin 10 mg/m² IV bolus days 1 and 29 (max 20 mg per course) with concurrent RT 45 Gy/25 fractions
Ⓑ Induction fluorouracil 1000 mg/m²/d days 1-4 and 29-32 + cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV days 1 and 29 → same chemotherapy days 57-60 and 85-88 (cisplatin days 57 and 85) with concurrent RT starting day 57
・Boost: Both arms boost 10-14 Gy to 55-59 Gy for T3, T4, N+ or residual T2 after 45 Gy Primary: 5-year disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, time to relapse, 2-year colostomy rate, nonhematologic grade 3 or 4 toxic effects, local-regional failure, distant metastases, cumulative colostomy rate, colostomy-free survival, acute and long-term toxicity Long-term update: Ⓐ fluorouracil/mitomycin chemoradiation improved DFS and OS vs Ⓑ induction plus concurrent fluorouracil/cisplatin chemoradiation
・DFS (long-term update): Ⓐ 67.8% vs Ⓑ 57.8%; HR 1.39 (95% CI 1.10–1.76); initial analysis not significant
・OS (long-term update): Ⓐ 78.3% vs Ⓑ 70.7%; HR 1.37 (95% CI 1.04–1.81); initial analysis not significant
・CFS: Ⓐ 71.9% vs Ⓑ 65.0% (5-yr, long-term update); HR 1.29 (95% CI 0.99–1.67); borderline (P=.05)
・Colostomy failure: Ⓐ 11.9% vs Ⓑ 17.3% (5-yr, long-term update); HR 1.48 (95% CI 0.98–2.23), trend only; initial 5-yr Ⓐ 10% vs Ⓑ 19%, significant
・Local-regional failure: Ⓐ 20% vs Ⓑ 26.4% (5-yr, long-term update); HR 1.33 (95% CI 0.97–1.83); not significant
・Distant metastasis: Ⓐ 13.1% vs Ⓑ 18.1% (5-yr, long-term update); HR 1.37 (95% CI 0.94–2.02); not significant
・Toxicity: Acute G3–4 hematologic Ⓐ 61.8% vs Ⓑ 42.0% (post hoc); acute nonhematologic G3–4 74% both arms; late G3–4 treatment-related Ⓐ 13.1% vs Ⓑ 10.7%, not significant
・Limitations: Open-label; tested a strategy (induction plus concurrent cisplatin), not concurrent agents alone; induction prolonged total treatment time (median Ⓐ 49 vs Ⓑ 101 days)

records.title: INT 0035
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant chemotherapy — fluoropyrimidine & oxaliplatin backbone · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 1990
records.body:
Resected colon adenocarcinoma; adjuvant setting after potentially curative en bloc resection with no gross or microscopic residual disease; Stage B2 (invasion at least to serosa or pericolonic fat) or Stage C (regional lymph node metastasis), randomized as separate studies; entry one to five weeks after surgery; rectal carcinoma and other cancer within five years excluded Ⓐ Levamisole 50 mg orally every eight hours for three days, repeated every two weeks for one year + fluorouracil 450 mg/m² rapid IV daily for five consecutive days (no earlier than 21 days after surgery), then weekly fluorouracil 450 mg/m² IV from twenty-eight days after the start of that course for 48 weeks
Ⓑ Observation Primary: overall survival. Secondary: time to recurrence, recurrence-free survival, site of initial recurrence, toxicity, second primary cancers, treatment compliance Levamisole plus fluorouracil reduced recurrence and death rate vs observation in resected Stage C colon cancer, sustained at final analysis
・OS (final, median follow-up 6.5 yr): Death rate reduced 33% (95% CI 16–47%); P = 0.0007; curves did not converge
・Recurrence (final): Rate reduced 40% (P < 0.0001); no convergence of recurrence-free curves
・Recurrence pattern: Reduced at all common distant sites; minimal effect on local or regional recurrence
・Post-recurrence survival: Ⓐ 11 vs Ⓑ 15 mo
・Other comparison (levamisole alone vs observation, Stage C, final): Recurrence reduced 2% (P = 0.86); death rate reduced 6% (P = 0.57)
・Subgroups: Stage B2 3½-yr recurrence-free 84% vs 77%; survival 85% vs 91%; immature, authors regard as inconclusive
・Toxicity: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomatitis, dermatitis, leukopenia, rarely severe; neurologic symptoms 18% incl. cerebellar ataxia; single drug-related death (leukopenic sepsis); 30% stopped early; liver test abnormalities 40%, reversible; no late side effects
・Limitations: Open-label, no placebo; no fluorouracil-alone arm; rectal cancer excluded

records.title: IMPACT (GIVIO SITAC-01, NCIC-CTG C-03, FFCD 8802)
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant chemotherapy — fluoropyrimidine & oxaliplatin backbone · Pooled analysis of randomised trials · 1995
records.body:
Resected colon carcinoma, Dukes' B or C; adjuvant therapy after radical surgery, randomised postoperatively; colon defined as >12 cm from anal margin (FFCD) or colon and proximal rectum covered by peritoneum (GIVIO, NCIC-CTG); age limit 75 years in one trial; intestinal obstruction allowed; rectal primaries excluded from this analysis Ⓐ Fluorouracil 370–400 mg/m² plus folinic acid 200 mg/m² (L-form 100 mg/m² in about 150 GIVIO patients) daily for 5 days, every 28 days for 6 cycles
Ⓑ Surgery alone (control) Primary: overall survival. Secondary: event-free survival, site of first event, treatment compliance, toxicity Adjuvant fluorouracil plus high-dose folinic acid for 6 months improved overall and event-free survival vs surgery alone in resected Dukes' B/C colon cancer
・3-yr OS: Ⓐ 83% vs Ⓑ 78%; mortality reduced 22% (95% CI 3–38)
・3-yr EFS: Ⓐ 71% vs Ⓑ 62%; events reduced 35% (95% CI 22–46)
・Subgroups: Stage-by-treatment interaction borderline for EFS, not OS; longer follow-up needed to judge stage B benefit
・Toxicity: Mainly gastrointestinal, varying by trial; grade 4 GI <3%; grade 4 neutropenia 14% (NCIC-CTG); 1 treatment-related death (septic shock)
・Limitations: Pooled analysis of 3 trials; median follow-up 40 vs 37 mo; stage C accrual stopped early, so 56% stage B

records.title: MOSAIC
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant chemotherapy — fluoropyrimidine & oxaliplatin backbone · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2004
records.body:
Histologically proven colon cancer (inferior tumour pole above peritoneal reflection, at least 15 cm from anal margin); adjuvant after complete resection of stage II (T3 or T4,N0,M0) or stage III (any T,N1 or N2,M0), treatment started within seven weeks of surgery; age 18 to 75 years, Karnofsky ≥60, CEA <10 ng/ml; no prior chemotherapy, immunotherapy or radiotherapy Ⓐ Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² 2-hour infusion day 1 + FL regimen
Ⓑ FL: leucovorin 200 mg/m² then fluorouracil 400 mg/m² bolus and 600 mg/m² 22-hour infusion on 2 consecutive days
・Duration: Every 14 days for 12 cycles (six months) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: safety, long-term adverse effects, overall survival Oxaliplatin added to FL improved 5-yr DFS and 6-yr OS after resection of stage II/III colon cancer; benefit driven by stage III, not significant in stage II or age 70–75
・3-yr DFS (primary analysis): Ⓐ 78.2% vs Ⓑ 72.9%; HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.65–0.91)
・5-yr DFS (final): Ⓐ 73.3% vs Ⓑ 67.4%; HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.68–0.93)
・6-yr OS (final): Ⓐ 78.5% vs Ⓑ 76.0%; HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.71–1.00)
・Subgroups: Stage III 6-yr OS Ⓐ 72.9% vs Ⓑ 68.7%, HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.65–0.97); stage II (post hoc) not significant, HR 1.00 (95% CI 0.70–1.41); high-risk stage II post-relapse OS worse with oxaliplatin, HR 1.61 (95% CI 1.06–2.46); age 70–75 (post hoc) not significant, DFS HR 0.93 (95% CI 0.64–1.35)
・Toxicity: G3–4 neutropenia Ⓐ 41.1% vs Ⓑ 4.7%; febrile neutropenia Ⓐ 1.8% vs Ⓑ 0.2%; G3 neuropathy Ⓐ 12.5% vs Ⓑ 0.2% on treatment; on-treatment deaths 0.5% each arm; second cancers Ⓐ 5.5% vs Ⓑ 6.1%; age 70–75 (post hoc) second cancers Ⓐ 11.0% vs Ⓑ 6.2%, second cancer deaths 9 vs 1
・Limitations: Open-label; sponsor-collected/analysed data (primary report); age 18–75 only

records.title: X-ACT
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant chemotherapy — fluoropyrimidine & oxaliplatin backbone · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2005
records.body:
Histologically confirmed stage III colon carcinoma; adjuvant treatment after resection, surgery within eight weeks before randomization; age 18 to 75 years, ECOG 0 or 1, at least five years' life expectancy; excluded metastatic disease (including tumour cells in ascites or microscopic residual disease) and prior cytotoxic chemotherapy Ⓐ Oral capecitabine 1250 mg per square meter twice daily on days 1 through 14 every 21 days for eight cycles (24 weeks)
Ⓑ Mayo Clinic bolus regimen: IV leucovorin 20 mg per square meter followed immediately by IV bolus fluorouracil 425 mg per square meter on days 1 through 5 every 28 days for six cycles (24 weeks) Primary: disease-free survival, grade 3 or 4 fluoropyrimidine toxic effects. Secondary: relapse-free survival, overall survival, safety, three-year disease-free survival, quality of life Ⓐ Capecitabine was at least equivalent to Ⓑ bolus fluorouracil/leucovorin for DFS and OS, with fewer severe toxic effects
・DFS (primary analysis, 3-yr): Ⓐ 64.2% vs Ⓑ 60.6%; not significant (P=0.12)
・DFS (final analysis, 6.9-yr follow-up): HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.77–1.01); at least equivalent (margin 1.20, P<0.0001); superiority not shown (P=0.068)
・5-yr DFS (final): Ⓐ 60.8% vs Ⓑ 56.7%
・RFS (final): HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.78–1.02); not significant (P=0.104)
・OS (final): HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.74–1.01); at least equivalent (margin 1.14, P<0.001); superiority not shown (P=0.060); 5-yr Ⓐ 71.4% vs Ⓑ 68.4%
・Adjusted (final, preplanned multivariate): DFS HR 0.849 (95% CI 0.739–0.976); OS HR 0.826 (95% CI 0.705–0.971); not primary
・QoL: Global health status similar in both arms; small increases from baseline at week 25
・Subgroups: ≥70 yr DFS HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.72–1.31), OS HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.65–1.26); no treatment-by-age interaction
・HFS (post hoc): DFS HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.60–1.15) with HFS vs 1.01 (95% CI 0.85–1.21) without; hypothesis-generating
・Toxicity: G3/4 HFS Ⓐ 17% vs Ⓑ <1%; neutropenia Ⓐ 2% vs Ⓑ 26%; stomatitis Ⓐ 2% vs Ⓑ 14%; hyperbilirubinemia Ⓐ 20% vs Ⓑ 6%; treatment delays Ⓐ 46% vs Ⓑ 29%
・Limitations: Open-label; comparator bolus fluorouracil/leucovorin, not oxaliplatin-based therapy; HFS–efficacy link post hoc

records.title: NSABP C-07
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant chemotherapy — fluoropyrimidine & oxaliplatin backbone · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2007
records.body:
Colon cancer with distal tumour end >12 cm from anal verge; stage II (T3-4, N0, M0) or III (T1-4, N1-2, M0) after potentially curative resection, adjuvant; no residual disease, randomised within 42 days of surgery; excluded grade 2 or higher peripheral neuropathy, history of colon or other invasive cancer Ⓐ Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² IV days 1, 15 and 29 + FULV, each 8-week cycle, 3 cycles (6 months)
Ⓑ FU 500 mg/m² IV bolus + LV 500 mg/m² IV weekly for 6 weeks of each 8-week cycle, 3 cycles (24 weeks) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: relapse-free interval, overall survival, toxicity, oxaliplatin-specific neurotoxicity Adding oxaliplatin to weekly bolus FULV improved DFS in resected stage II–III colon cancer; OS not significantly improved at 8-yr follow-up
・DFS (8-yr median follow-up): 5-yr Ⓐ 69.4% vs Ⓑ 64.2%; HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.72–0.93)
・RFI: 4-yr Ⓐ 78.1% vs Ⓑ 72.9%; HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.67–0.95)
・OS (8-yr median follow-up): 5-yr Ⓐ 80.2% vs Ⓑ 78.4%; HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.75–1.02); not significant
・Subgroups (unplanned, exploratory): OS age interaction P=.039; <70 yr HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.68–0.95); ≥70 yr HR 1.18 (95% CI 0.86–1.62); no stage interaction (P=.38)
・Toxicity: G3 neurosensory Ⓐ 8.2% vs Ⓑ 0.7%; G3–4 diarrhoea Ⓐ 38% vs Ⓑ 32%; bowel-wall-injury hospitalisation Ⓐ 5.5% vs Ⓑ 3.0%; enteropathy deaths Ⓐ 0.4% vs Ⓑ 0.08%; age ≥70: G4–5 Ⓐ 19.3% vs Ⓑ 13.0%, G5 Ⓐ 3.6% vs Ⓑ 1.4%
・Limitations: Age/stage subset analyses unplanned and underpowered; trial not powered for subsets

records.title: QUASAR
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant chemotherapy — fluoropyrimidine & oxaliplatin backbone · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2007
records.body:
Colon or rectal cancer after apparently complete (curative) resection, no distant metastases; adjuvant setting, mostly stage II (node negative); clinician-judged uncertain indication for adjuvant chemotherapy; no definite contraindication to chemotherapy; no prior chemotherapy other than a 1 week postoperative portal vein fluorouracil infusion Ⓐ Fluorouracil 370 mg/m² IV + folinic acid (low-dose 25 mg or high-dose 175 mg IV), 30 doses given as six 5-day courses every 4 weeks or as 30 once-weekly courses; until October 1997 also randomised to levamisole 50 mg three times daily for 3 days every 2 weeks for 12 courses or placebo; after October 1997 low-dose folinic acid only
Ⓑ Observation (chemotherapy considered on recurrence) Primary: all-cause mortality. Secondary: death from colorectal cancer, recurrence, quality of life, toxicity, cost-effectiveness Adjuvant fluorouracil plus folinic acid could improve survival in stage II colorectal cancer, though absolute benefit is small
・Death: Ⓐ vs Ⓑ; RR 0.82 (95% CI 0.70–0.95); median follow-up 5.5 yr
・Absolute benefit: 3.6% (95% CI 1.0–6.0), assuming 20% 5-yr mortality without chemotherapy
・Recurrence: Ⓐ vs Ⓑ; RR 0.78 (95% CI 0.67–0.91); benefit confined to first 2 yr (RR 0.64), none thereafter
・CRC death: Ⓐ vs Ⓑ; RR 0.81 (95% CI 0.68–0.96)
・Subgroups: Stage II death RR 0.84 (95% CI 0.68–1.00; p=0.046), borderline significant; no significant difference by site, stage, sex, age or schedule; recurrence not reduced in patients aged over 70
・Toxicity: Non-colorectal deaths within 30 wk: Ⓐ 8 (0.5%) vs Ⓑ 4 (0.25%), one possibly chemotherapy-related; grade 3/4 toxicity 31% with 4-week courses vs 10% with weekly courses
・Limitations: Pathology data available for only 20% of patients, precluding a high- vs low-risk stage II comparison

records.title: NO16968 (XELOXA)
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant chemotherapy — fluoropyrimidine & oxaliplatin backbone · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2011
records.body:
Histologically confirmed stage III colon carcinoma (T1-4/N1-2/M0), tumour ≥15 cm from anal verge or above peritoneal reflection; adjuvant therapy after curative-intent surgery ≤8 weeks before randomization with full recovery; excluded prior chemotherapy, radiotherapy or immunotherapy for colon cancer, known peripheral neuropathy, clinically significant cardiac disease or CNS disorders; stage II not included Ⓐ Oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1 + oral capecitabine 1,000 mg/m² twice daily days 1 to 14, every 3 weeks for 8 cycles (24 weeks)
Ⓑ Bolus FU/FA, one regimen prespecified per centre: Mayo Clinic (24 weeks; 6 cycles) or Roswell Park (32 weeks, 4 cycles) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, relapse-free survival, safety, tumour DPD, TP and TS expression XELOX improved DFS and, at final analysis, OS versus bolus FU/FA in stage III colon cancer
・DFS: Ⓐ 63% vs Ⓑ 56% (7-yr); HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.69–0.93); median follow-up 74 mo
・RFS: Favoured Ⓐ; HR 0.78
・OS (final): Ⓐ 73% vs Ⓑ 67% (7-yr; median follow-up 83 mo); HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.70–0.99)
・OS (primary analysis): Non-significant; HR 0.87; final P values descriptive only
・Subgroups: Low tumour DPD expression associated with better outcomes with Ⓐ only (exploratory)
・Toxicity: Grade 3/4 AEs Ⓐ 55% vs Ⓑ 47%; grade 3/4 neurosensory toxicity Ⓐ 11% (persistent in 5%); grade 3/4 neutropenia Ⓐ 9% vs Ⓑ 16%; grade 3 hand-foot syndrome and grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia Ⓐ 5% each; 60-day mortality 1% both arms; toxic deaths Ⓐ 7 vs Ⓑ 6 (final cut)
・Limitations: Bolus FU/FA comparator pre-dates oxaliplatin-based standard of care; stage II disease not studied

records.title: ACCENT pooled analysis (Sargent et al.)
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant chemotherapy — fluoropyrimidine & oxaliplatin backbone · Pooled analysis · 2001
records.body:
Stage II/III colon cancer; adjuvant therapy; individual patient data from seven phase III ACCENT trials (accrual 1997-2004) comparing IV FU and LV with oxaliplatin- or irinotecan-based combinations or oral fluoropyrimidines; age analysed as <70 vs ≥70 years; MOSAIC and PETACC-3 restricted eligibility at age 75 years Ⓐ Oxaliplatin-based (FOLFOX4 in MOSAIC, FLOX in NSABP-C07, XELOX in XELOXA)
Ⓑ Irinotecan-based (IFL in CALGB-89803, FOLFIRI in PETACC-3)
Ⓒ Oral fluoropyrimidine (uracil/tegafur in NSABP-C06, capecitabine in X-ACT)
Ⓓ IV FU and LV Disease-free survival, overall survival, time to recurrence, age-by-treatment interaction, death within 6 months of therapy initiation In patients ≥70 yr, adding oxaliplatin showed reduced benefit without significant age interaction, whereas oral fluoropyrimidines retained efficacy across age groups
・DFS (≥70 yr): Ⓐ vs Ⓓ HR 0.94 (95% CI 0.78-1.13); P interaction .09
・OS (≥70 yr): Ⓐ vs Ⓓ HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.85-1.27); P interaction .05
・TTR (≥70 yr): P interaction .36
・Exploratory censoring: Short-term DFS benefit of Ⓐ in ≥70 yr lost by 3 yr
・Age interaction (all 7 trials): Significant (P .001 DFS, .004 OS, .002 TTR); DFS HR 1.05 (95% CI 0.94-1.19) at ≥70 yr
・Irinotecan (Ⓑ vs Ⓓ): Older patients did not benefit from adding irinotecan
・Oral fluoropyrimidine (Ⓒ vs Ⓓ): Nonsignificant age interaction; noninferiority supported in both age groups
・Toxicity: Not reported; 6-mo mortality higher in ≥70 vs <70 yr (2.80% vs 0.85%)

records.title: NSABP C-08
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant targeted therapy — negative trials · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2011
records.body:
Stage II–III colon adenocarcinoma after surgical removal of the primary tumour; adjuvant therapy; ECOG 0–1, randomized within 21–50 days after surgery; excluded any history of cerebral vascular accident, transient ischemic attack, symptomatic peripheral vascular disease, or arterial thrombotic episode (eg myocardial infarction) within the 12 months before randomization Ⓐ mFOLFOX6 (leucovorin 400 mg/m² IV d1, FU 400 mg/m² IV bolus d1 then 2,400 mg/m² IV infusion, oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² IV d1) every 2 weeks for 12 doses (6 months)
Ⓑ Same mFOLFOX6 for 6 months plus bevacizumab 5 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks for 26 doses (1 year), starting concurrently with chemotherapy Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: survival, toxicity related to study therapy, recurrence, second primary cancer, survival after recurrence Adding bevacizumab to mFOLFOX6 did not significantly prolong DFS in stage II–III colon cancer
・DFS: HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.76 to 1.04; P = .15); 3-yr DFS Ⓑ 77.4% vs Ⓐ 75.5%; median follow-up 35.6 mo
・15-mo landmark (exploratory): Ⓑ reduced DFS events before landmark (HR 0.61; 95% CI 0.48 to 0.78) but not after (HR 1.22; 95% CI 0.98 to 1.52; P = .076)
・Toxicity: Ⓑ did not increase mortality; grade ≥3 hypertension, wound complications, pain and proteinuria significantly more frequent with Ⓑ

records.title: AVANT
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant targeted therapy — negative trials · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2012
records.body:
Histologically confirmed colon carcinoma; adjuvant setting after curative-intent surgery 4–8 weeks before randomisation; stage III or high-risk stage II (AJCC/UICC), with efficacy analysed in stage III only; excluded remaining tumour, postoperative CEA >1·5 times the upper normal limit, previous antiangiogenic treatment Ⓐ FOLFOX4 (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² IV, leucovorin 200 mg/m², fluorouracil 400 mg/m² bolus then 600 mg/m² 22-h infusion day 1; leucovorin 200 mg/m², fluorouracil 400 mg/m² bolus then 600 mg/m² 22-h infusion day 2) every 2 weeks for 12 cycles (24 weeks) → 24 weeks of observation
Ⓑ Bevacizumab 5 mg/kg IV day 1 + FOLFOX4 every 2 weeks for 12 cycles (24 weeks) → bevacizumab 7·5 mg/kg day 1 every 3 weeks for a further 24 weeks (eight cycles)
Ⓒ Bevacizumab 7·5 mg/kg IV + XELOX (oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1; capecitabine 1000 mg/m² orally twice daily, day 1 evening to day 15 morning) every 3 weeks for eight cycles (24 weeks) → bevacizumab 7·5 mg/kg every 3 weeks for a further 24 weeks (eight cycles) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: 3-year DFS rate, overall survival, survival after recurrence or new occurrence, cumulative DFS hazard ratios over time, site of tumour recurrence, safety Adding bevacizumab to adjuvant FOLFOX4 or XELOX did not prolong DFS in resected stage III colon cancer
・DFS: HR Ⓑ vs Ⓐ 1·17 (95% CI 0·98–1·39); Ⓒ vs Ⓐ 1·07 (0·90–1·28); global DFS test not rejected (p=0·2024); median 48-mo follow-up
・3-yr DFS: Ⓐ 76% vs Ⓑ 73% vs Ⓒ 75%
・OS (exploratory, ≥60-mo follow-up): HR Ⓑ vs Ⓐ 1·27 (1·03–1·57); Ⓒ vs Ⓐ 1·15 (0·93–1·42); suggests potential harm
・DFS at 1 yr (exploratory): Cumulative HR Ⓑ vs Ⓐ 0·63; Ⓒ vs Ⓐ 0·61; early advantage reversed thereafter
・Toxicity: Serious AEs Ⓐ 20% vs Ⓑ 26% vs Ⓒ 25%; G3–5 hypertension Ⓐ 1% vs Ⓑ 11% vs Ⓒ 10%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 1 vs Ⓑ 2 vs Ⓒ 5

records.title: NCCTG N0147
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant targeted therapy — negative trials · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2012
records.body:
Completely resected, histologically proven stage III (any TN1-2M0) colon adenocarcinoma at least 12 cm from the anal verge; adjuvant therapy after resection; KRAS centrally determined, primary analysis in wild-type KRAS, with randomization restricted to centrally confirmed wild-type KRAS from August 2008; at least 1 pathologically confirmed involved lymph node, en bloc resection for locally advanced tumours, ECOG 0-2; no prior chemotherapy, immunotherapy or radiotherapy for colon cancer Ⓐ mFOLFOX6 (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² day 1, leucovorin 400 mg/m² and fluorouracil 400 mg/m² bolus, then IV fluorouracil 2400 mg/m² over 46 hours days 1-2)
Ⓑ mFOLFOX6 + cetuximab 400 mg/m² day 1 of cycle 1, then 250 mg/m² day 8 of cycle 1 and days 1 and 8 of cycles 2-12
・Schedule: Every 2 weeks for 12 cycles, starting within 10 weeks of surgery Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: time to recurrence, overall survival, toxicity, dose intensity, completion of 12 cycles Adding cetuximab to adjuvant mFOLFOX6 did not improve DFS in resected stage III colon cancer
・DFS (wild-type KRAS): Ⓐ 74.6% vs Ⓑ 71.5% at 3 yr; HR 1.21 (95% CI 0.98-1.49; P=.08)
・DFS (mutated KRAS): Ⓐ 67.1% vs Ⓑ 65.0% at 3 yr; HR 1.12 (95% CI 0.86-1.46)
・Subgroups: No subgroup benefited, including wild-type KRAS/BRAF (HR 1.22)
・Subgroups: OS worse with cetuximab in wild-type KRAS patients aged ≥70 (3-yr Ⓐ 86.2% vs Ⓑ 72.5%; HR 2.00)
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 52.3% vs Ⓑ 72.5%; failure to complete 12 cycles Ⓐ 23% vs Ⓑ 33%
・Toxicity: Death during treatment with Ⓑ: 4.2% in patients aged ≥70 vs 0.5% in younger patients
・Limitations: Accrual halted after second planned interim analysis (246/515 events)

records.title: PETACC-8
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant targeted therapy — negative trials · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2014
records.body:
Pathologically confirmed stage III colon adenocarcinoma; adjuvant therapy after curative (R0) resection 14–56 days before randomisation; KRAS exon 2 (codons 12 and 13) wild-type required after the June 17, 2008 amendment (2096 unselected patients randomised earlier); aged 18–75 years, WHO PS 0–1, CEA <1·5 times ULN after surgery; excluded prior chemotherapy or abdominal/pelvic irradiation, metastases, rectal cancer within 15 cm of the anal verge, grade ≥1 peripheral neuropathy Ⓐ FOLFOX4 (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² infusion day 1, leucovorin 200 mg/m² days 1 and 2, fluorouracil 400 mg/m² bolus then 600 mg/m² continuous infusion) plus weekly cetuximab 400 mg/m² first week then 250 mg/m² weekly, for 12 cycles
Ⓑ FOLFOX4 alone for 12 cycles
・Duration: Until completion, unacceptable toxicity, recurrence or consent withdrawal Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival (including 5-year and 7-year survival), treatment compliance, prognostic factors for relapse or treatment efficacy, predictive factors for relapse or treatment efficacy, safety Adding cetuximab to adjuvant FOLFOX4 did not improve DFS in KRAS exon 2 wild-type resected stage III colon cancer
・DFS: Interim analysis (median follow-up 3·3 yr); 3-yr DFS Ⓐ 75·1% vs Ⓑ 78·0%; HR 1·05 (95% CI 0·85–1·29; p=0·66)
・OS: Did not differ; HR 1·09 (95% CI 0·81–1·47)
・Subgroups: Exploratory; favoured Ⓑ in women and right-sided tumours, favoured Ⓐ in pT4/N2 disease; HR 0·56 (95% CI 0·35–0·89); numbers small
・Toxicity: G3/4 acne-like rash Ⓐ 27% vs Ⓑ <1%; grade 5 events possibly treatment-related Ⓐ 7 vs Ⓑ 3; toxicity discontinuation 12% each
・Limitations: Authors state trial cannot conclude on cetuximab's benefit; subgroup heterogeneity noted

records.title: IDEA Collaboration
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Duration of adjuvant therapy · Pooled analysis · 2018
records.body:
Stage III colon cancer; adjuvant oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy (FOLFOX or CAPOX); pooled from six randomized phase 3 trials, analysis limited to randomized patients who received at least one dose of trial drug; stage II and rectal cancer patients enrolled in some component trials excluded from this report Ⓐ 3 months of adjuvant FOLFOX or CAPOX
Ⓑ 6 months of adjuvant FOLFOX or CAPOX
・FOLFOX: FOLFOX4 or modified FOLFOX6; oxaliplatin 85 mg per square meter every 2 weeks with 46-hour fluorouracil infusion every 2 weeks
・CAPOX: Oxaliplatin 130 mg per square meter every 3 weeks with capecitabine 1000 mg per square meter twice daily for 2 of every 3 weeks
・Design: Regimen chosen by treating physician, not randomized; CALGB/SWOG trial restricted to FOLFOX Primary: 3-year disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, treatment adherence, adverse events 3 months of adjuvant chemotherapy failed to show noninferiority to 6 months for DFS or OS; 6 months improved DFS
・DFS: HR 1.08 (95% CI 1.02 to 1.15); Ⓑ superior (FDRadj p 0.044)
・OS: 5-yr OS Ⓐ 82.4% vs Ⓑ 82.8%; HR 1.02 (95% CI 0.95 to 1.11); NI FDRadj p 0.058
・Subgroups: CAPOX - NI of 3 months narrowly missed (DFS HR 0.98, p 0.027; OS HR 0.96, p 0.033)
・Subgroups: FOLFOX - 6 months improved DFS (HR 1.16; 95% CI 1.07 to 1.26; interaction P 0.011); OS HR 1.07 (95% CI 0.97 to 1.18)
・Subgroups: 6 months improved DFS in high-risk (T4 and/or N2) disease (HR 1.13; 95% CI 1.03 to 1.22); NI not shown for T1-3 N1 (interaction P 0.24)
・Toxicity: Grade ≥2 neurotoxicity Ⓐ vs Ⓑ: FOLFOX 16.6% vs 47.7%, CAPOX 14.2% vs 44.9%; 19 grade 5 events; AEs not updated
・Limitations: Regimen (FOLFOX vs CAPOX) not randomized, limiting interpretation of regimen-specific figures
records.keywords: Grothey et al. N Engl J Med 2018;378:1177-1188  29590544 André et al. Lancet Oncol 2020;21:1620-1629  33271092

records.title: ACHIEVE-2
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Duration of adjuvant therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body:
High-risk stage II colon cancer after potentially curative resection; adjuvant setting; high-risk factors: T4 disease, poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma, inadequate nodal harvest (<12 lymph nodes), lymphovascular invasion, or bowel obstruction or perforation; Asian patients treated in Japan Ⓐ 3 months of adjuvant oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy: mFOLFOX6 for 6 cycles or CAPOX for 4 cycles, regimen at physician discretion
Ⓑ 6 months of adjuvant oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy: mFOLFOX6 for 12 cycles or CAPOX for 8 cycles, regimen at physician discretion
・mFOLFOX6: Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², l-leucovorin 200 mg/m² and bolus fluorouracil 400 mg/m² day 1, then infusional fluorouracil 2400 mg/m² days 1–3, every 2 weeks
・CAPOX: Oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1 plus oral capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily days 1–15 (750 mg/m² if creatinine clearance 30–50 mL/min and/or age ≥70), every 3 weeks
・Duration: No further adjuvant chemotherapy after the study regimen Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, time-to-treatment failure, safety, treatment completion rate, dose intensity, association between clinical outcome and high-risk factors, incidence and longitudinal pattern of peripheral sensory neuropathy, incidence and longitudinal pattern of hand-foot syndrome, treatment discontinuation rate 3-month oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy showed similar 3-yr DFS to 6 months without a defined non-inferiority margin, and reduced grade ≥2 PSN
・DFS (3-yr): Ⓐ 88.2% vs Ⓑ 87.9%; HR 1.12 (95% CI 0.67–1.87)
・Subgroups: CAPOX Ⓐ 88.2% vs Ⓑ 88.4%; HR 1.13 (95% CI 0.65–1.96); mFOLFOX6 subgroup too small to assess
・Subgroups: T4 disease Ⓐ 76.2% vs Ⓑ 79.7%; HR 1.28 (95% CI 0.68–2.43), less favourable trend with 3 months
・Toxicity: Grade ≥2 PSN Ⓐ 16% vs Ⓑ 43%; grade ≥3 PSN Ⓐ 1% vs Ⓑ 7%; grade ≥2 HFS (CAPOX) Ⓐ 3% vs Ⓑ 15%; discontinuation Ⓐ 10% vs Ⓑ 31% (mFOLFOX6), Ⓐ 15% vs Ⓑ 35% (CAPOX); no treatment-related deaths
・Limitations: No non-inferiority margin or power defined, so non-inferiority could not be established; 3-month CAPOX suggestion rests on subgroup data

records.title: IDEA Collaboration (Stage II)
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Duration of adjuvant therapy · Pooled analysis · 2021
records.body:
High-risk stage II colon or rectal cancer (rectal cancer recruited only in SCOT); adjuvant oxaliplatin–fluoropyrimidine doublet; no biomarker selection (MSI data not available); high risk = one or more of T4, poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma, vascular/perilymphatic/perineural invasion, inadequate nodal harvest (<10 nodes in SCOT, <12 in TOSCA, HORG and ACHIEVE2), bowel obstruction or perforation; primary analysis excluded patients receiving no chemotherapy and SCOT rectal patients given preoperative short-course radiotherapy Ⓐ 3 months of adjuvant CAPOX or FOLFOX
Ⓑ 6 months of adjuvant CAPOX or FOLFOX
・Design: Regimen (CAPOX or FOLFOX) chosen by clinician and/or patient before randomization to duration, not randomized Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: adverse events, peripheral neuropathy, treatment intensity 3-month adjuvant oxaliplatin doublet did not show noninferiority to 6 months for 5-year DFS in high-risk stage II colon cancer
・DFS: Ⓐ 80.7% vs Ⓑ 83.9% (5-yr); HR 1.17 (80% CI 1.05 to 1.31), crossing noninferiority margin of 1.2
・Subgroups: Preplanned, non-randomized regimen subgroup: CAPOX HR 1.02 (80% CI 0.88 to 1.17) vs FOLFOX HR 1.41 (80% CI 1.18 to 1.68); interaction not significant after multiplicity adjustment
・Toxicity: Grade ≥II peripheral neuropathy Ⓐ 13% vs Ⓑ 36%; 6-month arm had significantly more adverse events
・Limitations: OS data immature; MSI data unavailable; only 130 patients had rectal cancer
records.keywords: Iveson et al. J Clin Oncol 2021;39:631-641  33439695

records.title: SCOT
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Duration of adjuvant therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body:
Colon or rectal adenocarcinoma, stage III or high-risk stage II (one or more of T4, preoperative obstruction/perforation, fewer than ten nodes harvested, poor differentiation, perineural or extramural venous/lymphatic invasion); adjuvant, within 11 weeks of curative resection; normal CT and CEA <1·2× ULN; rectal cancer required TME with margins >1 mm; excluded prior chemotherapy, long-course chemoradiotherapy (short-course radiotherapy allowed) and DPD deficiency Ⓐ 3 months of adjuvant oxaliplatin-fluoropyrimidine (CAPOX four cycles or FOLFOX six cycles)
Ⓑ 6 months of adjuvant oxaliplatin-fluoropyrimidine (CAPOX eight cycles or FOLFOX 12 cycles)
・CAPOX: Oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day one + oral capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily for the first 14 days, every 3 weeks
・FOLFOX: Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² IV day one with L-folinic acid 175 mg or folinic acid 350 mg, fluorouracil 400 mg/m² bolus then 2400 mg/m² over 46 h, every 2 weeks
・Design: Open-label; regimen (CAPOX or FOLFOX) chosen by physician and patient before randomisation, not randomised Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, safety, quality of life, cost-effectiveness, patient-reported peripheral neuropathy (FACT/GOG-Ntx4) 3 months of adjuvant oxaliplatin-fluoropyrimidine was non-inferior to 6 months for DFS, with reduced toxicity, in an underpowered trial
・DFS: Final analysis; 5-yr Ⓐ 72.9% vs Ⓑ 72.9%; HR 0.99 (95% CI 0.90–1.09)
・OS: Final analysis; 5-yr Ⓐ 82.4% vs Ⓑ 82.4%; HR 0.96 (95% CI 0.86–1.07); non-inferior
・QoL: Worse with Ⓑ (6 months) during months 4–6; no clinically important difference thereafter
・Subgroups: Post-hoc by regimen: non-inferior with CAPOX (DFS HR 0.944; OS HR 0.90) but not FOLFOX (DFS HR 1.158; OS HR 1.10); OS non-inferior in low-risk but not high-risk stage III (HR 0.87 vs 1.02); OS HR 0.74 in rectal cancer
・Toxicity: G≥2 neuropathy Ⓐ 25% vs Ⓑ 58%; G3–5 AEs Ⓐ 36% vs Ⓑ 59% (safety subset); patient-reported neuropathy persisted ≥5 yr; 16 treatment-related deaths in each arm
・Limitations: Open-label; regimen not randomised, confounding the by-regimen and site subgroup analyses; by actual treatment duration received, non-inferiority was not shown
records.keywords: Iveson et al. Lancet Oncol 2018;19:562-578  29611518 Iveson et al. J Clin Oncol 2026;44:534-539  41512219

records.title: FOxTROT
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Neoadjuvant chemotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body:
Biopsy-confirmed colon cancer; operable locally advanced disease, radiologically staged T3-4, N0-2, M0; no biomarker selection (RAS-wildtype tumours could also be randomised to panitumumab); CT-predicted T3-4 with extramural extension ≥5 mm (modified to ≥1 mm after the pilot phase), fit for both surgery and chemotherapy; bowel obstruction eligible only if first defunctioned with a stoma Ⓐ NAC: 6-wk preoperative oxaliplatin-fluoropyrimidine (OxFU: oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² plus l-folinic acid 175 mg, fluorouracil 400 mg/m² bolus then 2,400 mg/m² over 46 h, every 2 wk × 3 cycles; or OxCap, permitted only if not entering the panitumumab randomisation: oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1 plus oral capecitabine 1,000 mg/m² twice daily days 1-14, 3-weekly × 2 cycles) → surgery 4-6 wk after NAC → 18 wk postoperative chemotherapy (9 OxFU or 6 OxCap cycles)
Ⓑ Control: surgery as soon as possible → 24 wk postoperative chemotherapy (12 OxFU or 8 OxCap cycles)
・From 2014: Optional 12-wk total chemotherapy (6-wk NAC + 6-wk AC vs 12-wk AC) in lower-risk or older patients
・RAS-wildtype subrandomisation (NAC group only, from June 2011): Panitumumab 6 mg/kg before each of the first three OxFU cycles vs none Primary: residual disease or recurrence within 2 years. Secondary: surgical morbidity, histopathologic stage, regression grade, completeness of resection, cause-specific mortality, all-cause mortality, depth of extramural spread, chemotherapy toxicity Preoperative chemotherapy improved 2-year disease control and resection completeness versus postoperative-only chemotherapy, without increasing perioperative morbidity
・Recurrence/residual disease (2-yr): Ⓐ 16.9% vs Ⓑ 21.5%; RR 0.72 (95% CI 0.54 to 0.98), P = .037
・Panitumumab: Did not enhance the benefit of NAC (RAS-wildtype subrandomisation, no figures reported)
・R0 resection: Ⓐ 94% vs Ⓑ 89%
・Mortality: Colon cancer-specific RR 0.74; all-cause RR 0.76 (95% CI 0.55 to 1.06); not significant, trial underpowered for these outcomes
・Subgroups: dMMR tumours showed no apparent reduction in 2-yr recurrence (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.42 to 1.76); subgroup power limited
・Toxicity: Obstructive symptoms 4.3% (NAC only); pulmonary embolism/DVT 2.5% vs 0.6%; postoperative death 0.6% in each arm
records.keywords: Morton et al. J Clin Oncol 2023;41:1541-1552  36657089

records.title: NeoCol
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Neoadjuvant chemotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Histologically confirmed locally advanced colon cancer; non-metastatic, enrolled before surgery; no biomarker selection (MMR status collected post hoc); CT-staged cT3 with extramural tumour invasion ≥5 mm or cT4, ECOG performance status 0 to 2; distant metastases excluded Ⓐ Upfront surgery → adjuvant CAPOX or capecitabine monotherapy, up to 8 cycles, according to postoperative risk stratification and age
Ⓑ Neoadjuvant CAPOX for 3 cycles → surgery → up to 5 further cycles of CAPOX or capecitabine only if indicated by histopathological stage (no adjuvant therapy if criteria not met)
・CAPOX: Capecitabine 2000 mg/m² orally days 1-14 + oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1, every 3 weeks Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, rate of patients meeting criteria for adjuvant chemotherapy, toxicity, response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, quality of life, surgical and pathological outcomes, adjuvant chemotherapy use, adverse events, DFS and OS by MMR status and age, CT staging accuracy Neoadjuvant CAPOX did not improve DFS versus upfront surgery; feasible and surgically safe, but results are nonconfirmatory
・DFS: Ⓐ 87% vs Ⓑ 83% (3-yr); P = .36
・OS: Ⓐ 85% vs Ⓑ 87% (5-yr; P = .83); Ⓐ 75% vs Ⓑ 81% (10-yr; P = .36)
・Adjuvant eligibility: Ⓐ 73% vs Ⓑ 59% met criteria; P = .02
・QoL: No clinically meaningful differences
・Subgroups: dMMR (post hoc, not prespecified): Ⓐ 95% vs Ⓑ 79% 3-yr DFS, favouring upfront surgery; P = .09
・Toxicity: G3-4 diarrhoea Ⓐ 14% vs Ⓑ 13%; sensory neuropathy Ⓐ 11% vs Ⓑ 7%; anastomotic leak Ⓐ 8% vs Ⓑ 2%
・Limitations: Underpowered (38 of 56 planned DFS events); nonconfirmatory

records.title: DYNAMIC
records.subtitle: Early CRC · CtDNA / minimal residual disease-guided therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2022
records.body:
Resected stage II (T3 or T4, N0, M0) colon or rectal adenocarcinoma with negative resection margins; adjuvant-decision setting, enrolled within 3 weeks after surgery; medically able to receive adjuvant oxaliplatin-based or single-agent fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy; excluded: macroscopic metastases on CT, another primary cancer within 3 years, synchronous colorectal primary, neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy Ⓐ ctDNA-guided management: tumour-informed ctDNA at weeks 4 and 7 after surgery; ctDNA-positive at either time point → adjuvant oxaliplatin-based or single-agent fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy (regimen at clinician's discretion; most scheduled for 24 weeks); ctDNA-negative at both → no adjuvant chemotherapy
Ⓑ Standard management: adjuvant chemotherapy decided by conventional clinicopathological criteria
・Amendment: February 2018 protocol amendment allowed 3 months of chemotherapy Primary: recurrence-free survival at 2 years. Secondary: adjuvant chemotherapy use, recurrence-free survival in ctDNA-positive and ctDNA-negative patients, time to recurrence, overall survival, ctDNA clearance rate, fear of recurrence, cost-effectiveness ctDNA-guided management reduced adjuvant chemotherapy use and was non-inferior to standard management for recurrence-free survival
・Chemotherapy use: Ⓐ 15% vs Ⓑ 28%; RR 1.82 (95% CI 1.25–2.65)
・2-yr RFS: Ⓐ 93.5% vs Ⓑ 92.4%; difference 1.1 percentage points (95% CI −4.1 to 6.2; non-inferiority margin −8.5)
・5-yr RFS: Ⓐ 88.3% vs Ⓑ 87.2% (median follow-up 59.7 mo)
・5-yr OS: Ⓐ 93.8% vs Ⓑ 93.3%; HR 1.05 (95% CI 0.47–2.37); not powered for OS non-inferiority
・ctDNA clearance: Ⓐ 87.5% at end of treatment
・Chemo start: Ⓐ median 83 vs Ⓑ 53 days
・Subgroups: Within Ⓐ, 5-yr RFS 76.7% in treated ctDNA-positive vs 90.4% in untreated ctDNA-negative; not randomized, no multiplicity control
・Toxicity: Adverse events not assessed; chemotherapy stopped for toxicity in 6/45 Ⓐ vs 7/41 Ⓑ; no treatment-related deaths

records.title: DYNAMIC-III
records.subtitle: Early CRC · CtDNA / minimal residual disease-guided therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase II/III) · 2025
records.body:
Resected, histologically confirmed colon or rectal adenocarcinoma; stage III (any T, N1−2, M0) with negative resection margins, adjuvant setting; post-surgery tumor-informed ctDNA tested at weeks 5−6 and randomized irrespective of result; medically fit for at least adjuvant fluoropyrimidine monotherapy, enrolled up to 6 weeks after surgery; excluded: neoadjuvant chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy, multiple primary colorectal cancers, another primary cancer within 3 years Ⓐ ctDNA-guided management: ctDNA negative → de-escalation of the clinician-prespecified regimen (6 months oxaliplatin-based doublet → 6 months FP or 3 months doublet; 3 months doublet → 3 or 6 months FP; 6 months FP → no chemotherapy or 3 months FP); ctDNA positive → escalation (no chemotherapy → 6 months FP; 6 months FP → 6 months doublet; 3 months doublet → 6 months doublet or at least 3 months FOLFOXIRI; 6 months doublet → at least 3 months FOLFOXIRI, extendable to 6 months by tolerability)
Ⓑ Standard management: clinician-nominated before randomization 6 or 3 months oxaliplatin doublet (FOLFOX/CAPOX), 6 months fluoropyrimidine or no adjuvant treatment Primary: 3-year recurrence-free survival (ctDNA-negative cohort), 2-year recurrence-free survival (ctDNA-positive cohort). Secondary: compliance with de-escalation strategy, ctDNA clearance, overall survival, treatment-related hospitalization, selected high-grade toxicities, end-of-treatment ctDNA status in ctDNA-negative patients, ctDNA burden, ctDNA kinetics, tumor mutation profile, sites of recurrence, cost-effectiveness ctDNA-guided adjuvant selection did not improve outcomes: de-escalation missed RFS non-inferiority and escalation did not improve RFS vs standard management
・3-yr RFS (ctDNA-negative): Ⓐ 85.3% vs Ⓑ 88.1%; difference −2.8% (97.5% lower CI −8.0% vs −7.5% margin); missed non-inferiority
・2-yr RFS (ctDNA-positive, exploratory phase 2): Ⓐ 51% vs Ⓑ 61%; HR 1.16 (95% CI 0.87–1.53)
・Prognostic value: Post-surgery ctDNA-negative vs positive 3-yr RFS 87% vs 49%; fell from 77% to 23% across ctDNA-burden quartiles
・Clearance: 3-yr RFS 14% with persistent vs 79% with cleared end-of-treatment ctDNA
・Toxicity: Oxaliplatin doublet use Ⓐ 34.8% vs Ⓑ 88.6%; hospitalization Ⓐ 8.5% vs Ⓑ 13.2%; grade 3-4 AESIs Ⓐ 6.2% vs Ⓑ 10.6%; 6 patients had grade 5 events
・Limitations: Escalation analysis exploratory (phase 2); high-risk features overrepresented in escalation arm; OS not yet reported

records.title: GALAXY (CIRCULATE-Japan)
records.subtitle: Early CRC · CtDNA / minimal residual disease-guided therapy · Registry study · 2023
records.body:
Colorectal adenocarcinoma of colon or rectum (excluding appendix and anal canal); curative resection planned for clinical stage II–III, or R0 resection planned for stage IV or relapsed disease; tumour-informed ctDNA result at the 4-week postsurgical time point required for analysis; excluded other malignancy within 5 years, enrolment in interventional CIRCULATE cohorts, incomplete/noncurative resection, unknown or stage 0 pathology Ⓐ Adjuvant chemotherapy at treating-team discretion, blinded to ctDNA (single-agent capecitabine or capecitabine plus oxaliplatin-based therapy)
Ⓑ Observation
・Design: Non-randomised
・Monitoring: ctDNA (personalised tumour-informed Signatera assay) before surgery and 4, 12, 24, 36, 48, 72 and 96 weeks after surgery until recurrence, CT every 6 months Primary: disease-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: ctDNA clearance, ctDNA dynamics from week 4 to week 12, recurrence rate, ctDNA concentration, ctDNA–CEA concordance, molecular recurrence, post-recurrence survival Postsurgical ctDNA positivity was a stronger prognostic biomarker than clinicopathological risk features and potentially predictive of ACT benefit
・Update: 2024 update (2,240 patients; 23-mo median follow-up) extended ctDNA's prognostic value to OS
・DFS: MRD-window ctDNA positive vs negative 20.57% vs 85.10% at 24 mo; HR 11.99
・OS: MRD-window ctDNA positive vs negative 83.65% vs 98.50% at 24 mo; HR 9.68
・Multivariate: ctDNA strongest factor; DFS HR 12.08, OS HR 9.87
・Presurgical ctDNA: Not prognostic; HR 0.89
・Subgroups: MRD-positive: Ⓐ vs Ⓑ improved DFS, adjusted HR 0.23; MRD-negative: no significant benefit, adjusted HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.46–1.06); clearance (ACT-treated, MRD-positive): sustained vs transient 24-mo DFS 89.0% vs 3.3%
・Limitations: Observational, non-randomised ACT comparisons; 23-mo follow-up may be insufficient for OS
records.keywords: Kotani et al. Nat Med 2023;29:127-134  36646802 Nakamura et al. Nat Med 2024;30:3272-3283  39284954

records.title: ALTAIR
records.subtitle: Early CRC · CtDNA / minimal residual disease-guided therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Resected colorectal cancer (stage II or lower, stage III or oligometastatic stage IV) after radical resection of primary and/or metastatic tumours; post-adjuvant setting after completion of standard-of-care therapy, with no radiographic evidence of relapse; tumour-informed ctDNA (Signatera) positive in blood collected within 3 months of any timepoint between 1 month and 24 months after surgery; excluded prior FTD/TPI or two or more postoperative chemotherapy regimens Ⓐ FTD/TPI 35 mg/m² per dose orally twice daily for five consecutive days then a 2-day break, repeated twice, then a 14-day break (28-day course), for six courses or until discontinuation
Ⓑ Placebo on the same schedule
・Design: Double-blind Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: ctDNA clearance rate, DFS2, overall survival, incidence of adverse events, treatment completion rate, quality of life Post-adjuvant FTD/TPI did not significantly improve DFS in ctDNA-positive, radiologically disease-free patients; primary endpoint not met
・DFS: Ⓐ 9.30 vs Ⓑ 5.55 mo; HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.60–1.05), P=0.107
・DFS (landmark): 6-mo Ⓐ 70.5% vs Ⓑ 45.5%; 24-mo Ⓐ 16.9% vs Ⓑ 14.5%, consistent with recurrence-delaying rather than curative effect
・DFS2: HR 0.78 (P=0.073)
・OS: Immature (24 events at median 23.29 mo follow-up)
・ctDNA clearance: Ⓐ 17.2% vs Ⓑ 12.4% (P=0.367)
・QoL: Worsened during FTD/TPI treatment at week 8 (P=0.028), minimal difference from week 24 onward
・Subgroups: Stage IV HR 0.53 (P=0.012) vs stages I–III HR 0.86; post hoc blinded central review HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.55–0.98); exploratory, multiplicity-unadjusted
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 AEs Ⓐ 73.0% vs Ⓑ 3.3%, mainly neutropenia 56.6%; serious AEs Ⓐ 4.9% vs Ⓑ 0%; no treatment-related deaths
・Limitations: OS immature; subgroup and sensitivity analyses exploratory, multiplicity-unadjusted

records.title: ALASCCA
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant aspirin — PI3K pathway-altered disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Colorectal cancer after radical resection of the primary tumour; pTNM stage II or III colon or stage I, II or III rectal cancer, age 18 to 80 years; somatic PI3K pathway alteration: group A PIK3CA hotspot mutations in exon 9 or 20 (patients with group A and group B alterations included as group A), group B other moderate- or high-impact somatic variants in PIK3CA, PIK3R1 or PTEN; randomised within 12 weeks after surgery Ⓐ Aspirin 160 mg once daily for 3 years
Ⓑ Matched placebo once daily for 3 years
・Timing: Started within 12 weeks after surgery
・Chemotherapy: Alone or with adjuvant chemotherapy chosen by the local investigator per national guidelines Primary: colorectal cancer recurrence in group A alterations. Secondary: disease-free survival in group A, overall survival in group A, colorectal cancer recurrence in group B, disease-free survival in group B, overall survival in group B, adverse events, severe adverse events Adjuvant aspirin lowered 3-yr colorectal cancer recurrence vs placebo in PIK3CA exon 9/20-mutated tumours (group A); group B benefit was exploratory
・3-yr recurrence (group A): Ⓐ 7.7% vs Ⓑ 14.1%; HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.24–0.98; P=0.04)
・3-yr recurrence (group B, exploratory): Ⓐ 7.7% vs Ⓑ 16.8%; HR 0.42 (95% CI 0.21–0.83)
・3-yr DFS (group A): Ⓐ 88.5% vs Ⓑ 81.4%; HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.34–1.08)
・3-yr DFS (group B): Ⓐ 89.1% vs Ⓑ 78.7%; HR 0.51
・5-yr OS (group A): Ⓐ 91.6% vs Ⓑ 90.1%; HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.37–1.68)
・Subgroups: Post hoc, greater benefit in women (HR 0.25) than men (HR 0.75; 95% CI 0.39–1.44)
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 AEs Ⓐ 16.8% vs Ⓑ 11.6%; four severe events (including GI bleeding, subarachnoid hemorrhage) and one grade 5 event potentially aspirin-related
・Limitations: Secondary and subgroup results descriptive, without multiplicity adjustment; sex subgroup finding is post hoc
records.keywords: Martling et al. N Engl J Med 2025;393:1051-1064  40961426

records.title: NICHE-2
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Immunotherapy for dMMR / MSI-H disease · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2024
records.body:
Locally advanced dMMR colon adenocarcinoma; previously untreated, resectable clinical stage II or III with no distant metastases, neoadjuvant setting; dMMR by IHC (absent staining of ≥1 of MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, MSH6); NICHE-2 cohort (after October 2020 amendment) required radiographic cT3 or higher, N+, or both; excluded clinical obstruction, previous immunotherapy, active autoimmune disease requiring immunosuppressive therapy (single-arm) Neoadjuvant nivolumab 3 mg/kg on days 1 and 15 plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg on day 1 (4-week treatment period) → surgery scheduled within 6 weeks after enrollment Primary: timely surgery, 3-year disease-free survival. Secondary: pathological response, translational genomic analyses, major pathological response, pathological complete response, disease recurrence, immune-related adverse events, surgery-related adverse events, R0 resection Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab produced pathological responses in a high proportion of patients with locally advanced dMMR colon cancer; single-arm data without a comparator
・Primary endpoint (timely surgery): 113 of 115 (98%; 97.5% CI 93 to 100) had timely surgery; 2 delays due to myositis
・R0 resection: 100%
・Pathological response: 98%; major pathological response 95%; pathological complete response 68% (95% CI 58 to 76)
・DFS: Co-primary 3-year DFS not mature; no recurrences at median follow-up of 26 months (range 9 to 65)
・Toxicity: Grade 3 or 4 immune-related adverse events in 5 patients (4%), no discontinuations; surgery-related grade 3 events in 12 (10%); anastomotic leakage in 4 (3%)
・Limitations: Single-arm, no comparator; co-primary DFS endpoint immature

records.title: ATOMIC
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Immunotherapy for dMMR / MSI-H disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Histologically confirmed stage III colon adenocarcinoma, completely resected (R0; any T, N1 or N2, M0); adjuvant, randomized within 10 weeks after surgery; dMMR by local immunohistochemistry or site-selected reference laboratory (retrospective central confirmation); age ≥12 yr, ECOG 0–2, known Lynch syndrome eligible; no prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy except one cycle of mFOLFOX6 before enrollment Ⓐ Atezolizumab 840 mg IV every 2 weeks + mFOLFOX6 for 12 cycles (6 months) → atezolizumab monotherapy for 13 cycles (12 months total)
Ⓑ mFOLFOX6 alone for 12 cycles (6 months)
・mFOLFOX6: Fluorouracil 400 mg per square meter bolus + 2400 mg per square meter continuous infusion over 46 hours, oxaliplatin 85 mg per square meter, leucovorin 400 mg per square meter
・Duration: Continued to protocol-defined duration or until recurrence, metastasis, unacceptable adverse events or consent withdrawal Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, adverse-event profile, PRO-CTCAE, quality of life Atezolizumab plus mFOLFOX6 improved disease-free survival vs mFOLFOX6 alone in resected stage III dMMR colon cancer; primary endpoint met at interim analysis
・DFS: Ⓐ 86.3% vs Ⓑ 76.2% at 3 yr (median follow-up 40.9 mo); HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.35–0.73)
・OS: Ⓐ 89.7% vs Ⓑ 87.9% at 5 yr; HR 0.90 (95% CI 0.55–1.47); not significant
・Subgroups: DFS benefit with >6 cycles of mFOLFOX6 (HR 0.41) but not with ≤6 cycles (HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.44–2.11); exploratory
・Toxicity: Grade 3–4 AEs Ⓐ 84.1% vs Ⓑ 71.9%, including fatigue 10.1% vs 3.3% and decreased neutrophil count 43.6% vs 35.9%; grade 5 events in six vs two patients, two Ⓐ-arm deaths treatment-related; early discontinuation 52.7% vs 32.5%
・Limitations: OS analysis is first and immature; future OS differences may be hard to interpret because of post-recurrence immunotherapy; cycle-number subgroup finding exploratory

records.title: CHALLENGE
records.subtitle: Early CRC · Adjuvant lifestyle intervention — structured exercise · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Completely resected colon adenocarcinoma, stage III or high-risk stage II (T4 tumor with resection of fewer than 12 lymph nodes and poorly differentiated histology); adjuvant chemotherapy completed within the past 2 to 6 months; exercising less than 150 minutes/week of moderate-to-vigorous intensity; able to complete at least two stages of a submaximal treadmill test or the 6-minute walk test Ⓐ Structured exercise program for 3 years: health-education materials plus behavioral support, aiming to increase recreational aerobic exercise by at least 10 MET-hours/week; first 6 months 12 mandatory in-person behavioral-support sessions every 2 weeks plus 12 mandatory and 12 recommended supervised exercise sessions; second 6 months 12 mandatory sessions every 2 weeks; last 2 years 24 mandatory monthly in-person or remote sessions
Ⓑ Health-education materials alone (physical activity and healthy nutrition) with standard surveillance
・Duration: Delivered while free of recurrence or new primary cancer Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, patient-reported physical functioning (SF-36 physical-functioning subscale), objective physical functioning, cardiorespiratory fitness, recreational moderate-to-vigorous physical activity, body weight, waist circumference, adverse events Structured exercise program significantly prolonged disease-free survival and was associated with longer overall survival versus health education alone
・DFS: HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.55–0.94) at median follow-up 7.9 yr; P=0.02; 5-yr Ⓐ 80.3% vs Ⓑ 73.9% (difference 6.4 percentage points, 95% CI 0.6 to 12.2)
・OS: HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.43–0.94); 8-yr Ⓐ 90.3% vs Ⓑ 83.2%
・QoL: Fitness, 6-minute walk distance, and SF-36 physical functioning improved more with Ⓐ than Ⓑ
・Toxicity: As-treated: musculoskeletal AEs Ⓐ 18.5% vs Ⓑ 11.5% (8 of 79 in Ⓐ deemed exercise-related); grade ≥3 AEs Ⓐ 15.4% vs Ⓑ 9.1%
・Limitations: Final analysis had only 224 of 380 targeted events after an accrual deadline was set because of slow recruitment; secondary-endpoint CIs were not adjusted for multiplicity

records.title: de Gramont et al.
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line cytotoxic backbones · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2000
records.body:
Adenocarcinoma of the colon or rectum; unresectable metastatic disease, previously untreated (first-line); at least one bidimensionally measurable lesion ≥2 cm, WHO PS 0-2, age 18-75 yr, prior adjuvant chemotherapy completed ≥6 months before inclusion; excluded CNS metastases, second malignancies or disease confined to previous radiation fields Ⓐ LV5FU2: LV 200 mg/m²/d → 5FU bolus 400 mg/m²/d + 22-h infusion 600 mg/m²/d, on 2 consecutive days every 2 weeks
Ⓑ FOLFOX4: same LV5FU2 + oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² on day 1 (concurrent with LV)
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or patient choice to discontinue Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: response rate, overall survival, tolerability, quality of life, time to response, duration of response, secondary resection of metastases, time to deterioration of global health status FOLFOX4 improved PFS vs LV5FU2 as first-line therapy; OS improvement was not significant
・PFS: Ⓐ 6.0 vs Ⓑ 8.2 mo (external review); P = .0003; investigator-assessed Ⓐ 6.2 vs Ⓑ 9.0 mo
・RR: Ⓐ 22.3% vs Ⓑ 50.7% (external review, assessable patients)
・OS: Ⓐ 14.7 vs Ⓑ 16.2 mo; P = .12 (log-rank), not significant
・QoL: Median scores comparable; time to 40% global health status deterioration longer with Ⓑ; P = .0004
・Toxicity: G3/4 neutropenia Ⓐ 5.3% vs Ⓑ 41.7% (febrile 1.0%); G3/4 diarrhea Ⓐ 5.3% vs Ⓑ 11.9%; G3 neurosensory Ⓐ 0% vs Ⓑ 18.2% (reversed in 25 of 34); withdrawals Ⓐ 3.4% vs Ⓑ 10.6%; Ⓑ one therapy-related death, four severe allergic reactions

records.title: Saltz et al.
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line cytotoxic backbones · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2000
records.body:
Metastatic colorectal cancer, histologically documented, with measurable metastatic disease; first-line, no prior therapy for metastatic disease; prior adjuvant fluorouracil allowed if disease-free for at least one year after completion; ECOG 0–2; prior pelvic irradiation excluded Ⓐ Irinotecan 125 mg/m² IV + fluorouracil 500 mg/m² IV bolus + leucovorin 20 mg/m² IV bolus weekly for four weeks every six weeks
Ⓑ Fluorouracil 425 mg/m² IV bolus + leucovorin 20 mg/m² IV bolus daily for five consecutive days every four weeks (Mayo Clinic regimen)
Ⓒ Irinotecan alone 125 mg/m² IV weekly for four weeks every six weeks
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable adverse effects or withdrawal of consent Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, confirmed objective response rate, duration of confirmed response, quality of life, safety Weekly irinotecan plus bolus fluorouracil/leucovorin improved PFS and OS versus Mayo Clinic fluorouracil/leucovorin as first-line therapy, without compromising quality of life
・PFS: Ⓐ 7.0 vs Ⓑ 4.3 mo; P=0.004 (primary endpoint)
・Other arm: Ⓒ irinotecan alone gave similar results to Ⓑ (PFS 4.2, OS 12.0 mo); not formally tested
・ORR: Ⓐ 39% vs Ⓑ 21% (confirmed response)
・OS: Ⓐ 14.8 vs Ⓑ 12.6 mo; P=0.04 (56% of Ⓑ later received an irinotecan-based regimen)
・Toxicity: G3/4 diarrhea Ⓐ 22.7% vs Ⓑ 13.2% (G4 7.6% vs 7.3%); G3/4 mucositis Ⓐ 2.2% vs Ⓑ 16.9%; G4 neutropenia Ⓐ 24.0% vs Ⓑ 42.5%; neutropenic fever Ⓐ 7.1% vs Ⓑ 14.6%; drug-related deaths Ⓐ 0.9% vs Ⓑ 1.4%

records.title: Douillard et al.
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line cytotoxic backbones · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2000
records.body:
Metastatic colorectal cancer, histologically proven adenocarcinoma of the colon or rectum; first-line, no previous chemotherapy other than adjuvant, finished more than 6 months before randomisation; age 18–75 years, WHO performance status 2 or less, life expectancy more than 3 months; excluded CNS metastasis, unresolved bowel obstruction or diarrhoea, fluorouracil contraindications (angina pectoris, myocardial infarction in past 6 months) Ⓐ Irinotecan + infusional fluorouracil/calcium folinate, centre-chosen schedule: weekly irinotecan 80 mg/m² + fluorouracil 2300 mg/m² by 24 h infusion + calcium folinate 500 mg/m², or every 2 weeks irinotecan 180 mg/m² day 1 + fluorouracil 400 mg/m² bolus and 600 mg/m² by 22 h infusion + calcium folinate 200 mg/m² days 1 and 2
Ⓑ Fluorouracil/calcium folinate alone: weekly fluorouracil 2600 mg/m² by 24 h infusion + calcium folinate 500 mg/m², or the same 2-weekly fluorouracil/calcium folinate doses
・Duration: Until progression, unacceptable toxicity or consent withdrawal Primary: response rate. Secondary: time to progression, duration of response, time to treatment failure, overall survival, duration of response and stabilisation, quality of life, time to definitive deterioration in performance status, safety Adding irinotecan to infusional fluorouracil/calcium folinate improved response rate, TTP and OS vs fluorouracil/calcium folinate alone, with later QoL deterioration
・ORR: Ⓐ 34.8 vs Ⓑ 21.9%; p=0.005
・TTP: Ⓐ 6.7 vs Ⓑ 4.4 mo; p<0.001
・OS: Ⓐ 17.4 vs Ⓑ 14.1 mo; p=0.031
・QoL: Global QL did not differ significantly without imputation
・Subgroups: Weekly-regimen subset too small to compare efficacy
・Toxicity: G3-4 neutropenia Ⓐ 46.2 vs Ⓑ 13.4%; diarrhoea (2-weekly) Ⓐ 13.1 vs Ⓑ 5.6%, (weekly) Ⓐ 44.4 vs Ⓑ 25.6%; one Ⓐ death from septic shock with G4 neutropenia
・Limitations: More Ⓑ patients received further chemotherapy (58.3 vs 39.4%), confounding the OS comparison

records.title: NCCTG-N9741
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line cytotoxic backbones · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2004
records.body:
Histologically proven unresectable colorectal adenocarcinoma, metastatic; previously untreated for advanced disease (first-line); at least one measurable lesion (≥2 cm) or assessable disease; excluded prior treatment for advanced disease, adjuvant fluorouracil in previous 12 months, symptomatic peripheral neuropathy, known brain or meningeal metastases Ⓐ Irinotecan 125 mg/m² + bolus FU 500 mg/m² + LV 20 mg/m² days 1, 8, 15, 22 every 6 weeks
Ⓑ Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² day 1 + bolus FU 400 mg/m² + LV 200 mg/m² → FU 600 mg/m² 22-hour infusion days 1 and 2 every 2 weeks
Ⓒ Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + irinotecan 200 mg/m² every 3 weeks
・Duration: Until progression, unmanageable toxicity or withdrawal of consent Primary: time to progression. Secondary: overall survival, confirmed tumor response rate, time to treatment discontinuation, toxicity, 60-day mortality FOLFOX improved time to progression, response and overall survival compared with IFL in advanced colorectal cancer
・TTP: Ⓑ 8.7 vs Ⓐ 6.9 mo; HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.61–0.89)
・OS: Ⓑ 19.5 vs Ⓐ 15.0 mo; HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.54–0.82)
・ORR: Ⓑ 45% vs Ⓐ 31%
・Other comparisons: Ⓒ vs Ⓐ TTP 6.5 mo (HR 1.02), not improved; OS 17.4 mo (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.66–1.00; P=.04); Ⓑ vs Ⓒ OS not different (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.67–1.03)
・Toxicity: G≥3 diarrhea Ⓐ 28% vs Ⓑ 12%; febrile neutropenia Ⓐ 15% vs Ⓑ 4%; paresthesias Ⓐ 3% vs Ⓑ 18%; neutropenia Ⓐ 40% vs Ⓑ 50%; 60-day deaths Ⓐ 4.5% vs Ⓑ 2.6% vs Ⓒ 2.7%

records.title: Tournigand et al.
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line cytotoxic backbones · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2004
records.body:
Metastatic adenocarcinoma of the colon or rectum; unresectable metastases, previously untreated (prior adjuvant chemotherapy completed ≥6 months before inclusion); ≥1 bidimensionally measurable lesion ≥2 cm or residual nonmeasurable lesion; WHO PS 0–2, age 18–75 years; excluded CNS metastases, second malignancies, bowel obstruction, current diarrhea ≥grade 2, disease confined to previous radiation fields Ⓐ FOLFIRI (irinotecan 180 mg/m² IV day 1) → FOLFOX6 (oxaliplatin 100 mg/m² IV day 1)

records.title: TRIBE
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line cytotoxic backbones · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2014
records.body:
Unresectable metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma; first-line, no prior chemotherapy or biologic therapy for metastatic disease (prior adjuvant allowed); first occurrence of metastatic disease deemed unresectable with curative intent; age 18–75 years, ECOG ≤2 (age >70 only if ECOG 0); excluded adjuvant oxaliplatin completed <12 months before relapse, grade ≥1 peripheral neuropathy, need for full-dose anticoagulation Ⓐ FOLFOXIRI plus bevacizumab (bevacizumab 5 mg/kg, irinotecan 165 mg/m², oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², leucovorin 200 mg/m², fluorouracil 3200 mg/m² 48-hour continuous infusion) every 14 days for up to 12 cycles
Ⓑ FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab (bevacizumab 5 mg/kg, irinotecan 180 mg/m², leucovorin 200 mg/m², fluorouracil 400 mg/m² bolus then 2400 mg/m² 46-hour continuous infusion) every 14 days for up to 12 cycles
・Duration: Until progression, unacceptable adverse event or consent withdrawal
・Maintenance: Bevacizumab, fluorouracil and leucovorin Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: response rate, overall survival, treatment efficacy in molecular subgroups, resection rate of metastases, adverse event rate FOLFOXIRI plus bevacizumab improved PFS and OS vs FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab in untreated metastatic colorectal cancer, at the cost of more adverse events
・PFS: Ⓐ 12.3 vs Ⓑ 9.7 mo; HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.65–0.93)
・OS: Ⓐ 29.8 vs Ⓑ 25.8 mo; HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.65–0.98; p=0.03); secondary endpoint, previously preliminary, now significant at updated follow-up
・ORR: Ⓐ 65.1% vs Ⓑ 53.1%
・R0 resection: Ⓐ 15% vs Ⓑ 12%; not significant
・Subgroups: Prior adjuvant therapy, no PFS benefit (interaction P=0.04); RAS/BRAF status did not modify OS effect (interaction p=0.52)
・Toxicity: G3–4 neutropenia Ⓐ 50.0% vs Ⓑ 20.5%; diarrhoea 18.8% vs 10.6%; stomatitis 8.8% vs 4.3%; peripheral neuropathy 5.2% vs 0; AE deaths 6 (2.4%) vs 4 (1.6%)

records.title: TRIPLETE

Ⓑ modified FOLFOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², leucovorin 200 mg/m², FU 400 mg/m² bolus then 2,400 mg/m² 48-h infusion) plus panitumumab 6 mg/kg IV every 14 days, up to 12 cycles → same maintenance
・Duration: Until progression, refusal, unacceptable toxicity or consent withdrawal Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: safety, progression-free survival, early tumor shrinkage rate, deepness of response, R0 resection rate, overall survival, disease control rate mFOLFOXIRI plus panitumumab did not improve ORR or PFS over FOLFOX plus panitumumab in RAS/BRAF wild-type mCRC and increased gastrointestinal toxicity; primary endpoint not met

records.title: NO16966 (XELOX-1)
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line cytotoxic backbones · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2008
records.body:
Histologically confirmed colorectal cancer with unresectable metastatic disease and one or more unidimensionally measurable lesions; first-line, no prior systemic therapy for metastatic disease and no prior oxaliplatin or bevacizumab; excluded known CNS metastases, clinically significant cardiovascular disease, clinically detectable ascites, full-dose anticoagulants or thrombolytics, bleeding diathesis Ⓐ XELOX: oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1 + oral capecitabine 1,000 mg/m² twice daily for 2 weeks, 3-week cycles
Ⓑ FOLFOX-4: biweekly bolus and infusional FU/folinic acid + oxaliplatin
・Design: After 2003 amendment, 2×2 factorial adding double-blind bevacizumab or placebo (7.5 mg/kg every third week with XELOX; 5 mg/kg every second week with FOLFOX-4)
・Duration: Until progression or 48 weeks (up to 16 XELOX or 24 FOLFOX-4 cycles), then optional continuation until progression Primary: progression-free survival. ・OS: Ⓐ 19.8 vs Ⓑ 19.6 mo; HR 0.99 (97.5% CI 0.88-1.12); descriptive analysis, January 2007 cut

records.title: Cremolini et al.
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line cytotoxic backbones · Individual patient data meta-analysis · 2020
records.body:
Unresectable metastatic colorectal cancer; first-line therapy; IPD from 5 randomized trials of FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab vs doublet + bevacizumab, entry criteria varying by trial (age 18-75 in TRIBE, STEAM and TRIBE2; ECOG PS 0-2 or 0-1; OLIVIA liver-only metastases); TRIBE2 excluded prior oxaliplatin-based adjuvant therapy; STEAM sequential FOLFOXIRI arm excluded Ⓐ FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab
Ⓑ Doublet (FOLFOX or FOLFIRI) + bevacizumab
・Induction: 4 to 6 months
・Maintenance: Fluoropyrimidine (fluorouracil/leucovorin or capecitabine) + bevacizumab
・Duration: Until disease progression, patient refusal, unacceptable adverse events or consent withdrawal Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, R0 resection rate, grade 3/4 adverse events, subgroup analyses by clinical and molecular characteristics, 5-year overall survival rate, toxic deaths FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab significantly improved OS vs doublet + bevacizumab in mCRC, with gains in PFS, ORR and R0 resection
・OS: Ⓐ 28.9 vs Ⓑ 24.5 mo; HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.72 to 0.91); follow-up 39.9 mo
・Heterogeneity: I2 2%, no significant heterogeneity among trials
・5-yr OS: Ⓐ 22.3% vs Ⓑ 10.7% (estimated)
・PFS: Ⓐ 12.2 vs Ⓑ 9.9 mo; HR 0.74
・ORR: Ⓐ 64.5% vs Ⓑ 53.6%
・R0 resection: Ⓐ 16.4% vs Ⓑ 11.8%
・Subgroups: No significant interaction between treatment and investigated characteristics; BRAF-mutant OS HR 1.11 (95% CI 0.75 to 1.73), no increased benefit
・Toxicity: Grade 3/4 neutropenia Ⓐ 45.8% vs Ⓑ 21.5%; febrile neutropenia Ⓐ 6.3% vs Ⓑ 3.7%; diarrhea Ⓐ 17.8% vs Ⓑ 8.4%; toxic deaths Ⓐ 2.3% vs Ⓑ 1.4%, not significantly increased

records.title: Hurwitz et al.
