・Duration: Until progression, unacceptable toxicity or maximum 96 weeks Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, safety, quality of life, one-year survival rate Adding bevacizumab to bolus IFL improved OS, PFS and response rate in first-line metastatic colorectal cancer
・OS: Ⓐ 20.3 vs Ⓑ 15.6 mo; HR 0.66; P<0.001
・1-yr OS: Ⓐ 74.3% vs Ⓑ 63.4%
・PFS: Ⓐ 10.6 vs Ⓑ 6.2 mo; HR 0.54
・ORR: Ⓐ 44.8% vs Ⓑ 34.8%
・DoR: Ⓐ 10.4 vs Ⓑ 7.1 mo
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 84.9% vs Ⓑ 74.0%; hypertension Ⓐ 11.0% vs Ⓑ 2.3%; GI perforation Ⓐ 1.5% (1 fatal) vs Ⓑ 0%; all grade 4 bleeds with Ⓐ
・Limitations: AE rates not adjusted for longer therapy duration (Ⓐ 40.4 vs Ⓑ 27.6 wk)
records.keywords: Hurwitz et al. N Engl J Med 2004;350:2335-2342  15175435

records.title: NO16966
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · First-line antiangiogenic therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2008
records.body:
Histologically confirmed metastatic colorectal cancer not amenable to curative resection; first-line, no prior systemic therapy for MCRC and no prior oxaliplatin or bevacizumab; one or more unidimensionally measurable lesions; excluded known CNS metastases, clinically significant cardiovascular disease, full-dose anticoagulants or thrombolytics, bleeding diathesis/coagulopathy, proteinuria ≥500 mg/24 hours Ⓐ Bevacizumab 7.5 mg/kg IV day 1 q3w with XELOX or 5 mg/kg IV day 1 q2w with FOLFOX-4
Ⓑ Placebo added to XELOX or FOLFOX-4
・XELOX: Oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1 + capecitabine 1,000 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1–14, 21-day cycle
・Duration: Until PD or 48 weeks (up to 16 XELOX or 24 FOLFOX-4 cycles), then optional continuation until PD Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: On-treatment progression-free survival, overall survival, response rate, duration of response, time to treatment failure, safety Adding bevacizumab to first-line oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy improved PFS but did not improve OS or response rate
・PFS: Ⓐ 9.4 vs Ⓑ 8.0 mo; HR 0.83 (97.5% CI 0.72–0.95)
・OS: Ⓐ 21.3 vs Ⓑ 19.9 mo; HR 0.89 (97.5% CI 0.76–1.03; January 31, 2007 cutoff)
・RR: Ⓐ 47% vs Ⓑ 49% by investigators; 38% vs 38% by independent review
・Subgroups: PFS benefit significant with XELOX (HR 0.77); not significant with FOLFOX-4 (HR 0.89)
・Toxicity: Grade 3/4 AEs Ⓐ 80% vs Ⓑ 75%; bevacizumab-related G3/4 events of special interest 16% vs 8%, mostly thromboembolic; AE-related discontinuation 30% vs 21%; treatment-related mortality 2.0% vs 1.5%; one of four GI perforations fatal
・Limitations: Only Ⓐ 29% vs Ⓑ 47% treated until progression; prespecified on-treatment PFS HR 0.63
records.keywords: Saltz et al. J Clin Oncol 2008;26:2013-2019  18421054

records.title: CRYSTAL
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Anti-EGFR therapy & primary tumour sidedness (RAS wild-type) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2009
records.body:
Metastatic adenocarcinoma of the colon or rectum; first-line, first occurrence of metastatic disease not resectable for curative purposes; immunohistochemical evidence of tumour EGFR expression (KRAS status analysed retrospectively); ECOG PS ≤2; excluded prior anti-EGFR or irinotecan-based therapy, prior chemotherapy for metastatic disease, or adjuvant treatment ended ≤6 months before study start Ⓐ Cetuximab 400 mg/m² day 1 then 250 mg/m² weekly + FOLFIRI every 14 days
Ⓑ FOLFIRI alone every 14 days (irinotecan 180 mg/m², racemic leucovorin 400 or l-leucovorin 200 mg/m², fluorouracil 400 mg/m² bolus then 2400 mg/m² over 46 h, day 1)
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal of consent Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, best overall response rate, safety, rate of surgery with curative intent, R0 resection rate Adding cetuximab to first-line FOLFIRI improved PFS; OS did not differ at primary analysis but improved at an updated, exploratory cut
・PFS: Ⓐ 8.9 vs Ⓑ 8.0 mo; HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.72–0.99; P=0.048)
・OS (primary analysis): HR 0.93; not significant
・OS (updated, exploratory cut, May 31 2009): Ⓐ 19.9 vs Ⓑ 18.6 mo; HR 0.878 (95% CI 0.774–0.995; P=.0419)
・ORR: Ⓐ 46.9% vs Ⓑ 38.7%; OR 1.40
・R0 resection: Ⓐ 4.8% vs Ⓑ 1.7%
・Subgroups: KRAS wild-type (exploratory, retrospective): OS Ⓐ 23.5 vs Ⓑ 20.0 mo (HR 0.796), PFS HR 0.696, ORR 57.3% vs 39.7%; mutant OS HR 1.035
・Subgroups: BRAF V600E indicated poor prognosis, not shown to be predictive
・Toxicity: Grade 3/4 AEs Ⓐ 79.3% vs Ⓑ 61.0%; skin reactions 19.5% vs 0.2%, diarrhoea 15.7% vs 10.5%, infusion reactions 2.3% vs 0%; no cetuximab-related deaths
・Limitations: Primary OS analysis not significant; updated OS exploratory with differential post-study EGFR therapy (Ⓐ 11.0% vs Ⓑ 29.7%); KRAS/BRAF subgroup analyses retrospective and unadjusted
records.keywords: Van Cutsem et al. N Engl J Med 2009;360:1408-1417  19339720 Van Cutsem et al. J Clin Oncol 2011;29:2011-2019  21502544

records.title: PRIME
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Anti-EGFR therapy & primary tumour sidedness (RAS wild-type) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2010
records.body:
Previously untreated metastatic adenocarcinoma of the colon or rectum; first-line; KRAS status not required at entry, efficacy analysed prospectively by central tumour KRAS status (WT vs MT); ECOG PS 0-2, tumour tissue available for central biomarker analysis, prior fluorouracil-based adjuvant chemotherapy allowed if recurrence occurred 6 months after completion; prior oxaliplatin not allowed Ⓐ Panitumumab 6 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks on day 1 before FOLFOX4 (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² IV day 1; leucovorin 200 mg/m² IV then fluorouracil 400 mg/m² IV bolus and 600 mg/m² 22-hour continuous infusion days 1 and 2; every 2 weeks)
Ⓑ FOLFOX4 alone
・Duration: Until progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, resection rate, safety, antipanitumumab antibodies, patient-reported outcomes In WT KRAS mCRC, panitumumab plus FOLFOX4 improved PFS vs FOLFOX4 alone; OS improvement was not significant
・PFS: Ⓐ 9.6 vs Ⓑ 8.0 mo (WT KRAS); HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.66-0.97)
・OS: Ⓐ 23.9 vs Ⓑ 19.7 mo (WT KRAS); HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.67-1.02), not statistically significant
・Subgroups: MT KRAS: PFS inferior with panitumumab; Ⓐ 7.3 vs Ⓑ 8.8 mo; HR 1.29 (95% CI 1.04-1.62)
・Subgroups: MT KRAS: OS Ⓐ 15.5 vs Ⓑ 19.3 mo; HR 1.24 (95% CI 0.98-1.57)
・Toxicity: WT KRAS: grade 3/4 treatment-related AEs Ⓐ 82% vs Ⓑ 63%; skin toxicity Ⓐ 36% vs Ⓑ 2%; diarrhoea Ⓐ 18% vs Ⓑ 9%; fatal AEs Ⓐ 5% vs Ⓑ 6% (2 panitumumab-related: pneumonitis, pneumonia)
・Toxicity: MT KRAS: fatal AEs Ⓐ 8% vs Ⓑ 3%
・Limitations: KRAS status determined in only 93% of randomised patients
records.keywords: Douillard et al. J Clin Oncol 2010;28:4697-4705  20921465

records.title: FIRE-3
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Anti-EGFR therapy & primary tumour sidedness (RAS wild-type) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2014
records.body:
Stage IV histologically confirmed adenocarcinoma of the colon or rectum; first-line, no previous chemotherapy except adjuvant therapy completed at least 6 months before; KRAS exon 2 (codon 12/13) wild-type, restricted by protocol amendment; age 18–75 years, ECOG 0–2, ≥1 RECIST measurable lesion; excluded known/suspected brain metastases, previous EGFR-targeting agent or bevacizumab Ⓐ FOLFIRI (irinotecan 180 mg/m², folinic acid 400 mg/m², fluorouracil 400 mg/m² bolus then 2400 mg/m² over 46 h) on day 1 of each 14-day cycle + cetuximab 400 mg/m² initially then 250 mg/m² weekly
Ⓑ FOLFIRI + bevacizumab 5 mg/kg every 2 weeks
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, complete response, resectability or withdrawal Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall survival, depth of remission, secondary resection of liver metastases with curative intent, safety and tolerability, complete response rate FOLFIRI-cetuximab did not improve ORR or PFS vs FOLFIRI-bevacizumab, but secondary OS was longer with cetuximab
・ORR (missed primary): Ⓐ 62% vs Ⓑ 58%; OR 1·18 (95% CI 0·85–1·64)
・PFS: Ⓐ 10·0 vs Ⓑ 10·3 mo; HR 1·06
・OS: Ⓐ 28·7 vs Ⓑ 25·0 mo; HR 0·77 (95% CI 0·62–0·96)
・Subgroups: RAS wild-type OS Ⓐ 33·1 vs Ⓑ 25·6 mo; HR 0·70 (95% CI 0·53–0·92), similar response and PFS; other RAS-mutant PFS Ⓐ 6·1 vs Ⓑ 12·2 mo; HR 2·22, favouring bevacizumab
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 AEs Ⓐ 71% vs Ⓑ 64%; grade ≥3 skin reactions Ⓐ 26% vs Ⓑ 2%; discontinuation for drug-related toxicity Ⓐ 15% vs Ⓑ 11%; five AE-related deaths, all with bevacizumab (two treatment-related)
・Limitations: Secondary endpoints exploratory; OS events few with wide CIs; open-label without independent radiological review

records.title: CALGB/SWOG 80405
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Anti-EGFR therapy & primary tumour sidedness (RAS wild-type) · Randomised clinical trial · 2017
records.body:
Previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic colorectal cancer; first-line; KRAS wild-type (codons 12 and 13), centrally confirmed; candidates for mFOLFOX6 or FOLFIRI, prior adjuvant therapy ≤6 months concluded ≥12 months before recurrence; excluded known CNS metastases, grade ≥II peripheral neuropathy, BP ≥160/90 mm Hg on treatment, congestive heart failure, significant bleeding within 6 months, GI perforation within 12 months unless resected Ⓐ Cetuximab 400 mg/m² IV day 1, then 250 mg/m² every week + chemotherapy
Ⓑ Bevacizumab 5 mg/kg IV every other week + chemotherapy
・Chemotherapy: mFOLFOX6 (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m²) or FOLFIRI (irinotecan 180 mg/m²), each with leucovorin 400 mg/m², fluorouracil 400 mg/m² bolus then 2400 mg/m² over 46–48 h, every 2 weeks; chosen by patient and physician before randomisation
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxic effects, a gap of more than 28 days between treatments, or decision to discontinue Primary: overall survival. Secondary: response rate, progression-free survival, 60-day mortality, arterial thrombotic events, adverse events Cetuximab vs bevacizumab added to first-line chemotherapy gave no significant OS difference in KRAS wt advanced colorectal cancer
・OS: Ⓐ 30.0 vs Ⓑ 29.0 mo; HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.77–1.01)
・PFS: Ⓐ 10.5 vs Ⓑ 10.6 mo; HR 0.95 (95% CI 0.84–1.08); exploratory
・ORR: Ⓐ 59.6% vs Ⓑ 55.2%; P = .13; exploratory
・60-day mortality: Ⓐ 2.0% vs Ⓑ 1.4%; P = .50
・Subgroups: Post hoc; OS HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.71–0.98) with mFOLFOX6, 1.04 (95% CI 0.79–1.35) with FOLFIRI; interaction P = .11
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs 53%, G≥4 14% overall; deaths on therapy Ⓐ 15 vs Ⓑ 16; acneiform rash with Ⓐ, hypertension with Ⓑ
・Limitations: Chemotherapy backbone chosen, not randomised; secondary endpoints not adjusted for multiplicity; subsequent therapy not captured

records.title: PARADIGM
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Anti-EGFR therapy & primary tumour sidedness (RAS wild-type) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body:
Unresectable metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma; first line, no prior chemotherapy for metastatic disease; KRAS/NRAS wild-type (exons 2, 3, 4); age 20 to 79 years; enrolled regardless of tumor side, primary analysis in left-sided primaries (descending colon, sigmoid colon, rectosigmoid, rectum); excluded: prior (neo)adjuvant oxaliplatin (fluoropyrimidine alone allowed if completed ≥24 weeks before), brain metastases, synchronous/metachronous cancers Ⓐ Panitumumab 6 mg/kg IV day 1 + mFOLFOX6 (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², l-leucovorin 200 mg/m², fluorouracil 400 mg/m² bolus day 1, then 2400 mg/m² continuous infusion days 1-3) every 14 days
Ⓑ Bevacizumab 5 mg/kg IV day 1 + the same mFOLFOX6 every 14 days
・Duration: Until progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal, physician decision or curative-intent surgery Primary: overall survival (left-sided tumors, then overall population). Secondary: progression-free survival, response rate, duration of response, curative (R0) resection rate, adverse events, early tumor shrinkage, depth of response, disease control rate, time to treatment failure Panitumumab plus mFOLFOX6 improved OS versus bevacizumab plus mFOLFOX6 in RAS wild-type left-sided and overall populations
・OS (left-sided): Ⓐ 37.9 vs Ⓑ 34.3 mo; HR 0.82 (95.798% CI 0.68-0.99)
・OS (overall): Ⓐ 36.2 vs Ⓑ 31.3 mo; HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.72-0.98); median follow-up 61 mo
・PFS (left-sided): Ⓐ 13.1 vs Ⓑ 11.9 mo; HR 1.00; did not differ
・ORR/R0 (exploratory): ORR Ⓐ 80.2% vs Ⓑ 68.6%; R0 resection Ⓐ 18.3% vs Ⓑ 11.6%
・Subgroups: Right-sided (exploratory) OS Ⓐ 20.2 vs Ⓑ 23.2 mo; HR 1.09
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 AEs Ⓐ 71.8% vs Ⓑ 64.9%; treatment-related deaths 10 (Ⓐ, 4 interstitial lung disease) vs 2 (Ⓑ); acne-like dermatitis Ⓐ 74.8% vs Ⓑ 3.2%
・Limitations: OS curves crossed at ~28 mo, so HRs are hard to interpret; left-sided population defined after enrollment; Japan-only enrollment

records.title: VELOUR
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Second-line & antiangiogenic continuation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2012
records.body:
Metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma not amenable to potentially curative treatment; progression on or after a single prior oxaliplatin-containing regimen, including relapse within 6 months of oxaliplatin-based adjuvant therapy; ECOG PS 0 to 2, prior bevacizumab permitted, measurable disease not required; excluded prior irinotecan, known brain metastases, uncontrolled hypertension within 3 months Ⓐ Aflibercept 4 mg/kg IV day 1 every 2 weeks, followed immediately by FOLFIRI (irinotecan 180 mg/m², leucovorin 400 mg/m², FU 400 mg/m² bolus then 2400 mg/m² over 46 hours)
Ⓑ Placebo plus the same FOLFIRI
・Design: Double-blind
・Duration: Until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response, treatment-emergent adverse events, laboratory abnormalities Aflibercept plus FOLFIRI improved OS over placebo plus FOLFIRI in oxaliplatin-pretreated mCRC
・OS: Ⓐ 13.50 vs Ⓑ 12.06 mo; HR 0.817 (95.34% CI 0.713 to 0.937)
・PFS: Ⓐ 6.90 vs Ⓑ 4.67 mo; HR 0.758 (95% CI 0.661 to 0.869)
・ORR: Ⓐ 19.8% vs Ⓑ 11.1% among patients with measurable disease
・Subgroups: OS and PFS benefit consistent across stratification subgroups including prior bevacizumab, no significant interaction
・Toxicity: Grade 3-4 AEs Ⓐ 83.5% vs Ⓑ 62.5%; grade 3 hypertension Ⓐ 19.1% vs Ⓑ 1.5%; grade 3-4 diarrhea Ⓐ 19.3% vs Ⓑ 7.8%, neutropenia Ⓐ 36.7% vs Ⓑ 29.5%, proteinuria Ⓐ 7.9% vs Ⓑ 1.2%; AE-related discontinuation Ⓐ 26.8% vs Ⓑ 12.1%
records.keywords: Van Cutsem et al. J Clin Oncol 2012;30:3499-3506  22949147

records.title: ML18147
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Second-line & antiangiogenic continuation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2013
records.body:
Unresectable, histologically confirmed, measurable metastatic colorectal cancer; second line after progression on first-line bevacizumab plus fluoropyrimidine with oxaliplatin or irinotecan; progression up to 3 months after discontinuing first-line bevacizumab, not candidates for primary metastasectomy, ECOG 0–2; excluded: first-line PFS <3 months or <3 months (consecutive) of first-line bevacizumab Ⓐ Second-line fluorouracil (infusional or bolus) or oral capecitabine plus irinotecan or oxaliplatin (switched from the first-line partner) plus bevacizumab 2·5 mg/kg per week equivalent (5 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks or 7·5 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks)
Ⓑ The same chemotherapy alone
・Duration: Until progressive disease, unacceptable toxicity or patient refusal
・Design: Open-label Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall survival from start of first-line treatment, confirmed best overall response, safety, on-treatment progression-free survival, disease control, overall survival and progression-free survival by KRAS status, subsequent anticancer treatment by KRAS status Continuing bevacizumab with switched second-line chemotherapy improved OS and PFS vs chemotherapy alone in metastatic colorectal cancer
・OS: Ⓐ 11·2 vs Ⓑ 9·8 mo; HR 0·81 (95% CI 0·69–0·94); p=0·0062
・PFS: Ⓐ 5·7 vs Ⓑ 4·1 mo; HR 0·68 (95% CI 0·59–0·78)
・ORR: Confirmed response rates low, Ⓐ 5% vs Ⓑ 4%; p=0·31
・OS (from start of first-line, retrospective): Ⓐ vs Ⓑ did not differ significantly; HR 0·90 (95% CI 0·77–1·05)
・Subgroups: Exploratory KRAS analysis found no treatment-by-KRAS interaction
・Toxicity: Grade 3–5 AEs Ⓐ 64% vs Ⓑ 57%; bleeding Ⓐ 2% vs Ⓑ <1%; GI perforation Ⓐ 2% vs Ⓑ <1%; venous thromboembolism Ⓐ 5% vs Ⓑ 3%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ four vs Ⓑ three
・Limitations: Open-label design; primary endpoint changed from PFS to OS during the study

records.title: RAISE
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Second-line & antiangiogenic continuation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2015
records.body:
Metastatic colorectal carcinoma; second line after progression during or within 6 months of last dose of first-line bevacizumab + oxaliplatin + fluoropyrimidine (at least one cycle); known KRAS exon 2 status (mutant or wild-type); excluded brain metastases, poorly controlled hypertension, arterial thromboembolism within 12 months or during first line, and grade 4 hypertension, grade 3 proteinuria, grade 3–4 bleeding or bowel perforation during first line Ⓐ Ramucirumab 8 mg/kg IV + FOLFIRI (irinotecan 180 mg/m², leucovorin 400 mg/m², fluorouracil 400 mg/m² bolus then 2400 mg/m² over 48 h) on day 1 every 2 weeks
Ⓑ Placebo + same FOLFIRI
・Design: Double-blind
・Duration: Until radiographic progression, unacceptable toxicity, death or patient/physician decision Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, adverse events, patient-reported outcomes (EORTC QLQ-C30, EQ-5D) Ramucirumab plus FOLFIRI improved OS vs placebo plus FOLFIRI as second-line therapy for metastatic colorectal carcinoma
・OS: Ⓐ 13.3 vs Ⓑ 11.7 mo (median follow-up 21.7 mo); HR 0.844 (95% CI 0.730–0.976); p=0.0219
・PFS: Ⓐ 5.7 vs Ⓑ 4.5 mo; HR 0.793 (95% CI 0.697–0.903); p=0.0005
・ORR: Ⓐ 13.4% vs Ⓑ 12.5%; p=0.63
・Subgroups: Numerically favoured ramucirumab; trial not powered for subgroup analysis
・Toxicity: G≥3 TEAEs Ⓐ 79% vs Ⓑ 62%, including neutropenia (Ⓐ 38% vs Ⓑ 23%; febrile neutropenia Ⓐ 3% vs Ⓑ 2%) and hypertension (Ⓐ 11% vs Ⓑ 3%); discontinuation for AEs Ⓐ 11% vs Ⓑ 4%; deaths possibly related to study drug Ⓐ eight vs Ⓑ five, including intestinal perforations and haemorrhage with ramucirumab

records.title: CORRECT
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Refractory disease — oral cytotoxics & multikinase inhibitors · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2013
records.body:
Metastatic adenocarcinoma of the colon or rectum; progression during or within 3 months after the last standard therapy (or stopped for unacceptable toxicity) after all locally approved standard therapies, including as many as licensed of a fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin, irinotecan, bevacizumab and, for KRAS wild-type, cetuximab or panitumumab; ECOG 0 or 1, life expectancy ≥3 months; excluded prior regorafenib or uncontrolled medical disorders Ⓐ Best supportive care + oral regorafenib 160 mg once daily for the first 3 weeks of each 4-week cycle
Ⓑ Best supportive care + matching placebo on the same schedule
・Duration: Until disease progression, death, unacceptable toxicity, consent withdrawal or physician decision
・Design: Double-masked Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, safety, duration of response, duration of stable disease, health-related quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30), EQ-5D health utility Regorafenib plus best supportive care improved overall survival vs placebo in metastatic colorectal cancer after all standard therapies
・OS: Ⓐ 6·4 vs Ⓑ 5·0 mo; HR 0·77 (95% CI 0·64–0·94; one-sided p=0·0052); second planned interim analysis
・PFS: Ⓐ 1·9 vs Ⓑ 1·7 mo; HR 0·49 (95% CI 0·42–0·58)
・ORR: Ⓐ 1·0% vs Ⓑ 0·4% (p=0·19)
・Disease control: Ⓐ 41% vs Ⓑ 15%
・QoL: Deterioration similar in both groups
・Subgroups: Exploratory OS HR 0·70 for colon vs 0·95 (95% CI 0·63–1·43) for rectal primaries
・Toxicity: Grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs Ⓐ 54% vs Ⓑ 14%; grade ≥3 hand-foot skin reaction 17%, fatigue 10%, diarrhoea 7%, hypertension 7%; one fatal regorafenib-related drug-induced liver injury; dose modification Ⓐ 67% vs Ⓑ 23%

records.title: CONCUR
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Refractory disease — oral cytotoxics & multikinase inhibitors · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2015
records.body:
Asian adults with metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma; ≥2 prior lines including a fluoropyrimidine plus oxaliplatin or irinotecan, or intolerant of standard treatment; prior bevacizumab, cetuximab or panitumumab allowed but not required; progression during or within 3 months after last standard treatment (or within 6 months of stopping adjuvant oxaliplatin), ECOG 0–1, life expectancy ≥3 months; excluded uncontrolled medical disorders Ⓐ Regorafenib 160 mg orally once daily on days 1–21 of each 28-day cycle + best supportive care
Ⓑ Matching placebo + best supportive care
・Duration: Until disease progression, death, unacceptable toxicity, consent withdrawal or physician decision
・Design: Double-blind Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, duration of response, duration of stable disease, health-related quality of life, safety Regorafenib improved overall survival vs placebo in Asian patients with treatment-refractory metastatic colorectal cancer
・OS: Ⓐ 8.8 vs Ⓑ 6.3 mo; HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.40–0.77); one-sided p=0.00016; median follow-up 7.4 mo
・PFS: Ⓐ 3.2 vs Ⓑ 1.7 mo; HR 0.31
・ORR: Ⓐ 4% (all partial) vs Ⓑ none
・Disease control: Ⓐ 51% vs Ⓑ 7%
・Subgroups: Exploratory, unstratified; OS HR 0.31 (95% CI 0.19–0.53) without prior targeted therapy vs 0.78 (95% CI 0.51–1.19) with it
・QoL: Declined to a similar extent in both groups
・Toxicity: Drug-related G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 54% vs Ⓑ 15%, mainly hand–foot skin reaction (16%) and hypertension (11%) with regorafenib; two drug-related deaths (cardiac arrests) on regorafenib; discontinuation due to AEs Ⓐ 14% vs Ⓑ 6%
・Limitations: Preceding treatments did not necessarily include targeted agents

records.title: RECOURSE
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Refractory disease — oral cytotoxics & multikinase inhibitors · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2015
records.body:
Biopsy-documented adenocarcinoma of the colon or rectum, metastatic; refractory after at least two prior standard chemotherapy regimens (adjuvant counted if recurrence within 6 months), with progression within 3 months of last chemotherapy or intolerance precluding re-treatment; known KRAS status; prior fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin, irinotecan, bevacizumab and, if KRAS wild-type, cetuximab or panitumumab required; ECOG 0 or 1 Ⓐ TAS-102 (oral trifluridine/tipiracil) 35 mg per square meter twice daily, 5 days a week with 2 days rest for 2 weeks, then a 14-day rest, repeated every 4 weeks
Ⓑ Placebo on the same schedule
・BSC: Plus best supportive care
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal or physician decision
・Design: Double-blind Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, response rate, disease control rate, safety, time to worsening of ECOG performance status TAS-102 improved overall survival vs placebo in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer
・OS: Ⓐ 7.1 vs Ⓑ 5.3 mo; HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.58–0.81); P<0.001
・1-yr OS: Ⓐ 27% vs Ⓑ 18%
・PFS: Ⓐ 2.0 vs Ⓑ 1.7 mo; HR 0.48 (95% CI 0.41–0.57)
・Disease control: Ⓐ 44% vs Ⓑ 16%
・ORR: Ⓐ 1.6% vs Ⓑ 0.4%; P=0.29, not significant
・Time to ECOG PS≥2: Ⓐ 5.7 vs Ⓑ 4.0 mo; HR 0.66
・Toxicity: Grade≥3 AEs Ⓐ 69% vs Ⓑ 52%; with TAS-102, neutropenia 38%, anemia 18%, febrile neutropenia 4%, one treatment-related death from septic shock
records.keywords: Mayer et al. N Engl J Med 2015;372:1909-1919  25970050

records.title: SUNLIGHT
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Refractory disease — oral cytotoxics & multikinase inhibitors · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body:
Histologically confirmed unresectable adenocarcinoma of the colon or rectum; refractory metastatic disease after no more than two previous chemotherapy regimens for advanced disease, with progression or unacceptable adverse effects (adjuvant therapy counted if recurrence during or within 6 months); previous fluoropyrimidine, irinotecan, oxaliplatin, anti-VEGF antibody (not necessarily bevacizumab) or anti-EGFR antibody (if RAS wild-type); known RAS status required; ECOG 0 or 1 Ⓐ FTD–TPI 35 mg per square meter orally twice daily on days 1–5 and 8–12 plus bevacizumab 5 mg/kg IV on days 1 and 15, every 28 days
Ⓑ FTD–TPI alone on the same schedule
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or consent withdrawal
・Note: Bevacizumab monotherapy not allowed Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response, disease control, quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30, EQ-5D-5L), safety, time to worsening of ECOG performance status from 0 or 1 to 2 or more Adding bevacizumab to FTD–TPI prolonged overall survival vs FTD–TPI alone in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer
・OS: Ⓐ 10.8 vs Ⓑ 7.5 mo; HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.49–0.77); P<0.001
・12-mo OS: Ⓐ 43% vs Ⓑ 30%
・PFS: Ⓐ 5.6 vs Ⓑ 2.4 mo; HR 0.44 (95% CI 0.36–0.54); P<0.001
・ORR: Ⓐ 6.1% vs Ⓑ 1.2%
・Time to ECOG worsening to ≥2: Ⓐ 9.3 vs Ⓑ 6.3 mo; HR 0.54
・QoL: QLQ-C30/EQ-5D-5L maintained to cycle 6 without clinically relevant change in either arm; time to GHS deterioration Ⓐ 8.54 vs Ⓑ 4.70 mo; HR 0.50
・Subgroups: OS and PFS benefit seen in all subgroups examined (CIs not adjusted for multiplicity)

records.title: FRESCO-2
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Refractory disease — oral cytotoxics & multikinase inhibitors · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body:
Refractory metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma; previously treated with all standard therapies (fluoropyrimidine, oxaliplatin, irinotecan, anti-VEGF, anti-EGFR if RAS wild type) and progressed on or intolerant to trifluridine–tipiracil or regorafenib, or both; RAS, BRAF and MSI/MMR status documented, with prior immune-checkpoint inhibitor required for dMMR/MSI-H and BRAF inhibitor for BRAFV600E-mutant tumours, if approved and available; ECOG 0–1, RECIST 1.1 measurable disease Ⓐ Fruquintinib 5 mg orally once daily on days 1–21 of 28-day cycles plus best supportive care
Ⓑ Matched placebo plus best supportive care
・Design: Double-blind
・Duration: Until disease progression, death, unacceptable toxicity, consent withdrawal, physician discontinuation or study completion Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, duration of response, safety, health-related quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30, EQ-5D-5L), health-care resource utilisation, population pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics Fruquintinib improved overall survival vs placebo in refractory metastatic colorectal cancer, meeting primary and key secondary endpoints
・OS: Ⓐ 7·4 vs Ⓑ 4·8 mo; HR 0·66 (95% CI 0·55–0·80); p<0·0001; median follow-up 11·3 vs 11·2 mo
・PFS: Ⓐ 3·7 vs Ⓑ 1·8 mo; HR 0·32 (95% CI 0·27–0·39)
・ORR: Ⓐ 2% vs Ⓑ 0%; p=0·059; no complete responses; DCR 56% vs 16%
・Subgroups: OS and PFS benefit consistent across nearly all prespecified subgroups
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 63% vs Ⓑ 50% (fruquintinib: hypertension 14%, asthenia 8%, hand-foot syndrome 6%); dose reductions for AEs 24% vs 4%; 1 treatment-related death per arm (intestinal perforation with fruquintinib)
・Toxicity (AESI analysis): Treatment-related AESIs 64.9% vs 23.0% (grade ≥3 24.1% vs 3.0%); treatment-related GI perforation 1.3%, all grade ≥3; discontinuation for treatment-related AESIs 5.9% vs 0.9%
・Limitations: Quality-of-life results not yet reported

records.title: ReDOS
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Refractory disease — oral cytotoxics & multikinase inhibitors · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2019
records.body:
Advanced or metastatic adenocarcinoma of the colon or rectum with no curative options; refractory, progressed on irinotecan, oxaliplatin, fluoropyrimidines and a VEGF inhibitor, plus anti-EGFR therapy if KRAS wild-type; ECOG 0–1, no prior regorafenib; excluded heart failure worse than NYHA class II, MI or unstable angina <6 months, uncontrolled hypertension, thrombotic or embolic events, hepatitis B or C, symptomatic brain or meningeal metastases Ⓐ Regorafenib dose escalation: 80 mg/day in week 1, 120 mg/day in week 2 and 160 mg/day in week 3 of cycle 1 if no significant drug-related toxicity, then the highest tolerated cycle 1 dose in later cycles
Ⓑ Regorafenib standard dose 160 mg/day from day 1
・Schedule: Both oral for 21 consecutive days of each 28-day cycle
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or consent withdrawal, and stopped if the dose had to fall below 80 mg, if toxicity required more than 4 weeks' delay or if more than two dose-level reductions were needed
・Design: Patients were also randomised to pre-emptive or reactive 0·05% clobetasol cream twice daily to palms and soles (clobetasol groups pooled for analysis) Primary: proportion of patients completing two cycles and initiating cycle 3. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall survival, time to progression, cumulative dose, dose intensity, grade 3 hand-foot skin reaction, grade 3 fatigue, quality of life (HFS-14, BFI, LASA), safety Dose escalation increased cycle 3 initiation versus standard dosing, meeting the trial's primary endpoint
・Cycle 3 initiation: Ⓐ 43% vs Ⓑ 26%; one-sided p=0·043 (prespecified threshold p<0·2)
・OS: Ⓐ 9·8 vs Ⓑ 6·0 mo; HR 0·72 (95% CI 0·47–1·10); not significant
・PFS: Ⓐ 2·8 vs Ⓑ 2·0 mo; HR 0·84 (95% CI 0·57–1·24); similar

・Limitations: Survival analyses not powered for non-inferiority; small randomised phase 2 trial; clobetasol groups pooled for analysis

records.title: STELLAR-303

records.body:

・Design: Open-label; treatment beyond radiographic progression allowed per investigator Primary: overall survival, overall survival in patients without liver metastases. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, sum of target lesion diameters, disease control rate, duration of response, overall survival in patients with liver metastases, plasma concentration of zanzalintinib, serum concentration of atezolizumab, antidrug antibody response against atezolizumab, safety Zanzalintinib–atezolizumab improved ITT overall survival vs regorafenib in relapsed/refractory non-MSI-H/dMMR metastatic colorectal cancer

records.title: PARERE

records.title: BEACON CRC

BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer after 1-2 prior regimens; centrally confirmed BRAF V600E; no prior BRAF, MEK or EGFR inhibitors Ⓐ Encorafenib 300 mg daily + binimetinib 45 mg twice daily + cetuximab 400 mg/m² then 250 mg/m² weekly

Secondary: overall survival with doublet therapy, progression-free survival, duration of response, safety, ORR for doublet vs triplet, OS for doublet vs triplet Encorafenib+binimetinib+cetuximab and encorafenib+cetuximab each improved OS and response rate versus cetuximab+irinotecan-based chemotherapy at prespecified interim analysis

records.title: MOUNTAINEER
records.subtitle: Advanced CRC · Other actionable drivers (HER2, KRAS G12C) · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2023
records.body:
Chemotherapy-refractory HER2-positive, RAS wild-type unresectable or metastatic colorectal cancer; previously treated with fluoropyrimidines, oxaliplatin, irinotecan, an anti-VEGF antibody and anti-PD-1/PD-L1 if dMMR/MSI-high (anti-EGFR not required); local HER2 positivity: IHC 3+, IHC 2+ with FISH/CISH amplification, or NGS amplification; ECOG 0–2; excluded prior HER2-directed therapy, LVEF <50% Ⓐ Tucatinib 300 mg orally twice daily plus trastuzumab 8 mg/kg IV loading dose then 6 mg/kg every 21 days until progression, death or intolerable toxicity (cohort A, non-randomised; cohort B, randomised)

Secondary: duration of response, objective response rate at 12 weeks, progression-free survival, overall survival, tucatinib monotherapy objective response rate by 12 weeks, tucatinib monotherapy duration of response, EORTC QLQ-C30, safety Tucatinib plus trastuzumab showed durable antitumour activity in chemotherapy-refractory HER2-positive, RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer

・OS: Ⓐ 24.1 mo

records.body:

Secondary: progression-free survival, adverse events, serious adverse events, treatment-related complications, unplanned readmissions, 90-day mortality, OS and PFS by extent of debulking, OS and PFS by primary tumor sidedness and BRAF/RAS status Adding tumor debulking to first-line chemotherapy did not improve OS in multiorgan mCRC

records.title: ASAC

Colorectal cancer liver metastases; adjuvant setting after curative-intent treatment by resection (macroscopically free margin, R0/R1), ablation, or both; no radiological evidence of residual disease at inclusion, ambulatory and candidates for oral treatment; excluded contraindications to aspirin, clinically relevant bleeding risk, ongoing aspirin or incompatible antithrombotic therapy Ⓐ Aspirin 160 mg orally once daily
Ⓑ Matching placebo

・Start: Approximately 4 weeks after surgery following postoperative low-molecular-weight heparin thromboprophylaxis
・Duration: Until the 36-month visit, disease recurrence, or death (up to 3 years) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, time to recurrence, safety, health-related quality of life, disease-free survival by PIK3CA and KRAS mutation status Adjuvant aspirin did not improve disease-free survival in resected colorectal liver metastases and was associated with lower overall survival
・DFS: Ⓐ 1.13 vs Ⓑ 1.40 yr; HR 1.08 (95.44% CI 0.85–1.38; p=0.58)
・OS (36-mo): Ⓐ 76% vs Ⓑ 85%; HR 1.64 (95% CI 1.01–2.65; p=0.045); secondary endpoint, underpowered, not adjusted for multiplicity
・Time to recurrence: Did not differ; HR 1.06
・Subgroups: No benefit signal in exploratory PIK3CA-mutated (HR 0.91, n=47) or KRAS subgroups
・Toxicity: Serious AEs Ⓐ 8% vs Ⓑ 2%; myocardial infarction, duodenal ulcer, cerebral haemorrhage Ⓐ 2 vs Ⓑ 0 each; no treatment-related deaths
・Limitations: Enrolment stopped before planned sample size once target events reached
records.keywords: Yaqub et al. Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2026 (online ahead of print)  42777749

records.title: MAGIC
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2006
records.body: Adenocarcinoma of the stomach or lower third of the oesophagus, including the oesophagogastric junction; resectable, potentially curable disease; stage II (through the submucosa) or higher with no evidence of distant metastases or locally advanced inoperable disease, WHO PS 0 or 1, any age; lower-oesophageal tumours added in 1999; excluded prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy, uncontrolled cardiac disease, creatinine clearance ≤60 ml/min Perioperative ECF: 3 cycles preoperatively → surgery (three to six weeks after cycle 3) → 3 cycles postoperatively (starting 6 to 12 weeks after surgery); each 3-week cycle epirubicin 50 mg per square meter IV bolus day 1 + cisplatin 60 mg per square meter IV day 1 + fluorouracil 200 mg per square meter/day continuous IV infusion for 21 days vs surgery alone (within six weeks of randomization) Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, tumour diameter, tumour stage, nodal status, surgeon-assessed curative resection, quality of life, postoperative complications, safety Compared with surgery alone, perioperative ECF reduced the size and stage of resected tumours and significantly improved overall and progression-free survival in operable gastric or lower oesophageal adenocarcinoma. OS HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.60–0.93; P=0.009); five-year survival 36% vs 23% at a median follow-up of four years; PFS HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.53–0.81). The surgeon judged resection curative in 79.3% vs 70.3% of patients who had radical surgery. Only 104 of 250 (41.6%) patients assigned to chemotherapy completed all six cycles, and the effects of the pre- and postoperative parts cannot be separated. Postoperative complications were 46% vs 45%, with similar 30-day deaths. Grade 3/4 granulocytopenia occurred in 23.8% of patients preoperatively and 27.8% postoperatively. Of 237 patients who started chemotherapy, 4 died within 60 days (2 from cardiac causes).
records.keywords: Cunningham et al. N Engl J Med 2006;355:11-20  16822992

records.title: ACCORD-07 (FFCD 9703)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2011
records.body: Histologically proven adenocarcinoma of the lower third of the esophagus, GEJ or stomach; judged suitable for curative resection (perioperative setting); age 18–75 years, WHO PS 0 or 1; originally limited to lower esophagus/GEJ, with stomach added in 1998; excluded in situ carcinoma, non-adenocarcinoma histology, prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy Perioperative cisplatin 100 mg/m² IV (1-hour) day 1 + fluorouracil 800 mg/m²/d continuous IV infusion days 1 to 5 every 28 days: two or three preoperative cycles → surgery 4 to 6 weeks after the last cycle → 3 to 4 postoperative cycles if well tolerated and no progression (total 6 cycles) vs surgery alone within 4 weeks of randomization; surgery was complete excision with extended lymphadenectomy (D2 recommended) Primary: overall survival. Secondary: disease-free survival, R0 resection rate, safety, postoperative morbidity, postoperative mortality Perioperative fluorouracil plus cisplatin significantly improved OS, DFS and curative resection rate vs surgery alone in resectable adenocarcinoma of the lower esophagus, GEJ or stomach. 5-yr OS 38% vs 24% (HR 0.69; 95% CI 0.50–0.95); 5-yr DFS 34% vs 19% (HR 0.65; 95% CI 0.48–0.89; 6-month landmark); ITT R0 resection 84% vs 74%; median follow-up 5.7 yr. The planned sample size was not reached, and only 50% of the 109 chemotherapy-treated patients received postoperative chemotherapy. Benefit was significant only in the GEJ subgroup (about two thirds of patients); other sites were too small to assess, and there was no significant variation by site. Grade 3–4 toxicity occurred in 38% of treated patients (neutropenia 20.2%), with one drug-related death (acute renal failure); postoperative morbidity (25.7% vs 19.1%) and mortality (4.6% vs 4.5%) were similar.
records.keywords: Ychou et al. J Clin Oncol 2011;29:1715-1721  21444866

records.title: CRITICS
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body: Resectable gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (Siewert types II and III, bulk predominantly in stomach); stage IB–IVA (AJCC sixth edition), randomised before preoperative chemotherapy; no previous radiotherapy or chemotherapy affecting gastric cancer treatment, WHO performance status 0 or 1; excluded Siewert type I, T1N0 tumours by endoscopic ultrasound, previous malignancy Three preoperative 21-day cycles of epirubicin 50 mg/m² IV day 1 plus cisplatin 60 mg/m² IV day 1 (with capecitabine 1000 mg/m² orally twice daily for 14 days) or oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1 (with capecitabine 625 mg/m² orally twice daily for 21 days) → radical resection with at least D1+ lymph node dissection → three postoperative cycles of the same regimen vs the same preoperative chemotherapy → surgery → chemoradiotherapy 45 Gy in 25 fractions of 1·8 Gy over 5 weeks with capecitabine 575 mg/m² orally twice daily on radiotherapy days and cisplatin 20 mg/m² IV on day 1 of each of the 5 weeks; postoperative treatment started within 4–12 weeks after surgery Primary: overall survival. Secondary: event-free survival, toxicity, health-related quality of life, prediction of response and recurrence risk by genomic and proteomic profiling, Maruyama Index, predictive nomograms for disease recurrence, postoperative complications, pathological outcomes, treatment compliance Postoperative chemoradiotherapy did not improve overall survival compared with postoperative chemotherapy after preoperative chemotherapy and adequate surgery, and tolerability was similar; given poor postoperative compliance, the authors propose optimising preoperative treatment. At a median follow-up of 61·4 mo, median OS was 43 mo (95% CI 31–57) with chemotherapy vs 37 mo (30–48) with chemoradiotherapy; HR 1·01 (95% CI 0·84–1·22), p=0·90; 5-year OS 42% vs 40%. Median EFS was 28 vs 25 mo; HR 0·99 (0·82–1·19). Only 180 (46%) of 393 vs 197 (50%) of 395 completed the allocated treatment. A significant sex-by-treatment interaction appeared in a post-hoc subgroup analysis; its reason is unclear. During preoperative chemotherapy (n=781): grade 3 AEs 47%, grade 4 17%, 13 (2%) deaths. Postoperative grade 3 AEs 48% vs 41% and grade 4 9% vs 4%; grade 3–4 non-febrile neutropenia 34% vs 4%; no deaths during postoperative treatment.

records.title: FLOT4
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase II/III) · 2019
records.body: Histologically confirmed gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (GEJ classified by Siewert); locally advanced, resectable disease for perioperative chemotherapy; clinical stage cT2 or higher, nodal positive (cN+), or both (UICC TNM 7th edition); no clinical evidence of distant metastases Perioperative ECF/ECX: epirubicin 50 mg/m² d1 + cisplatin 60 mg/m² d1 + fluorouracil 200 mg/m² continuous IV infusion d1–21 or capecitabine 1250 mg/m² orally d1–21 (investigator's choice), three preoperative → surgery → three postoperative 3-week cycles vs perioperative FLOT: docetaxel 50 mg/m² + oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + leucovorin 200 mg/m² + fluorouracil 2600 mg/m² 24-h infusion, all d1, four preoperative → surgery → four postoperative 2-week cycles; therapy stopped early for unacceptable toxicity, progression, death or patient request Primary: overall survival. Secondary: margin-free (R0) resection rate, disease-free survival, surgical morbidity, surgical mortality, adverse events, pathological ypT and ypN stage Perioperative FLOT improved overall survival vs perioperative ECF/ECX in locally advanced, resectable gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma. Median OS FLOT vs ECF/ECX was 50 vs 35 mo (HR 0·77; 95% CI 0·63–0·94; p=0·012), with median follow-up of 43 mo; estimated 3-yr OS 57% vs 48% and 5-yr OS 45% vs 36% (5-yr rates are estimates that could change with longer follow-up). Median DFS 30 vs 18 mo (HR 0·75; 95% CI 0·62–0·91); R0 resection 85% vs 78%. The primary endpoint was changed from DFS to OS during the trial. Only 46% vs 37% completed all allocated cycles. FLOT had more grade 3–4 neutropenia (51% vs 39%), infections (18% vs 9%), diarrhoea (10% vs 4%) and neuropathy (7% vs 2%), and less grade 3–4 nausea (7% vs 16%). Treatment-related serious adverse events (27% in each arm) and toxic deaths (2 per arm) were similar.

records.title: PRODIGY
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body: Newly histologically confirmed gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma in Korean patients; resectable locally advanced disease before any treatment, cT2-3N1 or cT4Nany (AJCC 7th) on centrally reviewed CT, node-positive if short axis ≥8 mm or shortest diameter ≥5 mm with central necrosis, round shape, perinodal infiltration or prominent enhancement; age 20-75, ECOG PS 0-1; excluded distant metastasis including distant nodes, prior gastric cancer surgery or chemo/radiotherapy, or not curatively resectable Neoadjuvant DOS (docetaxel 50 mg/m² IV + oxaliplatin 100 mg/m² IV day 1, S-1 40 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1-14, every 3 weeks × 3 cycles; stopped on progression) → D2 gastrectomy 1-3 weeks later → adjuvant S-1 40-60 mg orally twice daily by BSA, days 1-28 every 6 weeks × 8 cycles (CSC) vs D2 gastrectomy within 2 weeks of randomisation → adjuvant S-1 40-60 mg orally twice daily, days 1-28 every 6 weeks × 8 cycles (SC) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, postoperative pathologic stage, R0 resection rate, safety, pathologic complete response rate Adding neoadjuvant DOS to D2 gastrectomy and adjuvant S-1 led to significant tumour downstaging and improved PFS with acceptable safety. At median follow-up 38.6 mo (183 PFS events), PFS HR was 0.70 (95% CI 0.52-0.95; P=.023) in the FAS; three-year PFS was 66.3% with CSC vs 60.2% with SC; ITT sensitivity HR 0.69. PFS counted R1/R2 resection and distant metastasis found at surgery as progression. The final analysis came after a protocol revision, as events fell short of the planned 244, partly because early-stage patients were included. OS was not significantly improved (HR 0.84; 95% CI 0.60-1.19; three-year 74.2% vs 73.4%); OS is immature and the trial was not powered for it. Among operated patients, R0 resection was 95% vs 84%; pCR 10.4% with CSC. Neoadjuvant grade ≥3 neutropenia 12.6%, febrile neutropenia 9.2%, diarrhoea 5.0%; two grade 5 AEs (febrile neutropenia, dyspnoea) during neoadjuvant DOS; one surgery-related death with CSC.
records.keywords: Kang et al. J Clin Oncol 2021;39:2903-2913  34133211

records.title: RESOLVE
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body: Histologically confirmed gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; locally advanced cT4a N+ M0 or cT4b Nany M0, no previous treatment, candidates for radical D2 gastrectomy; Karnofsky performance score ≥70; excluded serious hypersensitivity to S-1, capecitabine or oxaliplatin and severe uncontrolled comorbidities Adjuvant CapOx: eight 21-day cycles starting 4–8 weeks after D2 gastrectomy, oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1 + capecitabine 1000 mg/m² orally twice daily for 2 weeks vs adjuvant SOX: eight 21-day cycles starting 4–8 weeks after D2 gastrectomy, oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1 + S-1 40–60 mg (by body surface area) orally twice daily for 2 weeks vs perioperative SOX: three preoperative SOX cycles → D2 gastrectomy 3–6 weeks later → five postoperative SOX cycles starting 4–8 weeks after surgery → three cycles of S-1 monotherapy Primary: 3-year disease-free survival. Secondary: 5-year overall survival, R0 resection rate, safety, objective response rate, pathological complete response, surgical complications Perioperative SOX gave a clinically meaningful 3-year DFS improvement over adjuvant CapOx after D2 gastrectomy, and adjuvant SOX was non-inferior to adjuvant CapOx. 3-year DFS (mITT, n=1022): 59.4% perioperative SOX vs 51.1% adjuvant CapOx, HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.61–0.97); adjuvant SOX 56.5%, HR 0.86 (0.68–1.07) vs CapOx, within the 1.33 non-inferiority margin. The analysis set was changed from ITT to mITT by protocol amendment. Final 5-year OS (median follow-up 62.8 months): 60.0% perioperative SOX and 61.0% adjuvant SOX vs 52.1% adjuvant CapOx (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.62–1.00, and 0.77, 0.61–0.98). OS was a secondary endpoint; perioperative vs adjuvant SOX was not powered or compared. R0 resection 93% perioperative SOX vs 87% adjuvant CapOx; post-hoc pCR 5.6%. Grade ≥3 AEs in treated patients: 21% perioperative SOX, 19% adjuvant SOX, 17% adjuvant CapOx; grade 3–4 thrombocytopenia and anaemia higher with perioperative SOX than adjuvant CapOx; no treatment-related deaths.
records.keywords: Zhang et al. Lancet Oncol 2021;22:1081-1092  34252374 Zhang et al. Lancet Oncol 2025;26:312-319  39952264

records.title: RESONANCE
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Gastric cancer; resectable stage II/III, locally advanced, candidates for perioperative or adjuvant chemotherapy with surgical resection Perioperative S-1 plus oxaliplatin (SOX): 2–4 cycles SOX → surgery → 4–6 cycles SOX vs adjuvant SOX: upfront surgery → 8 cycles SOX Three-year disease-free survival, R0 resection rate, pathological complete response rate, surgical outcomes, postoperative complications, chemotherapy completion, adverse events Perioperative SOX gave higher three-year DFS than adjuvant SOX in resectable stage II/III gastric cancer, which the authors describe as a trend, with well-tolerated toxicity. In the mITT population (382 PC, 374 AC), three-year DFS was 61.7% vs 53.8%; HR 0.76 (95%CI 0.61–0.96), log-rank p=0.019; per-protocol 63.0% vs 55.5% (HR 0.77). R0 resection 94.9% vs 83.7%; pCR 23.6% after preoperative SOX; postoperative complications 18.1% vs 19.5%. In subgroups the DFS difference was significant in stage III but not stage II. 41.1% of PC vs 19.2% of AC patients completed eight cycles. Limitations include no Lauren or MSI data and uneven centre enrolment. Neutropenia was the most frequent grade 3/4 AE (19.6% preoperative PC, 14.8% postoperative PC, 18.9% AC); deaths from thrombotic, cardiovascular and abdominal infection events occurred in two PC and one AC patient.
records.keywords: Wang et al. J Hematol Oncol 2024;17:17  38589926

records.title: TOPGEAR
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Histologically proven adenocarcinoma of the stomach or gastroesophageal junction (Siewert type II with ≤2 cm of esophageal involvement or Siewert type III); resectable, tumor stage T3 or T4 as judged by the treating surgeon, node-positive or node-negative, for perioperative curative-intent treatment; ECOG performance status 0 or 1 Preoperative chemoradiotherapy: perioperative chemotherapy with one fewer preoperative cycle → chemoradiotherapy starting 2–4 weeks after preoperative chemotherapy (45 Gy in 25 fractions, 5 days per week for 5 weeks, plus continuous fluorouracil 200 mg/m² per day 7 days per week or capecitabine 825 mg/m² twice daily days 1–5 each week) → surgery 4–6 weeks later → same postoperative chemotherapy vs perioperative chemotherapy alone: 3 cycles ECF/ECX (epirubicin 50 mg/m² IV day 1, cisplatin 60 mg/m² IV day 1, fluorouracil 200 mg/m² per day by 21-day continuous infusion or capecitabine 625 mg/m² twice daily days 1–21) or, after the 2017 amendment, 4 cycles FLOT (fluorouracil 2600 mg/m² 24-hour infusion, leucovorin 200 mg/m², oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², docetaxel 50 mg/m², all IV day 1), both pre- and postoperatively Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, pathological complete response, toxic effects, quality of life, surgical complications, operative mortality, R0 resection, major pathological response Adding preoperative chemoradiotherapy to perioperative chemotherapy did not improve overall survival in resectable gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma, despite better pathological outcomes. At median follow-up 67 mo, median OS was 46 vs 49 mo (HR for death 1.05; 95% CI 0.83–1.31); 5-yr OS was 44% vs 46%; median PFS was 31 vs 32 mo (HR 0.98; 95% CI 0.79–1.22). Pathological complete response was 17% vs 8% among resected patients (13% vs 6% by intention to treat); R0 was 92% vs 88%. Fewer patients in the chemoradiotherapy arm started postoperative chemotherapy (56% vs 66%). A trend toward poorer survival with chemoradiotherapy in lower-third gastric tumors was a subgroup finding, with tests unadjusted for multiplicity. Grade ≥3 toxic effects were 66% vs 61% and grade ≥3 surgical complications 18% vs 16%; only esophagitis differed significantly (4% vs 1%). Death within 90 days after surgery was 1% vs 2%. Quality of life is still being assessed.
records.keywords: Leong et al. N Engl J Med 2024;391:1810-1821  39282905

records.title: SWOG-9008
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Adjuvant therapy — resected gastric adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2001
records.body: Histologically confirmed adenocarcinoma of the stomach or gastroesophageal junction; postoperative adjuvant setting after complete resection with curative intent and negative margins, stage IB through IVM0 (1988 AJCC); registration 20–41 days after surgery, caloric intake >1500 kcal per day, SWOG performance status ≤2; D2 lymphadenectomy recommended but not required Surgery followed by fluorouracil 425 mg/m² per day + leucovorin 20 mg/m² per day for 5 days → chemoradiotherapy beginning 28 days after start of first cycle: 4500 cGy in 25 fractions (180 cGy per day, five days per week for five weeks) to tumor bed, regional nodes and 2 cm beyond resection margins, with IV bolus fluorouracil 400 mg/m² per day + leucovorin 20 mg/m² per day on the first four and last three days of radiotherapy → one month after radiotherapy, two five-day cycles of fluorouracil 425 mg/m² per day + leucovorin 20 mg/m² per day given one month apart vs surgery alone Overall survival, relapse-free survival, toxic effects, sites of relapse Postoperative chemoradiotherapy significantly improved overall and relapse-free survival vs surgery alone; the authors conclude it should be considered for all patients at high risk of recurrence after curative resection. At median follow-up of 5 years, median OS 36 vs 27 mo (HR for death, surgery-only vs chemoradiotherapy, 1.35; 95% CI 1.09–1.66; P=0.005); 3-yr OS 50% vs 41%. Median RFS 30 vs 19 mo (HR for relapse 1.52; 95% CI 1.23–1.86; P<0.001); 3-yr RFS 48% vs 31%. Surgery was mostly limited (54% D0, only 10% D2); no significant survival difference by extent of dissection (P=0.80). Only 181 of 281 (64%) completed chemoradiotherapy as planned; 17% stopped for toxic effects. Grade 3 toxicity occurred in 41% and grade 4 in 32% of the chemoradiotherapy group, mainly hematologic and gastrointestinal; 3 of 273 treated patients (1%) died of toxicity (pulmonary fibrosis, cardiac event, sepsis).
records.keywords: Macdonald et al. N Engl J Med 2001;345:725-730  11547741

records.title: ACTS-GC
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Adjuvant therapy — resected gastric adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2007
records.body: Histologically proven gastric cancer; Japanese stage II (excluding T1), IIIA or IIIB after gastrectomy with D2 or more extensive lymph-node dissection and R0 resection, randomised within 6 weeks of surgery; no hepatic, peritoneal or distant metastasis and no tumour cells in peritoneal fluid on cytology; age 20 to 80 years; no previous cancer treatment except the initial gastric resection S-1 40 mg/m² orally twice daily (80, 100 or 120 mg/day by BSA <1.25, 1.25 to <1.5, ≥1.5 m2) for 4 weeks → 2 weeks off, 6-week cycles for 1 year after surgery, started within 6 weeks of surgery vs surgery only (no anticancer treatment until confirmed relapse) Primary: overall survival. Secondary: relapse-free survival, safety, site of first relapse Adjuvant S-1 was effective after D2 dissection for locally advanced gastric cancer in East Asian patients. The trial stopped early on data monitoring committee advice after the first interim analysis showed better OS with S-1. At median follow-up 2.9 yr, 3-yr OS was 80.1% with S-1 vs 70.1% with surgery only (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.52-0.87); 3-yr RFS 72.2% vs 59.6% (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.50-0.77). The trial was open-label and stopped early with short follow-up; authors note results may not apply where D2 surgery is not standard. Grade 3/4 anorexia 6.0%, nausea 3.7%, diarrhoea 3.1%; S-1 was continued for 12 months in 65.8% and dose-reduced in 42.4%.
records.keywords: Sakuramoto et al. N Engl J Med 2007;357:1810-1820  17978289

records.title: CLASSIC
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Adjuvant therapy — resected gastric adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2012
records.body: Gastric adenocarcinoma; AJCC/UICC stage II (T2N1, T1N2, T3N0), IIIA (T3N1, T2N2, T4N0) or IIIB (T3N2) without metastatic disease, adjuvant setting after curative D2 gastrectomy with R0 resection within 6 weeks before randomisation and at least 15 lymph nodes examined; Karnofsky performance status ≥70%; excluded prior chemotherapy, immunotherapy or radiotherapy for gastric cancer Capecitabine 1000 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1 to 14 plus oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1, eight 3-week cycles (6 months) after D2 gastrectomy vs D2 gastrectomy alone Primary: 3-year disease-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, safety Adjuvant capecitabine plus oxaliplatin after curative D2 gastrectomy improved 3-year DFS vs surgery alone and should be considered a treatment option for operable gastric cancer. At the prespecified interim analysis (trial stopped on data monitoring committee recommendation; median follow-up 34·2 vs 34·3 mo), 3-year DFS was 74% vs 59% (HR 0·56, 95% CI 0·44–0·72; p<0·0001). OS was immature: 3-year OS 83% vs 78% (HR 0·72, 95% CI 0·52–1·00; p=0·0493). In subgroup analyses, DFS benefit was significant across stages II–IIIB and in N1 and N2 disease, but not in N0 disease. Grade 3/4 AEs occurred in 56% vs 6%, mainly neutropenia (22%), thrombocytopenia (8%) and nausea (8%). Peripheral neuropathy affected 56% (grade 3/4 2%). AEs led to dose modifications in 90%, and 67% received all eight cycles. One death from sepsis was possibly treatment-related.

records.title: JACCRO GC-07
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Adjuvant therapy — resected gastric adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body: Gastric cancer; pathologic stage III (Japanese classification 3rd English edition/TNM 7th: IIIA T2N3, T3N2, T4aN1; IIIB T3N3, T4aN2, T4bN0, T4bN1; IIIC T4aN3, T4bN2, T4bN3); postoperative adjuvant therapy after R0 resection by D2 or more extensive gastrectomy; age 20 to 80 years, treatment start within 42 days of surgery S-1 + docetaxel: oral S-1 twice daily (daily dose 80 mg if BSA <1.25 m2, 100 mg if 1.25 to <1.5 m2, 120 mg if ≥1.5 m2) days 1-14 q3w in the first course → docetaxel 40 mg/m² IV day 1 + S-1 days 1-14 q3w in the second to seventh courses → S-1 days 1-28 q6w after the eighth course, for up to 1 year vs S-1 alone (same dosing) days 1-28 q6w for up to 1 year Primary: 3-year relapse-free survival. Secondary: 3-year overall survival, 5-year overall survival, 5-year relapse-free survival, adverse events, treatment compliance, sites of relapse The authors concluded that adding docetaxel to adjuvant S-1 is effective with few safety concerns in stage III gastric cancer. At the second interim analysis (216 events among 915 patients; median follow-up 12.5 months), the combination showed superior 3-year RFS: 66% vs 50% (HR 0.632; 99.99% CI 0.400 to 0.998). Enrollment was stopped early on the recommendation of the independent data and safety monitoring committee. This is an early, immature result: actual 3-year RFS was observable in only 179 patients, and 3-year RFS in the S-1 arm (50%) was far below the 62% planning estimate. OS showed no significant difference (44 vs 60 deaths; P = .13). Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 58% vs 42% (341 vs 348 treated), led by grade 3/4 neutropenia (38.1% vs 16.1%) and leukopenia (22.6% vs 2.0%); febrile neutropenia was 4.7% vs 0.3%. One death from respiratory failure in the S-1 arm was considered drug-related.
records.keywords: Yoshida et al. J Clin Oncol 2019;37:1296-1304  30925125

records.title: ARTIST 2
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Adjuvant therapy — resected gastric adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body: Gastric adenocarcinoma; adjuvant therapy after curative gastrectomy with D2 lymph node dissection and no residual (R0) disease; stage II or III by AJCC 2010 staging with lymph node-positive disease S-1 40-60 mg twice daily days 1-28 followed by 14 days of rest, eight cycles (1 year) vs SOX: S-1 days 1-14 (2 weeks on/1 week off) + oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1 every 3 weeks, up to eight cycles (6 months) vs SOXRT: SOX two cycles → radiotherapy 45 Gy (1.8 Gy daily, 5 days a week over 5 weeks) with concurrent S-1 40-60 mg twice daily → four additional cycles of SOX Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: safety, overall survival, pattern of recurrence, quality of life, exploratory biomarkers Adjuvant SOX prolonged DFS vs S-1 after D2 resection of stage II/III node-positive gastric cancer; SOXRT showed only a nonsignificant trend vs S-1, and adding chemoradiotherapy to SOX did not significantly reduce recurrence. At median follow-up 47 months, 3-year DFS was 64.8% (S-1), 74.3% (SOX) and 72.8% (SOXRT); HR SOX vs S-1 0.693 (95% CI 0.409-0.987; P = 0.042), SOXRT vs S-1 0.724 (95% CI 0.507-1.032; P = 0.074), SOX vs SOXRT 0.971 (P = 0.879). Recruitment ended early (546 rather than 900 patients), reducing power; median DFS was not reached and further follow-up is needed. Grade 3 or 4 neuropathy: 12% SOX, 6% SOXRT; four patients died during or within 30 days of treatment, one (S-1) of sudden cardiac arrest after the first cycle.

records.title: KEYNOTE-585
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative immunotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Gastric or gastro-oesophageal adenocarcinoma, including Siewert type 2 or 3; previously untreated, locally advanced, resectable: T3 or greater primary lesion or any positive nodes without metastatic disease (AJCC); planned surgery after pre-operative chemotherapy, ECOG 0–1; excluded active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment in past 2 years, non-infectious pneumonitis requiring steroids, immunodeficiency, active infection requiring systemic treatment Main cohort: neoadjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks for 3 cycles + cisplatin 80 mg/m² IV day 1 + capecitabine 1000 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1–14 or fluorouracil 800 mg/m² per day IV days 1–5 → surgery → adjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg + chemotherapy for 3 cycles → pembrolizumab 200 mg for 11 cycles, until maximum administrations, progression, unacceptable toxicity or patient/physician decision vs placebo (saline) on the same schedule; FLOT cohort: pembrolizumab or placebo + docetaxel 50 mg/m², oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², fluorouracil 2600 mg/m², leucovorin 200 mg/m² every 2 weeks for 4 cycles neoadjuvant and 4 adjuvant → pembrolizumab or placebo for 11 cycles Primary: pathological complete response, event-free survival, overall survival, safety (FLOT cohort). Secondary: disease-free survival, overall survival (main plus FLOT cohorts), event-free survival (main plus FLOT cohorts), safety, pathological complete response (main plus FLOT cohorts), complete surgical resection rate, PD-L1 status, microsatellite instability status Perioperative pembrolizumab plus cisplatin-based chemotherapy improved pathological complete response but did not significantly improve event-free survival, the endpoint that defined trial success. pCR (first interim analysis) was 12.9% vs 2.0% with placebo (difference 10.9%, 95% CI 7.5–14.8). At the third interim analysis (median follow-up 47.7 mo), median EFS was 44.4 vs 25.3 mo; HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.67–0.99), p=0.0198, which did not meet the 0.0178 significance boundary; the proportional hazards assumption was not met. OS was immature and not formally tested: median 60.7 vs 58.0 mo; HR 0.90 (95% CI 0.73–1.12). Grade ≥3 all-cause AEs occurred in 78% vs 74%; grade ≥3 adverse events of interest in 10% vs 3%; treatment-related deaths in four (1%) vs two (<1%). In the FLOT safety cohort, treatment-related serious AEs occurred in 44% vs 20%.

records.title: MATTERHORN
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative immunotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body: Previously untreated resectable stage II-IVA gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma eligible for radical surgery, irrespective of PD-L1 or MSI; excluded peritoneal/distant disease, squamous/adenosquamous histology and GIST Durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 4 weeks + FLOT every 2 weeks ×2 preop → surgery → ×2 postop → durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 4 weeks for ten additional cycles vs matched placebo plus the same FLOT and maintenance schedule Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, pathological complete response, disease-free survival, surgery, R0 resection, metastasis-free survival, disease-specific survival, health-related quality of life, 24-month and 36-month overall survival, 24-month and 36-month event-free survival, 24-month and 36-month disease-free survival, overall survival by PD-L1 expression, association of PD-L1 expression with event-free survival, disease-free survival and pathological complete response, pharmacokinetics, anti-drug antibodies, safety Durvalumab plus FLOT improved interim EFS (24-month 67.4% vs 58.5%; HR 0.71) and final pCR (19.2% vs 7.2%). At the final OS analysis (data cutoff Sept 1, 2025; 37% maturity), durvalumab plus FLOT significantly improved OS (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.63-0.96; p=0.021); OS was 76% vs 70% at 24 months and 69% vs 62% at 36 months, median not reached, with no evidence of proportional-hazards violation. The OS benefit was not evident in clinically node-negative disease (HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.67-1.51; interaction p=0.19), and the PD-L1 TAP <1% estimate was imprecise (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.41-1.50). EFS analyses by pathological and nodal response were post-hoc, exploratory and restricted to patients who completed surgery. Severe adverse events were similar (71.6% vs 71.2%), while serious events, regimen discontinuation and immune-mediated events were numerically more frequent with durvalumab; deaths possibly related to treatment occurred in 6 of 475 vs 2 of 469.
