records.title: DRAGON IV/CAP 05
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative immunotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Locally advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; perioperative setting, no previous antitumor treatment, clinical T3-4aN+M0 by CT or MRI and eligible for curative resection; age 18-75 years, ECOG 0-1; excluded known HER2 positivity SOXRC: camrelizumab 200 mg IV day 1 + rivoceranib 250 mg PO once daily days 1-21 (14 days in cycle 3) + SOX q3w × 3 neoadjuvant cycles → D2 gastrectomy 3-6 weeks later → 3 adjuvant cycles of the same regimen → 3 cycles camrelizumab + rivoceranib, optional continuation (maximum 1 year rivoceranib, 17 camrelizumab doses) vs SOX: oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1 + S-1 40/50/60 mg (by BSA) PO twice daily days 1-14 q3w × 3 → D2 gastrectomy → 3 adjuvant SOX cycles, optional S-1 up to 1 year Primary: pathologic complete response (ypT0), event-free survival. Secondary: major pathologic response, total pathologic complete response (ypT0N0), ypN stage, R0 resection rate, disease-free survival, overall survival, safety, surgical complications Adding camrelizumab and low-dose rivoceranib to perioperative SOX significantly improved pCR vs SOX alone, with a tolerable safety profile; the co-primary EFS endpoint is still being evaluated. ITT pCR (ypT0) 18.3% (33/180) vs 5.0% (9/180); difference 13.7% (95% CI 7.2 to 20.1), OR 4.5, one-sided P<.0001 against a prespecified .005 threshold. MPR 51.1% vs 37.8%; ypT0N0 16.7% vs 4.4%. Surgery rates were 86% vs 87%, and R0 resection 99% vs 94% of operated patients. No survival data yet. The trial was open-label, enrolled only patients from China aged 75 or younger, and had no camrelizumab-SOX arm to isolate rivoceranib's contribution. Neoadjuvant grade ≥3 TRAEs 34% vs 17% (neutrophil count decrease 12% vs 4%, hypertension 4% vs 0%); grade ≥3 irAEs 6%; no TRAE deaths; surgical complications 27% vs 33%.
records.keywords: Li et al. J Clin Oncol 2024;43:464-474  39383487

records.title: ASTRUM-006
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative immunotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Locally advanced, resectable, histologically confirmed gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; untreated, perioperative setting; PD-L1-positive (CPS ≥5, central 22C3 IHC); aged 18–70 years; excluded prior antibodies or drugs targeting immune checkpoints Neoadjuvant serplulimab 4·5 mg/kg IV day 1 + SOX (oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1; S-1 40–60 mg orally twice daily days 1–14) every 21 days for three cycles → surgery → adjuvant serplulimab monotherapy for up to 17 cycles vs neoadjuvant placebo 4·5 mg/kg IV day 1 + SOX for three cycles → surgery → adjuvant SOX for five cycles Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: BICR-assessed event-free survival, overall survival, disease-free survival, pathological complete response rate, R0 resection rate, objective response rate, safety, pharmacokinetics, immunogenicity, potential predictive biomarkers, quality of life Neoadjuvant serplulimab + SOX followed by adjuvant serplulimab significantly improved investigator-assessed EFS vs neoadjuvant and adjuvant SOX in PD-L1-positive resectable gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma, meeting the primary endpoint; mature OS is awaited. In CPS ≥10 (median follow-up 42·7 mo), median EFS was NR vs 42·0 mo; HR 0·65 (95% CI 0·47–0·90). In ITT (CPS ≥5; follow-up 35·9 mo), median EFS was NR vs 35·9 mo; HR 0·73 (0·56–0·94); this was the final EFS analysis. BICR-assessed EFS was consistent (ITT HR 0·67). pCR was 26% vs 6% (CPS ≥10) and 22% vs 6% (ITT). OS is immature (about 30% of events). Patients were exclusively Asian and aged up to 70 years, and the design cannot isolate the contribution of adjuvant immunotherapy. Grade 3 or worse TRAEs occurred in 47% vs 59%. Immune-related AEs occurred in 40% vs 6% (grade 3 or worse 6% vs 1%; none fatal). AEs leading to death occurred in 5% vs 3%; treatment-related deaths were two vs one patients.

records.title: CROSS
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Neoadjuvant chemoradiation & perioperative strategy — esophageal & GEJ adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2012
records.body: Esophageal or esophagogastric-junction squamous-cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma or large-cell undifferentiated carcinoma; resectable, potentially curable, clinical T1N1 or T2-3N0-1 M0 (UICC TNM), no prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy; upper tumor border at least 3 cm below upper esophageal sphincter, tumor length ≤8 cm and width ≤5 cm, age 18 to 75 years, weight loss ≤10%; excluded proximal gastric tumors with minimal esophageal invasion and history of other cancer Carboplatin AUC 2 mg/mL/min + paclitaxel 50 mg/m² IV on days 1, 8, 15, 22 and 29 (5 weeks) with concurrent radiotherapy 41.4 Gy in 23 fractions of 1.8 Gy, 5 fractions/week, from day 1 → surgery as soon as possible after completion (preferably within 4 to 6 weeks) vs surgery alone as soon as possible after randomization Primary: overall survival. Secondary: R0 resection rate, pathological complete response rate, disease-free survival, toxicity during chemoradiotherapy, postoperative complications, in-hospital mortality, 30-day postoperative mortality Preoperative carboplatin/paclitaxel chemoradiotherapy improved survival vs surgery alone in potentially curable esophageal or esophagogastric-junction cancer, with acceptable adverse-event rates. Median OS 49.4 vs 24.0 mo (HR 0.657; 95% CI 0.495 to 0.871; P = 0.003); 5-yr OS 47% vs 34%; median follow-up 45.4 mo. Benefit was consistent across predefined subgroups, including histologic subtype, without significant interaction. R0 resection 92% vs 69%; pathological complete response 47 of 161 resected (29%). Median DFS among resected patients not reached vs 24.2 mo (HR 0.498). Most common major chemoradiotherapy toxic effects were leukopenia 6% and anorexia 5%; one patient died awaiting surgery, probably from esophageal perforation. Postoperative complications were similar, and in-hospital mortality was 4% in both groups.
records.keywords: van Hagen et al. N Engl J Med 2012;366:2074-2084  22646630

records.title: Neo-AEGIS
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Neoadjuvant chemoradiation & perioperative strategy — esophageal & GEJ adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body: Histologically proven adenocarcinoma of the oesophagus or oesophagogastric junction (Siewert types I, II and III); locally advanced clinical T2–3, N0–3, M0 disease, staged with CT-PET, treated with curative-intent preoperative therapy; primary tumour length ≤8 cm or combined tumour and nodal length for radiotherapy planning ≤10 cm, ECOG 0–2, cardiac ejection fraction >50%; excluded previous chemotherapy and radiotherapy Perioperative chemotherapy: modified MAGIC, three preoperative and three postoperative 3-week cycles of epirubicin 50 mg/m² IV day 1 + cisplatin 60 mg/m² IV or oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1 + fluorouracil 200 mg/m² daily continuous infusion or capecitabine 625 mg/m² orally twice daily for 21 days; from May 1, 2018, optional FLOT at the oncologist's discretion: four preoperative and four postoperative 2-week cycles of fluorouracil 2600 mg/m², oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², leucovorin 200 mg/m², docetaxel 50 mg/m² IV day 1 vs trimodality therapy (CROSS): 41.4 Gy in 23 fractions of 1.8 Gy with 5 weekly cycles of paclitaxel 50 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 2 IV on days 1, 8, 15, 22 and 29 → surgery 3–10 weeks after the last treatment Primary: overall survival. Secondary: disease-free survival, site of treatment failure, operative complications, toxicity, pathological complete response, major pathological response, margin-free resection (R0), quality of life, endoscopic response Perioperative chemotherapy (mainly modified MAGIC) gave survival similar to CROSS trimodality therapy despite inferior pathological response and margin rates. Non-inferiority was not established: the trial closed early (377 randomised, 70% of target) and was underpowered; the authors encourage continued clinical equipoise. At a median follow-up of 38.8 mo, median OS was 48.0 vs 49.2 mo and 3-yr OS 55% vs 57%; HR 1.03 (95% CI 0.77–1.38), above the prespecified 1.16 margin. DFS did not differ (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.68–1.17). pCR (4% vs 12%) and R0 (82% vs 96%) favoured trimodality therapy. Only 27 (15%) patients received FLOT, too few for subset analysis. Grade 3–4 neutropenia occurred in 27% vs 6% and diarrhoea in 11% vs none; only 41% completed all chemotherapy cycles. 90-day mortality was 3% vs 2%. Deaths from serious adverse events were one vs three, two possibly treatment-related. Quality of life was worse after trimodality therapy before surgery and largely equalised by 1 and 3 yr, except for persistent coughing.
records.keywords: Reynolds et al. Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2023;8:1015-1027  37734399

records.title: ESOPEC
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Neoadjuvant chemoradiation & perioperative strategy — esophageal & GEJ adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body: Histologically confirmed resectable esophageal adenocarcinoma, including tumours with epicenter within 5 cm of the esophagogastric junction extending into the esophagus; UICC cT1 cN+, cT2–4a cN+ or cT2–4a cN0, no metastatic spread on CT; no prior radiotherapy or chemotherapy Perioperative FLOT (fluorouracil 2600 mg/m², leucovorin 200 mg/m², oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², docetaxel 50 mg/m² IV day 1): four 2-week cycles → surgery 4–8 weeks later → four 2-week cycles starting 4–6 weeks after discharge vs preoperative chemoradiotherapy (CROSS): carboplatin AUC 2 + paclitaxel 50 mg/m² IV weekly days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 with radiotherapy 41.4 Gy (23 fractions of 1.8 Gy) → surgery 4–8 weeks after last dose Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, site of treatment failure, UICC TNM pathological stage after surgery, pathological tumor regression grade after preoperative therapy, complications and death related to surgery, adverse events, R0 resection, pathological complete response Perioperative FLOT improved survival compared with preoperative chemoradiotherapy in resectable esophageal adenocarcinoma. At a median follow-up of 55 mo, 3-yr OS was 57.4% vs 50.7% (HR 0.70; 95% CI 0.53–0.92; P=0.01) and 5-yr OS 50.6% vs 38.7%; median OS 66 vs 37 mo. 3-yr PFS was 51.6% vs 35.0% (HR 0.66; 95% CI 0.51–0.85); secondary endpoints were not adjusted for multiplicity. In resected patients, pCR was 16.7% vs 10.1%; R0 resection 94.3% vs 95.0% in the surgery population. In the safety population, grade ≥3 AEs occurred in 58.0% vs 50.0% and serious AEs in 47.3% vs 41.8%; grade ≥3 neutropenia occurred in 19.8% with FLOT. 90-day postoperative mortality was 3.1% vs 5.6%.
records.keywords: Hoeppner et al. N Engl J Med 2025;392:323-335  39842010

records.title: CheckMate 577
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Adjuvant immunotherapy — resected esophageal & GEJ cancer · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body: Esophageal or gastroesophageal junction cancer, predominant adenocarcinoma or squamous-cell carcinoma; stage II or III (AJCC 7th edition) at initial diagnosis, adjuvant setting after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy and complete R0 resection (no vital tumor within 1 mm of margins); enrolled regardless of PD-L1 expression; residual pathological disease (no pathological complete response) of at least ypT1 or ypN1, resection 4 to 16 weeks before randomization Nivolumab 240 mg IV every 2 weeks for 16 weeks, then 480 mg IV every 4 weeks from week 17 vs matching placebo on the same schedule (double-blind); continued until disease recurrence, unacceptable toxic effects or withdrawal of consent, maximum 1 year Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, survival at 1, 2 and 3 years, safety, distant metastasis–free survival, patient-reported outcomes (FACT-E, EQ-5D-3L) Adjuvant nivolumab significantly prolonged disease-free survival vs placebo after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy and resection. At the prespecified interim analysis (median follow-up 24.4 mo), median DFS was 22.4 vs 11.0 mo (HR 0.69; 96.4% CI 0.56–0.86; P<0.001). DFS favored nivolumab across prespecified subgroups, including tumor-cell PD-L1 expression. In an exploratory analysis, median distant metastasis–free survival was 28.3 vs 17.6 mo (HR 0.74; 95% CI 0.60–0.92). Overall survival had not yet been analysed. Health-related quality of life was maintained in both groups. Treatment-related grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 13% vs 6% of patients, treatment-related serious adverse events in 8% vs 3%, and related events led to discontinuation in 9% vs 3%. One grade 5 nivolumab-related event (cardiac arrest) was recorded; after database lock, the investigator deemed it not related.
records.keywords: Kelly et al. N Engl J Med 2021;384:1191-1203  33789008

records.title: JCOG9907
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma — neoadjuvant / perioperative therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2012
records.body: Histologically proven squamous cell carcinoma of the thoracic esophagus; resectable clinical stage II or III (UICC TNM), excluding T4, for perioperative chemotherapy with esophagectomy; age 75 years or younger, ECOG PS 0 to 2; no previous chemo- or radiotherapy for any malignancy Esophagectomy with regional lymphadenectomy → postoperative cisplatin 80 mg/m² IV day 1 + 5-FU 800 mg/m² continuous infusion days 1–5, every 3 weeks × 2 courses, starting 2 to 10 weeks after surgery (omitted for pN0) vs same cisplatin + 5-FU every 3 weeks × 2 courses (second course withheld after progressive disease) → esophagectomy within 5 weeks Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, chemotherapy toxicities, operative morbidity, operative mortality, response rate to preoperative chemotherapy, complete resection rate, pathologic downstaging Preoperative cisplatin + 5-FU did not significantly improve the primary endpoint, PFS, but improved OS compared with postoperative chemotherapy. At the second interim analysis, PFS missed the stopping criterion (HR 0.76; adjusted 95% CI 0.56–1.04) while OS differed (HR 0.64; 95% CI 0.45–0.91), prompting early publication. In the final analysis (median follow-up 62 months), post vs pre: 5-yr PFS 39% vs 44% (HR 0.84; 95% CI 0.63–1.11; P = 0.22); 5-yr OS 43% vs 55% (HR 0.73; 95% CI 0.54–0.99). Pathologic stage II or lower: 33% vs 48%; R0 among resected patients: 91% vs 96%. Completion of 2 postoperative courses: 75% of R0 pN+ group 1 patients, compared with 85.4% completing 2 preoperative courses. Grade 3/4 chemotherapy toxicity was uncommon (mucositis 8% vs 3%) and there were no chemotherapy-related deaths; postoperative renal dysfunction was 3% vs 6%; there was one surgical death per arm.
records.keywords: Ando et al. Ann Surg Oncol 2012;19:68-74  21879261

records.title: NEOCRTEC5010
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma — neoadjuvant / perioperative therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body: Thoracic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma; potentially resectable, untreated, clinically staged T1-4N1M0/T4N0M0 (stage IIB or III, AJCC 6th edition); age 18 to 70 and Karnofsky score ≥90; excluded prior malignancy, comorbidity precluding surgery, and prior gastrectomy making a gastric conduit infeasible Vinorelbine 25 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8 plus cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV day 1 or 25 mg/m² IV days 1 to 4, every 3 weeks for two cycles, with concurrent radiotherapy 40.0 Gy in 20 fractions of 2.0 Gy (five fractions per week) → McKeown or Ivor Lewis esophagectomy with two-field lymphadenectomy and total mediastinal lymph node dissection 4 to 6 weeks after chemoradiotherapy vs surgery alone (same esophagectomy as soon as possible after randomization) Primary: overall survival. Secondary: disease-free survival, safety, R0 resection rate, pathologic response, postoperative complications, peritreatment mortality NCRT plus surgery improved survival over surgery alone in locally advanced ESCC, with acceptable and manageable adverse events. Median OS 100.1 vs 66.5 mo (HR 0.71; 95% CI 0.53 to 0.96; P = .025); 3-yr OS 69.1% vs 58.9%. Among 389 R0-resected patients, median DFS 100.1 vs 41.7 mo (HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.43 to 0.78). R0 resection 98.4% vs 91.2%; pCR 43.2% in the CRT arm. Median follow-up of survivors 41.0 vs 34.6 mo; 38 of 224 (17.0%) CRT-arm patients did not proceed to surgery, mostly by refusal. Older patients and those with poorer performance status were not recruited, and all centres were Chinese. Grade 3 or 4 leukopenia 48.9% and neutropenia 45.7% during CRT; postoperative arrhythmia 13.0% vs 4.0% (P = .001); peritreatment mortality 2.2% vs 0.4% (P = .212).
records.keywords: Yang et al. J Clin Oncol 2018;36:2796-2803  30089078

records.title: JCOG1109 (NExT)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma — neoadjuvant / perioperative therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Oesophageal squamous cell, adenosquamous or basal cell carcinoma; previously untreated locally advanced disease, clinical stage IB, II or III (but not T4) by UICC TNM 7th edition, treated neoadjuvantly before oesophagectomy; aged 20–75 years, ECOG PS 0 or 1, R0 resection by thoracotomy and laparotomy expected; excluded prior oesophageal cancer treatment other than curative endoscopic resection of superficial lesions, and prior treatment for another cancer NeoCF: fluorouracil 800 mg/m² IV days 1–5 + cisplatin 80 mg/m² day 1, 2 courses 3 weeks apart vs NeoCF+D: docetaxel 70 mg/m² day 1 + cisplatin 70 mg/m² day 1 + fluorouracil 750 mg/m² days 1–5 every 3 weeks, 3 courses vs NeoCF+RT: cisplatin 75 mg/m² day 1 + fluorouracil 1000 mg/m² days 1–4, 2 courses 4 weeks apart, with radiotherapy 41·4 Gy in 23 fractions over 5 weeks; all arms → total or subtotal thoracic oesophagectomy with regional lymphadenectomy via right thoracotomy within 56 days Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, R0 resection rate, response, pCR rate, adverse event rates, surgical complications, ypT0N0M0 rate, recurrence pattern Neoadjuvant triplet NeoCF+D followed by oesophagectomy significantly improved OS vs doublet NeoCF and might be a new standard for fit patients with locally advanced OSCC in Japan; NeoCF+RT did not significantly improve OS. At median follow-up 50·7 mo, 3-yr OS was 72·1% NeoCF+D vs 62·6% NeoCF (HR 0·68, 95% CI 0·50–0·92; one-sided p=0·006) and 68·3% NeoCF+RT (HR 0·84, 0·63–1·12; p=0·12). 3-yr PFS 61·8% NeoCF+D vs 47·7% NeoCF (HR 0·67; no α allocated). pCR 19·8% NeoCF+D and 38·5% NeoCF+RT vs 2·0% NeoCF, without OS benefit for RT; post-hoc NeoCF+D vs NeoCF+RT OS HR 0·80 (0·59–1·10), not significant. Non-cancer deaths were more frequent with NeoCF+RT (26% vs 12% NeoCF, 9% NeoCF+D). Grade 3 or higher febrile neutropenia 16% NeoCF+D vs 5% NeoCF+RT vs 1% NeoCF; treatment-related deaths during neoadjuvant therapy 4, 2 and 3 patients, respectively. Limitations: open-label, Japan-only, age ≤75 years, no quality-of-life data.

records.title: ESCORT-NEO/NCCES01
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma — neoadjuvant / perioperative therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Resectable locally advanced thoracic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma; neoadjuvant setting, no prior anti-tumor therapy; clinical T1b-3N1-3M0 or T3N0M0 (AJCC 8th edition), expected R0 resection, age 18-75 years, ECOG PS 0-1; excluded obvious invasion of adjacent organs (e.g. major arteries, trachea), supraclavicular nodal metastases, BMI <18.5 kg/m², active or past autoimmune disease, other malignancy within 5 years Camrelizumab 200 mg d1 + nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² d1, 8 + cisplatin 75 mg/m² d1, two 3-week cycles → esophagectomy 4–6 weeks later → adjuvant camrelizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for up to 15 cycles vs camrelizumab 200 mg d1 + paclitaxel 175 mg/m² d1 + cisplatin 75 mg/m² d1, two 3-week cycles → esophagectomy → adjuvant camrelizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for up to 15 cycles vs paclitaxel 175 mg/m² d1 + cisplatin 75 mg/m² d1, two 3-week cycles → esophagectomy Primary: pathological complete response rate, event-free survival. Secondary: major pathological response rate, R0 resection rate, ypTNM stage, overall survival, disease-free survival, adverse events, surgical complications, 30- and 90-day postoperative mortality, immune-related adverse events Adding camrelizumab to neoadjuvant chemotherapy significantly increased pCR in the ITT population, with no unexpected increase in toxicity; the co-primary EFS endpoint, DFS and OS are immature (median follow-up 8.2 mo). pCR 28.0% with Cam+nab-TP (difference 23.5%, 95% CI 15.1–32.0; P<0.0001) and 15.4% with Cam+TP (difference 10.9%, 95% CI 3.7–18.1; P=0.0034) vs 4.7% with TP; MPR 59.1%, 36.2% and 20.9%. Cam+nab-TP vs Cam+TP was not a prespecified comparison; open-label, China-only. Grade ≥3 TRAEs 34.1%, 29.2% and 28.8%, mainly neutrophil and white blood cell count decreased; one grade 5 TRAE (acute liver failure, Cam+TP). Postoperative complications 34.2%, 38.8% and 32.0%; 90-day mortality 1.8%, 1.7% and 1.0%.

records.title: RTOG 85-01
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Definitive chemoradiation — non-surgical curative therapy (especially esophageal SCC) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 1999
records.body: Squamous cell carcinoma or adenocarcinoma of the thoracic esophagus; nondisseminated T1-3 N0-1 M0, previously untreated; adenocarcinoma eligible only after October 1986; Karnofsky score ≥50, normal tracheobronchial tree; excluded prior chest irradiation or chemotherapy and prior or concurrent other malignancy Cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV day 1 + fluorouracil 1 g/m²/day continuous infusion days 1-4, in weeks 1, 5, 8 and 11, with concurrent RT 50 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks (then adjuvant chemotherapy) vs RT alone 64 Gy in 32 fractions over 6.4 weeks; randomization stopped early when the preplanned interim analysis favoured combined therapy, after which a nonrandomized cohort received the combined therapy Primary: overall survival. Secondary: patterns of treatment failure, acute toxic effects, late toxic effects, time to local failure Combined chemoradiotherapy increased survival over RT alone in T1-3 N0-1 M0 squamous cell or adenocarcinoma of the esophagus. In the randomized part, 5-yr OS was 26% (95% CI, 15%-37%) with combined therapy vs 0% with RT (log-rank P<.001); median 14.1 vs 9.3 mo; no deaths after 5 yr were due to esophageal cancer. Randomization stopped early after an interim analysis (P = .005). The nonrandomized combined-therapy cohort had 5-yr OS of 14% (95% CI, 6%-23%). Persistent disease was the commonest failure, less frequent with combined therapy (34/130 [26%] vs 23/62 [37%]). Chemotherapy was given as planned in only 89 (68%) of 130 patients. Randomized combined therapy caused acute grade 4 toxicity in 8% and treatment-related death in 2%, vs 2% grade 4 and no toxic deaths with RT; severe late toxicity did not differ significantly.

records.title: INT 0123 (RTOG 94-05)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Definitive chemoradiation — non-surgical curative therapy (especially esophageal SCC) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2002
records.body: Squamous cell carcinoma or adenocarcinoma of the cervical, mid or distal esophagus; AJCC clinical stage T1 to T4, N0/1, M0, selected for a nonsurgical approach (definitive combined-modality therapy); tumour not extending to within 2 cm of the gastroesophageal junction, KPS ≥60, adequate nutritional intake, cervical primaries with supraclavicular nodes (N1) allowed; excluded tracheobronchial invasion or tracheoesophageal fistula, M1 disease, prior chemotherapy, thoracic radiation or resection 5-FU 1,000 mg/m²/24 h continuous infusion days 1 through 4 + cisplatin 75 mg/m² bolus day 1, every 28 days for four cycles (the last two after a 4-week rest following RT), with concurrent RT 64.8 Gy (1.8 Gy/d, 5 days per week; 50.4 Gy then 14.4 Gy cone down to the primary) vs same chemotherapy with concurrent RT 50.4 Gy (1.8 Gy/d) Local/regional control, survival, toxicity, time to local/regional failure and persistence, patterns of first failure, treatment-related mortality, quality of life Escalating concurrent RT from 50.4 to 64.8 Gy with 5-FU/cisplatin did not improve survival or local/regional control; the authors conclude 50.4 Gy is the standard dose. The trial closed early at 236 of a planned 298 patients after an interim analysis showed a ≤2.5% chance of a significant high-dose survival advantage. Among 218 eligible patients (64.8 vs 50.4 Gy), median survival was 13.0 vs 18.1 mo and 2-yr survival 31% vs 40%, not significantly different; 2-yr cumulative incidence of local/regional failure/persistence was 56% vs 52%. An analysis restricted to patients receiving their assigned dose also showed no high-dose survival advantage. Treatment-related deaths were 11 (10%) vs two (2%); seven of the 11 occurred at ≤50.4 Gy, so the authors judged the excess unlikely to reflect the higher dose. Only 67% vs 83% received RT per protocol. Median follow-up was 16.4 mo.
records.keywords: Minsky et al. J Clin Oncol 2002;20:1167-1174  11870157

records.title: PRODIGE5/ACCORD17
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Definitive chemoradiation — non-surgical curative therapy (especially esophageal SCC) · Randomised clinical trial (phase II/III) · 2014
records.body: Oesophageal squamous-cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma or adenosquamous carcinoma; previously untreated stage I–IVA (TNM sixth edition, incl. metastatic celiac or cervical nodes), selected for definitive chemoradiotherapy as unsuitable for surgery; ECOG 0–2, caloric intake >1000 kcal/m²/day; excluded distant metastases, weight loss ≥20% within 3 months, tracheobronchial invasion or fistula, symptomatic arteritis/angina/MI within 6 months FOLFOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² IV day 1, leucovorin 200 mg/m², fluorouracil 400 mg/m² IV bolus day 1, then infusional fluorouracil 1600 mg/m² over 46 h) every 2 weeks for six cycles, first three concurrent with radiotherapy vs cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV day 1 + fluorouracil 1000 mg/m² per day continuous IV infusion days 1–4 for four cycles (two during radiotherapy at 4-week intervals, two after chemoradiotherapy 3 weeks apart); both with radiotherapy 50 Gy in 25 fractions (five per week); chemotherapy stopped for progression, unacceptable toxicity or refusal Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, endoscopic complete response, time to treatment failure, occurrence of grade 3 or 4 toxicities, quality of life, overall response rate, complete response rate, safety Definitive chemoradiotherapy with FOLFOX did not improve PFS vs fluorouracil-cisplatin; the authors suggest FOLFOX might be a more convenient option for localised oesophageal cancer unsuitable for surgery. Median PFS 9.7 vs 9.4 mo (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.70–1.24; p=0.64) at median follow-up 25.3 mo; PFS at 3 years 18.2% vs 17.4%. Median OS 20.2 vs 17.5 mo (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.68–1.29; p=0.70). The trial was not designed for non-inferiority, so similar efficacy does not establish equivalence; most patients had squamous-cell carcinoma. Treatment-related deaths: one of 131 with FOLFOX vs six of 128 with fluorouracil-cisplatin (five from neutropenic sepsis; p=0.066). The most frequent grade 3 or 4 events did not differ. All-grade paraesthesia (47% vs 2%) and sensory neuropathy (18% vs 1%) were more common with FOLFOX; creatinine increases (3% vs 12%) and alopecia (2% vs 9%) were more common with fluorouracil-cisplatin.

records.title: CRTCOESC
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Definitive chemoradiation — non-surgical curative therapy (especially esophageal SCC) · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body:
Pathologically confirmed oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma; locally advanced, inoperable (medical reasons or patient choice), definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy; clinical stage cT1bN1-2M0 or T2-T4aN0-2M0 (AJCC 7th edition); age 18-75 years, ECOG PS 0-2, pulmonary ventilation function >80% of predicted Capecitabine 625 mg/m² twice daily days 1-5, 8-12, 15-19 every 3 weeks for two cycles vs XELOX (oxaliplatin 65 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8 + capecitabine 625 mg/m² twice daily days 1-5, 8-12, 15-19 every 3 weeks for two cycles) vs PF (cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV day 1 + fluorouracil 750 mg/m² IV days 1-4 every 4 weeks for two cycles); all with concurrent IMRT 50 Gy/25 fractions; then second randomisation to two cycles of the same regimen as consolidation vs none Primary: 2-year overall survival rate, incidence of grade ≥3 adverse events. Secondary: progression-free survival, clinical complete response, overall survival, progression-free survival and adverse events with vs without consolidation chemotherapy Capecitabine or XELOX did not significantly improve 2-year OS over PF in DCRT; capecitabine had fewer grade ≥3 AEs than PF
・2-yr OS: 75% vs 66.7% vs 70.9%; HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.61–1.35) capecitabine vs PF; HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.58–1.27) XELOX vs PF
・Grade ≥3 AEs: 28.8% vs 36.5% vs 45.7%; capecitabine vs PF nominal P = .034; XELOX vs PF nominal P = .270
・PFS: Median 26.1 vs 30.2 vs 28.2 mo; HR 1.15 (95% CI 0.79–1.68) capecitabine vs PF; HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.62–1.33) XELOX vs PF
・cCR: 35% vs 37.6% vs 33.3%
・Consolidation: Median OS 41.9 vs 36.9 mo with vs without; HR 0.71 (95% CI 0.52–0.99); nominal, exploratory; no OS gain in XELOX arm
・Limitations: Open-label; superiority design, not non-inferiority, so similarity to PF is not established; small sample; Chinese patients only
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 leukopenia 2.5% vs 7.1% vs 21%; mucositis 1.3% vs 2.4% vs 8.6%; esophagotracheal fistula 1.3% vs 3.5% vs 0; no AE deaths

records.title: Hulscher (Dutch THTC)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · Randomised clinical trial · 2002
records.body: Resectable mid-to-distal oesophageal or gastric-cardia adenocarcinoma involving the distal oesophagus, without distant metastases or unresectable local disease; fit for surgery; no prior gastric/oesophageal surgery or neoadjuvant therapy Limited transhiatal oesophagectomy without formal lymphadenectomy (single procedure) vs extended transthoracic oesophagectomy with en-bloc two-field lymphadenectomy (single procedure) Primary: Overall survival, disease-free survival. Secondary: Early postoperative morbidity, in-hospital mortality, quality-adjusted survival, cost-effectiveness, disease-free interval Extended transthoracic resection did not improve the primary ITT OS comparison versus limited transhiatal resection (median 2.0 vs 1.8 years; 5-year 39% vs 29%; absolute-difference 95% CI -3 to 23), and DFS also did not reach statistical significance. Pulmonary complications were 57% vs 27% and in-hospital mortality 4% vs 2%; any survival trend remained inconclusive at median 4.7 years' follow-up.

records.title: JCOG9501
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2008
records.body: Potentially curable gastric adenocarcinoma, intraoperatively confirmed T2b/T3/T4 with no gross para-aortic nodal metastases and negative peritoneal cytology; age <75 years; Borrmann type 4 excluded D2 gastrectomy (single procedure) vs D2 gastrectomy + para-aortic nodal dissection (single procedure); no adjuvant therapy before recurrence Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Recurrence-free survival, surgery-related complications, hospital death Adding PAND to D2 did not improve final modified-ITT OS (HR for death 1.03, 95% CI 0.77-1.37) or recurrence-free survival (HR 1.08, 95% CI 0.83-1.42). Overall surgery-related complications were 28.1% vs 20.9%, minor complications 20.0% vs 9.1%, and hospital death 0.8% in both arms. D2 was already the regional standard; the result supports not extending it with PAND in experienced centres.

records.title: Dutch D1D2 (Songun)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · Randomised clinical trial · 2010
records.body: Histologically proven gastric adenocarcinoma without distant metastases and suitable for D1 or D2 lymphadenectomy; curative-intent analysis required a macroscopically removable tumour without peritoneal, hepatic or distant-nodal metastases at laparotomy D1 gastrectomy vs D2 gastrectomy (single procedure) Primary: Overall survival, recurrence. Secondary: Disease-free survival, cause-specific death, postoperative mortality, complications, reoperation D2 reduced local recurrence and gastric-cancer death (37% vs 48%) versus D1, but excess operative harm offset these gains: the final modified-ITT 15-year OS difference did not reach statistical significance (29% vs 21%; HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.78-1.09). Operative mortality was 10% vs 4%, complications 43% vs 25% and reoperation 18% vs 8%.

records.title: TIME
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · Randomised clinical trial · 2012
records.body: Resectable intrathoracic oesophageal or GEJ cancer, cT1-3 N0-1 M0, with adenocarcinoma, squamous or undifferentiated histology; age 18-75 years; cervical oesophageal cancer excluded Open transthoracic oesophagectomy with two-field resection (single procedure) vs minimally invasive thoracoscopic/laparoscopic oesophagectomy with two-field resection (single procedure) Primary: Postoperative pulmonary infection. Secondary: Hospital stay, quality of life, pathology, operative outcomes, non-pulmonary complications, ICU stay, mortality, pain Minimally invasive oesophagectomy reduced pulmonary infection within 2 weeks (9% vs 29%) and during admission (12% vs 34%), shortened median stay (11 vs 14 days), and improved several 6-week quality-of-life domains. R0 resection, retrieved nodes, reoperation and short-term mortality were not clearly different; the trial did not test long-term oncologic equivalence.

records.title: CLASS-01
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · Randomised clinical trial · 2019
records.body: Resectable cT2-4aN0-3M0 gastric adenocarcinoma (AJCC7 stages IB-IIIC, excluding T1/T4b) in the middle or lower stomach, planned for curative distal gastrectomy with D2 dissection; bulky regional nodes >3 cm or distant metastases excluded Laparoscopic vs open distal gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy (single procedure) Primary: 3-year disease-free survival. Secondary: 3-year overall survival, recurrence patterns, intraoperative and postoperative morbidity and mortality Laparoscopic distal gastrectomy met the 3-year DFS noninferiority margin in the primary analysis set (76.5% vs 77.8%); 3-year OS was 83.1% vs 85.2%. In a post hoc sensitivity excluding pathologic stage I, the lower confidence bound crossed the noninferiority margin.

records.title: KLASS-01
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · Randomised clinical trial · 2019
records.body: Resectable clinical stage I gastric adenocarcinoma suitable for distal gastrectomy: cT1N0M0, cT1N1M0 or cT2aN0M0; excluded prior chemotherapy/radiotherapy, another malignancy or need for combined resection other than cholecystectomy Laparoscopic vs open radical distal gastrectomy with D1+beta or D2 lymphadenectomy and partial omentectomy (single procedure) Primary: 5-year overall survival. Secondary: Gastric cancer-specific survival, morbidity and mortality, quality of life, cost-effectiveness, recurrence Laparoscopic distal gastrectomy met the prespecified 5-year OS noninferiority criterion (94.2% vs 93.3%); gastric cancer-specific survival and recurrence were similar. In-hospital deaths were reported in 4 vs 2 patients.

records.title: KLASS-02
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · Randomised clinical trial · 2020
records.body: Resectable gastric adenocarcinoma planned for curative distal subtotal gastrectomy, clinical T2-4a with no or limited perigastric nodal metastasis; excluded possible distant metastasis, prior gastric resection, gastric-cancer complications or prior gastric chemo/radiotherapy Laparoscopic vs open radical distal gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy and total omentectomy (single procedure) Primary: 3-year relapse-free survival. Secondary: Postoperative morbidity and mortality, postoperative recovery, quality of life, 3-year overall survival, recurrence Laparoscopic distal gastrectomy met the reported 3-year RFS noninferiority conclusion (80.3% vs 81.3%; HR 1.04), but event maturity was truncated at 165 of 330 planned events and longer follow-up was needed. Early (15.7% vs 23.4%) and late complications (4.7% vs 9.5%) were lower; no baseline subgroup interaction supported a treatment mandate.

records.title: V325
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line chemotherapy backbone — HER2-negative · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2006
records.body:
Histologically proven gastric or esophagogastric junction adenocarcinoma; untreated advanced disease, first-line, no prior palliative chemotherapy; measurable and/or assessable metastatic disease (WHO) or locally recurrent disease with one or more measurable lymph nodes, Karnofsky performance status higher than 70; excluded concurrent cancer, neuropathy, brain or leptomeningeal involvement, uncontrolled significant comorbidity, and patients who could potentially undergo resection after response Ⓐ Docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV + cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV day 1, then fluorouracil 750 mg/m²/d continuous IV infusion days 1 to 5, every 3 weeks (DCF)
Ⓑ Cisplatin 100 mg/m² day 1 + fluorouracil 1,000 mg/m²/d days 1 to 5, every 4 weeks (CF)
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, death or consent withdrawal Primary: time to progression. Secondary: overall survival, overall response rate, time to 5% definitive deterioration in global health status (EORTC QLQ-C30), time to definitive worsening of Karnofsky performance status, safety Adding docetaxel to CF significantly improved TTP, survival and response rate in untreated advanced gastric cancer, with increased toxicity
・TTP: Ⓐ 5.6 vs Ⓑ 3.7 mo; HR 1.47 (95% CI 1.19 to 1.82), favouring DCF
・OS: Ⓐ 9.2 vs Ⓑ 8.6 mo (median follow-up 23.4 mo); HR 1.29 (95% CI 1.0 to 1.6); curves converged near the median; 2-yr OS Ⓐ18% vs Ⓑ9%
・ORR: Confirmed, Ⓐ 37% vs Ⓑ 25%
・QoL: Time to deterioration of global health status and to definitive worsening of Karnofsky PS longer with DCF
・Toxicity: Related G3–4 AEs Ⓐ69% vs Ⓑ59%; neutropenia Ⓐ82% vs Ⓑ57%; diarrhea Ⓐ19% vs Ⓑ8%; complicated neutropenia Ⓐ29% vs Ⓑ12%; 30-day deaths Ⓐ23 (10%) vs Ⓑ19 (8%), mainly infection in DCF cycle one
records.keywords: Van Cutsem et al. J Clin Oncol 2006;24:4991-4997  17075117

records.title: REAL-2
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line chemotherapy backbone — HER2-negative · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2008
records.body:
Adenocarcinoma, squamous-cell or undifferentiated carcinoma of the esophagus, gastroesophageal junction or stomach; locally advanced (inoperable) or metastatic, previously untreated; measurable disease per RECIST, ECOG PS 0–2; positive resection margin after radical surgery (tumour within 1 mm) without measurable disease also eligible, survival only; excluded prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy (unless adjuvant with relapse outside the field), uncontrolled cardiac disease, previous or concurrent cancer Ⓐ ECF: epirubicin 50 mg/m² IV bolus + cisplatin 60 mg/m² IV day 1 + fluorouracil 200 mg/m² daily by continuous infusion
Ⓑ ECX: epirubicin + cisplatin + capecitabine 625 mg/m² twice daily continuously
Ⓒ EOF: epirubicin + oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1 + fluorouracil
Ⓓ EOX: epirubicin + oxaliplatin + capecitabine
・Duration: Every 3 weeks for a maximum of eight cycles unless progression, unacceptable toxicity, consent withdrawal or death Primary: overall survival. Secondary: overall survival among the four regimens, progression-free survival, response rate, toxic effects, quality of life Capecitabine was noninferior to fluorouracil and oxaliplatin was noninferior to cisplatin for OS in previously untreated advanced esophagogastric cancer
・OS (capecitabine vs fluorouracil, per-protocol): HR for death 0.86 (95% CI 0.80–0.99); noninferiority margin HR 1.23
・OS (oxaliplatin vs cisplatin, per-protocol): HR for death 0.92 (95% CI 0.80–1.10); noninferiority margin HR 1.23
・OS (secondary, ITT): Ⓓ 11.2 vs Ⓐ 9.9 mo; HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.66–0.97); P=0.02, unadjusted for multiple testing
・PFS/ORR: Did not differ significantly among regimens
・Toxicity: Oxaliplatin vs cisplatin: less neutropenia, alopecia, renal toxicity, thromboembolism (7.6% vs 15.1%); more diarrhea, neuropathy; Ⓑ more neutropenia (51.1% vs 41.7%) and hand-foot syndrome (10.3% vs 4.3%) than Ⓐ
・Limitations: Secondary EOX vs ECF OS comparison used unadjusted P value
records.keywords: Cunningham et al. N Engl J Med 2008;358:36-46  18172173

records.title: GASTFOX (PRODIGE 51)
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line chemotherapy backbone — HER2-negative · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Histologically confirmed gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; locally advanced unresectable or metastatic, no previous treatment for advanced cancer (first line); HER2-negative; RECIST 1.1 measurable disease, ECOG 0-1, prior (neo)adjuvant chemoradiotherapy allowed if relapse occurred 12 months after end of treatment; excluded grade ≥2 peripheral neuropathy, cerebral or meningeal metastases, known DPD deficiency, prior docetaxel-based treatment Ⓐ Docetaxel 50 mg/m², folinic acid 400 mg/m² and oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², then 5-fluorouracil 2400 mg/m² continuous 46 h infusion, IV every 2 weeks
Ⓑ Folinic acid 400 mg/m², oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², 5-fluorouracil bolus 400 mg/m², then 5-fluorouracil 2400 mg/m² continuous 46 h infusion, IV every 2 weeks
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, investigator decision or patient refusal Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, safety, quality of life, therapeutic index ratio, disease control rate TFOX improved PFS, OS and ORR vs FOLFOX in previously untreated advanced HER2-negative gastric/GOJ adenocarcinoma
・PFS: Ⓐ 7.59 vs Ⓑ 5.98 mo (median); proportional hazards violated, so 12-mo RMST Ⓐ 7.52 vs Ⓑ 6.62 mo (p=0.0072)
・OS: Ⓐ 15.08 vs Ⓑ 12.65 mo; HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.68–0.99); p=0.048
・ORR: Ⓐ 62.3% vs Ⓑ 53.4%; p=0.045
・Subgroups: Greater OS benefit with ECOG 0 or age <70 years (post-hoc exploratory finding)
・Toxicity: G3–4 neuropathy Ⓐ 32% vs Ⓑ 20%; neutropenia Ⓐ 27% vs Ⓑ 18%; diarrhoea Ⓐ 15% vs Ⓑ 7%; febrile neutropenia Ⓐ 3% vs Ⓑ 2%; serious treatment-related AEs Ⓐ 27% vs Ⓑ 13%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 2 vs Ⓑ 1
・Limitations: Open-label, single-country trial; findings do not apply to patients with prior FLOT for resectable disease

records.title: GO2
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line chemotherapy backbone — HER2-negative · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body:
Locally advanced and/or metastatic gastroesophageal cancer; not pretreated, palliative chemotherapy; no biomarker selection (ERBB2-positive could add trastuzumab); oncologist considered full-dose standard combination chemotherapy unsuitable because of advanced age and/or frailty, no chronological age limit or fixed PS threshold, fit for the treatments of the selected randomization; CHEMO-BSC entry when the indication for chemotherapy was uncertain Ⓐ Oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² day 1 + capecitabine 625 mg/m² twice daily days 1-21, 21-day cycles (Level A)
Ⓑ Level B (80% of Level A doses)
Ⓒ Level C (60% of Level A doses)
Ⓓ Best supportive care alone
・Duration: Until radiological or clinical progression, unacceptable toxic effects or patient choice (chemotherapy arms)
・ERBB2-positive disease: Optional trastuzumab Primary: progression-free survival (CHEMO-INTENSITY), overall survival (CHEMO-BSC). Secondary: overall treatment utility, toxic effects, symptoms (QLQ-C30/OG25), quality of life, RECIST response, overall survival, quality-adjusted survival, time to deterioration of fatigue (CHEMO-INTENSITY); patient-reported fatigue, quality of life (CHEMO-BSC) Reduced-intensity oxaliplatin/capecitabine (Levels B and C) was non-inferior to full-intensity Level A for PFS, under a permissive margin, with less toxicity
・PFS: HR Ⓑ vs Ⓐ 1.09 (95% CI 0.89-1.32); Ⓒ vs Ⓐ 1.10 (95% CI 0.90-1.33); noninferiority margin HR 1.34
・OS: No evidence higher dose improved OS; Ⓒ vs Ⓐ HR 1.14 (95% CI 0.92-1.41)
・OTU: Ⓒ more good (43%) and fewer poor (29%) outcomes than Ⓐ or Ⓑ; not statistically significant
・Other comparison: Exploratory Ⓒ vs Ⓓ (n=45); OS nonsignificantly longer: 6.1 vs 3.0 mo; HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.32-1.48)
・Subgroups: No subgroup benefited from higher doses
・Toxicity: G≥3 nonhematological (within 9 wk) Ⓐ 38% vs Ⓑ 36% vs Ⓒ 23%; completed 3 cycles without reduction/stoppage Ⓐ 32% vs Ⓑ 44% vs Ⓒ 58%
records.keywords: Hall et al. JAMA Oncol 2021 (online ahead of print)

records.title: RELIGHT
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line chemotherapy backbone — HER2-negative · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
HER2-negative gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma, unresectable locally advanced or metastatic; previously untreated, first-line; any PD-L1 expression (stratified by CPS ≥5 vs <5); prior neoadjuvant/adjuvant therapy allowed if recurrence or progression interval ≥6 months; conducted at 64 centers across China Ⓐ Retlirafusp alfa 30 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks + CAPOX (capecitabine 1,000 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1–14 + oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1, every 3 weeks) for up to six cycles; retlirafusp alfa for up to 2 years or until progression or unacceptable toxicity
Ⓑ Matching placebo IV every 3 weeks + CAPOX on the same schedule
・Design: Double-blind Primary: overall survival in PD-L1 CPS ≥5 and overall populations. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, duration of response, safety Retlirafusp alfa plus CAPOX prolonged OS versus placebo plus CAPOX at the interim analysis
・OS (PD-L1 CPS ≥5): Ⓐ 16.8 vs Ⓑ 10.4 mo; HR 0.53
・OS (ITT): Ⓐ 15.8 vs Ⓑ 11.2 mo; HR 0.66
・PFS (ITT, BICR): Ⓐ 7.0 vs Ⓑ 5.5 mo; HR 0.57
・ORR: Ⓐ 53.4% vs Ⓑ 32.8%
・Subgroups: PD-L1 CPS <1, OS worse with Ⓐ; Ⓐ 8.1 vs Ⓑ 12.8 mo; HR 2.22
・Toxicity: G≥3 TRAEs Ⓐ 62.6% vs Ⓑ 59.0%; serious TRAEs Ⓐ 34.9% vs Ⓑ 24.0%; discontinuation Ⓐ 10.4% vs Ⓑ 3.0%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 7 (1.9%) vs Ⓑ 4 (1.1%)
・Limitations: Interim analysis (median follow-up 13.6 mo); Chemotherapy-alone comparator (not PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy); Chinese patients only
records.keywords: Peng et al. J Clin Oncol 2026 (online ahead of print)  42784781

records.title: Shitara et al.
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line chemotherapy backbone — HER2-negative · Network meta-analysis · 2026
records.body:
Locally advanced unresectable or metastatic gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma, HER2-negative or unknown HER2 status; first-line; RCTs of zolbetuximab or ICI plus chemotherapy in global trials, analysed by PD-(L)1 CPS ≥1 to <5, ≥5 to <10 and ≥10 (TAP used for tislelizumab); CLDN18.2 status not evaluated in ICI trials; Asia-only trials excluded Ⓐ Zolbetuximab + CAPOX/FOLFOX
Ⓑ Pembrolizumab + CF/CAPOX (CF/CX/CAPOX for CPS ≥10)
Ⓒ Tislelizumab + CF/CAPOX
Ⓓ Nivolumab + CAPOX/FOLFOX
Ⓔ Chemotherapy alone (common comparator)
・Design: Network meta-analysis; chemotherapy backbones assumed interchangeable Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: treatment ranking (SUCRA) Zolbetuximab + chemotherapy had similar or numerically favourable OS and PFS vs ICI + chemotherapy at CPS 1 to <10; ICIs were favourable at CPS ≥10
・PFS (CPS ≥5 to <10): Ⓐ vs Ⓑ HR 0.75 (95% CrI 0.53, 1.06); not significant
・PFS (CPS ≥1 to <5): Ⓐ vs Ⓒ HR 0.73 (95% CrI 0.54, 0.97)
・OS (CPS ≥10): Ⓐ vs Ⓒ HR 1.36 (95% CrI 0.98, 1.87)
・OS (CPS ≥10, optimal zolbetuximab exposure): Ⓐ 0.67 vs Ⓑ 0.67 vs Ⓒ 0.57 vs Ⓓ 0.68 (HR vs Ⓔ chemotherapy); selection bias possible
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: ITT zolbetuximab HR applied to every CPS stratum; CLDN18.2 not evaluated in most trials; most network links rest on a single trial

records.title: ToGA
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · HER2-positive disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2010
records.body:
Histologically confirmed inoperable locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic adenocarcinoma of the stomach or gastro-oesophageal junction; first-line; centrally tested HER2-positive: IHC 3+ or FISH positive (HER2:CEP17 ratio ≥2); ECOG 0–2, measurable or non-measurable disease; excluded previous chemotherapy for metastatic disease, congestive heart failure, LVEF <50% or other significant cardiac disease, active gastrointestinal bleeding, brain metastases Ⓐ Trastuzumab 8 mg/kg IV day 1 of cycle 1, then 6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal of consent, plus chemotherapy
Ⓑ Chemotherapy alone
・Chemotherapy: Investigator's choice of capecitabine 1000 mg/m² orally twice daily for 14 days then 1-week rest, or fluorouracil 800 mg/m²/day continuous IV infusion days 1–5, with cisplatin 80 mg/m² IV day 1, every 3 weeks for six cycles Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, time to progression, overall tumour response rate, duration of response, safety Adding trastuzumab to chemotherapy improved overall survival in HER2-positive advanced gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction cancer
・OS: Ⓐ 13·8 vs Ⓑ 11·1 mo; HR 0·74 (95% CI 0·60–0·91); p=0·0046 (75%-of-events interim analysis, deemed final; n=584)
・PFS: Ⓐ 6·7 vs Ⓑ 5·5 mo; HR 0·71 (95% CI 0·59–0·85)
・ORR: Ⓐ 47% vs Ⓑ 35%
・Subgroups: Benefit concentrated in IHC 2+/FISH-positive or IHC 3+ tumours (post-hoc exploratory; n=446; OS Ⓐ 16·0 vs Ⓑ 11·8 mo; HR 0·65, 95% CI 0·51–0·83), not in IHC 0/1+/FISH-positive tumours (n=131; HR 1·07, 95% CI 0·70–1·62); interaction p=0·036
・Toxicity: Grade 3/4 AEs Ⓐ 68% vs Ⓑ 68%; diarrhoea Ⓐ 9% vs Ⓑ 4%; treatment-related mortality Ⓐ 3% vs Ⓑ 1%
・Limitations: Open-label, without independent response review

records.title: KEYNOTE-811
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · HER2-positive disease · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body:
Gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; previously untreated unresectable or metastatic disease, first-line; HER2-positive by central review (IHC 3+ or IHC 2+ with positive ISH/FISH), unselected for PD-L1 CPS; measurable disease per RECIST v1.1, ECOG 0 or 1, life expectancy >6 months; excluded previous therapy for advanced disease, previous checkpoint inhibitor, active CNS metastases, active autoimmune disease Ⓐ Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks
Ⓑ Placebo IV every 3 weeks
・Backbone: Trastuzumab 8 mg/kg IV loading dose then 6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks + investigator's choice of fluorouracil 800 mg/m² IV days 1–5 and cisplatin 80 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks, or capecitabine 1000 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1–14 and oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks
・Duration: Up to 35 cycles (about 2 years) or until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, investigator decision or withdrawal of consent
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, safety Adding pembrolizumab to first-line trastuzumab and chemotherapy improved PFS; OS improvement not established at interim analyses
・PFS (2nd interim): Ⓐ 10.0 vs Ⓑ 8.1 mo; HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.60–0.87); superiority criteria met
・PFS (3rd interim, final PFS): Ⓐ 10.0 vs Ⓑ 8.1 mo; HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.61–0.87)
・OS (3rd interim): Ⓐ 20.0 vs Ⓑ 16.8 mo; HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.70–1.01); not significant, continues to final analysis
・ORR (2nd interim): Ⓐ 72.6% vs Ⓑ 59.8%; CR Ⓐ 14% vs Ⓑ 11%
・DoR (2nd interim): Ⓐ 11.2 vs Ⓑ 9.0 mo
・Subgroups: PD-L1 CPS ≥1 (3rd interim): PFS HR 0.71 (0.59–0.86), OS HR 0.81 (0.67–0.98); CPS <1: PFS HR 1.03 (0.65–1.64); not powered
・Toxicity: G≥3 TRAEs Ⓐ 58% vs Ⓑ 51%; G≥3 immune-mediated Ⓐ 10% vs Ⓑ 3%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 1% vs Ⓑ 1%
・Limitations: Interim analysis with immature OS; small CPS <1 subgroup; only 15% received cisplatin-based chemotherapy

records.title: DESTINY-Gastric04
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · HER2-positive disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
HER2-positive gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; unresectable or metastatic, second line after progression on trastuzumab-based therapy; HER2 IHC 3+ or IHC 2+ and ISH-positive, locally or centrally confirmed on a tumour biopsy taken after that progression; excluded history of noninfectious ILD/pneumonitis needing glucocorticoids, or current or suspected ILD/pneumonitis at screening Ⓐ Trastuzumab deruxtecan 6.4 mg/kg IV day 1 of each 21-day cycle
Ⓑ Ramucirumab 8 mg/kg IV days 1 and 15 plus paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle
・Duration: Until disease progression, consent withdrawal, physician decision or unacceptable adverse events Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, confirmed objective response, disease control, duration of response, safety, quality of life Trastuzumab deruxtecan significantly prolonged OS and PFS vs ramucirumab plus paclitaxel in HER2-positive metastatic gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma at interim analysis
・OS: Ⓐ 14.7 vs Ⓑ 11.4 mo; HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.55–0.90); interim analysis (median follow-up 16.8 vs 14.4 mo)
・PFS: Ⓐ 6.7 vs Ⓑ 5.6 mo; HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.59–0.92)
・ORR: Ⓐ 44.3% vs Ⓑ 29.1% (confirmed, response-eligible); median DoR Ⓐ 7.4 vs Ⓑ 5.3 mo
・Toxicity: Drug-related G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 50.0% vs Ⓑ 54.1%; ILD/pneumonitis Ⓐ 13.9% vs Ⓑ 1.3% (Ⓐ grade 3 in 1; Ⓑ grade 3 in 2, grade 5 in 1); drug-related deaths Ⓐ 1.6% vs Ⓑ 0.9%
・Limitations: Open-label; subgroups not powered; 25.8% of controls crossed to trastuzumab deruxtecan or disitamab vedotin

records.title: HERIZON-GEA-01
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · HER2-positive disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
HER2-positive adenocarcinoma of the stomach, gastroesophageal junction or esophagus; unresectable locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic, previously untreated (first-line); centrally confirmed HER2 IHC 3+ or IHC 2+ with ISH-positive status, PD-L1 not required; excluded prior systemic therapy for advanced disease and any prior HER2-targeted agent or checkpoint inhibitor Ⓐ Zanidatamab 1800 mg (<70 kg) or 2400 mg (≥70 kg) IV + tislelizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks + investigator's-choice chemotherapy
Ⓑ Zanidatamab 1800 mg (<70 kg) or 2400 mg (≥70 kg) IV every 3 weeks + the same chemotherapy
Ⓒ Trastuzumab 8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg every 3 weeks + the same chemotherapy
・Chemotherapy: Investigator's-choice capecitabine–oxaliplatin or fluorouracil–cisplatin in 21-day cycles
・Duration: Chemotherapy could be stopped after six cycles at physician discretion Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival, confirmed objective response rate, duration of response, safety, complete response rate Zanidatamab-based chemotherapy, with or without tislelizumab, improved PFS over trastuzumab-chemotherapy; interim OS was improved with the tislelizumab-containing regimen but not with zanidatamab-chemotherapy alone
・PFS: Ⓐ 12.4 vs Ⓒ 8.1 mo (HR 0.63; 95% CI 0.51–0.78; P<0.001); Ⓑ 12.4 vs Ⓒ 8.1 mo (HR 0.65; 95% CI 0.52–0.81; P<0.001); mFU 25.9 mo
・OS (interim): Ⓐ 26.4 vs Ⓒ 19.2 mo (HR 0.72; 95% CI 0.57–0.90; P=0.004); Ⓑ 24.4 mo (HR 0.80; 95% CI 0.64–1.01; P=0.06; not significant)
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 83.3% vs Ⓑ 73.8% vs Ⓒ 74.5%; G≥3 diarrhoea Ⓐ 24.8% vs Ⓑ 20.0% vs Ⓒ 12.9%; drug-related G5 events Ⓐ 2.4% vs Ⓑ 0.3% vs Ⓒ 1.3%
・Limitations: Comparator did not include pembrolizumab; subgroup analyses were exploratory; Ⓑ vs Ⓒ OS not significant at this interim, further analyses planned

records.title: CheckMate 649
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line immunotherapy — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (HER2-negative) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body:
Gastric, gastro-oesophageal junction or oesophageal adenocarcinoma; previously untreated, unresectable advanced or metastatic (first-line); enrolled regardless of PD-L1 expression, primary population amended to PD-L1 CPS ≥5; prior adjuvant/neoadjuvant therapy allowed if given ≥6 months before randomisation, unknown HER2 status allowed; excluded known HER2-positive status, untreated CNS metastases, peripheral neuropathy >grade 1, autoimmune disease, hepatitis B/C or HIV Ⓐ Nivolumab 360 mg IV every 3 weeks or 240 mg IV every 2 weeks (maximum 2 years) plus investigator's choice of chemotherapy
Ⓑ Chemotherapy alone
・Chemotherapy: XELOX (capecitabine 1000 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1–14, oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² day 1, every 3 weeks) or FOLFOX (leucovorin 400 mg/m² day 1, fluorouracil 400 mg/m² day 1 and 1200 mg/m² days 1–2, oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² day 1, every 2 weeks)
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, consent withdrawal or study end Primary: overall survival, progression-free survival in PD-L1 CPS five or more. Secondary: overall survival in PD-L1 CPS one or more, overall survival in all randomised patients, progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, landmark survival rates, predictive biomarkers, health-related quality of life, time to symptom deterioration, safety and tolerability Nivolumab plus chemotherapy improved OS and PFS versus chemotherapy alone in PD-L1 CPS ≥5, meeting both primary endpoints
・OS (CPS ≥5, interim): Ⓐ 14·4 vs Ⓑ 11·1 mo; HR 0·71 (98·4% CI 0·59–0·86)
・PFS (CPS ≥5, interim): Ⓐ 7·7 vs Ⓑ 6·0 mo; HR 0·68 (98% CI 0·56–0·81)
・OS (CPS ≥1 and ITT): HR 0·77 and 0·80 respectively
・ORR (CPS ≥5): Ⓐ 60% vs Ⓑ 45%
・Subgroups: Exploratory unstratified OS HR 0·92 (95% CI 0·70–1·23) CPS <1, 0·94 (0·78–1·13) CPS <5; significant interaction at CPS cutoff of five
・Toxicity: G3–4 treatment-related AEs Ⓐ 59% vs Ⓑ 44%; discontinuation Ⓐ 36% vs Ⓑ 24%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 16 (2%) vs Ⓑ four (1%)
・Limitations: PFS benefit in CPS ≥1 and ITT not formally tested

records.title: KEYNOTE-859
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line immunotherapy — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (HER2-negative) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body:
Gastric or gastro-esophageal junction adenocarcinoma; locally advanced unresectable or metastatic, previously untreated (first-line); HER2-negative (IHC 0 or 1+, or ISH HER2:CEP17 <2 with average HER2 copy number <4·0 signals/cell), any PD-L1 CPS with tissue adequate for PD-L1 assessment; excluded squamous cell or undifferentiated gastric cancer, active CNS metastases, active autoimmune disease requiring treatment, immunodeficiency, HBV, active HCV or HIV Ⓐ Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV day 1 every 3 weeks for up to 35 cycles (approximately 2 years) + investigator's-choice chemotherapy
Ⓑ Placebo IV every 3 weeks for up to 35 cycles + the same chemotherapy
・Chemotherapy: Fluorouracil 800 mg/m² per day IV days 1–5 + cisplatin 80 mg/m² IV day 1, or capecitabine 1000 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1–14 + oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1 (platinum could be limited to six cycles per local guidelines)
・Duration: Until progression, unacceptable toxicity or completion of maximum cycles Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, safety, quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC QLQ-STO22), time to deterioration Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy improved OS versus chemotherapy alone across the ITT and PD-L1-selected populations at 4.5-year follow-up
・OS (ITT): Ⓐ 12.9 vs Ⓑ 11.5 mo; HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.70-0.86); 48-mo OS 14% vs 8%
・OS (CPS≥1): Ⓐ 13.0 vs Ⓑ 11.4 mo; HR 0.74
・OS (CPS≥10): Ⓐ 15.8 vs Ⓑ 11.8 mo; HR 0.64
・PFS: Ⓐ 6.9 vs Ⓑ 5.6 mo; HR 0.76
・ORR: Ⓐ 51.1% vs Ⓑ 42.0%
・Subgroups: CPS<1 unstratified OS HR 0.92 (95% CI 0.73-1.17) at interim; CPS 1-9 analyses post-hoc, not powered
・Toxicity: Grade 3-5 treatment-related AEs Ⓐ 59.4% vs Ⓑ 51.3%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 1.0% vs Ⓑ 2.0%; grade 3-5 immune-mediated AEs/infusion reactions Ⓐ 10.1% vs Ⓑ 2.0%; serious treatment-related AEs Ⓐ 23% vs Ⓑ 19% at interim
・Limitations: CPS 1-9 and CPS<1 analyses post-hoc/underpowered; toxicity figures from an earlier interim cut, not the 4.5-yr OS/PFS/ORR cut
