records.title: RATIONALE-305
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line immunotherapy — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (HER2-negative) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body:
HER2-negative locally advanced unresectable or metastatic gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; first line, no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease (prior neoadjuvant/adjuvant therapy allowed after a progression-free interval of at least six months); any PD-L1 expression; excluded active leptomeningeal disease or uncontrolled brain metastasis, active autoimmune disease, need for systemic corticosteroids/immunosuppressants, prior checkpoint inhibitor Ⓐ Tislelizumab 200 mg IV every three weeks + investigator's choice chemotherapy every three weeks (capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily days 1-14 + oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² day 1, or 5-fluorouracil 800 mg/m² days 1-5 + cisplatin 80 mg/m² day 1) for up to six cycles → tislelizumab ± optional capecitabine maintenance (capecitabine/oxaliplatin patients only)
Ⓑ Placebo + same chemotherapy and maintenance
・Duration: Until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; may stop after two years with CR, PR or SD Primary: overall survival (PD-L1 TAP score ≥5% and all randomised patients). Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, clinical benefit rate, time to response, duration of response, safety and tolerability, health related quality of life Tislelizumab plus chemotherapy significantly improved OS vs placebo plus chemotherapy in PD-L1 TAP ≥5% and in all randomised patients
・OS (TAP ≥5%): Ⓐ 17.2 vs Ⓑ 12.6 mo; HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.59-0.94) at interim; HR 0.71 at final-analysis update
・OS (all randomised, final, ≥24.6 mo follow-up): Ⓐ 15.0 vs Ⓑ 12.9 mo; HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.70-0.92)
・24-month OS: Ⓐ 33% vs Ⓑ 23%
・PFS (investigator-assessed): HR 0.67 (TAP ≥5%); HR 0.78 (all randomised)
・ORR (TAP ≥5%): Non-significant gain
・Subgroups: TAP <5% (exploratory, not powered for testing) OS HR 0.92 (95% CI 0.75-1.13)
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 TRAEs Ⓐ 54% vs Ⓑ 50%; serious TRAEs Ⓐ 23% vs Ⓑ 15%; discontinuation for TRAEs Ⓐ 16% vs Ⓑ 8%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ six of 498 vs Ⓑ two of 494; grade ≥3 immune-mediated AEs Ⓐ 8% vs Ⓑ 2%
・Limitations: No independent review of tumour response

records.title: SPOTLIGHT
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Claudin 18.2-positive disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body:
Gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; previously untreated, locally advanced unresectable or metastatic; CLDN18.2-positive (≥75% of tumour cells with moderate-to-strong membranous CLDN18 staining by central IHC, VENTANA CLDN18 [43-14A] assay) and HER2-negative; radiologically evaluable disease (measurable or non-measurable) per RECIST 1.1 Ⓐ Zolbetuximab IV 800 mg/m² cycle 1 day 1, then 600 mg/m² every 3 weeks + mFOLFOX6 for four 42-day cycles → zolbetuximab ± folinic acid and fluorouracil (investigator's discretion)
Ⓑ Placebo + mFOLFOX6 on the same schedule
・Duration: Until disease progression, toxic effects, start of another anticancer treatment or other protocol discontinuation criteria
・mFOLFOX6: Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², folinic acid 400 mg/m², fluorouracil 400 mg/m² bolus then 2400 mg/m² over 46–48 h; days 1, 15 and 29 Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, time to confirmed deterioration, objective response, duration of response, safety, tolerability, patient-reported outcomes, pharmacokinetics, immunogenicity Zolbetuximab plus mFOLFOX6 improved PFS and OS vs placebo plus mFOLFOX6 in CLDN18.2-positive, HER2-negative advanced gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma
・PFS: Ⓐ 10·61 vs Ⓑ 8·67 mo; HR 0·75 (95% CI 0·60–0·94); p=0·0066
・OS (interim): Ⓐ 18·23 vs Ⓑ 15·54 mo; HR 0·75 (95% CI 0·60–0·94); p=0·0053 vs prespecified boundary p=0·0135
・Subgroups: GEJ subgroup too small for conclusions
・Toxicity: G≥3 TEAEs Ⓐ 87% vs Ⓑ 78%; nausea Ⓐ 82% vs Ⓑ 61%; vomiting Ⓐ 67% vs Ⓑ 36% (mainly first cycle); discontinuation Ⓐ 14% vs Ⓑ 2%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 2% vs Ⓑ 1%
・Limitations: OS is from an interim analysis; final OS analysis planned after 396 deaths; testing of time to confirmed deterioration pending

records.title: GLOW
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Claudin 18.2-positive disease · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body:
Gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma; previously untreated locally advanced unresectable or metastatic, first-line; CLDN18.2-positive (≥75% of tumour cells with moderate-to-strong membranous CLDN18 staining, central IHC) and HER2-negative; RECIST 1.1 evaluable disease, ECOG 0 or 1, prior (neo)adjuvant therapy completed ≥6 months before randomisation; excluded CNS metastases, gastric outlet syndrome with persistent vomiting, peripheral sensory neuropathy grade >1 Ⓐ Zolbetuximab 800 mg/m² IV day 1 of cycle 1 → 600 mg/m² IV day 1 of subsequent cycles
Ⓑ Placebo, in identical volumes, routes and schedules
・CAPOX: Capecitabine 1,000 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1–14 + oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1, for eight 21-day cycles
・Duration: Beyond eight cycles, zolbetuximab or placebo (± capecitabine at investigator's discretion) until progression, unacceptable toxicity, another anticancer treatment or other protocol discontinuation criteria
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, time to confirmed deterioration in EORTC global health status/quality of life, physical functioning and abdominal pain and discomfort, objective response rate, duration of response, safety and tolerability, additional patient-reported outcomes, pharmacokinetics, immunogenicity Adding zolbetuximab to CAPOX improved PFS and OS vs placebo plus CAPOX in CLDN18.2-positive, HER2-negative G/GEJ adenocarcinoma
・PFS: Ⓐ 8.21 vs Ⓑ 6.80 mo; HR 0.687 (95% CI 0.544–0.866)
・OS (interim): Ⓐ 14.39 vs Ⓑ 12.16 mo; HR 0.771 (95% CI 0.615–0.965)
・ORR: Ⓐ 42.5% vs Ⓑ 40.3%; DoR Ⓐ 6.14 vs Ⓑ 6.08 mo; responses similar between arms
・Subgroups: PFS HR 1.351 (95% CI 0.731–2.496) in GEJ primaries; subgroups underpowered
・Toxicity: G≥3 TEAEs Ⓐ 72.8% vs Ⓑ 69.9%; nausea Ⓐ 68.5% vs Ⓑ 50.2%; vomiting Ⓐ 66.1% vs Ⓑ 30.9%; grade 5 TRAEs Ⓐ 2.4% vs Ⓑ 2.8%
・Limitations: OS interim analysis; quality-of-life (time to deterioration) results not yet reported; no nivolumab-containing arm

records.title: REGARD
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Second-line & later — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2014
records.body:
Metastatic or unresectable, locally recurrent gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; second line, progression within 4 months of last dose of first-line platinum- or fluoropyrimidine-containing chemotherapy for metastatic disease, or within 6 months of such adjuvant treatment; measurable or evaluable disease; excluded grade ≥3 GI bleeding within 3 months, arterial thromboembolic event within 6 months, poorly controlled hypertension Ⓐ Ramucirumab 8 mg/kg IV once every 2 weeks
Ⓑ Placebo IV once every 2 weeks
・BSC: Best supportive care in both arms, excluding other antineoplastic treatment
・Duration: Until radiographically confirmed progression, unacceptable toxicity or death
・Design: Double-blind; no crossover Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, 12 week progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, quality of life, safety, ramucirumab immunogenicity, disease control rate, duration of disease control, time to deterioration in ECOG performance status Ramucirumab monotherapy improved overall survival vs placebo in advanced gastric/GOJ adenocarcinoma progressing after first-line chemotherapy
・OS: Ⓐ 5.2 vs Ⓑ 3.8 mo; HR 0.776 (95% CI 0.603–0.998)
・PFS: Ⓐ 2.1 vs Ⓑ 1.3 mo; HR 0.483 (95% CI 0.376–0.620)
・12-wk PFS: Ⓐ 40.1% vs Ⓑ 15.8%
・ORR: Ⓐ 3% vs Ⓑ 3% (p=0.76); disease control rate Ⓐ 49% vs Ⓑ 23%
・Time to ECOG PS ≥2: Ⓐ 5.1 vs Ⓑ 2.4 mo; HR 0.586 (95% CI 0.414–0.829)
・QoL: Stable/improved global QoL at 6 weeks numerically favoured Ⓐ, not significant (p=0.23); data provided by only Ⓐ 48% vs Ⓑ 25%
・Subgroups: OS attenuated in women, HR 1.431 (95% CI 0.852–2.405); men HR 0.676 (95% CI 0.499–0.916); sex difference not significant (p=0.063)
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 57% vs Ⓑ 58%; hypertension Ⓐ 16% vs Ⓑ 8% (G≥3 Ⓐ 8% vs Ⓑ 3%); treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 2% vs Ⓑ 2%
・Limitations: Placebo comparator; sparse quality-of-life data; relatively few Asian patients enrolled

records.title: RAINBOW
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Second-line & later — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2014
records.body:
Metastatic or non-resectable locally advanced gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; second line; progression during or within 4 months of last dose of first-line platinum plus fluoropyrimidine doublet with or without anthracycline; excluded squamous or undifferentiated histology, GI perforation, fistulae or arterial thromboembolism within 6 months, significant GI bleeding or venous thromboembolism within 3 months, or poorly controlled hypertension Ⓐ Ramucirumab 8 mg/kg IV days 1 and 15 + paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle
Ⓑ Placebo IV days 1 and 15 + paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal of consent Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, EORTC QLQ-C30, EQ-5D-3L, immunogenicity, safety, duration of response Ramucirumab plus paclitaxel improved overall survival vs placebo plus paclitaxel after first-line chemotherapy
・OS: Ⓐ 9·6 vs Ⓑ 7·4 mo; HR 0·807 (95% CI 0·678–0·962); p=0·017
・12-mo OS: Ⓐ 40% vs Ⓑ 30%
・PFS: Ⓐ 4·4 vs Ⓑ 2·9 mo; HR 0·635
・ORR: Ⓐ 28% vs Ⓑ 16%
・Subgroups: OS HR 0·986 (95% CI 0·727–1·337) in Asian region 3 vs 0·732 (0·591–0·907) in regions 1 and 2
・QoL: Similar between groups (descriptive)
・Toxicity: G≥3 neutropenia Ⓐ 41% vs Ⓑ 19%; febrile neutropenia Ⓐ 3% vs Ⓑ 2%; G≥3 hypertension Ⓐ 14% vs Ⓑ 2%; fatigue Ⓐ 12% vs Ⓑ 5%; fatal AEs attributed to study drug Ⓐ 6 (2%) vs Ⓑ 5 (2%); G≥3 GI perforation only with Ⓐ (4 patients, one death)

records.title: TAGS
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Second-line & later — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body:
Histologically confirmed non-resectable metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (AJCC 7th edition); two or more prior regimens for advanced disease including a fluoropyrimidine, a platinum agent, and a taxane and/or irinotecan, plus anti-HER2 therapy if HER2 positive and available; radiological progression within 3 months of the last dose of the last therapy or intolerance of it; ECOG 0–1; excluded CNS metastasis, other active malignancy Ⓐ Trifluridine/tipiracil 35 mg/m² orally twice daily on days 1–5 and 8–12 of each 28-day cycle plus best supportive care
Ⓑ Placebo orally twice daily on the same schedule plus best supportive care
・Duration: Until disease progression, intolerable toxicity or patient withdrawal
・Design: Double-blind Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, safety, tolerability, objective response rate, disease control rate, time to deterioration of ECOG performance status, health-related quality of life Trifluridine/tipiracil improved OS vs placebo in heavily pretreated advanced gastric cancer
・OS: Ⓐ 5.7 vs Ⓑ 3.6 mo; HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.56–0.85)
・12-mo OS: Ⓐ 21% vs Ⓑ 13%
・PFS: Ⓐ 2.0 vs Ⓑ 1.8 mo; HR 0.57; medians confounded by first tumour assessment at about 8 weeks
・Time to ECOG deterioration ≥2: Ⓐ 4.3 vs Ⓑ 2.3 mo; HR 0.69
・ORR: Ⓐ 4% vs Ⓑ 2%; not significant (p=0.28)
・Disease control: Ⓐ 44% vs Ⓑ 14% among assessable patients
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 AEs Ⓐ 80% vs Ⓑ 58%, mainly neutropenia 34% and anaemia 19%; grade ≥3 febrile neutropenia 2%; serious AEs Ⓐ 43% vs Ⓑ 42%; one treatment-related death in each arm

records.title: ATTRACTION-2 (ONO-4538-12)
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Second-line & later — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body:
Unresectable advanced or recurrent gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; refractory to, or intolerant of, standard therapy including two or more previous chemotherapy regimens; unselected for PD-L1 tumour expression; aged ≥20 years, ECOG 0–1, life expectancy ≥3 months; excluded: previous anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1/PD-L2, anti-CD137 or anti-CTLA-4 antibodies, autoimmune or interstitial lung disease, symptomatic or treated brain metastases Ⓐ Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks
Ⓑ Placebo (saline) IV every 2 weeks
・Duration: Until investigator-assessed progression or toxicity requiring permanent discontinuation; continuation beyond first progression allowed with clinical benefit and tolerance
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response, disease control, duration of response, time to response, best overall response, maximum percentage change from baseline in the sum of diameters of target lesions, overall survival by PD-L1 expression, overall survival by previous ramucirumab treatment, adverse events, treatment-related adverse events Nivolumab improved overall survival vs placebo in heavily pretreated advanced gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction cancer
・OS: Ⓐ 5.26 vs Ⓑ 4.14 mo; HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.51–0.78)
・12-mo OS: Ⓐ 26.2% vs Ⓑ 10.9%
・PFS: Ⓐ 1.61 vs Ⓑ 1.45 mo; HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.49–0.75)
・ORR: Ⓐ 11.2% vs Ⓑ 0% in patients with target lesions; median DoR 9.53 mo with nivolumab
・Subgroups: Exploratory post-hoc PD-L1 ≥1%: HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.21–1.25); <1%: HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.49–1.05); small subsets
・Toxicity: Grade 3 or 4 TRAEs Ⓐ 10% vs Ⓑ 4%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 2% vs Ⓑ 1%; interstitial lung disease among serious TRAEs
・Limitations: Asian sites only (Japan, South Korea, Taiwan); median OS gain 1.1 mo; no quality-of-life data

records.title: Li et al.
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Second-line & later — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Histologically or cytologically confirmed unresectable, recurrent or metastatic gastric cancer; second line after progression on fluoropyrimidine- or fluoropyrimidine plus platinum-based first-line therapy; ECOG PS ≤2 and ≥1 RECIST 1.1 measurable lesion; excluded squamous cell or undifferentiated gastric cancer and taxane use within 12 months before first dosing Ⓐ Paclitaxel oral solution 200 mg/m² orally twice daily on days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle
Ⓑ Paclitaxel injection (Taxol) 175 mg/m² IV on day 1 of a 21-day cycle Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, disease control rate, safety, pharmacokinetics Oral paclitaxel was non-inferior to IV paclitaxel for PFS and improved OS in second-line gastric cancer
・PFS: Ⓐ 3.02 vs Ⓑ 2.89 mo (BIRC, 31 Jan 2022 cut); HR 0.894 (95% CI 0.719-1.112); upper bound below 1.18 noninferiority margin
・OS: Ⓐ 9.13 vs Ⓑ 6.54 mo (final, 15 Feb 2023 cut); HR 0.770 (95.5% CI 0.635-0.934)
・ORR: Ⓐ 13.6% vs Ⓑ 9.8% (confirmed)
・Toxicity: G≥3 TRAEs Ⓐ 66.8% vs Ⓑ 71.8%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 4 (1.5%) vs Ⓑ 3 (1.1%); Ⓐ more dose interruptions (46.8% vs 9.8%), diarrhea (32.5% vs 8.3%), febrile neutropenia (7.2% vs 4.1%); Ⓑ more peripheral sensory neuropathy (22.3% vs 38.7%), hypersensitivity (0.0% vs 3.4%)
・Limitations: Open-label; three-weekly control no longer standard in many regions, where weekly paclitaxel plus ramucirumab is reference; conducted only in Chinese patients

records.title: KEYNOTE-590
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal & GEJ — first-line immunotherapy · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body:
Oesophageal adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma, or Siewert type 1 gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; previously untreated locally advanced unresectable or metastatic disease, first-line; enrolled regardless of PD-L1 status (tissue sample required); ECOG 0–1, measurable disease per RECIST 1.1; excluded known HER2-positive tumour, disease resectable or potentially curable with radiation, active autoimmune disease, non-infectious pneumonitis Ⓐ Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks
Ⓑ Saline placebo IV every 3 weeks
・Chemotherapy: 5-fluorouracil 800 mg/m² IV days 1–5 plus cisplatin 80 mg/m² IV day 1 every 3 weeks (for a maximum of six cycles)
・Duration: Up to 35 cycles or until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, complete response or withdrawal
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled; no crossover Primary: overall survival (ESCC with PD-L1 CPS ≥10, ESCC, CPS ≥10, all randomised), progression-free survival (ESCC, CPS ≥10, all randomised). Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, health-related quality of life, safety and tolerability At first interim analysis, pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy improved OS and PFS vs placebo plus chemotherapy in ESCC, CPS ≥10 and all randomised patients
・OS (ESCC CPS ≥10): Ⓐ 13.9 vs Ⓑ 8.8 mo; HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.43–0.75)
・OS (ESCC): Ⓐ 12.6 vs Ⓑ 9.8 mo; HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.60–0.88)
・OS (CPS ≥10): Ⓐ 13.5 vs Ⓑ 9.4 mo; HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.49–0.78)
・OS (all randomised): Ⓐ 12.4 vs Ⓑ 9.8 mo; HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.62–0.86); 24-mo OS Ⓐ 28% vs Ⓑ 16%
・PFS (ESCC): Ⓐ 6.3 vs Ⓑ 5.8 mo; HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.54–0.78)
・PFS (CPS ≥10): Ⓐ 7.5 vs Ⓑ 5.5 mo; HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.41–0.65)
・PFS (all randomised): Ⓐ 6.3 vs Ⓑ 5.8 mo; HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.55–0.76)
・ORR (all randomised): Ⓐ 45.0% vs Ⓑ 29.3%; difference 15.8% (95% CI 9.0–22.5); DoR Ⓐ 8.3 vs Ⓑ 6.0 mo
・Subgroups: CPS <10 (exploratory) OS HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.68–1.10), PFS HR 0.80 (0.64–1.01); adenocarcinoma OS HR 0.74 (0.54–1.02)
・Toxicity: G≥3 TRAEs Ⓐ 72% vs Ⓑ 68%; treatment-related deaths 2% vs 1%; G≥3 immune-mediated AEs 7% vs 2%; AE discontinuation 24% vs 20%
・Limitations: Interim analysis; subgroups not powered or multiplicity-adjusted; no PD-L1 stratification

records.title: ESCORT-1st
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma — first-line chemoimmunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body:
Histologically or cytologically confirmed esophageal squamous cell carcinoma; unresectable locally advanced or recurrent disease precluding esophagectomy or definitive chemoradiation, or distant metastatic disease; first-line, no previous systemic therapy (progression ≥6 months after [neo]adjuvant therapy or definitive chemoradiation allowed); tumour sample for PD-L1 assessment required; age 18-75, ECOG 0-1; excluded CNS metastases, active or prior autoimmune disease, other malignancies Ⓐ Camrelizumab 200 mg IV day 1 every 3 weeks until progression, unacceptable toxicity, consent withdrawal, death or new antitumour therapy + paclitaxel 175 mg/m² and cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV day 1 every 3 weeks for up to 6 cycles
Ⓑ Placebo (double-blind) on the same schedule + the same paclitaxel-cisplatin Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, duration of response, probability of overall survival, adverse events, health-related quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30, QLQ-OES18) Adding camrelizumab to paclitaxel-cisplatin improved OS and PFS vs placebo-chemotherapy in untreated advanced/metastatic ESCC
・OS: Interim analysis (median follow-up 10.8 mo); Ⓐ 15.3 vs Ⓑ 12.0 mo; HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.56-0.88)
・PFS: Final analysis, IRC-assessed; Ⓐ 6.9 vs Ⓑ 5.6 mo; HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.46-0.68)
・ORR: Exploratory secondary endpoint, investigator-assessed; Ⓐ 72.1% vs Ⓑ 62.1%
・Subgroups: OS HR 0.59 for PD-L1 TPS ≥1% vs 0.79 (95% CI 0.57-1.11) for <1%; interaction test not significant (P=.32), no definite PD-L1 association
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 TRAEs Ⓐ 63.4% vs Ⓑ 67.7%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 3.0% vs Ⓑ 3.7%; treatment-related serious AEs Ⓐ 30.2% vs Ⓑ 23.2% (mostly pneumonitis); reactive capillary endothelial proliferation Ⓐ 79.9% vs Ⓑ 10.8% (mostly grade 1-2; grade 3 1.0%)
・Limitations: Interim OS analysis; post-progression crossover to checkpoint inhibitors in placebo arm may affect OS estimates

records.title: ORIENT-15
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma — first-line chemoimmunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body:
Unresectable locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma unsuitable for curative surgery or definitive chemoradiotherapy; first line, no previous systemic treatment (progression >6 months after (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy or definitive chemoradiotherapy allowed); PD-L1 tumour sample required, not selected; excluded aorta or trachea invasion, hepatic metastasis >50% of liver volume, active autoimmune disease, ILD requiring corticosteroids Ⓐ Sintilimab IV 3 mg/kg (<60 kg) or 200 mg (≥60 kg) day 1 every three weeks + investigator-chosen cisplatin 75 mg/m² day 1 plus paclitaxel (87.5 mg/m² days 1 and 8 of cycle 1; 175 mg/m² day 1 thereafter) or 5-fluorouracil 800 mg/m² continuous infusion days 1-5, chemotherapy for a maximum of six cycles → sintilimab alone
Ⓑ Placebo with the same chemotherapy and schedule
・Duration: Sintilimab until progression or intolerable toxicity, maximum 24 months Primary: overall survival (all patients and PD-L1 CPS ≥10). Secondary: objective response rate, progression-free survival, disease control rate, duration of response, safety, health-related quality of life Sintilimab plus cisplatin-paclitaxel significantly improved OS and PFS vs placebo plus chemotherapy as first-line treatment
・OS: Ⓐ 16.7 vs Ⓑ 12.5 mo (interim); HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.51–0.78)
・PFS: Ⓐ 7.2 vs Ⓑ 5.7 mo; HR 0.56
・ORR: Ⓐ 66% vs Ⓑ 45%
・Subgroups: PD-L1 CPS ≥10: OS Ⓐ 17.2 vs Ⓑ 13.6 mo; HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.48–0.85)
・Toxicity: G≥3 TRAEs Ⓐ 60% vs Ⓑ 55%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 3% vs Ⓑ 2%; G≥3 immune-related AEs Ⓐ 10% vs Ⓑ 2%; discontinuation for TRAEs Ⓐ 21% vs Ⓑ 12%
・Limitations: Cisplatin–5-fluorouracil subgroup small and exploratory (43/659; OS HR 0.31, 95% CI 0.08–1.20); 640/659 enrolled in China, limiting applicability to Western populations

records.title: RATIONALE-306
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma — first-line chemoimmunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body:
Unresectable locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma; first-line (no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease), not amenable to definitive therapy; any PD-L1 expression; prior neoadjuvant/adjuvant platinum allowed if treatment-free interval ≥6 months; excluded symptomatic/treated brain or leptomeningeal metastases, untreatable complete obstruction, fistula, active autoimmune disease, prior PD-1/PD-L1/PD-L2 therapy Ⓐ Tislelizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks + investigator-chosen chemotherapy
Ⓑ Placebo IV every 3 weeks + investigator-chosen chemotherapy
・Chemotherapy: Cisplatin 60–80 mg/m² IV day 1 or oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1, plus fluorouracil 750–800 mg/m² IV days 1–5, capecitabine 1000 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1–14, or paclitaxel 175 mg/m² IV day 1, in 21-day cycles
・Duration: Until progression, unacceptable toxicity, death or consent withdrawal; platinum could stop after six cycles; tislelizumab/placebo could stop after 2 years with CR, PR or stable disease
・Design: Double-blind Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall response rate, overall survival in PD-L1 TAP score ≥10% subgroup, duration of response, safety, health-related quality of life Tislelizumab plus chemotherapy improved overall survival vs placebo plus chemotherapy as first-line treatment; interim analysis met superiority boundary (primary analysis)
・OS: Ⓐ 17.2 vs Ⓑ 10.6 mo; stratified HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.54–0.80)
・PFS: Ⓐ 7.3 vs Ⓑ 5.6 mo (investigator-assessed); HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.52–0.75)
・ORR: Ⓐ 63% vs Ⓑ 42%
・Subgroups: OS HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.44–0.87) with PD-L1 TAP ≥10%; HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.59–1.01) with TAP <10%, favourable but non-significant (exploratory); post-hoc interaction testing showed no significant difference by PD-L1 status
・Toxicity: G≥3 TRAEs Ⓐ 67% vs Ⓑ 64%; serious TRAEs Ⓐ 29% vs Ⓑ 19%; treatment-related discontinuation Ⓐ 29% vs Ⓑ 19%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ six vs Ⓑ four (Ⓐ included GI haemorrhage n=2, myocarditis n=1)

records.title: CheckMate 648
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma — first-line chemoimmunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body:
Unresectable advanced, recurrent or metastatic oesophageal squamous-cell or adenosquamous carcinoma not amenable to curative treatment; no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease; enrolled regardless of PD-L1 Ⓐ Nivolumab 240 mg IV q2w + cisplatin/fluorouracil
Ⓑ Nivolumab 3 mg/kg q2w + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg q6w
Ⓒ Cisplatin/fluorouracil
・Duration: Immunotherapy ≤2 y; treatment otherwise until progression/toxicity/withdrawal/trial end Primary: overall survival, progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, safety, PFS2 Nivolumab plus chemotherapy and nivolumab plus ipilimumab both significantly prolonged OS vs chemotherapy at 5-year minimum follow-up
・OS (PD-L1 ≥1%, 5-yr follow-up): Ⓐ 15.0 vs Ⓑ 13.1 vs Ⓒ 9.1 mo; HR 0.62 (both); 5-yr OS Ⓐ 12% vs Ⓑ 18% vs Ⓒ 7%
・OS (ITT, 5-yr follow-up): Ⓐ 13.2 vs Ⓑ 12.7 vs Ⓒ 10.7 mo; HR 0.77 (both)
・PFS (PD-L1 ≥1%, 5-yr follow-up): Ⓐ 6.8 vs Ⓒ 4.4 mo; HR 0.67
・PFS (ITT): Ⓐ vs Ⓒ did not meet its significance criterion
・PFS (PD-L1 ≥1%, 5-yr follow-up): Ⓑ vs Ⓒ failed; HR 1.03; overall PFS testing stopped
・PFS2 (exploratory): Favoured Ⓐ and Ⓑ vs Ⓒ
・Toxicity: G3-4 treatment-related events Ⓐ 49% vs Ⓑ 33% vs Ⓒ 37%; treatment-related deaths 2% in each arm
records.keywords: Doki et al. N Engl J Med 2022;386:449-462  35108470 Kato et al. Ann Oncol 2026 (online ahead of print)  42575473

records.title: ATTRACTION-3
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal squamous — second-line immunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body:
Unresectable advanced or recurrent oesophageal squamous or adenosquamous cell carcinoma (cervical/thoracic, incl. OGJ); refractory or intolerant to one previous fluoropyrimidine- and platinum-based regimen (progression during or ≤8 weeks after last dose, or ≤24 weeks after CR or R0 neoadjuvant/adjuvant therapy); regardless of PD-L1 expression; excluded taxane-refractory disease, prior nivolumab or T-cell-regulating therapy, adjacent-organ invasion, interstitial lung disease Ⓐ Nivolumab 240 mg IV every 2 weeks
Ⓑ Investigator's choice of paclitaxel 100 mg/m² IV weekly for 6 weeks then 1 week off or docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks
・Duration: Until investigator-assessed progression (RECIST 1.1) or unacceptable toxicity Primary: overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, best overall response, progression-free survival, disease control rate, maximum percentage change from baseline in sum of target lesion diameters, time to response, duration of response, quality of life (EQ-5D-3L), safety Nivolumab improved overall survival versus chemotherapy in previously treated advanced oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma
・OS: Ⓐ 10.9 vs Ⓑ 8.4 mo; HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.62–0.96), p=0.019; minimum follow-up 17.6 mo
・PFS: Ⓐ 1.7 vs Ⓑ 3.4 mo; HR 1.08 (95% CI 0.87–1.34), no significant difference; curves favoured Ⓐ beyond 5 months
・ORR: Ⓐ 19% vs Ⓑ 22% of response-evaluable patients; median DoR Ⓐ 6.9 vs Ⓑ 3.9 mo
・Subgroups: OS benefit regardless of tumour PD-L1 expression
・QoL: Exploratory EQ-5D-3L favoured Ⓐ
・Toxicity: Grade 3–4 treatment-related AEs Ⓐ 18% vs Ⓑ 63%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 2 (interstitial lung disease, pneumonitis) vs Ⓑ 3
・Limitations: Open-label; 96% Asian population; OS curves crossed, difference supported by post-hoc weighted log-rank test

records.title: DRAGON-01
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Peritoneal metastasis — intraperitoneal (bidirectional) therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Histologically confirmed gastric adenocarcinoma with laparoscopically confirmed peritoneal metastasis; first-line, no prior anticancer therapy; ERBB2-negative; age 18 to 75 years, ECOG 0 to 1; excluded extraperitoneal distant metastases (ovarian involvement alone permitted) and gastric outlet or bowel obstruction Ⓐ IV paclitaxel 50 mg/m² plus IP paclitaxel 20 mg/m² (via IP port) days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle plus oral S-1 80 mg/m² once daily days 1 to 14
Ⓑ IV paclitaxel 70 mg/m² days 1 and 8 plus S-1 80 mg/m² once daily days 1 to 14
・Duration: Until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal
・Conversion surgery: Considered when protocol criteria met (gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy), then protocol chemotherapy resumed Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, safety, conversion surgery rate, major pathological response rate, adverse events, R0 resection rate, peritoneal cytology conversion, postoperative complications, post-progression survival Ⓐ IV plus IP paclitaxel plus S-1 improved OS over Ⓑ IV paclitaxel plus S-1
・OS: Ⓐ 19.4 vs Ⓑ 13.9 mo; HR 0.67 (95% CI 0.50-0.90); follow-up 72.2 mo
・3-yr OS: Ⓐ 25.0% vs Ⓑ 12.2%
・PFS: Ⓐ 11.2 vs Ⓑ 7.2 mo; HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.54-0.96)
・Conversion surgery: Ⓐ 50.7% vs Ⓑ 35.1%
・Toxicity: Grade 3-4 AEs Ⓐ 38.5% vs Ⓑ 41.9%; no treatment-related deaths; port-related complications in 27.0% of Ⓐ, 10.8% requiring surgical intervention
・Limitations: Open-label; Chinese centers only; chemotherapy backbone does not reflect current first-line standards; surgery-stratified OS comparisons are post hoc and hypothesis-generating

records.title: PERISCOPE II
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Peritoneal metastasis — intraperitoneal (bidirectional) therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Resectable cT3 or cT4a gastric adenocarcinoma with limited peritoneal metastases (PCI <7) or tumour-positive peritoneal cytology or both; metastatic setting after three or more cycles of systemic therapy without RECIST disease progression; complete criteria in appendix (pp 5–6) Ⓐ Continuation of palliative systemic therapy
Ⓑ (Partial) gastrectomy with cytoreductive surgery plus HIPEC: intraperitoneal oxaliplatin 460 mg/m² at 41°C for 30 min then docetaxel 50 mg/m² at 37°C for 90 min; surgery within 12 weeks of last systemic course; PCI ≥7 or unresectable disease found intraoperatively did not proceed to HIPEC Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, Treatment-related toxicity, Health-related quality of life Gastrectomy with cytoreductive surgery plus HIPEC did not improve OS versus systemic therapy alone in gastric cancer with limited peritoneal metastases
・OS: 16.6 vs 15.7 mo; HR 1.10 (95% CI 0.69–1.74)
・PFS: 7.6 vs 9.3 mo; HR 0.93; p=0.73
・PFS (post-hoc per-protocol, exploratory): Ⓐ 7.2 vs Ⓑ 13.2 mo; HR 0.51; p=0.0092; unbalanced groups
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 20% vs Ⓑ 42%; serious AEs Ⓐ 6% vs Ⓑ 44%; 3 treatment-related deaths, all Ⓑ (ARDS, anastomotic leak, bleeding)
・Limitations: Closed early after unplanned futility interim analysis

records.title: IKF-575/RENAISSANCE
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oligometastatic disease — role of surgery · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body:
Previously untreated limited-metastatic adenocarcinoma of the stomach or esophagogastric junction; first-line systemic induction; limited metastatic disease defined as retroperitoneal lymph node (RPLN) metastases only or a maximum of one incurable organ site that is potentially resectable or locally controllable, with or without RPLN; randomized only if no progression after 4 cycles of induction FLOT Ⓐ Radical complete surgical resection of primary and metastases followed by the same systemic treatment
Ⓑ Additional FLOT
・Induction: FLOT for 4 cycles (+ trastuzumab if HER2+ or + nivolumab if PD-L1 positive)
・Design: Randomized if no progression after induction Primary: overall survival. Secondary: quality of life, R0 resection rate, 30-day and 90-day postoperative mortality, delivery of additional chemotherapy cycles Adding radical surgery after induction did not improve OS (primary endpoint not met), with increased early mortality and crossing survival curves in the surgery arm
・OS: Ⓐ 10 vs Ⓑ 14 mo (25th percentile); Ⓐ 65 vs Ⓑ 41 mo (75th percentile)
・Subgroups: RPLN-only benefited from surgery (Ⓐ 30 vs Ⓑ 17 mo mOS; 5-yr OS Ⓐ 38% vs Ⓑ 19%, still more early deaths); chemo non-responders worse with surgery (Ⓐ 13 vs Ⓑ 22 mo); peritoneal disease worse with surgery (Ⓐ 12 vs Ⓑ 19 mo)
・Toxicity: 30-d/90-d mortality in surgery population 3%/8%
・Limitations: Stopped early for slow accrual (141 randomized of 176 planned); ITT population 139
records.keywords: Al-Batran et al. J Clin Oncol 2024;42(17_suppl):LBA4001

records.title: TROG 03.01
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal — palliative radiotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body:
Biopsy-proven oesophageal cancer (excluding Seifert 2 and 3 lesions); locally advanced or metastatic, unsuitable for curative treatment, palliative setting; symptomatic dysphagia (Mellow scale grade 1–4), ECOG 0–2; excluded prior chemotherapy or chest radiotherapy for oesophageal cancer, other active malignancies, tracheo-oesophageal fistula or stent in situ Ⓐ Chemoradiotherapy: radiotherapy 35 Gy in 15 fractions over 3 weeks (Australia, New Zealand) or 30 Gy in 10 fractions over 2 weeks (Canada, UK) plus one cycle of IV cisplatin (80 mg/m² day 1 or 20 mg/m²/day days 1–4, clinician's discretion) and IV fluorouracil 800 mg/m²/day continuous infusion days 1–4 of radiotherapy
Ⓑ Radiotherapy alone (same site-based schedules) Primary: dysphagia relief. Secondary: dysphagia progression-free survival, time to achieve any response in dysphagia, time to any complete response, patient's assessment of dysphagia response, number of patients receiving secondary treatment, overall survival, quality of life, complete dysphagia relief, acute toxicity, late toxicity Chemoradiotherapy did not significantly improve dysphagia relief over radiotherapy alone, with minimal survival benefit and more toxicity
・Dysphagia relief (primary): Ⓐ 45% vs Ⓑ 35%; difference 10.6% (95% CI –2 to 23)
・Dysphagia PFS: Ⓐ 4.1 vs Ⓑ 3.4 mo; HR 0.93 (p=0.58)
・OS: Ⓐ 6.9 vs Ⓑ 6.7 mo; HR 0.98 (p=0.88)
・Toxicity: Grade 3–4 acute Ⓐ 36% vs Ⓑ 16% (p=0.0017); grade 3–4 late Ⓐ 17% vs Ⓑ 14% (p=0.83)
・Limitations: Power fell from 80% to 57% (assumed control relief 75%, observed 35%); 28% not assessable at week 13
records.keywords: Penniment et al. Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2018;3:114-124  29248399

records.title: ESPAC-1
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2004
records.body:
Histologically proven pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma; adjuvant setting after complete macroscopic (potentially curative) resection; positive or negative resection margins eligible, with randomization stratified by margin status and centre Ⓐ Chemoradiotherapy: 20 Gy in 10 daily fractions over a two-week period plus IV bolus fluorouracil 500 mg per square meter on each of the first three days of radiotherapy and again after a planned two-week break; protocol total 40 Gy
Ⓑ Chemotherapy: IV bolus leucovorin 20 mg per square meter then IV bolus fluorouracil 425 mg per square meter on 5 consecutive days every 28 days for six cycles
Ⓒ Chemoradiotherapy → Chemotherapy
Ⓓ Observation
・Design: 2×2 factorial Primary: two-year survival rate. Secondary: adverse effects, recurrence, quality of life, overall survival, time to recurrence, recurrence-free survival Adjuvant chemotherapy improved survival after pancreatic resection; adjuvant chemoradiotherapy reduced survival
・OS (chemotherapy vs none): Median 20.1 vs 15.5 mo; HR 0.71 (95% CI 0.55–0.92; P=0.009); adjusted HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.58–1.01)
・OS (chemoradiotherapy vs none): Median 15.9 vs 17.9 mo; HR 1.28 (95% CI 0.99–1.66; P=0.05); adjusted HR 1.47 (95% CI 1.10–1.95)
・QoL: No difference within 12 months
・Toxicity: Grade 3–4 AEs in 29 patients; 2 treatment-related deaths (1 Ⓐ, 1 Ⓒ)
・Limitations: Factorial design not powered for four-group comparisons; only 61 of 122 chemotherapy patients completed six cycles
records.keywords: Neoptolemos et al. N Engl J Med 2004;350:1200-1210  15028824

records.title: ESPAC-3
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2010
records.body:
Histologically confirmed pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma; adjuvant therapy after complete macroscopic (R0 or R1) resection; no malignant ascites, peritoneal metastasis or spread to the liver or other distant abdominal or extra-abdominal organs, WHO performance score of 2 or lower, life expectancy more than 3 months; excluded prior neoadjuvant or concomitant chemotherapy, pancreatic lymphoma, R2 resection or TNM stage IVb disease Ⓐ Fluorouracil plus folinic acid (folinic acid 20 mg/m² IV bolus, then fluorouracil 425 mg/m² IV bolus on 5 consecutive days every 28 days) for 6 cycles (24 weeks)
Ⓑ Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² IV infusion once a week for 3 out of every 4 weeks for 6 cycles (24 weeks) Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, Toxicity, Quality of life Adjuvant gemcitabine did not improve overall survival compared with fluorouracil plus folinic acid in completely resected pancreatic cancer
・OS: 23.0 vs 23.6 mo; HR 0.94 (95% CI 0.81-1.08); final ITT analysis, median follow-up 34.2 mo
・PFS: 14.1 vs 14.3 mo; HR 0.96 (95% CI 0.84-1.10)
・QoL: No significant difference (P=.08)
・Toxicity: Serious AEs 14% vs 7.5%; Ⓐ more G3/4 stomatitis (10% vs 0%) and diarrhoea (13% vs 2%); Ⓑ more G3/4 hematologic toxicity (P=.003)
・Limitations: Powered to detect 10% increase in 2-yr survival with gemcitabine

records.title: CONKO-001
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2007
records.body:
Histologically verified pancreatic cancer; adjuvant setting after macroscopic complete (R0 or R1) resection of T1-4 N0-1 M0 disease; no prior radiation or neoadjuvant chemotherapy, Karnofsky ≥50%; excluded postoperative CEA/CA19-9 >2.5× ULN or other prior malignancy Ⓐ Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² IV on days 1, 8 and 15 every 4 weeks for 6 cycles
Ⓑ Observation Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, treatment safety, quality of life Adjuvant gemcitabine delayed recurrence and, at final analysis, prolonged OS versus observation after complete resection of pancreatic cancer
・DFS: Ⓐ 13.4 vs Ⓑ 6.7 mo; HR 0.55
・5-yr DFS: Ⓐ 16.6% vs Ⓑ 7.0%
・10-yr DFS: Ⓐ 14.3% vs Ⓑ 5.8%
・OS (final, 136-mo follow-up; secondary, exploratory P values): Ⓐ 22.8 vs Ⓑ 20.2 mo; HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.61-0.95)
・5-yr OS: Ⓐ 20.7% vs Ⓑ 10.4%
・10-yr OS: Ⓐ 12.2% vs Ⓑ 7.7%
・OS (earlier cut, 53-mo follow-up): Not significantly different; Ⓐ 22.1 vs Ⓑ 20.2 mo; P=.06
・Toxicity: 62% of Ⓐ completed all 6 cycles; grade 3 leukopenia in 2.4% of cycles; 2 fatal events, both in Ⓐ, not considered gemcitabine-related
・QoL: No difference (Spitzer index)
・Limitations: Almost all Ⓑ patients received gemcitabine at relapse (crossover); OS not significant at earlier 53-mo cut

records.title: ESPAC-4
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body:
Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma; adjuvant, randomised within 12 weeks of complete macroscopic (R0 or R1) resection; no restriction by postoperative CA19-9; WHO performance status ≤2, clear CT chest/abdomen/pelvis within 3 months; excluded prior neoadjuvant chemotherapy, R2 resection, TNM stage IV, malignant ascites, liver or peritoneal metastasis Ⓐ Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² IV once weekly for 3 of every 4 weeks
Ⓑ Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² IV once weekly for 3 of every 4 weeks plus oral capecitabine 1660 mg/m² daily for 21 days followed by 7 days' rest
・Duration: Six cycles (24 weeks) Primary: overall survival. Secondary: survival estimates at 24 months, 5-year survival, relapse-free survival, toxicity, quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30) Adjuvant gemcitabine plus capecitabine improved overall survival vs gemcitabine alone after resection of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
・OS: Ⓑ 28.0 vs Ⓐ 25.5 mo; HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.68–0.98); p=0.032; stopped early at 458 of 480 target deaths, median follow-up 43.2 mo
・5-yr OS: Ⓑ 28.8% vs Ⓐ 16.3%
・RFS: Ⓑ 13.9 vs Ⓐ 13.1 mo; HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.73–1.02); p=0.082, not significant
・QoL: No significant difference
・Toxicity: Grade 3–4 AEs Ⓑ 226/359 vs Ⓐ 196/366; neutropenia Ⓑ 38% vs Ⓐ 24%, diarrhoea Ⓑ 5% vs Ⓐ 2%, hand-foot syndrome Ⓑ 7% vs Ⓐ 0%; one grade 5 infection (Ⓑ); all six cycles completed by 54% vs 65%
・Limitations: Stopped early before target event count; RFS not significantly improved

records.title: PRODIGE 24–ACCORD 24/CCTG PA.6
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body:
Resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma; adjuvant therapy after complete macroscopic R0 or R1 (cancer cells within 1 mm of ≥1 margin) resection 3 to 12 weeks before randomization; age 18 to 79 years, no previous chemotherapy or radiotherapy, no metastatic disease, malignant ascites or pleural effusion; excluded nonductal tumours, R2 resection, serum CA 19-9 >180 U/ml within 21 days before randomization, symptomatic heart failure or coronary heart disease Ⓐ Modified FOLFIRINOX: oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², leucovorin 400 mg/m², irinotecan 180 mg/m² (reduced to 150 mg/m² after enrollment of 162 patients per protocol-specified safety analysis) and fluorouracil 2400 mg/m² by 46-hour continuous IV infusion without bolus, every 14 days for 24 weeks (12 cycles)
Ⓑ Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² IV on days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days for 24 weeks (6 cycles) Primary: Disease-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, Metastasis-free survival, Cancer-specific survival, Safety Adjuvant modified FOLFIRINOX improved disease-free and overall survival over gemcitabine after resection of pancreatic cancer, with higher toxicity
・DFS: Ⓐ 21.6 vs Ⓑ 12.8 mo; HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.46-0.73); 3-yr DFS 39.7% vs 21.4%
・OS: Ⓐ 54.4 vs Ⓑ 35.0 mo; HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.48-0.86); immature (61% alive)
・Subgroups: In patients ≥70 yr (n=101), DFS benefit not significant; Ⓐ vs Ⓑ HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.53-1.39)
・Toxicity: Grade 3-4 AEs Ⓐ 75.9% vs Ⓑ 52.9% (diarrhea 18.6% vs 3.7%; paresthesia 12.7% vs 0); 1 treatment-related death (interstitial pneumonitis) with Ⓑ; G-CSF used in 62.2% of Ⓐ; planned cycles completed 66.4% vs 79.0%; oxaliplatin neuropathy persisted at 3 yr in 2 patients
・Limitations: OS data immature; analysis brought forward on DMC recommendation at 314 DFS events
records.keywords: Conroy et al. N Engl J Med 2018;379:2395-2406  30575490

records.title: APACT
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body:
Histologically confirmed ductal pancreatic adenocarcinoma; adjuvant, treatment-naive after macroscopic complete (R0/R1) resection, starting therapy ≤12 weeks after surgery; serum CA19-9 <100 U/mL and no recurrence on CT/MRI at screening, ECOG PS ≤1; no prior neoadjuvant, radiation or systemic therapy for PDAC and no history of metastatic or locally recurrent disease Ⓐ Nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² IV → gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² IV on days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle
Ⓑ Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² IV on days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle
・Duration: Six cycles unless radiologic recurrence, unacceptable toxicity or patient/physician decision
・Design: Open-label Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, Safety Nab-paclitaxel + gemcitabine did not improve independently assessed DFS vs gemcitabine alone; OS was longer in descriptive analyses
・DFS (independent, primary cutoff): Ⓐ 19.4 vs Ⓑ 18.8 mo; HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.729-1.063; P=.18)
・DFS (investigator, descriptive): Ⓐ 16.6 vs Ⓑ 13.7 mo; HR 0.82
・OS (5-yr follow-up, descriptive): Ⓐ 41.8 vs Ⓑ 37.7 mo; HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.678-0.947)
・≥5-yr OS: Ⓐ 38% vs Ⓑ 31%
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 TEAEs Ⓐ 86% vs Ⓑ 68%; neutropenia Ⓐ 49% vs Ⓑ 43%; peripheral neuropathy Ⓐ 15% vs Ⓑ 0%; serious TEAEs Ⓐ 41% vs Ⓑ 23%; two patients per arm died of TEAEs
・Limitations: Primary endpoint (independent DFS) not met; investigator-assessed DFS and OS comparisons are descriptive; open-label
records.keywords: Tempero et al. J Clin Oncol 2022;41:2007-2019  36521097

records.title: JASPAC 01
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body:
Resected invasive ductal carcinoma of the pancreas, excluding cystadenocarcinoma; adjuvant after R0 or R1 resection, pathological stage I, II, or stage III with combined coeliac artery resection; negative intraoperative peritoneal lavage cytology, no distant metastasis or malignant ascites, enrolment within 10 weeks after resection, no chemotherapy or radiotherapy within past 3 years; excluded prior gemcitabine or S-1, recurrence before registration Ⓐ Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² IV on days 1, 8 and 15 every 4 weeks for up to six cycles
Ⓑ S-1 40 mg, 50 mg or 60 mg by body-surface area orally twice daily for 28 days followed by 14-day rest, every 6 weeks for up to four cycles
・Duration: Until recurrence or serious adverse events Primary: overall survival. Secondary: relapse-free survival, incidence of adverse events, health-related quality of life Adjuvant S-1 was non-inferior and superior to gemcitabine for overall survival after pancreatic cancer resection
・OS: Final analysis (per-protocol): Ⓑ 46·5 vs Ⓐ 25·5 mo; HR 0·57 (95% CI 0·44–0·72; p<0·0001 for non-inferiority and superiority)
・5-yr OS: Ⓑ 44·1% vs Ⓐ 24·4%
・RFS: 22·9 vs 11·3 mo; HR 0·60 (95% CI 0·47–0·76)
・QoL: EQ-5D did not differ within 6 months; later differences unadjusted for multiplicity
・Toxicity: Grade 3-4 leucopenia, neutropenia, AST and ALT more frequent with gemcitabine; stomatitis and diarrhoea more frequent with S-1; two grade 5 infections with gemcitabine
・Limitations: Trial stopped early after interim efficacy analysis; superiority tested in per-protocol population (consistent ITT results); all patients east Asian residents of Japan

records.title: GITSG
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemoradiation · Randomised clinical trial · 1985
records.body:
Histologically confirmed ductal, acinar or undifferentiated pancreatic adenocarcinoma; adjuvant setting after apparently curative partial or total pancreatectomy, margins free of disease, no peritoneal metastases; entry between four and ten weeks postoperatively; excluded periampullary, islet cell carcinoma and cystadenocarcinoma, prior chemotherapy within one year or prior radiation in the planned field Ⓐ Split-course radiotherapy 4,000 rad (two courses of 2,000 rad separated by two weeks, five days a week) + fluorouracil 500 mg/sq m IV bolus for three consecutive days at the start of each course, then fluorouracil once weekly for two years or until recurrence
Ⓑ Observation (no adjuvant treatment) Primary: Overall survival, Disease-free survival. Secondary: Toxicity, Treatment compliance, Radiotherapy quality assurance Adjuvant radiotherapy plus fluorouracil suggested prolonged survival after curative resection, but the small trial is not definitive
・OS: Ⓐ 20 vs Ⓑ 11 mo median; adjusted one-sided P = .03
・2-yr OS: Ⓐ .42 vs Ⓑ .15 (Kaplan-Meier)
・DFS: Ⓐ 11 vs Ⓑ 9 mo median; adjusted P = .01; curves separated only after one year
・Toxicity: Severe leukopenia in 3/21 (14%) treated patients; no life-threatening toxicity or treatment-related deaths
・Limitations: Closed early for low accrual, short of planned 100 patients, after unadjusted interim P<.05 at two analyses; 6 randomized patients excluded from analysis; retrospective review judged 6 patients (32%) to have received inappropriate radiotherapy

records.title: EORTC 40891
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemoradiation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 1999
records.body:
Histologically proven adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic head (T1-2N0-1aM0) or periampullary region (distal common bile duct, papilla of Vater or duodenum; T1-3N0-1aM0); adjuvant after Whipple or pylorus-preserving pancreatoduodenectomy, with N1a defined as positive nodes within the resection specimen; randomized after recovery, with treatment to start within 8 weeks of surgery; excluded T3 pancreatic head, T4 periampullary and N1b (nodes outside the resection area) Ⓐ Observation
Ⓑ Radiotherapy 40 Gy (2 Gy daily, 5 fractions/week for 2 weeks, repeated after a 2-week interval) starting 2 to 8 weeks after surgery, with concurrent continuous-infusion 5-FU 25 mg/kg per 24 hours (max 1500 mg/day) limited to the first week of each radiation course; second-course 5-FU given for 0, 3 or 5 days according to toxicity; no 5-FU after radiotherapy Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, toxicity, locoregional recurrence Adjuvant chemoradiotherapy with 5-FU did not significantly improve survival after resection of pancreatic head or periampullary cancer
・OS: Ⓐ 19.0 vs Ⓑ 24.5 mo; 2-yr 41% vs 51%; RR 0.8 (95% CI 0.6-1.1); p=0.208
・PFS: Ⓐ 16 vs Ⓑ 17.4 mo; 2-yr 38% vs 37%; p=0.643
・Locoregional recurrence: Not reduced by chemoradiotherapy
・Subgroups: Pancreatic head (exploratory): Ⓐ 12.6 vs Ⓑ 17.1 mo; p=0.099; too few patients for separate conclusions
・Toxicity: Worst grade 3 (mainly nausea/vomiting, 7 patients) among 81 evaluable patients; 1 major toxicity; in-hospital deaths Ⓑ 3 vs Ⓐ 0
・Limitations: 21 patients (20%) assigned to Ⓑ received no treatment; pancreatic head subgroup underpowered; only 81 of 207 patients toxicity-evaluable

records.title: RTOG 97-04
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemoradiation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2008
records.body:
Resected pancreatic adenocarcinoma, histologically confirmed; adjuvant after gross total resection (centrally reviewed), no prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy; AJCC 1997 T1–T4, N0–N1, M0, KPS ≥60, caloric intake >1500 kcal/d, CT within 3 weeks of randomization excluding persistent/recurrent local or metastatic disease, therapy 3–8 weeks after resection; excluded if no identifiable lymph nodes in the specimen Ⓐ Fluorouracil CI 250 mg/m²/day for 3 weeks → chemoradiation → fluorouracil CI 250 mg/m²/day for 12 weeks (3 months; 4 weeks on plus 2 weeks off)
Ⓑ Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² weekly for 3 weeks → same chemoradiation → gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² weekly for 12 weeks (3 months; 3 weeks on plus 1 week off)
・Chemoradiation: 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions with CI fluorouracil 250 mg/m² daily throughout Primary: overall survival (all patients), overall survival in patients with pancreatic head tumors. Secondary: disease-free survival, toxicity, site of first relapse, treatment completion Gemcitabine before and after chemoradiation did not significantly improve overall survival or DFS versus fluorouracil in this trial
・OS: No significant difference among all patients (median follow-up 1.5 yr; 4.7 yr in survivors)
・DFS: No significant difference among all patients
・Subgroups: Pancreatic head tumors (n=388) - OS Ⓐ 16.9 vs Ⓑ 20.5 mo; 3-yr OS Ⓐ 22% vs Ⓑ 31%; HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.65-1.03; P=.09); multivariate HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.63-1.00; P=.05)
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 hematologic Ⓐ 9% vs Ⓑ 58%; grade 4 Ⓐ 1% vs Ⓑ 14%, without more febrile neutropenia/infection; 1 grade 5 nonneutropenic infection with Ⓑ; chemotherapy completed as planned 90% vs 87%
・Limitations: Gemcitabine salvage at relapse in 93/113 Ⓐ-arm patients may have diluted OS effect; distant first relapse exceeded 70% in both arms

records.title: Prep-02/JSAP05
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase II/III) · 2026
records.body:
Resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, histologically or cytologically confirmed and treatment-naïve; localized with no distant metastasis, R0/R1 resectable without involvement of the hepatic, celiac or superior mesenteric arteries, candidate for curative resection; age 20–79 years, ECOG PS 0 or 1; excluded pulmonary fibrosis/interstitial pneumonia, severe diarrhea, active infection, synchronous malignancy Ⓐ Neoadjuvant gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8 + S-1 40–60 mg orally twice daily (by BSA) days 1–14 every 3 wk for 2 cycles (stopped for unacceptable toxicity such as grade 4) → surgery 2–4 wk after final S-1 dose → adjuvant S-1 for 6 months
Ⓑ Upfront surgery within 8 weeks of enrollment → adjuvant S-1 for 6 months Primary: resection rate (phase II); overall survival (phase III). Secondary: resection rate, adverse events, recurrence-free survival, patterns of recurrence, residual tumor status, nodal metastasis, tumor marker kinetics, dose intensity, radiologic response, histologic response, surgical morbidity, adjuvant chemotherapy completion Neoadjuvant gemcitabine plus S-1 improved OS vs upfront surgery in resectable PDAC
・OS: Ⓐ 37.0 vs Ⓑ 26.6 mo; HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.56–0.95); P=0.018
・RFS: Ⓐ 14.3 vs Ⓑ 11.3 mo; HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.61–0.98)
・Resection rate (phase II): Ⓐ 93% vs Ⓑ 82%
・Liver recurrence (phase II): Ⓐ 30.0% vs Ⓑ 47.9%
・Toxicity: Ⓐ Grade 3 AEs 48.8%, grade 4 23.8% (neutropenia 22.7%); no operative deaths in either arm
・Limitations: Japanese population only; optimal neoadjuvant regimen/duration undefined; some after NAC did not undergo surgery (mainly distant metastases)

records.title: SWOG S1505
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2021
records.body:
Pancreatic adenocarcinoma, histologically or cytologically confirmed (other or mixed histologies excluded); resectable, previously untreated, perioperative setting; resectable per Intergroup criteria: no celiac, common hepatic or superior mesenteric arterial interface, <180° portal/superior mesenteric vein interface, patent portal-splenic vein confluence, no metastases or lymphadenopathy outside the surgical basin; age 18-75 years, Zubrod PS 0-1 Ⓐ mFOLFIRINOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², irinotecan 180 mg/m², fluorouracil 2400 mg/m² over 46 h) every 2 weeks: 6 preoperative doses → resection → 6 postoperative doses
Ⓑ Gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel (nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m², gemcitabine 1000 mg/m²) weekly, 3 weeks on/1 week off: 9 preoperative doses → resection → 9 postoperative doses
・Design: Perioperative; resection 4-8 weeks after last preoperative dose if no RECIST progression Primary: 2-year overall survival. Secondary: toxicity, overall resection rate, R0 resection rate, pathologic response rate, disease-free survival from resection, overall response rate, node-negative resection rate, median overall survival, treatment completion, postoperative complications Perioperative mFOLFIRINOX and gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel each failed to improve 2-year OS above the prespecified 40% threshold in resectable pancreatic cancer
・2-yr OS: Ⓐ 47% (95% CI, 31%-61%) vs Ⓑ 48% (95% CI, 31%-63%); neither exceeded prespecified 40% threshold
・OS (median): Ⓐ 23.2 vs Ⓑ 23.6 mo
・Resection: Ⓐ 73% vs Ⓑ 70%; R0 85% in each arm
・DFS (median, from resection): Ⓐ 10.9 vs Ⓑ 14.2 mo
・Completion: Ⓐ 49% vs Ⓑ 40% completed all treatment
・Toxicity: Grade 3/4 mainly hematologic, fatigue, GI; neoadjuvant neutropenia Ⓐ 19% vs Ⓑ 27%; adjuvant neutropenia Ⓐ 0% vs Ⓑ 27%
・Limitations: Trial not designed for between-arm comparison; 29% of enrolled patients did not meet resectability criteria on central review

records.title: NORPACT-1
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2024
records.body:
Resectable pancreatic head tumour radiologically strongly suspected to be pancreatic adenocarcinoma; NCCN resectable: no SMV/portal vein contact or ≤180° contact without contour irregularity, no coeliac, common hepatic or superior mesenteric artery contact, no distant metastasis on CT; WHO PS 0 or 1; tissue confirmation required only in neoadjuvant arm after Dec 2017; excluded comorbidity precluding pancreatoduodenectomy, grade ≥2 neuropathy, percutaneous tumour biopsy Ⓐ Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², irinotecan 180 mg/m², leucovorin 400 mg/m², fluorouracil 400 mg/m² bolus then 2400 mg/m² over 46 h, day 1 every 14 days) × 4 cycles → surgery within 4 weeks of last infusion → adjuvant gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² days 1, 8, 15 plus capecitabine 830 mg/m² twice daily 3 of 4 weeks × 4 cycles, or after the Aug 2018 amendment modified FOLFIRINOX × 8 cycles
Ⓑ Upfront surgery within 4 weeks of randomisation → adjuvant gemcitabine plus capecitabine × 6 cycles, or after amendment modified FOLFIRINOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², irinotecan 150 mg/m², leucovorin 400 mg/m², fluorouracil 2400 mg/m² over 46 h every 14 days) × 12 cycles Primary: overall survival at 18 months. Secondary: progression-free survival at 18 months, progression-free survival, overall mortality at 1 year in patients who underwent resection, overall survival, overall survival following resection, R0 resection, (y)pN0 disease, complication rates at 90 days after surgery, feasibility of neoadjuvant and adjuvant chemotherapy, completion rates of multimodal treatment, health economics, quality of life, exploratory translational research, resection rate, grade ≥3 adverse events, postoperative mortality within 90 days, proportion alive and disease free at 18 months, radiological response, CA19-9 response Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX did not improve OS vs upfront surgery in resectable PDAC
・18-mo OS: Ⓐ 60% vs Ⓑ 73% (p=0.032)
・OS: Ⓐ 25.1 vs Ⓑ 38.5 mo; HR 1.52 (95% CI 1.00–2.33)
・PFS: Ⓐ 11.9 vs Ⓑ 16.2 mo; HR 1.30 (95% CI 0.85–1.99)
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 58% vs Ⓑ 40%; Ⓐ 2 deaths after first cycle; 90-day postoperative mortality Ⓐ 5% vs Ⓑ 2%; Ⓐ 61% (37/61) completed all 4 cycles
・Limitations: Exploratory phase 2 results not conclusive; 8% had non-PDAC pathology

records.title: PREOPANC
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant therapy — borderline resectable disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body:
Pathologically confirmed pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma; resectable or borderline resectable, M0 (TNM 7th edition), randomised before biliary drainage; resectable: no arterial involvement and venous involvement <90°; borderline: arterial involvement <90° and/or venous involvement 90°-270° without occlusion; excluded cT1 tumour (<2 cm, no vascular involvement), malignancy within 5 years, prior radiotherapy or chemotherapy precluding treatment Ⓐ Staging laparoscopy → gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² days 1 and 8 of 3 weeks → radiotherapy 15 fractions of 2.4 Gy in 3 weeks with gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² days 1, 8 and 15 of 4 weeks → gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² days 1 and 8 of 3 weeks → explorative laparotomy/resection at 14-18 weeks → adjuvant gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² days 1, 8 and 15 for 4 courses of 4 weeks
Ⓑ Immediate surgery within 4 weeks → adjuvant gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² days 1, 8 and 15 for 6 courses of 4 weeks Primary: overall survival. Secondary: disease-free survival, locoregional failure-free interval, distant metastasis-free interval, resection rate, R0 resection rate, toxicity of surgery and pre- and postoperative treatment, serious adverse events, postoperative complications, postoperative mortality, pathologic lymph nodes, perineural invasion, venous invasion Neoadjuvant gemcitabine-based CRT improved OS vs upfront surgery in resectable and borderline resectable pancreatic cancer
・OS: Ⓐ 15.7 vs Ⓑ 14.3 mo (median follow-up 59 mo); HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.56-0.96); P=.025
・5-yr OS: Ⓐ 20.5% vs Ⓑ 6.5%
・OS (initial analysis, 27 mo): Not significant; HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.58-1.05); P=.096
・DFS: HR 0.69, favoured Ⓐ
・LFFI: HR 0.57, favoured Ⓐ
・DMFI: Not significantly different; HR 0.74; P=.070
・Resection rate: Ⓐ 61% vs Ⓑ 72%; P=.058
・R0 rate: Ⓐ 71% vs Ⓑ 40% among resected patients
・Toxicity: SAEs Ⓐ 52% vs Ⓑ 41%; P=.096; grade 5 SAEs in 8 patients per arm, including 3 postoperative deaths each; postoperative complications Ⓐ 68% vs Ⓑ 50% among resected patients
・Limitations: No safety data collected after initial report

records.title: Alliance A021501
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant therapy — borderline resectable disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2022
records.body:
Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, borderline resectable (localized primary tumor with substantial radiographic interface with the major mesenteric blood vessels); neoadjuvant setting before planned pancreatectomy; disease stage confirmed by central review of all radiologic images at 2-step registration Ⓐ mFOLFIRINOX 8 cycles
Ⓑ mFOLFIRINOX 7 cycles → SBRT 33–40 Gy in 5 fractions (preferred) or HIGRT 25 Gy in 5 fractions
・mFOLFIRINOX: Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², irinotecan 180 mg/m², leucovorin 400 mg/m² IV, then fluorouracil 2400 mg/m² IV over 46 h, every 2 weeks; restaging after 4 cycles
・Surgery: Pancreatectomy within 4 to 8 weeks if no progression and ECOG PS 0 or 1
・Adjuvant: FOLFOX6 4 cycles every 2 weeks (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², leucovorin 400 mg/m², bolus fluorouracil 400 mg/m², infusional fluorouracil 2400 mg/m² over 46 h), starting 4 to 12 weeks after surgery
・Duration: Until progression, unacceptable adverse event or completion of the treatment program Primary: 18-month overall survival rate. Secondary: event-free survival, R0 resection rate, pathologic complete response rate, rate of adverse events, overall survival Neoadjuvant mFOLFIRINOX met its prespecified efficacy rule vs historical control; the hypofractionated RT arm closed for futility, its role undefined
・18-mo OS: Ⓐ 66.7% (95% CI 56.1–79.4) vs Ⓑ 47.3% (95% CI 35.8–62.5); Ⓐ deemed efficacious vs 50% historical control; Ⓑ not assessable
・Interim R0 (first 30 per arm): Ⓐ 57% vs Ⓑ 33%; Ⓑ closed for futility
・Median OS: Ⓐ 29.8 vs Ⓑ 17.1 mo; descriptive, no between-arm test
・Median EFS: Ⓐ 15.0 vs Ⓑ 10.2 mo
・Resection: Pancreatectomy Ⓐ 49% vs Ⓑ 35%; R0 among resected Ⓐ 88% vs Ⓑ 74%; pCR Ⓐ 0 vs Ⓑ 2 patients
・Toxicity: G≥3 treatment-related AEs Ⓐ 57% vs Ⓑ 64%; 1 treatment-related death (sepsis) in Ⓐ; all therapy completed Ⓐ 31% vs Ⓑ 18%
・Limitations: Each arm tested only vs historical control; Ⓑ terminated at interim; last 16 Ⓐ patients not randomised

records.title: ESPAC5
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant therapy — borderline resectable disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2023
records.body:
Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (including variants), histologically or cytologically proven, of the pancreatic head; borderline resectable by contrast-enhanced CT criteria (based on NCCN) after central review, before any resection; WHO performance status 0 or 1, fit for surgical resection, chemotherapy and radiotherapy, able to undergo biliary drainage by metal stent; excluded distant metastatic disease and previous or concurrent malignancy Ⓐ Immediate surgery
Ⓑ Neoadjuvant gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 + capecitabine 830 mg/m² orally twice a day days 1–21, 28-day cycle × 2 cycles
Ⓒ Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², irinotecan 180 mg/m², folinic acid per local practice, fluorouracil 400 mg/m² bolus then 2400 mg/m² 46 h infusion on days 1 and 15) every 2 weeks × 4 cycles
Ⓓ Neoadjuvant capecitabine-based chemoradiotherapy 50·4 Gy in 28 daily fractions over 5·5 weeks with capecitabine 830 mg/m² twice a day (Monday to Friday)
・Restaging: Neoadjuvant arms (Ⓑ Ⓒ Ⓓ) → restaging CT at 4–6 weeks → surgical exploration if no progression
・Adjuvant therapy: After resection at clinician discretion Primary: recruitment rate, resection rate. Secondary: R0 resection rate, toxicity, postoperative complication rate, 30-day postoperative mortality, response rate, disease-free survival, local disease-free survival, overall survival, quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30), event-free survival, 90-day postoperative mortality Resection rate did not differ with immediate surgery vs neoadjuvant therapy; secondary-endpoint OS favoured neoadjuvant therapy in this underpowered trial
・Recruitment: 90/100 target randomised (2·16 patients/month); feasibility endpoint not met
・Resection: Ⓐ 68% (21/31) vs pooled Ⓑ Ⓒ Ⓓ 55% (30/55); p=0·33
・R0: Ⓐ 14% (3/21) vs pooled Ⓑ Ⓒ Ⓓ 23% (7/30)
・OS (1-yr): Ⓐ 39% vs pooled Ⓑ Ⓒ Ⓓ 76%; HR 0·29 (95% CI 0·14–0·60); secondary endpoint
・OS by arm (1-yr): Ⓑ 78% vs Ⓒ 84% vs Ⓓ 60%
・DFS (1-yr, from surgery): Ⓐ 33% vs pooled Ⓑ Ⓒ Ⓓ 59%; HR 0·53 (95% CI 0·28–0·98)
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 AEs Ⓐ 7% (2/28) vs pooled Ⓑ Ⓒ Ⓓ 34% (17/50); surgical complications 43% (29/68); 90-day mortality 7% (5/68), no 30-day deaths
・Limitations: Underpowered feasibility trial; recruitment below target; short follow-up (median 12·2 mo); OS a secondary endpoint
