records.title: PREOPANC-2
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant therapy — borderline resectable disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Histologically or cytologically confirmed resectable or borderline resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma without distant metastases; previously untreated, neoadjuvant setting; resectable: no arterial involvement and <90° venous involvement; borderline: arterial involvement <90°, venous involvement 90–270° without occlusion, or both; WHO PS 0 or 1, no upper age limit; excluded prior PDAC treatment, comorbidity precluding study treatment, pregnancy Ⓐ Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², irinotecan 180 mg/m², leucovorin 400 mg/m², fluorouracil 400 mg/m² IV bolus then 2400 mg/m² continuous IV over 46 h) every 14 days for 8 cycles → surgery → no adjuvant therapy
Ⓑ Neoadjuvant gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days (days 1 and 8 only in cycles 1 and 3) for 3 cycles with hypofractionated radiotherapy 36 Gy in 15 fractions during cycle 2 only → surgery → 4 cycles adjuvant gemcitabine
・Duration: Treatment stopped early for unacceptable toxicity, progression, death or patient request Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, locoregional failure-free interval, distant metastases-free interval, disease-free survival, locoregional recurrence-free interval, treatment start rate, treatment completion rate, dose intensity, dose reduction rate, staging laparoscopy rate, staging laparoscopy yield, surgical exploration rate, resection rate, R0 resection, N0 resection, tumour size, pathological response, postoperative complications, clinical response rate, tumour marker response, adverse events, quality of life, cost-effectiveness, biomarkers, serious adverse events Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX did not improve OS compared with neoadjuvant gemcitabine-based chemoradiotherapy plus adjuvant gemcitabine in resectable or borderline resectable PDAC
・OS: Median follow-up 42.3 mo; Ⓐ 21.9 vs Ⓑ 21.3 mo; HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.69–1.13); p=0.32; 3-yr OS Ⓐ 36% vs Ⓑ 33%
・PFS: Ⓐ 12.1 vs Ⓑ 11.9 mo
・Resection: Ⓐ 77% vs Ⓑ 75%; R0 Ⓐ 60% vs Ⓑ 67%; pathological complete response did not differ
・ypN0: Ⓐ 47% vs Ⓑ 58% (higher with chemoradiotherapy)
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 AEs Ⓐ 67% vs Ⓑ 60% (p=0.20); serious AEs Ⓐ 49% vs Ⓑ 43%; grade 3–4 diarrhoea Ⓐ 23% vs Ⓑ 1%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 2 (1%) vs Ⓑ 1 (1%)
・Toxicity: Dose reductions Ⓐ 82% vs Ⓑ 27%; only 62% completed all eight FOLFIRINOX cycles

records.title: PACT-21 CASSANDRA
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant therapy — borderline resectable disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Pathologically confirmed pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma; AJCC stage I–III, resectable or borderline resectable by NCCN criteria (local investigators), preoperative setting; borderline resectable also biologically defined by CA19-9 ≥500 IU/mL; age 18–75 years, Karnofsky ≥70; DPYD/UGT dysfunctional polymorphism carriers allowed after an amendment introduced after 21 patients Ⓐ PAXG: oral capecitabine 625 mg/m² twice daily (1250 mg/m²/day) + IV cisplatin 30 mg/m², nab-paclitaxel 150 mg/m² and gemcitabine 800 mg/m² every 14 days
Ⓑ mFOLFIRINOX: IV fluorouracil 2400 mg/m², leucovorin 400 mg/m², irinotecan 150 mg/m² and oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² every 14 days
・Duration: Each arm given for 4 months
・Design: If no progression or limiting toxicity, second randomisation to 2 further months of the same chemotherapy before vs after surgery Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: radiological response rate, CA19-9 response rate, resection rate, complete pathological response rate, absence of pathological lymph-node involvement, absence of pathological resection margin infiltration, detection of metastases during or within 3 months of surgery, surgical morbidity, chemotherapy toxicity, quality of life, overall survival, disease control rate, pathological stage Preoperative PAXG improved event-free survival versus mFOLFIRINOX in resectable or borderline resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
・EFS: Ⓐ 16.0 vs Ⓑ 10.2 mo; HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.47–0.84); p=0.0018
・3-yr EFS: Ⓐ 33% vs Ⓑ 13%
・Disease control: Ⓐ 98% vs Ⓑ 91%
・Node-negative (ITT): Ⓐ 36% vs Ⓑ 23%
・Intraoperative/early postoperative metastases: Ⓐ 5% vs Ⓑ 12%
・Resection rate: Ⓐ 75% vs Ⓑ 67%; not significantly different
・ORR/margin status: Did not differ significantly
・OS: Not tested (immature); preliminary median Ⓐ 32.1 vs Ⓑ 26.4 mo
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 66% vs Ⓑ 61%; 1 treatment-related sepsis death (Ⓑ); G3 neutropenia Ⓐ 36% vs Ⓑ 24%
・Limitations: Open-label; EFS events included CA19-9 rises; no central radiology review

records.title: Burris (gemcitabine)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 1997
records.body: Symptomatic, pathologically diagnosed unresectable locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic cancer; no prior chemotherapy; Karnofsky performance status >=50 and protocol-specified organ function; symptom burden required before randomisation. Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 IV weekly (7 weeks on/1 off, then 3 weeks on/1 off; escalation to 1,250 mg/m2 allowed) versus 5-fluorouracil 600 mg/m2 IV weekly (escalation allowed but never used); until progression or clinically significant tumour-related deterioration Primary: clinical benefit response. Secondary: objective response, overall survival, time to progressive disease, safety Gemcitabine improved the principal clinical-benefit composite (23.8% versus 4.8%) and median OS (5.65 versus 4.41 months) versus weekly 5-fluorouracil. It also increased neutropenia and nausea/vomiting, without serious infections. This small 1992-1994 symptomatic population used an unvalidated clinical-benefit construct and a historical comparator; no printed alpha hierarchy, follow-up, or modern-combination comparison limits current applicability

records.title: NCIC PA.3
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2007
records.body: Locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma with measurable or assessable disease, ECOG 0-2 and adequate organ function; no prior chemotherapy except radiosensitising fluorouracil or gemcitabine; prior local radiotherapy allowed only after documented progression. Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 weekly for 7 of 8 weeks then days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days plus erlotinib 100 or 150 mg orally daily versus matched placebo; until progression or unmanageable toxicity Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response and duration, safety, quality of life, baseline EGFR correlation Adding erlotinib to gemcitabine produced a small OS difference (6.24 versus 5.91 months; HR 0.82) and PFS difference, with more grade 3-4 diarrhoea and rash and six protocol-related deaths in the erlotinib group. No global endpoint hierarchy was printed. EGFR and on-treatment rash analyses lack treatment-interaction tests, so neither supports predictive selection; the gemcitabine-era backbone and source-internal reporting conflicts further limit inference

records.title: GEM-CAP (Cunningham)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2009
records.body: Previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic ductal adenocarcinoma or undifferentiated pancreatic carcinoma not amenable to curative resection; WHO performance status 0-2 with protocol-specified organ function; no previous cancer-directed chemotherapy or radiotherapy. Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 IV weekly plus oral capecitabine 830 mg/m2 twice daily for 3 weeks of each 4-week cycle versus gemcitabine alone; until progression or intolerable toxicity. Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response, toxicity, quality of life and pain GEM-CAP did not meet its primary OS comparison (7.1 versus 6.2 months; HR 0.86; P=.08), although PFS and response were higher as nominal secondary outcomes. Grade 3-4 neutropenia, thrombocytopenia and hand-foot syndrome were more frequent with the combination. A publication-level meta-analysis cannot convert the within-trial OS result; the historical open-label backbone and unfiled appendix leave post-treatment, subgroup and detailed quality-of-life results unresolved

records.title: PRODIGE 4/ACCORD 11 (FOLFIRINOX)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2011
records.body: Metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, measurable disease, age 18-75 years, ECOG 0-1, bilirubin <=1.5 times ULN, adequate marrow and renal function, and no previous chemotherapy; selected fit first-line population. FOLFIRINOX every 2 weeks: oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, irinotecan 180 mg/m2, leucovorin 400 mg/m2, fluorouracil 400 mg/m2 bolus then 2,400 mg/m2 over 46 hours; versus gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 weekly. Six months was recommended, with stop-and-go reintroduction allowed after 12 cycles Primary: phase 2 tumour response; phase 3 overall survival. Secondary: phase 2 safety; phase 3 progression-free survival, tumour response, safety and quality of life FOLFIRINOX improved OS (11.1 versus 6.8 months; HR 0.57) and PFS versus gemcitabine in fit metastatic patients. It increased neutropenia, febrile neutropenia, diarrhoea and neuropathy; one treatment-related death occurred in each arm, while deterioration in several quality-of-life domains was delayed. Eligibility was restricted to ECOG 0-1 and age <=75 years; phase-2 patients rolled into phase 3, secondary findings were nominal and supplement details are unfiled

records.title: MPACT
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2013
records.body: Previously untreated measurable metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma diagnosed within 6 weeks, Karnofsky performance status >=70 and adequate organ function; locally advanced disease and prior cytotoxic adjuvant therapy excluded. nab-Paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 then gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days versus gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 weekly for 7 of 8 weeks then days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days; until progression or unacceptable adverse events Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival and objective response nab-Paclitaxel plus gemcitabine improved OS (8.5 versus 6.7 months; HR 0.72), independent-review PFS and response versus gemcitabine. Peripheral neuropathy, myelosuppression and fatigue were more frequent; serious adverse events were 50% versus 43% and adverse events leading to death occurred in 4% of each arm without event-specific causality, while severe neuropathy generally improved after interruption. This first-line metastatic KPS >=70 population used a historical single-agent comparator; no protected secondary hierarchy, quality-of-life assessment or subgroup interaction testing was printed

records.title: NAPOLI-3 (NALIRIFOX)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body: Treatment-naive metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with measurable disease, ECOG 0-1 and metastatic diagnosis within 6 weeks; prior adjuvant therapy permitted only when completed >12 months earlier without persistent toxicity. NALIRIFOX every 2 weeks: liposomal irinotecan 50 mg/m2, oxaliplatin 60 mg/m2, leucovorin 400 mg/m2 and fluorouracil 2,400 mg/m2 over 46 hours; versus nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 plus gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days; until progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival and objective response NALIRIFOX improved OS (11.1 versus 9.2 months; HR 0.83) and PFS versus nab-paclitaxel-gemcitabine under the prespecified sequence, but objective response was not significantly different. Gastrointestinal adverse events, hypokalaemia and treatment-related serious events were more frequent; neutropenia and neuropathy were less frequent, and treatment-related deaths occurred in 6 versus 8 patients. It applies to ECOG 0-1 measurable metastatic disease; the open-label source has unfiled protocol/SAP/appendix details and no predictive subgroup interaction results

records.title: GEST (Gemcitabine and S-1 Trial)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2013
records.body: Chemotherapy-naive patients with locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma or adenosquamous carcinoma in Japan and Taiwan; ECOG PS 0–1; no prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy; age >20 years, amended to <80 after serious adverse events in patients ≥80 Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² IV d1, 8, 15 of 28-day cycle vs S-1 orally twice daily 80/100/120 mg/d by BSA d1–28 of 42-day cycle vs gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² d1, 8 plus S-1 60/80/100 mg/d by BSA d1–14 of 21-day cycle; all cycles repeated until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or patient refusal Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, safety, quality of life First-line S-1 monotherapy was noninferior to gemcitabine for OS in locally advanced/metastatic pancreatic cancer (HR 0.96; 97.5% CI, 0.78 to 1.18; P < .001 for noninferiority), while gemcitabine plus S-1 (GS) did not significantly improve OS (HR 0.88; 97.5% CI, 0.71 to 1.08; P = .15). Median OS 8.8 months gemcitabine, 9.7 months S-1, 10.1 months GS; GS significantly improved PFS (HR 0.66; 97.5% CI, 0.54 to 0.81; P < .001). Grade ≥3 neutropenia 41.0% gemcitabine vs 8.8% S-1 vs 62.2% GS; GS had more grade ≥3 GI toxicities than gemcitabine. Noninferiority margin 1.33 may be large.
records.keywords: Ueno et al. J Clin Oncol 31:1640-1648, 2013  23547081

records.title: PANOPTIMOX (PRODIGE 35)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Maintenance therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2021
records.body: Previously untreated measurable metastatic pancreatic cancer, age <=75 years, ECOG 0-1 and adequate organ function; prior perioperative chemotherapy allowed if completed >6 months earlier. Three baseline-assigned strategies: 12 cycles FOLFIRINOX; 8 cycles FOLFIRINOX then LV5FU2 maintenance with FOLFIRINOX reintroduction at progression; or alternating FOLFIRI.3 and gemcitabine. Primary: 6-month progression-free survival rate. Secondary: overall survival, progression-free survival, best response, duration of disease control, safety, oxaliplatin dose intensity, quality of life and second-line therapy This noncomparative phase II strategy trial found that the induction-to-LV5FU2-maintenance arm met its arm-specific 6-month PFS decision rule; it was not a direct three-arm efficacy comparison. Maintenance involved later FOLFIRINOX reintroduction and greater cumulative oxaliplatin exposure, with more late grade 3-4 neuropathy; treatment-related deaths were sepsis in arm A and hypertonic coma in arm C. Median OS was descriptive across arms. Results apply to the baseline-assigned strategy in fit patients, not maintenance-only randomisation among responders; several source-internal denominator inconsistencies remain

records.title: POLO
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Maintenance therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body: Metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA1/2 mutation and no progression during >=16 weeks of continuous first-line platinum chemotherapy; protocol-specified organ and toxicity recovery criteria required. Maintenance olaparib 300 mg orally twice daily versus matching placebo, started 4-8 weeks after platinum chemotherapy and continued until investigator-assessed progression or unacceptable toxicity. Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, second progression-free survival, objective response, global quality of life and safety In the dual-selected germline BRCA/platinum-controlled population, maintenance olaparib improved blinded-central-review PFS (7.4 versus 3.8 months; HR 0.53) without a demonstrated benefit at the immature interim OS analysis. Grade >=3 adverse events, interruptions and reductions were more common with olaparib, while global quality of life did not show a clinically meaningful between-group difference. This source does not establish benefit beyond patients without progression after at least 16 weeks of platinum or final OS

records.title: CONKO-003
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Second-line therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2014
records.body: Advanced pancreatic cancer progressing during first-line gemcitabine monotherapy, measurable disease, Karnofsky performance status >=70 and protocol-specified organ function; treatment planned within 4 weeks of progression. OFF: oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2 on days 8 and 22 plus folinic acid 200 mg/m2 and 24-hour fluorouracil 2,000 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, 15 and 22; versus the same fluorouracil/folinic-acid regimen without oxaliplatin, both with best supportive care, every 6 weeks until progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: overall survival. Secondary: time to progression and tolerability After gemcitabine monotherapy, OFF improved median OS (5.9 versus 3.3 months; HR 0.66) and time to progression versus fluorouracil/folinic acid, crossing the interim-adjusted primary boundary. Neurotoxicity was substantially more common with OFF. The analysis excluded eight randomised patients and contains treated-population discrepancies; recruitment predated current first-line multiagent therapy, so it does not directly establish benefit after modern sequences or with a standard FOLFOX schedule

records.title: NAPOLI-1
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Second-line therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body: Metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma progressing after gemcitabine-based therapy; neoadjuvant or adjuvant exposure qualified only if distant metastases developed within 6 months. KPS >=70, normal bilirubin, albumin >=30 g/L and adequate marrow and renal function; prior irinotecan or fluorouracil permitted Liposomal irinotecan 80 mg/m2 plus folinic acid 400 mg/m2 and 46-hour fluorouracil 2,400 mg/m2 every 2 weeks versus version-2 fluorouracil/folinic-acid control; separate liposomal-irinotecan 120 mg/m2 every 3 weeks versus pooled control; until progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, time to treatment failure, objective response, CA19-9 response, clinical benefit response, quality of life and safety Liposomal irinotecan plus fluorouracil/folinic acid improved OS (6.1 versus 4.2 months; HR 0.67) and PFS after gemcitabine; liposomal-irinotecan monotherapy did not improve OS. The combination increased grade 3-4 neutropenia, diarrhoea, vomiting and fatigue, with one investigator-attributed treatment-related death. Combination and monotherapy used distinct amended/pool-control contexts and should not be merged; applicability immediately after FOLFIRINOX or in lower-performance patients remains unestablished

records.title: CodeBreaK 100 (sotorasib)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Biomarker-directed therapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2023
records.body: Previously treated locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic cancer with locally identified KRAS p.G12C mutation; phase 1 allowed ECOG <=2 and phase 2 ECOG 0-1. All analysed patients had metastatic disease and prior chemotherapy. Single-arm oral sotorasib 960 mg once daily until progression, unacceptable adverse effects or withdrawal; pooled pancreatic cohort from phase 1 and phase 2. Primary: phase 1 safety and recommended phase 2 dose; phase 2 objective response. Secondary: duration and time to response, disease control, progression-free survival, overall survival and safety In phase 2, sotorasib produced centrally confirmed responses in 5/26 patients (19%); pooled phase 1-2 response was 8/38 (21%), with median PFS 4.0 months and OS 6.9 months. Treatment-related adverse events were generally manageable; no treatment-related grade 4-5 event occurred, while all-cause fatal events must not be attributed to sotorasib. This small pooled, nonrandomised KRAS G12C cohort has no comparator, no response benchmark and unfiled protocol/SAP/appendix details, so it supports no comparative or predictive claim beyond the enrolled subset

records.title: RASolute 302 (daraxonrasib)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Biomarker-directed therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Previously treated measurable metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with ECOG 0-1, adequate organ function and documented RAS G12/G13/Q61 mutation or no RAS mutation identified; required progression after one fluoropyrimidine- or gemcitabine-based metastatic regimen, or metastatic relapse <6 months after perioperative therapy. Prior RAS-targeted therapy was excluded; patients without identified RAS but another actionable driver required approved targeted therapy first Daraxonrasib 300 mg orally once daily versus investigator-choice gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel, modified FOLFIRINOX, FOLFOX, or liposomal irinotecan plus fluorouracil/folinic acid; until progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal. Primary: overall survival and progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, progression-free survival, objective response, pain deterioration, global-health deterioration, time to response and safety At the first interim OS analysis, daraxonrasib improved RAS G12 OS (13.2 versus 6.6 months; HR 0.40) and final PFS (7.3 versus 3.5 months; HR 0.45) under the graphical testing plan. Treatment-related severe events, dose modifications and discontinuations were less frequent, but one related pneumonitis death occurred. Interpretation is limited by interim OS maturity, open-label differential treatment noninitiation and a multi-regimen investigator-choice control; non-G12 data are small and lack interaction evidence
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2026 (online ahead of print)  42223072

records.title: FOLFIRINOX in LAPC (Suker meta-analysis)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Locally advanced disease · Meta-analysis · 2016
records.body: Locally advanced pancreatic cancer; treatment-naive, first-line FOLFIRINOX irrespective of subsequent treatment, any age; LAPC defined by NCCN or AHPBA/SSO/SSAT criteria or multidisciplinary/retrospective imaging review, no staging laparoscopy reported; excluded other or concurrent combined chemotherapy, non-first-line FOLFIRINOX and resected-only cohorts (from survival analysis) (single-arm) First-line FOLFIRINOX (PRODIGE 4 regimen): oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² IV, leucovorin 400 mg/m² IV, irinotecan 180 mg/m² IV, then fluorouracil 400 mg/m² bolus and 2400 mg/m² 46-h continuous infusion, every 2 weeks; two studies used modified dosing (no fluorouracil bolus, or 80% dose intensity); median three to 11 cycles across studies Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, grade 3 or 4 adverse events, rate of radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy, surgical resection rate, R0 resection rate, 1-year overall survival, 2-year overall survival Patients with locally advanced pancreatic cancer treated with first-line FOLFIRINOX had a pooled patient-level median OS of 24.2 mo (95% CI 21.7–26.8), longer than reported with gemcitabine (6–13 mo); the authors state this needs confirmation in a randomised trial. Median PFS was 15.0 mo (13.7–16.3); OS was 79.5% at 1 yr and 50.1% at 2 yr. Pooled resection rate was 25.9%, with R0 in 78.4% of resections; 63.5% received radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy (I² 90%). All included studies were non-randomised and most were retrospective, with differing definitions of locally advanced disease; the favourable OS may partly reflect patient selection. In ten studies (490 patients), 296 grade 3 or 4 adverse events were reported (60.4 per 100 patients); the pooled neutropenia rate was 19.6 per 100. No deaths were attributed to FOLFIRINOX, but toxicity is probably underestimated.

records.title: LAP07
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Locally advanced disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body: Locally advanced pancreatic cancer, histologically or cytologically confirmed stage III (UICC); untreated, with no prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy; measurable or evaluable disease (RECIST 1.0) and WHO PS ≤2; second randomisation limited to patients progression-free with WHO PS ≤2 after 4 months of gemcitabine-based induction First randomisation: gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² IV weekly for 3 weeks then 1-week rest, for 4 cycles vs the same gemcitabine plus erlotinib 100 mg orally once daily; second randomisation (progression-free after induction): 2 months of the same chemotherapy vs chemoradiotherapy 54 Gy in 30 daily fractions over 6 weeks with capecitabine 800 mg/m² twice daily on radiation days; erlotinib maintenance 150 mg daily for progression-free patients with WHO PS ≤2 allocated gemcitabine plus erlotinib Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall survival with gemcitabine plus erlotinib vs gemcitabine, progression-free survival with gemcitabine plus erlotinib and erlotinib maintenance vs gemcitabine, tolerance of erlotinib maintenance, effect of radiotherapy quality assurance on overall survival, toxic effects, locoregional progression, time without treatment, secondary resection rate In locally advanced pancreatic cancer controlled after 4 months of induction chemotherapy, chemoradiotherapy did not significantly improve OS vs continued chemotherapy, and adding erlotinib to gemcitabine did not improve OS. The interim analysis at 221 deaths crossed the futility boundary and served as the final analysis. Median OS from the first randomisation was 15.2 mo with chemoradiotherapy vs 16.5 mo with chemotherapy (HR 1.03; 95% CI 0.79-1.34), and 11.9 mo with gemcitabine-erlotinib vs 13.6 mo with gemcitabine (HR 1.19; 95% CI 0.97-1.45). PFS did not differ significantly (HR 0.78; 95% CI 0.61-1.01). Chemoradiotherapy was associated with less locoregional progression (32% vs 46%) and a longer time without treatment (6.1 vs 3.7 mo). The chemotherapy used predates FOLFIRINOX and nab-paclitaxel. Grade 3-4 nausea occurred in 5.9% with chemoradiotherapy vs none with chemotherapy; erlotinib increased grade 3-4 anaemia, febrile neutropenia, diarrhoea and acneiform rash.

records.title: PANOVA-3
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Locally advanced disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body: Unresectable, locally advanced, biopsy-confirmed pancreatic adenocarcinoma; first-line, previously untreated; ECOG PS 0-2 and life expectancy ≥3 months; excluded implantable electronic devices (e.g. pacemakers) in the torso and known severe hypersensitivity to medical adhesives, hydrogel or the study chemotherapies TTFields (150 kHz, NovoTTF-200T; recommended average usage ≥75%, ≥18 hours/d) + nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² IV immediately followed by gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² IV on days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle vs gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel alone; treatment until local disease progression per RECIST v1.1, lack of compliance, intolerable toxicity, pregnancy or withdrawal of consent Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, local PFS, 1-year survival rate, pain-free survival, puncture-free survival, overall response rate, resectability rate, safety, distant PFS Adding TTFields to first-line gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel significantly prolonged OS and pain-free survival in unresectable LA-PAC, with no additive systemic toxicity; distant PFS was also longer in a post hoc analysis. Median OS was 16.2 vs 14.2 mo (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.68-0.99; P=.039), and 1-year survival was 68.1% vs 60.2%. Pain-free survival was 15.2 vs 9.1 mo (HR 0.74). Post hoc distant PFS was 13.9 vs 11.5 mo (HR 0.74). PFS (10.6 vs 9.3 mo; HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.68-1.05), local PFS and ORR (36.1% vs 30.0%) were not improved, and resectability did not differ (7.0% vs 10.1%). Limitations: open-label design without a sham device, investigator-assessed imaging, and a median device usage of 62%, below the recommended 75%. Device-related skin AEs occurred in 76.3% (grade ≥3 in 7.7%). No deaths were due to TTFields-related AEs, and 4 patients (0.7%) died of chemotherapy-related AEs.
records.keywords: Babiker et al. J Clin Oncol 2025;43:2350-2360  40448572

records.title: SURF Trial
records.subtitle: HCC · Curative-intent locoregional therapy — ablation · Randomised clinical trial · 2022
records.body: Initial HCC, ≤3 nodules and largest lesion ≤3 cm, amenable to both resection and percutaneous RFA after multidisciplinary review; excludes lesions near vasculature, biliary tree or adjacent organs, or not clearly visualised by ultrasound, when RFA is infeasible Surgical resection (open or laparoscopic, local technique) vs percutaneous ultrasound-guided RFA with CT margin confirmation; repeat RFA within 2 weeks for incomplete treatment. Single local-treatment course; no fixed postoperative course reported. Primary: recurrence-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: local recurrence, serious adverse effects, treatment for recurrence Resection did not improve OS or RFS over RFA for small initial HCC; early closure means the results do not establish equivalence. At median follow-up 6.4/6.6 years, 5-year OS was 74.6% versus 70.4% (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.64-1.43) and 5-year RFS 42.9% versus 42.7% (HR 0.90, 0.67-1.22). Local recurrence was 8.0% versus 15.8%; serious adverse effects 3.3% versus none. Accrual stopped at 308 of 600 target.
records.keywords: Liver Cancer 2022;11:209-218  35949295 J Clin Oncol 2025;43:2628-2638 final OS and updated RFS analysis 40554738

records.title: Llovet (BCLC)
records.subtitle: HCC · Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) · Randomised clinical trial · 2002
records.body: Unresectable HCC, Child-Pugh A/B, Okuda I/II, not for curative therapy Arterial embolisation or chemoembolisation (doxorubicin) vs symptomatic care Overall survival Chemoembolisation improved survival (1- and 2-year 82% and 63% vs 63% and 27% for control; HR of death 0.47); established TACE as standard of care for unresectable intermediate-stage HCC.

records.title: SARAH
records.subtitle: HCC · Transarterial radioembolization (Y-90 / SIRT) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body: Locally advanced or inoperable HCC, including portal vein invasion Y-90 resin microsphere radioembolisation (SIRT) vs sorafenib Overall survival SIRT did not improve OS over sorafenib (median 8.0 vs 9.9 months, HR 1.15) despite higher tumour response (19% vs 12%) and better tolerability/quality of life; Y-90 is not a substitute for systemic therapy in advanced HCC.

records.title: DOSISPHERE-01
records.subtitle: HCC · Transarterial radioembolization (Y-90 / SIRT) · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2021
records.body: Locally advanced HCC ≥7 cm, eligible for Y-90 glass microspheres Personalised dosimetry (≥205 Gy to index lesion) vs standard dosimetry (120 Gy) Objective response rate (EASL) Personalised dosimetry doubled response (71% vs 36%) and markedly improved OS (median 26.6 vs 10.7 months); established tumour-dose–guided Y-90 radioembolisation.

records.title: TACTICS
records.subtitle: HCC · Locoregional + systemic combination therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2020
records.body: Adults with liver-confined unresectable HCC amenable to TACE but unsuitable for resection/ablation; no vascular invasion or extrahepatic spread, ≤10 tumours each ≤10 cm, ECOG 0-1, Child-Pugh ≤7. Prior systemic therapy excluded. On-demand conventional TACE plus sorafenib 400 mg/day for 2-3 weeks before first TACE, held around TACE then restarted 400 mg/day with optional escalation to 800 mg/day vs on-demand conventional TACE alone; continue until unTACEable progression, refractoriness, intolerable toxicity or withdrawal. Primary: TACE-specific progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, safety TACE plus sorafenib improved the trial-specific PFS endpoint but did not improve final OS. In 156 ITT patients, TACE-specific PFS, which did not count new intrahepatic lesions as progression, was 22.8 versus 13.5 months (HR 0.661, 95% CI 0.466-0.938); OS was 36.2 versus 30.8 months (HR 0.861, 0.607-1.223). In 77/71 treated, grade-3 hypertension within 8 weeks after first TACE was 10.4% versus 4.2%.

records.title: EMERALD-1
records.subtitle: HCC · Locoregional + systemic combination therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body: Adults with HCC not amenable to resection, ablation or transplant but amenable to up to four TACE procedures within 16 weeks; no extrahepatic disease, Child-Pugh A-B7, ECOG 0-1 and measurable intrahepatic disease. Endoscopy assessed variceal bleeding risk. TACE 1-4 procedures within 16 weeks plus durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 4 weeks starting ≥7 days after first TACE → durvalumab 1120 mg IV plus bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks starting ≥14 days after last TACE vs the same durvalumab schedule plus bevacizumab placebo vs double placebo; continue to mRECIST progression, toxicity, withdrawal or other discontinuation, with treatment beyond progression allowed for clinical benefit Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, quality of life, objective response rate, disease control rate, duration of response, time to progression, safety Adding bevacizumab to durvalumab-TACE improved PFS; durvalumab-TACE alone did not. BICR RECIST PFS was 15.0 versus 8.2 months with durvalumab-bevacizumab versus placebo (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.61-0.98) and 10.0 versus 8.2 months with durvalumab alone (HR 0.94, 0.75-1.19). In the 154/232/200 treatment-received safety sets, grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs were 27%/6%/6%; haemorrhagic AEs 28%/10%/14%, with fatal haemorrhage 0%/3%/1%.

records.title: LEAP-012
records.subtitle: HCC · Locoregional + systemic combination therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body: Adults with unresectable, non-metastatic liver-only HCC amenable to TACE, no portal-vein invasion or extrahepatic spread, measurable disease, ECOG 0-1 and Child-Pugh A; excluded tumour ≥10 cm, >10 tumours or ≥50% liver involvement. TACE plus lenvatinib 12 mg orally daily (≥60 kg) or 8 mg daily (<60 kg) plus pembrolizumab 400 mg IV every 6 weeks for up to 2 years vs matched oral/IV placebos plus TACE; oral therapy held around TACE and otherwise continued to progression, toxicity, physician discontinuation or withdrawal. Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, disease control rate, time to progression, safety Lenvatinib-pembrolizumab-TACE improved PFS, but first-interim OS did not reach statistical significance. In 480 randomised patients, BICR RECIST PFS was 14.6 versus 10.0 months (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.51-0.84); interim OS HR was 0.80 (0.57-1.11), with 29% versus 34% deaths. In 237/241 treated, grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs were 71%/32% and treatment-related deaths 2%/<1%.

records.title: EMERALD-3
records.subtitle: HCC · Locoregional + systemic combination therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Confirmed HCC (imaging or histopathology) not amenable to curative surgery, ablation or transplantation but amenable to TACE; embolisation-eligible setting; Child–Pugh class A, ECOG 0–1, at least one measurable intrahepatic target lesion per mRECIST; excluded previous HCC systemic therapy, more than one previous palliative embolisation, major portal vein thrombosis (Vp3/Vp4) and investigator-assessed upper gastrointestinal bleeding risk TACE plus STRIDE (tremelimumab 300 mg plus durvalumab 1500 mg on day 1, then durvalumab 1500 mg every 4 weeks) plus lenvatinib 8 mg (<60 kg) or 12 mg (≥60 kg) once daily vs TACE plus STRIDE vs TACE; durvalumab and lenvatinib continued for ≤36 months, progression, toxicity or consent withdrawal; TACE technique and number at investigator discretion, first procedure ≥7 days after first durvalumab dose or ≤7 days after randomisation (TACE arm) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, disease control rate at 20 weeks, duration of response, time to progression, time to second progression or death, EORTC QLQ-HCC18, EORTC QLQ-C30, α-fetoprotein associations with outcomes, pharmacokinetics, antidrug antibodies, time to first subsequent therapy or death, safety STRIDE plus lenvatinib plus TACE significantly improved primary PFS versus TACE, but interim OS did not meet significance; STRIDE-TACE had favourable PFS and OS estimates versus the first 175 TACE controls, in descriptive analyses not formally tested. Triplet versus TACE had PFS 13.0 versus 9.8 months (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.57-0.86) and interim OS 39.5 versus 34.7 months (HR 0.84, 0.65-1.09; 40% maturity). STRIDE-TACE versus TACE had PFS 12.9 versus 8.1 months (HR 0.71, 0.56-0.91) and median OS not reached versus 32.9 months (HR 0.70, 0.51-0.95; 45% maturity). Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related AEs occurred in 63% (180 of 287), 49% (85 of 175) and 19% (54 of 290) with triplet, STRIDE-TACE and TACE; treatment-related deaths occurred in seven of 287 (2%; two myocarditis), none of 175 and two of 290 (1%).

records.title: STORM
records.subtitle: HCC · Adjuvant therapy after resection / ablation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2015
records.body: HCC at high recurrence risk after curative resection or ablation Adjuvant sorafenib vs placebo Recurrence-free survival Sorafenib did not improve RFS (median 33.4 vs 33.8 months, HR 0.94) or OS; showed adjuvant TKI therapy has no role after curative HCC treatment.

records.title: IMbrave050
records.subtitle: HCC · Adjuvant therapy after resection / ablation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body: Resected or ablated HCC at high risk of recurrence Adjuvant atezolizumab + bevacizumab (1 year) vs active surveillance Recurrence-free survival Improved RFS at the interim analysis (HR 0.72), but the benefit was not maintained on updated analysis; adjuvant atezolizumab/bevacizumab is not established as standard.

records.title: SHARP
records.subtitle: HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2008
records.body: Advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (pathology-confirmed) not eligible for or progressed after surgical or locoregional therapy; no prior systemic treatment; Child-Pugh class A, ECOG performance status 2 or less, at least one untreated measurable RECIST lesion; prior molecularly targeted or other systemic therapy excluded Sorafenib 400 mg (two 200-mg tablets) orally twice daily continuously vs matching placebo; treatment continued until both radiologic (RECIST) and symptomatic (FHSI8) progression, unacceptable adverse events, or death; no placebo crossover before the definitive survival analysis Primary: Overall survival, Time to symptomatic progression. Secondary: Time to radiologic progression, Disease-control rate, Response rate, Safety Sorafenib improved median OS (10.7 vs 7.9 months, HR 0.69; 95% CI 0.55–0.87) and time to radiologic progression (5.5 vs 2.8 months, HR 0.58); established the first systemic standard for advanced HCC. Final results at second planned interim analysis (321 deaths); 1-yr survival 44% vs 33%. Co-primary time to symptomatic progression did not differ (4.1 vs 4.9 months, HR 1.08, P=0.77). Disease-control 43% vs 32%, no complete responses. Grade 3 drug-related diarrhea and hand-foot skin reaction each 8%, grade 3 hypophosphatemia 11%; serious AEs similar (52% vs 54%)

records.title: Cheng et al. (Asia-Pacific sorafenib in advanced HCC)
records.subtitle: HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2009
records.body: Advanced (unresectable or metastatic) hepatocellular carcinoma, histologically or cytologically proven; first-line systemic therapy (no previous systemic therapy); Child-Pugh class A and ECOG PS 0–2 with at least one measurable RECIST lesion not previously treated locally; prior local therapy allowed if target lesion grew ≥25% or was untreated; enrolled in China, South Korea and Taiwan; excluded previous or concomitant systemic therapy, HIV, CNS tumour, cardiac disease, GI bleeding within 30 days Oral sorafenib 400 mg twice daily continuously vs matching placebo, in 6-week cycles, stratified by macroscopic vascular invasion/extrahepatic spread, ECOG PS and region, randomised 2:1; dose reductions to 200 mg twice daily then 200 mg once daily allowed for drug-related toxicity (removal if further reduction needed); continued until death or stopping criterion (toxicity requiring termination, progression, ECOG PS 4, second cancer, withdrawal) Overall survival Sorafenib is effective for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma in Asia-Pacific patients and well tolerated; with SHARP data it seems an appropriate treatment option (no predefined primary endpoint; ITT n=226). Median OS 6.5 vs 4.2 months (HR 0.68, p=0.014); median TTP 2.8 vs 1.4 months (HR 0.57, p=0.0005); DCR 35.3% vs 15.8% (p=0.0019); no meaningful TTSP difference (3.5 vs 3.4 months, HR 0.90, p=0.50). Population 73.0% HBV; benefit suggested in all preplanned exploratory subgroups (HRs <1, mostly non-significant). Grade 3/4 drug-related HFSR 10.7%, diarrhoea 6.0%, fatigue 3.4%; AE discontinuation 19.5% vs 13.3%; no drug-related deaths

records.title: REFLECT
records.subtitle: HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body: Unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (histological/cytological or AASLD clinical diagnosis); first-line, no prior systemic therapy; BCLC stage B or C, Child-Pugh class A, ECOG PS 0–1, ≥1 mRECIST-measurable target lesion; excluded ≥50% liver occupation, obvious bile duct invasion or main portal vein invasion Lenvatinib orally once daily, 12 mg/day (bodyweight ≥60 kg) or 8 mg/day (bodyweight <60 kg), 28-day cycles vs sorafenib 400 mg orally twice daily, 28-day cycles Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, time to progression, objective response rate, quality of life, plasma pharmacokinetic lenvatinib exposure parameters, safety Lenvatinib was non-inferior to sorafenib for overall survival in untreated advanced HCC, with safety consistent with prior experience; OS superiority was not achieved. Median OS 13.6 vs 12.3 mo (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.79–1.06; non-inferiority margin 1.08). Secondary endpoints (investigator-assessed, mRECIST) favoured lenvatinib: median PFS 7.4 vs 3.7 mo (HR 0.66), TTP 8.9 vs 3.7 mo (HR 0.63), ORR 24.1% vs 9.2%. Open-label design; the QoL summary score did not differ significantly between arms (HR 0.87). Serious TEAEs 43% vs 30%; grade ≥3 hypertension 23% vs 14%; any-grade palmar-plantar erythrodysaesthesia 27% vs 52%; treatment-related fatal AEs 11 (2%) vs 4 (1%), including hepatic failure and cerebral haemorrhage with lenvatinib.

records.title: IMbrave150
records.subtitle: HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body: Unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (locally advanced, metastatic or both), confirmed histologically/cytologically or by AASLD clinical criteria in cirrhosis; first-line, no prior systemic therapy; RECIST 1.1 measurable disease not amenable to curative or locoregional therapy or progressed thereafter, ECOG 0 or 1, Child-Pugh A; excluded autoimmune disease, hepatitis B or C virus coinfection, untreated/incompletely treated varices with bleeding or high bleeding risk Atezolizumab 1200 mg + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks vs sorafenib 400 mg orally twice daily; both until unacceptable toxicity or loss of clinical benefit (treatment beyond progression allowed with clinical benefit) Primary: overall survival, progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, time to deterioration of quality of life, time to deterioration of physical functioning, time to deterioration of role functioning, disease control rate, safety Atezolizumab-bevacizumab significantly improved OS and PFS vs sorafenib in unresectable HCC not previously treated systemically, and delayed deterioration of patient-reported QoL and functioning; with 12 more months of follow-up the survival benefit was maintained and safety was consistent. First interim OS analysis (median follow-up 8.6 mo): death HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.42-0.79). Post hoc descriptive update (median follow-up 15.6 mo): median OS 19.2 vs 13.4 mo (HR 0.66; 95% CI 0.52-0.85); median PFS 6.9 vs 4.3 mo (HR 0.65); confirmed ORR 30% vs 11%; CR 8% vs <1%. Median time to QoL deterioration 11.2 vs 3.6 mo (HR 0.63). Open-label; only Child-Pugh A patients with lower variceal bleeding risk were enrolled. Update safety: grade 3/4 AEs 63% vs 57%; serious AEs 49% vs 33%; grade 5 AEs 7% vs 6%; 5 fatal upper GI bleeds with the combination, all with macrovascular invasion. Primary analysis: grade 3-4 hypertension 15.2% with the combination; upper GI bleeding 7% vs 4.5%.

records.title: HIMALAYA
records.subtitle: HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body: Adults aged ≥18 years with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma and no prior systemic therapy, randomised first-line; participants with thrombosis in the main trunk of the portal vein were excluded STRIDE: tremelimumab 300 mg (1 dose) plus durvalumab 1,500 mg every 4 weeks vs durvalumab monotherapy 1,500 mg every 4 weeks vs sorafenib 400 mg twice daily; treatment beyond disease progression allowed if predefined protocol criteria met Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Depth of response, Serious adverse events At 5 years' follow-up (cut-off 01 March 2024), STRIDE sustained an OS benefit vs sorafenib with a manageable safety profile: in ITT 393/389, OS HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.65-0.89), median OS 16.43 vs 13.77 months, 60-month OS 19.6% vs 9.4% (exploratory updated analysis). Durvalumab remained noninferior, not superior (OS HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.73-1.00). OS with STRIDE was improved with disease control (60-month OS 28.7% vs 12.7%) and >25% tumour shrinkage (50.7% vs 26.3%). Extended long-term survivors (≥48 months): 83/393 (21.1%) vs 45/389 (11.6%). Serious treatment-related AEs in 388/388/374 treated: 17.5%, 8.5%, 9.9%; no additional STRIDE events after primary analysis

records.title: CheckMate 9DW
records.subtitle: HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body: Histologically confirmed advanced hepatocellular carcinoma, ineligible for or progressed after curative surgical or locoregional therapy; first-line (no previous systemic therapy); Child–Pugh score 5 or 6, ECOG 0–1, ≥1 measurable untreated RECIST 1.1 lesion; excluded fibrolamellar, sarcomatoid or mixed cholangiocarcinoma–HCC, previous liver transplant, grade ≥2 hepatic encephalopathy within 12 months, clinically significant ascites, Vp4 portal vein invasion, HBV–HCV or HBV–HDV co-infection Nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks for up to 4 doses → nivolumab 480 mg every 4 weeks, until progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent or a maximum of 2 years vs investigator's choice of oral lenvatinib 8 mg daily (<60 kg) or 12 mg daily (≥60 kg) or oral sorafenib 400 mg twice daily, until progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal of consent Primary: overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, time to symptom deterioration, safety, progression-free survival, time to response, progression-free survival on next-line therapy, quality of life (FACT-Hep, EQ-5D-3L), influence of PD-L1 on overall survival At the preplanned interim analysis, nivolumab plus ipilimumab significantly improved OS vs lenvatinib or sorafenib in previously untreated unresectable HCC, with manageable safety. Median OS 23·7 vs 20·6 mo (HR 0·79, 95% CI 0·65–0·96; p=0·018) at median follow-up 35·2 mo; 24-month OS 49% vs 39%, 36-month 38% vs 24%. Curves crossed early: more deaths in the first 6 months with nivolumab plus ipilimumab (piecewise HR 1·65), then HR 0·61 thereafter. ORR by BICR 36% vs 13%; median DoR 30·4 vs 12·9 mo. Exploratory median PFS by BICR was similar, 9·1 vs 9·2 mo (HR 0·87, 0·72–1·06). Grade 3–4 treatment-related AEs 41% vs 42%. Treatment-related deaths 12 vs 3; of the 12, 11 occurred within 6 months of randomisation and nine were fatal hepatic events in patients with advanced liver disease. Grade 3–4 immune-mediated AEs 28%; 29% needed high-dose steroids.

records.title: CARES-310
records.subtitle: HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body: Unresectable or metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma; BCLC stage B or C not amenable to or progressed after surgical/locoregional therapy, no prior systemic therapy; Child-Pugh A, ECOG 0-1, HBV DNA <500 IU/mL with antiviral therapy; excluded hepatocholangiocarcinoma/sarcomatoid/mixed/lamellar histology, GI bleeding within 6 months or high bleeding risk, uncontrolled hypertension, CNS metastases, vena cava invasion or complete main portal trunk occlusion, autoimmune disease Camrelizumab 200 mg IV every 2 weeks + rivoceranib (apatinib) 250 mg orally once daily vs sorafenib 400 mg orally twice daily (open-label); 28-day cycles until unacceptable toxicity, consent withdrawal, BIRC-confirmed progression per RECIST 1.1 (treatment beyond progression allowed with clinical benefit) or investigator decision Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival by modified RECIST, objective response rate, disease control rate, duration of response, time to progression, pharmacokinetics, immunogenicity, safety, PD-L1 expression and efficacy, time to deterioration in EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status, physical functioning and role functioning Camrelizumab–rivoceranib significantly improved PFS and OS vs sorafenib as first-line therapy for unresectable HCC, with a manageable safety profile. Median PFS (BIRC, RECIST 1.1; primary analysis) 5.6 vs 3.7 mo, HR 0.52 (95% CI 0.41–0.65); updated at final cutoff HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.44–0.67; nominal p values only). At final OS analysis (median follow-up 22.1 vs 14.9 mo), median OS 23.8 vs 15.2 mo, HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.52–0.79); post-hoc 36-mo OS 38% vs 25%. ORR 27% vs 6% at final analysis; median DoR 17.5 vs 9.2 mo. The trial was open-label, and most patients were enrolled in Asia with viral aetiology. At final analysis, grade ≥3 TRAEs 81% vs 54%, most commonly hypertension; treatment-related serious AEs 25% vs 7%; deaths due to AEs regardless of cause 13% vs 7%; 1 treatment-related death in each arm. Primary report: grade ≥3 hepatotoxicity 33% vs 12%; TRAEs led to discontinuation of any study drug in 24% vs 4%.

records.title: CheckMate 459
records.subtitle: HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · Randomised, open-label clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body:
Advanced hepatocellular carcinoma, histologically confirmed, not eligible for or progressed after surgery or locoregional therapy; first line, no previous systemic therapy; Child-Pugh class A, ECOG 0–1, any viral hepatitis status; excluded fibrolamellar, sarcomatoid or mixed cholangiocarcinoma-HCC, previous liver transplant, hepatic encephalopathy, clinically significant ascites, portal hypertension with bleeding or varices within 6 months, active brain metastases Nivolumab 240 mg IV every 2 weeks vs sorafenib 400 mg orally twice daily, each until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent or study closure (treatment beyond progression allowed at investigator decision) Primary: overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, progression-free survival, efficacy (overall survival, progression-free survival, objective response) by baseline tumour cell PD-L1 expression, duration of response, time to response, disease control rate, duration of disease control, time to progression, safety, quality of life First-line nivolumab did not significantly improve overall survival vs sorafenib in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma
・OS: 16.4 vs 14.7 mo; HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.72–1.02); p=0.075, boundary p=0.0419 not met
・ORR: 15% vs 7%; complete response 4% vs 1%
・PFS: 3.7 vs 3.8 mo; HR 0.93 (95% CI 0.79–1.10)
・QoL: Minimally important differences favouring nivolumab in some FACT-Hep subscales; descriptive, not multiplicity-adjusted
・Subgroups: Tumour cell PD-L1 ≥1% ORR 28% vs 9%; PD-L1 not predictive for OS or PFS
・Limitations: Open-label; more subsequent immunotherapy in sorafenib arm may confound OS; delayed curve separation, non-proportional hazards
・Toxicity: Grade 3 treatment-related AEs 18% vs 47%; palmar-plantar erythrodysaesthesia <1% vs 14%; four vs one treatment-related deaths

records.title: RESORCE
records.subtitle: HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body: Hepatocellular carcinoma with documented radiological progression during sorafenib, BCLC stage B or C, not eligible for resection, ablation or chemoembolisation; sorafenib-tolerant (≥400 mg/day for ≥20 of last 28 days) with last dose within 10 weeks of randomisation; Child-Pugh A liver function; measurable lesion by mRECIST and RECIST 1.1; excluded prior other systemic HCC treatment or sorafenib stopped for toxicity Best supportive care plus oral regorafenib 160 mg once daily during weeks 1–3 of each 4-week cycle vs matching placebo plus BSC (2:1 randomisation); treatment continued until mRECIST or clinical progression, death, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal or physician decision; dose reductions to 120 mg then 80 mg allowed, re-escalation to 160 mg permitted after toxicity resolution Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, Time to progression, Objective response rate, Disease control rate, Quality of life, Safety This study met its primary endpoint: regorafenib improved overall survival after sorafenib progression in HCC (final analysis, cutoff Feb 29, 2016; 573 randomised, ITT). Median OS 10·6 vs 7·8 months (HR 0·63, 95% CI 0·50–0·79; one-sided p<0·0001); benefit maintained in all preplanned subgroups. Median PFS 3·1 vs 1·5 months; objective response 11% vs 4%; disease control 65% vs 36%. Grade 3/4 events: hypertension 15% vs 5%, hand-foot skin reaction 13% vs 1%; 7 (2%) drug-related deaths with regorafenib vs 2 (1%) with placebo. No firm conclusions possible for sorafenib-intolerant patients

records.title: CELESTIAL
records.subtitle: HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body: Adults with pathological advanced HCC not amenable to curative treatment, previously treated with sorafenib and progressed after ≥1 systemic regimen; up to 2 prior systemic regimens, Child-Pugh A and ECOG 0-1 Cabozantinib 60 mg orally once daily versus placebo; reductions to 40 then 20 mg permitted. Treatment continued until progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal or protocol discontinuation. Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, safety Cabozantinib improved OS and PFS after sorafenib, but most patients required dose reduction. In the 707-patient ITT second interim, OS was 10.2 versus 8.0 months (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.63-0.92) and PFS 5.2 versus 1.9 months (HR 0.44, 0.36-0.52). In 467/237 treated, grade 3/4 AEs were 68%/36%; 62% reduced dose to median 35.8 mg from 60 mg. Treatment-related deaths were 6/1.

records.title: REACH-2
records.subtitle: HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body: Advanced hepatocellular carcinoma, BCLC stage B or C refractory or not amenable to locoregional therapy; second-line after first-line sorafenib discontinued for intolerance or progression; AFP ≥400 ng/mL; Child-Pugh class A, ECOG 0–1; excluded prior liver transplantation, hepatic encephalopathy, varices requiring endoscopic treatment, uncontrolled hypertension, clinically meaningful ascites (>grade 1 CTCAE v4.0) Ramucirumab 8 mg/kg intravenously over 1 h every 14 days plus best supportive care vs placebo intravenously every 14 days plus best supportive care, until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or withdrawal of consent Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, Objective response rate, Time to radiographic progression, Safety, Time to deterioration in FHSI-8 score, Time to deterioration in ECOG performance status REACH-2 met its primary endpoint, showing improved OS for ramucirumab vs placebo in HCC with AFP ≥400 ng/mL after sorafenib (8.5 vs 7.3 months; HR 0.710 [0.531–0.949]; p=0.0199; ITT, cutoff 15 Mar 2018, median follow-up 7.6 mo); per authors, the first positive phase 3 trial in a biomarker-selected HCC population. PFS 2.8 vs 1.6 months (HR 0.452; p<0.0001); time to radiographic progression 3.0 vs 1.6 months (HR 0.427); disease control 59.9% vs 38.9%; objective response did not differ (5% vs 1%). FHSI-8 and ECOG deterioration did not differ. Pooled with REACH (AFP ≥400, n=542): OS 8.1 vs 5.0 months, HR 0.694 (p=0.0002). Grade ≥3 TEAEs ≥5%: hypertension 13% vs 5%, hyponatraemia 6% vs 0; 3 ramucirumab deaths judged treatment-related (AKI, hepatorenal syndrome, renal failure). Placebo-arm OS notably long; small placebo group (n=95).

records.title: CheckMate 040
records.subtitle: HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · Open-label, non-comparative dose-escalation and expansion clinical trial (phase I/II) · 2017
records.body:
Advanced hepatocellular carcinoma not amenable to curative surgery or local treatment (histologically confirmed); sorafenib-naive, intolerant or progressor (escalation and HCV/HBV cohorts: progression on ≥1 previous systemic line including sorafenib, or sorafenib intolerance/refusal); with or without HCV/HBV, HBV on antiviral therapy with viral load <100 IU/mL; Child-Pugh ≤7 (A/B7) for escalation, ≤6 (A) for expansion; ECOG ≤1; excluded previous checkpoint or T-cell costimulation agents (single-arm) Nivolumab IV every 2 weeks: dose escalation 0·1–10 mg/kg (3+3 design; 0·1 mg/kg HBV only, 10 mg/kg uninfected only) until confirmed complete response, progression, unacceptable toxicity or completion of 2 years of therapy; dose expansion 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks in four cohorts (sorafenib untreated/intolerant uninfected, sorafenib progressor uninfected, HCV infected, HBV infected) until progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: safety and tolerability (dose escalation), objective response rate (dose expansion). Secondary: objective response rate (dose escalation), complete response rate, disease control rate, duration of response, time to response, time to progression, progression-free survival, overall survival, response by PD-L1 expression, quality of life, objective response rate by mRECIST Nivolumab produced durable objective responses in advanced HCC, maintained at 5-year follow-up, with no new safety signals; comparative benefit not established (single-arm)
・ORR (primary): 20% in dose expansion (3 mg/kg); 15% in dose escalation
・ORR (5-yr follow-up): 20% sorafenib-naive; 14% sorafenib-experienced
・MTD: Not reached; one dose-limiting toxicity (grade 2 hepatic impairment at 10 mg/kg)
・DoR (primary): Median 9·9 mo (expansion); 17 mo (escalation)
・DoR (5-yr follow-up): Median 22.6 mo sorafenib-naive; 39.7 mo sorafenib-experienced
・DCR: 64% (expansion); 58% (escalation)
・OS (primary): 6-mo 83%, 9-mo 74% (expansion; median not reached); median 15·0 mo (escalation)
・OS (5-yr follow-up): Median 26.6 mo sorafenib-naive, 15.1 mo sorafenib-experienced; 3-yr 28% vs 20%; 5-yr 14% vs 12%
・PFS: Median 4·0 mo; 6-mo PFS 37% (expansion)
・ORR by mRECIST (5-yr follow-up): 24% sorafenib-naive; 18% sorafenib-experienced (exploratory)
・Nivo+ipi cohort: Randomised dosing arms A, B, C; ORR 32%, 27%, 29%; median OS 22.8, 12.5, 12.7 mo; not powered to compare
・Subgroups: ORR 23% sorafenib untreated/intolerant, 21% progressor, 20% HCV, 14% HBV; PD-L1 ≥1% 26% vs <1% 19%
・Biomarkers (5-yr follow-up): PD-L1 ≥1% associated with higher ORR and longer OS; higher CD8 T-cell density with OS ≥3 years (sorafenib-naive); exploratory
・QoL: EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-VAS stable through week 25 (exploratory)
・Limitations: No randomised control; OS immature in expansion cohorts at primary analysis; not powered for comparisons between aetiologies
・Toxicity (primary): Grade 3/4 TRAEs 25% (escalation), 19% (expansion); no treatment-related deaths; no HBV reactivation; frequent AST, ALT, lipase, amylase rises
・Toxicity (5-yr follow-up): Grade 3/4 TRAEs 33% sorafenib-naive, 21% sorafenib-experienced; one treatment-related death (pneumonitis); grade 3/4 immune-mediated hepatitis 5% per group

records.title: KEYNOTE-394
records.subtitle: HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body: Asian adults with advanced HCC after progression on/intolerance to sorafenib or oxaliplatin chemotherapy, BCLC B/C not amenable to curative/locoregional therapy, Child-Pugh A, ECOG 0-1 and measurable disease. Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks plus best supportive care versus saline placebo IV every 3 weeks plus best supportive care, each for up to 35 cycles. Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, disease control, time to progression, safety and tolerability Pembrolizumab modestly improved OS, PFS and ORR after sorafenib or oxaliplatin chemotherapy in Asian patients. In 453 ITT patients, final OS was 14.6 versus 13.0 months (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.63-0.99); PFS was 2.6 versus 2.3 months (HR 0.74) and BICR ORR 12.7% versus 1.3%. In 299/153 treated, treatment-related grade 3/4 AEs were 12.0%/1.3% versus 5.9%/0%. Three grade-5 treatment-related AEs occurred with pembrolizumab—gastrointestinal haemorrhage, immune-mediated hepatitis and soft-tissue infection—and none with placebo.

records.title: IMbrave251
records.subtitle: HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Locally advanced/metastatic HCC after ≥4 cycles of atezolizumab-bevacizumab, ≥2 tumour assessments and prior disease control before progression; hepatic function, ECOG status and other exclusion criteria were not reported Atezolizumab 1200 mg every 3 weeks plus lenvatinib 8 mg (<60 kg) or 12 mg (≥60 kg) QW or sorafenib 800 mg QW vs the same TKI alone, preserving the source-printed schedules; 92.1% received lenvatinib and 7.9% sorafenib overall, but arm-specific TKI allocation, atezolizumab route and stopping rule were not reported; median lenvatinib duration 5.6 versus 4.7 months and sorafenib 2.9 versus 2.3 months Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, time to progression, quality of life, safety Continuing atezolizumab with a TKI after atezolizumab-bevacizumab progression did not improve OS or PFS over TKI alone. In 557 patients, OS was 14.6 versus 12.5 months (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.72-1.08), PFS 4.3 versus 4.8 months (HR 1.05, 0.88-1.25), and ORR 7.5% versus 5.8%. In 279/275 safety patients, grade 3/4 AEs were 74.2%/66.2%, grade-5 AEs 5.4%/5.8%, serious AEs 40.1%/36.7%, and withdrawal for AEs 11.8%/6.9%.

records.title: NEO-GAP
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2023
records.body: Resectable high-risk intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (>5 cm, multifocal, vascular invasion, or node+) Single-arm neoadjuvant gemcitabine + cisplatin + nab-paclitaxel (GAP) x4 Feasibility (completion of therapy and resection) Neoadjuvant GAP was feasible: 77% completed chemotherapy and underwent resection (PR 23%, DCR 90%) without excess surgical morbidity; supported further perioperative study.

records.title: GAIN (AIO/CALGP/ACO)
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body: Resectable biliary tract cancer / incidental gallbladder carcinoma Neoadjuvant gem-cis then resection vs immediate resection (± adjuvant) Overall survival Neoadjuvant gem-cis improved median OS (27.8 vs 14.6 months) and R0 resection (62.5% vs 33.3%) vs upfront surgery; closed early at N=68, so signal-generating rather than definitive.

records.title: GOLP (ZSAB-neoGOLP)
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Resectable high-risk intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma Neoadjuvant GEMOX + lenvatinib + toripalimab then surgery vs immediate surgery Event-free survival Neoadjuvant GOLP prolonged EFS (18.0 vs 8.7 months, HR 0.43) without compromising resection at the interim analysis (not yet crossing the significance boundary); first randomized support for neoadjuvant therapy in high-risk iCCA.

records.title: PRODIGE 12/ACCORD 18
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Adjuvant therapy after resection · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body: Resected (R0/R1) biliary tract cancer, all sites Adjuvant gemcitabine + oxaliplatin (GEMOX) x12 vs surveillance Relapse-free survival GEMOX did not improve RFS (median 30.4 vs 18.5 months, HR 0.88) or OS; a negative trial that did not support adjuvant GEMOX.

records.title: BILCAP
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Adjuvant therapy after resection · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body: Resected (R0/R1) cholangiocarcinoma or muscle-invasive gallbladder cancer Adjuvant capecitabine 1250 mg/m² twice daily, days 1–14 of a 21-day cycle ×8 vs observation Overall survival Missed the ITT OS endpoint (51.1 vs 36.4 months, HR 0.81, p=0.097) but improved OS in the prespecified per-protocol analysis (53 vs 36 months, HR 0.75); adopted as the adjuvant standard of care.

records.title: ASCOT (JCOG1202)
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Adjuvant therapy after resection · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body: Resected biliary tract cancer (extrahepatic or intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, gallbladder or ampullary carcinoma), adenocarcinoma or adenosquamous; adjuvant after curative resection with D1 or more extensive lymphadenectomy, R0 or R1, enrolled 2–10 weeks after resection; T2–4 N0 M0 or T1–4 N1 M0 (intrahepatic: T1–4 N0–1 M0, UICC 7th edition); Japanese patients aged 20–80 years; no distant metastases or moderate to severe ascites or pleural effusion Adjuvant S-1 (40/50/60 mg by body-surface area, twice daily) 4 weeks on / 2 weeks off ×4 cycles vs observation Primary: overall survival. Secondary: relapse-free survival, adverse events, proportion of treatment completion, serious adverse events The prespecified final 5-year analysis confirmed a durable OS benefit of adjuvant S-1 vs observation after resected biliary tract cancer; authors conclude it supports S-1 as standard postoperative treatment. At median follow-up 61.5 months, 5-year OS was 64% vs 52% (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.55–0.95); median OS 8.2 vs 5.9 years. The primary analysis (179 deaths; median follow-up 45.4 months) showed 3-year OS 77.1% vs 67.6% (HR 0.69). RFS was not significant at the primary analysis (3-year 62.4% vs 50.9%; HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.61–1.04); at 5 years, analysed descriptively, median RFS was 6.1 vs 3.5 years (stratified HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.59–0.98; unstratified 0.80, 95% CI 0.62–1.03), and curves converged, possibly from more non-recurrence deaths with S-1 (7% vs 5%). The trial was open-label and enrolled only Japanese patients. Main grade 3–4 AEs with S-1 were decreased neutrophil count (14%) and biliary tract infection (7%); 150 of 207 (72%) completed treatment; no treatment-related deaths.

records.title: ABC-02
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · First-line advanced — chemotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2010
records.body: Untreated locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract cancer Cisplatin + gemcitabine vs gemcitabine alone Overall survival Cisplatin-gemcitabine improved OS (11.7 vs 8.1 months, HR 0.64) and PFS (8.0 vs 5.0 months); established gem-cis as the first-line standard for over a decade.

records.title: TOPAZ-1
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · First-line advanced — chemotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body: Histologically confirmed previously untreated unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract adenocarcinoma (intrahepatic or extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, gallbladder cancer); first-line, or recurrent disease ≥6 months after curative-intent surgery and completion of adjuvant therapy; ECOG 0–1, ≥1 measurable RECIST v1.1 lesion, no previous immune-mediated therapy; excluded ampullary carcinoma and active or documented autoimmune/inflammatory disorders Durvalumab 1500 mg IV day 1 every 3 weeks + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² and cisplatin 25 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks, up to 8 cycles → durvalumab 1500 mg monotherapy every 4 weeks until disease progression or other discontinuation criteria vs placebo + same gemcitabine–cisplatin → placebo monotherapy every 4 weeks Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, Objective response rate, Duration of response, Disease control rate, Safety Updated analysis (data cutoff Feb 25, 2022; 76.9% maturity) shows robust and sustained overall survival benefit with durvalumab plus gemcitabine–cisplatin, no new safety signals; findings continue to support the regimen as standard of care in untreated advanced biliary tract cancer. Median OS 12.9 vs 11.3 months (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.64–0.91); 24-month OS 23.6% vs 11.5%, more than twice as many alive at 24 months; benefit across all clinically relevant subgroups. Long-term (≥18-month) survivors 88 (26%) of 341 vs 65 (19%) of 344 (post-hoc). Max grade 3–4 AEs 250 (74%) of 338 vs 257 (75%) of 342; treatment-related deaths 2 (1%) vs 1 (<1%). All analyses here exploratory, no multiplicity adjustment

records.title: KEYNOTE-966
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · First-line advanced — chemotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body: Untreated metastatic or unresectable biliary tract cancer Pembrolizumab + gem-cis vs placebo + gem-cis Overall survival Adding pembrolizumab improved OS (12.7 vs 10.9 months, HR 0.83); a second first-line chemo-immunotherapy option.

records.title: SWOG S1815
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · First-line advanced — chemotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Newly diagnosed advanced biliary tract cancer (histologically or cytologically confirmed ICC, ECC or GBC); metastatic or locally advanced unresectable, first-line; no biomarker selection; no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease and no adjuvant therapy within 6 months of registration, Zubrod PS 0 or 1; ampullary cancer and grade 2 or higher peripheral neuropathy excluded GAP: gemcitabine 800 mg/m² + cisplatin 25 mg/m² + nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle vs GC: gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² + cisplatin 25 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle; both until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall response rate, disease control rate, toxicity, change in CA 19-9 from baseline to post-treatment, dose modifications Adding nab-paclitaxel to gemcitabine-cisplatin (GAP) did not improve OS in newly diagnosed advanced BTC and caused more toxicity. Among 441 eligible analyzable participants, median OS 14.0 vs 13.6 mo with GC; HR 0.91 (95% CI, 0.72 to 1.14); P = .41. Median PFS 7.5 vs 6.3 mo; HR 0.89 (95% CI, 0.71 to 1.12). ORR 31% vs 21% and DCR 78% vs 67% favoured GAP among patients with measurable disease, without OS benefit. Exploratory subsets suggested greater PFS benefit in GBC (interaction P = .01) but not OS; larger OS/PFS gains in locally advanced disease were not significant. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related hematologic AEs 60% vs 45%; dose modifications 88% vs 78%; seven grade 5 events attributed to GAP (three from sepsis) vs one on GC.

records.title: ABC-06
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Second-line chemotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body: Advanced BTC progressing after first-line gem-cis Active symptom control (ASC) + FOLFOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + L-folinic acid 175 mg + 5-FU 400 mg/m² bolus then 2400 mg/m² 46-h infusion, Q2W, ≤12 cycles) vs ASC alone Overall survival FOLFOX modestly improved OS (6.2 vs 5.3 months, HR 0.69; 12-month OS 25.9% vs 11.4%); established FOLFOX as a second-line standard.

records.title: NIFTY
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Second-line chemotherapy · Randomised clinical trial · 2021
records.body: Metastatic BTC progressing after first-line gem-cis, Korea Liposomal irinotecan (nal-IRI) + 5-FU/LV vs 5-FU/LV Progression-free survival nal-IRI plus 5-FU/LV improved central-review PFS (7.1 vs 1.4 months, HR 0.56) and OS (8.6 vs 5.5 months); a second-line option, though a later independent re-review tempered the PFS magnitude.

records.title: FIGHT-202
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Targeted therapy — FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements (intrahepatic CCA) · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2020
records.body: Previously treated advanced cholangiocarcinoma with FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements Single-arm pemigatinib (FGFR1-3 inhibitor) Objective response rate ORR 35.5% with median DOR 7.5 months in FGFR2-fusion patients (none in other/no FGFR alterations); led to first FGFR-targeted approval in cholangiocarcinoma.

records.title: FOENIX-CCA2
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Targeted therapy — FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements (intrahepatic CCA) · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2023
records.body: Previously treated FGFR2-rearranged intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma Single-arm futibatinib (covalent FGFR1-4 inhibitor) Objective response rate ORR 42% with median DOR 9.7 months, PFS 9.0 and OS 21.7 months; supported approval of futibatinib, active including after prior FGFR inhibitors.

records.title: FIGHT-302
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Targeted therapy — FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements (intrahepatic CCA) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Untreated advanced/metastatic cholangiocarcinoma with FGFR2 rearrangement First-line pemigatinib vs gemcitabine + cisplatin (crossover to pemigatinib allowed) Progression-free survival In a trial that closed early when first-line standard of care changed and did not meet its accrual target, first-line pemigatinib improved progression-free survival (8.3 versus 6.8 months; HR 0.584, 95% CI 0.393-0.868), objective response (47.0% versus 15.5%) and duration of response (14.2 versus 6.3 months), while overall survival was not improved (24.4 versus 25.0 months; HR 1.095, 95% CI 0.733-1.637) - roughly 80% of the chemotherapy group went on to an FGFR inhibitor, so the survival comparison is confounded by crossover. The publication states no testing hierarchy, and the authors label the primary progression-free survival p-value nominal, cautioning that it 'should be interpreted with caution in the context of the reduced sample size and event count'. In the 83 and 73 patients treated, hyperphosphatemia - the FGFR class effect - affected 81.9% versus 2.7% but was almost always mild, with one grade >=3 case; dry eye (36.1% versus 4.1%) was the other characteristic toxicity. Grade >=3 events were 78.3% versus 67.1%, and three fatal events versus none were judged unrelated to pemigatinib. Pemigatinib needed more dose interruption (84.3% versus 64.4%) yet caused fewer discontinuations for toxicity (6.0% versus 11.0%). The gemcitabine-cisplatin comparator predates TOPAZ-1 and KEYNOTE-966 and first-line pemigatinib is not FDA-approved, so this informs sequencing more than it changes first-line practice.

records.title: ClarIDHy
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Targeted therapy — IDH1 mutation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body: Previously treated IDH1-mutant cholangiocarcinoma Ivosidenib 500 mg once daily (continuous 28-day cycles) vs placebo (IDH1-mutant) Progression-free survival Ivosidenib improved PFS (2.7 vs 1.4 months, HR 0.37); OS favored ivosidenib after crossover adjustment (10.3 vs 5.1 months); established IDH1-targeted therapy.

records.title: MyPathway
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Targeted therapy — HER2 amplification / overexpression · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2021
records.body: Previously treated HER2-amplified/overexpressed metastatic BTC Single-arm pertuzumab + trastuzumab Objective response rate ORR 23% with median PFS 4.0 and OS 10.9 months; early proof-of-concept for dual HER2 blockade in BTC.

records.title: HERIZON-BTC-01
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Targeted therapy — HER2 amplification / overexpression · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2023
records.body: Previously treated HER2-amplified advanced BTC (IHC 2+/3+) Zanidatamab 20 mg/kg IV Q2W (single-arm; HER2-amplified) Objective response rate Confirmed ORR 41.3% (cohort 1) with median DOR 12.9 months; supported FDA accelerated approval of zanidatamab (2024) for HER2 IHC 3+ BTC.

records.title: ROAR
records.subtitle: Biliary Tract Cancer · Targeted therapy — BRAF V600E & mismatch-repair deficiency · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2020
records.body: Previously treated BRAF V600E-mutated biliary tract cancer Single-arm dabrafenib + trametinib Objective response rate In the 2020 interim BTC cohort (n=43; 91% intrahepatic), investigator-assessed ORR was 51% (95% CI 36-67), versus 47% (31-62) by independent review; all responses were partial. Median PFS was 9 months (95% CI 5-10) and OS 14 months (10-33) at 10-month median follow-up. Single-arm study; no comparative efficacy inference.

records.title: PROMID
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Somatostatin analogues — antiproliferative control · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2009
records.body: Locally inoperable or metastatic well-differentiated midgut NET (or unknown primary believed midgut with pancreas/chest/elsewhere excluded by CT/MRI), treatment-naive, measurable disease, no curative options; excluded prior somatostatin analogs ≥4 weeks, interferon alfa, chemotherapy, or chemoembolization Octreotide LAR 30 mg IM every 28 days until CT- or MRI-documented tumor progression vs placebo (sodium chloride) IM every 28 days Primary: Time to tumor progression. Secondary: Survival time, Tumor response, Quality of life, Clinical response, Biochemical response, Safety Long-term follow-up (to May 2014): octreotide LAR did not improve OS vs placebo in the whole cohort (median 84.7 vs 83.7 months; HR 0.83; 95% CI 0.47-1.46; p=0.51; 48/85 deaths); crossover (38/43 placebo patients received octreotide LAR after progression) may have confounded OS, and in asymptomatic patients a watch-and-wait strategy offered no significant survival disadvantage vs early treatment. Octreotide LAR significantly lengthens TTP vs placebo in metastatic midgut NETs (planned interim, cITT, 85 randomized): median TTP 14.3 vs 6.0 months (HR 0.34; 0.20-0.59; P=.000072); stable disease at 6 months 66.7% vs 37.2%. High hepatic tumor load (>10%) predicted shorter OS (median 57.5 vs 107.6 months; HR 2.49; 1.36-4.55; p=0.002); low-load octreotide subgroup showed only a non-significant OS trend (HR 0.59; 0.29-1.20). No treatment-related deaths; AEs stopped treatment in 5 octreotide LAR and 0 placebo patients; bile stones six times, five in octreotide LAR
