records.title: CLARINET
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Somatostatin analogues — antiproliferative control · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2014
records.body: Advanced well/moderately differentiated nonfunctioning grade 1-2 (Ki-67 <10%) enteropancreatic NET (pancreas, midgut, hindgut or unknown origin), unresectable or metastatic; somatostatin-receptor scintigraphy uptake grade 2 or higher and documented progression status required; excluded if interferon, chemoembolization or chemotherapy within 6 months, radionuclide at any time, or somatostatin analogue at any time (unless >6 months previously and <15 days) Lanreotide Autogel (Depot) 120 mg deep subcutaneous injection every 28 days without dose adjustment, to a maximum of 24 injections over 96 weeks vs placebo (sodium chloride) on the same schedule; withdrawal for centrally assessed RECIST v1.0 progression, investigator judgment, patient request or safety-threatening adverse event Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, Quality of life, Safety, Alive without disease progression at 48 and 96 weeks, Time to tumor progression, Chromogranin A level, Pharmacokinetic data Lanreotide was associated with significantly prolonged progression-free survival in metastatic grade 1-2 (Ki-67 <10%) nonfunctioning enteropancreatic NETs. Median PFS not reached vs 18.0 months with placebo (HR for progression or death 0.47, 95% CI 0.30-0.73; P<0.001); PFS at 24 months 65.1% vs 33.0%. No significant between-group differences in overall survival or quality of life. Applicability limited: 96% of patients had no progression in the 3-6 months before randomization, so data are lacking for documented progressive disease, and OS analysis was complicated by placebo crossover. Most common treatment-related adverse event diarrhea (26% vs 9%); study drug-related events 50% vs 28%, cholelithiasis 10% vs 3%; few withdrawals for adverse events

records.title: NETTER-1
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body: Well-differentiated (Ki67 ≤20%) midgut neuroendocrine tumours, metastatic or locally advanced and inoperable; RECIST progression within a maximum of 3 years on octreotide LAR 20-30 mg every 3-4 weeks (≥12 weeks); somatostatin receptors on all target lesions by blinded central review; Karnofsky ≥60; excluded any prior PRRT, creatinine >150 µmol/L or clearance <50 ml/min, >30 mg octreotide LAR within 12 weeks 177Lu-Dotatate 7.4 GBq IV every 8 weeks for four infusions (stopped early for unacceptable toxicity, centrally confirmed RECIST progression, nonadherence, consent withdrawal or death) plus octreotide LAR 30 mg IM about 24 hours after each infusion, then monthly vs high-dose octreotide LAR 60 mg IM every 4 weeks; centrally confirmed progression or completion of the 18-month treatment period ended trial treatment in both arms Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, overall survival, quality of life, safety, side-effect profile 177Lu-Dotatate gave markedly longer PFS and a significantly higher response rate than high-dose octreotide LAR in advanced midgut NETs but did not significantly improve final OS; the authors consider the 11.7-mo median OS difference possibly clinically relevant. PFS at month 20 was 65.2% vs 10.8%; median PFS not reached vs 8.4 mo; HR 0.21 (95% CI 0.13-0.33), reassessed as 0.18 (0.11-0.29) at the same cutoff. ORR 18% vs 3% (P<0.001) among 201 response-evaluable patients. Final OS (142 deaths): median 48.0 vs 36.3 mo; HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.60-1.17), P=0.30; 36% of controls crossed over to PRRT. The trial was open-label. Grade 3/4 neutropenia, thrombocytopenia and lymphopenia 1%, 2% and 9% vs none; treatment-related serious AEs 9% vs 1%; nausea 59% and vomiting 47%, mostly attributed to amino acid infusions. MDS in 2 of 111 (2%), one fatal (the only treatment-related death); no AML; grade ≥3 nephrotoxicity (any cause) 5% vs 4%; no new safety signals in long-term follow-up.

records.title: NETTER-2
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Well-differentiated gastroenteropancreatic NETs, higher grade 2 (Ki67 ≥10% and ≤20%) or grade 3 (Ki67 >20% and ≤55%); inoperable locally advanced or metastatic, diagnosed within 6 months before screening, first-line; somatostatin receptor-positive on all target lesions (uptake score 3 or 4); excluded prior peptide receptor radionuclide therapy, hepatic artery embolisation or radiofrequency ablation, and prior systemic therapy unless <1 month and not within 12 weeks before randomisation ¹⁷⁷Lu-Dotatate 7·4 GBq IV every 8 weeks for four cycles plus octreotide 30 mg LAR IM after each infusion, then octreotide 30 mg LAR IM every 4 weeks vs high-dose octreotide 60 mg LAR IM every 4 weeks; randomised treatment until centrally confirmed progression or discontinuation for another reason Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, time to deterioration in global health status, diarrhoea, fatigue and pain (EORTC QLQ-C30), disease control rate, duration of response, safety, overall survival First-line ¹⁷⁷Lu-Dotatate plus octreotide LAR significantly extended median PFS (by 14 months) vs high-dose octreotide 60 mg LAR in grade 2 or 3 advanced GEP-NETs. At the final PFS analysis, centrally assessed median PFS was 22·8 vs 8·5 mo (stratified HR 0·276, 95% CI 0·182–0·418; p<0·0001), with median follow-up of 23·2 mo; benefit was consistent across prespecified subgroups. ORR was 43·0% vs 9·3% (CR 8 [5%] vs 0); median DoR was 23·3 mo among ¹⁷⁷Lu-Dotatate responders; disease control was 90·7% vs 66·7%. Time to QoL deterioration (EORTC QLQ-C30) did not differ significantly. OS was immature: medians not reached and no difference; 36 (48%) controls received ¹⁷⁷Lu-Dotatate or ¹⁷⁷Lu-Dotatoc after progression, which may confound OS. Grade ≥3 AEs occurred in 35% vs 27%; one case of myelodysplastic syndrome occurred at about 14 months with ¹⁷⁷Lu-Dotatate; there were no study drug-related deaths during treatment. The trial was open label, and no adolescents were enrolled, so the data apply to adults only.

records.title: COMPETE
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Well-differentiated GEP NETs, grade 1–2 (Ki-67 ≤20%; non-functional gastrointestinal or functional/non-functional pancreatic); unresectable or metastatic, RECIST 1.1-progressive within 36 months before randomisation, treatment-naive or previously treated; somatostatin receptor-positive on imaging within 4 months (all target and ≥90% of non-target lesions with diameters ≥15 mm on SPECT or ≥10 mm on PET); excluded functional gastrointestinal NETs and previous PRRT or mTOR inhibitors Intravenous [177Lu]Lu-edotreotide 7·5 ± 0·7 GBq every 3 months, maximum four cycles over 9 months, with lysine–arginine amino acid nephroprotection vs oral everolimus 10 mg/day for up to 30 months; treatment until progression, unacceptable toxicity, consent withdrawal, end of study or death; somatostatin analogues permitted for symptom control only Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, overall survival, disease control rate, duration of disease control, harms and tolerability, quality of life, dosimetry of target organs and tumour lesions [177Lu]Lu-edotreotide significantly and clinically meaningfully improved PFS vs everolimus; the authors conclude this supports its use in early lines for advanced, progressive GEP NETs. Median PFS by BICR 23·9 vs 14·1 mo; stratified HR 0·67 (95% CI 0·48–0·95); p=0·022, below the 0·044 final boundary; final analysis at month 30 with 152 events, fewer than the planned 180. ORR 22% vs 4% (p<0·0001); disease control rate similar. OS immature and not significantly different: 63·4 vs 58·7 mo; HR 0·78 (0·53–1·15); p=0·21; 53 (52%) everolimus patients received subsequent PRRT. The first-line subgroup was exploratory and underpowered (HR 0·60, 95% CI 0·25–1·45). Treatment-related grade 3–4 AEs 18% vs 40%; treatment-related SAEs 3% vs 15%; TEAEs leading to discontinuation 6% vs 23%; no treatment-related deaths. MDS in two of 217 PRRT patients (one treatment-related), no AML; long-term follow-up ongoing.

records.title: OCLURANDOM
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT) · Randomised non-comparative clinical trial (phase II) · 2026
records.body: Sporadic advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours; at least one prior line of systemic treatment (somatostatin analogues, cytotoxic chemotherapy or everolimus) with RECIST 1.1 progression within 12 months; somatostatin receptor scintigraphy-positive on central review (Krenning grade ≥2 uptake, at least equal to liver, in all RECIST-evaluable lesions ≥15 mm); excluded more than one line of cytotoxic chemotherapy, prior multikinase inhibitors or PRRT, uncontrolled functioning syndrome or brain metastasis [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-dota-tate 7·4 GBq IV every 8 weeks, up to four cycles, with concomitant amino acid infusion vs sunitinib 37·5 mg orally once daily; treatment until RECIST 1.1 progression, completion of four [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-dota-tate cycles, unacceptable adverse events, patient decision or death Primary: progression-free survival rate at 12 months. Secondary: progression-free survival, time to progression, overall survival, objective response rate at 12 months, best overall response, duration of response, safety, late adverse events, quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC GI-NET 21) Using sunitinib as an internal control, [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-dota-tate showed clinically significant antitumour activity and better quality of life during treatment in pretreated, progressive, somatostatin receptor-positive pancreatic NETs, with late adverse events that might affect tolerance of later lines. Primary endpoint met: 12-mo PFS 33/41 (80·5%, 90% CI 67·5–89·9) vs 18/43 (41·9%) with sunitinib, whose CI encompassed the prespecified 35%. The design was non-comparative, so between-arm comparisons are post hoc: median PFS 20·7 vs 11·0 mo (HR 0·33); partial response 63·4% vs 30·2%; OS not significantly different (55·8 vs 64·4 mo), with 65% of the sunitinib group later receiving [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-dota-tate. QLQ-C30 global health status differed by 10·3 points in favour of [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-dota-tate. Grade 3–4 AEs 44% vs 72%. Grade ≥2 late AEs occurred in 24/40 (60%) [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-dota-tate patients, mainly haematological and kidney; one treatment-related death from acute leukaemia following MDS.

records.title: RADIANT-3
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Targeted therapy — mTOR & antiangiogenic agents · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2011
records.body: Low- or intermediate-grade advanced (unresectable or metastatic) pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours; radiologic progression (unequivocal increase in tumour size) within 12 months before randomisation; prior antineoplastic therapy allowed; excluded prior mTOR inhibitor, long-term glucocorticoids/immunosuppressants, hepatic-artery embolization within 6 months (1 month if other measurable sites) or hepatic cryoablation/radiofrequency ablation within 2 months Oral everolimus 10 mg once daily + best supportive care vs matching placebo + best supportive care; until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, drug interruption ≥3 weeks or consent withdrawal Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: confirmed objective response rate, duration of response, overall survival, safety Everolimus, as compared with placebo, significantly prolonged PFS in progressive advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours and was associated with a low rate of severe adverse events. Median investigator-assessed PFS 11.0 vs 4.6 mo (HR 0.35; 95% CI 0.27–0.45; P<0.001); central review 11.4 vs 5.4 mo (HR 0.34); 18-mo PFS 34% vs 9%. Confirmed responses (all partial) 5% vs 2%; benefit came mainly from disease stabilisation. OS median not reached with no significant difference (HR 1.05; 95% CI 0.71–1.55), confounded by 148 of 203 placebo patients (73%) crossing over to everolimus; final OS analysis planned at about 250 deaths. Drug-related grade 3/4 stomatitis 7%, anaemia 6% vs 0% and hyperglycaemia 5% vs 2%; pneumonitis 12% vs 0%; drug-related discontinuation 13% vs 2%; one treatment-related death (acute respiratory distress syndrome).

records.title: Raymond et al. (Sunitinib)
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Targeted therapy — mTOR & antiangiogenic agents · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2011
records.body: Well-differentiated pancreatic endocrine tumours, advanced or metastatic and not candidates for surgery; RECIST-documented progression within previous 12 months and one or more measurable target lesions, ECOG 0–1; excluded poorly differentiated tumours, prior tyrosine kinase or VEGF inhibitor treatment, cardiac events or pulmonary embolism within 12 months, ongoing dysrhythmia or prolonged QTc, symptomatic brain metastases, or LVEF of 50% or less Sunitinib 37.5 mg orally once daily, continuous vs matching placebo (1:1, double-blind, both with best supportive care), until RECIST progression, unacceptable adverse events or death; dose reduction to 25 mg and escalation to 50 mg permitted; placebo progressors could enter open-label sunitinib extension Progression-free survival Continuous daily sunitinib 37.5 mg improved progression-free survival, overall survival and objective response rate vs placebo in advanced progressive well-differentiated panNET (authors' conclusion). Trial stopped early after the monitoring committee observed more deaths and serious adverse events on placebo. Median PFS 11.4 vs 5.5 months (HR 0.42; 95% CI 0.26–0.66; P<0.001; 81 events, ITT); observed z 3.85 did not exceed the adjusted 3.88 boundary, but two sensitivity analyses supported robustness. ORR 9.3% vs 0%. OS immature: median not reached; 9 vs 21 deaths (HR 0.41; 95% CI 0.19–0.89; P=0.02). Grade 3/4 neutropenia 12%, hypertension 10%; one grade 5 cardiac failure on sunitinib. Early termination may overestimate treatment effect
records.keywords: Raymond et al. N Engl J Med 2011;364:501-13  21306237

records.title: RADIANT-4
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Targeted therapy — mTOR & antiangiogenic agents · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body: Advanced (unresectable or metastatic), progressive, non-functional, well-differentiated (grade 1 or 2) neuroendocrine tumours of lung or gastrointestinal origin; documented radiological progression within 6 months; prior somatostatin analogue, interferon, one chemotherapy line or PRRT allowed if progressing during or after last treatment; excluded history or presence of carcinoid syndrome, poorly differentiated histology, pancreatic NET, >1 prior chemotherapy line, prior mTOR inhibitor Everolimus 10 mg orally daily plus best supportive care vs identical placebo plus best supportive care (double-blind); best supportive care excluded antitumour agents such as somatostatin analogues; continued until radiological progression, new cancer therapy, intolerable adverse event or consent withdrawal Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, health-related quality of life, WHO performance status, pharmacokinetics, changes in chromogranin A levels, changes in neuron-specific enolase levels, safety Everolimus significantly improved progression-free survival vs placebo in progressive lung or gastrointestinal NETs, with safety consistent with its known profile. Central-review median PFS 11.0 vs 3.9 mo (HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.35-0.67); investigator-assessed 14.0 vs 5.5 mo (HR 0.39). Confirmed responses were rare (2% vs 1%, all partial); benefit reflected disease stabilisation. The first interim OS analysis (70 deaths) favoured everolimus but was not significant (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.40-1.05; one-sided p=0.037 vs boundary 0.0002); median OS was not estimable. Grade 3/4 drug-related stomatitis 9% vs 0, diarrhoea 7% vs 2%, infections 7% vs 0; non-infectious pneumonitis 16% with everolimus (grade 3 1%). Dose reductions/interruptions 67% vs 30%; discontinuation for grade 3/4 drug-related AEs 12% vs 3%. Three on-treatment everolimus deaths were not attributed to progression (respiratory failure, septic shock, cardiac failure).

records.title: SANET-ep
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Targeted therapy — mTOR & antiangiogenic agents · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body: Advanced progressive well-diff extrapancreatic NET (China) Surufatinib 300 mg vs placebo Progression-free survival Surufatinib prolonged PFS (9.2 vs 3.8 months, HR 0.33) in extrapancreatic NET; stopped early for efficacy, adding a multitargeted (VEGFR/FGFR/CSF1R) option.

records.title: SANET-p
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Targeted therapy — mTOR & antiangiogenic agents · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body: Advanced progressive well-diff pancreatic NET (China) Surufatinib 300 mg vs placebo Progression-free survival Surufatinib prolonged PFS (10.9 vs 3.7 months, HR 0.49) in advanced panNET; stopped early for efficacy, confirming activity across NET subtypes.

records.title: CABINET (Alliance A021602)
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Targeted therapy — mTOR & antiangiogenic agents · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body: Well- or moderately differentiated extrapancreatic or pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, WHO grade 1 to 3, in two independent cohorts; locally advanced or metastatic, with RECIST 1.1 progression in the 12 months before enrollment; progression or intolerance on at least one site-specific FDA-approved therapy (everolimus; from November 2020 also Lu-177 dotatate for non-lung NET or sunitinib for pancreatic); excludes poorly differentiated or unspecified high-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma Cabozantinib 60 mg orally once daily vs placebo orally once daily (double-blind), randomized separately within extrapancreatic and pancreatic NET cohorts, until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal of consent Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, overall survival, safety, quality of life Cabozantinib significantly improved PFS vs placebo in previously treated, progressive extrapancreatic or pancreatic NET. Extrapancreatic cohort (n=203): median PFS 8.4 vs 3.9 mo, HR 0.38 (95% CI 0.25-0.59); pancreatic cohort (n=95): 13.8 vs 4.4 mo, HR 0.23 (95% CI 0.12-0.42). Confirmed ORR 5% and 19% vs 0%. No OS difference was observed, but OS data were immature and possibly affected by crossover (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.56-1.31; HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.45-2.00). Early termination after interim analyses may overestimate the effect. Treatment-related grade ≥3 AEs 62% vs 27% (extrapancreatic) and grade 3 or 4 AEs 65% vs 23% (pancreatic), chiefly hypertension, fatigue, diarrhea and thromboembolic events; cabozantinib dose reductions in 66% and 68%. Four possibly treatment-related grade 5 events with cabozantinib in the extrapancreatic cohort (gastric hemorrhage, cardiac arrest, two unspecified).
records.keywords: Chan et al. N Engl J Med 2025;392:653-665  39282913

records.title: ECOG-ACRIN E2211
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Cytotoxic chemotherapy — pancreatic NET · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2023
records.body: Low-grade or intermediate-grade pancreatic NETs; locally unresectable or metastatic, prior somatostatin analogs, everolimus and/or sunitinib allowed; radiographic progression within 12 months of random assignment (not defined by RECIST 1.1); no prior temozolomide, dacarbazine, capecitabine or fluorouracil Temozolomide 200 mg/m² orally once daily days 1-5 every 28 days vs capecitabine 750 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1-14 + temozolomide 200 mg/m² orally once daily days 10-14 every 28 days (open-label); temozolomide capped at 400 mg once daily; maximum 13 cycles or until progression, unacceptable toxicity, nonprotocol therapy, withdrawal or death, with continuation beyond 13 cycles at investigator discretion Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, response rate, safety, central pathology review, MGMT by immunohistochemistry, MGMT promoter methylation, best percentage change in target lesion size, duration of response, disease control rate Capecitabine/temozolomide was associated with a significant PFS improvement vs temozolomide alone in advanced pancreatic NETs. The primary endpoint was met at the interim analysis (January 2018): median PFS 22.7 vs 14.4 mo; HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.36 to 0.93). At the final analysis (May 2021 cutoff), median PFS was 23.2 vs 15.1 mo; HR 0.71 (95% CI 0.46 to 1.07). Final OS improvement did not reach significance: 58.7 vs 53.8 mo; HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.51 to 1.33). RR 39.7% vs 33.7% was not significantly different; the trial was not powered for RR. MGMT deficiency was associated with response (low vs high IHC: 52% vs 15%), but with temozolomide in both arms the trial was not designed to test MGMT as predictive. Treatment-related grade 3-4 toxicity was 45% vs 22%, and discontinuation for AEs was 14.9% vs 6.3%. One myelodysplastic syndrome case occurred in the combination arm; there were no treatment-related deaths.
records.keywords: Kunz et al. J Clin Oncol 2022;41:1359-1369  36260828

records.title: TELESTAR
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Carcinoid syndrome — symptom control · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body: Carcinoid syndrome with >=4 bowel movements/day despite somatostatin analogue Telotristat ethyl 250 or 500 mg TID vs placebo (added to SSA) Change in bowel movement frequency Telotristat ethyl (250 mg TID) increased the proportion with durable >=30% reduction in bowel movements (44% vs 20%) and lowered urinary 5-HIAA; first oral agent for refractory carcinoid syndrome diarrhea.

records.title: TOPIC-NEC (JCOG1213)
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body: Untreated advanced/recurrent poorly-diff digestive-system NEC Etoposide + cisplatin vs irinotecan + cisplatin Overall survival Etoposide-cisplatin and irinotecan-cisplatin gave similar OS (12.5 vs 10.9 months, HR 1.04); confirmed platinum-etoposide as a standard first-line backbone for digestive NEC.

records.title: NET-02
records.subtitle: Neuroendocrine Tumors · Poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC) · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2023
records.body: Progressive poorly-diff extrapulmonary NEC, second-line Liposomal irinotecan/5-FU/folinic acid vs docetaxel 6-month progression-free survival rate nal-IRI/5-FU met its 6-month PFS endpoint (29.6%) while docetaxel did not (13.8%), with no OS difference; supports nal-IRI/5-FU as a second-line option in extrapulmonary NEC.

records.title: ACOSOG Z9001 (Alliance)
records.subtitle: GIST · Localized / resectable GIST — adjuvant therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2009
records.body: Resected KIT+ primary GIST ≥3 cm 1 year adjuvant imatinib vs placebo Recurrence-free survival Imatinib improved 1-year RFS (98% vs 83%, HR 0.35) with no early overall-survival difference; established 1 year of adjuvant imatinib after resection of primary GIST.

records.title: SSG XVIII / AIO
records.subtitle: GIST · Localized / resectable GIST — adjuvant therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2012
records.body: Resected high-risk KIT+ GIST 3 years vs 1 year adjuvant imatinib Recurrence-free survival Three years of imatinib improved recurrence-free survival, the primary endpoint: 5-year RFS 71.1% vs 52.3% (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.44-0.81, P<.001), ITT at a median 90 months' follow-up. Overall survival, a secondary endpoint, was 91.9% vs 85.3% (HR 0.60, 0.37-0.97, P=.036); the trial adjusted no p-value for multiple testing, so everything below the primary is nominal. Established 3 years as the adjuvant standard for high-risk GIST. Grade 3-4 adverse events 32.8% (65/198) vs 20.1% (39/194), P=.006, on top of a chronic low-grade burden — periorbital oedema 74.2% vs 59.3% (P=.002), muscle cramps 49.0% vs 30.9%, anaemia 80.3% vs 72.2%. By the 2016 analysis 26.8% vs 12.6% had stopped imatinib for a reason other than recurrence, and 13.6% vs 7.7% for an adverse event; the 2012 report gave 25.8% for the 36-month group. Cardiac events over the 2016 follow-up were similar (3.0% vs 5.2%, no formal test).

records.title: EORTC 62024
records.subtitle: GIST · Localized / resectable GIST — adjuvant therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2015
records.body: Resected intermediate/high-risk KIT+ GIST 2 years adjuvant imatinib vs observation Imatinib failure-free survival 5-year imatinib failure-free survival was similar (87% vs 84%, p=0.44), but relapse-free survival was improved (3-year 84% vs 66%); supported adjuvant imatinib while suggesting longer duration is needed.

records.title: PERSIST-5
records.subtitle: GIST · Localized / resectable GIST — adjuvant therapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2018
records.body: Resected intermediate/high-risk primary GIST 5 years adjuvant imatinib (single arm) Recurrence-free survival 5-year RFS was 90% and OS 95%, with no recurrences among patients with imatinib-sensitive genotypes who stayed on drug; supports extended adjuvant duration in high-risk disease.

records.title: IMADGIST (FSG)
records.subtitle: GIST · Localized / resectable GIST — adjuvant therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Resected localized GIST, ≥35% relapse risk, on imatinib 3 years 6 years vs 3 years adjuvant imatinib Disease-free survival Extending imatinib to 6 years improved 3-year DFS from randomization (87% vs 55%, HR 0.40); OS was not yet different, supporting longer adjuvant duration for the highest-risk GIST.

records.title: B2222
records.subtitle: GIST · Advanced / metastatic GIST — first-line imatinib · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2002
records.body: Advanced unresectable/metastatic KIT+ GIST Imatinib 400 vs 600 mg/day Objective response rate Imatinib produced a partial response in 53.7% with durable disease control and a later median OS of ~57 months; first trial to establish imatinib as standard first-line therapy for advanced GIST.

records.title: EORTC 62005
records.subtitle: GIST · Advanced / metastatic GIST — first-line imatinib · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2004
records.body: Advanced/metastatic KIT+ GIST Imatinib 800 vs 400 mg/day Progression-free survival 800 mg/day modestly prolonged PFS (HR 0.82, p=0.026) without an OS benefit; the advantage was concentrated in KIT exon 9 tumors, supporting 400 mg as standard except for exon 9.

records.title: MetaGIST
records.subtitle: GIST · Advanced / metastatic GIST — first-line imatinib · Meta-analysis · 2010
records.body: Advanced GIST (pooled EORTC 62005 + S0033) Imatinib 800 vs 400 mg/day Progression-free survival Pooled analysis showed a small PFS advantage for 800 mg/day confined to KIT exon 9-mutant GIST, with no OS difference; defined 400 mg as standard and 800 mg for exon 9 tumors.

records.title: BFR14 (FSG)
records.subtitle: GIST · Advanced / metastatic GIST — first-line imatinib · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2010
records.body: Advanced GIST, non-progressing after 3 years of imatinib Interrupt vs continue imatinib Progression-free survival Interruption led to rapid progression (most within months) versus continuation, and rechallenge seldom restored prior depth of response; established continuous imatinib until progression.

records.title: A6181004 (Sunitinib)
records.subtitle: GIST · Advanced GIST — second-line & beyond · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2006
records.body: Advanced GIST after imatinib failure/intolerance Sunitinib vs placebo Time to tumor progression Sunitinib quadrupled time to progression (27.3 vs 6.4 weeks, HR 0.33) and improved OS (HR 0.49); established sunitinib as second-line therapy for imatinib-resistant GIST.

records.title: GRID
records.subtitle: GIST · Advanced GIST — second-line & beyond · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2013
records.body: Advanced GIST after imatinib and sunitinib Regorafenib vs placebo Progression-free survival Regorafenib improved PFS (4.8 vs 0.9 months, HR 0.27); OS was not significant due to 85% crossover; established regorafenib as third-line standard.

records.title: INVICTUS
records.subtitle: GIST · Advanced GIST — second-line & beyond · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body: Advanced GIST after imatinib, sunitinib, and regorafenib Ripretinib vs placebo Progression-free survival Ripretinib improved PFS (6.3 vs 1.0 months, HR 0.15) and median OS (15.1 vs 6.6 months); established ripretinib as fourth-line standard.

records.title: INTRIGUE
records.subtitle: GIST · Advanced GIST — second-line & beyond · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body: Advanced GIST progressing on first-line imatinib Ripretinib 150 mg once daily (continuous) vs sunitinib 50 mg once daily (4 weeks on / 2 weeks off) — second-line Progression-free survival Ripretinib was not superior to sunitinib (PFS 8.0 vs 8.3 months ITT; KIT exon 11 8.3 vs 7.0 months, HR 0.88) but was better tolerated; sunitinib remained the second-line standard.

records.title: PEAK
records.subtitle: GIST · Advanced GIST — second-line & beyond · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Advanced GIST after imatinib failure/intolerance (second-line) Bezuclastinib + sunitinib vs sunitinib Progression-free survival The combination improved PFS (16.5 vs 9.2 months, HR 0.50) and ORR (46% vs 26%); poised to redefine second-line therapy (FDA priority review, PDUFA Nov 2026).

records.title: NAVIGATOR
records.subtitle: GIST · Mutation-specific therapy — PDGFRA D842V · Single-arm clinical trial (phase I) · 2020
records.body: Advanced PDGFRA D842V-mutant GIST (imatinib-insensitive) Avapritinib (single arm) Objective response rate Avapritinib produced an ORR of 88% (9% complete responses) with durable benefit (12-month DOR 70%); established avapritinib as standard for PDGFRA D842V-mutant GIST.

records.title: VOYAGER
records.subtitle: GIST · Mutation-specific therapy — PDGFRA D842V · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body: Advanced molecularly unselected GIST, third/fourth line Avapritinib 300 mg once daily (continuous) vs regorafenib 160 mg once daily (3 weeks on / 1 week off) Progression-free survival Avapritinib did not improve PFS over regorafenib (4.2 vs 5.6 months, HR 1.25, p=0.055), missing its primary endpoint; confirmed avapritinib's role is restricted to PDGFRA D842V disease.

records.title: POTOMAC
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) — BCG ± immunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body: High-risk NMIBC (transitional cell carcinoma confined to mucosa or submucosa); BCG-naive (no intravesical BCG within 3 years), within 4 months of TURBT with complete Ta/T1 resection (residual CIS allowed); high risk per EAU: T1, high-grade/G3, CIS, or multiple and recurrent and large tumours (≥3 cm); no prior bladder radiotherapy or immune-mediated cancer therapy; excluded concurrent extravesical NMIBC, immediate cystectomy indicated, autoimmune disorder Durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 4 weeks for 13 cycles (up to 1 year) + intravesical BCG induction (weekly for 6 weeks) and maintenance (three weekly doses at months 3, 6, 12, 18 and 24) vs durvalumab (same schedule) + BCG induction only vs BCG induction and maintenance alone (comparison group); durvalumab stopped early for unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent, or recurrence/persistence of high-risk disease or progression; persistent CIS at 3 months could receive one BCG re-induction, with discontinuation if no response Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: disease-free survival with durvalumab plus BCG induction only vs comparison, proportion alive and disease-free at 24 months, complete response rate at 6 months in carcinoma in situ, EORTC QLQ-C30, time to muscle-invasive bladder cancer or metastatic disease, time to cystectomy, time to development of upper tract urothelial carcinoma, any disease-free survival, overall survival at 5 years, EORTC QLQ-NMIBC24, PRO-CTCAE, pharmacokinetics, immunogenicity, overall survival, duration of complete response, safety In BCG-naive, high-risk NMIBC, 1 year of durvalumab plus BCG induction and maintenance significantly improved disease-free survival vs BCG induction and maintenance alone, with a manageable safety profile. DFS events 67/339 (20%) vs 98/340 (29%); HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.50–0.93); p=0.015 at median follow-up 60.7 mo; 24-mo DFS 86.5% vs 81.6%. Durvalumab plus BCG induction only did not significantly differ in DFS from the comparison group (HR 1.14 [95% CI 0.86–1.50]). OS was descriptive only (HR 0.80 [95% CI 0.53–1.20]; median not reached). In the carcinoma in situ subgroup (not powered), DFS HR was 1.01 (95% CI 0.62–1.64). EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status difference was –2.7 (95% CI –4.85 to –0.54). Grade 3–4 treatment-related AEs: 21% (induction and maintenance) vs 15% (induction only) vs 4% (BCG alone); immune-mediated AEs 27%, 34% and 1% (grade 3–4: 8%, 8%, <1%); no treatment-related deaths.

records.title: SWOG-8710
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Neoadjuvant & perioperative chemotherapy — muscle-invasive bladder cancer · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2003
records.body: Transitional-cell carcinoma of the bladder; muscle-invasive clinical stage T2N0M0 to T4aN0M0 (invasion of superficial muscle up to surrounding viscera but not the pelvic side wall), candidates for radical cystectomy, neoadjuvant setting; SWOG performance status 0 or 1 with adequate renal, hepatic and hematologic function; prior pelvic irradiation excluded Three 28-day cycles of neoadjuvant M-VAC (methotrexate 30 mg/m² days 1, 15, 22; vinblastine 3 mg/m² days 2, 15, 22; doxorubicin 30 mg/m² and cisplatin 70 mg/m² day 2) → radical cystectomy with bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy vs radical cystectomy with bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy alone Primary: overall survival. Secondary: tumor down-staging (pT0 rate), disease-specific survival, adverse effects, postoperative complications Neoadjuvant M-VAC before radical cystectomy increased the likelihood of no residual cancer at cystectomy and was associated with improved survival vs cystectomy alone. Median OS 77 vs 46 mo (two-sided P=0.06 by stratified log-rank; design specified one-sided testing, only two-sided P values reported); survival at five years 57% vs 43%; HR for death with cystectomy alone 1.33 (95% CI 1.00 to 1.76); median follow-up 8.7 and 8.4 yr. pT0 at cystectomy 38% (48 of 126) vs 15% of 121 (P<0.001); 85% of patients with a pT0 specimen were alive at five years. Exploratory disease-specific HR 1.66 (95% CI 1.22 to 2.45; P=0.002). Among 150 evaluable M-VAC patients, 33% had grade 4 granulocytopenia and 17% grade 3 GI toxicity; no deaths were attributable to M-VAC, and postoperative complications did not differ significantly.
records.keywords: Grossman et al. N Engl J Med 2003;349:859-866  12944571

records.title: Advanced Bladder Cancer (ABC) Meta-analysis Collaboration
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Neoadjuvant & perioperative chemotherapy — muscle-invasive bladder cancer · Individual patient data meta-analysis · 2003
records.body: Biopsy-proven invasive transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder, clinical stage T2–T4a; patients receiving local definitive treatment (radical cystectomy, radical radiotherapy, or preoperative radiotherapy and cystectomy); properly randomised trials, closed to accrual, of the same local treatment with vs without neoadjuvant chemotherapy; excluded: comparisons confounded by additional agents or interventions Neoadjuvant platinum-based chemotherapy (single-agent cisplatin; cisplatin combined with one or more of doxorubicin/epirubicin, methotrexate and vinblastine; or carboplatin 300 mg/m² in two cycles with methotrexate and vinblastine; cisplatin 70 mg/m² per cycle for two to four cycles to 100 mg/m² per cycle given in two or three cycles, every 2–4 weeks) → local definitive treatment (radical cystectomy, radical radiotherapy, or preoperative radiotherapy and cystectomy) vs the same local treatment alone Primary: overall survival. Secondary: overall disease-free survival, locoregional disease-free survival, metastases-free survival Neoadjuvant platinum-based combination chemotherapy improved overall survival in invasive bladder cancer, encouraging its use; no evidence supported single-agent platinum. Combination trials: OS HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.78–0.97, p=0.016); 5-year absolute benefit 5% (1%–9%), survival 45% to 50%; DFS HR 0.81 (0.74–0.90); metastases-free survival HR 0.82 (0.73–0.92). All trials: OS HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.83–1.01), not significant (p=0.084). Single-agent cisplatin trials (376 patients): HR 1.15 (0.90–1.47), not significant; interaction p=0.044. Benefit did not differ by local treatment (interaction p=0.628). Median follow-up was 6.2 years. Patient subgroup analyses were exploratory with low power. IPD were unavailable for one eligible trial of 317 patients. Toxicity and quality of life could not be combined across trials.
records.keywords: Advanced Bladder Cancer (ABC) Meta-analysis Collaboration. Lancet 2003;361:1927-1934  12801735

records.title: GETUG-AFU V05 VESPER
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Neoadjuvant & perioperative chemotherapy — muscle-invasive bladder cancer · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body: Muscle-invasive urothelial bladder carcinoma (variants only if combined with classical urothelial carcinoma); perioperative chemotherapy before or after radical cystectomy, no prior chemotherapy for muscle-invasive disease; neoadjuvant: cT2, cT3 or cT4a N0 (nodes ≤10 mm on CT) M0; adjuvant: pT3, pT4 or pN1–2 any pT, M0; creatinine clearance ≥50 mL/min; excluded pure adenocarcinoma, pure squamous or small-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma, LVEF <50%, cancer within 5 years, age >80 years dd-MVAC: methotrexate 30 mg/m² day 1, vinblastine 3 mg/m² day 2, doxorubicin 30 mg/m² day 2, cisplatin 70 mg/m² day 2 with G-CSF days 3-9, every 2 weeks for 6 cycles vs GC: gemcitabine 1,250 mg/m² days 1 and 8 plus cisplatin 70 mg/m² day 1, every 3 weeks for 4 cycles; either regimen given neoadjuvant before or adjuvant after radical cystectomy Primary: 3-year progression-free survival. Secondary: time to progression, overall survival, time to death due to bladder cancer, chemotherapy toxicity, response rate, pathologic response, postoperative complications Three-year PFS was numerically higher with dd-MVAC than GC, but the trial did not meet its primary endpoint: 64% vs 56%; HR 0.77 (95% CI, 0.57 to 1.02), P = .066. TTP was significantly longer with dd-MVAC (3-year 69% vs 58%; HR 0.68). In the neoadjuvant group (437 patients; after a treatment-by-setting interaction), 3-year PFS was 66% vs 56% (HR 0.70 [95% CI, 0.51 to 0.96]), organ-confined response 77% vs 63% and pCR 42% vs 36% (P = .2); adjuvant results (56 patients) were inconclusive. Final 5-year analysis (median follow-up 5.3 years; descriptive): OS 64% vs 56% (HRstrat 0.79 [0.59-1.05]; no evidence of benefit); neoadjuvant 66% vs 57% (HR 0.71 [0.52-0.97]); bladder-cancer death 27% vs 40%, other-cause death 10% vs 4%. Grade ≥3 hematologic toxicity 52% vs 55%; asthenia 14% vs 4.1%, more severe anemia and GI toxicity on dd-MVAC; 4 deaths during chemotherapy, 3 with dd-MVAC (sudden death, pulmonary embolism, septic shock).
records.keywords: Pfister et al. J Clin Oncol 2022;40:2013-2022  35254888 Pfister et al. Lancet Oncol 2024;25:255-264  38142702

records.title: IMvigor010
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Perioperative & adjuvant immunotherapy — muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body: Muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma of bladder or upper tract (latter capped at 10%); adjuvant, ≤14 weeks after radical cystectomy/nephroureterectomy with lymph node dissection and negative margins; PD-L1 IC2/IC3 (≥5%) until amendment, then all-comers; ypT2–4a or ypN+ after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, or pT3–4a or pN+ if none and cisplatin-ineligible/declining; no residual disease, metastasis, autoimmune disease or post-surgical radiotherapy/adjuvant chemotherapy Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV every 3 weeks for 16 cycles or 1 year, whichever first, or until recurrence or unacceptable toxicity (no dose reductions) vs observation over the same period Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, disease-specific survival, distant metastasis-free survival, non-urinary tract recurrence-free survival, pharmacokinetics, patient-reported outcomes (EQ-5D), safety Adjuvant atezolizumab did not improve disease-free survival over observation (primary endpoint not met); the authors conclude these data do not support adjuvant checkpoint inhibitor therapy in this setting. Median DFS 19.4 vs 16.6 mo; stratified HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.74–1.08), p=0.24; median follow-up 21.9 mo. No prespecified subgroup, including PD-L1 status, showed significant benefit. At the first interim OS analysis (immature; formal testing not permitted), deaths were 118/406 vs 124/403 and median OS was not reached; HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.66–1.09). Serious adverse events 31% vs 18%; treatment-related grade 3 or 4 adverse events in 16% with atezolizumab; adverse events led to atezolizumab discontinuation in 16%, more often than in metastatic studies; one treatment-related death (acute respiratory distress syndrome).

records.title: CheckMate 274
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Perioperative & adjuvant immunotherapy — muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body: High-risk muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma (bladder, ureter or renal pelvis); adjuvant setting after R0 radical surgery within 120 days before randomization; pT3, pT4a or pN+ and ineligible for or declined adjuvant cisplatin if no neoadjuvant cisplatin, or ypT2 to ypT4a or ypN+ after neoadjuvant cisplatin; disease-free on examination and imaging within 4 weeks; upper tract enrollment capped at approximately 20% Nivolumab 240 mg IV every 2 weeks vs placebo every 2 weeks (double-blind), each for up to 1 year or until disease recurrence or discontinuation from the trial Primary: disease-free survival in all randomized patients and in patients with tumour PD-L1 ≥1%. Secondary: survival free from recurrence outside the urothelial tract, overall survival, disease-specific survival, distant metastasis–free survival, safety, side-effect profile, health-related quality of life, PFS2 Adjuvant nivolumab significantly prolonged DFS vs placebo after radical surgery for high-risk muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma, in all randomized patients and in PD-L1 ≥1%, with benefit sustained at a median 36.1-mo follow-up. At that cut: all randomized median DFS 22.0 vs 10.9 mo, HR 0.71 (95% CI 0.58–0.86); PD-L1 ≥1% 52.6 vs 8.4 mo, HR 0.52 (95% CI 0.37–0.72). NUTRFS (all randomized): 25.9 vs 13.7 mo; HR 0.72. Interim OS did not cross the significance boundary: all randomized median 69.5 vs 50.1 mo, HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.61–0.96); PD-L1 ≥1% HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.36–0.86). Subgroup signals of a larger effect in bladder primaries and after neoadjuvant chemotherapy are hypothesis-generating. No QoL deterioration vs placebo. Treatment-related grade ≥3 AEs 17.9% vs 7.2%; treatment-related AEs led to discontinuation in 12.8% vs 2.0%; treatment-related deaths with nivolumab: two from pneumonitis, one from bowel perforation; no new signals at extended follow-up.
records.keywords: Bajorin et al. N Engl J Med 2021;384:2102-2114  34077643 Galsky et al. J Clin Oncol 2024;43:15-21  39393026 J Clin Oncol 2025;43:15-21 expanded efficacy 39393026

records.title: NIAGARA
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Perioperative & adjuvant immunotherapy — muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Muscle-invasive urothelial bladder cancer, including divergent differentiation or other histologic subtypes; cisplatin-eligible, clinical T2, T3 or T4a, N0 or N1, M0, medically fit for radical cystectomy, no prior systemic chemotherapy or immunotherapy for MIBC; creatinine clearance ≥40 ml/min/1.73 m2 (40 to <60 limited to up to 20%; T2N0 limited to approximately 40%); excluded pure nonurothelial carcinoma or any small-cell features Neoadjuvant durvalumab 1500 mg IV plus gemcitabine 1000 mg per square meter days 1 and 8 and cisplatin 70 mg per square meter day 1 (split 35 mg per square meter days 1 and 8 if creatinine clearance 40 to <60) every 3 weeks for four cycles → radical cystectomy → adjuvant durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 4 weeks for up to eight cycles vs same neoadjuvant gemcitabine–cisplatin → radical cystectomy alone Primary: pathological complete response, event-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, event-free survival at 24 months, safety, overall survival at 5 years, health-related quality of life, radical cystectomy rate Perioperative durvalumab with neoadjuvant gemcitabine–cisplatin significantly improved EFS and OS vs neoadjuvant chemotherapy alone (interim analyses). 24-mo EFS 67.8% vs 59.8%; HR 0.68 (95% CI, 0.56–0.82); median follow-up 42.3 mo. 24-mo OS 82.2% vs 75.2%; HR 0.75 (95% CI, 0.59–0.93). The pCR dual primary endpoint was not significant at its 0.001 threshold: 33.8% vs 25.8% (P=0.004); an unplanned descriptive reanalysis gave 37.3% vs 27.5%. Radical cystectomy 88.0% vs 83.2%. Open-label; the contribution of each treatment phase was not isolated. Grade 3–4 treatment-related AEs 40.6% vs 40.9%; treatment-related deaths 0.6% in each group; immune-mediated AEs 20.9% vs 3.0%; surgery-related deaths within 90 days 2.1% vs 1.8%.

records.title: AMBASSADOR (Alliance A031501)
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Perioperative & adjuvant immunotherapy — muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body: Muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma of the urinary tract (upper-tract or urethral allowed) or lymph node–positive disease; adjuvant, radical surgery 4–16 weeks before preregistration; after neoadjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy ypT2 or higher, ypN+ or positive margins, otherwise pT3 or higher, pN+ or positive margins; any PD-L1 status, tissue for central testing; no metastases on imaging; variant histology allowed if urothelial predominant, neuroendocrine excluded Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks for up to 1 year (18 cycles) or until disease progression or unacceptable adverse events vs observation at similar intervals until disease progression Primary: disease-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: disease-free survival in PD-L1-positive tumours, disease-free survival in PD-L1-negative tumours, overall survival in PD-L1-positive tumours, overall survival in PD-L1-negative tumours, safety Adjuvant pembrolizumab significantly lengthened disease-free survival vs observation after radical surgery for high-risk muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma. Median DFS was 29.6 vs 14.2 mo (HR 0.73; 95% CI 0.59–0.90) at a median follow-up of 44.8 mo. OS is immature: at the second interim analysis it did not cross the efficacy boundary; 3-yr OS was 60.8% vs 61.9% (HR 0.98; 95% CI 0.76–1.26), and 52.2% of observation patients with progression later received a checkpoint inhibitor. DFS HR was 0.71 (95% CI 0.53–0.95) in PD-L1-negative and 0.81 (95% CI 0.61–1.08) in PD-L1-positive (CPS ≥10) tumours; the authors judged PD-L1 prognostic but not predictive. The trial closed early after adjuvant nivolumab was approved, and more observation patients withdrew. Any-cause grade ≥3 AEs occurred in 50.6% vs 31.6%; 19.7% stopped pembrolizumab for AEs; 5 grade 5 events were attributed to pembrolizumab.

records.title: KEYNOTE-905/EV-303
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Perioperative & adjuvant immunotherapy — muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Muscle-invasive bladder cancer with predominantly (≥50%) urothelial histology on central review; clinically nonmetastatic T2 to T4a N0M0 or T1 to T4a N1M0, able to undergo surgery; ineligible for cisplatin (Galsky criteria, modified to omit peripheral neuropathy) or declined cisplatin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy; ECOG 0 to 2 Enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg IV days 1 and 8 + pembrolizumab 200 mg day 1 every 3 weeks × 3 neoadjuvant cycles → radical cystectomy with pelvic lymph-node dissection → adjuvant enfortumab vedotin × 6 cycles + pembrolizumab × 14 cycles (9 and 17 total cycles), until progression/recurrence, unacceptable toxicity or maximum cycles vs radical cystectomy with pelvic lymph-node dissection alone (adjuvant nivolumab permitted when clinically indicated) Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, pathological complete response, disease-free survival, pathological downstaging, safety, event-free survival by pathological complete response status Perioperative enfortumab vedotin–pembrolizumab plus surgery significantly improved event-free and overall survival and pCR vs surgery alone in predominantly cisplatin-ineligible MIBC. At the first interim analysis (median follow-up 25.6 mo), 2-yr EFS was 74.7% vs 39.4% (HR 0.40; 95% CI 0.28–0.57) and 2-yr OS 79.7% vs 63.1% (HR 0.50; 95% CI 0.33–0.74); pCR 57.1% vs 8.6% (difference 48.3 percentage points). Surgery rates were similar (87.6% vs 89.7%); 58.8% of the EV–pembrolizumab group started adjuvant therapy, and 18.6% of operated controls received adjuvant nivolumab. Grade ≥3 AEs 71.3% vs 45.9% (longer reporting window with EV–pembrolizumab); drug-related grade ≥3 45.5%, drug-related discontinuation 37.1%. AEs led to death in 7.8% vs 5.7%, including 2 drug-related deaths (myasthenia gravis, toxic epidermal necrolysis).

records.title: KEYNOTE-B15/EV-304
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Perioperative & adjuvant immunotherapy — muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Muscle-invasive bladder cancer with predominant (≥50%) urothelial histology; clinical stage T2–T4a N0M0 or T1–T4a N1M0 confirmed by central review, perioperative curative-intent setting; not selected by PD-L1 (randomization stratified by CPS ≥10 vs <10); eligible for radical cystectomy with pelvic lymph-node dissection and cisplatin-eligible (none of the Galsky et al. ineligibility criteria), ECOG 0–1 Neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg days 1 and 8 + pembrolizumab 200 mg day 1 every 3 weeks for 4 cycles → radical cystectomy with pelvic lymph-node dissection → adjuvant 5 cycles of enfortumab vedotin + 13 cycles of pembrolizumab vs neoadjuvant cisplatin 70 mg/m² day 1 + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks for 4 cycles → cystectomy (adjuvant nivolumab permitted by amendment when clinically indicated); trial treatment stopped at an event, unacceptable adverse effects, declined cystectomy or pembrolizumab interruption lasting 12 weeks or more Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, pathological complete response, safety, disease-free survival, pathological downstaging Perioperative enfortumab vedotin–pembrolizumab significantly improved event-free and overall survival and pathological complete response vs neoadjuvant cisplatin–gemcitabine, with more grade ≥3 adverse events. At the first interim analysis (median 33.6 mo from randomization), 24-mo EFS was 79.4% vs 66.2% (HR 0.53; 95% CI 0.41–0.70) and 24-mo OS 86.9% vs 81.3% (HR 0.65; 95% CI 0.48–0.89); pCR 55.8% vs 32.5%. Grade ≥3 adverse events of any cause occurred in 75.7% vs 67.2% and serious adverse events in 63.3% vs 48.0%, partly reflecting longer therapy; drug-related adverse events led to discontinuation in 35.2% vs 11.1%. Fatal adverse events occurred in 4.2% vs 2.8%; deaths were attributed to treatment in 0.5% vs 0.3%.

records.title: IMvigor011
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Perioperative & adjuvant immunotherapy — muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body: Muscle-invasive bladder cancer after cystectomy; adjuvant setting, (y)pT2–4aN0M0 or (y)pT0–4aN+M0, enrolled 6 to 24 weeks after cystectomy, with or without prior neoadjuvant chemotherapy (if none, adjuvant chemotherapy considered inappropriate); ctDNA-positive on serial surveillance for up to 1 year; radiographically disease-free, confirmed at independent review; persistently ctDNA-negative patients not randomized or treated Atezolizumab 1680 mg IV every 4 weeks for 12 cycles or up to 1 year, or until disease recurrence or unacceptable toxicity vs placebo IV on the same schedule (double-blind) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, distant metastasis-free survival, disease-specific survival, ctDNA clearance, patient-reported outcomes, safety, disease-free survival in persistently ctDNA-negative patients, overall survival in persistently ctDNA-negative patients In ctDNA-positive muscle-invasive bladder cancer after cystectomy, ctDNA-guided adjuvant atezolizumab significantly prolonged disease-free and overall survival vs placebo. Median DFS 9.9 vs 4.8 mo (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.47–0.87); median OS 32.8 vs 21.1 mo (HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.39–0.90; interim OS analysis); median follow-up 16.1 mo. Survival follow-up is short and subgroups small; DFS appeared similar between arms when first ctDNA positivity occurred >20 weeks after cystectomy. In 357 persistently ctDNA-negative untreated patients (exploratory), DFS was 95% at 1 yr and 88% at 2 yr. records.title: BC2001
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Bladder-preservation — trimodality therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2012
records.body: Node-negative, nonmetastatic T2–T4a bladder cancer of transitional-cell, squamous-cell or adenocarcinoma histology, treated with bladder-preserving radiotherapy; prior neoadjuvant platinum was allowed Radiotherapy 55 Gy in 20 fractions over 4 weeks or 64 Gy in 32 fractions over 6.5 weeks plus fluorouracil 500 mg/m2 body-surface area/day by continuous infusion during radiotherapy fractions 1-5 and 16-20 (10 days total) and mitomycin C 12 mg/m2 IV bolus on day 1 vs Radiotherapy 55 Gy in 20 fractions over 4 weeks or 64 Gy in 32 fractions over 6.5 weeks Primary: Locoregional disease-free survival. Secondary: Disease-free survival, metastasis-free survival, overall survival, invasive locoregional recurrence, salvage cystectomy, bladder-cancer mortality, safety, bladder function, quality of life Concurrent fluorouracil–mitomycin improved 2-year locoregional DFS over radiotherapy alone (67% vs 54%; HR 0.68) and reduced invasive locoregional recurrence. 5-year OS was 48% vs 35%, but statistical significance was not reached (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.63–1.09). Acute grade 3–5 events were 36.0% vs 27.5%; late grade 3–4 toxicity was not increased. Quality-of-life data were not shown and time to cystectomy was underpowered with nonproportional hazards.

records.title: von der Maase et al.
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · First-line therapy — advanced / metastatic urothelial carcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2000
records.body: Histologically proven transitional-cell carcinoma of the urothelium; locally advanced (T4b, N2, N3) or metastatic (M1), stage IV, no prior systemic chemotherapy or immunotherapy (prior intravesical therapy, immunotherapy or radiation allowed if completed ≥4 weeks before); measurable or assessable disease, Karnofsky ≥70, creatinine clearance ≥60 mL/min; excluded CNS metastases, second primary malignancy, clinically significant pleural effusions or ascites GC: gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² days 1, 8 and 15 + cisplatin 70 mg/m² day 2 vs standard MVAC: methotrexate 30 mg/m² days 1, 15 and 22, vinblastine 3 mg/m² days 2, 15 and 22, doxorubicin 30 mg/m² day 2, cisplatin 70 mg/m² day 2; both every 28 days for a maximum of six cycles unless progressive disease, unacceptable toxicity or a patient, physician or sponsor request to discontinue Primary: overall survival. Secondary: objective tumor response, duration of response, time to progressive disease, time to treatment failure, toxicity, changes in performance status, changes in weight, quality of life, medical resource utilization GC gave survival similar to MVAC with better safety and tolerability; the trial was powered to detect a 33% survival difference, so this shows no significant difference rather than proven equivalence. Median OS 13.8 vs 14.8 mo (HR 1.04, 95% CI 0.82–1.32; P=.75) at 19 mo median follow-up; median time to progressive disease 7.4 vs 7.4 mo; independently reviewed response rate 49.4% vs 45.7%. Toxic deaths were 1% vs 3% (not significant), mostly from neutropenic complications. MVAC caused more neutropenic fever (14% vs 2%), neutropenic sepsis (12% vs 1%) and grade 3/4 mucositis (22% vs 1%); GC caused more grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia (57% vs 21%) and anemia (27% vs 18%), with grade 3 bleeding at 2% on each arm. QoL was maintained on both arms, but the generic questionnaire did not capture the toxicity advantage.

records.title: CheckMate 901
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · First-line therapy — advanced / metastatic urothelial carcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body: Histologically confirmed unresectable or metastatic urothelial carcinoma of the renal pelvis, ureter, bladder or urethra; previously untreated, first-line; no biomarker selection (PD-L1 used for stratification); cisplatin-eligible, including GFR ≥60 ml per minute, ECOG 0 or 1; prior neoadjuvant therapy, radiation or adjuvant platinum allowed only with recurrence ≥12 months after completion Nivolumab 360 mg IV + gemcitabine–cisplatin every 3 weeks for up to six cycles → nivolumab 480 mg every 4 weeks until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent or a maximum of 2 years vs gemcitabine–cisplatin alone every 3 weeks for up to six cycles (open-label) Primary: overall survival, progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival in PD-L1 ≥1%, progression-free survival in PD-L1 ≥1%, change in health-related quality of life by European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire–Core 30 (EORTC QLQ-C30) global health status, objective response rate, complete response rate, duration of response, duration of complete response, safety Adding nivolumab to gemcitabine–cisplatin significantly improved outcomes vs gemcitabine–cisplatin alone in previously untreated advanced urothelial carcinoma. At median follow-up 33.6 mo, OS HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.63–0.96; P=0.02); median OS 21.7 vs 18.9 mo. PFS by central review HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.59–0.88; P=0.001); median 7.9 vs 7.6 mo; 12-mo PFS 34.2% vs 21.8%. Exploratory: ORR 57.6% vs 43.1%, CR 21.7% vs 11.8%, median duration of CR 37.1 vs 13.2 mo. In PD-L1 ≥1%, OS HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.53–1.06), not adjusted for multiplicity. QLQ-C30 global health status was stable through week 16. Grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs 61.8% vs 51.7%; 1 grade 5 treatment-related event per arm (sepsis; acute kidney injury).

records.title: EV-302 (KEYNOTE-A39)
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · First-line therapy — advanced / metastatic urothelial carcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Unresectable locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma, including squamous or mixed differentiation; previously untreated (first-line); no nectin-4 or PD-L1 preselection; cisplatin-eligible or -ineligible, ECOG ≤2; excluded prior PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor or other systemic therapy (except neoadjuvant/adjuvant chemotherapy with recurrence >12 months after completion), uncontrolled diabetes, grade ≥2 neuropathy, autoimmune disease treated systemically within 2 years Enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg IV (max 125 mg) days 1 and 8 + pembrolizumab 200 mg IV day 1, every 3 weeks, until progression, unacceptable toxicity or subsequent therapy (pembrolizumab max 35 cycles; enfortumab vedotin no set maximum) vs gemcitabine 1000 mg per square meter IV days 1 and 8 + cisplatin 70 mg per square meter or carboplatin AUC 4.5 to 5 IV day 1 (by cisplatin eligibility), every 3 weeks, max 6 cycles; maintenance therapy permitted where available Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: overall response rate, duration of response, time to pain progression, safety, complete response rate, adverse events of special interest Enfortumab vedotin–pembrolizumab significantly improved PFS and OS over platinum-based chemotherapy in untreated locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma, with a safety profile consistent with prior reports. Median PFS 12.5 vs 6.3 mo (HR 0.45; 95% CI 0.38–0.54); median OS 31.5 vs 16.1 mo (HR 0.47; 95% CI 0.38–0.58) at the interim OS analysis, considered final, after 359 of 489 required deaths (median follow-up 17.2 mo). Benefit was consistent across prespecified subgroups, including cisplatin eligibility and PD-L1 status. Confirmed ORR 67.7% vs 44.4%; CR 29.1% vs 12.5%. Time to pain progression did not differ significantly (HR 0.92; 95% CI 0.72–1.17). Grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs 55.9% vs 69.5%; with EV-pembrolizumab, grade ≥3 skin reactions 15.5%, peripheral neuropathy 6.8%, hyperglycemia 6.1%, pneumonitis 3.6%; treatment-related discontinuation 35.0% vs 18.5%; 4 treatment-related deaths per group.

records.title: RC48-C016

records.body: Histopathologically confirmed unresectable locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer; first-line: no prior systemic chemotherapy and no progression or recurrence within 12 months after neoadjuvant or adjuvant treatment; centrally confirmed HER2 expression (IHC 1+, 2+ or 3+; VENTANA 4B5), IHC 1+ limited to up to 33% of enrolment; cisplatin-eligible or -ineligible Disitamab vedotin 2.0 mg/kg + toripalimab 3 mg/kg once every 2 weeks, no set maximum number of cycles, until progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal vs gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² days 1 and 8 + cisplatin 70 mg/m² or (if cisplatin-ineligible) carboplatin AUC 4.5 IV day 1, every 3 weeks, maximum 6 cycles Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, duration of response, safety, quality of life, pharmacokinetics, immunogenicity Disitamab vedotin–toripalimab significantly improved PFS and OS vs chemotherapy in untreated HER2-expressing locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer. records.title: KEYNOTE-052
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · First-line therapy — advanced / metastatic urothelial carcinoma · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2017
records.body: Urothelial carcinoma of renal pelvis, ureter, bladder or urethra (transitional or mixed histology); locally advanced unresectable or metastatic, first-line (prior perioperative platinum allowed if recurrence >12 months after completion); cisplatin-ineligible by at least one of ECOG PS 2, creatinine clearance 30–60 mL/min, grade ≥2 hearing loss or neuropathy, NYHA class III heart failure; not PD-L1 selected; excluded active CNS metastases, autoimmune disease, prior checkpoint inhibitor (single-arm) Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks until confirmed progression, intolerable toxicity, withdrawal or completion of 24 months; optional discontinuation after confirmed CR with at least 24 weeks of treatment Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: PD-L1 strongly positive expression cutoff, duration of response, overall survival, progression-free survival, safety, tolerability, disease control rate, time to response First-line pembrolizumab had antitumour activity and acceptable tolerability in cisplatin-ineligible patients, most of whom were elderly or had poor prognostic factors; this was a single-arm, estimation-only study with no hypothesis testing, so comparative benefit is unestablished. At ~5-yr follow-up (median 56.3 mo), responses remained durable: centrally assessed ORR 28.9% (CR 9.5%), median DoR 33.4 mo, 36-mo DoR rate 44.8%. ORR was 47.3% (52/110) with CPS ≥10 vs 20.7% (52/251) with CPS <10, and median OS was 18.5 vs 9.7 mo; these subgroup analyses are hypothesis generating. Median PFS was 2.5 mo; median OS was 11.3 mo and 48-mo OS 19.0%. No new safety signals emerged: treatment-related grade 3-5 AEs 21.1%, immune-mediated AEs or infusion reactions (any cause) 26.5%, serious treatment-related AEs 11.6%; 9.5% discontinued for treatment-related AEs. One treatment-related death (myositis, with grade 4 myocarditis); no additional deaths at this cut.

records.title: IMvigor210 (cohort 1)
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · First-line therapy — advanced / metastatic urothelial carcinoma · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2017
records.body: Inoperable locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (renal pelvis, ureters, bladder or urethra); previously untreated, first-line; not selected by PD-L1, but tumour sample for PD-L1 testing required; cisplatin-ineligible by ≥1 of GFR >30 and <60 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault), grade ≥2 hearing loss or peripheral neuropathy, or ECOG PS 2; ECOG PS ≤2; prior neoadjuvant/adjuvant chemotherapy or radiation only if >12 months before recurrence (single-arm) Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV every 21 days until unacceptable toxicity or investigator-assessed radiographic progression Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: investigator-assessed objective response rate, duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, clinical benefit rate, safety, biomarker correlates of response and survival Atezolizumab showed encouraging durable responses, survival and tolerability in untreated cisplatin-ineligible metastatic urothelial cancer, but this single-arm study missed its primary hierarchical test. Final safety: treatment-related AEs 74.8%, grade 3/4 21.8%; one treatment-related death (sepsis); any-cause AE discontinuation 13.4%; grade 3/4 AESIs 10.9%; no new safety signals.

records.title: JAVELIN Bladder 100
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Switch-maintenance therapy — advanced urothelial carcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body: Unresectable locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma; stage IV (RECIST 1.1-measurable) before first-line chemotherapy, maintenance setting; not PD-L1 selected (SP263-positive subset co-primary); no progression (CR, PR or SD) after four to six cycles of gemcitabine plus cisplatin or carboplatin, 4 to 10 weeks since last dose; excluded adjuvant/neoadjuvant systemic therapy within 12 months, prior or contraindicated checkpoint inhibitor Avelumab 10 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks plus best supportive care until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or consent withdrawal (no dose reductions) vs best supportive care alone (no other systemic antitumor therapy; palliative local radiotherapy for isolated lesions allowed) Primary: overall survival (overall population and PD-L1-positive population). Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response, time to response, duration of response, disease control, safety Maintenance avelumab plus best supportive care significantly prolonged OS vs best supportive care alone in patients without progression on first-line platinum chemotherapy, in both primary populations; benefit persisted with ≥2 yr follow-up (exploratory update, descriptive P values). Overall population, ≥2-yr cut: median OS 23.8 vs 15.0 mo; 2-yr OS 49.8% vs 38.4%; HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.63–0.91), closer to 1 than initially. PD-L1-positive, initial analysis: 1-yr OS 79.1% vs 60.4%; HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.40–0.79). Investigator-assessed PFS, ≥2-yr cut: median 5.5 vs 2.1 mo (HR 0.54). Initial PD-L1-negative OS HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.62–1.18). Subsequent PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor in 53.1% of controls. Initial safety: grade ≥3 AEs 47.4% vs 25.2%; immune-related AEs 29.4% (grade 3 7.0%); AE-related discontinuation 11.9%; two deaths (0.6%) attributed to avelumab toxicity. ≥2-yr cut: avelumab grade ≥3 AEs 53.8%; one treatment-related death (immune-mediated nephritis) after ≥12 mo; no new safety signals.
records.keywords: Powles et al. N Engl J Med 2020;383:1218-1230  32945632 Powles et al. J Clin Oncol 2023;41:3486-3492  37071838

records.title: KEYNOTE-045
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Second-line & later therapy — metastatic urothelial carcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body: Advanced urothelial carcinoma (renal pelvis, ureter, bladder or urethra) with predominantly transitional-cell features; progression after platinum-based chemotherapy for advanced disease or recurrence within 12 months of platinum adjuvant/neoadjuvant therapy, two or fewer prior chemotherapy lines; PD-L1-evaluable tumour sample required; excluded ECOG 2 with Hb <10 g/dl, liver metastases or last chemotherapy <3 months before enrollment, and prior anti-PD-1/PD-L1/CTLA-4 therapy Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks for up to 2 years vs investigator's choice of paclitaxel 175 mg/m², docetaxel 75 mg/m² or vinflunine 320 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks; open-label, treatment until RECIST progression, unacceptable toxicity, consent withdrawal or investigator decision Primary: overall survival, progression-free survival (total population and PD-L1 CPS ≥10%). Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, safety, time to response Pembrolizumab significantly prolonged OS (by about 3 mo) and caused fewer treatment-related adverse events than investigator's-choice chemotherapy after platinum. At the second interim analysis (median follow-up 14.1 mo; early termination for OS superiority), median OS was 10.3 vs 7.4 mo (HR 0.73; 95% CI 0.59–0.91) and 8.0 vs 5.2 mo with PD-L1 CPS ≥10% (HR 0.57; 95% CI 0.37–0.88). Co-primary PFS was not improved: median 2.1 vs 3.3 mo (HR 0.98; 95% CI 0.81–1.19); HR 0.89 with CPS ≥10%. ORR was 21.1% vs 11.4%; median DoR not reached vs 4.3 mo (≥12 months: 68% vs 35%). Treatment-related AEs 60.9% vs 90.2%, grade 3–5 15.0% vs 49.4%; discontinuation 5.6% vs 11.0%; 4 treatment-related deaths in each arm, including one pneumonitis death with pembrolizumab.
records.keywords: Bellmunt et al. N Engl J Med 2017;376:1015-1026  28212060

records.title: EV-301
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Second-line & later therapy — metastatic urothelial carcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body: Urothelial carcinoma, including squamous or mixed differentiation; unresectable locally advanced or metastatic disease after platinum-containing chemotherapy and progression or relapse during/after a PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor; nectin-4 expression not required; progression within 12 months of neoadjuvant/adjuvant platinum; excluded grade ≥2 sensory or motor neuropathy, active CNS metastases, uncontrolled diabetes, active keratitis, >1 prior chemotherapy regimen (including neoadjuvant/adjuvant) Enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg (maximum weight 100 kg) IV on days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle vs investigator-chosen chemotherapy (preselected before randomization): docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV, paclitaxel 175 mg/m² IV or vinflunine 320 mg/m² IV (where approved; capped at 35% of patients), on day 1 of a 21-day cycle, each until radiologic disease progression, other discontinuation criteria or study completion Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall response rate, disease control rate, complete response rate, duration of response, safety Enfortumab vedotin significantly prolonged overall survival vs standard chemotherapy after prior platinum and PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor therapy. The trial met its superiority threshold at the prespecified interim analysis and was stopped early. In an exploratory update (median follow-up 23.75 mo; ITT; 18 chemotherapy patients crossed over), OS benefit was maintained: median 12.91 vs 8.94 mo (HR 0.70; 95% CI 0.58–0.85). Interim 12-month OS was 51.5% vs 39.2%. At the update, median PFS was 5.55 vs 3.71 mo (HR 0.63) and confirmed ORR 41.32% vs 18.58%; interim CR was 4.9% vs 2.7%. Subgroup analyses showed no advantage in women (22.7% of patients). At the update, grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs were 52.4% vs 50.5%, with no new safety signals; with enfortumab vedotin, skin reactions 47.3% (grade ≥3 14.9%), peripheral neuropathy 48.0% (grade ≥3 7.4%), hyperglycemia 6.8% (grade ≥3 4.4%; 1 death at interim). Treatment-related deaths: 7 (2.4%) vs 3 (1.0%) at interim, none added at the update.
