records.title: THOR (Cohort 1)
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Second-line & later therapy — metastatic urothelial carcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body: Metastatic or surgically unresectable urothelial carcinoma; progression during or after previous systemic therapy that included an anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 agent, no more than two previous lines; select FGFR3/2 alterations: FGFR3 mutations (R248C, S249C, G370C or Y373C) or fusions (FGFR2–BICC1, FGFR2–CASP7, FGFR3–TACC3_V1, FGFR3–TACC3_V3, FGFR3–BAIAP2L1) on central or local tissue/blood testing; ECOG 0, 1 or 2 Oral erdafitinib 8 mg per day with pharmacodynamically guided increase to 9 mg on day 14, 21-day cycles vs investigator's choice of chemotherapy (docetaxel 75 mg per square meter IV or vinflunine 320 mg per square meter IV every 3 weeks); until disease progression or unacceptable toxic effects Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response, duration of response, safety, change from baseline in patient-reported outcomes (Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy–Bladder Cancer, Patient Global Impression of Severity, EQ-5D-5L), confirmed objective response Erdafitinib significantly prolonged OS vs investigator's-choice chemotherapy in FGFR-altered metastatic urothelial carcinoma after anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy. At the interim analysis (155 deaths; median follow-up 15.9 mo), median OS was 12.1 vs 7.8 mo; HR 0.64 (95% CI, 0.47–0.88); the IDMC recommended stopping and allowing crossover. Median PFS 5.6 vs 2.7 mo (HR 0.58); investigator-assessed ORR 45.6% vs 11.5%; median DoR 4.9 vs 5.6 mo. No patients had FGFR2 alterations and only 1 Black patient enrolled, limiting extrapolation. Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related AEs 45.9% vs 46.4%; treatment-related deaths 0.7% vs 5.4%. Leading grade ≥3 treatment-related erdafitinib toxicities: palmar–plantar erythrodysesthesia 9.6%, stomatitis 8.1%, onycholysis 5.9%, hyperphosphatemia 5.2%; grade 3 or 4 central serous retinopathy 2.2%.
records.keywords: Loriot et al. N Engl J Med 2023;389:1961-1971  37870920

records.title: POUT
records.subtitle: Bladder & UTUC · Upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) — adjuvant therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body: Upper tract urothelial carcinoma with predominantly transitional cell histology; adjuvant setting after en-bloc radical nephroureterectomy with resection of all abnormal nodes; muscle-invasive (pT2–pT4, Nany) or node-positive (pTany, N1–3) M0 disease, fit for chemotherapy within 90 days of surgery, GFR ≥30 mL/min; excluded residual lymphadenopathy on postoperative imaging and patients otherwise unsuitable for cisplatin Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8 + cisplatin 70 mg/m² IV day 1 (carboplatin AUC4·5 or AUC5 IV day 1 only if GFR ≥30 and <50 mL/min), every 21 days for four cycles, starting within 90 days of nephroureterectomy vs surveillance Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: metastasis-free survival, overall survival, treatment compliance, acute toxicity, late toxicity, patient-reported quality of life Adjuvant gemcitabine–platinum chemotherapy started within 90 days after nephroureterectomy significantly improved disease-free survival in locally advanced UTUC. DFS HR 0·45 (95% CI 0·30–0·68; p=0·0001) at median follow-up 30·3 mo; 3-yr DFS 71% vs 46% (chemotherapy vs surveillance), absolute difference 25%. Recruitment stopped early for efficacy at a preplanned interim analysis after 261 participants (target 345). Metastasis-free survival also improved (HR 0·48, 95% CI 0·31–0·74; 3-yr 71% vs 53%). OS is immature: 62 deaths (24 chemotherapy, 38 surveillance); analysis planned at 88 deaths. Global health status was lower during chemotherapy and at 3 mo, resolving by 6 mo. Grade ≥3 acute treatment-emergent AEs 55 (44%) of 126 vs 5 (4%) of 129, including grade ≥3 neutrophil decrease 36% and febrile neutropenia 6%; serious AEs 32% with chemotherapy; no treatment-related deaths; late toxicity not yet analysed.

records.title: SPCG-4
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Active surveillance & definitive local therapy — clinically localized disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2014
records.body: Clinically localized prostate cancer (largely palpable, pre-PSA era) Radical prostatectomy vs watchful waiting Death from any cause, prostate-cancer death, metastasis Radical prostatectomy reduced prostate-cancer mortality (RR 0.56) and all-cause mortality vs watchful waiting over 23 years (NNT 8 to avoid one death); confirmed a survival benefit of surgery in clinically detected disease.

records.title: ProtecT
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Active surveillance & definitive local therapy — clinically localized disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body: PSA-detected clinically localized prostate cancer Active monitoring vs radical prostatectomy vs radiotherapy Prostate-cancer-specific mortality At a median 15 years prostate-cancer mortality was low and did not differ across monitoring, surgery and radiotherapy (45/1643, 2.7% overall; 3.1% vs 2.2% vs 2.9%; P=0.53, the trial's only alpha-protected comparison); monitoring roughly doubled metastases (9.4% vs 4.7% vs 5.0%) with all-cause deaths similar (356/1643, 21.7%; adjusted HR 0.89 [95% CI 0.69-1.15] and 0.88 [0.68-1.13] vs monitoring, no p reported and intervals unadjusted for multiplicity). Active monitoring was protocol-driven deferral of radical treatment, not sustained surveillance - over half that arm had been treated radically by 10 years - and up to 34% of the cohort was intermediate- or high-risk, so the trial supports a shared trade-off discussion rather than surveillance in a named risk band.

records.title: POP-RT
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Active surveillance & definitive local therapy — clinically localized disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body: Prostate adenocarcinoma, nonmetastatic and node-negative; high-risk/very high-risk, radical radiotherapy with long-term ADT; Roach pelvic nodal risk at least 20%: T1-T3a with Gleason 8-10 and any PSA, Gleason 7 with PSA >15 ng/mL or Gleason 6 with PSA >30 ng/mL, or T3b-T4a with any Gleason/PSA; life expectancy at least 5 years; excluded prior pelvic RT, prior malignancy within 5 years or unsuitable for pelvic RT PORT: image-guided IMRT 68 Gy/25 fractions to prostate only vs WPRT: image-guided IMRT 68 Gy/25 fractions to prostate + 50 Gy/25 fractions to pelvic nodes from L4-5 including common iliac, as simultaneous integrated boost; both arms ADT (LHRH analog or bilateral orchiectomy) starting at least 8 weeks before RT, continued concurrently and after, total 2 years Primary: 5-year biochemical failure-free survival. Secondary: disease-free survival, overall survival, acute toxicity, late toxicity, quality of life, distant metastasis-free survival Prophylactic whole-pelvic RT improved biochemical failure-free survival and DFS vs prostate-only RT in high-risk, locally advanced prostate cancer, but OS did not appear to differ. At median follow-up 68 months, 5-year BFFS was 95.0% with WPRT vs 81.2% with PORT (HR 0.23; 95% CI 0.10-0.52) and 5-year DFS 89.5% vs 77.2% (HR 0.40; 95% CI 0.22-0.73); 5-year OS 92.5% vs 90.8% (HR 0.92; 95% CI 0.41-2.05). Post hoc exploratory DMFS also favoured WPRT (HR 0.35). Only 36 biochemical failures occurred against 120 planned events, so the trial was analysed before the planned event count; single-centre trial. Cumulative late grade ≥II GU toxicity was higher with WPRT (20.0% vs 8.9%); late grade ≥II GI toxicity did not differ significantly (8.2% vs 4.5%), and no grade IV GU or GI toxicity occurred.
records.keywords: Murthy et al. J Clin Oncol 2021;39:1234-1242  33497252

records.title: EORTC 22863
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiotherapy with androgen deprivation — intermediate & high risk · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 1997
records.body: Histologically proved prostatic adenocarcinoma; no previous treatment for prostate cancer; T1–T2 N0-X WHO histologic grade 3, or T3–T4 N0–1 M0 any grade; age under 80; excluded distant metastases (including common iliac or paraaortic nodes) and previous malignancy except treated basal-cell skin carcinoma External irradiation: pelvis 50 Gy over 5 wk, then prostatic boost 20 Gy over 2 wk (2 Gy/fraction, 5 days/wk) vs same radiotherapy + goserelin 3.6 mg SC every 4 wk from day 1 of pelvic irradiation for 3 yr, with cyproterone acetate 50 mg orally three times a day for 1 mo starting 1 wk before first goserelin dose Primary: 5-year clinical disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, disease-free interval, time until first treatment failure after a biologic response, local control, sites of progression, acute and late toxicity, specific survival, biochemically defined disease-free survival, distant metastases, distant metastasis-free survival, cause-specific mortality, cardiovascular mortality, bone fractures, second cancers Immediate androgen suppression with goserelin during and for 3 years after external irradiation improved 10-year disease-free and overall survival in high-metastatic-risk prostate cancer without increasing late cardiovascular toxicity. At median 9.1-yr follow-up, 10-yr clinical DFS (primary) was 47.7% (95% CI 39.0–56.0) with combined treatment vs 22.7% (16.3–29.7) with RT alone; HR 0.42 (0.33–0.55). 10-yr OS 58.1% vs 39.8%, HR 0.60; prostate-cancer mortality 10.3% vs 30.4%, HR 0.38. 10-yr locoregional failure 6.0% vs 23.5%; distant-metastasis-free survival 51% vs 30.2%. 66-month report: biochemical DFS 76% vs 45%; benefit did not differ by risk group (interaction p=0.20). Cardiovascular deaths did not differ (8/53 vs 11/63 with, 14/154 vs 6/145 without baseline cardiovascular disease). 45-month report: grade 3 late effects ≤1% per group; late grade 1–3 incontinence 29% vs 16%; hot flashes 62% with goserelin. Two fractures, both with combined treatment; 19 had <3 yr goserelin.

records.title: RTOG 9408
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiotherapy with androgen deprivation — intermediate & high risk · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2011
records.body: Localized prostate cancer, PSA ≤20 (mostly intermediate-risk) RT + 4-month ADT vs RT alone Overall survival Adding 4 months of ADT to RT improved 10-yr OS (62% vs 57%) and reduced prostate-cancer death (4% vs 8%), with benefit concentrated in intermediate-risk men; defined short-course ADT with RT.

records.title: RTOG 9202
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiotherapy with androgen deprivation — intermediate & high risk · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2003
records.body: Locally advanced (T2c-T4) prostate cancer RT + long-term (28-mo) vs short-term (4-mo) ADT Disease-free survival Long-term ADT improved disease-free and disease-specific survival vs 4 months, with an overall-survival benefit in Gleason 8-10 disease; supported prolonged ADT for high-risk disease.

records.title: EORTC 22961
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiotherapy with androgen deprivation — intermediate & high risk · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2009
records.body: Locally advanced prostate cancer treated with RT 6 months vs 3 years of androgen suppression Overall survival (non-inferiority) Six months of ADT was not non-inferior to 3 years (5-yr mortality 19.0% vs 15.2%, HR 1.42); confirmed long-course ADT as standard with RT for locally advanced disease.

records.title: CAN-2409 (aglatimagene besadenovec)
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiotherapy combination — novel agents · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Intermediate- or high-risk localised prostate cancer planned for EBRT, ECOG 0–2 (USA/Puerto Rico); ADT optional Intraprostatic aglatimagene besadenovec + valacyclovir + EBRT vs placebo + valacyclovir + EBRT (2:1) Disease-free survival (intention-to-treat) Adding intratumoral aglatimagene besadenovec (gene-mediated immunotherapy) + valacyclovir to standard EBRT improved the primary endpoint, disease-free survival, in intermediate/high-risk localised prostate cancer (median not reached vs 86.1 months, HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.52-0.94; p=0.016, ITT, alpha-protected). Grade >=3 TEAEs were 8% (40/479) vs 7% (17/232) in the safety population; no safety comparison is tested, so tolerability is similar on descriptive counts rather than demonstrated equivalent. Overall survival was immature and numerically favoured placebo (HR 1.18, 95% CI 0.64-2.15, nominal p=0.59, 51 deaths). ADT use was optional and stratified, not mandated - so this is an RT-combination, not an RT+ADT, trial.

records.title: CHHiP
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiation dose & fractionation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body: Localized T1b-T3a prostate cancer Moderate hypofractionation (60 Gy/20) vs conventional (74 Gy/37) Biochemical/clinical failure (non-inferiority) 60 Gy in 20 fractions was non-inferior to 74 Gy in 37 (5-yr biochemical/clinical control 90.6% vs 88.3%, HR 0.84) with similar toxicity; established moderate hypofractionation as standard.

records.title: HYPO-RT-PC
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiation dose & fractionation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body: Intermediate-to-high-risk localized prostate cancer Ultra-hypofractionation (42.7 Gy/7) vs conventional (78 Gy/39) Failure-free survival (non-inferiority) Ultra-hypofractionation was non-inferior to conventional RT for failure-free survival (per-protocol; prespecified margin 4% absolute at 5 years, critical HR 1.338): 5-yr FFS 84% in both arms (Widmark 2019; restated as 85% in the 10-yr report), and at 10 years 72% vs 65% with adjusted HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.69-1.03 (Nilsson 2026). Late grade >=2 cumulative incidence was similar - genitourinary 28% vs 30%, gastrointestinal 14% vs 14% (1 minus Kaplan-Meier from start of RT). Non-inferiority licenses no superiority claim, and the two post-hoc analyses point differently: a log-rank test gave p=0.12 (superiority not reached) while a separate fixed-timepoint analysis at 10 years was significant (p=0.025), favouring ultra-hypofractionation; both are post hoc with nominal p, so neither establishes superiority. Only 11% of patients were high-risk and no ADT was permitted, so both reports draw their conclusion for intermediate-risk disease.

records.title: PACE-B
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiation dose & fractionation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Low/favorable-intermediate-risk localized prostate cancer (no ADT) 5-fraction SBRT (36.25 Gy) vs conventional/moderate hypofractionated RT Freedom from biochemical/clinical failure (non-inferiority) Five-fraction SBRT was non-inferior to conventional RT (5-yr freedom from failure 95.8% vs 94.6%) with similar late toxicity; established SBRT as a standard option for lower-risk disease.

records.title: ASCENDE-RT
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiation dose & fractionation · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body: Intermediate- and high-risk localized prostate cancer LDR brachytherapy boost vs dose-escalated EBRT boost (both + 12-mo ADT + pelvic RT) Biochemical progression-free survival An LDR brachytherapy boost roughly halved biochemical failure vs dose-escalated EBRT (b-PFS HR 2.04 favoring brachytherapy; 9-yr ~83% vs 62%) at the cost of more genitourinary toxicity; established brachytherapy boost for higher-risk disease.
records.keywords: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys 2017;98:275-285  28262473

records.title: STAMPEDE
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Intensification in high-risk non-metastatic disease · Meta-analysis · 2022
records.body: Histologically confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma, high-risk non-metastatic (no distant metastases on conventional imaging), starting long-term ADT; node positive or, if node negative, ≥2 of T3/T4, Gleason 8–10, PSA ≥40 ng/mL, or relapsing with high-risk features (≤12 months total ADT with ≥12 months off treatment and PSA ≥4 ng/mL with doubling time <6 months, or PSA ≥20 ng/mL, or nodal relapse); WHO PS 0–2; no age restriction; excluded clinically significant cardiovascular disease Abiraterone trial: ADT alone vs ADT + abiraterone acetate 1000 mg + prednisolone 5 mg orally once daily; abiraterone and enzalutamide trial: ADT alone vs ADT + abiraterone acetate 1000 mg + prednisolone 5 mg + enzalutamide 160 mg orally once daily; ADT (surgery or LHRH agonists/antagonists) for 3 years, with local radiotherapy (74 Gy in 37 fractions or hypofractionated equivalent) mandated for node-negative and encouraged for node-positive disease; combination therapy for 2 years or until progression, whichever came first, or until progression if radiotherapy was omitted Primary: metastasis-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, prostate cancer-specific survival, failure-free survival, progression-free survival, toxicity, adverse events Combination therapy (abiraterone and prednisolone, with or without enzalutamide) added to ADT was associated with significantly longer metastasis-free survival than ADT alone in high-risk non-metastatic prostate cancer (pooled analysis of two trials). At median follow-up 72 months, MFS HR 0·53 (95% CI 0·44–0·64); 6-year MFS 82% vs 69%. OS HR 0·60 (0·48–0·73); 6-year OS 86% vs 77%. Prostate cancer-specific survival (HR 0·49), PFS (HR 0·44) and failure-free survival (HR 0·39) also improved. Adding enzalutamide showed no evidence of a different effect (interaction HR 1·02, 0·70–1·50), though the indirect comparison cannot exclude a small benefit, and it increased toxicity. Relapsed patients were under-represented; heterogeneity was seen for WHO PS 1–2 (HR 0·86, 0·58–1·28). Grade ≥3 AEs in the first 24 months: 37% vs 29% (abiraterone trial) and 57% vs 32% (abiraterone and enzalutamide trial); seven grade 5 events, all in the combination groups.

records.title: PROTEUS
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Intensification in high-risk non-metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Newly diagnosed prostate adenocarcinoma, high-risk localized or locally advanced; candidates for radical prostatectomy with pelvic lymph-node dissection; high risk by NCCN criteria (Gleason score ≥8, PSA ≥20 ng/ml or clinical stage T3) plus trial-specific positive-biopsy-core criteria; clinical N1 allowed; able to receive ADT for ≥13 months by cardiovascular risk; excluded metastatic disease on conventional imaging by blinded central review ADT (GnRH agonist or antagonist) + apalutamide 240 mg orally once daily vs ADT + matched placebo; 6 neoadjuvant 28-day cycles → radical prostatectomy with pelvic lymph-node dissection (apalutamide/placebo paused from 2 weeks before to 4 weeks after surgery) → 6 adjuvant 28-day cycles; ADT continuous throughout the 12-cycle treatment phase Primary: pathological complete response or minimal residual disease, metastasis-free survival. Secondary: event-free survival, first subsequent local or systemic treatment, distant metastasis on conventional imaging or PSMA PET, freedom from disease at 4 years, metastasis-free survival by conventional imaging alone, PSA-free survival with testosterone recovery, safety, low residual cancer burden, castration-resistant prostate cancer, testosterone recovery, overall survival Perioperative ADT plus apalutamide was associated with better oncologic outcomes after radical prostatectomy than ADT plus placebo, with more adverse events; both dual primary endpoints were met. pCR/MRD 8.9% vs 1.0% (OR 10.17; 95% CI 5.27–19.64); MFS at 5 yr 78.2% vs 73.5% (HR 0.80; 95% CI 0.67–0.96; P=0.02) at median follow-up 61.7 mo. EFS (HR 0.71), time to first subsequent therapy (HR 0.65) and time to distant metastasis (HR 0.68) favoured apalutamide; MFS by conventional imaging alone did not differ significantly (HR 0.84; 95% CI 0.67–1.07). OS, assessed as a safety measure with follow-up short for survival, HR 1.08. Grade 3–4 AEs 39.6% vs 31.0%, mainly from rash; discontinuation 7.4% vs 2.7%; AEs leading to death 1.3% vs 0.5%; mortality among patients ≥75 yr 15.2% vs 12.8%. The comparator was ADT plus placebo, not surgery alone.
records.keywords: Taplin et al. N Engl J Med 2026;395:546-560  42223077

records.title: RTOG 9601
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Postoperative radiotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body: Biochemical recurrence after prostatectomy (pT2-3 N0) Salvage RT + 24-mo bicalutamide 150 mg vs salvage RT + placebo Overall survival Adding 2 years of bicalutamide to salvage RT improved 12-yr OS (76.3% vs 71.3%, HR 0.77) and halved prostate-cancer death, with benefit greatest at higher PSA; supported hormone-intensified salvage.

records.title: GETUG-AFU 16
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Postoperative radiotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body: Rising PSA after prostatectomy (0.2-2.0 ng/mL) Salvage RT + 6-mo goserelin vs salvage RT alone Progression-free survival Adding 6 months of goserelin to salvage RT improved 5-yr biochemical/clinical PFS (80% vs 62%, HR 0.50), sustained at 10 years (64% vs 49%); validated short-course ADT with salvage RT.

records.title: RADICALS-RT
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Postoperative radiotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body: Post-prostatectomy with ≥1 risk factor (pT3-4, Gleason 7-10, margin+, PSA≥10) Adjuvant RT vs observation with early salvage RT Freedom from distant metastasis (biochemical PFS reported) Adjuvant RT did not improve 5-yr biochemical PFS vs early salvage (85% vs 88%, HR 1.10) but doubled urinary/bowel toxicity; established observation with early salvage RT as standard.

records.title: SPPORT (RTOG 0534)
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Postoperative radiotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body: Biochemical recurrence after prostatectomy Prostate-bed RT alone vs +short-term ADT vs +ADT + pelvic-node RT Freedom from progression Escalating salvage RT improved 5-yr freedom from progression stepwise (70.9% prostate-bed RT, 81.3% +ADT, 87.4% +ADT + pelvic-node RT); supported adding ADT and pelvic-node coverage in salvage.

records.title: RADICALS-HD
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Postoperative radiotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Postoperative radiotherapy after radical prostatectomy (PSA <5, M0) 24 months vs 6 months of ADT added to postoperative RT (companion randomisation: 6 months vs none) Metastasis-free survival Adding 24 months of ADT improved MFS over 6 months (10-yr MFS 78.1% vs 71.9%, HR 0.77, p=0.029) at the cost of more toxicity; in the companion randomisation, adding 6 months versus no ADT did not significantly improve MFS. Defines ADT duration with postoperative RT - long-course for those who can tolerate it.

records.title: RAVES
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Postoperative radiotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body: Prostate adenocarcinoma after radical prostatectomy; postoperative setting with high-risk pathology (positive surgical margins, extraprostatic extension or seminal vesicle invasion); postoperative PSA ≤0·10 ng/mL and able to start radiotherapy within 4 months of prostatectomy (6 months after a July 8, 2011 amendment); excluded ADT before or after prostatectomy, previous pelvic radiotherapy, total hip replacement, nodal or distant metastases Adjuvant prostate-bed radiotherapy 64 Gy in 32 fractions within 6 months of radical prostatectomy vs observation with PSA every 3 months for the first 5 years → early salvage prostate-bed radiotherapy 64 Gy in 32 fractions within 4 months of PSA ≥0·20 ng/mL; no androgen deprivation therapy in either arm Primary: freedom from biochemical progression. Secondary: time to initiation of androgen deprivation therapy, time to local progression, time to regional progression, time to distant progression, overall survival, quality of life, anxiety and depression, adverse events, disease-specific survival, quality-adjusted life-years, cost-utility Early salvage radiotherapy did not meet the trial-specified non-inferiority criteria, but the authors conclude it gave similar biochemical control to adjuvant radiotherapy, spared around half of men pelvic radiation and had significantly lower genitourinary toxicity. 5-yr freedom from biochemical progression (ITT, cut-off June 30, 2018; median follow-up 6·1 yr) was 86% adjuvant vs 87% salvage; stratified HR 1·12 (95% CI 0·65–1·90), p non-inferiority 0·15. Enrolment closed early for unexpectedly low event rates, reducing power. 84 (50%) salvage-arm patients had radiotherapy triggered by PSA ≥0·20 ng/mL. 5-yr OS 98% salvage vs 99% adjuvant. Grade 2 or worse genitourinary toxicity 54% salvage vs 70% adjuvant; gastrointestinal 10% vs 14% (similar); erectile dysfunction 96% vs 98%. No treatment-related deaths or serious adverse events.
records.keywords: Kneebone et al. Lancet Oncol 2020;21:1331-1340   Tilki et al. Lancet 2020;396:1374-1375  33002430

records.title: CHAARTED (ECOG E3805)
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - docetaxel intensification · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2015
records.body:
Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (pathological diagnosis, or clinical scenario with elevated PSA); radiologic metastases, at start of ADT (ADT for metastatic disease begun within 120 days before randomization without progression allowed); high volume (visceral metastases or ≥4 bone lesions with ≥1 beyond vertebral bodies and pelvis) or, after a July 2008 amendment, low volume; prior adjuvant ADT allowed only if ≤24 months and progression >12 months after completion Ⓐ ADT + docetaxel 75 mg/m² every 3 weeks for six cycles, started at the beginning of ADT (daily prednisone not required)
Ⓑ ADT alone
・ADT: Continuous Primary: overall survival. Secondary: PSA level <0.2 ng/ml at 6 months, PSA level <0.2 ng/ml at 12 months, time to castration-resistant prostate cancer, time to clinical progression, prostate-cancer deaths, safety Docetaxel added to ADT improved OS in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer overall, with benefit confirmed in high-volume disease but not low-volume disease
・OS: Ⓐ 57.6 vs Ⓑ 47.2 mo; HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.59–0.89); median follow-up 53.7 mo
・Subgroups: High-volume Ⓐ 51.2 vs Ⓑ 34.4 mo (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.50–0.79); low-volume HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.70–1.55; P=.86), vs 0.60 at early analysis; interaction P=.033
・Time to CRPC: Ⓐ 19.4 vs Ⓑ 11.7 mo; HR 0.61
・Time to clinical progression: Ⓐ 33.0 vs Ⓑ 19.8 mo; HR 0.62; not improved in low-volume disease (HR 0.86)
・PSA <0.2 ng/ml at 12 mo: Ⓐ 27.7% vs Ⓑ 16.8% (interim)
・Toxicity: Grade 3/4 febrile neutropenia 6.2%, infection with neutropenia 2.3% with docetaxel; 1 possible docetaxel-related sudden death; ADT-alone adverse events not routinely documented
・Limitations: Subgroups prospectively defined but not powered; low-volume OS benefit not confirmed

records.title: STAMPEDE (MRC PR08)
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - docetaxel intensification · Randomised, open-label, multiarm multistage platform clinical trial (phase II/III) · 2016
records.body:
Prostate cancer; newly diagnosed metastatic, node-positive or high-risk locally advanced (at least two of T3/4, Gleason score 8–10, PSA ≥40 ng/mL), or relapsing with high-risk features after radical surgery and/or radiotherapy; starting first-line long-term hormone therapy, begun no longer than 12 weeks before randomisation; fit for chemotherapy, no age restriction; excluded: clinically significant cardiovascular history Ⓐ Standard of care (SOC) only
Ⓑ SOC + zoledronic acid 4 mg IV for six 3-weekly cycles, then 4-weekly until 2 years
Ⓒ SOC + docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV for six 3-weekly cycles with prednisolone 10 mg daily
Ⓓ SOC + zoledronic acid and docetaxel (schedules as Ⓑ and Ⓒ)
・SOC: Hormone therapy for at least 2 years, lifelong for M1 (GnRH agonists or antagonists, or orchidectomy; oral anti-androgens alone allowed for non-metastatic disease only between 2006 and 2011); radiotherapy encouraged for N0M0 until November 2011, then mandated; optional for N+M0
・Duration: Trial therapy discontinued after disease progression or intolerable adverse events
・Design: Open-label; multiarm multistage platform Primary: overall survival (definitive), failure-free survival (intermediate). Secondary: prostate-cancer-specific survival, time to first skeletal-related event, osteonecrosis of the jaw, time to treatment after progression, adverse events, cost-effectiveness, patient-reported outcomes, time to first fracture-related hospitalisation Adding docetaxel, with or without zoledronic acid, to SOC improved OS, at the cost of more toxicity; zoledronic acid alone did not improve OS
・OS: Ⓐ 71 vs Ⓑ NR vs Ⓒ 81 vs Ⓓ 76 mo; Ⓑ vs Ⓐ HR 0.94 (95% CI 0.79–1.11); Ⓒ vs Ⓐ HR 0.78 (0.66–0.93); Ⓓ vs Ⓐ HR 0.82 (0.69–0.97)
・FFS: Ⓐ 20 vs Ⓑ 22 vs Ⓒ 37 vs Ⓓ 36 mo; Ⓑ vs Ⓐ HR 0.92 (0.81–1.04); Ⓒ vs Ⓐ HR 0.61 (0.53–0.70); Ⓓ vs Ⓐ HR 0.62 (0.54–0.70); non-proportional hazards for docetaxel comparisons
・SRE: Time to first SRE Ⓑ vs Ⓐ HR 0.89 (0.73–1.07); Ⓒ vs Ⓐ 0.60 (0.48–0.74); Ⓓ vs Ⓐ 0.55 (0.44–0.69)
・ZA added to docetaxel: Ⓓ vs Ⓒ OS HR 1.06 (95% CI 0.86–1.30)
・FRH (post hoc, linked data): M1 ZA (Ⓑ+Ⓓ vs Ⓐ+Ⓒ) SDHR 0.73 (95% CI 0.55–0.97); M0 inconclusive, SDHR 0.88 (0.59–1.32); docetaxel no clear effect
・FRH 10-yr incidence: M1 Ⓐ 32% vs Ⓑ 24% vs Ⓒ 34% vs Ⓓ 26%; M0 Ⓐ 26% vs Ⓑ 23% vs Ⓒ 24% vs Ⓓ 21%
・FRH sensitivity: M1 ZA effect not significant for non-pathological fractures only (SDHR 0.82, 95% CI 0.61–1.11)
・Subgroups: No heterogeneity across prespecified subsets; M1 OS Ⓒ vs Ⓐ HR 0.76 (0.62–0.92)
・Toxicity: G3–5 AEs Ⓐ 32% vs Ⓑ 32% vs Ⓒ 52% vs Ⓓ 52%; febrile neutropenia Ⓒ 15% vs Ⓓ 14%; ONJ Ⓑ 2% vs Ⓓ 4%; treatment-related deaths Ⓒ one vs Ⓓ seven; ONJ by hospital coding ZA 2.8% vs no ZA <0.8%
・Limitations: Open-label; M0 OS immature (<100 deaths per comparison); metastatic subset analysis added to the plan after CHAARTED/GETUG-15 reported

records.title: GETUG-AFU 15
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - docetaxel intensification · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2013
records.body:
Histologically confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma with radiologically proven metastatic disease; non-castrate (hormone-sensitive), first-line; Karnofsky score ≥70%; ADT started no more than 2 months before enrolment; prior neoadjuvant/adjuvant chemotherapy or ADT allowed if stopped ≥12 months before inclusion; excluded previous chemotherapy for metastatic disease, surgical castration before metastases, brain metastases, grade ≥2 peripheral neuropathy Ⓐ Continuous ADT (orchiectomy or LHRH agonist, alone or with a non-steroidal antiandrogen) + docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV day 1 of each 21-day cycle for up to 9 cycles (stopped early for progression, unacceptable toxicity or patient request)
Ⓑ Continuous ADT alone
・Duration: ADT continued until unacceptable toxicity or patient request Primary: overall survival. Secondary: clinical progression-free survival, biochemical progression-free survival, time to subsequent treatment, PSA response, quality of life, safety Adding docetaxel to ADT did not improve overall survival in metastatic non-castrate prostate cancer
・OS: Ⓐ 58.9 vs Ⓑ 54.2 mo; HR 1.01 (95% CI 0.75–1.36)
・bPFS: Ⓐ 22.9 vs Ⓑ 12.9 mo; HR 0.72
・cPFS: Ⓐ 23.5 vs Ⓑ 15.4 mo; HR 0.75; docetaxel's effect on progression decreased over time
・QoL: Lower with Ⓐ docetaxel at months 3 and 6; similar at 12 months
・Toxicity: Ⓐ grade 3–4 neutropenia 32%, febrile neutropenia 7%; 21% stopped for toxicity; 4 treatment-related deaths before G-CSF recommended, none after
・Limitations: Trial likely underpowered (OS with Ⓑ ADT alone underestimated); 62% of Ⓑ patients later received docetaxel

records.title: LATITUDE
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body:
Prostate cancer without neuroendocrine or small-cell features; newly diagnosed (≤3 months before randomization) high-risk metastatic castration-sensitive disease; at least two of Gleason score ≥8, ≥3 bone lesions, measurable visceral metastasis; ECOG 0 to 2; excluded prior chemotherapy, radiotherapy or surgery for metastatic disease, except 3 months or less of ADT and one course of palliative radiation or surgery Ⓐ ADT plus abiraterone acetate 1000 mg orally once daily (four 250-mg tablets) plus prednisone 5 mg orally daily
Ⓑ ADT plus dual placebos (double-blind)
・ADT: Testosterone maintained <50 ng/dL unless surgically castrated
・Duration: Until disease progression, withdrawal of consent, unacceptable toxicity or death Primary: overall survival, radiographic progression-free survival. Secondary: time to next symptomatic skeletal event, time to PSA progression, time to next therapy for prostate cancer, time to initiation of chemotherapy, time to pain progression, PSA response, safety, secondary progression-free survival Abiraterone plus prednisone added to ADT (Ⓐ) improved OS and rPFS vs ADT alone (Ⓑ) in newly diagnosed metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer
・OS (final analysis, 51.8 mo follow-up): Ⓐ 53.3 vs Ⓑ 36.5 mo; HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.56–0.78)
・rPFS: Ⓐ 33.0 vs Ⓑ 14.8 mo; HR 0.47 (95% CI 0.39–0.55); not re-analysed at final analysis
・Secondary endpoints: All favoured Ⓐ; time to PSA progression HR 0.31; time to chemotherapy HR 0.51; exploratory secondary PFS HR 0.58
・Subgroups: Low-volume disease (post-hoc): OS benefit not significant; HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.47–1.10)
・Toxicity: G3–4 AEs Ⓐ 68% vs Ⓑ 50%; G3 hypertension Ⓐ 21% vs Ⓑ 10%; G3 hypokalaemia Ⓐ 11% vs Ⓑ 1%; AEs leading to death Ⓐ 6% vs Ⓑ 4%; treatment-related deaths three per arm
・Limitations: Unblinding after first interim analysis; crossover of 72 placebo patients to abiraterone before final OS analysis

records.title: STAMPEDE (abiraterone)
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body:
Prostate cancer starting long-term ADT for the first time; newly diagnosed metastatic, node-positive or high-risk locally advanced (at least two of T3/T4, Gleason 8–10, PSA ≥40 ng/ml), or relapsing after radical surgery/radiotherapy with high-risk features (PSA >4 ng/ml doubling <6 months, PSA >20 ng/ml, nodal/metastatic relapse, or <12 months total ADT with >12 months off treatment); ADT started ≤12 weeks before randomization; excluded clinically significant cardiovascular disease Ⓐ ADT alone
Ⓑ ADT + abiraterone acetate 1000 mg + prednisolone 5 mg once daily
・ADT duration: ≥2 years
・Abiraterone duration: Until PSA, radiologic or clinical progression (metastatic, or nonmetastatic without planned radiotherapy) or for 2 years or until any progression, whichever first (nonmetastatic with planned radiotherapy)
・Design: Radiotherapy at 6–9 months mandatory for node-negative, optional for node-positive nonmetastatic disease Primary: overall survival, failure-free survival (intermediate primary). Secondary: adverse events, symptomatic skeletal events, progression-free survival, prostate cancer-specific survival, quality of life Abiraterone plus prednisolone added to ADT improved overall and failure-free survival vs ADT alone, with fewer symptomatic skeletal events
・OS: 3-yr Ⓐ 76% vs Ⓑ 83%; HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.52–0.76)
・FFS: 3-yr Ⓐ 45% vs Ⓑ 75%; HR 0.29 (95% CI 0.25–0.34)
・PFS: 3-yr Ⓐ 62% vs Ⓑ 80%; HR 0.40
・SSE: HR 0.46
・Subgroups: OS benefit HR 0.61 in metastatic vs HR 0.75 in nonmetastatic disease
・Toxicity: Grade 3–5 AEs Ⓐ 33% vs Ⓑ 47%; grade 5 Ⓐ 3 vs Ⓑ 9; hypertension Ⓐ 1% vs Ⓑ 5%; ALT increase Ⓐ <1% vs Ⓑ 6%
・Limitations: Open-label; nonmetastatic OS comparison immature (78 deaths)

records.title: TITAN
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body:
Metastatic castration-sensitive prostate adenocarcinoma with ≥1 bone-scan lesion, with or without visceral or nodal disease; newly diagnosed or relapsed after localized disease, not receiving ADT at progression; prior docetaxel ≤6 cycles without progression, ADT ≤6 mo for mCSPC or ≤3 yr for localized disease, and localized therapy ≥1 yr before randomization allowed; excluded severe angina, MI, CHF, thromboembolic events, seizure history/predisposition, recent ventricular arrhythmias Ⓐ Apalutamide 240 mg orally once daily + continuous ADT
Ⓑ matched placebo orally once daily + continuous ADT
・Duration: Until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
・Design: Double-blind Primary: radiographic progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: time to cytotoxic chemotherapy, time to pain progression, time to chronic opioid use, time to skeletal-related event, time to PSA progression, second progression-free survival, time to symptomatic local progression, undetectable PSA rate, time to castration resistance, FACT-P quality of life, safety Apalutamide plus ADT improved rPFS and final OS vs placebo plus ADT, despite substantial crossover
・rPFS (final at interim; 22.7 mo follow-up): Ⓐ 24-mo 68.2% vs Ⓑ 47.5%; HR 0.48 (95% CI 0.39–0.60)
・OS (final; 44.0 mo follow-up; 39.5% crossover; no formal inference): Ⓐ median NR vs Ⓑ 52.2 mo; HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.53–0.79); crossover-adjusted HR 0.52
・Time to pain progression: HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.70–1.08); not significant at first interim, so further secondary endpoints not formally tested
・Nominal HRs (final): Cytotoxic chemotherapy 0.47; PFS2 0.62; castration resistance (ad hoc) 0.34
・QoL: FACT-P maintained, no substantial between-group difference
・Toxicity (interim): Grade 3–4 AEs Ⓐ 42.2% vs Ⓑ 40.8%; AEs leading to death Ⓐ 1.9% vs Ⓑ 3.0%; rash Ⓐ 27.1% vs Ⓑ 8.5% (grade ≥3 6.3%); ischemic heart disease Ⓐ 4.4% vs Ⓑ 1.5%, fatal in two patients per group; no treatment-related deaths at final analysis
・Limitations: Crossover to apalutamide permitted (39.5%), so final OS comparison carries no formal inference; secondary endpoints not formally tested after time to pain progression missed significance at first interim

records.title: ENZAMET
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body:
Metastatic, hormone-sensitive prostatic adenocarcinoma with metastases on CT and/or technetium-99 bone scan; first-line testosterone suppression initiated up to 12 weeks before randomization, with or without early docetaxel (up to two cycles allowed before randomization); ECOG ≤2; prior adjuvant testosterone suppression for up to 24 months allowed if completed at least 12 months earlier; history of seizure or seizure-predisposing condition excluded Ⓐ Enzalutamide 160 mg orally daily
Ⓑ Standard nonsteroidal antiandrogen (bicalutamide, nilutamide or flutamide)
・Testosterone suppression: Continuous
・Duration: Until clinical progression or prohibitive toxicity
・Chemotherapy: Optional early docetaxel 75 mg per square meter every 3 weeks for a maximum of six cycles without prednisone/prednisolone (patient/physician choice; stratified; permitted after the first 88 patients)
・Design: Open-label Primary: overall survival. Secondary: PSA progression-free survival, clinical progression-free survival, adverse events, health-related quality of life, resource use, incremental cost-effectiveness Enzalutamide plus testosterone suppression improved OS, PSA PFS and clinical PFS versus a standard nonsteroidal antiandrogen in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer
・OS (planned primary analysis; 68-mo median follow-up): Ⓐ 208 vs Ⓑ 268 deaths; HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.58-0.84); 5-yr OS Ⓐ 67% vs Ⓑ 57%
・PSA PFS: 5-yr Ⓐ 54% vs Ⓑ 25%; HR 0.44
・Clinical PFS: 5-yr Ⓐ 56% vs Ⓑ 28%; HR 0.45
・Subgroups: No interaction across prespecified subgroups; planned-docetaxel OS HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.63-1.06); among docetaxel recipients, HR 0.73 synchronous vs 1.10 metachronous (exploratory, not randomised)
・Toxicity: Grade 3-4 fatigue Ⓐ 6% vs Ⓑ 1%; grade 3-4 hypertension Ⓐ 10% vs Ⓑ 6%; seizures (6 grade 1-2, 1 grade 3) in Ⓐ vs none in Ⓑ; serious grade 3-4 AEs Ⓐ 47% vs Ⓑ 33%; grade 5 AEs Ⓐ 13 vs Ⓑ 10, none treatment-related
・Limitations: Open-label; median OS not reached in either arm; docetaxel subgroup analyses exploratory and not randomised

records.title: ARCHES
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body:
Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate adenocarcinoma; de novo or recurrent after prior local therapy, metastases on bone scan or CT/MRI; prior ADT and up to six cycles of prior docetaxel permitted; excluded neuroendocrine, signet-cell or small-cell features and disease progression on ADT and/or docetaxel before randomization Ⓐ Enzalutamide 160 mg/day + ADT
Ⓑ Placebo + ADT
・Duration: Until unacceptable toxicity, radiographic progression confirmed by independent central review, or start of an investigational agent or new prostate cancer therapy
・Design: Double-blind; after the primary analysis, unblinded with progression-free placebo patients allowed to cross over to open-label enzalutamide + ADT Primary: radiographic progression-free survival. Secondary: time to PSA progression, time to initiation of new antineoplastic therapy, PSA undetectable rate, objective response rate, time to deterioration in urinary symptoms, overall survival, time to first symptomatic skeletal event, time to castration resistance, patient-reported outcomes, time to deterioration of quality of life, time to pain progression, quality of life over time, safety Enzalutamide + ADT reduced the risk of radiographic progression or death and significantly prolonged overall survival vs placebo + ADT in mHSPC
・rPFS (primary analysis; mFU 14.4 mo): HR 0.39 (95% CI 0.30-0.50)
・rPFS (final, investigator-assessed): HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.52-0.76)
・OS (final prespecified; mFU 44.6 mo): HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.53-0.81); significant despite 31.3% of Ⓑ crossing over to open-label Ⓐ
・Time to new antineoplastic therapy: HR 0.38
・PSA progression (primary analysis): HR 0.19
・Undetectable PSA (primary analysis): Ⓐ 68.1% vs Ⓑ 17.6%
・ORR (primary analysis): Ⓐ 83.1% vs Ⓑ 63.7%
・QoL/urinary symptoms (primary analysis): No significant difference in time to deterioration
・Pain progression (primary analysis; 30% threshold): Not delayed
・Subgroups: OS benefit generally consistent except soft-tissue-only disease
・Toxicity: Grade 3-4 TEAEs Ⓐ 39.2% vs Ⓑ 27.9%; TEAEs leading to death Ⓐ 5.2% vs Ⓑ 2.1%, none drug-related with Ⓐ; earlier, two grade 5 cardiovascular AEs of special interest with Ⓐ

records.title: ARANOTE
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body:
Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate adenocarcinoma; ADT started not earlier than 12 weeks before random assignment; metastases centrally confirmed on conventional imaging (nonregional nodes M1a, bone M1b and/or other sites M1c); excluded regional lymph node metastases only (N1, below the aortic bifurcation), baseline superscan, prior androgen receptor pathway inhibitors or chemotherapy, small cell/ductal/neuroendocrine histology, known brain or leptomeningeal metastases Ⓐ Darolutamide 600 mg twice daily + ADT
Ⓑ Placebo + ADT
・ADT: Investigator's choice of LHRH agonist/antagonist or orchiectomy
・Duration: Until radiological progression, unacceptable toxicity, new anticancer therapy, patient/physician decision or interruption >28 consecutive days Primary: radiological progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, time to initiation of subsequent systemic anticancer therapy, time to mCRPC, time to PSA progression, rate of PSA <0.2 ng/mL, time to pain progression, safety Darolutamide plus ADT improved rPFS vs placebo plus ADT in mHSPC
・rPFS: Ⓐ NR vs Ⓑ 25.0 mo; HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.41–0.71; P<.0001)
・24-mo rPFS: Ⓐ 70.3% vs Ⓑ 52.1%
・Time to mCRPC: HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.32–0.51)
・Time to PSA progression: HR 0.31 (95% CI 0.23–0.41)
・Time to pain progression: HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.54–0.96)
・Subgroups: Benefit consistent across high- and low-volume disease
・Toxicity: Ⓐ Grade 3–4 AEs 30.8% vs Ⓑ 30.3%; grade 5 AEs Ⓐ 4.7% vs Ⓑ 5.4%; discontinuation for AEs Ⓐ 6.1% vs Ⓑ 9.0%; fatigue Ⓐ 5.6% vs Ⓑ 8.1%
・Limitations: Interim OS immature, only suggestive of benefit (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.59–1.12); trial not powered for OS; final OS planned at ~180 events

records.title: ARASENS
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - triplet therapy (ADT + docetaxel + ARPI) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body:
Metastatic, hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, histologically or cytologically confirmed; metastases detected on bone scanning, contrast-enhanced CT or MRI; candidates for androgen-deprivation therapy and docetaxel, ECOG 0 or 1; excluded regional lymph-node involvement only (N1, below the aortic bifurcation), androgen-deprivation therapy more than 12 weeks before randomization, or prior second-generation androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors, chemotherapy or immunotherapy Ⓐ Darolutamide 600 mg (two 300-mg tablets) twice daily with food
Ⓑ Matched placebo
・ADT: LHRH agonist/antagonist or orchiectomy, started within 12 weeks before randomization
・Docetaxel: 75 mg per square meter day 1 every 21 days for six cycles, started within 6 weeks after randomization
・Duration: Darolutamide/placebo continued until symptomatic disease progression, change in antineoplastic therapy, unacceptable toxic effects, patient or physician decision, death or nonadherence Primary: overall survival. Secondary: time to castration-resistant prostate cancer, time to pain progression, symptomatic skeletal event–free survival, time to first symptomatic skeletal event, time to initiation of subsequent systemic antineoplastic therapy, time to worsening of disease-related physical symptoms, time to initiation of opioid treatment for 7 or more consecutive days, safety Adding darolutamide to ADT and docetaxel significantly prolonged OS and improved key secondary endpoints
・OS (primary analysis): HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.57–0.80); 4-yr OS Ⓐ 62.7% vs Ⓑ 50.4%; despite subsequent life-prolonging therapy in 75.6% of placebo patients
・Time to CRPC: HR 0.36 (95% CI 0.30–0.42)
・Secondary endpoints: First five hierarchically tested endpoints were significant
・Symptomatic progression: Time to worsening of disease-related physical symptoms not improved; HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.89–1.22)
・Subgroups (post hoc, exploratory): OS benefit in high-volume HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.57–0.82) and high-risk HR 0.71 (95% CI 0.58–0.86); low-volume only suggestive HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.41–1.13)
・Toxicity: Grade 3/4 AEs Ⓐ 66.1% vs Ⓑ 63.5% (neutropenia Ⓐ 33.7% vs Ⓑ 34.2%); grade 3/4 hypertension Ⓐ 6.4% vs Ⓑ 3.2%; AE deaths Ⓐ 4.1% vs Ⓑ 4.0%
・Limitations: 86.1% had de novo metastatic disease, limiting data for recurrent or node-only disease; only ECOG 0–1 enrolled

records.title: PEACE-1
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - triplet therapy (ADT + docetaxel + ARPI) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body:
Histologically or cytologically confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma; de novo metastatic castration-sensitive disease documented by bone scan, CT or MRI; ECOG 0–1 (or 2 due to bone pain), ADT for no more than 3 months before randomisation, at least 6 weeks from ADT initiation to first docetaxel dose, docetaxel mandatory in SOC from the Aug 10, 2017 amendment; excluded pure small-cell carcinoma or previous prostate cancer treated by definitive local treatment Ⓐ SOC (continuous ADT alone or with docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks for six cycles)
Ⓑ SOC + radiotherapy to the prostate (74 Gy in 37 fractions over 7–8 weeks)
Ⓒ SOC + abiraterone 1000 mg orally once daily plus prednisone 5 mg orally twice daily until progression to castration resistance, withdrawal of consent, unacceptable toxicity or death
Ⓓ SOC + radiotherapy + abiraterone
・Design: Open-label Primary: radiographic progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: CRPC-free survival, serious genitourinary event-free survival, prostate-cancer-specific survival, time to next skeletal-related event, PSA response rate, prognostic study of serum PSA measured 6–8 months after initiation of systemic therapy, time to pain progression, time to chemotherapy for CRPC, quality of life, changes in bone mineral density, correlation of biomarkers with outcome, event rate per 100 person-years of treatment, toxicity Adding abiraterone to ADT plus docetaxel in de novo mCSPC improved rPFS and OS
・rPFS (ADT+docetaxel population): 4.46 vs 2.03 yr; HR 0.50 (99.9% CI 0.34–0.71)
・OS (ADT+docetaxel population): Not reached vs 4.43 yr; HR 0.75 (95.1% CI 0.59–0.95)
・rPFS (overall population): HR 0.54 (99.9% CI 0.41–0.71)
・OS (overall population): HR 0.82 (95.1% CI 0.69–0.98)
・Subgroups: High-volume OS HR 0.72 (95.1% CI 0.55–0.95); low-volume OS immature, HR 0.83 (95.1% CI 0.50–1.39)
・RT: Did not improve low-volume OS, HR 0.98 (95.1% CI 0.74–1.28); improved rPFS with abiraterone, HR 0.65 (99.9% CI 0.36–1.19), not without, HR 1.08; GU events 55 vs 102; grade ≥3 AEs 58.8% vs 56.1%
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 AEs 63% vs 52%; hypertension 22% vs 13%; hepatotoxicity 6% vs 1%; fatal AEs 2% vs 1%; neutropenia and febrile neutropenia not increased
・Limitations: Open-label; triplet not compared with ADT plus abiraterone

records.title: AMPLITUDE
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - PARP inhibitor + ARPI (HRR/BRCA-altered) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer, metastases on conventional imaging; at least one deleterious HRR alteration (BRCA1, BRCA2, BRIP1, PALB2, RAD51B, RAD54L, CDK12, CHEK2 or FANCA) on central tissue, plasma or germline testing or approved local test; ADT started at least 14 days and no longer than 6 months before randomization; prior docetaxel (up to six cycles, completed within 3 months of randomization) and up to 45 days of abiraterone plus prednisone allowed Ⓐ Niraparib 200 mg plus abiraterone acetate 1,000 mg (dual-action tablet) plus prednisone 5 mg orally once daily
Ⓑ Matched placebo plus abiraterone acetate plus prednisone
・Duration: Continuously in 28-day cycles until progression
・ADT: Continued in both arms Primary: radiographic progression-free survival. Secondary: time to symptomatic progression, overall survival, time to subsequent therapy, safety, second progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, time to PSA progression, PSA response rate, quality of life (FACT-P) Niraparib added to abiraterone-prednisone improved rPFS in HRR-altered mCSPC, meeting the primary endpoint in all three hierarchically tested populations
・rPFS: BRCA HR 0.52 (95% CI 0.37–0.72), Ⓐ not reached vs Ⓑ 26.0 mo; HRR effector HR 0.57 (0.42–0.77); ITT HR 0.63 (0.49–0.80), Ⓐ not reached vs Ⓑ 29.5 mo
・TTSP: ITT HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.36–0.69)
・OS: First interim analysis, immature; BRCA HR 0.75 (0.51–1.11), not significant; ITT HR 0.79 (0.59–1.04)
・Subgroups: Post hoc non-BRCA HRR alterations rPFS HR 0.81 (0.56–1.18)
・QoL: Ⓐ FACT-P scores declined cycles 2–4 with niraparib; no difference from cycle 5

records.title: TALAPRO-3
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - PARP inhibitor + ARPI (HRR/BRCA-altered) · Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Metastatic androgen pathway modulation–sensitive (APMS) prostate adenocarcinoma; up to 3 months of prior ADT with or without an approved ARPI allowed; alteration in one or more HRR genes on a 12-gene panel, in blood, tumour or both; ongoing GnRH agonist/antagonist ADT unless bilateral orchiectomy; prior docetaxel excluded after a September 2021 amendment Ⓐ Talazoparib 0.5 mg orally once daily (0.35 mg if moderate renal impairment)
Ⓑ Placebo orally once daily
・Backbone: Enzalutamide 160 mg orally once daily, with ongoing ADT
・Duration: Until investigator-assessed imaging-based progression (continuation allowed if still benefiting), unacceptable toxicity, patient decision or death
・Design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled Primary: imaging-based progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response, duration of response, PSA decrease of at least 50%, time to PSA progression, time to initiation of antineoplastic therapy, safety, patient-reported outcomes Adding talazoparib to enzalutamide significantly improved imaging-based PFS vs placebo plus enzalutamide in HRR-altered metastatic APMS prostate cancer
・3-yr rPFS: Ⓐ 77% vs Ⓑ 56%; HR 0.48 (95% CI 0.36–0.65); median NC vs 45.8 mo
・OS (interim): 3-yr Ⓐ 78% vs Ⓑ 72%; HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.56–1.04); efficacy boundary not crossed
・PSA progression: 3-yr free Ⓐ 78% vs Ⓑ 63%; HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.37–0.71); not multiplicity-adjusted
・Next therapy: 3-yr not started Ⓐ 79% vs Ⓑ 62%; HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.38–0.70); not multiplicity-adjusted
・ORR: Ⓐ 75% vs Ⓑ 67% in measurable disease
・Subgroups: BRCA 3-yr rPFS Ⓐ 77% vs Ⓑ 49%, HR 0.37 (95% CI 0.22–0.61); non-BRCA Ⓐ 76% vs Ⓑ 60%, HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.39–0.82); CIs unadjusted
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 81% vs Ⓑ 44%; serious AEs 42% vs 32%; G≥3 anaemia 51% in Ⓐ; transfusions 40% vs 2%; talazoparib/placebo discontinuation 19% vs 10%; MDS three vs one, AML two vs none; two treatment-related deaths in Ⓐ
・Limitations: OS interim, immature; possible unblinding from talazoparib toxicity; no comparison with docetaxel-based therapy

records.title: CAPItello-281
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - PTEN deficiency · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Prostate adenocarcinoma; de novo metastatic hormone-sensitive disease; PTEN deficiency by central IHC: ≥90% of viable malignant cells with no specific cytoplasmic PTEN staining; prior ADT ± abiraterone for de novo disease allowed up to 93 days before randomization; excluded any other prior prostate cancer therapy Ⓐ Capivasertib 400 mg twice daily (4 days on, 3 days off) + abiraterone 1000 mg once daily + prednisone/prednisolone + ADT

Secondary: Overall survival, Time to first subsequent therapy, Symptomatic skeletal event-free survival, Time to pain progression, Time to PSA progression, Time to castration resistance, Safety Adding capivasertib to abiraterone and ADT improved rPFS in PTEN-deficient mHSPC
・rPFS: Ⓐ 33.2 vs Ⓑ 25.7 mo; HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.66-0.98), P = 0.034

・TTCR: HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.63-0.94); nominal P value only

records.title: PSMAddition
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - radioligand therapy (PSMA) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Metastatic androgen pathway modulator-naive/sensitive (hormone-sensitive) prostate adenocarcinoma; treatment-naive, ≤45 days' prior ADT and/or ARPI for metastatic disease, or neoadjuvant/adjuvant ADT discontinued >12 months without progression; at least one distant metastasis PSMA-positive (uptake greater than liver) on centrally read 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET, and at least one PSMA-positive liver lesion if liver metastases; excluded rapidly progressing tumours needing urgent taxane chemotherapy Ⓐ 177Lu-PSMA-617 7·4 GBq (200 mCi) ±10% IV once every 6 weeks for up to six cycles plus ADT plus investigator-chosen ARPI (abiraterone, enzalutamide, apalutamide, darolutamide or rezvilutamide), ADT plus ARPI continued after the six cycles

records.title: STAMPEDE
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - radiotherapy to the primary tumour · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body:
Newly diagnosed metastatic prostate cancer with no previous radical treatment; metastases confirmed on bone scintigraphy and soft-tissue imaging done within 12 weeks of starting androgen deprivation therapy; intended for long-term androgen deprivation therapy, started no earlier than 12 weeks before randomisation; no age restrictions; excluded contraindications to radiotherapy or clinically significant cardiovascular history Ⓐ Standard of care alone
Ⓑ Standard of care plus external-beam radiotherapy to the prostate, 36 Gy in six consecutive weekly fractions of 6 Gy or 55 Gy in 20 daily fractions of 2·75 Gy over 4 weeks (schedule nominated before randomisation), starting as soon as practicable after randomisation and within 3–4 weeks after the last docetaxel dose
・SOC: Lifelong androgen deprivation therapy (GnRH agonist/antagonist or orchidectomy), with up-front docetaxel 75 mg/m² for six 3-weekly cycles ± prednisolone 10 mg daily permitted from Dec 17, 2015 Primary: overall survival. Secondary: failure-free survival, progression-free survival, metastatic progression-free survival, prostate cancer-specific survival, symptomatic local event-free survival, safety, time to first life-prolonging therapy Adding prostate radiotherapy to standard of care did not improve overall survival in unselected men with newly diagnosed metastatic prostate cancer
・OS: Ⓐ 62% vs Ⓑ 65% (3-yr); HR 0·92 (95% CI 0·80–1·06; p=0·266); median follow-up 37 mo
・FFS: Improved; HR 0·76 (95% CI 0·68–0·84)
・Subgroups: Low metastatic burden (40%) OS improved, Ⓐ 73% vs Ⓑ 81% (3-yr); HR 0·68 (95% CI 0·52–0·90; interaction p=0·0098); high burden no effect, HR 1·07 (95% CI 0·90–1·28)
・Toxicity: RTOG grade 3–4 48 (5%) during radiotherapy and 37 (4%) after; CTCAE grade ≥3 AEs Ⓐ 38% vs Ⓑ 39%; no treatment-related deaths
・Limitations: Low-burden subgroup hypothesis prespecified after trial start (May 2018); metastatic burden classified retrospectively from scans

records.title: EMBARK
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M0 CSPC- high-risk biochemical recurrence · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body:
Prostate adenocarcinoma without neuroendocrine, signet-cell or small-cell features; biochemical recurrence after local therapy, nonmetastatic on conventional imaging; high risk: PSA doubling time ≤9 months and PSA ≥1 ng/ml after prostatectomy or ≥2 ng/ml above nadir after radiotherapy (RT), testosterone ≥150 ng/dl; excluded: salvage-RT candidates, prior chemotherapy, seizure history, prior hormonal therapy except ≤36-month neoadjuvant/adjuvant or ≤6-month course ≥9 months before randomization Ⓐ Enzalutamide 160 mg orally once daily + leuprolide 22.5 mg IM or SC every 12 weeks (double-blind)
Ⓑ Placebo + leuprolide 22.5 mg IM or SC every 12 weeks (double-blind)
Ⓒ Enzalutamide 160 mg orally once daily monotherapy (open-label)
・Suspension: Treatment suspended at week 37 if PSA <0.2 ng/ml, restarted at PSA ≥5.0 ng/ml (no prior prostatectomy) or ≥2.0 ng/ml (prior prostatectomy)
・Duration: Until centrally confirmed imaging-based progression, unacceptable adverse event, seizure or death Primary: metastasis-free survival (enzalutamide plus leuprolide vs leuprolide alone). Secondary: metastasis-free survival (enzalutamide monotherapy vs leuprolide alone), time to PSA progression, time to new antineoplastic therapy, overall survival, safety, time to distant metastasis, time to resumption of hormonal therapy, time to castration resistance, time to symptomatic progression, time to first symptomatic skeletal event, time to first deterioration in FACT-P total score, progression-free survival with first subsequent therapy Enzalutamide plus leuprolide and enzalutamide monotherapy both improved metastasis-free survival versus leuprolide alone; only the combination later improved overall survival

・OS (8-yr, final analysis, median follow-up 93.8–94.2 mo): Ⓐ 78.9% vs Ⓑ 69.5% vs Ⓒ 73.1%; HR Ⓐ vs Ⓑ 0.60 (95% CI 0.44–0.80; P<0.001); HR Ⓒ vs Ⓑ 0.83 (95% CI 0.63–1.10; P=0.19), not superior
・QoL: No apparent detrimental effect
・Toxicity (final cut): G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 52.4% vs Ⓑ 49.4% vs Ⓒ 57.3%; AE-related discontinuation Ⓐ 27.5% vs Ⓑ 12.7% vs Ⓒ 20.6%; gynecomastia Ⓒ 46.0%; fractures Ⓐ 22.4% vs Ⓑ 15.0% vs Ⓒ 14.1%; fatal AEs Ⓐ 2.8% vs Ⓑ 1.4% vs Ⓒ 3.4%, none treatment-related; seizures (primary analysis) Ⓐ 1.1%, Ⓒ 0.8%
・Limitations: Ⓒ arm open-label vs double-blind Ⓐ/Ⓑ; seizure incidence reported only at primary analysis, not updated at final cut

records.title: SPARTAN
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M0 CRPC · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body:
Prostate adenocarcinoma, castration-resistant during continuous ADT (orchiectomy or GnRH agonist/antagonist); nonmetastatic, at high risk of metastasis: PSA doubling time ≤10 months; N0 or N1 pelvic nodes <2 cm in short axis below the aortic bifurcation allowed; excluded: distant metastasis on screening bone scan and CT of pelvis, abdomen, chest and head Ⓐ Apalutamide 240 mg per day orally, continuous daily dosing + continued ADT

records.title: COU-AA-302

records.body:

Secondary: time to opiate use for cancer-related pain, time to initiation of cytotoxic chemotherapy, time to decline in ECOG performance status, time to PSA progression, PSA response rate, objective response rate, health-related quality of life, time to increase in pain, time to functional-status decline, safety Abiraterone–prednisone improved radiographic PFS and, at the final analysis, overall survival vs prednisone alone

・Toxicity: Final analysis G3–4 AEs Ⓐ 54% vs Ⓑ 44%; G3–4 cardiac Ⓐ 8% vs Ⓑ 4%; G3–4 ALT increase Ⓐ 6% vs Ⓑ <1%; AEs leading to death Ⓐ 4% vs Ⓑ 3%, none treatment-related

Secondary: time until initiation of cytotoxic chemotherapy, time until first skeletal-related event, best overall soft-tissue response, time until PSA progression, PSA decline of 50% or more from baseline, quality of life (FACT-P), PSA decline of 90% or more from baseline, safety Enzalutamide decreased the risk of radiographic progression and death and delayed chemotherapy initiation versus placebo in chemotherapy-naive metastatic prostate cancer

records.title: PROfound
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CRPC - PARP inhibitors (HRR / BRCA alterations) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body:
Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer; progression during enzalutamide or abiraterone given for nmCRPC, mCRPC or mHSPC, previous taxane chemotherapy allowed; deleterious or suspected deleterious tumour alteration in at least 1 of 15 prespecified HRR genes by central tissue testing, irrespective of zygosity; cohort A: BRCA1, BRCA2 or ATM; cohort B: any of 12 other genes Ⓐ Olaparib tablets 300 mg twice daily
Ⓑ Physician's choice of enzalutamide 160 mg once daily or abiraterone 1000 mg once daily plus prednisone 5 mg twice daily
・Duration: Until imaging-based progression by blinded independent central review or unacceptable toxicity Primary: imaging-based progression-free survival in cohort A. Secondary: imaging-based progression-free survival in the overall population, confirmed objective response rate, time to pain progression, overall survival, PSA50 response, circulating-tumor-cell conversion rate, time to second progression or death, safety In HRR-altered mCRPC progressing on enzalutamide/abiraterone, olaparib was associated with longer imaging-based PFS and better response and patient-reported endpoints than control
・rPFS (cohort A): Ⓐ 7.4 vs Ⓑ 3.6 mo; HR 0.34 (95% CI 0.25-0.47)
・rPFS (overall population): Ⓐ 5.8 vs Ⓑ 3.5 mo; HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.38-0.63)
・ORR (cohort A): Ⓐ 33% vs Ⓑ 2% among evaluable patients
・Time to pain progression (cohort A): HR 0.44 (95% CI 0.22-0.91)
・OS (cohort A, final, 60% maturity): Ⓐ 19.1 vs Ⓑ 14.7 mo; HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.50-0.97); despite 67% crossover
・OS (cohort B): HR 0.96 (95% CI 0.63-1.49); not alpha-controlled
・OS (overall population): HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.61-1.03); not alpha-controlled
・Subgroups: Exploratory gene-level analyses suggested most benefit with BRCA1 or BRCA2 alterations
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 AEs Ⓐ 52% vs Ⓑ 40%; grade ≥3 anaemia Ⓐ 23% vs Ⓑ 5%; AE discontinuation Ⓐ 20% vs Ⓑ 8%; pulmonary embolism Ⓐ 4% vs Ⓑ 1% at primary analysis, none fatal; one fatal AML after olaparib; one treatment-related death per group
・Limitations: OS in cohort B and overall population not alpha-controlled; cohort A OS confounded by 67% crossover; gene-level subgroup findings exploratory

records.title: TALAPRO-2

・OS (final analysis, median follow-up 52.5 mo): Ⓐ 45.8 vs Ⓑ 37.0 mo; HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.66–0.96); significant (p=0.016 vs boundary 0.022)

records.body: Resected high-risk locoregional clear-cell or non-clear-cell RCC Adjuvant sunitinib vs sorafenib vs placebo (1 year) Disease-free survival Neither sunitinib nor sorafenib improved median DFS vs placebo (5.8 and 6.1 vs 6.6 years; HR 1.02 and 0.97) and both added substantial toxicity; a definitively negative trial that argued against adjuvant VEGFR-TKI therapy.

records.title: S-TRAC
records.subtitle: RCC · Adjuvant therapy — resected localized / locoregional RCC · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body: Resected high-risk locoregional clear-cell RCC (UISS high risk) Adjuvant sunitinib vs placebo (1 year) Disease-free survival Sunitinib prolonged median DFS (6.8 vs 5.6 years, HR 0.76); the first adjuvant trial positive for DFS and the basis for FDA approval, though no OS benefit and notable toxicity limited uptake.

records.title: KEYNOTE-564
records.subtitle: RCC · Adjuvant therapy — resected localized / locoregional RCC · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body: Adults ≥18 with intermediate-high/high-risk or M1 NED clear-cell RCC after nephrectomy, or nephrectomy plus metastasectomy; surgery ≤12 weeks before randomization; no prior systemic therapy for RCC Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W for up to 17 cycles (~1 year) vs placebo Primary: disease-free survival per investigator assessment. Secondary: overall survival, safety; post-hoc exploratory: distant metastasis-free survival, time to recurrence Adjuvant pembrolizumab sustained DFS and OS benefit versus placebo at a median 69.5 months from randomization (fourth interim analysis, cutoff September 25, 2024). DFS HR 0.71 (95% CI 0.59–0.86); median DFS NR vs 68.3 months; 5-year DFS 60.9% vs 52.2%. OS HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.48–0.90); median OS NR both arms; 5-year OS 87.7% vs 82.3%. Benefit consistent across key subgroups; no formal statistical testing at this analysis since prior endpoints met significance. Safety unchanged since prior analyses; most common grade ≥3 AEs with pembrolizumab were hypertension (2.9%), increased ALT (2.3%), diarrhea (1.8%)
