records.title: IMmotion010
records.subtitle: RCC · Adjuvant therapy — resected localized / locoregional RCC · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body: Resected high-risk clear-cell / sarcomatoid RCC Adjuvant atezolizumab vs placebo (1 year) Disease-free survival Atezolizumab did not improve median DFS (57.2 vs 49.5 months, HR 0.93); a negative adjuvant PD-L1 trial.

records.title: CheckMate 914 (Part A)
records.subtitle: RCC · Adjuvant therapy — resected localized / locoregional RCC · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body: Localised predominantly clear cell renal cell carcinoma at high risk of relapse; adjuvant after partial or radical nephrectomy, randomised >4 and ≤12 weeks post-nephrectomy; pT2a (grade 3–4) N0M0, pT2b N0M0, pT3 N0M0, pT4 N0M0 or pT any N1M0, negative margins, no residual disease or distant metastases (M0) confirmed by BICR; excluded prior systemic RCC therapy, autoimmune disease, or corticosteroids >10 mg prednisone/day or other immunosuppressants within 14 days Nivolumab 240 mg IV every 2 weeks for 12 doses + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV every 6 weeks for four doses (expected 24 weeks; until completion, week 36, unacceptable toxicity, recurrence or consent withdrawal) vs matching placebo IV at the same frequency (double-blind) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, safety, tolerability Adjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab did not improve disease-free survival vs placebo in localised RCC at high risk of recurrence after nephrectomy; the primary endpoint was not met. At median follow-up 37·0 mo, median DFS was not reached vs 50·7 mo (HR 0·92; 95% CI 0·71–1·19; p=0·53); 24-mo DFS 76% vs 74%. OS was immature (33 vs 28 deaths). An exploratory DFS benefit in a small subgroup of 40 patients with sarcomatoid features (HR 0·29; 95% CI 0·09–0·91) does not establish benefit. All-cause grade 3–5 AEs 38% vs 10%; AEs led to discontinuation in 32% vs 2%; four treatment-related deaths with nivolumab plus ipilimumab (cardiac arrest, diarrhoea/colitis, aortic dissection/ischaemic cerebral infarction/pulmonary embolism, myocarditis); 23% needed ≥40 mg prednisone-equivalent for immune-mediated AEs.

records.title: PROSPER (ECOG-ACRIN EA8143)
records.subtitle: RCC · Adjuvant therapy — resected localized / locoregional RCC · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Renal cell carcinoma of any histology (clear or non-clear cell); planned radical or partial nephrectomy, no prior systemic or local anti-cancer therapy; clinical stage ≥T2 or Tany N+ without metastases on CT or MRI, or (Amendment 4) select oligometastatic disease resectable to no evidence of disease within 12 weeks of nephrectomy (≤3 metastases; no brain, bone, or liver); excluded prior partial nephrectomy of the primary, autoimmune disease, corticosteroids >10 mg daily prednisone equivalent Mandatory baseline core biopsy → nivolumab 480 mg IV, 1 dose 1–4 weeks before radical or partial nephrectomy → up to 9 adjuvant doses of 480 mg IV every 4 weeks started 4–10 weeks post-operatively (original schedule: 240 mg IV every 2 weeks for 2 doses preoperatively, then 240 mg IV every 2 weeks for 9 months) vs nephrectomy followed by surveillance (open-label, no placebo) Primary: recurrence-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, recurrence-free survival in clear cell RCC, safety, tolerability, patient-reported outcomes, quality of life Perioperative nivolumab did not improve RFS and is not supported in this population; the DSMC stopped the trial for futility at a planned interim analysis. RFS nivolumab vs surgery alone (381 vs 399 RCC patients; 125 vs 133 events): HR 0.95 (95% CI 0.74–1.22; one-sided p=0.34); median follow-up 30.4 vs 30.1 mo. A pre-planned sensitivity analysis censoring patients without surgery or not rendered disease-free was not significant (one-sided p=0.08); clear cell RFS HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.68–1.22). OS was inconclusive: HR 1.28 (95% CI 0.84–1.95; p=0.26), 48 vs 40 deaths, medians not reached. Only 197/356 (55%) completed at least 9 cycles; 78/356 (22%) discontinued for AEs. Treatment-related grade 3–5 lipase elevation 17 (5%) of 366 vs 1 (0.3%) of 387; treatment-related deaths 9 (2%) of 366 vs 3 (1%) of 387.

records.title: RAMPART (Arm C)
records.subtitle: RCC · Adjuvant therapy — resected localized / locoregional RCC · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body: Resected intermediate/high-risk clear-cell or non-clear-cell RCC (Leibovich 3-11) Adjuvant durvalumab + tremelimumab vs active monitoring Disease-free survival Durvalumab plus tremelimumab improved 2-yr DFS (84% vs 78%, HR 0.65; high-risk subgroup HR 0.52) but with grade ≥3 toxicity in 40%; a second positive adjuvant immunotherapy signal (durvalumab-monotherapy arm pending).

records.title: LITESPARK-022
records.subtitle: RCC · Adjuvant therapy — resected localized / locoregional RCC · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Histologically confirmed, surgically resected clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma; adjuvant after nephrectomy or nephrectomy and metastasectomy, last surgery ≤12 weeks before randomization; intermediate-to-high risk (T2 with nuclear grade 4 or sarcomatoid features, or T3 any grade; no nodal or distant metastases), high risk (T4 without nodal or distant metastases, or any T with nodal involvement, no distant metastases), or M1 with no evidence of disease after complete resection of soft-tissue metastases ≤2 years after nephrectomy; microscopically positive margins without gross residual disease allowed Pembrolizumab 400 mg IV every 6 weeks (≤9 doses, approximately 1 year) + belzutifan 120 mg orally daily (concurrent with pembrolizumab, or ≤54 weeks if pembrolizumab discontinued) vs pembrolizumab 400 mg IV every 6 weeks (≤9 doses) + placebo daily (double-blind); regimen stopped at recurrence confirmed by central review, unacceptable toxicity, intercurrent illness or pregnancy Primary: Disease-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, safety Adjuvant pembrolizumab–belzutifan significantly improved DFS vs pembrolizumab–placebo after nephrectomy in clear-cell RCC at increased recurrence risk, with more grade ≥3 toxicity. Investigator-assessed DFS HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.59–0.87; P<0.001); 24-month DFS 80.7% vs 73.7% (median time from randomization to cutoff 28.4 mo). Central-review sensitivity analysis HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.64–0.92). OS was immature at the first interim analysis (29% of final-analysis events) and did not differ significantly: HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.51–1.19); 24-month OS 96.2% vs 95.7%. Grade ≥3 AEs 52.1% vs 30.2%; serious AEs 29.5% vs 19.9%; discontinuation of any regimen for AEs 34.3% vs 19.5%. Anemia 84.0% (grade ≥3 12.1%) vs 11.4%; hypoxia 7.0% (grade ≥3 4.6%) vs 0.1%. Treatment-related deaths: 3 (0.3%) in each group.
records.keywords: Choueiri et al. N Engl J Med 2026;395:32-43  42384869

records.title: Motzer et al.
records.subtitle: RCC · First-line metastatic — VEGF-targeted therapy (historical standards) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2007
records.body: Metastatic renal-cell carcinoma with a clear-cell histologic component; previously untreated (first-line), no prior systemic therapy for renal-cell carcinoma; measurable disease, ECOG performance status 0 or 1; excluded brain metastases, uncontrolled hypertension, or clinically significant cardiovascular events or disease during the preceding 12 months Sunitinib 50 mg orally once daily for 4 weeks followed by 2 weeks without treatment (6-week cycles) vs interferon alfa-2a subcutaneously three times weekly on nonconsecutive days at 3 MU per dose in week 1, 6 MU in week 2 and 9 MU thereafter; both continued until disease progression, unacceptable adverse events or withdrawal of consent Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, overall survival, patient-reported outcomes, safety Sunitinib prolonged progression-free survival and increased response rates vs interferon alfa in previously untreated metastatic renal-cell carcinoma, meeting the primary endpoint at the planned interim analysis (second of three). Median PFS by independent central review 11 vs 5 months (HR 0.42; 95% CI, 0.32 to 0.54; P<0.001); ORR by central review 31% vs 6% (P<0.001). OS was immature: median not reached in either group; HR for death 0.65 (95% CI, 0.45 to 0.94) did not meet the prespecified interim significance level, and interferon patients with progression could later cross over. Patient-reported quality of life (FACT-G, FKSI) was better with sunitinib (P<0.001). Sunitinib caused more grade 3 hypertension (8% vs 1%), diarrhea (5% vs none) and hand-foot syndrome (5% vs none) and grade 3/4 neutropenia (12% vs 7%); treatment-related grade 3/4 fatigue was higher with interferon alfa (12% vs 7%).
records.keywords: Motzer et al. N Engl J Med 2007;356:115-124  17215529

records.title: AVOREN
records.subtitle: RCC · First-line metastatic — VEGF-targeted therapy (historical standards) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2007
records.body: Untreated metastatic clear-cell RCC Bevacizumab + interferon alfa-2a vs placebo + interferon Overall survival (PFS co-reported) Adding bevacizumab to interferon improved median PFS (10.2 vs 5.4 months, HR 0.63); validated VEGF-ligand blockade, though the OS gain was not statistically significant.

records.title: COMPARZ
records.subtitle: RCC · First-line metastatic — VEGF-targeted therapy (historical standards) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2013
records.body: Adults (≥18) with advanced or metastatic renal-cell carcinoma with a clear-cell histologic component and no prior systemic treatment, first-line; KPS ≥70, measurable RECIST disease; excluded brain metastases, poorly controlled hypertension, and cardiac/vascular conditions within 6 months Pazopanib 800 mg orally once daily, continuous vs sunitinib 50 mg orally once daily for 4 weeks followed by 2 weeks off, in 6-week cycles; both treated until progression, unacceptable toxic effects, or consent withdrawal; dose reductions for adverse events Primary: Progression free survival by independent review, powered for non-inferiority. Secondary: Overall survival, safety, QoL Pazopanib was noninferior to sunitinib for independently reviewed PFS (HR 1.05; 95% CI 0.90–1.22, upper bound <1.25 margin); median PFS 8.4 mo pazopanib (557) vs 9.5 mo sunitinib (553). OS was similar (HR 0.91; 95% CI 0.76–1.08; medians 28.4 vs 29.3 mo; 502 deaths). ORR was higher with pazopanib (31% vs 25%, P=0.03). HRQoL during first 6 months favored pazopanib in 11 of 14 domains. Sunitinib caused more fatigue (63% vs 55%), hand-foot syndrome (50% vs 29%) and thrombocytopenia (78% vs 41%); pazopanib more ALT elevation (60% vs 43%), with more discontinuations for liver-test abnormalities (6% vs 1%). Fatal AEs: 13 pazopanib vs 19 sunitinib (drug-related 3 vs 8). Noninferiority does not establish superiority or equivalence; day-28 HRQoL timing could bias toward pazopanib.
records.keywords: Motzer et al. N Engl J Med 2013;369:722-31.  23964934

records.title: CheckMate 214
records.subtitle: RCC · First-line metastatic — immunotherapy-based combinations · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body: Advanced renal-cell carcinoma with a clear-cell component; previously untreated; all IMDC risk groups enrolled (favorable score 0, intermediate 1 or 2, poor 3 to 6), with coprimary analyses in intermediate/poor risk; measurable disease per RECIST 1.1, Karnofsky performance-status score ≥70; excluded CNS metastases, autoimmune disease, glucocorticoid or immunosuppressant use Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks for 4 doses (induction) → nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks, 240 mg every 2 weeks or 480 mg every 4 weeks (maintenance) vs sunitinib 50 mg orally once daily for 4 weeks of each 6-week cycle; both arms could continue beyond initial RECIST progression with clinical benefit, stopping at further progression (additional ≥10% increase in tumor burden); a protocol amendment allowed maintenance nivolumab to stop after 2 years even without progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: objective response rate, progression-free survival, overall survival in IMDC intermediate/poor-risk patients. Secondary: objective response rate, progression-free survival, overall survival in all risk groups, adverse events, complete response rate, duration of response, outcomes in favorable-risk patients, outcomes by PD-L1 expression, quality of life (FKSI-19) Nivolumab plus ipilimumab significantly improved OS and ORR vs sunitinib in previously untreated intermediate/poor-risk advanced RCC; two of three coprimary endpoints were met, and PFS was not (primary analysis, median follow-up 25.2 mo: PFS HR 0.82; P=0.03, not significant at the 0.009 threshold). Benefit was maintained at final descriptive analysis (median follow-up 9.3 yr): intermediate/poor-risk OS HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.59–0.81), median 46.7 vs 26.0 mo; ORR 42.4% vs 27.5%; CR 11.8% vs 2.6% (exploratory comparison); PFS HR 0.73 (0.61–0.87). ITT OS HR 0.71 (0.62–0.82); PFS HR 0.88 (0.76–1.04). In exploratory favorable-risk analyses, ORR (29.6% vs 51.6%) and PFS (HR 1.78) favored sunitinib; OS HR 0.80 (0.59–1.09). At 9.3 yr, treatment-related grade 3/4 AEs 48.6% vs 64.1%; treatment-related AE discontinuation 23.8% vs 13.3%; deaths due to study drug toxicity eight vs five; at the primary analysis, 35% of combination patients with immune-mediated AEs received high-dose glucocorticoids.
records.keywords: Motzer et al. N Engl J Med 2018;378:1277-1290  29562145 Tannir et al. Ann Oncol 2024;35:1026-1038  39098455 Choueiri et al. Ann Oncol 2026;37:960-973  41786248

records.title: KEYNOTE-426
records.subtitle: RCC · First-line metastatic — immunotherapy-based combinations · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body: Clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma; newly diagnosed or recurrent stage IV (AJCC seventh edition), no previous systemic therapy for advanced disease; Karnofsky score ≥70, ≥1 RECIST 1.1 measurable lesion, available tumour sample for biomarker assessment; excluded symptomatic CNS metastases, active autoimmune disease, poorly controlled hypertension (systolic ≥150 or diastolic ≥90 mm Hg), ischemic cardiovascular event or NYHA class III/IV heart failure within 1 year, systemic immunosuppression Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks (maximum 35 cycles) plus axitinib 5 mg orally twice daily (could be increased to 7 mg, then 10 mg, twice daily if safety criteria met) vs sunitinib 50 mg orally once daily for the first 4 weeks of each 6-week cycle; treatment until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or physician or patient decision; patients with a confirmed complete response could discontinue Primary: overall survival, progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, safety, complete response rate Pembrolizumab plus axitinib resulted in significantly longer OS and PFS and a higher ORR than sunitinib in previously untreated advanced renal-cell carcinoma, at the protocol-specified first interim analysis (median follow-up 12.8 mo). 12-month OS 89.9% vs 78.3%; HR for death 0.53 (95% CI, 0.38–0.74); median OS not reached in either group. Median PFS 15.1 vs 11.1 mo; HR 0.69 (95% CI, 0.57–0.84). ORR 59.3% vs 35.7%; CR 5.8% vs 1.9%. Benefit was observed across IMDC risk groups and PD-L1 subgroups, but subgroup analyses are hypothesis-generating, and short follow-up left few deaths in some subgroups, with wide CIs. Grade ≥3 any-cause AEs 75.8% vs 70.6%; grade 3–5 ALT increase 13.3% vs 3.1%; AEs led to discontinuation of either drug in 30.5% with the combination vs discontinuation in 13.9% with sunitinib; treatment-related deaths 0.9% vs 1.6%.

records.title: JAVELIN Renal 101
records.subtitle: RCC · First-line metastatic — immunotherapy-based combinations · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body: Advanced renal-cell carcinoma with a clear-cell component; previously untreated (first-line), all MSKCC and IMDC prognostic risk groups; PD-L1-unselected (positive, negative or unknown), primary endpoints in PD-L1-positive tumours (≥1% of immune cells staining positive, SP263 assay); fresh or archival tumour specimen required; excluded active CNS metastases, autoimmune disease, glucocorticoids or other immunosuppressants within 7 days before randomization Avelumab 10 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks plus axitinib 5 mg orally twice daily (starting dose, continuous) vs sunitinib 50 mg orally once daily for 4 weeks of a 6-week cycle; treatment beyond RECIST progression permitted if investigator-judged benefit Primary: progression-free survival in PD-L1-positive tumours, overall survival in PD-L1-positive tumours. Secondary: progression-free survival in the overall population, overall survival in the overall population, objective response rate, adverse events, pharmacokinetic measures, tumour-tissue biomarkers, patient-reported outcomes, complete response rate, time to response, duration of response First-line avelumab plus axitinib significantly prolonged PFS vs sunitinib in advanced RCC, with a higher ORR. At the first interim analysis, median PFS was 13.8 vs 7.2 mo in PD-L1-positive tumours (n=560; HR 0.61; 95% CI 0.47-0.79) and 13.8 vs 8.4 mo overall (HR 0.69; 95% CI 0.56-0.84). Confirmed ORR was 55.2% vs 25.5% (PD-L1-positive) and 51.4% vs 25.7% (overall). OS was immature (81 of 368 required deaths in PD-L1-positive tumours): HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.53-1.28) in PD-L1-positive tumours and 0.78 (95% CI 0.55-1.08) overall; the trial continued to evaluate OS. Grade ≥3 AEs occurred in 71.2% vs 71.5%. Deaths from treatment toxicity: 3 (0.7%; sudden death, myocarditis, necrotizing pancreatitis) vs 1 (0.2%; intestinal perforation). Immune-related AEs occurred in 38.2% with the combination (grade ≥3 in 9.0%); 11.1% received high-dose glucocorticoids.
records.keywords: Motzer et al. N Engl J Med 2019;380:1103-1115  30779531

records.title: CheckMate 9ER
records.subtitle: RCC · First-line metastatic — immunotherapy-based combinations · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body: Advanced renal-cell carcinoma with a clear-cell component, not amenable to curative surgery or radiation, or metastatic (AJCC stage IV); previously untreated, first-line (one prior adjuvant/neoadjuvant therapy for completely resectable disease permitted); any IMDC risk score, PD-L1 ≥1% or <1%/indeterminate (stratified); excluded active CNS metastases, active autoimmune disease, or glucocorticoids >10 mg/day prednisone equivalent or other immunosuppressants within 14 days Nivolumab 240 mg IV every 2 weeks (maximum 2 years) plus cabozantinib 40 mg orally once daily vs sunitinib 50 mg orally once daily for 4 weeks then 2 weeks off (6-week cycles); all treatment until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response, time to response, duration of response, safety, complete response rate, PFS2, quality of life Nivolumab plus cabozantinib had significant benefits over sunitinib in PFS, OS and response in previously untreated advanced RCC. At 18.1 mo median OS follow-up, median PFS was 16.6 vs 8.3 mo (HR 0.51; 95% CI 0.41–0.64). At the first OS interim analysis, 12-mo OS was 85.7% vs 75.6% (HR 0.60; 98.89% CI 0.40–0.89); median OS was not reached in either group. ORR 55.7% vs 27.1%; CR 8.0% vs 4.6%. Benefits were consistent across prespecified subgroups (no multiplicity adjustment). Exploratory health-related quality of life favoured the combination (nominal P values). Limitations: relatively short follow-up and open-label design. Grade ≥3 any-cause AEs 75.3% vs 70.6%; 19.7% discontinued at least one combination drug for AEs (5.6% both); 19.1% received glucocorticoids ≥40 mg prednisone/day for immune-mediated AEs; one treatment-related death with the combination (small-intestine perforation) vs two with sunitinib.
records.keywords: Choueiri et al. N Engl J Med 2021;384:829-841  33657295

records.title: CLEAR
records.subtitle: RCC · First-line metastatic — immunotherapy-based combinations · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body: Advanced renal cell carcinoma with a clear-cell component; first-line, previously untreated (no previous systemic therapy); at least one measurable lesion per RECIST version 1.1, Karnofsky performance-status score ≥70 and adequately controlled blood pressure with or without medications Lenvatinib 20 mg orally once daily + pembrolizumab 200 mg IV on day 1 of each 21-day cycle (pembrolizumab up to 35 cycles, then lenvatinib alone) vs lenvatinib 18 mg + everolimus 5 mg orally once daily (21-day cycles) vs sunitinib 50 mg orally once daily, 4 weeks on → 2 weeks off Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, safety, duration of response, complete response rate, PFS2 Lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab significantly prolonged PFS and OS vs sunitinib as first-line therapy for advanced RCC. Final PFS analysis (independent review): median 23.9 vs 9.2 mo (HR 0.39; 95% CI 0.32–0.49); lenvatinib plus everolimus also prolonged PFS (14.7 vs 9.2 mo; HR 0.65; 95% CI 0.53–0.80). Interim OS (26.6-mo follow-up): HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.49–0.88) for lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab; OS not significantly longer with lenvatinib plus everolimus (HR 1.15; 95% CI 0.88–1.50). Final prespecified OS (follow-up about 4 yr; descriptive, nominal P): HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.63–0.99); median 53.7 vs 54.3 mo; 36-mo OS 66.4% vs 60.2%; same-cut PFS HR 0.47, ORR 71.3% vs 36.7%, CR 18.3% vs 4.8%. Open-label. Grade ≥3 AEs 82.4% vs 83.1% vs 71.8%, including hypertension, diarrhea and elevated lipase; lenvatinib was dose-reduced in 68.8% with pembrolizumab. Fatal AEs not attributed to progression: 11, 10 and 2 patients, respectively; final-cut fatal TEAEs 16 vs 12 (treatment-related 4 vs 1).
records.keywords: Motzer et al. N Engl J Med 2021;384:1289-1300  33616314 Motzer et al. J Clin Oncol 2024;42:1222-1228  38227898

records.title: COSMIC-313
records.subtitle: RCC · First-line metastatic — immunotherapy-based combinations · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body: Advanced or metastatic renal-cell carcinoma with a clear-cell component; previously untreated for advanced disease (one prior adjuvant therapy allowed, except PD-L1 or PD-1 plus CTLA-4 combinations); IMDC intermediate or poor risk; Karnofsky ≥70; excluded brain or cranial epidural disease unless adequately treated and stable, uncontrolled autoimmune disease and prednisone >10 mg/day (or equivalent) within 14 days Cabozantinib 40 mg orally once daily + nivolumab 3 mg/kg and ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks for four cycles → nivolumab 480 mg every 4 weeks for up to 2 years vs matched placebo orally once daily + the same nivolumab-ipilimumab → nivolumab maintenance; treatment until loss of clinical benefit or unacceptable toxicity Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, safety, disease control, time to response Adding cabozantinib to nivolumab plus ipilimumab significantly prolonged PFS in previously untreated IMDC intermediate- or poor-risk advanced RCC, with more grade 3 or 4 toxicity; the final analysis showed no OS benefit. In the first 550 randomized patients (primary analysis, median follow-up 14.9 mo), 12-month PFS was 0.57 vs 0.49 (HR 0.73; 95% CI 0.57-0.94; P=0.01); median PFS not reached vs 11.3 mo. At the final analysis (ITT, median follow-up 45.0 mo), median PFS was 16.6 vs 11.2 mo (HR 0.82; 95% CI 0.69-0.98); median OS 41.9 vs 42.0 mo (HR 1.02; 95% CI 0.85-1.23; P=0.84). PFS benefit was not seen in poor-risk patients (HR 1.04). ORR 46% vs 37% (CR 4% vs 3%). Exploratory: M2-like macrophage-high tumours showed triplet PFS and OS benefit. Grade 3 or 4 AEs occurred in 79% vs 56% at the primary analysis, including ALT increase in 27% vs 6%; at final analysis, grade 3/4 TRAEs 75% vs 43%, TRAE-led discontinuation of any component 49% vs 26%, grade 5 TRAEs three (0.7%) vs five (1.2%).

records.title: SWOG 1500 (PAPMET)
records.subtitle: RCC · Non-clear-cell RCC · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2021
records.body: Metastatic papillary RCC (treatment-naïve or prior non-VEGF therapy) Cabozantinib vs sunitinib (crizotinib/savolitinib arms closed for futility) Progression-free survival Cabozantinib improved median PFS over sunitinib (9.0 vs 5.6 months, HR 0.60) with higher ORR (23% vs 4%); established cabozantinib as a standard for metastatic papillary RCC.

records.title: SUNNIFORECAST
records.subtitle: RCC · Non-clear-cell RCC · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2025
records.body: Adults with previously untreated advanced or metastatic RCC with ≥50% non-clear-cell component, measurable disease, KPS ≥70%, tissue available and any IMDC risk; randomisation used papillary versus non-papillary classification, with local diagnosis allowed pending mandatory central review Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV then ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks for four doses, then nivolumab 240 mg IV every 2 weeks or 480 mg IV every 4 weeks vs heterogeneous investigator-choice SOC, mostly sunitinib Primary: 12-month overall survival rate. Secondary: 6- and 18-month overall survival rates; median overall survival; progression-free survival; objective response rate; safety; quality of life Ipilimumab-nivolumab improved the primary 12-month OS rate (78% vs 68%; one-sided P=0.026). Exploratory median OS numerically favored the combination (33.2 vs 25.2 months; HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.61-1.09; nominal P=0.163), and PFS estimates were 5.4 vs 5.7 months (HR 0.99). ORR among patients with valid response assessment was 33% vs 20%. Among treated participants (n=156 vs 143), serious AEs occurred in 48% vs 39%; toxicity discontinuation was 17% vs 9%, and five vs three fatal AEs were reported, none treatment-related. FKSI-DRS showed no significant between-arm difference among questionnaire respondents, with participation declining at later timepoints.

records.title: RECORD-1
records.subtitle: RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2008
records.body: Metastatic renal cell carcinoma with a clear-cell component; progressed on or within 6 months of stopping sunitinib, sorafenib or both (prior bevacizumab, interleukin 2 or interferon alfa permitted); measurable disease (RECIST), Karnofsky performance status ≥70%; excluded prior mTOR inhibitor (temsirolimus), untreated CNS metastases or uncontrolled medical conditions Everolimus 10 mg orally once daily, continuous, + best supportive care vs placebo + best supportive care (double-blind); 28-day cycles until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, death or discontinuation for any other reason Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: safety, objective tumour response rate, overall survival, disease-related symptoms, quality of life Everolimus prolonged PFS vs placebo in metastatic RCC that had progressed on VEGF-targeted therapy. The trial was halted at the second interim analysis; final central PFS (266 events) was 4.9 vs 1.9 mo; HR 0.33 (95% CI 0.25–0.43). Partial responses 1.8% vs 0%; benefit probably reflected disease stabilisation. Mature OS (November 2008) did not differ significantly: 14.8 vs 14.4 mo; HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.65–1.15), likely confounded by 80% placebo crossover; an exploratory crossover adjustment estimated 1.9-fold longer survival (95% CI 0.5–8.5). EORTC QLQ-C30 deterioration did not differ (interim); final FKSI-DRS deterioration HR 0.75, 1-sided p=0.053; KPS deterioration delayed (p=0.004). AEs were mostly grade 1 or 2: stomatitis 44% vs 8%; grade 3 pneumonitis 4%, grade 3 hyperglycaemia 15% and AE discontinuation 13% with everolimus (final). One everolimus death from candidal sepsis might have been attributable to study drug; 3 of 4 non-progression deaths were infection-related.

records.title: AXIS
records.subtitle: RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2011
records.body: Advanced renal cell carcinoma, histologically or cytologically confirmed with a clear-cell component; second-line after RECIST-defined progression on one previous first-line regimen based on sunitinib, bevacizumab plus interferon-alfa, temsirolimus or cytokines; measurable disease, ECOG PS 0 or 1; excluded CNS metastasis, uncontrolled hypertension, MI, uncontrolled angina, CHF or cerebrovascular accident within 12 months, and DVT/PE within 6 months Axitinib 5 mg orally twice daily, escalable to 7 mg then a maximum of 10 mg twice daily if no adverse reactions above grade 2 for at least 2 weeks and blood pressure not higher than 150/90 mm Hg without antihypertensive medication vs sorafenib 400 mg twice daily; open-label; both until RECIST progression, unacceptable toxic effects, death or withdrawal of consent Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, time to deterioration, safety Axitinib produced a statistically significant and clinically meaningful PFS improvement vs sorafenib and is a treatment option for second-line therapy of advanced RCC. Median PFS by masked independent review 6.7 vs 4.7 mo (HR 0.665; 95% CI 0.544–0.812); ORR 19% vs 9% (p=0.0001); time to deterioration HR 0.829 (FKSI-15) and 0.838 (FKSI-DRS). In preplanned subgroups, median PFS was 12.1 vs 6.5 mo after cytokines and 4.8 vs 3.4 mo after sunitinib (HR 0.741); prior-bevacizumab and prior-temsirolimus subgroups were too small for conclusions. OS was immature (223 of 417 required events). The trial was open-label, and only the axitinib arm allowed dose escalation. Grade ≥3 hypertension 16% vs 11%, diarrhoea 11% vs 7%, fatigue 11% vs 5%, palmar-plantar erythrodysaesthesia 5% vs 16%; discontinuation for toxic effects 4% vs 8%; no treatment-toxicity deaths with axitinib vs two with sorafenib.

records.title: METEOR
records.subtitle: RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2015
records.body: Advanced or metastatic renal-cell carcinoma with a clear-cell component and measurable disease; previously treated with at least one VEGFR-targeting tyrosine kinase inhibitor, with radiographic progression during treatment or within 6 months after the most recent dose; no limit on prior therapies (including VEGF, PD-1 or PD-L1 antibodies), adequately treated stable brain metastases eligible; excluded prior mTOR inhibitor or cabozantinib Cabozantinib 60 mg orally once daily vs everolimus 10 mg orally once daily; both continued as long as the investigator observed clinical benefit or until unacceptable toxicity Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival; objective response rate; safety Progression-free survival was longer with cabozantinib than with everolimus in renal-cell carcinoma that had progressed after VEGFR-targeted therapy. In the first 375 randomized patients, median PFS by independent review was 7.4 vs 3.8 mo (HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.45 to 0.75; P<0.001) and ORR 21% vs 5%. At the prespecified interim analysis (202 deaths), OS favoured cabozantinib (HR 0.67; 95% CI 0.51 to 0.89) but did not reach the required P≤0.0019 boundary; OS data were immature and follow-up continues to the final analysis. Grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 68% vs 58% (with cabozantinib mainly hypertension 15%, diarrhea 11%, fatigue 9%); dose reductions were needed in 60% vs 25%; discontinuation for adverse events not related to RCC was 9% vs 10%. Grade 5 events occurred in 7% vs 8%, primarily from disease progression; treatment-related grade 5 events occurred in 1 vs 2 patients.
records.keywords: Choueiri et al. N Engl J Med 2015;373:1814-1823  26406150

records.title: CheckMate 025
records.subtitle: RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2015
records.body: Advanced or metastatic renal-cell carcinoma with a clear-cell component; previously treated with one or two antiangiogenic regimens and no more than three total systemic regimens; progression during or after the last regimen and within 6 months before enrollment, Karnofsky performance status ≥70; excluded CNS metastasis, prior mTOR inhibitor, or conditions requiring glucocorticoids >10 mg prednisone daily Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks vs everolimus 10 mg orally once daily (open-label); treatment could continue beyond initial progression if the investigator judged clinical benefit with acceptable side effects Primary: overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, progression-free survival, association between overall survival and tumor PD-L1 expression, incidence of adverse events, duration of response, quality of life Among patients with previously treated advanced renal-cell carcinoma, OS was longer and grade 3/4 adverse events were fewer with nivolumab than with everolimus. At the planned interim analysis (398 of 569 required deaths; minimum follow-up 14 mo), median OS was 25.0 vs 19.6 mo; HR 0.73 (98.5% CI 0.57–0.93; P=0.002), meeting the prespecified superiority criterion. ORR 25% vs 5%. Median PFS did not differ significantly: 4.6 vs 4.4 mo; HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.75–1.03; P=0.11). OS HR was 0.79 (95% CI 0.53–1.17) with ≥1% and 0.77 (95% CI 0.60–0.97) with <1% PD-L1 expression; the authors state the data do not support PD-L1 as a marker of treatment benefit. FKSI-DRS symptom score changes favoured nivolumab through week 104. Treatment-related grade 3/4 AEs 19% vs 37%; discontinuation for treatment-related AEs 8% vs 13%; no deaths from study-drug toxic effects with nivolumab vs two with everolimus.
records.keywords: Motzer et al. N Engl J Med 2015;373:1803-1813  26406148

records.title: TIVO-3
records.subtitle: RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body: Metastatic renal cell carcinoma with a clear cell component; third-line or fourth-line after unsuccessful treatment with two or three systemic regimens, one including a VEGFR TKI other than tivozanib or sorafenib (prior checkpoint inhibitor allowed); excluded prior tivozanib or sorafenib, CNS metastases unless radiographically stable without steroids for ≥3 months, substantial cardiovascular disease, or MI, angina or thromboembolic/vascular disorder within 6 months Tivozanib 1·5 mg orally once daily, 21 days on/7 days off in 4-week cycles vs sorafenib 400 mg orally twice daily continuously; open-label; until IRC-confirmed disease progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, safety Third-line or fourth-line tivozanib improved progression-free survival and was better tolerated than sorafenib in metastatic RCC. IRC-assessed median PFS 5·6 vs 3·9 mo (HR 0·73, 95% CI 0·56–0·94; p=0·016); objective response 18% vs 8% among patients with measurable disease, with no complete responses. OS did not differ at the later OS analysis (median 16·4 vs 19·7 mo; HR 0·99, 95% CI 0·76–1·29); subsequent therapies were not controlled. In subgroup analyses, PFS HR was 0·55 (95% CI 0·32–0·94) after prior checkpoint inhibitor but 1·15 in poor IMDC risk. The trial was open-label. Grade 3–4 treatment-related hypertension 20% vs 14%; serious treatment-related AEs 11% vs 10%; dose reductions 24% vs 38%; no treatment-related deaths.

records.title: CONTACT-03
records.subtitle: RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body: Locally advanced or metastatic RCC, clear-cell or non-clear-cell (papillary, chromophobe or unclassifiable only), with or without sarcomatoid features; progression during or after anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy in the first- or second-line advanced setting, or during or within 6 months after adjuvant checkpoint therapy; two or more cycles in the immediately preceding line; excluded prior cabozantinib or mTOR inhibitor, more than one checkpoint inhibitor or more than two advanced-setting lines Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV every 3 weeks plus cabozantinib 60 mg orally once daily vs cabozantinib 60 mg orally once daily alone; continued until unacceptable toxicity or loss of clinical benefit, treatment beyond progression allowed Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, time to response, safety Adding atezolizumab to cabozantinib did not improve clinical outcomes and increased toxicity; the authors concluded that sequential checkpoint inhibitor use in renal cell carcinoma outside clinical trials should be discouraged. Co-primary PFS by central review was not improved: median 10·6 vs 10·8 mo, atezolizumab–cabozantinib vs cabozantinib (HR 1·03, 95% CI 0·83–1·28; p=0·78). At the first interim OS analysis (176 deaths), OS was not significantly different: median 25·7 mo vs not evaluable (HR 0·94, 95% CI 0·70–1·27); median follow-up 15·2 mo. Confirmed ORR by central review was 41% in both arms. Serious AEs 48% vs 33%; treatment-related grade 3–4 AEs 55% vs 47%. Deaths due to AEs 17 (6%) vs nine (4%), including three treatment-related deaths with the combination (renal failure, enterocolitis, GI perforation) and none with cabozantinib.

records.title: LITESPARK-005
records.subtitle: RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Advanced clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma; stage IV (AJCC); progression after both a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor and a VEGFR-TKI (in sequence or combination); three or fewer previous systemic therapies with radiographic progression during or after the most recent regimen, Karnofsky ≥70; previous everolimus not permitted Belzutifan 120 mg orally once daily vs everolimus 10 mg orally once daily (open-label), each until disease progression, unacceptable toxic effects or a decision to discontinue Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response, duration of response, safety, time to confirmed worsening of disease-related symptoms (FKSI-DRS), time to confirmed deterioration in global health status and quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30), complete response rate, time to response Belzutifan significantly improved progression-free survival and objective response vs everolimus after immune checkpoint and antiangiogenic therapy, with no new safety signals. At the first interim analysis (median follow-up 18.4 months), median PFS was 5.6 months in both groups and the curves crossed, but 18-month PFS was 24.0% vs 8.3% (P = 0.002); confirmed ORR was 21.9% vs 3.5% (P<0.001). At the second interim analysis (median follow-up 25.7 months), OS did not reach significance: median 21.4 vs 18.1 months; HR 0.88 (95% CI, 0.73 to 1.07; P = 0.20); final analysis pending. Grade ≥3 AEs 61.8% vs 62.5% (grade 5 in 3.5% vs 5.3%); AE discontinuation 5.9% vs 14.7%. With belzutifan, anemia 82.8% (grade 3–5 32.5%) and hypoxia 14.5% (grade ≥3 10.5%); one death (multiple organ dysfunction syndrome) attributed to belzutifan.
records.keywords: Choueiri et al. N Engl J Med 2024;391:710-721  39167807

records.title: TiNivo-2
records.subtitle: RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Advanced renal cell carcinoma with a clear cell component; progression during or after one or two previous lines of therapy, one including an ICI (anti-PD-1/PD-L1; combinations with CTLA-4 inhibitors allowed); measurable disease per RECIST 1.1; excluded more than two previous lines, active autoimmune disease, uncontrolled hypertension, systemic corticosteroids within 14 days of first dose or other immunosuppressants within 30 days of randomisation Tivozanib 0·89 mg orally once daily for 21 days of each 28-day cycle plus nivolumab 480 mg IV on day 1 of each cycle (nivolumab for a maximum of 2 years) vs tivozanib 1·34 mg orally once daily for 21 days of each 28-day cycle; tivozanib continued in the absence of progression or intolerable toxicity Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, investigator-assessed progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, safety, quality of life (FKSI-DRS) TiNivo-2 did not meet its primary endpoint: adding nivolumab to tivozanib did not improve outcomes after an ICI, and the authors conclude ICI rechallenge should be discouraged in advanced RCC. Median PFS by independent review was 5·7 vs 7·4 months with tivozanib–nivolumab vs tivozanib (HR 1·10, 95% CI 0·84–1·43; p=0·49). There was no benefit in the predefined strata with an ICI (7·4 vs 9·2 months) or a non-ICI (3·7 vs 3·7 months) as most recent therapy. ORR was 19% vs 20%. OS was immature at 33% of events (median 17·7 vs 22·1 months) at a median follow-up of 12·0 months. The authors' suggestion that tivozanib monotherapy is active after an ICI rests on the control arm, with no comparator. The reduced combination tivozanib dose may have lowered its efficacy. Serious AEs occurred in 54 (32%) of 168 vs 64 (37%) of 171 patients and grade ≥3 hypertension in 75 (22%) overall. AE deaths were 7 (4%) vs 5 (3%); 1 death was treatment related (tivozanib arm).

records.title: LenCabo
records.subtitle: RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2026
records.body: Metastatic or advanced clear-cell RCC or RCC with a clear-cell component; 1-2 prior metastatic systemic lines including a PD-(L)1 ICI, or adjuvant PD-(L)1 ICI with last dose within 6 months before enrollment; progression on/after PD-(L)1 ICI or no further ICI due to immune-mediated AEs; excluded prior lenvatinib, mTOR or MET inhibitor (e.g. cabozantinib), proteinuria (dipstick ≥1+ or urine protein:creatinine ≥2 mg/mg), active IBD Lenvatinib 18 mg daily + everolimus 5 mg daily vs cabozantinib 60 mg daily; continuous daily dosing in 30-day cycles Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, disease control rate, overall survival, health-related quality of life, grade 3-5 adverse events, time to response, duration of response In metastatic ccRCC that progressed on prior PD-1 ICI, lenvatinib + everolimus significantly prolonged PFS over cabozantinib. Median PFS 15.7 vs 10.2 mo in treated patients at 20 mo median follow-up; adjusted HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.29-0.89); an ITT sensitivity analysis also showed PFS benefit. The design allowed a one-sided type I error of 0.15, and the authors note a possible false-positive finding; with shrinkage priors, the posterior probability of a clinically meaningful PFS benefit (HR <0.80) was 75%. ORR 52.6% vs 38.6% was numerically higher, but the comparison was inconclusive (OR 1.71, 95% CI 0.72-4.0). OS was immature with 24 deaths and the comparison was inconclusive (HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.47-2.38). Treatment-related grade ≥3 AEs 67.5% vs 50%; discontinuation due to toxicity 20% vs 10.9%; one grade 5 treatment-related epistaxis with cabozantinib.

records.title: LITESPARK-011
records.subtitle: RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Unresectable locally advanced or metastatic stage IV clear-cell RCC progressing on or after one prior anti-PD-1/PD-L1 as first- or second-line treatment, or ≤6 months after last dose as adjuvant or neoadjuvant-adjuvant therapy; KPS ≥70%, resting pulse oximetry ≥92%, ≤2 prior systemic regimens with anti-PD-1/PD-L1 immediately preceding enrolment; no previous belzutifan or other HIF-2α inhibitor, cabozantinib or lenvatinib Belzutifan 120 mg orally once daily plus lenvatinib 20 mg orally once daily vs cabozantinib 60 mg orally once daily, both until radiographic progression, unacceptable adverse events, pregnancy, prohibited medication, or participant discontinuation Primary: Progression-free survival, Overall survival. Secondary: Objective response rate, Duration of response, Safety, Patient-reported outcomes Belzutifan–lenvatinib improved central-review PFS (final PFS analysis at second interim; median follow-up 29 months; median 14·8 vs 10·7 months; HR 0·70, 95% CI 0·59-0·84; one-sided p<0·0001) and the authors conclude it might be a new standard of care after anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy. Overall survival was not significantly different at this second interim (median 34·9 vs 27·6 months; HR 0·85, 95% CI 0·68-1·05; one-sided p=0·061) and will be tested at final analysis. ORR crossed its first-interim boundary (53% vs 40%; CR 5% vs 1%); median duration of response 23·0 vs 12·3 months. Among treated participants (n=370 vs 371), grade 3-5 TEAEs 84% vs 83%; serious TEAEs 52% vs 44%; treatment-related deaths two vs one; treatment-related discontinuation 19% vs 5%; anaemia 69% vs 26% and hypoxia 15% vs 0% with belzutifan-lenvatinib

records.title: Adjuvant Mitotane (Terzolo)
records.subtitle: Adrenocortical Carcinoma · Adrenocortical carcinoma · Retrospective cohort study · 2007
records.body: Adults with radically resected adrenocortical carcinoma at Italian tertiary centres or German registry centres, without distant metastases, incomplete staging/resection, major comorbidity, recent other cancer or non-mitotane adjuvant therapy Adjuvant mitotane after radical surgery: 3–5 g/day (n=20) or 1–3 g/day (n=27) vs Italian contemporaneous no-adjuvant control (n=55) vs German registry no-adjuvant control (n=75) Primary: Recurrence-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, Mitotane-associated adverse events Adjuvant mitotane was associated with longer RFS than untreated Italian and German controls (median 42 vs 10 and 25 months; recurrence in 23/47 vs 50/55 and 55/75), with directionally favourable adjusted analyses. Median OS was 110 vs 52 and 67 months, but secondary comparisons were nominal. Toxicity was mainly grade 1–2; 6/47 (13%) required temporary interruption or dose reduction. Nonrandomised centre-policy allocation, baseline imbalance and retrospective safety ascertainment preclude definitive causal benefit

records.title: FIRM-ACT (Fassnacht)
records.subtitle: Adrenocortical Carcinoma · Adrenocortical carcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2012
records.body: Adults with histologically confirmed, radiologically measurable, unresectable locally advanced or metastatic adrenocortical carcinoma; no prior cytotoxic therapy other than mitotane; ECOG 0-2 and adequate organ function EDP-M: etoposide 100 mg/m2 IV days 2–4, doxorubicin 40 mg/m2 IV day 1 and cisplatin 40 mg/m2 IV days 3–4 every 4 weeks plus continuous oral mitotane; vs Sz-M: streptozocin 1 g IV days 1–5 in cycle 1 then 2 g IV day 1 every 3 weeks plus mitotane; mitotane began at least 1 week before chemotherapy, targeting 14–20 mg/L Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, Tumour response, Quality of life, Mitotane-level association, Second-line regimen response EDP-M did not meet the alpha-controlled primary OS endpoint (median 14.8 vs 12.0 months; HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.61–1.02; P=0.07) but improved nominal secondary PFS (5.0 vs 2.1 months; HR 0.55, 0.43–0.69; P<0.001) and response (23.2% vs 9.2%; P<0.001) versus Sz-M. Serious events per treatment-month (0.092 vs 0.099; P=0.64) and QoL were similar, with low questionnaire completion; mandated crossover may attenuate OS and second-line comparisons are selection-biased

records.title: International Germ Cell Cancer Collaborative Group (IGCCCG)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Risk classification & prognosis · Retrospective cohort study · 1997
records.body: Adult men with metastatic seminoma or nonseminomatous germ cell tumour (NSGCT), gonadal or extragonadal primary; treated between 1975 and 1990 with cisplatin- or carboplatin-containing chemotherapy; mixed seminoma/NSGCT or pure seminoma with raised AFP analysed as NSGCT; prior irradiation or retroperitoneal lymph-node dissection permitted, previous chemotherapy disallowed No assigned treatment arms (retrospective prognostic analysis); all patients received cisplatin- (or carboplatin-) containing chemotherapy, regimens not specified Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: response to induction chemotherapy, cause of death An easily applicable, clinically based prognostic classification for metastatic germ cell tumours was agreed by the major trial groups for use in practice and in trial design and reporting. Independent adverse factors in NSGCT were mediastinal primary, degree of AFP, hCG and LDH elevation, and NPVM; NPVM was the predominant adverse feature in seminoma. Good prognosis comprised 60% of GCT (5-yr survival 91%), intermediate 26% (79%) and poor 14%, all NSGCT (48%). NSGCT 5-yr PFS/survival: good 89%/92%, intermediate 75%/80%, poor 41%/48%. In the 30% NSGCT validation set, 5-yr survival was 90%, 79% and 57%. Data were retrospective (1975-1990) and seminoma had too few events for split-sample validation. In a separate retrospective MSKCC cohort (Mazumdar 2001), satisfactory vs unsatisfactory early AFP/hCG decline predicted CR 92% vs 62%, 2-yr EFS 91% vs 69% and 2-yr OS 95% vs 72%, independent of IGCCCG risk and most pronounced in poor risk (small samples).
records.keywords: International Germ Cell Cancer Collaborative Group. J Clin Oncol 1997;15:594-603  9053482 Mazumdar et al. J Clin Oncol 2001;19:2534-2541

records.title: IGCCCG Update (Non-seminoma)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Risk classification & prognosis · Registry study · 2021
records.body: Adult men with nonseminomatous germ cell tumours (by histology and/or unequivocal AFP elevation); metastatic disease, or primary retroperitoneal/mediastinal NSGCT even when not metastatic, treated 1990–2013 with first-line cisplatin- and etoposide-based chemotherapy (conventional-dose, at least three cycles intended, or upfront high-dose with stem-cell support); excluded prior chemotherapy for metastatic disease, patients in the original IGCCCG analysis and primary brain GCT Observational cohort with no assigned arms: first-line cisplatin- and etoposide-based chemotherapy, either conventional-dose (at least three cycles; mostly three cycles of BEP or four of EP for good prognosis, four of BEP or an equivalent for intermediate/poor prognosis) or upfront high-dose chemotherapy with stem-cell support Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: prognostic factors for PFS, integrated Brier score, time-dependent 3-year AUC, calibration The IGCCCG Update model improved individual prognostication in metastatic NSGCT, adding increasing age and lung metastases as adverse factors and a single LDH cutoff of 2.5x ULN. The original IGCCCG classification remains relevant for treatment decisions. Versus the 1997 IGCCCG cohort (historical, non-randomised comparison), 5-year OS rose in good (92% to 96%), intermediate (80% to 89%) and poor prognosis (48% to 67%). 5-year PFS improved significantly only in poor prognosis (41% to 54%), staying similar in good (89% vs 90%) and intermediate (75% vs 78%). In the PFS training set of 3,542, the HR for progression was 1.25 per 10-year age increase and 1.66 for lung metastases; 3-year AUC was 0.75 in training and 0.73 in independent validation. More than 30% of poor-prognosis patients may still die of their disease. Model endpoints were censored at 3 years, and postchemotherapy marker decline could not be included.
records.keywords: Gillessen et al. J Clin Oncol 2021;39:1563-1574  33822655

records.title: IGCCCG Update (Seminoma)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Risk classification & prognosis · Retrospective cohort study · 2021
records.body: Adult men with metastatic pure seminoma (or retroperitoneal/mediastinal seminoma even if not metastatic); first-line cisplatin- and etoposide-based conventional-dose chemotherapy, minimum three cycles given or intended, treated 1990-2013 (validation set also 2013-March 2016); original IGCCCG good or intermediate prognosis; excluded AFP >30 ng/mL, prior chemotherapy for metastatic disease, patients in the 1997 IGCCCG analysis, primary brain GCT Observational cohort: first-line cisplatin- and etoposide-based chemotherapy (mostly three cycles BEP or four cycles EP for good prognosis; four cycles BEP or three cycles BEP plus one cycle EP for intermediate prognosis); good prognosis subgrouped by pre-chemotherapy LDH ≤2.5x vs >2.5x ULN Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: prognostic variable importance, time-dependent AUC at 3 years The original IGCCCG classification kept its relevance in metastatic seminoma treated in 1990-2013, with higher survival than the 1997 series, and pre-chemotherapy LDH >2.5x ULN was an additional adverse prognostic factor within good prognosis. 5-year PFS 89% good vs 79% intermediate (1997: 82% and 67%); 5-year OS 95% vs 88% (1997: 86% and 72%); formal comparison with 1997 was not possible. Good prognosis with LDH >2.5x ULN: 3-year PFS 80% (95% CI, 75 to 84) and OS 92% vs 92% and 97% with lower LDH, similar to intermediate prognosis; 3-year AUC 0.61. In validation (764 patients), 3-year PFS was 75% vs 93% (AUC 0.64); the OS difference could not be tested owing to few events. Retrospective data cannot show the best treatment, e.g. four vs three cycles BEP with high LDH.
records.keywords: Beyer et al. J Clin Oncol 2021;39:1553-1562  33729863

records.title: MRC TE19/EORTC 30982
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I seminoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2005
records.body: Testicular seminomatous germ-cell tumour (histologically confirmed, classic or anaplastic); adjuvant therapy after orchidectomy, randomised within 8 weeks of orchidectomy; pathological stage pT1–pT3 with clinical and radiological stage I disease, normal alpha-fetoprotein before and after orchidectomy and normal human chorionic gonadotropin after orchidectomy; excluding pT4 (involvement of the cut end of the spermatic cord) Adjuvant radiotherapy to para-aortic strip or dog-leg field (dog-leg recommended after previous inguinal surgery), 30 Gy in 15 fractions or 20 Gy in 10 fractions by optional sub-randomisation, otherwise a 20–30 Gy total-dose schedule vs carboplatin AUC 7 as a single intravenous injection (dose 7 × [GFR + 25] mg; 90% of this dose when GFR was measured by 24-hour urinary creatinine clearance rather than EDTA) Primary: relapse-free rate. Secondary: death from any cause, second cancer incidence, second primary testicular germ-cell tumours, morbidity by patient diary card, EORTC QLQ-C30, adverse effects, gonadal function At median 6.5-year follow-up, single-dose carboplatin (AUC 7) remained non-inferior to radiotherapy for relapse-free rate and significantly reduced contralateral GCTs. Relapse-free rates: 97.3% vs 96.5% at 2 years and 94.7% vs 96.0% at 5 years (carboplatin vs radiotherapy; HR 1.25, 90% CI 0.83–1.89); the 90% CI excluded a carboplatin relapse excess above 3% at 2 years and 3.5% at 5 years. Carboplatin relapses were mostly para-aortic (74% vs 9%); 15 of 26 were detected by routine abdominal CT; only 1 occurred after 3 years. Contralateral GCTs: 2 carboplatin vs 15 radiotherapy (HR 0.22, 95% CI 0.05–0.95). Seminoma deaths: 1 radiotherapy vs none carboplatin. Exploratory nonrandomised: 5-year RFR 96.1% with ≥AUC 7 vs 92.6% with lower doses (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.24–1.07). Carboplatin caused less lethargy and time off work but more grade 3 or 4 thrombocytopenia (none with radiotherapy vs 17 [4%]), without bleeding. Radiotherapy caused more dyspepsia (17% vs 8%).
records.keywords: Oliver et al. Lancet 2005;366:293-300  16039331 Oliver et al. J Clin Oncol 2011;29:957-962  21282539 Mead et al. J Natl Cancer Inst 2011;103:241-249  21212385

records.title: MRC TE18 / EORTC 30942
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I seminoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2005
records.body: Clinical stage I seminoma, adjuvant radiotherapy Para-aortic RT 20 Gy/10 fractions vs 30 Gy/15 fractions Relapse rate (non-inferiority) 20 Gy non-inferior to 30 Gy: 11 vs 10 relapses (HR 1.11), 2-yr relapse-rate difference 0.7%, with less acute lethargy and faster return to work. Established 20 Gy as the standard adjuvant RT dose when RT is used.

records.title: van de Wetering et al
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I seminoma · Editorial · 2018
records.body: Clinical stage I testicular seminoma after orchiectomy; adjuvant management choice (surveillance, radiotherapy or carboplatin); risk factors for relapse discussed: tumour size >4 cm and rete testis invasion; expert commentary, no enrolled population Narrative comparison of surveillance vs adjuvant radiotherapy (dogleg, 24 to 26 Gy) vs adjuvant carboplatin (AUC 7; one or two cycles); no assigned treatment Relapse rate, relapse-free rate, site of relapse, disease-specific survival, second primary germ cell tumour, second malignant neoplasms, cardiovascular disease The authors conclude that surveillance is the treatment of choice for most, if not all, compliant patients with CS I seminoma. They hold that one cycle of carboplatin (AUC 7) should no longer be an option in any risk group, and that two cycles need further study. In the non-randomized SWENOTECA cohort (897 patients; median follow-up 5.6 yr), one carboplatin cycle cut relapse by only approximately 50% in all risk groups (both risk factors: 16.7% surveillance vs 10.4% carboplatin). After carboplatin, the retroperitoneum was the only relapse site in 90%, so CT surveillance remains mandatory. In MRC TE19/EORTC 30982, 5-yr noninferiority to RT held only after the margin was adjusted to 5%. Adjuvant dogleg RT (24 to 26 Gy) is the only therapy shown to reduce relapse in high-risk patients. In a Danish cohort with tumours 6 cm or larger, 32.0% relapsed on surveillance vs 2.8% after RT. Risks of second malignancies and cardiovascular disease remain a concern. This is expert opinion with no new patient data.
records.keywords: van de Wetering et al. J Clin Oncol 2018;36:837-840  29389229

records.title: SGCCG risk-adapted studies (Aparicio et al.)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I seminoma · Prospective cohort study · 2014
records.body: Clinical stage I testicular seminoma after orchiectomy, staged with chest X-ray, abdominopelvic CT and serum markers; enrolled 1994–2008; risk criteria for adjuvant therapy differed by study: first study vascular invasion and/or >T1 tumors; second study tumor size >4 cm and/or rete testis invasion; third study both criteria required Low-risk: active surveillance vs high-risk: adjuvant carboplatin, two cycles (first study 400 mg/m² 28 days apart; second and third studies AUC 7 every 21 days); allocation by study-specific risk factors, not randomised Disease-free survival, relapse rate, prognostic factors for relapse, time to relapse, pattern and site of relapse, salvage outcome, contralateral germ-cell tumors, second malignancies, cause-specific survival Long-term follow-up supports the risk-adapted approach as an effective option in stage I seminoma, with similar relapse patterns after surveillance or adjuvant carboplatin. At median follow-up 80 months, 63 patients (11.1%) relapsed: 51/396 (14.8%) on surveillance vs 12/348 (3.2%) after carboplatin; 5-yr DFS 88.3% vs 96.8%. These groups were selected by risk, not randomised. Median time to relapse was 13.7 months, and some relapses (0.8% of all patients) occurred after 5 years. All relapsed patients were made disease-free by salvage therapy, and no patient died of seminoma. In surveillance patients, rete testis invasion and tumor size independently predicted relapse; the proposed 3-year DFS nomogram (Somers' Dxy 0.28) needs prospective validation. Limitations: retrospective chart review, risk criteria that varied between studies, and 19.8% of patients with <5 years of follow-up. Second malignancies were similar between groups.

records.title: SWENOTECA V
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I seminoma · Prospective cohort study · 2011
records.body: Testicular seminomatous germ cell tumour with normal AFP before orchiectomy; all clinical stages (modified Royal Marsden staging), registered at diagnosis in a population-based Swedish and Norwegian cohort, January 2000 to December 2006; excluded spermatocytic seminoma and extragonadal germ cell tumours Stage-adapted protocol treatment, non-randomised: CS1: surveillance vs adjuvant radiotherapy 25.2 Gy in 14 fractions of 1.8 Gy to an L-field within 6 weeks of orchiectomy vs single-course adjuvant carboplatin AUC 7 (added by protocol amendment); CS2A: L-field radiotherapy including nodal metastases, 27 Gy in 15 fractions of 1.8 Gy; CS2B or higher: four courses of EP (etoposide 100 mg/m² days 1 to 5, cisplatin 20 mg/m² days 1 to 5), BEP (bleomycin 30,000 IU days 1, 5 and 15 added) for large-volume disease, intensified to BEP-if if marker or tumour response after two courses was inadequate Relapse-free interval, overall survival, cancer-specific survival, prognostic factors for relapse in CS1 surveillance, relapse pattern and treatment A binational, population-based seminoma protocol was feasible with excellent results; surveillance remained a good option in CS1, and no factor predicted relapse on surveillance. At median follow-up 5.2 yr, 5-yr cause-specific survival was 99.6%. CS1 relapse: surveillance 14.3% (65 of 512), carboplatin 3.9% (seven of 188), radiotherapy 0.8% (four of 481); adjusted HR carboplatin vs radiotherapy 4.7 (95% CI 1.1–14.4), but treatment was not randomized and rete testis invasion was not recorded. Adjuvant radiotherapy was dropped over secondary-cancer concerns. CS2A: three of 29 relapsed after radiotherapy vs zero of 73 CS2A/B after chemotherapy. CS2C/D relapse was 14.9%; OS was 50% in six IGCCC intermediate-prognosis patients. One treatment-related death followed relapse on surveillance; toxicity, including two myocardial infarctions and one cerebral infarction, cut short salvage EP in some patients.
records.keywords: Tandstad et al. J Clin Oncol 2011;29:719-725  21205748

records.title: AUO AH 01/94 (GTCSG)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I non-seminoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2008
records.body: Histologically confirmed nonseminomatous germ cell tumour of the testis after orchidectomy; clinical stage I (TNM) by CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis plus serum AFP, HCG and LDH, adjuvant setting, unselected by risk factors; excluded if CT showed ipsilateral-template lymph nodes larger than 10 mm in transverse diameter; treatment to start fewer than 4 weeks after orchidectomy One cycle of BEP (cisplatin 20 mg/m² days 1 to 5, etoposide 100 mg/m² days 1 to 5, bleomycin 30,000 IU (30 mg) days 1, 8 and 15) vs open RPLND (ipsilateral nerve-sparing or modified ipsilateral template dissection recommended) → two 21-day cycles of BEP at the same doses if pathologic stage II Primary: recurrence rate. Secondary: overall survival, cancer-specific survival, toxicity, 2-year recurrence-free survival One course of adjuvant BEP was superior to RPLND performed according to community standards in preventing recurrence in clinical stage I NSGCT; the authors state it is not standard treatment and merits further investigation. ITT, median follow-up 4.7 years: 2 vs 15 recurrences (P = .0011); 2-year recurrence-free survival 99.46% vs 91.87%, difference 7.59% (95% CI, 3.13% to 12.05%); HR for recurrence with surgery vs chemotherapy 7.937 (95% CI, 1.808 to 34.48). Per protocol: 2 vs 13 recurrences (P = .0033). One BEP relapse was a marker-negative retroperitoneal teratoma 5 years after treatment; seven of 13 RPLND relapses were retroperitoneal. No cancer-specific deaths. Cumulative grade 3 toxicity events: 37.4% with one course of BEP (mostly short-lasting leukopenia) vs 8.7% with surgery (mostly from two adjuvant BEP courses in pathologic stage II); neutropenic fever in four BEP patients.
records.keywords: Albers et al. J Clin Oncol 2008;26:2966-2972  18458040

records.title: SWENOTECA
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I non-seminoma · Prospective cohort study · 2009
records.body: Clinical stage I nonseminoma after orchiectomy; adjuvant setting; risk-adapted by lymphovascular invasion (LVI): LVI-positive patients recommended one course of BEP, LVI-negative patients chose between surveillance and BEP; CS I confirmed by second staging 6–8 weeks after orchiectomy (CT chest, abdomen and pelvis plus serum tumor markers); only patients receiving one course of BEP reported (single-arm) One course of adjuvant BEP: cisplatin 20 mg/m² daily days 1–5, etoposide 100 mg/m² daily days 1–5, bleomycin 30 mg daily days 1, 5 and 15, given 6–10 weeks after orchiectomy Relapse rate, time to relapse, overall survival, cause-specific survival, relapse treatment, relapse-free survival, short-term toxicity, burden of chemotherapy Updated and expanded results confirm a low relapse rate after one course of adjuvant BEP in CS I nonseminoma; this is a non-randomised single-arm series with no comparator. At median follow-up 7.9 yr, 12 relapses occurred, all IGCCC good prognosis. 5-yr relapse rate 3.2% (95% CI 1.6–6.4) with LVI (n=258) and 1.6% (95% CI 0.6–4.2) without LVI (n=255). 5-yr OS 99.0% and CSS 100%; 10-yr OS 96.9% and CSS 99.6%. Ten patients died, one from progressive testicular cancer after multiple relapses. Only 9 of 517 (1.7%) received salvage chemotherapy. One patient died of acute myeloid leukemia (M7, i12p) diagnosed 2.5 months after adjuvant BEP. In the earlier 2009 report, WHO grade 3/4 leukopenia occurred in 33% and infection in 2% of 312 patients after one BEP (toxicity reported for 75% to 80%). Data on secondary cancers and cardiovascular disease are still lacking.
records.keywords: Tandstad et al. J Clin Oncol 2009;27:2122-2128  19307506 Tandstad et al. Ann Oncol 2014;25:2167-2172  25114021

records.title: Spanish GCCG (Garcia-del-Muro)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage II seminoma · Prospective cohort study · 2008
records.body: Pure testicular seminoma after inguinal orchiectomy; clinical stage IIA (retroperitoneal nodal metastases up to 2 cm) or IIB (2 to 5 cm), at diagnosis or as relapse of previous stage I; no prior radiotherapy or chemotherapy; normal AFP before and after orchidectomy; prior malignancy or significant cardiac or hepatic disease excluded (single-arm) E400P: cisplatin 25 mg/m²/d + etoposide 100 mg/m²/d for 4 days, every 3 weeks for 4 cycles, or alternatively BE500P: cisplatin 20 mg/m²/d + etoposide 100 mg/m²/d for 5 days + weekly bleomycin 30 mg, every 3 weeks for 3 cycles (given: E400P 60, BE500P 12); resection of residual masses larger than 3 cm or at investigator discretion Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: response, toxicity, late toxicity, relapse The authors conclude that cisplatin-based chemotherapy is highly effective and well tolerated in stage IIA/IIB seminoma and an available alternative to radiotherapy; this single-arm observational cohort made no comparison with radiotherapy. CR 83% and PR with residual mass and normal markers 17%; no first-line failures. At median follow-up 71.5 months, 6 stage IIB patients relapsed, all after E400P, and 1 died of seminoma. 5-year PFS was 100% (IIA) vs 87% (95% CI, 77.5% to 97%) (IIB); whole-group 5-year PFS 90% (95% CI, 82% to 98%) and OS 95% (95% CI, 89% to 100%). The authors cannot rule out an effect of lower-dose etoposide (E400P) on relapse. No toxic deaths; grade 3 or 4 granulocytopenia in 9 patients (8 with febrile neutropenia), grade 3 thrombocytopenia in 2, reversible grade 3 pneumonitis in 1. Three non-seminoma deaths, including 2 esophageal carcinomas.
records.keywords: Garcia-del-Muro et al. J Clin Oncol 2008;26:5416-5421  18936476

records.title: Williams (Intergroup)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — good prognosis · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 1987
records.body: Disseminated germ-cell tumours, first-line Cisplatin/bleomycin + etoposide (BEP) vs + vinblastine (PVB) Disease-free response & survival Substituting etoposide for vinblastine gave equal-to-higher disease-free rates (83% vs 74% in advanced disease) with markedly less neuromuscular toxicity. Established BEP as the standard first-line regimen.

records.title: Loehrer et al.
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — good prognosis · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 1995
records.body: Disseminated testicular or extragonadal germ cell tumours (seminoma or nonseminoma); first-line, no prior systemic chemotherapy; good-risk minimal or moderate Indiana stage (eg, unresectable nonpalpable >3 cm retroperitoneal disease; lung metastases <5 per lung field with largest <2 cm, or 5 to 10 with largest <3 cm; abdominal mass >10 cm without supradiaphragmatic disease; mediastinal adenopathy <50% intrathoracic diameter); no age or performance status restriction; advanced stage excluded Cisplatin 20 mg/m² IV days 1 to 5 + etoposide 100 mg/m² IV days 1 to 5 every 3 weeks for 3 cycles + bleomycin 30 IU/wk for 9 weeks (PVP16B) vs the same cisplatin + etoposide for 3 cycles without bleomycin (PVP16); residual radiographic disease → surgical resection, with two additional PVP16 cycles if carcinoma was resected Response rate, duration of remission, overall survival, disease-free (NED) rate, failure-free survival, unfavourable outcomes, toxicity The authors conclude bleomycin is an essential component of three-cycle PVP16B in minimal- or moderate-stage disseminated germ cell tumours. Disease-free status did not differ significantly (81 of 86 [94%] PVP16B vs 75 of 85 [88%] PVP16; P = .20), but unfavourable outcomes were more frequent without bleomycin (32 of 85 [38%] vs 15 of 86 [17%]; P = .004), including relapse in 17 of 75 (23%) vs eight of 81 (10%) disease-free patients. 3-year failure-free survival was 86% vs 69% and 3-year OS 95% vs 86% (both P = .01); 4 vs 14 deaths. Median follow-up 4.1 years. Accrual stopped at 178 of a planned 300 after excess PVP16 recurrences at one institution; the interim analysis was not prespecified. No clinically significant pulmonary toxicity; severe nonhaematologic toxicity 8% vs 9%; grade 4 myelosuppression 14% vs 5% (P = .06); one drug-related sepsis death with PVP16B.
records.keywords: Loehrer et al. J Clin Oncol 1995;13:470-476  7531223

records.title: de Wit et al.
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — good prognosis · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2001
records.body: Metastatic germ cell cancer, nonseminoma or pure seminoma; chemotherapy-naive, IGCCC good prognosis; nonseminoma: testis or retroperitoneal primary, AFP <1,000 U/L, HCG <5,000 U/L, LDH <1.5 × ULN, no liver, bone, brain or other nonpulmonary visceral metastases; pure seminoma: stage ≥IIC (Royal Marsden) or relapse after radiotherapy, no liver, bone or brain metastases, any primary site; excluded age >65 years or creatinine clearance <40 mL/min 2 × 2 factorial; cycles: 3 cycles BEP (3BEP) vs 3 cycles BEP → 1 cycle EP (3BEP–1EP); schedule: 5-day (etoposide 100 mg/m² days 1-5, cisplatin 20 mg/m² days 1-5) vs 3-day (etoposide 165 mg/m² days 1-3, cisplatin 50 mg/m² days 1 and 2), same per-cycle totals of etoposide 500 mg/m² and cisplatin 100 mg/m²; bleomycin 30 mg weekly for 9 weeks (days 1, 8, 15 of cycles 1-3; total 270 mg) in all arms Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, complete response rate, no evidence of disease status, quality of life, toxicity Three cycles of BEP with etoposide 500 mg/m² were sufficient therapy in good-prognosis germ cell cancer, and giving the chemotherapy over 3 days had no detrimental effect on efficacy. Noninferiority and equivalence (5% margin, 80% CL) were claimed for both comparisons: 2-year PFS 90.4% for 3BEP vs 89.4% for 3BEP–1EP, difference -1.0% (80% CL -3.8% to +1.8%), HR 0.93; 89.7% for 3-day vs 88.8% for 5-day (80% CL for the difference -4.1% to +2.2%), HR 1.05. 2-year OS was 97.0% vs 97.1% for 3BEP vs 3BEP–1EP. Median follow-up was 25 months. QoL favoured 3 cycles, most at 3 months, with no difference at 1 year. Four cycles caused more acute and late sensory neuropathy; the 3-day schedule caused more nausea and late ototoxicity, without measurable audiometric hearing loss. Deaths included two from infection and one from pulmonary toxicity in each cycles arm, and three vs two treatment-related deaths on the 3-day vs 5-day schedule.
records.keywords: de Wit et al. J Clin Oncol 2001;19:1629-1640  11250991

records.title: MRC TE09/EORTC 30896
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — good prognosis · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 1997
records.body: Metastatic nonseminomatous germ cell tumour (histologically confirmed, or seminoma with unequivocally raised AFP) with testicular primary; first-line chemotherapy; good prognosis: abdominal mass at most 10 cm, supraclavicular/mediastinal masses at most 5 cm, <20 lung metastases, AFP <1,000 KU/L, HCG <10,000 IU/L, GFR >50 mL/min; no liver, bone or brain metastases BEP: bleomycin 30 U day 2, etoposide 120 mg/m² days 1–3, cisplatin 100 mg/m² total (20 mg/m²/d days 1–5 or 50 mg/m² days 1 and 2), every 21 days for four cycles vs CEB: same bleomycin and etoposide with carboplatin dosed from GFR to AUC 5 mg/mL x minutes (escalated in later cycles according to nadir counts), every 21 days for four cycles Primary: failure-free survival. Secondary: response to chemotherapy, overall survival, toxicity, renal function With these doses and schedules, carboplatin-based CEB was inferior to cisplatin-based BEP in this equivalence-designed trial; this BEP with moderate etoposide and bleomycin doses was effective. Treatment failures BEP 30/300 vs CEB 79/298; 1-yr failure-free rate 91% vs 77% (HR 2.75; 95% CI 1.88 to 4.03). Deaths 10 vs 27; 3-yr OS 97% vs 90% (HR 2.65; 95% CI 1.39 to 5.05). CR among assessable patients 253/268 (94.4%) vs 227/260 (87.3%; P = .009). The FFS difference was larger in stage III/IV, but heterogeneity by stage was not significant. CEB caused more thrombocytopenia (nadir platelets <50 x 10^9/L: 25 [12%] vs 2 [1%] with BEP); BEP caused more mild mucosal toxicity, sensory neuropathy and hearing loss and a small GFR fall (median 123 to 110 mL/min vs 120 with CEB). One early death occurred in each arm.
records.keywords: Horwich et al. J Clin Oncol 1997;15:1844-1852  9164194

records.title: GETUG T93BP
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — good prognosis · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2007
records.body: Histologically confirmed metastatic nonseminomatous germ-cell tumour, testicular or retroperitoneal primary, men only; chemotherapy-naive; good-risk by Institut Gustave Roussy prognostic model based on serum AFP and hCG levels, metastatic disease shown radiographically or by raised serum tumour markers; excluded: pure seminoma, no proof of metastasis, second primary tumour, poor-prognosis AFP/hCG features or primary mediastinal tumour Three cycles of BE500P: bleomycin 30 IU days 1, 8 and 15, etoposide 100 mg/m² days 1–5, cisplatin 20 mg/m² days 1–5, every 3 weeks vs four cycles of E500P: the same regimen without bleomycin, every 3 weeks; both arms → recommended resection of all residual supracentimetric masses, then two cycles of vinblastine, ifosfamide and cisplatin if viable cancer was found Primary: favorable response rate. Secondary: event-free survival, overall survival, toxicity In this equivalence trial, 3BE500P and 4E500P gave similar favorable response rates, with slightly different toxicity profiles. Favorable response was 94.7% (124/131) with 3BE500P vs 96.8% (122/126) with 4E500P (P = 0.34). The trial was underpowered for its secondary survival endpoints, and the authors note the trends may be due to chance: 4-year EFS 91% vs 86% (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.29–1.19; P = 0.135); 4-year OS 96% vs 92% (5 vs 12 deaths; HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.15–1.20; P = 0.096). The authors still call 3BE500P the treatment of choice, with 4E500P only if bleomycin is contraindicated. No toxic deaths occurred. Grade 3–4 neutropenia affected 72% vs 90% of patients. Grade 1+ neurologic (16% vs 5%) and dermatologic (29% vs 8%) toxicity were more frequent with 3BE500P. Pulmonary toxicity was 9% vs 6% (not significant).

records.title: Nichols et al.
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — intermediate & poor prognosis · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 1998
records.body: Men with disseminated germ cell tumors, all primary sites and histologic subtypes; previously untreated, advanced stage by Indiana classification: >10 pulmonary metastases per lung field or multiple pulmonary metastases >3 cm, primary mediastinal nonseminoma, palpable abdominal mass plus pulmonary metastases, or hepatic, osseous or CNS metastases; all ages and performance status eligible; excluded prior chemotherapy or creatinine above ULN unless due to obstructive uropathy BEP: etoposide 100 mg/m² IV days 1–5, cisplatin 20 mg/m² days 1–5, bleomycin 30 U IV weekly for 12 weeks vs VIP: etoposide 75 mg/m² days 1–5, ifosfamide 1.2 g/m² days 1–5 with mesna, cisplatin 20 mg/m² days 1–5; both every 3 weeks for four courses → resection of residual disease where feasible; patients with resected viable cancer received two additional courses of their arm's regimen (cisplatin and etoposide on the BEP arm) Complete response rate, favorable response rate, time to treatment failure, overall survival, toxicity Substituting ifosfamide for bleomycin (VIP) did not significantly improve favorable response, overall survival or time to treatment failure over BEP in advanced disseminated germ cell tumors and was more toxic; the authors conclude four courses of BEP remain standard. VIP vs BEP: complete response 37% vs 31% (P = .26); favorable response 63% vs 60%. Final analysis at median follow-up 7.3 years: PFS 64% vs 58%, OS 69% vs 67%; VIP may be an alternative with underlying pulmonary disease. Retrospective IGCCCG poor-risk subset (181, underpowered): 5-year OS 62% vs 57%, PFS 56% vs 49%, not significant. Grade 4 hematologic toxicity 60% vs 34% (P < .001); poor-risk grade 3–5 toxicity 93% vs 79% (P = 0.0002); grade 3 genitourinary (mostly renal) toxicity in eight vs one patients (P = .036). Treatment-related deaths: five on VIP (4 sepsis, 1 cerebral hemorrhage) and six on BEP, including three early pulmonary deaths. Late recurrence 4 of 286; one AML death after BEP.
records.keywords: Nichols et al. J Clin Oncol 1998;16:1287-1293  9552027 Hinton et al. Cancer 2003;97:1869-1875  12673712

records.title: GETUG-13
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — intermediate & poor prognosis · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2014
records.body: Poor-prognosis non-seminomatous germ-cell tumour (testicular, retroperitoneal or mediastinal); first-line, no prior chemotherapy; IGCCCG poor prognosis: primary mediastinal NSGCT, non-pulmonary visceral metastases and/or hCG > 50,000 UI/l, AFP > 10,000 ng/ml or LDH > 10-fold upper normal; randomised only if unfavourable AFP/hCG decline at day 18–21 after one BEP cycle; age >16 years; excluded HIV, prior malignancy except basal-cell carcinoma; no performance-status exclusion All: BEP cycle 1 (cisplatin 20 mg/m²/day IV × 5 days, etoposide 100 mg/m²/day IV × 5 days, bleomycin 30 mg IV/IM day 1, 8, 15) → favourable decline: 3 further BEP cycles (Fav-BEP, not randomised); unfavourable decline randomised: 3 further BEP cycles (Unfav-BEP) vs dose-dense: 2 cycles T-BEP-oxaliplatin (paclitaxel 175 mg/m² IV day 1 + BEP, oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 10; every 21 days) → 2 cycles cisplatin 100 mg/m² IV day 1, ifosfamide 2 g/m² IV days 10, 12, 14 + mesna, bleomycin 25 units/day continuous infusion day 10 to 14, with G-CSF Primary: progression-free survival.
