Secondary: overall survival, complete response rate, salvage high-dose chemotherapy with stem-cell transplant, toxicity, prognostic validation of tumour marker decline Dose-dense intensification reduced the risk of progression or death in poor-prognosis GCT with an unfavourable marker decline, but the PFS gain was borderline. 3-yr PFS dose-dense vs BEP 59% vs 48%; HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.44–1.00), p=0.05 (final nominal level 0.048). 3-yr OS 73% vs 65% was not significantly different (HR 0.78, 0.46–1.31; p=0.34). Salvage high-dose chemotherapy + stem-cell transplant 6% vs 16% (p=0.015); CR 40% vs 30% (p=0.12). Marker decline was prospectively validated as prognostic (non-randomised): Fav-BEP vs Unfav-BEP 3-yr PFS 70% vs 48%, OS 84% vs 65%. Early deaths before the 3-week marker assessment were excluded, which limits comparability. Dose-dense therapy caused more grade 3–4 neuropathy (7% vs 1%), haematotoxicity and auditory toxicity; febrile neutropenia 17% vs 18%; 1 toxic death per arm; six second malignancies (acute leukaemia in 5), all in mediastinal primaries.

records.title: Kondagunta et al. (MSKCC)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Relapsed / salvage therapy · Single-arm clinical trial · 2005
records.body: Testicular germ cell tumour (nonseminoma or seminoma), histologically confirmed advanced-stage progressive metastatic disease; second-line after failure to achieve a continuous CR to a prior platinum-based regimen; favourable features required: single prior program of six or fewer cisplatin cycles, gonadal primary, and CR or marker-negative PR for more than 6 months; late relapse (>2 years) and multiple sites allowed; prior paclitaxel or ifosfamide excluded (single-arm) TIP every 21 days for four cycles: paclitaxel 250 mg/m² IV 24-hour continuous infusion on day 1, then ifosfamide 1,500 mg/m² IV daily and cisplatin 25 mg/m² IV daily on days 2 to 5 (first 30 patients received the same doses as a 6-day regimen), with prophylactic G-CSF → resection of residual masses recommended if markers normalized Complete response rate, durable complete response rate, progression-free survival, overall survival, toxicity Four cycles of second-line TIP achieved a durable CR in a high proportion of patients with relapsed testicular GCT who were selected by favourable prognostic features; the study was single-arm, so it does not establish benefit over other regimens. CR in 32 of 46 (70%; 95% CI, 54% to 82%); 3 CRs relapsed; 29 (63%) continuously disease free at a median follow-up of 69 months. 2-year PFS 65% (95% CI, 51% to 79%); 2-year survival 78% (95% CI, 66% to 90%). Among 14 late-relapse patients, seven (50%) achieved CR with TIP plus resection, none relapsing at a median of 51 months. Myelosuppression predominated: neutropenic fever caused 26 hospitalizations in 22 patients (48%); three (7%) had grade 4 or 5 renal toxicity, including one treatment-related death from neutropenic sepsis with multiorgan failure; grade 3 neurotoxicity stopped treatment in two.
records.keywords: Kondagunta et al. J Clin Oncol 2005;23:6549-6555  16170162

records.title: Einhorn (Indiana) HDCT
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Relapsed / salvage therapy · Retrospective cohort study · 2007
records.body: Relapsed/refractory metastatic germ-cell tumours (mostly second-line) Two sequential cycles high-dose carboplatin + etoposide with PBSC rescue Durable complete remission Tandem high-dose carboplatin/etoposide gave durable disease-free status in 116/184 (63%), including 18/40 platinum-refractory patients. Established high-dose chemotherapy with stem-cell rescue as a curative salvage option.

records.title: TI-CE (Feldman, MSKCC)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Relapsed / salvage therapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2010
records.body: Relapsed germ-cell tumours with unfavourable salvage-risk features TI-CE: paclitaxel/ifosfamide then high-dose carboplatin/etoposide x3 + PBSC Disease-free survival TI-CE produced 5-yr DFS 47% and OS 52% in poor-risk relapse; mediastinal primary and >=2 prior lines predicted worse outcome. Validated TI-CE high-dose chemotherapy for unfavourable-risk salvage.

records.title: CLIMATE (ANZUP 1906)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Post-chemotherapy management & biomarkers · Observational cohort study · 2026
records.body: Clinical stage I testicular germ-cell tumour, post-orchidectomy MRD assessment Plasma miR-371a-3p detectable vs undetectable (observational cohort) Recurrence-free survival Detectable post-orchidectomy plasma miR-371a-3p strongly predicted relapse (HR 10.3, 95% CI 5.3-19.8; 20% of the cohort relapsed), outperforming conventional markers. Positions miR-371 as an MRD tool to refine adjuvant decisions (not yet standard of care).

records.title: RTOG 90-01 (Morris)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — concurrent chemoradiation (foundation) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 1999
records.body: High-risk locally advanced cervical cancer (FIGO IIB-IVA, or IB-IIA ≥5 cm/node+) Pelvic RT + concurrent cisplatin/5-FU vs extended-field (pelvic + para-aortic) RT Overall survival Concurrent chemoradiation improved 5-year OS (73% vs 58%, HR for death 0.52) and reduced local failure and distant metastases; helped establish cisplatin-based chemoradiation as standard.

records.title: GOG 120 (Rose)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — concurrent chemoradiation (foundation) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 1999
records.body: Locally advanced cervical cancer, FIGO IIB-IVA Cisplatin-based chemoradiation (cisplatin or cisplatin/5-FU/hydroxyurea) vs hydroxyurea + RT Progression-free survival Cisplatin-containing chemoradiation improved PFS and OS vs hydroxyurea (relative risk of progression 0.57 and 0.55 for the cisplatin arms); weekly cisplatin became the standard radiosensitizer.

records.title: GOG 123 (Keys)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — concurrent chemoradiation (foundation) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 1999
records.body: Bulky stage IB2 cervical carcinoma (tumor ≥4 cm), pre-hysterectomy Weekly cisplatin + RT vs RT alone, both followed by adjuvant hysterectomy Progression-free survival Adding weekly cisplatin to RT reduced risk of progression (RR 0.51) and death (RR 0.54), with significantly higher 4-year PFS and OS; cemented concurrent cisplatin for bulky early-stage disease.

records.title: CCCMAC (IPD meta-analysis)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — concurrent chemoradiation (foundation) · Meta-analysis · 2008
records.body: Locally advanced cervical cancer across 18 randomized chemoradiation trials (individual patient data) Concurrent chemoradiation vs radiotherapy alone Overall survival Chemoradiation improved 5-year OS by 6% (66% vs 60%, HR 0.81) and DFS by 8%, with benefit greatest for platinum-based regimens; confirmed chemoradiation as the standard of care.

records.title: OUTBACK (GOG-0274)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — treatment intensification · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body: Locally advanced cervical cancer after primary cisplatin-based chemoradiation Adjuvant carboplatin + paclitaxel after chemoradiation vs chemoradiation alone Overall survival Adjuvant chemotherapy did not improve 5-year OS (72% vs 71%, HR 0.90) and added toxicity; sequential adjuvant chemotherapy should not be given after chemoradiation.

records.title: INTERLACE (GCIG)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — treatment intensification · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Locally advanced cervical cancer (FIGO 2008 IB1 node+ to IVA) Induction weekly IV carboplatin AUC 2 + paclitaxel 80 mg/m² for 6 weeks, then standard cisplatin-based chemoradiation (weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² for 5 weeks concurrent with external-beam RT plus brachytherapy) vs the same chemoradiation alone Progression-free survival Short induction chemotherapy improved 5-year PFS (72% vs 64%, HR 0.65) and OS (80% vs 72%, HR 0.60); a feasible intensification using existing drugs.

records.title: KEYNOTE-A18 (ENGOT-cx11/GOG-3047)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — treatment intensification · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Newly diagnosed high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer (FIGO 2014 III-IVA, or IB2-IIB node+) Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W ×5 cycles concurrent with cisplatin-based chemoradiation (weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² + external-beam RT plus brachytherapy), then pembrolizumab 400 mg IV Q6W ×15 cycles vs placebo plus the same chemoradiation Progression-free survival Pembrolizumab added to chemoradiation met both dual primary endpoints, at two different interim analyses. At the first interim analysis progression-free survival improved (2-year PFS 68% vs 57%, HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.55-0.89, p=0.0020). All alpha then passed to overall survival, tested at the second interim analysis: HR 0.67 (95% CI 0.50-0.90; one-sided p=0.0040) against a prespecified boundary of 0.01026, on 75 deaths (14%) vs 109 (21%) at a 76.7% information fraction, median overall survival not reached in either group, 36-month OS 82.6% vs 74.8%; the paper calls this the final, formally tested overall survival result. Progression-free survival was not formally tested again there, so the more mature HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.56-0.84) reported alongside it carries no alpha and does not supersede the 0.70. Potentially immune-mediated adverse events 39% vs 17% (grade >=3 5% vs 1%); grade >=3 treatment-emergent events 78% vs 70%; two treatment-related deaths in each group. The authors conclude that the two analyses together support pembrolizumab plus chemoradiotherapy as a new standard of care.
records.keywords: Lancet 2024;403:1341-1350  38521086 Lancet 2024;404:1321-1332 overall survival results, second interim analysis 39288779

records.title: GOG 204 (Monk)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line chemotherapy & antiangiogenics · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2009
records.body: Stage IVB, recurrent, or persistent cervical carcinoma, first-line Cisplatin + paclitaxel vs cisplatin + vinorelbine, gemcitabine, or topotecan Overall survival No doublet was superior to cisplatin/paclitaxel (median OS ~12.9 months), with trends favoring it; established cisplatin/paclitaxel as the chemotherapy backbone.

records.title: GOG 240 (Tewari)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line chemotherapy & antiangiogenics · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2014
records.body: Recurrent, persistent, or metastatic cervical cancer, first-line Bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W + chemotherapy vs chemotherapy alone (2×2 factorial), chemo being cisplatin 50 mg/m² + paclitaxel 135–175 mg/m² or topotecan 0.75 mg/m² days 1–3 + paclitaxel 175 mg/m²; 21-day cycles to progression Overall survival Adding bevacizumab improved OS (17.0 vs 13.3 months, HR 0.71) and PFS (8.2 vs 5.9 months); the first antiangiogenic and first survival gain in this setting.

records.title: JCOG0505 (Kitagawa)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line chemotherapy & antiangiogenics · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2015
records.body: Metastatic or recurrent cervical cancer, first-line (Japan; JCOG) Paclitaxel + carboplatin (TC) vs paclitaxel + cisplatin (TP) Overall survival (non-inferiority) Non-inferiority met: median OS 17.5 (TC) vs 18.3 (TP) months (HR 0.994, 90% CI 0.789-1.253). In cisplatin-naive patients OS favoured TP (23.2 vs 13.0 months). Established carboplatin-paclitaxel as a convenient standard except in cisplatin-naive disease.

records.title: KEYNOTE-826 (Colombo)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body: Persistent, recurrent, or metastatic cervical cancer, first-line Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W to 35 cycles + platinum doublet (paclitaxel 175 mg/m² + cisplatin 50 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5, capped at 6 cycles) ± bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W (investigator's discretion) vs placebo + the same chemotherapy ± bevacizumab Progression-free and overall survival Pembrolizumab improved PFS (10.4 vs 8.2 months, HR 0.65) and OS (HR 0.67; final median 26.4 vs 16.8 months); established first-line chemo-immunotherapy.

records.title: BEATcc (Oaknin)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Metastatic, persistent, or recurrent cervical cancer, first-line Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV Q3W added to bevacizumab 15 mg/kg + platinum–paclitaxel (cisplatin 50 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5 + paclitaxel 175 mg/m², day 1 Q3W) vs the same bevacizumab + platinum–paclitaxel alone; treatment to progression or toxicity Progression-free survival Atezolizumab improved PFS (13.7 vs 10.4 months, HR 0.62) and OS (32.1 vs 22.8 months, HR 0.68); a bevacizumab-containing chemo-immunotherapy option regardless of PD-L1.

records.title: COMPASSION-16
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Untreated persistent, recurrent, or metastatic cervical cancer (China; regardless of PD-L1) Cadonilimab (PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific) + platinum chemotherapy +/- bevacizumab vs placebo + chemotherapy +/- bevacizumab Progression-free and overall survival (dual) At prespecified interim analyses, cadonilimab improved PFS (12.7 vs 8.1 months, stratified HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.49–0.80, p<0.0001 against a boundary of 0.0005) and OS (not reached vs 22.8 months, HR 0.64, 0.48–0.86, p=0.0011 against 0.006), the OS interim firing at 193 of the 290 deaths required for the final analysis. Bevacizumab was optional and used by 60%; the trial reports both strata with no interaction test — without bevacizumab PFS HR 0.46 (0.32–0.66) and OS 0.50 (0.33–0.75), with bevacizumab 0.81 (0.58–1.13) and 0.84 (0.56–1.26) — and the authors conclude benefit “regardless of the use of bevacizumab”, speculating only that it might suit those not eligible for it. No treatment-by-PD-L1 interaction test is reported either, so PD-L1 consistency is directional only. Conducted wholly in China; adverse events led to discontinuation in 28% vs 11%. At publication the NMPA approval covered cadonilimab monotherapy at second line or later, not this first-line combination.

records.title: KEYNOTE-158 (Chung)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — second-line immunotherapy & ADCs · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2019
records.body: Previously treated advanced cervical cancer (cervical cohort) Single-arm pembrolizumab monotherapy Objective response rate ORR 14.3% overall and 14.6% in PD-L1+ (CPS ≥1) tumors with durable responses; led to accelerated approval for PD-L1+ pretreated disease.

records.title: EMPOWER-Cervical 1 (GOG-3016)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — second-line immunotherapy & ADCs · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body: Recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer after first-line platinum Cemiplimab vs investigator's-choice single-agent chemotherapy Overall survival Cemiplimab improved OS (12.0 vs 8.5 months, HR 0.69) regardless of PD-L1 or histology; validated checkpoint blockade as a second-line standard.

records.title: innovaTV 204 (GOG-3023/ENGOT-cx6)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — second-line immunotherapy & ADCs · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2021
records.body: Previously treated recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer Single-arm tisotumab vedotin (tissue factor-directed ADC) Objective response rate Confirmed ORR 24% (7% complete) with median DOR 8.3 months; supported accelerated approval of the first ADC in cervical cancer.

records.title: innovaTV 301 (ENGOT-cx12)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — second-line immunotherapy & ADCs · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer after 1-2 prior lines Tisotumab vedotin (tissue factor-directed ADC) 2.0 mg/kg IV Q3W vs investigator's-choice single-agent chemotherapy (topotecan, vinorelbine, gemcitabine, irinotecan, or pemetrexed); to progression Overall survival Tisotumab vedotin improved OS (11.5 vs 9.5 months, HR 0.70) and PFS (4.2 vs 2.9 months); confirmatory phase 3 converting accelerated to full approval.

records.title: CheckMate 358 (Oaknin)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — second-line immunotherapy & ADCs · Randomised clinical trial (phase I/II) · 2024
records.body: Recurrent or metastatic squamous cell cervical carcinoma, ≤2 prior systemic therapies (first- and later-line) Nivolumab 240 mg IV Q2W (monotherapy); or nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV Q6W; or nivolumab 1 mg/kg IV Q3W + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 → nivolumab 240 mg IV Q2W; treatment to progression, toxicity, or 24 months Investigator-assessed objective response rate Multicohort phase 1–2 trial (176 treated of 193 enrolled; 90 randomised between the two combination regimens): objective response rate 26% (5/19) with nivolumab monotherapy, 31% (14/45) with NIVO3+IPI1, and 38% (43/112) with pooled NIVO1+IPI3 (40% in the randomised NIVO1+IPI3 group), with durable responses seen regardless of PD-L1 status. Serious treatment-related AEs were 16%, 27%, and 42% respectively, with one treatment-related death (immune-mediated colitis). Signal-generating support for chemotherapy-free dual immunotherapy; no randomised comparator arm, so hypothesis-generating rather than practice-defining.

records.title: EORTC 55971 (Vergote)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Primary surgery — debulking extent & chemotherapy timing · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2010
records.body: Stage IIIC or IV invasive epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal or fallopian-tube carcinoma; first-line, before primary debulking surgery or chemotherapy; biopsy-proven, or FNA adenocarcinoma with pelvic mass, extrapelvic metastases ≥2 cm, nodal metastasis or proven stage IV and CA-125:CEA ratio >25 (if ≤25, negative GI workup and mammography); WHO PS 0–2, no resectability selection; excluded serious disabling disease contraindicating cytoreductive surgery or platinum chemotherapy Neoadjuvant platinum-based chemotherapy ×3 courses → interval debulking surgery (if response or stable disease) → ≥3 further courses of platinum-based chemotherapy vs primary debulking surgery → ≥6 courses of platinum-based chemotherapy Primary: overall survival. Secondary: adverse effects, quality of life, progression-free survival, postoperative morbidity, postoperative mortality, residual tumour size Neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval debulking was non-inferior to primary debulking followed by chemotherapy in bulky stage IIIC or IV ovarian carcinoma; complete resection of all macroscopic disease remains the surgical objective. ITT HR for death NACT vs PDS 0.98 (90% CI 0.84–1.13; P=0.01 for non-inferiority, margin <1.25); median OS 30 vs 29 mo; median PFS 12 mo in both (HR 1.01, 90% CI 0.89–1.15); median follow-up 4.7 yr. Residual tumour ≤1 cm in 80.6% after interval vs 41.6% after primary debulking; no residual tumour was the strongest independent OS predictor (post hoc). Post hoc, patients with metastases <5 cm at randomization had longer OS with PDS (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.45–0.93). No significant QLQ-C30 global health difference. Postoperative death 2.5% after PDS vs 0.7% with NACT; grade 3/4 haemorrhage 7.4% vs 4.1%, infection 8.1% vs 1.7%, venous complications 2.6% vs 0% (not formally compared).
records.keywords: Vergote et al. N Engl J Med 2010;363:943-953  20818904

records.title: CHORUS
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Primary surgery — debulking extent & chemotherapy timing · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2015
records.body: Newly diagnosed suspected advanced ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer; first-line treatment; pelvic mass with extrapelvic disease compatible with FIGO 1988 stage III or IV on clinical or imaging evidence, fit for surgery and chemotherapy; serum CA125:CEA ratio >25 (if less, gastrointestinal carcinoma excluded before entry); histological/cytological confirmation not required before randomisation Primary debulking surgery → 6 cycles of chemotherapy (interval debulking allowed if >1 cm residual disease) vs 3 cycles of primary chemotherapy → delayed surgery → 3 cycles of completion chemotherapy; chemotherapy every 3 weeks: carboplatin AUC5 or AUC6 + paclitaxel 175 mg/m², another carboplatin combination, or carboplatin AUC5 or AUC6 alone, prespecified per patient before randomisation Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, quality of life, adverse events, residual disease after debulking, postoperative death within 28 days In women with stage III or IV ovarian cancer, overall survival with primary chemotherapy was non-inferior to primary surgery, and surgical morbidity and mortality were lower. Median ITT OS was 22·6 mo with primary surgery vs 24·1 mo with primary chemotherapy; HR 0·87 (95% CI 0·72–1·05), with the upper bound of the one-sided 90% CI at 0·98, below the 1·18 margin. Median PFS was 10·7 vs 12·0 mo; HR 0·91 (95% CI 0·76–1·09). Survival was lower than predicted (3-year OS 32% vs 34%), and CHORUS alone had 65% power. Residual disease <1 cm: 41% vs 73%. Global quality of life was slightly higher with primary chemotherapy at 6 and 12 months; the 12-month 95% CI crossed zero (–13·6 to 2·3). Grade 3–4 postoperative adverse events occurred in 24% vs 14% and deaths within 28 days of surgery in 6% vs <1%. Grade 3–4 chemotherapy toxicity occurred in 49% vs 40%, with one fatal neutropenic sepsis in the primary-chemotherapy group.
records.keywords: Kehoe et al. Lancet 2015 (online ahead of print)

records.title: SCORPION
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Primary surgery — debulking extent & chemotherapy timing · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body: Advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer; presumed FIGO stage IIIC or IV, chemotherapy naïve, upfront; high tumour load at staging laparoscopy: PI score between 8 and 12 and absence of mesenteric retraction, with metastatic disease presumed completely resectable on imaging; aged 18 to 75 years, ECOG 0–2; excluded pregnancy/breast-feeding or other invasive malignancy in the previous 5 years Primary debulking surgery aiming for R0 (no secondary cytoreduction if residual >1 cm) → six cycles carboplatin AUC 5 + paclitaxel 175 mg/m² (every three weeks or weekly) vs neoadjuvant carboplatin/paclitaxel for three or four cycles → interval debulking surgery if stable/responding disease, after 3 or 4 weeks of rest (not allowed on progression) → chemotherapy to complete six cycles; bevacizumab with chemotherapy and as maintenance allowed in both arms from January 2014 Primary: peri-operative morbidity, progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, quality of life, complete resection rate, surgical complexity, operative time, hospital stay In patients with high tumour load, neoadjuvant chemotherapy did not improve PFS over primary debulking surgery, so the PFS superiority co-primary failed, but it substantially reduced peri-operative morbidity. ITT, median follow-up 59 months: median PFS 15 (PDS) vs 14 months (NACT), HR 1.05 (95% CI 0.77 to 1.44; p=0.73); median OS 41 vs 43 months, HR 1.12 (95% CI 0.76 to 1.65). The trial was underpowered (66% power for HR 0.67), so equivalence is not established; the authors call the study hypothesis generating. Per protocol, R0 was 47.6% vs 77.0%, and early major complications occurred in 46.4% vs 9.5% of patients. Seven of 84 (8.3%) PDS patients died of post-operative complications vs none after IDS. In an exploratory analysis, residual tumour was the main prognostic factor. QoL results are not reported.
records.keywords: Fagotti et al. Int J Gynecol Cancer 2020;30:1657-1664  33028623

records.title: LION
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Primary surgery — debulking extent & chemotherapy timing · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body: Newly diagnosed advanced epithelial ovarian cancer, FIGO stage IIB–IV (stage IV only with resectable metastases in pleura, liver, spleen or abdominal wall); primary surgery; intraoperative randomization only after macroscopically complete resection with normal lymph nodes both before and during surgery; age 18–75, ECOG 0–1; excluded: any macroscopically involved (bulky) nodes or residual tumour Systematic pelvic and paraaortic lymphadenectomy after macroscopically complete primary resection vs no lymphadenectomy (no node resection permitted) Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30, QLQ-OV28), number of resected lymph nodes, postoperative complications Systematic pelvic and paraaortic lymphadenectomy after macroscopically complete resection with clinically negative nodes was not associated with longer OS or PFS than no lymphadenectomy and increased postoperative complications. Median OS 65.5 vs 69.2 mo (HR for death 1.06; 95% CI 0.83–1.34; P=0.65); median PFS 25.5 mo in both groups (HR 1.11; 95% CI 0.92–1.34); per-protocol analysis concordant. No benefit despite microscopic nodal metastases in 55.7% of the lymphadenectomy group. No clinically meaningful QoL differences. Randomized patients were highly selected (650 of 1895 registered). Lymphadenectomy vs none: repeat laparotomy 12.4% vs 6.5%, 60-day mortality 3.1% vs 0.9% (all deaths within 30 days), infections treated with antibiotics 25.8% vs 18.6%, symptomatic lymph cysts 3.1% vs 0; median surgery duration 340 vs 280 min.
records.keywords: Harter et al. N Engl J Med 2019;380:822-832  30811909

records.title: JCOG0602
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Primary surgery — debulking extent & chemotherapy timing · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body: Ovarian, tubal or peritoneal cancer; FIGO (1988) stage III or IV diagnosed clinically by imaging and cytology of ascites, pleural effusion or tumour-centesis fluid, without diagnostic laparoscopy/laparotomy; CA125 >200 U/ml and CEA <20 ng/ml; age 20–75 years, ECOG PS 0–3; breast or digestive-tract primaries excluded by endoscopy, opaque enema or ultrasonography when suspected PDS → eight cycles of paclitaxel 175 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 6 on day 1 every 3 weeks; IDS allowed for residual tumour >1 cm and mandatory if the uterus, adnexa or omentum was not removed, unless progression vs four cycles of neoadjuvant paclitaxel + carboplatin (same doses) → IDS unless progression → four cycles of postoperative paclitaxel + carboplatin Primary: overall survival. Secondary: adverse events, frequency of surgery, duration of surgery, amount of blood loss, frequency of blood infusions, frequency of plasma infusions, frequency of albumin infusions, surgical procedures performed, optimal debulking rate, treatment completion, treatment-related deaths NAC followed by IDS was less invasive than PDS-based standard therapy. The authors say NAC may become standard only if non-inferior survival is confirmed in the planned 2017 primary analysis, and overall survival is not reported here. NACT vs STDT: fewer surgeries (mean 0.86 vs 1.32), shorter total operation time (median 273 vs 341 min), and less abdominal organ resection (23.7% vs 37.6%) and distant metastasis resection (3.9% vs 10.7%). IDS vs PDS: smaller blood/ascites loss (median 787 vs 3235 ml), less albumin transfusion (26.2% vs 58.5%) and fewer grade 3–4 adverse events after surgery (4.6% vs 15.0%). However, IDS took longer (median 302 vs 240 min), with more pelvic (72.3% vs 27.2%) and para-aortic (49.2% vs 11.6%) lymphadenectomy. Treatment-related deaths: 2 (1.3%) STDT vs 1 (0.7%) NACT. The trial was open-label and quality of life was not assessed.
records.keywords: Onda et al. Eur J Cancer 2016;64:22-31  27323348

records.title: GOG-0213
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Secondary cytoreductive surgery (platinum-sensitive relapse) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body: Platinum-sensitive recurrent epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal or fallopian-tube cancer; recurrence after one previous therapy, with complete clinical response to at least three cycles of primary platinum-based chemotherapy and platinum-free interval ≥6 months; measurable disease (RECIST 1.0) investigator-deemed amenable to complete gross resection; excluded: unfit for surgery, diffuse carcinomatosis, ascites or extraabdominal disease Secondary surgical cytoreduction within 4 weeks of registration (goal: no gross residuum) → platinum-based chemotherapy vs platinum-based chemotherapy alone; chemotherapy in both arms: paclitaxel 175 mg per square meter + carboplatin AUC 5 IV every 3 weeks for six cycles, or (after August 2011 amendment) gemcitabine 1000 mg per square meter days 1 and 8 + carboplatin AUC 4 every 3 weeks for six cycles, each without or with bevacizumab 15 mg/kg every 3 weeks, then bevacizumab maintenance 15 mg/kg every 3 weeks until progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, 30-day surgical morbidity, 30-day surgical mortality, treatment-related adverse events, quality of life (FACT-O TOI), physical functioning (RAND 36-item Short Form Survey), surgery-related symptoms, complete gross resection rate Secondary surgical cytoreduction followed by chemotherapy did not result in longer OS than chemotherapy alone in platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian cancer. OS HR (surgery vs no surgery) 1.29 (95% CI 0.97–1.72; P=0.08); median 50.6 vs 64.7 mo at 48.1 mo median follow-up (197 deaths, 79% maturity; results released after the interim futility boundary was crossed). PFS was numerically longer but not superior: HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.66–1.01); median 18.9 vs 16.2 mo. Complete gross resection was achieved in 67% (150 of 224) of operated patients; in an ad hoc exploratory analysis, complete resection vs the entire no-surgery group showed no OS benefit (HR 1.03; 95% CI 0.74–1.46). 84% received bevacizumab-containing chemotherapy with maintenance. Quality of life fell significantly after surgery but reached parity by 6 weeks. 30-day grade ≥3 surgery-related morbidity 9% (20/225); 1 postoperative death (0.4%).
records.keywords: Coleman et al. N Engl J Med 2019;381:1929-1939  31722153

records.title: DESKTOP III
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Secondary cytoreductive surgery (platinum-sensitive relapse) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body: Relapsed epithelial ovarian cancer; first relapse after a platinum-free interval of 6 months or more (platinum-sensitive; stratified 6 to 12 vs >12 months), diagnosed histologically or radiologically; positive AGO score: ECOG PS 0, ascites of less than 500 ml and complete resection at initial surgery; an elevated CA-125 level alone not acceptable for entry Secondary cytoreductive surgery → physician's choice of platinum-based chemotherapy vs physician's choice of platinum-based chemotherapy alone; combination therapy strongly recommended, single agent allowed Primary: overall survival. Secondary: quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30, FACT-General, FACT-Ovarian, FACT-Ovarian Symptom Index), progression-free survival, complete resection as a prognostic factor, complications associated with surgery up to 60 days, surgical characteristics, applied chemotherapy, perioperative mortality In recurrent ovarian cancer with a positive AGO score, secondary cytoreductive surgery followed by chemotherapy resulted in longer overall survival than chemotherapy alone. Final ITT analysis after 254 deaths (median follow-up 69.8 mo): median OS 53.7 vs 46.0 mo (HR 0.75; 95% CI 0.59–0.96; P = 0.02); median PFS 18.4 vs 14.0 mo (HR 0.66; 95% CI 0.54–0.82). Complete resection in 75.5% (145 of 192) of operated patients; median OS 61.9 mo with vs 27.7 mo without complete resection (non-randomized comparison). Quality of life did not differ through 12 mo; insomnia and constipation favoured no surgery at 6 mo, when more surgery-group patients were still on chemotherapy. Open-label, not placebo-controlled; CIs not adjusted for multiplicity; 32 of 201 (15.9%) no-surgery patients crossed over to surgery at relapse. No deaths within 30 days after surgery; reoperation 3.7% (7 of 191).
records.keywords: Harter et al. N Engl J Med 2021;385:2123-2131  34874631

records.title: SOC-1
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Secondary cytoreductive surgery (platinum-sensitive relapse) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body: Platinum-sensitive relapsed epithelial ovarian cancer; first relapse, platinum-free interval ≥6 months after first-line platinum-based chemotherapy, no more than one prior chemotherapy line; predicted completely resectable by iMODEL score ≤4.7 plus PET-CT (amendment: iMODEL >4.7 allowed if CA125 >105 U/mL and investigators judged disease resectable on PET-CT); excluded comorbidity contraindicating surgery or chemotherapy Secondary cytoreductive surgery within 4 weeks of randomisation → IV chemotherapy (six 3-weekly cycles of paclitaxel 175 mg/m² or docetaxel 75 mg/m² plus carboplatin AUC 5; 2–3 additional cycles allowed for partial response) vs the same chemotherapy alone started within 4 weeks of randomisation; targeted maintenance (bevacizumab or PARP inhibitor) allowed Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: accumulating treatment-free survival, overall survival adjusted for one-way treatment switching, safety, quality of life, predictive and prognostic value of the iMODEL score, patient compliance, time to first subsequent anticancer therapy, time to second subsequent anticancer therapy, complete resection rate, 30-day surgical complications, 60-day mortality Secondary cytoreduction followed by chemotherapy was associated with significantly longer PFS than chemotherapy alone in platinum-sensitive relapsed ovarian cancer selected by iMODEL and PET-CT; the authors advise counselling about surgery in specialised centres. Median PFS was 17.4 vs 11.9 mo (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.45–0.74; p<0.0001); 2-year PFS was 38% vs 22%. Interim OS (105 deaths) was immature and showed no difference: median 58.1 vs 53.9 mo (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.57–1.19). Of 130 no-surgery patients who relapsed, 48 (37%) crossed over to surgery, which the authors call the major limitation. Time to first subsequent therapy was 18.1 vs 13.6 mo (HR 0.59). Complete resection was achieved in 132 (77%) of 172 operated patients. Quality of life did not differ. Grade 3–4 surgical morbidity at 30 days occurred in 5% (nine of 172). Grade ≥3 chemotherapy AEs: 25% vs 20%. No patient died within 60 days and there were no treatment-related deaths.

records.title: GOG 111 (McGuire)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 1996
records.body: Stage III epithelial ovarian cancer with >1 cm residual disease after surgery or stage IV disease; no prior ovarian cancer chemotherapy; GOG PS 0–2 Cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m² plus cisplatin 75 mg/m² q3w for 6 cycles vs paclitaxel 135 mg/m² over 24 h → cisplatin 75 mg/m² q3w for 6 cycles progression-free survival, overall survival, clinical response, pathological response, toxicity Paclitaxel/cisplatin improved PFS (18 vs 13 mo; RR 0.7, 95% CI 0.5–0.8) and OS (38 vs 24 mo; RR 0.6, 95% CI 0.5–0.8) in the eligible randomized population. Clinical response among measurable disease was 73% vs 60%. Severe neutropenia, febrile neutropenia, alopecia and neuropathy were more frequent with paclitaxel/cisplatin

records.title: GOG 158 (Ozols)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2003
records.body: Optimally resected stage III epithelial ovarian cancer with no residual nodule >1 cm; no prior ovarian cancer chemotherapy; GOG PS 0–2 Cisplatin 75 mg/m² plus paclitaxel 135 mg/m² q3w for 6 cycles vs carboplatin AUC7.5 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m² q3w for 6 cycles Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: toxicity, second-look laparotomy results Carboplatin/paclitaxel was noninferior to cisplatin/paclitaxel for PFS (20.7 vs 19.4 mo; RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.75–1.03), with OS 57.4 vs 48.7 mo (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.70–1.02). Carboplatin increased grade 3–4 thrombocytopenia (19%/20% vs 3%/2%), whereas cisplatin increased gastrointestinal, metabolic and genitourinary toxicity

records.title: GOG 172 (Armstrong)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2006
records.body: Previously untreated stage III epithelial ovarian or primary peritoneal carcinoma after primary surgery with residual disease ≤1 cm; GOG PS 0–2 Paclitaxel 135 mg/m² IV over 24 h day 1 → cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV day 2 q3w for 6 cycles vs paclitaxel 135 mg/m² IV over 24 h day 1 → cisplatin 100 mg/m² IP day 2 plus paclitaxel 60 mg/m² IP day 8 q3w for 6 cycles Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: quality of life Intraperitoneal therapy improved PFS (23.8 vs 18.3 mo; RR 0.80, 95% CI 0.64–1.00) and OS (65.6 vs 49.7 mo; RR 0.75, 95% CI 0.58–0.97) among eligible patients. Only 42% received all assigned IP therapy; grade 3–4 gastrointestinal, neurologic, fatigue, metabolic, pain and infection events were more common, and 9 treatment-related deaths occurred (5 IP, 4 IV)

records.title: JGOG 3016 (Katsumata)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2009
records.body: Previously untreated FIGO II–IV epithelial ovarian, fallopian-tube or primary peritoneal cancer; ECOG 0–3; low-malignant-potential tumours and recent/active other malignancy excluded Paclitaxel 180 mg/m² IV over 3 h plus carboplatin AUC6 IV day 1 q3w for 6 cycles vs paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV over 1 h days 1, 8 and 15 plus carboplatin AUC6 IV day 1 q3w for 6 cycles; 3 additional cycles for measurable-disease CR/PR after 6 cycles Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, response rate, adverse events Dose-dense paclitaxel improved PFS (28.0 vs 17.2 mo; HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.58–0.88) in eligible ITT patients. Three-year OS was 72.1% vs 65.1% (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.57–0.98), but OS was a secondary interim analysis. Grade 3–4 anaemia was more frequent (69% vs 44%), and toxicity caused more discontinuations

records.title: MITO-7 (Pignata)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2014
records.body: Chemotherapy-naive FIGO IC–IV epithelial ovarian, fallopian-tube or primary peritoneal cancer after initial surgery/staging; ECOG ≤2; excluded clinically relevant heart disease, contraindicating disorders, prior chemotherapy, or other malignancy Carboplatin AUC6 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m² q3w for 6 cycles vs carboplatin AUC2 plus paclitaxel 60 mg/m² weekly for 18 weeks Primary: progression-free survival, quality of life. Secondary: overall survival, toxic effects, objective response Weekly treatment did not improve PFS (18.3 vs 17.3 mo; HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.80–1.16); interim 24-month OS was also not improved. It produced more favourable quality-of-life trajectories and reduced grade 3–4 neutropenia (42% vs 50%), febrile neutropenia (0.5% vs 3%), thrombocytopenia (1% vs 7%), grade ≥2 neuropathy (6% vs 17%) and grade 2 alopecia (29% vs 59%); 3 chemotherapy-attributed deaths occurred

records.title: GOG-262 (Chan)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body: Newly diagnosed untreated incompletely resected stage III or stage IV epithelial ovarian, fallopian-tube or primary peritoneal cancer; later stage II/III with residual lesions ≤1 cm permitted; GOG PS 0–2 Paclitaxel 175 mg/m² plus carboplatin AUC6 q3w for 6 cycles vs paclitaxel 80 mg/m² days 1, 8 and 15 plus carboplatin AUC6 day 1 q3w for 6 cycles; optional bevacizumab from cycle 2 until progression Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: quality of life, toxic effects, overall survival Weekly paclitaxel did not improve PFS overall (14.7 vs 14.0 mo; HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.74–1.06). Among the 16% who elected no bevacizumab, the randomized weekly comparison favoured PFS (14.2 vs 10.3 mo; HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.40–0.95), with interaction P=0.047; nonrandomized bevacizumab choice limits inference. Weekly therapy caused more grade 3–4 anaemia and grade 2–4 neuropathy but less neutropenia; 14 deaths were considered at least possibly treatment related (6 vs 8)

records.title: ICON8 (Clamp)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body: FIGO IC–IV epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal or fallopian-tube cancer; stage IC/IIA required high-risk histology; ECOG 0–2; primary, delayed, or no surgery permitted Carboplatin AUC5/6 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m² q3w for 6 cycles vs carboplatin q3w plus paclitaxel 80 mg/m² days 1, 8 and 15 q3w for 6 cycles vs weekly carboplatin AUC2 plus paclitaxel 80 mg/m² days 1, 8 and 15 q3w for 6 cycles Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: quality of life, toxic effects Neither weekly dose-dense regimen improved PFS over q3w treatment; restricted mean PFS was 24.9 and 25.3 vs 24.4 mo, with median PFS 20.8 and 21.0 vs 17.7 mo. Grade 3–4 toxicity was higher with weekly schedules (62% and 53% vs 42%), and longitudinal quality of life favoured q3w treatment

records.title: GOG 218 (Burger)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line antiangiogenic therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2011
records.body: Previously untreated, incompletely resectable stage III epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer after maximal debulking, with residual disease >1 cm initially and residual disease ≤1 cm permitted after amendment, or stage IV disease; GOG PS 0–2; no intestinal obstruction or clinically significant vascular-event history Carboplatin AUC6 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m² q3w for 6 cycles plus placebo through cycle 22 vs chemotherapy plus bevacizumab 15 mg/kg q3w cycles 2–6 then placebo vs chemotherapy plus bevacizumab 15 mg/kg q3w cycles 2–22; stop for progression, toxicity, completion, or withdrawal Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, quality of life, adverse events Bevacizumab throughout chemotherapy and maintenance improved PFS versus control (14.1 vs 10.3 mo; HR 0.717, 95% CI 0.625–0.824), whereas initiation only did not. OS was not improved at this cut. Bevacizumab increased grade ≥2 hypertension (22.9% vs 7.2%), gastrointestinal-wall disruption and grade ≥3 proteinuria; fatal adverse events were reported without treatment-causality attribution

records.title: ICON7 (Perren)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line antiangiogenic therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2011
records.body: High-risk early-stage (FIGO I–IIA clear-cell or grade 3) or FIGO IIB–IV epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer after surgery; ECOG 0–2; no further surgery planned Carboplatin AUC5/6 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m² q3w for 6 cycles vs the same chemotherapy plus bevacizumab 7.5 mg/kg IV q3w for 5–6 cycles → 12 additional cycles or until progression Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: biologic progression-free interval, response, toxicity, quality of life Bevacizumab modestly prolonged first-line PFS by 36-month restricted mean (21.8 vs 20.3 mo; difference 1.5 mo, 95% CI 0.1–2.9); the conventional HR was not meaningful because hazards were nonproportional. Updated OS was immature and not improved. Bevacizumab increased grade ≥2 hypertension (18% vs 2%), grade ≥3 thromboembolism (7% vs 3%), gastrointestinal perforation and treatment-related/treatment-and-disease deaths

records.title: SOLO-1 (Moore)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line maintenance — PARP inhibitors · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body: Newly diagnosed FIGO III–IV high-grade serous or endometrioid ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer with germline or somatic BRCA1/2 mutation and complete/partial response after platinum chemotherapy without bevacizumab Olaparib tablets 300 mg orally twice daily until investigator-assessed progression; stop at 2 years if no evidence of disease, with blinded continuation permitted for partial response vs matching placebo on the same rule Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: second progression-free survival, overall survival, time to first and second subsequent therapy or death, quality of life Maintenance olaparib markedly prolonged investigator-assessed PFS (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.23–0.41; 3-year freedom from progression/death 60% vs 27%) in BRCA-mutated disease. OS was interim at 21% maturity. Anaemia was more common (grade 3–4, 22% vs 2%); AML occurred in 3/260 olaparib recipients, all >30 days after treatment ended

records.title: PRIMA (González-Martín)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line maintenance — PARP inhibitors · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body: Newly diagnosed high-risk FIGO III–IV high-grade serous or endometrioid ovarian, peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer after response to first-line platinum; stage III required visible residual disease after primary debulking or inoperability, and neoadjuvant chemotherapy was permitted Niraparib orally once daily in 28-day cycles for 36 months or until progression; 300 mg initially, amended to 200 mg for baseline weight <77 kg or platelets <150,000/mm³ vs matched placebo on the same duration rule Primary: progression-free survival in HRD population, progression-free survival in overall population. Secondary: overall survival, time to first subsequent therapy, second progression-free survival, quality of life, safety Niraparib prolonged centrally reviewed PFS in HRD disease (21.9 vs 10.4 mo; HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.31–0.59) and overall (13.8 vs 8.2 mo; HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.50–0.76). OS was immature at 79 deaths. Grade ≥3 anaemia, thrombocytopenia and neutropenia were 31.0%, 28.7% and 12.8% vs 1.6%, 0.4% and 1.2%; adverse events caused dose reduction in 70.9% vs 8.2% and discontinuation in 12.0% vs 2.5%. An individualized starting dose was added during the study

records.title: PAOLA-1 (Ray-Coquard)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line maintenance — PARP inhibitors · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body: Adults with newly diagnosed FIGO III–IV high-grade serous or endometrioid ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer, or other nonmucinous epithelial ovarian cancer with deleterious germline BRCA1/2 mutation; no evidence of disease or complete/partial response after platinum–taxane plus bevacizumab Olaparib 300 mg orally twice daily for up to 24 months plus bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV q3w for up to 15 months total, until progression, toxicity or other discontinuation vs matching placebo plus bevacizumab on the same duration rules Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, second progression-free survival, time to first subsequent therapy, quality of life, safety Adding olaparib to bevacizumab maintenance improved PFS overall (22.1 vs 16.6 mo; HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.49–0.72). The prespecified HRD-positive subgroup also had longer PFS (37.2 vs 17.7 mo; HR 0.33), but no interaction test established differential benefit; a post hoc HRD-negative-or-unknown analysis did not establish benefit (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.72–1.17). Grade ≥3 anaemia was 17% vs <1%, and MDS/AML/aplastic anaemia occurred in 1% vs <1%; quality of life was maintained

records.title: ATHENA-MONO (Monk)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line maintenance — PARP inhibitors · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body: Newly diagnosed stage III–IV high-grade epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer after response to platinum doublet; R0 resection was permitted Rucaparib 600 mg orally twice daily from cycle 1 day 1 vs placebo; each in 28-day cycles with IV placebo q4w from cycle 2 day 1, until 24 months after IV-placebo initiation, progression, death, or unacceptable toxicity Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response, duration of response, quality of life, safety Rucaparib improved investigator-assessed PFS in the ITT population (20.2 vs 9.2 mo; HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.40–0.68) and HRD-positive disease. OS data were immature. Grade ≥3 anaemia and neutropenia were more common, and treatment interruption/reduction was frequent

records.title: DUO-O
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line maintenance — PARP inhibitors · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Treatment-naive, newly diagnosed FIGO III–IV high-grade epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer lacking a deleterious or suspected deleterious tumour BRCA mutation; planned platinum chemotherapy plus bevacizumab after upfront surgery or before interval debulking Carboplatin AUC5–6 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m² q3w for 6 cycles with bevacizumab 15 mg/kg q3w → bevacizumab to 15 months vs the same plus durvalumab 1120 mg IV q3w → durvalumab to 24 months plus bevacizumab to 15 months vs the same plus durvalumab → durvalumab and olaparib 300 mg twice daily to 24 months plus bevacizumab to 15 months Primary: progression-free survival for durvalumab plus olaparib vs control in non-tBRCAm HRD-positive disease and the non-tBRCAm ITT population. Secondary: progression-free survival for durvalumab vs control, overall survival, progression-free survival 2, quality of life, safety Durvalumab without olaparib did not improve PFS versus control (20.6 vs 19.3 mo; HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.73–1.04). Durvalumab plus olaparib improved primary PFS in non-tBRCAm HRD-positive disease (37.3 vs 23.0 mo; HR 0.49) and the non-tBRCAm ITT comparison (24.2 vs 19.3 mo; HR 0.63). Interim ITT OS was formally tested and did not meet its criterion; no further testing occurred. Grade ≥3 events were 72% vs 62%, and one death was attributed to olaparib-related AML

records.title: ENGOT-OV43/GOG-3036/KEYLYNK-001
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line maintenance — PARP inhibitors · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Newly diagnosed epithelial ovarian (non-mucinous, non-borderline), primary peritoneal or fallopian tube cancer; FIGO stage III or IV, first-line, after primary debulking surgery (within 7 weeks before chemotherapy) or planned interval debulking; no BRCA1/2 mutation on central tumour testing, enrolled regardless of PD-L1 status (CPS ≥10 hypothesis-tested subgroup); excluding germ cell tumours, prior PARP inhibitor or immune checkpoint inhibitor, CNS metastases, active autoimmune disease Carboplatin + paclitaxel (or docetaxel) per local standard for five cycles (one lead-in cycle before randomisation) with IV pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for 35 cycles → maintenance pembrolizumab + oral olaparib 300 mg twice daily vs same chemotherapy + pembrolizumab → pembrolizumab + placebo maintenance vs placebo + chemotherapy → placebo maintenance; olaparib/placebo until discontinuation or up to 2 years; optional bevacizumab at investigator discretion; treatment until planned cycles, radiographic progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, blinded independent central review-assessed progression-free survival, progression-free survival 2, time to first subsequent therapy, time to second subsequent therapy, time to discontinuation of treatment, pathological complete response, global health status/quality of life by EORTC QLQ-C30 and EORTC QLQ-OV28 (change from baseline, time to deterioration), safety Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy followed by pembrolizumab–olaparib maintenance significantly improved PFS versus chemotherapy in newly diagnosed BRCA non-mutated stage III–IV epithelial ovarian cancer. First interim analysis (median follow-up 30·1 mo): median PFS 23·7 vs 15·2 mo in CPS ≥10 (HR 0·63) and 22·1 vs 14·6 mo in ITT (HR 0·68); final analysis (49·6 mo) HR 0·66 and 0·71. Pembrolizumab alone did not improve PFS (CPS ≥10 HR 0·95; p=0·33), so OS was not formally tested; no OS improvement in either experimental group (ITT HR 1·04 pembrolizumab–olaparib and 1·06 pembrolizumab vs control). The control arm had no PARP inhibitor, so the benefit of pembrolizumab beyond olaparib cannot be isolated. Grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs 66% vs 56% vs 51%; treatment-related deaths four (1%) with pembrolizumab–olaparib and one (<1%) with pembrolizumab.

records.title: Study 19 (Ledermann)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — PARP maintenance (platinum-sensitive) · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2012
records.body: Platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian, fallopian-tube, or primary-peritoneal cancer with high-grade serous features or a serous component after ≥2 platinum courses and complete/partial response to the latest regimen Olaparib capsules 400 mg orally twice daily continuously until progression vs placebo continuously until progression Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: time to progression, objective response, disease control, overall survival, quality of life, safety Olaparib maintenance prolonged investigator-assessed PFS (8.4 vs 4.8 mo; HR 0.35, 95% CI 0.25–0.49), with no evidence of treatment-effect heterogeneity across prespecified subgroups (global interaction P=0.15). Interim OS at 38% maturity was 29.7 vs 29.9 mo (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.63–1.39). Grade 3–4 adverse events were 35.3% vs 20.3%, with more nausea, fatigue, vomiting and anaemia

records.title: SOLO-2 (Pujade-Lauraine)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — PARP maintenance (platinum-sensitive) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body: Platinum-sensitive relapsed high-grade serous or endometrioid ovarian, primary-peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer after ≥2 prior platinum lines and response to the latest; predicted/suspected deleterious BRCA1/2 mutation required and prior PARP inhibitor excluded; all randomized patients were germline BRCA-mutated Olaparib tablets 300 mg orally twice daily until disease progression or loss of benefit vs placebo until disease progression or investigator-determined loss of benefit Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, time to first and second subsequent therapy, time to treatment discontinuation, second progression-free survival, earliest progression or death, quality of life, safety Olaparib prolonged investigator-assessed PFS (19.1 vs 5.5 mo; HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.22–0.41). Final OS was 51.7 vs 38.8 mo (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.54–1.00) and missed its prespecified threshold; subsequent PARP inhibitor use was 10% vs 38%. At final follow-up, grade ≥3 anaemia was 21% vs 2% and MDS/AML 8% vs 4% (post-hoc RR 2.03, 95% CI 0.70–5.91). Fatal treatment-emergent events within the 30-day safety window were 4% vs 0, including six treatment-related MDS/AML deaths; later adverse-event deaths occurred in both arms
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2017;18:1274-1284  28754483 Lancet Oncol 2021;22:620-631 final OS analysis 33743851

records.title: NOVA (ENGOT-OV16, Mirza)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — PARP maintenance (platinum-sensitive) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body: Platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian, primary-peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer with predominantly high-grade serous histology after ≥2 platinum regimens; progression >6 months after the penultimate platinum and complete/partial response to the latest; germline-BRCA and non-germline-BRCA cohorts Niraparib 300 mg orally once daily in continuous 28-day cycles until progression, unacceptable toxicity, death, consent withdrawal, or loss to follow-up vs placebo on the same rule Primary: progression-free survival in germline BRCA-mutated and non-germline-BRCA cohorts. Secondary: chemotherapy-free interval, time to first and second subsequent therapy, second progression-free survival, overall survival, quality of life, safety Niraparib prolonged PFS in germline BRCA-mutated disease (21.0 vs 5.5 mo; HR 0.27), HRD-positive non-germline-BRCA disease (12.9 vs 3.8 mo; HR 0.38), and the overall non-germline-BRCA cohort (9.3 vs 3.9 mo; HR 0.45). OS and time to second subsequent therapy were immature. Grade 3–4 events occurred in 74.1% vs 22.9%; follow-up recorded three MDS/AML deaths, including one investigator-assessed treatment-related death in each arm

records.title: ARIEL3 (Coleman)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — PARP maintenance (platinum-sensitive) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body: Platinum-sensitive recurrent high-grade serous or endometrioid ovarian, primary-peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer after ≥2 prior platinum regimens; complete/partial response to the latest and progression >6 months after the penultimate platinum; latest platinum doublet ≥4 cycles required after amendment Rucaparib 600 mg orally twice daily until progression, death, toxicity, withdrawal, or study end vs placebo on the same rule Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, quality of life, objective response, safety, population pharmacokinetics Rucaparib prolonged investigator-assessed PFS in BRCA-mutated (16.6 vs 5.4 mo; HR 0.23), HRD (13.6 vs 5.4 mo; HR 0.32), and ITT populations (10.8 vs 5.4 mo; HR 0.36). In the BRCA-mutated population, time to worsening in FOSI-18 disease-related symptoms did not differ (HR 1.24, 95% CI 0.82–1.86), stopping formal testing before immature OS. Grade ≥3 events were 56% vs 15%; fatal treatment-emergent events were 6 vs 2, including two treatment-related MDS/AML deaths with rucaparib

records.title: OReO/ENGOT-ov38
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — PARP maintenance (platinum-sensitive) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body: Platinum-sensitive relapsed non-mucinous epithelial ovarian, primary-peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer after ≥2 platinum lines, response to ≥4-cycle latest platinum without bevacizumab, and one prior PARP inhibitor; BRCAm prior-PARP duration ≥18 months first-line or ≥12 months later-line, non-BRCAm ≥12 or ≥6 months Olaparib tablets 300 mg orally twice daily, or 250 mg twice daily if prior 300-mg intolerance, until objective radiological progression or while clinical benefit continued vs placebo on the same rule Primary: progression-free survival in BRCAm and non-BRCAm cohorts. Secondary: time to first and second subsequent therapy, overall survival, quality of life, safety Olaparib rechallenge modestly prolonged PFS in the separately randomized BRCAm cohort (4.3 vs 2.8 mo; HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.37–0.87) and non-BRCAm cohort (5.3 vs 2.8 mo; HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.26–0.71). Final BRCAm OS was 20.1 vs 20.9 mo (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.52–1.53); non-BRCAm OS was truncated at 21% deaths with no further evaluation planned. Grade ≥3 events were 15% vs 5% and 21% vs 8% in the respective cohorts, with no fatal adverse events

records.title: OCEANS (Aghajanian)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — antiangiogenics & antibody-drug conjugates · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2012
records.body: Measurable platinum-sensitive recurrent epithelial ovarian, primary-peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer progressing ≥6 months after frontline platinum; no prior chemotherapy for recurrence and no prior bevacizumab or other VEGF-pathway therapy Carboplatin AUC4 day 1 plus gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² days 1 and 8 q3w for 6 cycles, extendable to 10 with continued response, plus bevacizumab 15 mg/kg q3w → bevacizumab until progression/toxicity vs placebo plus the same chemotherapy → placebo on the same rule Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response, duration of response, overall survival, safety Adding bevacizumab improved PFS (12.4 vs 8.4 mo; HR 0.484, 95% CI 0.388–0.605) and objective response. At the second interim analysis, OS was 33.3 vs 35.2 mo (HR 1.027, 95% CI 0.792–1.331) with high censoring beyond 18 months. Grade ≥3 hypertension was 17.4% vs 0.4% and proteinuria 8.5% vs 0.9%; two delayed gastrointestinal perforations occurred, and one fatal adverse event occurred in each safety arm

records.title: GOG-0213 bevacizumab (Coleman)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — antiangiogenics & antibody-drug conjugates · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body: Recurrent measurable/evaluable epithelial ovarian, primary-peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer after complete response to ≥3 first-line platinum cycles and disease-free interval ≥6 months; no more than one prior chemotherapy regimen; surgical-objective participation was separately randomized in a subset Paclitaxel 175 mg/m² plus carboplatin AUC5 IV q3w for 6 planned cycles, with up to 2 extra cycles for response, plus bevacizumab 15 mg/kg q3w → bevacizumab until progression/toxicity vs the same chemotherapy alone Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, carboplatin/paclitaxel hypersensitivity, quality of life, objective response, safety The primary ITT OS comparison missed its criterion (42.2 vs 37.3 mo; HR 0.829, 95% CI 0.683–1.005); a post-hoc correction of misclassified platinum-free intervals gave HR 0.823 (95% CI 0.680–0.996). Bevacizumab improved secondary PFS (13.8 vs 10.4 mo; HR 0.628) and post-hoc response. Grade ≥3 events were 96% vs 86%; treatment-related deaths were 3% vs 1%, with more hypertension, proteinuria, gastrointestinal perforation and arterial thromboembolism

records.title: MITO-16b/MaNGO-OV2b (Pignata)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — antiangiogenics & antibody-drug conjugates · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body: FIGO IIIB–IV ovarian, fallopian-tube, or primary-peritoneal carcinoma at first recurrence/progression ≥6 months after first-line platinum that included bevacizumab; evaluable disease, ECOG 0–2, and available primary-surgery tumour sample Investigator-selected 6-cycle carboplatin/paclitaxel q3w, carboplatin/gemcitabine q3w, or carboplatin/PLD q4w vs the same doublet plus bevacizumab 15 mg/kg q3w, or 10 mg/kg q2w with PLD → bevacizumab 15 mg/kg q3w until progression/toxicity Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response, safety, prognostic and predictive biomarkers Continuing bevacizumab beyond first progression improved PFS (11.8 vs 8.8 mo; HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.41–0.65) and response. Interim OS did not favour continuation (26.7 vs 27.1 mo; HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.73–1.39). Grade ≥3 events were 79% vs 69%, including hypertension 29% vs 10% and proteinuria 4% vs 0; fatal toxicity occurred in 1/201 bevacizumab and 2/200 control patients

records.title: AURELIA (Pujade-Lauraine)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — antiangiogenics & antibody-drug conjugates · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2014
records.body: Measurable/CA-125-assessable platinum-resistant epithelial ovarian, primary-peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer progressing within 6 months after ≥4 platinum cycles; ≤2 prior regimens and investigator-selected weekly paclitaxel, PLD, or topotecan; refractory disease and bowel-perforation-risk features excluded Paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV days 1, 8, 15 and 22 q4w, PLD 40 mg/m² IV q4w, or topotecan 4 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 q4w or 1.25 mg/m² IV days 1–5 q3w, selected before randomization, vs the same chemotherapy plus bevacizumab 10 mg/kg q2w or 15 mg/kg q3w until progression/toxicity/withdrawal Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response, overall survival, safety, quality of life Adding bevacizumab improved primary PFS (6.7 vs 3.4 mo; HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.38–0.60) and response. Final OS did not establish benefit (16.6 vs 13.3 mo; HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.66–1.08); 40% of control patients received bevacizumab after progression. Post-hoc PFS estimates for randomized bevacizumab addition within investigator-selected weekly-paclitaxel, PLD and topotecan cohorts were HR 0.46, 0.57 and 0.32; they do not compare backbones. Bevacizumab after progression was associated with a lower death hazard than never receiving bevacizumab (HR 0.60, 95% CI 0.43–0.86), but future-defined exposure groups introduce selection and guarantee-time bias. Grade ≥3 GI perforation was 2% vs 0; five non-progression deaths occurred in each arm
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2014;32:1302-1308  24637997 Ann Oncol 2017;28:1842-1848 OS exploratory analysis 28481967 J Clin Oncol 2015;33:3836-3838 chemotherapy-cohort analysis 26282651

records.title: MIRASOL (Moore)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — antiangiogenics & antibody-drug conjugates · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body: Measurable FRα-high platinum-resistant high-grade serous ovarian, fallopian-tube, or primary-peritoneal cancer after 1–3 prior systemic lines; FRα-high required ≥75% viable tumour cells with 2+/3+ staining by VENTANA FOLR1 PS2+; excluded grade >1 neuropathy, chronic corneal disorder, corneal-transplant history, or active ocular disease requiring treatment/monitoring Mirvetuximab soravtansine 6 mg/kg adjusted ideal body weight IV q3w vs paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV days 1, 8, 15 and 22 q4w, PLD 40 mg/m² IV q4w, or topotecan 4 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 q4w or 1.25 mg/m² IV days 1–5 q3w; both until progression/toxicity/withdrawal/death Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response, overall survival, quality of life, duration of response, CA-125 response, second progression-free survival, safety In FRα-high platinum-resistant disease, mirvetuximab improved primary PFS (5.62 vs 3.98 mo; restricted mean at 12 months 6.13 vs 4.72 mo); no all-participants PFS HR was reported. It also improved response (42.3% vs 15.9%) and OS (16.46 vs 12.75 mo; HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.50–0.89). Grade ≥3 all-cause events were 41.7% vs 54.1%; ocular events occurred in 56.0%, and one treatment-related death occurred in each arm

records.title: ROSELLA (GOG-3073/ENGOT-ov72)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — antiangiogenics & antibody-drug conjugates · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body: Measurable platinum-resistant high-grade serous/endometrioid ovarian, primary-peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer, or carcinosarcoma with ≥30% epithelial component, after 1–3 prior lines including platinum; prior bevacizumab required, with progression/intolerance on most recent therapy Relacorilant 150 mg orally on the day before, day of, and day after nab-paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 q4w vs nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 q4w, each until progression, unmanageable toxicity, or death Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response, best response, duration of response, 24-week clinical benefit, CA-125 response, combined CA-125/radiographic response, safety Relacorilant plus nab-paclitaxel improved BICR PFS (6.54 vs 5.52 mo; HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.54–0.91). Planned interim OS was 15.97 vs 11.50 mo (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.52–0.92) but did not cross its boundary; final OS remains pending. Grade ≥3 events were 74% vs 59%, including neutropenia 44% vs 25%. Four on-treatment or ≤30-day adverse-event deaths occurred, all with combination; none was attributed to relacorilant and one septic-shock death to nab-paclitaxel

records.title: Gordon (PLD vs topotecan)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — chemotherapy (platinum-resistant) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2001
records.body: Measurable or measurable/assessable recurrent epithelial ovarian carcinoma after failed first-line platinum; prospectively stratified as platinum-sensitive if progression-free >6 months, otherwise platinum-refractory by the paper's definition Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 50 mg/m² IV q4w vs topotecan 1.5 mg/m²/day IV days 1–5 q3w; in the absence of progression both planned to 1 year, could continue with benefit, and counted protocol completion after 6 months Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, confirmed objective response, time to response, duration of response, quality of life, safety No significant overall difference was shown in primary PFS (16.1 vs 17.0 weeks) or OS (60.0 vs 56.7 weeks). The planned one-sided equivalence criterion cannot be confirmed because the observed HR and lower confidence bound were not reported; equivalence remains unestablished. The platinum-sensitive subgroup nominally favoured PLD for PFS and OS (108.0 vs 71.1 weeks), without an interaction test. Topotecan caused far more grade 3–4 cytopenias and four sepsis deaths; PLD caused more hand-foot syndrome

records.title: Mutch (gemcitabine vs PLD)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — chemotherapy (platinum-resistant) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2007
records.body: Epithelial ovarian, fallopian-tube, or primary-peritoneal carcinoma progressing within 6 months after the most recent platinum, after 1–2 prior regimens; measurable disease or CA-125 ≥100 U/mL; prior taxane was not required Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8 q3w vs pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 50 mg/m² IV day 1 q4w, each until progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response, time to treatment failure, overall survival, quality of life, safety Gemcitabine did not improve PFS over PLD (3.6 vs 3.1 mo; adjusted HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.7–1.4), OS (12.7 vs 13.5 mo) or response; negative comparisons do not establish equivalence, and crossover in 130/195 limits OS. PLD caused more hand-foot syndrome and mucositis, whereas gemcitabine caused more neutropenia, nausea/vomiting and fatigue. Six on-treatment deaths were attributed to disease

records.title: ENGOT-ov65/KEYNOTE-B96
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — chemotherapy (platinum-resistant) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian-tube, or primary-peritoneal carcinoma after 1–2 prior systemic lines including platinum and 4–9 first-line platinum cycles; progression ≤6 months after last platinum, ECOG 0–1; excluded primary platinum-refractory disease progressing during or ≤28 days after first-line platinum Pembrolizumab 400 mg IV q6w plus paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 q21d, with optional bevacizumab 10 mg/kg q2w, vs placebo plus the same regimen; pembrolizumab/placebo for up to 18 cycles, paclitaxel/bevacizumab until progression, prohibitive toxicity, label maximum, or local-practice stop Primary: progression-free survival in PD-L1 CPS ≥1 and overall populations. Secondary: overall survival in PD-L1 CPS ≥1 and overall populations, objective response, duration of response, quality of life, safety Pembrolizumab plus paclitaxel improved first-interim PFS in PD-L1 CPS ≥1 (8.3 vs 7.2 mo; HR 0.72) and overall (8.3 vs 6.4 mo; HR 0.70). OS met its criterion at the second interim in CPS ≥1 (18.2 vs 14.0 mo; HR 0.76) and at final analysis overall (17.7 vs 14.0 mo; HR 0.82). Planned-bevacizumab subgroup PFS estimates were exploratory, and no interaction test established a difference in pembrolizumab effect by planned bevacizumab. Because bevacizumab use was investigator-selected rather than randomized, its causal contribution cannot be isolated. Grade ≥3 treatment-related events were 68% vs 55%; two fatal immune-mediated events occurred with pembrolizumab

records.title: MILO/ENGOT-ov11
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Low-grade serous carcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body: Measurable recurrent/persistent low-grade serous ovarian, tubal, or peritoneal carcinoma confirmed by central pathology, after 1–3 prior chemotherapy lines including platinum; not amenable to curative surgery; prior MEK or BRAF inhibitor excluded Binimetinib 45 mg orally twice daily vs physician's choice PLD 40 mg/m² IV q4w, paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 q4w, or topotecan 1.25 mg/m² IV days 1–5 q3w, each until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or inability to continue protocol therapy Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response, duration of response, disease control, safety MILO stopped early for futility: BICR PFS at the 303-patient interim was 9.1 vs 10.6 mo (HR 1.21, 95% CI 0.79–1.86); a post-closure 341-patient update remained negative (10.4 vs 11.5 mo; HR 1.15). Grade ≥3 all-cause events were 76% vs 44%, discontinuation for adverse events 31% vs 17%, and retinal-vein occlusion occurred in 3% with binimetinib. Post-hoc within-arm KRAS associations had no treatment-by-KRAS comparison and do not establish predictive benefit

records.title: GOG-281/LOGS
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Low-grade serous carcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase II/III) · 2022
records.body: Measurable recurrent low-grade serous ovarian or peritoneal carcinoma confirmed by expert pathology after ≥1 prior platinum regimen; unlimited prior therapy permitted but not prior receipt of all 5 control options; mixed low-/high-grade serous carcinoma excluded Trametinib 2 mg orally once daily vs physician's choice paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 q4w, PLD 40–50 mg/m² IV q4w, topotecan 4 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 q4w, letrozole 2.5 mg daily, or tamoxifen 20 mg twice daily; each until progression/toxicity, with control crossover permitted after progression Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response, quality of life, adverse events, predictive/prognostic MAPK-pathway analyses, phosphorylated ERK prognostic effect, crossover progression-free survival and response Trametinib improved investigator-assessed PFS (13.0 vs 7.2 mo; HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.36–0.64) and response (26% vs 6%). OS did not establish benefit (37.6 vs 29.2 mo; HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.51–1.12); 68% of control patients crossed over and no adjusted OS analysis was reported. Grade 3–4 rash, anaemia and hypertension occurred in 13%, 13% and 12% with trametinib; no treatment-related deaths were reported

records.title: RAMP 201 (ENGOT-OV60/GOG-3052)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Low-grade serous carcinoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2025
records.body: Measurable recurrent low-grade serous ovarian or peritoneal cancer after ≥1 prior systemic therapy including platinum; local tumour KRAS status required before enrolment; one prior MEK or RAF inhibitor line permitted Parts A/B randomized avutometinib 3.2 mg orally twice weekly plus defactinib 200 mg orally twice daily vs avutometinib 4.0 mg orally twice weekly, each 3 weeks on/1 week off; Part C nonrandomized expansion used the combination Primary: confirmed objective response in the go-forward combination overall and in KRAS-mutant disease. Secondary: duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety, pharmacokinetics The go-forward combination showed activity in a pooled, partly nonrandomized cohort: confirmed BICR response was 31% (34/109 efficacy-evaluable; 95% CI 23–41), median PFS 12.9 mo, and median response duration 31.1 mo among 34 responders. The randomized Part A selection favoured combination by observed response without a formal hypothesis test. KRAS-mutant and wild-type results had no between-cohort or interaction test. Grade ≥3 treatment-related CPK increase was 24% of 115 treated patients; five on-treatment or ≤30-day deaths occurred, none considered treatment-related

records.title: GOG 3026
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Low-grade serous carcinoma · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2026
records.body: Centrally confirmed measurable recurrent low-grade serous ovarian, fallopian-tube, or peritoneal carcinoma; unlimited prior therapy, no prior CDK4/6 inhibitor; prior endocrine therapy allowed only if stopped ≥6 months before entry without progression on it (single-arm) Ribociclib 600 mg orally once daily on days 1–21 of each 28-day cycle plus letrozole 2.5 mg orally once daily continuously until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or other discontinuation Primary: confirmed objective response rate. Secondary: clinical benefit rate, progression-free survival, overall survival, duration of response, safety Ribociclib plus letrozole met its single-arm response criterion: confirmed investigator-assessed response was 30.6% (15/49; 90% CI 19.9–43.2), clinical benefit 84%, median PFS 14.5 mo and median OS 44.5 mo. Grade ≥3 neutropenia with any relation to therapy occurred in 47%; 98% required dose adjustment and 4% discontinued for adverse events. Three grade 5 events occurred, none attributed to treatment. Estrogen-receptor status was neither required nor measured

records.title: PORTEC-1 (Creutzberg)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Adjuvant / early-stage — radiation & risk-adapted therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2000
records.body: Stage I endometrioid endometrial cancer (intermediate-risk by grade/invasion) Postoperative pelvic EBRT vs observation Locoregional recurrence Pelvic radiotherapy halved 5-year locoregional recurrence (4% vs 14%) but did not improve overall survival (81% vs 85%); shifted many stage I patients to observation and defined the role of RT as local control only.

records.title: GOG 99 (Keys)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Adjuvant / early-stage — radiation & risk-adapted therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2004
records.body: Intermediate-risk stage IB-IIB (occult) endometrial cancer Adjuvant pelvic radiotherapy vs observation Cumulative recurrence Pelvic RT reduced 2-year cumulative recurrence (3% vs 12%, HR 0.58) without a significant survival benefit; defined a high-intermediate-risk subgroup (age, grade, LVSI, outer-third invasion) that derives most of the benefit.

records.title: PORTEC-2 (Nout)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Adjuvant / early-stage — radiation & risk-adapted therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2010
records.body: High-intermediate-risk stage I-IIA endometrial cancer Vaginal brachytherapy vs pelvic EBRT Vaginal recurrence Vaginal brachytherapy was non-inferior for vaginal control (5-year vaginal recurrence 1.8% vs 1.6%) with equal OS and far less gastrointestinal toxicity; established VBT as the adjuvant standard for high-intermediate-risk disease.

records.title: GOG 249 (Randall)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Adjuvant / early-stage — radiation & risk-adapted therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body: High-intermediate / high-risk early-stage endometrial cancer Pelvic RT vs vaginal brachytherapy + carboplatin/paclitaxel Recurrence-free survival Vaginal brachytherapy plus chemotherapy was not superior to pelvic RT for recurrence-free survival (HR 0.92) and produced more pelvic/nodal relapses; pelvic radiotherapy remained a standard for early-stage high-risk disease.

records.title: TCGA (Cancer Genome Atlas)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Molecular classification · Prospective · 2013
records.body: Endometrial carcinomas (endometrioid and serous) — integrated genomic analysis Genomic, transcriptomic and proteomic characterization Molecular classification Defined four molecular subgroups — POLE-ultramutated, MSI-hypermutated, copy-number-low, and copy-number-high (serous-like) — with distinct prognoses; the foundation for molecular classification now guiding risk stratification and adjuvant therapy.

records.title: PORTEC-3 molecular (Léon-Castillo)
records.subtitle: Endometrial Cancer · Molecular classification · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
