records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — immunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2010
records.body: Previously treated HLA-A*0201+ metastatic melanoma Ipilimumab ± gp100 vaccine vs gp100 vaccine Overall survival Ipilimumab improved OS versus vaccine alone (median 10.0 vs 6.4 months, HR ~0.66); first agent ever to improve survival in advanced melanoma and validated CTLA-4 blockade.

records.title: KEYNOTE-006
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — immunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2015
records.body: Advanced melanoma, ≤1 prior therapy (ipilimumab-naive) Pembrolizumab (Q2W or Q3W) vs ipilimumab Progression-free and overall survival Pembrolizumab improved OS (HR 0.63-0.69; 1-yr OS ~74% vs 58%) and PFS versus ipilimumab with less high-grade toxicity; established anti–PD-1 monotherapy as first-line over ipilimumab.

records.title: CheckMate 067
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — immunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2015
records.body: Untreated advanced melanoma Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W vs nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 doses → nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W vs ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 doses; all to progression or toxicity Progression-free survival and ORR Nivolumab + ipilimumab and nivolumab alone improved PFS (11.5 and 6.9 vs 2.9 months) and ORR (58% and 44% vs 19%) over ipilimumab, with durable long-term survival on extended follow-up; established first-line dual checkpoint blockade.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2015;373:23-34  26027431 N Engl J Med 2017;377:1345-1356 overall survival 28889792

records.title: RELATIVITY-047
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — immunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase II/III) · 2022
records.body: Untreated metastatic/unresectable melanoma Nivolumab + relatlimab (anti–LAG-3) fixed-dose vs nivolumab Progression-free survival Adding the LAG-3 inhibitor relatlimab improved PFS over nivolumab alone (median 10.1 vs 4.6 months, HR 0.75); established LAG-3 + PD-1 blockade as a first-line option with lower toxicity than nivolumab/ipilimumab.

records.title: OPTiM (T-VEC)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — oncolytic & cellular therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2015
records.body: Unresectable stage IIIB-IV melanoma Intralesional talimogene laherparepvec vs subcutaneous GM-CSF Durable response rate T-VEC improved durable response rate (16% vs 2%) and ORR (26% vs 6%) versus GM-CSF; first oncolytic immunotherapy approved for melanoma, useful for injectable locoregional disease.

records.title: C-144-01 (lifileucel)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — oncolytic & cellular therapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2025
records.body: Advanced melanoma refractory to anti–PD-1 (and BRAF/MEK if indicated) (single-arm) One-time lifileucel autologous TIL infusion (1×10⁹–150×10⁹ cells) after nonmyeloablative lymphodepletion (cyclophosphamide + fludarabine), then high-dose IL-2 (≤6 doses) Objective response rate Lifileucel produced an ORR of 31.4% with median duration of response 36.5 months in checkpoint-refractory melanoma; first FDA-approved cellular (TIL) therapy for a solid tumor.

records.title: Rohaan (TIL vs ipilimumab)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — oncolytic & cellular therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body: Unresectable stage IIIC/IV melanoma, 86% refractory to anti-PD-1 therapy TIL therapy: nonmyeloablative lymphodepletion (cyclophosphamide 60 mg/kg/day IV ×2 days + fludarabine 25 mg/m²/day IV ×5 days) → single adoptive transfer of ≥5×10⁹ TILs → high-dose IL-2 600,000 IU/kg IV Q8H (max 15 doses) vs ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 doses PFS Median PFS 7.2 vs 3.1 months (HR 0.50); ORR 49% vs 21%; median OS 25.8 vs 18.9 months; first phase III trial establishing TIL therapy's benefit over standard checkpoint immunotherapy.

records.title: IGNYTE (RP1)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — oncolytic & cellular therapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2025
records.body: Unresectable stage IIIB-IV cutaneous melanoma with confirmed progression while on ≥8 weeks of anti–PD-1 as the last prior therapy, given alone or combined with another anticancer agent and including adjuvant anti–PD-1; measurable disease plus an injectable lesion ≥1 cm required; prior oncolytic therapy or serious complications from checkpoint therapy excluded (single-arm) RP1 (vusolimogene oderparepvec) intratumorally 1 × 10⁶ PFU/mL then up to 7 further doses at 1 × 10⁷ PFU/mL Q2W (more allowed; ≤10 mL/dose) + nivolumab 240 mg Q2W from RP1 dose 2 ×8 cycles → 480 mg Q4W ×≤21 cycles (≤2 years) Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: duration of response, complete response rate, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety A third of anti-PD-1-failed melanomas responded to intratumoural RP1 with nivolumab (single-arm): the primary objective response rate by modified RECIST was 33.6% (95% CI 25.8-42.0) against a design null of below 15%, though no test result is reported; by conventional RECIST, response was 32.9% (25.2-41.3) with complete response in 15.0%. Responses were deep and durable - median duration 33.7 months (95% CI 14.1-not reached), 69.5% ongoing at 1 year - and noninjected lesions regressed nearly as often as injected. Median progression-free survival was only 3.6 months (2.0-5.0); overall survival 75.3% at 1 year and 63.3% at 2 years, median not reached. Treatment-related adverse events were 90.0% any-grade - commonest fatigue 32.9%, chills 32.1%, pyrexia 30.7%, almost all grade 1-2 - but 12.9% grade 3-4, with five grade 4 events including myocarditis and splenic rupture, and no treatment-related deaths.

records.title: IMCgp100-202 (tebentafusp)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Uveal & mucosal melanoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body: Untreated HLA-A*02:01+ metastatic uveal melanoma Tebentafusp (gp100×CD3 ImmTAC) vs investigator's choice (pembrolizumab/ipilimumab/dacarbazine) Overall survival Tebentafusp improved OS versus investigator's choice (median 21.7 vs 16.0 months, HR 0.51) despite low response rates; first therapy to improve survival in metastatic uveal melanoma.

records.title: OptimUM-02
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Uveal & mucosal melanoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase II/III) · 2026
records.body: First-line HLA-A*02:01-negative metastatic uveal melanoma Darovasertib (PKC inhibitor) + crizotinib vs investigator's choice (pembrolizumab, ipilimumab+nivolumab, or dacarbazine), 2:1 Progression-free survival Darovasertib plus crizotinib improved progression-free survival over investigator's choice (median 6.9 versus 3.1 months; HR 0.42, p<.0001) with objective response 37.1% versus 5.8% - the first randomised win in HLA-A2-negative metastatic uveal melanoma, the population tebentafusp cannot treat. These are the phase 2 efficacy primary results of a nested phase 2/3 trial; overall survival is the phase 3 primary endpoint and has not been reported. ASCO 2026 LBA9503 - a conference abstract, not yet a full publication.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2026;44(suppl 17):LBA9503   Orloff et al. - 2026 - Darovasertib plus crizotinib vs investigator's choice as first-line treatment for HLA-A2 negative [1126b8da]

records.title: Sheng et al (toripalimab + axitinib)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Uveal & mucosal melanoma · Clinical trial (phase Ib) · 2019
records.body: Treatment-naive metastatic mucosal melanoma Toripalimab (anti–PD-1) + axitinib Safety and objective response Toripalimab + axitinib achieved an ORR of 48.3% with median PFS 7.5 months in treatment-naive mucosal melanoma, a subtype largely resistant to single-agent checkpoint blockade; key early evidence for IO + VEGF-TKI in mucosal disease.

records.title: SECOMBIT (Ascierto)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — sequencing of targeted therapy & immunotherapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2023
records.body: Untreated BRAF V600-mutant metastatic melanoma Arm A: encorafenib 450 mg once daily + binimetinib 45 mg twice daily to progression → ipilimumab 3 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 → nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W; Arm B: ipilimumab 3 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 → nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W to progression → encorafenib 450 mg once daily + binimetinib 45 mg twice daily; Arm C: encorafenib 450 mg once daily + binimetinib 45 mg twice daily ×8 weeks → ipilimumab + nivolumab to progression → encorafenib + binimetinib 2-year OS 2-year/3-year OS 65%/54% (A), 73%/62% (B), 69%/60% (C); all arms exceeded the prespecified OS threshold; immunotherapy-first and sandwich sequencing trended better than targeted-therapy-first.

records.title: EBIN (Robert)
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Advanced — sequencing of targeted therapy & immunotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2025
records.body: Untreated, unresectable stage III/IV melanoma with BRAF V600E/K mutations Induction: encorafenib 450 mg once daily + binimetinib 45 mg twice daily ×12 weeks → nivolumab 3 mg/kg + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 doses → nivolumab 480 mg IV Q4W to progression, toxicity, or 2 years vs no induction: nivolumab 3 mg/kg + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 doses → nivolumab 480 mg IV Q4W to progression, toxicity, or 2 years PFS No PFS benefit from targeted-therapy induction before checkpoint inhibition (median PFS 9 vs 9 months, HR 0.87); more grade 3-5 treatment-related AEs with induction (42% vs 32%) — does not support induction sequencing.

records.title: MSLT-II
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Surgical management · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body: Adults 18–75 with clinically localized cutaneous melanoma and a tumor-positive sentinel node (pathology or RT-PCR assay), ECOG 0–1, randomization and dissection within 140 days of diagnostic biopsy; peri-diagnostic surgical staging setting Immediate completion lymph-node dissection of the involved nodal basin vs nodal observation with clinical examination and basin ultrasonography (every 4 months in years 1–2, every 6 months years 3–5, then annually) with dissection at clinically detected nodal recurrence Primary: Melanoma-specific survival. Secondary: Disease-free survival, Overall survival, Survival without nodal recurrence, Distant metastasis-free survival, Cumulative rate of nonsentinel-node metastasis, Extent of nodal involvement Immediate completion lymph-node dissection did not improve melanoma-specific survival vs nodal observation with ultrasonography. Per-protocol 3-year melanoma-specific survival 86±1.3% vs 86±1.2% (P=0.42); adjusted HR for death 1.08 (95% CI 0.88–1.34); median follow-up 43 months. Disease-free survival was slightly higher with dissection (68±1.7% vs 63±1.7%, P=0.05), driven by 3-year regional nodal control (92±1.0% vs 77±1.5%, P<0.001); secondary results warrant caution given the negative primary endpoint. Nonsentinel-node metastasis (11.5% at dissection) was an independent prognostic factor (HR 1.78, P=0.005). Lymphedema 24.1% vs 6.3% (P<0.001), mild in 64%, moderate in 33%, severe in 3%.
records.keywords: Faries et al. N Engl J Med 2017;376:2211-22  28591523

records.title: MSLT-I
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Surgical management · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2014
records.body: Patients with localized cutaneous melanomas of Clark level III with Breslow thickness ≥1.00 mm or Clark level IV/V with any Breslow thickness; primary analysis group intermediate thickness (1.20–3.50 mm), with thick (>3.50 mm) and exploratory thin (<1.20 mm) cohorts Wide excision + sentinel-node biopsy (60%) with immediate lymphadenectomy for sentinel-node metastases vs wide excision + nodal observation (40%) with delayed lymphadenectomy at nodal relapse; excision margins 2–3 cm recommended Primary: Melanoma-specific survival. Secondary: Disease-free survival, Survival with tumor-positive or tumor-negative sentinel nodes, Incidence of sentinel-node metastases vs clinically detected nodal metastases, Distant disease-free survival Sentinel-node biopsy with immediate lymphadenectomy did not improve overall 10-yr melanoma-specific survival but improved disease-free survival and identified node-positive patients who benefit from immediate dissection. In intermediate-thickness melanomas, 10-yr melanoma-specific survival 81.4±1.5% biopsy vs 78.3±2.0% observation (HR 0.84, P=0.18); disease-free survival 71.3±1.8% vs 64.7±2.3% (HR 0.76, P=0.01); thick melanomas 50.7±4.0% vs 40.5±4.7% (HR 0.70, P=0.03). Among node-positive intermediate-thickness patients, biopsy-based management improved 10-yr melanoma-specific survival (62.1±4.8% vs 41.5±5.6%; HR 0.56, P=0.006) and distant disease-free survival (HR 0.62, P=0.02); no such difference in thick melanomas (HR 0.92, P=0.78). Node-positive subgroup comparisons are subject to ascertainment bias; post hoc latent-subgroup analysis showed persistent significant benefit. Sentinel-node status was the strongest prognostic factor (HR for death 2.40, P<0.001).
records.keywords: Morton et al. N Engl J Med 2014;370:599-609  24521106

records.title: DeCOG-SLT
records.subtitle: Melanoma · Surgical management · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body: Cutaneous melanoma of trunk or extremities, age 18–75, tumour thickness ≥1.0 mm with SLN metastasis; head/neck melanoma, satellite/in-transit or distant metastases, SLN macrometastases, prior/concurrent malignancy (except nonmelanoma skin cancer) and immunosuppressive treatment excluded; adjuvant interferon allowed Complete lymph node dissection within 120 days of sentinel node biopsy vs observation with guideline follow-up (exams, sonography, S100b 3-monthly; imaging 6-monthly for 3 years); stratified by thickness, ulceration, intended interferon Primary: Distant metastasis-free survival. Secondary: Recurrence-free survival, Overall survival, Recurrence of regional lymph node metastases, Safety Final analysis (median follow-up 72 months) confirms immediate CLND is not superior to observation in SLN-positive melanoma. 5-year DMFS 64.9% CLND vs 67.6% observation (HR 1.08, 90% CI 0.83–1.39; 164 events vs 192 planned, power 74%); 5-year OS (HR 0.99) and RFS (HR 1.01) also did not differ. Regional nodal recurrence was less frequent with CLND (26 [10.8%] of 240 vs 38 [16.3%] of 233) without reducing distant metastasis. Grade 3/4 adverse effects in 32 (13%) of 240 CLND patients, most often lymphedema (20, 8.3%); no serious adverse events reported
records.keywords: Leiter et al. Lancet Oncol 2016;17:757-767  27161539 Leiter et al. J Clin Oncol 2019;37:3000-3008  31557067

records.title: Cavalieri et al.
records.subtitle: Non-melanoma skin cancers · Guidelines · Narrative review · 2023
records.body:
Cutaneous adnexal (appendageal) carcinomas across WHO groups: apocrine/eccrine, follicular, sebaceous and site-specific appendageal tumours (incl. extramammary Paget disease) and malignant adnexal tumours of the eyelid; diagnosis, staging, curative and advanced-disease management; narrative review, no defined patient cohort Radical surgery (margin-controlled/Mohs preferred) for local or regional disease
・Post-operative treatment: Selective radiotherapy ± concomitant chemotherapy
・Advanced disease: Chemotherapy (platinum salts, gemcitabine, anthracyclines, taxanes), immunotherapy and targeted therapy (hedgehog inhibitors, HER2, androgen receptor)
・Design: Narrative review of management options, not randomised treatment arms Age-adjusted incidence rate, 5-year relative survival Review recommends radical surgery as the first option for local or regional disease and clinical-trial enrolment for advanced disease
・Incidence: Lower than 1 per 100,000 subjects/year in the authors' registry query
・5-yr relative survival: 86% (95% CI 84-88%) Europe vs 93.8% USA; registries not comparable
・Adjuvant chemoradiation: No clinical studies support concomitant chemotherapy with adjuvant radiation; extrapolated from head and neck squamous cell carcinoma; not standard of care
・Advanced disease: ORR 62.5% with vismodegib in a cohort of 16 patients with inoperable trichoblastic carcinoma
・Molecular: MSI-high in only 2% of 103 patients with adnexal cancers
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: European and US registries not comparable; evidence for advanced disease limited to small, non-randomised cohorts
records.keywords: Cavalieri et al. EJC Skin Cancer 2023;1:100006

records.title: Stupp (EORTC-NCIC 26981-22981)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Newly diagnosed glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2005
records.body: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma, age ≤70, WHO PS 0-2 RT 60 Gy in 30 fractions + concurrent oral temozolomide 75 mg/m²/day throughout RT (max 49 days), then after a 4-week break six cycles of adjuvant temozolomide 150→200 mg/m² days 1–5 Q4W vs RT alone (60 Gy in 30 fractions) Overall survival Temozolomide added to RT improved median OS (14.6 vs 12.1 months, HR 0.63) and 2-yr OS (26.5% vs 10.4%), with benefit greatest in MGMT-methylated tumors; established the 'Stupp regimen' as standard of care.

records.title: AVAglio (Chinot)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Newly diagnosed glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2014
records.body: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma after surgery RT/temozolomide + bevacizumab vs RT/temozolomide + placebo Progression-free and overall survival (co-primary) Met one co-primary and missed the other: PFS 10.6 vs 6.2 months (stratified HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.55–0.74, p<0.001 against a prespecified alpha of 0.01) but OS 16.8 vs 16.7 months (HR 0.88, 0.76–1.02, p=0.10 against 0.04). Deterioration-free survival was longer on all five prespecified quality-of-life scales and on Karnofsky performance status, and among patients taking glucocorticoids at baseline these were discontinued in 66.3% vs 47.1% — all nominal, since no alpha sits below the two co-primaries. Grade ≥3 adverse events often associated with bevacizumab occurred in 32.5% vs 15.8%. The authors conclude a 4.4-month PFS gain “with quality of life and functional status maintained” at the cost of more adverse events; they do not conclude there is no role. The trial did not establish a survival benefit, and bevacizumab is not standard first-line.

records.title: RTOG 0825 (Gilbert)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Newly diagnosed glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2014
records.body: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma after surgery RT/temozolomide + bevacizumab vs RT/temozolomide + placebo Progression-free and overall survival (co-primary) Upfront bevacizumab did not improve OS (15.7 vs 16.1 months, HR 1.13) and the PFS gain (10.7 vs 7.3 months) missed the prespecified threshold, with more cognitive/QoL decline; reserved for symptomatic recurrence.

records.title: EF-14
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Newly diagnosed glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body: Newly diagnosed histologically confirmed supratentorial glioblastoma (WHO grade IV) after maximal safe debulking surgery or biopsy and completed standard radiotherapy with concomitant temozolomide; Karnofsky performance score 70 or higher; TTFields to start at least 4 weeks and not more than 7 weeks from the last day of radiotherapy; excluded progressive disease after radiochemotherapy, infratentorial tumour location and severe comorbidities TTFields (200 kHz via 4 transducer arrays on shaved scalp, ≥18 h/d) plus maintenance temozolomide 150–200 mg/m2/d for 5 days per 28-day cycle for 6 cycles (extension beyond 6 cycles allowed; TTFields continued until second radiologic progression or maximum 24 months) vs maintenance temozolomide alone Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, Annual survival rates, Progression-free survival at 6 months, Quality of life, Mini-Mental State Examination, Karnofsky performance score, Safety In the final analysis, adding TTFields to maintenance temozolomide significantly improved both PFS and overall survival vs temozolomide alone. Median PFS from randomization 6.7 vs 4.0 months (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.52–0.76; P<.001) and median OS 20.9 vs 16.0 months (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.53–0.76; P<.001) in the ITT population of 695 randomized patients, median follow-up 40 months; results consistent with the prior interim analysis. Open-label design; PFS by blinded central review. No significant increase in systemic adverse events (48% vs 44%); mild-to-moderate skin toxicity beneath transducer arrays 52% and grade 3 skin involvement 2% with TTFields

records.title: CeTeG/NOA-09 (Herrlinger)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Newly diagnosed glioblastoma (IDH-wildtype) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body: Newly diagnosed MGMT-methylated glioblastoma, age 18-70 Lomustine + temozolomide vs temozolomide (both with RT) Overall survival Lomustine-temozolomide improved median OS (48.1 vs 31.4 months, HR 0.60) in this small trial; an intensified option for fit MGMT-methylated patients.

records.title: Keime-Guibert et al. (Radiotherapy for Glioblastoma in the Elderly Study)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Elderly / frail glioblastoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2007
records.body: Newly diagnosed, histologically proven glioblastoma multiforme or anaplastic astrocytoma (WHO classification) after surgery, age ≥70, KPS ≥70; randomization and start of assigned treatment required within 4 weeks after surgery Supportive care (corticosteroids, anticonvulsants, physical and psychological support, palliative care team) plus focal radiotherapy 1.8 Gy per fraction once daily 5 days per week to a total of 50 Gy (CTV: contrast enhancement plus 2 cm margin) vs supportive care alone; randomized within 4 weeks after surgery, stratified by center Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, Tolerance of radiotherapy, Health-related quality of life, Cognition Adding radiotherapy to supportive care modestly prolonged survival without reducing quality of life or cognition in elderly glioblastoma. Median OS 29.1 wk with RT plus supportive care (n=39) vs 16.9 wk with supportive care alone (n=42); HR for death 0.47 (95% CI 0.29–0.76, P=0.002); median follow-up 21 wk; final analysis of the 81 glioblastoma patients after the trial was stopped at the first interim analysis at a preset efficacy boundary. Median PFS 14.9 vs 5.4 wk (HR 0.28, P<0.001). Quality-of-life and cognitive results over time did not differ significantly between groups, with analyses restricted to day 135 because few patients remained alive. No severe adverse events related to radiotherapy; one transient somnolence; corticosteroid complications: diabetes in 7 supportive-care vs 2 RT patients, myopathy in 3 vs 6
records.keywords: Keime-Guibert et al. N Engl J Med 2007;356:1527-35  17429084

records.title: Roa et al.
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Elderly / frail glioblastoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2004
records.body: Histologically confirmed glioblastoma multiforme (centrally reviewed), age ≥60 years and KPS ≥50 after surgery, adjuvant RT commencing within 6 weeks of surgical diagnosis; excluded previous cranial RT, prior/concomitant invasive cancer (except nonmelanomatous skin cancer and carcinoma-in-situ), and unavailable pre/postoperative imaging Postoperative RT randomized to standard 60 Gy in 30 fractions over 6 weeks (46 Gy/23 fractions then 14 Gy/7-fraction boost) vs short course 40 Gy in 15 daily fractions over 3 weeks; RT started within 6 weeks of surgery; no chemotherapy before or during RT Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Overall survival from date of diagnosis, Survival at 6 months, Health-related quality of life, Corticosteroid requirement There was no survival difference between standard and short-course RT in older GBM patients; short-course RT is a reasonable treatment option. Median OS from randomization 5.1 mo (6-week) vs 5.6 mo (3-week) (HR 0.89; log-rank P=.57); 6-month survival 44.7% vs 41.7%. Study not sufficiently powered to conclude equivalence, but a >14% difference in 6-month survival was excluded. Among RT completers, fewer short-course patients needed a posttreatment corticosteroid increase (10 [23%] of 43 vs 17 [49%] of 35; P=.02); KPS similar over time; FACT-Br completion 45% precluded comparison
records.keywords: Roa et al. J Clin Oncol 2004;22:1583-8  15051755

records.title: NOA-08
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Elderly / frail glioblastoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2012
records.body: De-novo anaplastic astrocytoma or glioblastoma, histologically confirmed after biopsy or resection, newly diagnosed post-surgery; age older than 65 years and Karnofsky performance score 60 or higher; excluded prior systemic chemotherapy or brain radiotherapy or inadequate bone-marrow, liver or renal function Temozolomide 100 mg/m² on days 1–7 of 1-week-on, 1-week-off cycles vs radiotherapy 60·0 Gy in 30 fractions of 1·8–2·0 Gy over 6–7 weeks to gross tumour volume plus 2 cm margin; stopped for progression or unacceptable toxic effects; temozolomide delays >4 consecutive weeks before 6 months prompted switch to radiotherapy Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Event-free survival, Best response, Health-related quality of life, Safety Temozolomide alone was non-inferior to radiotherapy alone in elderly patients with malignant astrocytoma; median OS 8.6 vs 9.6 months (HR 1.09, 95% CI 0.84–1.42, p_non-inf 0.033; per-protocol 0.028) and median EFS 3.3 vs 4.7 months (HR 1.15, 95% CI 0.92–1.43, p_non-inf 0.043; per-protocol 0.041) — non-inferiority is not superiority. MGMT promoter methylation (73 of 209 tested) was predictive: EFS on temozolomide 8.4 months with methylation vs 3.3 without; on radiotherapy EFS 4.6 months regardless of status; authors call MGMT a useful biomarker for outcomes by treatment. No grade 5 adverse events; grade 3–4 events more frequent with temozolomide (lymphocytopenia 46 vs 1, neutropenia 16 vs 2). Limitations: non-inferiority design with generous tolerance level, one-sided testing; MGMT conclusive in only 56% of samples

records.title: Nordic
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Elderly / frail glioblastoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2012
records.body: Newly diagnosed histologically confirmed glioblastoma (WHO grade IV astrocytoma), age 60 years or older, post-surgery first-line setting; WHO performance score 0–2 (score 3 allowed if caused by neurological deficits); after Oct 15, 2004, patients younger than 65 years fit for combined radiochemotherapy excluded; excluded other primary cancers (except curatively treated without relapse ≥2 years), prior brain tumour therapy except surgery, and prior head radiotherapy Temozolomide 200 mg/m² orally on days 1–5 of every 28 days for up to six cycles or until radiological/clinical progression, unacceptable adverse effects, or physician/patient choice to stop vs hypofractionated radiotherapy 34·0 Gy in ten fractions of 3·4 Gy over 2 weeks vs standard radiotherapy 60·0 Gy in 30 fractions of 2·0 Gy on weekdays over 6 weeks Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Health-related quality of life, Safety Standard 6-week radiotherapy was associated with poor outcomes, especially in patients older than 70 years, and both temozolomide and hypofractionated radiotherapy should be considered as standard treatment options in elderly patients with glioblastoma. Three-group randomisation (n=291): median OS significantly longer with temozolomide than standard RT (8.3 vs 6.0 months, HR 0.70, p=0.01) but not with hypofractionated RT (7.5 months, HR 0.85, p=0.24); TMZ vs hypofractionated RT similar (8.4 vs 7.4 months, p=0.12). Age >70: better OS with TMZ (HR 0.35, p<0.0001) and hypofractionated RT (HR 0.59, p=0.02) vs standard RT. On TMZ, MGMT-methylated vs unmethylated OS 9.7 vs 6.8 months (p=0.02), no difference with RT; post hoc, n=203. TMZ grade 3–4 neutropenia (n=12) and thrombocytopenia (n=18); two fatal infections; one TMZ death after GI-bleed surgery in grade 2 thrombocytopenia

records.title: Perry et al.
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Elderly / frail glioblastoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body: Newly diagnosed glioblastoma (WHO grade IV astrocytoma) histologically confirmed after surgery or biopsy <28 days before randomization; age 65+; ECOG 0–2; deemed by physician unsuitable for conventional radiotherapy (60 Gy in 30 fractions over 6 weeks) with temozolomide; glucocorticoids at stable or decreasing dose Radiotherapy alone (40.05 Gy in 15 daily fractions over 3 weeks) vs radiotherapy + concurrent temozolomide 75 mg/m²/day for 21 days → adjuvant temozolomide 150–200 mg/m²/day on 5 consecutive days of a 28-day cycle, up to 12 cycles or until disease progression Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, Quality of life, Safety Adding temozolomide to short-course radiotherapy resulted in longer survival than short-course radiotherapy alone in elderly patients with glioblastoma: median OS 9.3 vs 7.6 months (HR for death 0.67, 95% CI 0.56–0.80, P<0.001; ITT, 562 randomized); median PFS 5.3 vs 3.9 months (HR 0.50, P<0.001). Greatest benefit in MGMT-methylated tumours (OS 13.5 vs 7.7 months, HR 0.53, P<0.001, n=165); clinically meaningful but non-significant advantage with unmethylated MGMT (10.0 vs 7.9 months, HR 0.75, P=0.055; interaction P=0.08). Quality of life similar between groups. Grade 3/4 lymphopenia 27.2% vs 10.3% and thrombocytopenia 11.1% vs 0.4% with RT+TMZ vs RT
records.keywords: Perry et al. N Engl J Med 2017;376:1027-1037  28296618

records.title: EORTC 26101 (Wick)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Recurrent glioblastoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body: Glioblastoma at first progression after chemoradiation Lomustine + bevacizumab vs lomustine alone Overall survival Adding bevacizumab prolonged PFS (4.2 vs 1.5 months) but not OS (9.1 vs 8.6 months, HR 0.95); no survival role for the combination at recurrence.

records.title: REGOMA (Lombardi)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · Recurrent glioblastoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2019
records.body: Glioblastoma at first relapse after surgery and Stupp chemoradiation Regorafenib vs lomustine Overall survival Regorafenib improved median OS (7.4 vs 5.6 months, HR 0.50); a signal supporting regorafenib as a recurrence option pending phase 3 confirmation.

records.title: EORTC 22845 (van den Bent)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · IDH-mutant lower-grade (grade 2) glioma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2005
records.body: Adult grade 2 astrocytoma/oligodendroglioma after surgery Early postoperative RT (54 Gy) vs RT deferred until progression Overall and progression-free survival Early RT lengthened PFS (5.3 vs 3.4 years, HR 0.59) but not OS (7.4 vs 7.2 years); supported deferring RT in selected low-risk patients.

records.title: RTOG 9802 (Buckner)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · IDH-mutant lower-grade (grade 2) glioma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body: High-risk (age ≥40, or <40 with subtotal resection) grade 2 glioma RT + PCV (procarbazine/lomustine/vincristine) vs RT alone Overall survival Adding PCV to RT improved median OS (13.3 vs 7.8 years, HR 0.59) and PFS (10.4 vs 4.0 years), with benefit concentrated in IDH-mutant tumors; established RT+PCV for high-risk low-grade glioma.

records.title: INDIGO (Mellinghoff)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · IDH-mutant lower-grade (grade 2) glioma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body: Residual or recurrent grade 2 oligodendroglioma or astrocytoma (WHO 2016) with centrally confirmed IDH1 or IDH2 mutation; surgery as only prior glioma treatment (most recent surgery 1–5 years before randomization), watch-and-wait candidates with measurable nonenhancing disease (≥1 target lesion ≥1 cm by ≥1 cm); excluded high-risk features (uncontrolled seizures, brain-stem involvement, contrast enhancement) and QTc ≥450 msec Oral vorasidenib 40 mg once daily vs matched placebo, continuous 28-day cycles; continued until blinded-review-confirmed imaging progression, unacceptable toxic effects, indication for other anticancer therapy, or pregnancy; placebo crossover to vorasidenib permitted on confirmed progression Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Time to next intervention, Objective response, Safety, Tumor growth rate, Health-related quality of life, Overall survival Vorasidenib significantly improved progression-free survival and delayed time to next intervention vs placebo in grade 2 IDH-mutant glioma (prespecified second interim analysis, data cut Sept 6, 2022; median follow-up 14.2 mo): median PFS 27.7 vs 11.1 months (HR 0.39, 95% CI 0.27–0.56; P<0.001); time to next intervention HR 0.26 (95% CI 0.15–0.43; P<0.001). Grade ≥3 AEs 22.8% vs 13.5%; grade ≥3 ALT elevation 9.6% vs 0. Durability confirmed on extended follow-up; established targeted therapy that can delay chemoradiation. FDA-approved August 2024 (Voranigo) – first systemic therapy for grade 2 IDH-mutant glioma
records.keywords: Mellinghoff et al. N Engl J Med 2023;389:589-601  37272516

records.title: RTOG 9402 (Cairncross)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · IDH-mutant grade 3 (anaplastic) glioma & 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2006
records.body: Newly diagnosed anaplastic oligodendroglial tumors Neoadjuvant PCV → RT vs RT alone Overall survival PCV+RT doubled median OS in 1p/19q-codeleted tumors (14.7 vs 7.3 years, HR 0.59) but not in non-codeleted tumors; established PCV+RT for codeleted anaplastic oligodendroglioma.

records.title: EORTC 26951 (van den Bent)
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · IDH-mutant grade 3 (anaplastic) glioma & 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2006
records.body: Newly diagnosed anaplastic oligodendroglial tumors RT (59.4 Gy) → adjuvant PCV vs RT alone Overall survival Adjuvant PCV improved median OS (3.5 vs 2.6 years, HR 0.78), with the largest benefit in 1p/19q-codeleted tumors; confirmed PCV+RT for codeleted disease.

records.title: CATNON
records.subtitle: Adult Diffuse Glioma · IDH-mutant grade 3 (anaplastic) glioma & 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body: Newly diagnosed anaplastic glioma (WHO 2007 classification) without 1p/19q co-deletion, postoperative radiotherapy setting; central confirmation of grade 3 pathology, 1p/19q loss-of-heterozygosity status and MGMT promoter methylation (qPCR) required before randomisation; excluded known HIV, chronic hepatitis B or C infection Radiotherapy alone (59·4 Gy in 33 fractions) vs radiotherapy + concurrent daily oral temozolomide 75 mg/m² during radiotherapy vs radiotherapy + adjuvant oral temozolomide (12 4-week cycles of 150–200 mg/m² on days 1–5, starting 4 weeks after radiotherapy) vs radiotherapy + both; randomised 1:1:1:1, 2×2 factorial design Primary: Overall survival adjusted for stratification factors at randomisation in the intention-to-treat population Final analysis (database lock Oct 1, 2024; median OS follow-up 10·9 years): adjuvant temozolomide improved overall survival vs no adjuvant temozolomide (HR 0·65, 95% CI 0·54–0·77); concurrent temozolomide showed no benefit (HR 0·91, 0·76–1·08). Authors conclude 12 cycles of adjuvant temozolomide after radiotherapy should be standard of care in grade 3 IDHmt astrocytoma: in IDHmt tumours median OS 12·5 vs 6·0 years (HR 0·54, 0·42–0·69) and median PFS 7·0 years with adjuvant temozolomide; neither concurrent nor adjuvant temozolomide benefited IDHwt tumours. HD-CDKN2A and PDGFRA amplification were prognostic but not predictive (exploratory; study closed before the 534 required events). No new safety information; interim grade 3–4 events 8–12% of 549 temozolomide-assigned patients remain unchanged
records.keywords: van den Bent et al. Lancet 2017;390:1645-1653  28801186 van den Bent et al. The Lancet Oncology 2026;27:45-56  41449147

records.title: Aoyama (Intracranial GCT)
records.subtitle: Intracranial GCT · Induction chemotherapy · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2002
records.body: Primary CNS germ-cell tumour; age ≥3 years, histologic diagnosis, no prior chemotherapy/RT and no extra-CNS dissemination; includes pure germinoma, source-defined HCG-β-secreting germinoma (serum HCG-β ≥0.5 mIU/mL), immature teratoma/germinoma and highly malignant mixed GCT (single-arm) Surgery → pathology/extent/resection/response-adapted therapy; route unstated. Pure solitary germinoma: EP (etoposide 100 + cisplatin 20 mg/m²) d1–5 q4wk, 3–4 cycles by resection. Others: ICE (ifosfamide 900 + cisplatin 20 + etoposide 60 mg/m²) d1–5 q4wk, ≤6 cycles. RT within 2 wk: 2 Gy/fx; 24 Gy local/whole-ventricle/whole-CNS by extent; immature teratoma 24 Gy after GTR/40 Gy otherwise; highly malignant GCT WCNS 24 Gy + local 50–54 Gy. HCG-β pineal boost conflict (10 vs 16 Gy) Primary: relapse-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, disease-related survival, neurocognitive function, endocrine function, safety 5-year OS was 93%, disease-related survival 100% and RFS 69% after pathology-, extent- and era-adapted chemoradiotherapy in this prospective single-centre, nonrandomized phase II cohort. Relapse occurred after local-field irradiation in 6/18 pure/HCG-β germinoma patients but in 0/9 after whole-ventricle-or-larger fields; nonrandom treatment allocation precludes a comparative field-effect claim. Acute toxicity was reported only qualitatively. IQ follow-up covered 11 selected relapse-free patients and was too small/short to establish late neurocognitive or endocrine safety

records.title: O’Sullivan (NCIC SR2)
records.subtitle: STS · Localised / perioperative — soft tissue · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2002
records.body: Extremity soft-tissue sarcoma undergoing limb-conserving surgery + radiotherapy Preoperative RT (50 Gy) vs postoperative RT (66 Gy) Wound complications within 120 days Preoperative RT roughly doubled major wound complications (35% vs 17%, p=0.01) but uses a lower dose and smaller field, trading early morbidity for less late fibrosis; overall survival marginally favoured preoperative RT (p=0.048). Frames RT timing as a deliberate trade-off.

records.title: EORTC 62931 (Woll)
records.subtitle: STS · Localised / perioperative — soft tissue · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2012
records.body: Resected grade II–III soft-tissue sarcoma, any site Adjuvant doxorubicin + ifosfamide + lenograstim vs observation Overall survival Did not demonstrate a survival benefit: 5-year OS 66.5% vs 67.8% (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.68–1.31, p=0.72); relapse-free survival HR 0.91 (0.67–1.22). Metastases — the mechanism adjuvant chemotherapy should prevent — occurred in 35% of both arms. But the trial fell short of its own design: 141 of the 146 required deaths, with 38 of 351 (11%) ineligible after randomisation, so the interval does not exclude a 32% relative risk reduction. This same report's updated meta-analysis of 2145 patients gives HR 0.86 (p=0.02), and the authors leave the recommendation open pending individual-patient-data analysis. Adjuvant chemotherapy is not standard for resected STS.

records.title: ISG-STS 1001 (Gronchi)
records.subtitle: STS · Localised / perioperative — soft tissue · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body: Localised high-risk STS of extremity / trunk wall (five histotypes) Neoadjuvant standard epirubicin + ifosfamide (3 cycles) vs histotype-tailored regimen Disease-free survival Standard anthracycline + ifosfamide was superior to histotype-tailored therapy (46-month projected DFS 62% vs 38%; HR 2.00 favouring standard, p=0.006); stopped for futility. Defines 3 cycles of neoadjuvant epirubicin + ifosfamide as standard for high-risk extremity/trunk STS.

records.title: STRASS (EORTC-62092, Bonvalot)
records.subtitle: STS · Localised / perioperative — soft tissue · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body: Primary, operable retroperitoneal sarcoma Preoperative RT + surgery vs surgery alone Abdominal recurrence-free survival No benefit (median abdominal RFS 4.5 vs 5.0 years; HR 1.01, p=0.95), with substantial radiation toxicity. Preoperative RT should not be standard of care for retroperitoneal sarcoma.

records.title: EORTC 62012 (Judson)
records.subtitle: STS · Advanced soft tissue — first-line · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2014
records.body: High-grade (grades 2–3) soft-tissue sarcoma, locally advanced unresectable or metastatic; first-line, no chemotherapy for advanced disease (prior adjuvant allowed if no progression within 6 months of completion); measurable disease progressing within 6 weeks before treatment (RECIST 1.0), age 18–60 years, WHO PS 0–1; excluded GIST, osteosarcoma, Ewing's sarcoma, chondrosarcoma, embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma, alveolar soft part sarcoma and other listed types, CNS metastases Doxorubicin 75 mg/m² IV bolus day 1 or 72 h continuous IV infusion vs intensified doxorubicin 25 mg/m²/day days 1–3 (75 mg/m²) plus ifosfamide 2·5 g/m²/day days 1–4 (10 g/m²) with mesna and pegfilgrastim 6 mg SC day 5; both every 3 weeks until progression or unacceptable toxic effects, up to six cycles (open-label) Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, best overall response, toxic effects Intensified doxorubicin plus ifosfamide did not improve overall survival vs doxorubicin alone; the authors do not support it for palliation of advanced soft-tissue sarcoma unless tumour shrinkage is the specific goal. Primary endpoint missed: median OS 14·3 vs 12·8 mo (HR 0·83, 95·5% CI 0·67–1·03; p=0·076); median follow-up 59 vs 56 mo. The combination improved median PFS (7·4 vs 4·6 mo; HR 0·74; p=0·003) and overall response (60/227 [26%] vs 31/228 [14%]); the trial was open-label, with local response assessment and no central review. Grade 3–4 toxicity was higher with the combination, including febrile neutropenia (103/224 [46%] vs 30/223 [13%]) and thrombocytopenia (33% vs <1%); grade 3 ifosfamide-related encephalopathy occurred in 4%; there was no excess of toxic deaths. Data cannot be extrapolated to patients older than 60 years given the regimen's myelosuppression.

records.title: GeDDiS
records.subtitle: STS · Advanced soft tissue — first-line · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body: Adults and adolescents (≥13y) with histologically confirmed, high-grade (Trojani 2/3), locally advanced or metastatic soft-tissue sarcoma with disease progression before enrolment; first-line setting (no prior chemotherapy for sarcoma, no prior doxorubicin for any cancer); excluded alveolar soft part sarcoma, GIST, Ewing's, rhabdomyosarcoma and several other specified histologies Doxorubicin 75 mg/m² IV day 1 every 3 weeks vs gemcitabine 675 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8 plus docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV day 8 every 3 weeks; both arms up to six cycles, stopped for disease progression, intolerable side-effects or withdrawal of consent Primary: Proportion of patients alive and progression-free at 24 weeks (intention-to-treat population). Secondary: proportion of patients alive and progression free at 12 weeks, PFS, OS, ORR (RECIST 1.1 and Choi criteria), assessment of adverse events, quality of life, and health economics evaluation. Gemcitabine/docetaxel was not superior to doxorubicin as first-line therapy for advanced soft-tissue sarcoma; the primary endpoint of 24-week progression-free survival was not met for superiority (doxorubicin 46.3% vs gemcitabine/docetaxel 46.4%; median PFS 23.3 vs 23.7 weeks; HR 1.28, 95% CI 0.99–1.65, p=0.06). Overall survival did not differ (median 76.3 vs 67.3 weeks; HR 1.14, 95% CI 0.83–1.57, p=0.41). Planned exploratory subgroup analyses found no histological subtype, including leiomyosarcoma, with superior benefit from gemcitabine/docetaxel. Gemcitabine/docetaxel had worse treatment adherence (lower dose intensity, more delays, more early discontinuation for toxicity) and grade 3–4 fatigue (14% vs 6%), while doxorubicin had more grade 3–4 febrile neutropenia (20% vs 12%) and oral mucositis (14% vs 2%). No deaths were treatment-related; two deaths reflected a combination of progression and treatment.

records.title: ANNOUNCE (Tap)
records.subtitle: STS · Advanced soft tissue — first-line · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2020
records.body: Anthracycline-naive advanced STS Olaratumab 20 mg/kg IV cycle 1 (loading), then 15 mg/kg IV, days 1 and 8 Q3W + doxorubicin 75 mg/m² IV day 1, up to 8 21-day cycles, then olaratumab monotherapy to progression vs doxorubicin 75 mg/m² IV day 1 + placebo, up to 8 cycles Overall survival (total STS and leiomyosarcoma) No OS benefit (total STS HR 1.05, 20.4 vs 19.7 months; LMS HR 0.95). The confirmatory trial refuted the earlier phase II signal and olaratumab was withdrawn. Defining negative.

records.title: Trabectedin vs dacarbazine (Demetri)
records.subtitle: STS · Advanced soft tissue — later-line & histology-specific · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body: Metastatic liposarcoma / leiomyosarcoma after anthracycline + ≥1 line Trabectedin vs dacarbazine Overall survival PFS 4.2 vs 1.5 months (HR 0.55, p<0.001); OS non-significant (12.4 vs 12.9 months). Approval for L-sarcomas on disease control.

records.title: Eribulin vs dacarbazine (Schöffski)
records.subtitle: STS · Advanced soft tissue — later-line & histology-specific · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body: Advanced liposarcoma / leiomyosarcoma after ≥2 regimens Eribulin vs dacarbazine Overall survival OS 13.5 vs 11.5 months (HR 0.77, p=0.017); benefit driven by liposarcoma. Approval (liposarcoma after anthracycline).

records.title: SPEARHEAD-1 (afami-cel, D’Angelo)
records.subtitle: STS · Advanced soft tissue — later-line & histology-specific · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2024
records.body: HLA-A*02, MAGE-A4+ advanced synovial sarcoma / myxoid round-cell liposarcoma, pre-treated Afamitresgene autoleucel — single IV infusion day 1 (transduced dose 1.0–10.0×10⁹ T cells) after lymphodepletion (fludarabine 30 mg/m² IV days −7 to −4 + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² IV days −5 to −3); one infusion only, no re-treatment (single-arm) Overall response rate ORR 37% overall, 39% in synovial sarcoma, durable in heavily pre-treated patients. Basis for the first engineered TCR T-cell therapy approved in a solid tumour (synovial sarcoma). Phase II, single-arm registration study.

records.title: Atezolizumab in ASPS (Chen / Van Tine)
records.subtitle: STS · Advanced soft tissue — later-line & histology-specific · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2023
records.body: Advanced alveolar soft part sarcoma (adult + paediatric) Atezolizumab (anti-PD-L1), single-arm Objective response rate ORR 37% (1 complete, 18 partial responses), responses durable. First and only approved systemic therapy for ASPS — a low-mutation sarcoma that is nonetheless immunotherapy-responsive. Phase II, single-arm registration trial.

records.title: AMPECT (nab-sirolimus, Wagner)
records.subtitle: STS · Advanced soft tissue — later-line & histology-specific · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2021
records.body: Advanced malignant PEComa nab-Sirolimus 100 mg/m² IV over 30 min days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle (once weekly ×2, Q3W), to progression, toxicity, or patient preference (single-arm) Objective response rate ORR 39%, durable; responses enriched in TSC1/TSC2-mutant tumours (89% vs 13%). First approved therapy for malignant PEComa. Phase II, single-arm registration trial.

records.title: SARC041
records.subtitle: STS · Advanced soft tissue — later-line & histology-specific · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Recurrent or metastatic dedifferentiated liposarcoma with RECIST progression within 6 months; any number of prior systemic therapies Abemaciclib 200 mg orally twice daily vs matching placebo Progression-free survival Abemaciclib improved median PFS (9.67 vs 1.52 months; HR 0.39, 95% CI 0.25–0.59; P<0.001). ORR was 9.3% vs 0% (P=0.057); median OS was not reached vs 25.45 months (HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.28–1.07; P=0.077). Grade ≥3 adverse-event rates were similar and no new safety signals emerged.

records.title: PALETTE
records.subtitle: STS · Advanced soft tissue — later-line & histology-specific · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2012
records.body: Metastatic non-adipocytic soft-tissue sarcoma (excluding GIST and other listed subtypes) with RECIST progression after anthracycline-containing therapy; angiogenesis-inhibitor-naive; ≤4 prior lines; PS 0–1 Pazopanib 800 mg orally once daily vs placebo, continued until disease progression, unacceptable toxic effects, withdrawal of consent, or death; no crossover Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, response rate, safety, quality of life Pazopanib significantly prolonged PFS vs placebo in pretreated metastatic non-adipocytic STS. Median PFS 4.6 mo (95% CI 3.7–4.8) vs 1.6 mo (0.9–1.8), HR 0.31 (95% CI 0.24–0.40; p<0.0001, ITT, independent review, cutoff Nov 22, 2010). Final OS (cutoff Oct 24, 2011) not significant: 12.5 mo (10.6–14.8) vs 10.7 mo (8.7–12.8), HR 0.86 (0.67–1.11; p=0.25). Confirmed partial response 6% vs 0%. Frequent toxicities: fatigue 65%, diarrhoea 58%, hypertension 41%; 8 fatal SAEs on pazopanib (1 possibly drug-related). Global QOL not significantly different; QOL data only collected to 12 weeks.
records.keywords: van der Graaf et al. Lancet 2012; 379: 1879–86.  22595799

records.title: MANEUVER
records.subtitle: STS · Advanced soft tissue — later-line & histology-specific · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Histologically confirmed symptomatic TGCT, unresectable (extensively invasive, complex anatomical site, not completely resectable, or surgery risking dysfunction/serious complications per two experts); adults ≥18 with worst stiffness or worst pain ≥4/10 within 2 weeks before randomisation; measurable disease per RECIST v1.1 with ≥1 lesion ≥2 cm by MRI; excluded if previously treated with CSF-1/CSF-1R inhibitors (prior imatinib/nilotinib allowed) Pimicotinib 50 mg orally once daily (no food restrictions) in 28-day cycles for 24 weeks (six cycles) vs matching placebo; after part 1, completers continue/cross over to open-label pimicotinib 50 mg once daily for 24 weeks (part 2), then long-term open-label extension (part 3) Primary: Objective response rate at week 25 (BIRC per RECIST v1.1, ITT). Secondary: Objective response rate at week 25 (BIRC per tumour volume score), Relative range of motion change from baseline, Worst stiffness NRS score change from baseline, BPI worst pain NRS score change from baseline, PROMIS-PF score change from baseline, EQ-5D-5L visual analogue scale change from baseline, BPI-30 response rate, Safety (treatment-emergent adverse events) MANEUVER supports pimicotinib as a selective systemic option providing early and robust tumour reduction with a manageable safety profile in adults with TGCT. ORR at week 25 by BIRC/RECIST v1.1 (ITT) was 54% (34/63) with pimicotinib vs 3% (1/31) with placebo (absolute difference 51% [95% CI 33–63], p<0.0001); all key secondary endpoints were met, including ORR by tumour volume score 62% vs 3% (difference 59% [41–70]) and significant improvements in range of motion, stiffness, pain, PROMIS-PF and EQ-5D-5L. Grade 3/4 events in 22/35% pimicotinib patients, most commonly CPK increase (8/13%); no deaths, no cholestatic hepatotoxicity/DILI or hypopigmentation; dose reductions 5 (8%) and discontinuation 1 (2%) of 63. Duration of response not reached; median duration of exposure 169 days.

records.title: ANGIOTAX
records.subtitle: STS · Advanced soft tissue — later-line & histology-specific · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2008
records.body: Histologically proven metastatic or locally advanced unresectable angiosarcoma not amenable to radiotherapy or curative-intent surgery; any prior systemic therapy allowed; measurable or assessable RECIST disease; WHO performance status ≤2 and weight loss <20%; excluded: more than two prior chemotherapy lines, Kaposi's sarcoma or positive HIV serology, hepatic failure, paclitaxel/cremophor allergy (single-arm) Paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 IV 60-minute infusion on days 1, 8 and 15 of each 4-week cycle, six cycles total unless disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; dose reduced to 70 mg/m2, then 60 mg/m2, after grade 3-4 toxicity Primary: Nonprogression rate after two cycles. Secondary: Response rate at four cycles, Response rate at six cycles, Toxicity, Overall survival, Median time to progression Weekly paclitaxel at this dose schedule was well tolerated and demonstrated clinical benefit in unresectable angiosarcoma (single-arm phase II; no comparative claim). Nonprogression rate after two cycles 74% (95% CI, 57% to 90%); with median follow-up 8 months, median time to progression 4 months and median overall survival 8 months (7.6 months in discussion); OS at 6/12/18 months 56%/38%/21%. Five patients (18.5%) of 27 assessable had a partial response after two cycles; three with locally advanced breast angiosarcoma became amenable to curative-intent surgery, two with complete histologic response. One toxic death from thrombocytopenia; six grade 3 and one grade 4 toxicity; anemia and fatigue most frequent
records.keywords: Penel et al. J Clin Oncol 2008;26:5269-5274  18809609

records.title: DeFi (nirogacestat, Gounder)
records.subtitle: STS · Borderline / locally aggressive · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body: Progressing desmoid tumours (aggressive fibromatosis) Nirogacestat 150 mg orally twice daily, continuous in 28-day cycles, to progression vs placebo Progression-free survival PFS HR 0.29 (p<0.001); 2-year event-free 76% vs 44%; ORR 41% vs 8%. First approved systemic therapy for desmoid tumours.

records.title: Sorafenib for desmoid (Gounder, Alliance A091105)
records.subtitle: STS · Borderline / locally aggressive · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body: Desmoid tumour requiring treatment: unresectable or high-morbidity surgery, progressive, or symptomatic; about half newly diagnosed Sorafenib vs placebo (crossover allowed) Progression-free survival 2-year PFS 81% vs 36% (HR 0.13, 95% CI 0.05–0.31, p<0.001) in 84 of 87 randomised, but the trial was halted and unblinded after the DSMB requested an efficacy analysis at the preplanned interim, when 24 of the 52 required events had been observed, leaving the reported result on 29 events, so the effect size is likely overstated. ORR 33% vs 20% is reported descriptively, with no comparative test; the authors read the 20% placebo response as support for an initial period of observation in newly diagnosed disease. Established a systemic option for desmoid (predates nirogacestat).

records.title: ENLIVEN (pexidartinib, Tap)
records.subtitle: STS · Borderline / locally aggressive · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body: Advanced tenosynovial giant cell tumour not amenable to surgery Pexidartinib (CSF1R inhibitor) vs placebo Overall response at week 25 ORR 39% vs 0% (p<0.0001) with functional improvement; mixed/cholestatic hepatotoxicity is an identified risk. First systemic therapy for TGCT.

records.title: GENSARC
records.subtitle: STS · Molecular DIAGNOSTICS & PRECISION ONCOLOGY · Prospective cohort study · 2016
records.body: Patients whose biopsy or resection was reviewed by a French sarcoma-expert pathologist and raised a certain, probable or possible diagnosis of DFSP, dedifferentiated liposarcoma, Ewing family tumour, synovial sarcoma, alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma, or myxoid/round-cell liposarcoma; frozen tissue was required except for DFSP. Histology/IHC diagnosis by a sarcoma-expert pathologist, masked to focused molecular testing; final diagnosis integrated clinical, pathological and assay results across six suspected-histotype cohorts (n=384; no comparator) Primary: Not formally designated; diagnosis modification and expert-board-assessed clinical effect of focused molecular testing. Secondary: FFPE-versus-frozen assay performance; planned economic effect; molecular findings by diagnostic certainty and selected histotype Focused, entity-directed molecular testing changed the integrated diagnosis in 53/384 selected cases (13.8%). Changes occurred in 8/50 suspected DFSP, 7/30 dedifferentiated liposarcoma, 13/112 Ewing-family tumour, 16/97 synovial sarcoma, 7/46 alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma and 2/49 myxoid/round-cell liposarcoma. An expert board judged 45/53 changes to affect management or prognostic assessment, but this was not documented treatment delivery or outcome. All patients had one of six molecularly characterized diagnoses raised before testing, and assays were focused rather than broad NGS. The final diagnosis incorporated the molecular result without an independent reference standard; no comparative survival, quality-of-life, cost or cost-effectiveness result was reported.

records.title: Sreenath 2026 RNA-NGS Workflow
records.subtitle: STS · Molecular DIAGNOSTICS & PRECISION ONCOLOGY · Prospective cohort study · 2026
records.body: All-age patients with histologically confirmed bone or soft-tissue sarcoma selected by a specialist MDT for RNA-NGS, particularly for ambiguous histology, atypical clinicopathologic/IHC findings, negative FISH, or possible therapeutic targets; localized and advanced disease were included. MDT-selected targeted RNA-based NGS integrated with histopathology and immunohistochemistry (single cohort; no comparator) Primary: Not formally designated; diagnostic confirmation or reclassification after integrated RNA-NGS. Secondary: Testing completion and alteration detection; diagnostic yield by morphology; treatment-plan change; potentially actionable alterations and matched-treatment delivery; workflow feasibility and assay cost Integrated RNA-NGS reclassified 28/68 evaluable diagnoses (41.1%): 11/16 initially round-cell, 4/19 undifferentiated and 13/33 other-subtype cases. This was an MDT-selected diagnostically difficult cohort, not universal testing; no independent reference diagnosis or diagnostic-accuracy comparison was used. The paper's treatment-impact reporting is irreconcilable: 18/68 in the abstract/Table 5, 15/68 in Discussion, approximately 19% without a numerator in the Context box, and subgroup counts totaling 12/68. Potentially actionable KIT or PIK3CA findings were reported in 5.8% of 68 evaluable patients, without a reported numerator. The only genotype-matched treatment described was for one RAF1-positive DFSP case previously published separately; RAF1 was not part of that KIT/PIK3CA category. Survival and comparative outcomes were not assessed.

records.title: WIDE Sarcoma WGS
records.subtitle: STS · Molecular DIAGNOSTICS & PRECISION ONCOLOGY · Prospective cohort study · 2022
records.body: Eighty-three adults with a suspected sarcoma selected from the prospective WIDE implementation study at the Netherlands Cancer Institute, a tertiary sarcoma referral centre; all had advanced or suspected metastatic disease and underwent a tissue-retrieval procedure or had fresh-frozen archival tissue available. Single prospective WGS implementation cohort (n=83); no assigned treatment or comparator Primary: Not formally designated; clinical effect of adding WGS to the diagnostic work-up. Secondary: Diagnostic revision; standard-treatment-plan change; experimental treatment opportunities and delivery; germline findings; prior diagnostic procedures WGS integration revised the diagnosis in 12/83 selected patients (14%). Six revisions followed characteristic molecular events, three suspected sarcomas were reclassified as melanoma, and one presumed wild-type GIST had a large KIT exon 11 deletion missed by prior amplicon testing. The article reports treatment-plan changes inconsistently as 7 in Results and 8 in the Abstract/Discussion. The experimental-opportunity analysis is labelled n=80, yet the article reports 30 patients as 36% (30/83); 8/30 started biomarker-based experimental treatment, with no response or duration data. Paired blood WGS found 8 pathogenic germline variants in 7/83 patients; return of selected findings required opt-in. This was a diagnostically enriched referral cohort without a testing comparator, blinded reference diagnosis or clinical-outcome analysis.

records.title: STS Whole-Genome Sequencing (van der Laan)
records.subtitle: STS · Molecular DIAGNOSTICS & PRECISION ONCOLOGY · Observational cohort study · 2025
records.body: Patients evaluated at the Netherlands Cancer Institute from February 2017 to February 2023 with primary STS of unfavourable prognosis, metastatic STS, or STS for which broad molecular diagnostics were considered necessary. Of 201 selected for WGS, 161 remained after failed sequencing and exclusion/reclassification of GIST, benign and non-STS tumours. Single observational WGS cohort (201 selected; 161 STS with successful WGS retained); no assigned treatment or comparator Primary: Not formally designated; genomic alteration linked to a systemic therapy or clinical trial available in the Netherlands at the time of WGS. Secondary: Target prevalence overall and by subtype; testing timing; WGS-informed treatment delivery and reasons for non-delivery; tumour mutational load WGS found at least one alteration linked to a therapy or trial available in the Netherlands at the time of WGS in 74/161 patients (46%). Subtype yields included 22/22 DDLPS, 5/5 MPNST, 5/8 angiosarcoma, 12/28 UPS/sarcoma NOS, 7/36 leiomyosarcoma and 0/5 myxoid liposarcoma; all DDLPS were counted because expected CDK4/MDM2 amplification confirmed established biology, not because WGS found a new treatment target. WGS-informed treatment delivery is reported inconsistently as 23/161 in the abstract, conclusion and flow diagram and 22/161 in Results. All treatment occurred in trials; no response, duration, PFS or OS data were available. Among 51 target-positive patients not treated, reported reasons included remaining standard options, no current treatment need, deterioration or poor performance status, study ineligibility or withdrawal, and expected lack of benefit. The study-defined high tumour mutational load threshold was >140 mutations/genome, not TMB >=10 mut/Mb.

records.title: European Multicentre Sarcoma NGS Cohort
records.subtitle: STS · Molecular DIAGNOSTICS & PRECISION ONCOLOGY · Retrospective cohort study · 2025
records.body: Retrospective cohort of 694 bone/soft-tissue sarcoma patients (reported as 694 samples) from six sarcoma-expert centres in Greece, Poland and Spain, tested during 2008-2023 with centre-selected diagnostic and/or therapeutic NGS at MDT discretion; 58.1% had localized and 38.3% metastatic disease; ages 0-89 years. Retrospective non-comparative MDT-selected diagnostic and/or therapeutic NGS using heterogeneous centre-specific DNA/RNA panels (n=694) Primary: Not formally designated; diagnostic reclassification and therapeutic actionability of NGS. Secondary: Alteration frequency and class; OncoKB and investigator-defined potential actionability; matched-treatment delivery and duration; objective response NGS changed the diagnosis in 62/694 patients (8.9%), but the number receiving a diagnostic panel was not reported; 31/62 had a pathognomonic alteration. Results state that diagnostic change affected treatment strategy in 24 cases, whereas Discussion says 8/694 were led to a different approach. The authors reported 135 OncoKB-actionable findings (19.5% of 694 patients) plus four investigator-actionable findings; patient-level uniqueness was not established. Only 21/135 were level 1; named counts total 119/135 and some percentages are irreconcilable. The authors reported NGS-matched therapy in 17/694 patients (2.4% in Results; 2.6% in Discussion); no objective responses were reported. Five were said to benefit, defined as >6 months on treatment, but Table 3 shows only three durations >6 months and two exactly 6 months. Mixed stage, 90 histologies, non-uniform panels and unknown diagnostic-versus-therapeutic panel denominators preclude a uniform yield or causal-benefit estimate.

records.title: Foundation Medicine Sarcoma Profiling Cohort
records.subtitle: STS · Molecular DIAGNOSTICS & PRECISION ONCOLOGY · Retrospective cohort study · 2022
records.body: Patients with 44 soft-tissue, bone or other sarcoma histologies whose clinical tumour specimens underwent routine FoundationOne/FoundationOne Heme profiling during 2012-2018 (n=7,494; all ages); nested MSK clinical-action cohort n=118, with 106 successful tests. Stage, grade and treatment outcomes were unavailable for the full cohort. Single retrospective molecular-profiling cohort (n=7,494), with a nested clinically annotated MSK cohort (n=118; 106 successful tests); no assigned intervention or comparator Primary: Not formally designated; genomic alterations across 7,494 sarcomas. Secondary: Potential molecular diagnostic refinement; OncoKB-defined potential actionability; kinase fusions, TMB, MSI and other genomic features; in the nested MSK cohort, successful profiling, treatment-linked findings, matched treatment and reasons for non-delivery Among 7,494 profiled sarcomas, sequencing suggested that the submitted diagnosis might be incorrect or require review in 789 (10.5%); 126/1,411 sarcoma-NOS cases were molecularly reassigned, without central pathology confirmation. In the MSK subset, 4/106 successful tests changed diagnosis. Potentially actionable alterations were found in 2,372/7,494 (31.7%; OncoKB as of 8 June 2021); 439/7,494 (5.9%) were level 1, concentrated in GIST, and 196/7,494 (2.6%) were potentially actionable kinase fusions. Clinical outcomes came only from a nested n=118 subset; 106 tests succeeded. Clinicians deemed at least one finding treatment-linked in 50/106 patients; 31/106 enrolled in a matched trial or received off-label therapy. Figure 5c accounts for 49/50 cases (31 treated; 18 not treated), leaving one unreconciled. No cohort ORR, PFS or OS was reported; Figure 6 shows selected anecdotes, three outside n=118. Full-cohort stage, grade and outcomes were unavailable; there was no comparator.

records.title: ProfiLER-01 sarcoma cohort
records.subtitle: STS · Molecular DIAGNOSTICS & PRECISION ONCOLOGY · Prospective cohort study · 2020
records.body: 164 patients aged 6.8-84.6 years with locally advanced or metastatic soft-tissue sarcoma, bone sarcoma or GIST selected from 2,579 advanced-cancer ProfiLER-01 participants; all had progressed after at least one standard line, lacked curative options and had available tumour tissue. 59- or 69-gene tumour DNA NGS plus genome-wide aCGH → weekly molecular tumour board → optional off-label or trial molecular-based recommended therapy (single cohort) Primary: Frequency and distribution of relevant genomic alterations and molecular-tumour-board treatment recommendations. Secondary: Profiling feasibility; recommended-treatment delivery; best response, PFS and OS among treated patients; OS from metastatic diagnosis Of 164 selected patients, 158 were successfully profiled; 106/158 (67%) had at least one study-defined relevant alteration. The MTB issued 61 treatment recommendations to 47/158 patients (30%; 44% of 106 alteration-positive patients). Recommended therapy was delivered to 13/47 (28%; 8% of 158 profiled). Among 34 recommended patients not treated, standard care was favoured in 20 and clinical contraindications prevented treatment in six; remaining reasons were not fully enumerated. In the 13 treated patients, best response was 1 PR, 4 SD and 8 PD; the PR lasted no more than 3 months, median PFS was 2.3 months and median OS 6.1 months from treatment initiation. One selected chondrosarcoma had SD for 33.6 months. The 59/69-gene DNA panel plus aCGH did not initially detect oncogenic fusions, and 88/158 used archival tissue. With no comparator, the authors could not demonstrate benefit and advised against routine molecular screening outside trials.

records.title: Chinese Multicentre Sarcoma RNA Sequencing Cohort
records.subtitle: STS · Molecular DIAGNOSTICS & PRECISION ONCOLOGY · Retrospective cohort study · 2025
records.body: Retrospective multicentre Chinese cohort of 788 soft-tissue or bone sarcoma samples with an initial pathological diagnosis; available tumour specimens underwent targeted RNA Fusioncapture integrated with histopathology/IHC and retrieved DNA-NGS, including definite, unclassified and NOS groups. Paired targeted RNA Fusioncapture and DNA Onco PanScan profiling integrated with histopathology/IHC review Primary: Not prespecified; fusion detection and pathological classification after targeted RNA sequencing. Secondary: Concordance with DNA-NGS across shared targets; fusions outside DNA-panel coverage; diagnostic confirmation or reclassification; author-assigned potential therapeutic relevance; profiling success in degraded specimens The cohort comprised 595 pathologically definite, 43 unclassified and 150 NOS sarcomas (n=788). Across 28 genes shared by both panels, 115 fusion calls were reported: 100 by both assays, 7 DNA-only and 8 RNA-only; all 5/8 RNA-only calls tested were confirmed, while 4/7 DNA-only calls were tested (2 FISH-negative; 2 FISH-positive but IHC-negative). The broader RNA panel found 281 additional fusions in 221/788 samples (28.0%) outside DNA-panel coverage; this chiefly reflects panel breadth, not RNA-versus-DNA sensitivity for equal targets. Integrated expert review reclassified 94/788 cases (11.9%): 61/595 initially definite and 33/150 NOS; review was not blinded to the molecular result and had no independent reference diagnosis. The source separately labels 105/788 as diagnostic confirmations. Author-assigned potentially targetable cases increased from 26/788 (3.3%) with DNA alone to 51/788 (6.5%) with RNA plus DNA, without a formal comparison or matched-treatment or outcome data.

records.title: MULTISARC
records.subtitle: STS · Molecular DIAGNOSTICS & PRECISION ONCOLOGY · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: ESMO 2024 preliminary analysis of 439 adults with advanced soft-tissue sarcoma enrolled between October 2019 and October 2023; randomization-arm denominators, profiling-success denominator and follow-up were not reported in the abstract. NGS strategy: exome and RNA sequencing, national molecular-tumour-board review, and offer of a matched phase 2 substudy when an alteration and relevant treatment were available vs No-NGS strategy: standard management without sequencing-guided treatment assignment under the randomized strategy Primary: Feasibility of high-throughput exome and RNA profiling in advanced soft-tissue sarcoma. Secondary: Survival outcomes of the randomized strategy; efficacy and safety of single-arm matched-treatment substudies; molecular alteration and fusion landscape The ESMO 2024 preliminary analysis reported 439 enrolled patients but no randomized-arm denominators, profiling-success denominator or follow-up. In the NGS arm, 314 alterations across 62 genes and 47 fusions were reported; the abstract prints "SS12::SSX1," likely a typographical error that is retained here as printed. Forty-seven percent of NGS-arm patients had at least one alteration classified as targetable, but the denominator and evidence-tier definition were not reported. Thirty-six percent of this targetable group received an NGS-selected investigational agent; no numerator, denominator, reasons for non-delivery or full-group outcomes were given. In the single-arm durvalumab-olaparib substudy, 8/26 were progression-free at six months (30.8%; source reports 32%). The abstract reported no arm-specific feasibility rate, PFS, OS, ORR, safety or comparative NGS-versus-no-NGS estimate. These are preliminary molecular and substudy data, not a completed randomized strategy result.

records.title: EURAMOS-1
records.subtitle: Bone · Osteosarcoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body: Newly diagnosed, resectable high-grade localised or metastatic extremity or axial osteosarcoma aged 40 years or younger; poor histologic response (≥10% viable tumour) to preoperative MAP; macroscopically complete resection of primary, randomisation within 35 days of surgery, no local or metastatic progression Postoperative MAP: cisplatin 120 mg/m², doxorubicin 37·5 mg/m²/day on days 1–2, high-dose methotrexate 12 g/m², 29 weeks (cisplatin capped at cumulative 480 mg/m²) vs MAPIE: MAP plus ifosfamide 14 g/m² at 2·8 g/m²/day with mesna followed by etoposide 100 mg/m²/day on days 1–5 (three cycles), then two ifosfamide 9 g/m² cycles Primary: Event-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, Short-term toxicity, Long-term toxicity, Quality of life Intensifying postoperative chemotherapy with ifosfamide/etoposide in poor responders did not improve event-free survival (HR 0·98, 95% CI 0·78–1·23; 3-year EFS 55% vs 53%; RMST difference 0·8 months) and added toxicity; the authors argue strongly against adding MAPIE, defining MAP as standard of care. Overall survival immature (HR 0·97). More febrile neutropenia (50% vs 73%) and grade 4 non-haematological toxicity (12% vs 24%) with MAPIE; two deaths during postoperative therapy

records.title: INT-0091 (Grier)
records.subtitle: Bone · Ewing sarcoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2003
records.body: Newly diagnosed Ewing sarcoma / PNET of bone Standard VDC (+ dactinomycin) vs VDC alternating with ifosfamide + etoposide (VDC/IE) Event-free survival In non-metastatic disease, VDC/IE improved 5-year EFS 54%→69% (p=0.005) and OS 61%→72% (p=0.01); no benefit in metastatic disease. Established VDC/IE as the chemotherapy backbone.

records.title: AEWS0031 (Womer)
records.subtitle: Bone · Ewing sarcoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2012
records.body: Localised Ewing sarcoma Interval-compressed VDC/IE every 2 weeks vs every 3 weeks Event-free survival Dose-dense scheduling improved 5-year EFS 65%→73% (p=0.048) with no added toxicity. Established interval compression as the standard for localised Ewing.

records.title: rEECur (McCabe)
records.subtitle: Bone · Ewing sarcoma · Randomised clinical trial (phase II/III) · 2022
records.body: Recurrent / primary refractory Ewing sarcoma, age 4–50 High-dose ifosfamide vs topotecan + cyclophosphamide (4-arm RCT; also irinotecan/temozolomide, gemcitabine/docetaxel) Event-free survival High-dose ifosfamide outperformed topotecan + cyclophosphamide (median OS 16.8 vs 10.4 months; EFS 5.7 vs 3.7 months). First randomised trial in relapsed/refractory Ewing; positions high-dose ifosfamide as preferred salvage. Conference abstract (ASCO 2022) — full publication pending.

records.title: GELA LNH98-5
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Establishing R-CHOP immunochemotherapy · Randomised clinical trial · 2002
records.body:
Diffuse large-B-cell lymphoma (REAL or WHO classification); previously untreated; age 60 to 80 years, stage II, III or IV, ECOG performance status 0 to 2, fit for eight courses of CHOP; excluded T-cell lymphoma, history of indolent lymphoma, CNS involvement, cardiac contraindication to doxorubicin, neurologic contraindication to vincristine, HIV-positive or unresolved hepatitis B Ⓐ Rituximab 375 mg/m² on day 1 of each CHOP cycle + CHOP
Ⓑ CHOP alone
・CHOP: Cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m² day 1, doxorubicin 50 mg/m² day 1, vincristine 1.4 mg/m² (max 2 mg) day 1, prednisone 40 mg/m² per day for five days; every three weeks
・Duration: Eight cycles, stopped earlier for progression, patient decline or investigator decision; rituximab stopped when CHOP stopped; no radiotherapy scheduled Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, response rate, toxicity, disease-free survival, progression-free survival Adding rituximab to CHOP improved event-free, progression-free, disease-free and overall survival vs CHOP alone in elderly DLBCL, maintained at 5-year follow-up
・EFS: 5-yr Ⓐ 47% vs Ⓑ 29%; median Ⓐ 3.8 vs Ⓑ 1.1 yr; P=.00002
・OS: 5-yr Ⓐ 58% vs Ⓑ 45%; median Ⓐ NR vs Ⓑ 3.1 yr; P=.0073
・PFS: 5-yr Ⓐ 54% vs Ⓑ 30%; median Ⓐ NR vs Ⓑ 1 yr; P<.00001
・DFS: 5-yr Ⓐ 66% vs Ⓑ 45%; median Ⓐ NR vs Ⓑ 2.45 yr; P=.00031
・CR/CRu: Ⓐ 76% vs Ⓑ 63%; P=0.005
・Subgroups: 5-yr OS low-risk aaIPI Ⓐ 80% vs Ⓑ 62% (P=.023); high-risk Ⓐ 48% vs Ⓑ 39% (P=.062); EFS/PFS benefit in both
・Salvage: Non-randomised; 2-yr survival after relapse 58% with rituximab-containing vs 24% with non-rituximab salvage
・Toxicity: G3–4 infection Ⓐ 12% vs Ⓑ 20%; G3–4 cardiac 8% in both; G3–4 rituximab infusion reactions 9% in Ⓐ; non-lymphoma deaths Ⓐ 21 vs Ⓑ 13 (2-yr report)
・Toxicity (5-yr): Post-treatment infections Ⓐ 12 vs Ⓑ 6; deaths in CR Ⓐ 8% vs Ⓑ 2.5% (P=.33); cardiovascular deaths Ⓐ 9 vs Ⓑ 1; second tumours Ⓐ 9 vs Ⓑ 10
・Limitations: Age 60 to 80 only; 5-yr update reports log-rank P values, no hazard ratios
records.keywords: Coiffier et al. N Engl J Med 2002;346:235-242  11807147 Feugier et al. J Clin Oncol 2005;23:4117-4126  15867204

records.title: MInT (MabThera International Trial)
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Establishing R-CHOP immunochemotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2006
records.body:
Untreated CD20-positive diffuse large-B-cell lymphoma (WHO criteria, local pathologist); first-line; age 18–60 years with no or one age-adjusted IPI risk factor and stage II–IV disease, or stage I with bulk (bulk defined by cooperative-group cut-off >5 cm, >7·5 cm or >10 cm); excluded primary CNS or gastrointestinal MALT lymphoma, secondary lymphoma after prior chemotherapy/radiotherapy, HIV and post-transplant lymphoproliferative disease Ⓐ Six cycles of CHOP-like chemotherapy (country-chosen CHOP-21, CHOEP-21, MACOP-B or PMitCEBO) plus rituximab 375 mg/m² IV on days 1, 22, 43, 64, 85 and 106
Ⓑ Six cycles of CHOP-like chemotherapy (country-chosen CHOP-21, CHOEP-21, MACOP-B or PMitCEBO) alone
・Radiotherapy: 30–40 Gy to primary bulky sites, and to primary extranodal sites at physician discretion Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: complete response rate, progression under therapy, progression-free survival, overall survival, frequency of toxic effects, relapse-free survival Adding rituximab to CHOP-like chemotherapy improved EFS and OS in young, good-prognosis DLBCL patients; trial stopped early for benefit
・EFS: Ⓐ 79% vs Ⓑ 59% at 3 yr; difference 20% (log-rank p<0·0001)
・OS: Ⓐ 93% vs Ⓑ 84% at 3 yr (p=0·0001)
・PFS: Ⓐ 85% vs Ⓑ 68% at 3 yr
・CR/CRu: Ⓐ 86% vs Ⓑ 68% of response-evaluable patients
・Subgroups: With rituximab, IPI=0/no-bulk had better 3-yr EFS than IPI=1 and/or bulk (89% vs 76%) but not OS
・Other: CHOEP-21 vs CHOP-21 EFS advantage not seen with rituximab (p=0·52); not a trial endpoint
・Toxicity: Grade 3/4 AEs Ⓐ 37% vs Ⓑ 41%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 6 vs Ⓑ 1 (p=0·123)
・Limitations: Trial stopped early after first interim analysis crossed α-spending boundary

records.title: RICOVER-60
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Establishing R-CHOP immunochemotherapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2008
records.body:
Untreated aggressive CD20+ B-cell lymphoma, aged 61-80. 1,242 were enrolled and 1,222 randomly assigned after 20 were excluded for missing or retracted consent Ⓐ 6 cycles CHOP-14
Ⓑ 8 cycles CHOP-14
Ⓒ 6 cycles R-CHOP-14 (rituximab 375 mg/m² × 8 bi-weekly doses added to CHOP-14)
Ⓓ 8 cycles R-CHOP-14 (rituximab 375 mg/m² × 8 bi-weekly doses added to CHOP-14)
・Pre-phase: Vincristine 1 mg IV + prednisone 100 mg PO for 7 days
・CHOP-14: Cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m² IV, doxorubicin 50 mg/m² IV, vincristine 2 mg IV day 1, prednisone 100 mg PO days 1-5, every 2 weeks with G-CSF
・Radiotherapy: 36 Gy to initial bulky (≥7.5 cm) or extranodal sites Primary: 3-year event-free survival.
