Secondary: response, progression during treatment, frequency of toxic effects, progression-free survival, overall survival, treatment-associated deaths, second malignancies Six cycles of R-CHOP-14 improved EFS, PFS and OS over six cycles of CHOP-14; eight cycles were not better than six
・3-yr EFS: Ⓐ 47.2% vs Ⓑ 53.0% vs Ⓒ 66.5% vs Ⓓ 63.1%
・3-yr OS: Ⓐ 67.7% vs Ⓑ 66.0% vs Ⓒ 78.1% vs Ⓓ 72.5%; adjusted OS RR vs Ⓐ 0.63 (95% CI 0.46-0.85) for Ⓒ, 0.78 (0.58-1.05) for Ⓓ
・Toxicity: Treatment-related deaths (mostly infection) 8% with eight-cycle regimens vs 7% with six-cycle regimens; anaemia, mucositis, transfusions and antibiotic use more frequent with eight cycles
・Limitations: Stopped early at second interim analysis; median observation 34.5 mo

records.title: R-CHOP-14 v 21 (NCRI)
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Schedule & elderly / frail adaptations · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2013
records.body:
Histologically confirmed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (WHO); previously untreated, first-line, adults aged ≥18 years of all age and risk groups; Ann Arbor bulky stage IA (tumour mass diameter >10 cm) or stage IB–IV, WHO performance status 0–2; excluded T-cell lymphoma, transformed follicular lymphoma or history of indolent lymphoma, CNS involvement, HIV/hepatitis B/C positivity, heart failure or uncontrolled angina, active malignancy in the preceding 10 years Ⓐ R-CHOP-14: IV rituximab 375 mg/m², cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m², doxorubicin 50 mg/m², vincristine 2 mg day 1 + oral prednisolone 100 mg days 1–5, every 14 days for 6 cycles → 2 further rituximab 375 mg/m² infusions every 14 days; mandatory lenograstim (G-CSF) days 4–12 of each cycle
Ⓑ R-CHOP-21: IV rituximab 375 mg/m², cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m², doxorubicin 50 mg/m², vincristine 1·4 mg/m² (maximum 2 mg) day 1 + oral prednisolone 40 mg/m² days 1–5, every 21 days for 8 cycles; G-CSF at investigator discretion Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, toxicity, response rate, complete or unconfirmed complete response rate, treatment-related deaths, prognostic and predictive subgroup/biomarker analyses R-CHOP-14 did not improve 2-year OS or PFS compared with R-CHOP-21 in previously untreated DLBCL
・OS: Ⓐ 82·7% vs Ⓑ 80·8% at 2 years; HR 0·90 (95% CI 0·70–1·15); p=0·3763
・PFS: Ⓐ 75·4% vs Ⓑ 74·8% at 2 years; HR 0·94 (95% CI 0·76–1·17)
・Subgroups: No molecular or clinical subgroup benefited from dose intensification
・Toxicity: Grade 3/4 neutropenia Ⓐ 31% vs Ⓑ 60%; febrile neutropenia Ⓐ 5% vs Ⓑ 11%; grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia Ⓐ 9% vs Ⓑ 5%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 9 vs Ⓑ 3 (not significant)
・Limitations: Not powered for non-inferiority; statistical plan amended after fewer OS events than expected

records.title: LYSA LNH03-7B
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Schedule & elderly / frail adaptations · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2011
records.body:
Untreated histologically proven CD20+ diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (WHO); age >80 years; Ann Arbor stage I bulky (mass ≥10 cm) to IV, age-adjusted IPI 1–3, ECOG PS ≤2, life expectancy ≥3 months; excluded other lymphoma subtypes, prior indolent lymphoma, CNS/meningeal involvement, creatinine >150 μmol/L, cancer within past 5 years (single-arm) R-miniCHOP every 3 weeks: rituximab 375 mg/m², cyclophosphamide 400 mg/m², doxorubicin 25 mg/m², vincristine 1 mg on day 1; oral prednisone 40 mg/m² days 1–5
・Duration: Six cycles Primary: overall survival. Secondary: response to treatment, event-free survival, disease-free survival, progression-free survival, safety R-miniCHOP showed activity in patients aged >80 years with DLBCL, with median OS 29 mo; comparative benefit unestablished
・OS: Median 29 mo; 2-yr OS 59%; median follow-up 20 mo
・PFS: Median 21 mo; 2-yr PFS 47%
・ORR: 73% at end of treatment; CR/CRu 62%
・DFS: 2-yr 57% among patients with CR/CRu
・Prognostic factor: Serum albumin ≤35 g/L the only independent OS factor; HR 3·2 (95% CI 1·4–7·1)
・Toxicity: G≥3 neutropenia 40%; febrile neutropenia in 11 patients; 12 treatment-related deaths, most in cycle 1; 108 of 149 completed six cycles
・Limitations: Single-arm, no control; selected patients with ECOG PS ≤2; short follow-up

records.title: FLYER
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Schedule & elderly / frail adaptations · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body:
Previously untreated biopsy-confirmed aggressive CD20-positive B-cell lymphoma; first-line, stage I–II; aged 18–60 years with no age-adjusted IPI risk factor (LDH less than upper limit of normal, ECOG 0–1) and no bulky disease (single or conglomerate tumour <7·5 cm); excluded CNS involvement or primary CNS lymphoma, MALT lymphoma, planned radiotherapy of extranodal involvement Ⓐ Four 21-day cycles of R-CHOP → two cycles of rituximab monotherapy (six rituximab applications in total)
Ⓑ Six 21-day cycles of R-CHOP
・CHOP: Cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m², doxorubicin 50 mg/m², vincristine 1·4 mg/m² (max 2 mg) IV day 1 plus oral prednisone or prednisolone 100 mg days 1–5
・Rituximab: 375 mg/m²
・Design: No radiotherapy except mandatory 30·6 Gy to the contralateral testis for testicular involvement Primary: progression-free survival at 3 years. Secondary: event-free survival, overall survival, complete remission rate, progressive disease rate, safety, serious adverse events, secondary neoplasia rate, protocol adherence, health-economic aspects, relapse rate In young patients with favourable-prognosis aggressive B-cell lymphoma, R-CHOP x4+2 rituximab was non-inferior to R-CHOP x6 for 3-yr PFS, with fewer toxic effects
・PFS (3-yr): Ⓐ 96% (95% CI 94–99) vs Ⓑ 94% (91–97); non-inferior; difference 3%, one-sided 95% CI lower limit 0% vs margin –5·5%
・EFS (3-yr): Ⓐ 89% vs Ⓑ 89%
・OS (3-yr): Ⓐ 99% vs Ⓑ 98%
・Toxicity: Serious AEs Ⓐ 48 vs Ⓑ 45; secondary neoplasms Ⓐ 18 (6%) vs Ⓑ 14 (5%); two therapy-associated deaths (pneumonia), both in Ⓑ
・Limitations: Primary endpoint changed from 3-yr EFS to PFS by 2015 amendment after interim analysis; QoL not assessed systematically

records.title: Dunleavy et al. NCI prospective DA-EPOCH-R study
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Primary MEDIASTINAL B-cell LYMPHOMA · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2013
records.body:
Adults (median age 30, range 19–52) with previously untreated primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma; no prior systemic chemotherapy, HIV-negative; stage I mediastinal masses required ≥5 cm; bulky disease and stage IV allowed, treated without radiotherapy (single-arm) Infusional dose-adjusted EPOCH-R (etoposide, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide, vincristine, prednisone, rituximab) with filgrastim for 6–8 cycles without radiotherapy; >20% tumor shrinkage between cycles 4 and 6 → 8 cycles, ≤20% → stop after 6 cycles Primary: complete response rate, progression-free survival, toxicity. Secondary: event-free survival, overall survival DA-EPOCH-R showed high cure rates and obviated radiotherapy in untreated primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma
・EFS: 93% (95% CI 81–98) at median follow-up 63 months; 3 failures all disease-free after salvage
・OS: 97% (95% CI 81–99)
・RT: Only 2 of 51 (4%) received mediastinal radiotherapy
・Historical comparison: Exploratory vs DA-EPOCH-alone (n=18): EFS 93% vs 67% (P=0.007), OS 97% vs 78% (P=0.01)
・Validation cohort: Independent retrospective Stanford cohort (n=16): EFS 100% (95% CI 79–100) at 37 months
・Toxicity: Fever/neutropenia hospitalization in 13% of 294 cycles; one death from AML in remission at 49 months; no late morbidity or cardiac toxicity
・Limitations: Single-arm phase 2 design; no randomized comparator; historical/exploratory comparison nominal only
records.keywords: Dunleavy et al. N Engl J Med 2013;368:1408-16  23574119

records.title: Morris et al
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Primary MEDIASTINAL B-cell LYMPHOMA · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2013
records.body:
Primary CNS lymphoma, histologically confirmed; newly diagnosed, no prior treatment for PCNSL; immunocompetent, negative HIV serology, no systemic non-Hodgkin lymphoma on CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis and on bone marrow aspirate/biopsy, no performance-status restriction; excluded preexisting immunodeficiency or other active primary malignancy (single-arm) R-MPV induction, five 14-day cycles (rituximab 500 mg/m² day 1; methotrexate 3.5 g/m² and vincristine 1.4 mg/m² day 2; procarbazine 100 mg/m²/d days 1-7, odd cycles only), PR after five cycles → two additional cycles; CSF-positive: intra-Ommaya methotrexate 12 mg between cycles → CR: reduced-dose WBRT 23.4 Gy in 1.8-Gy fractions ×13; less than CR: standard WBRT 45 Gy in 25 fractions offered → consolidation cytarabine 3 g/m²/d days 1 and 2, two 28-day cycles Primary: 2-year progression-free survival in patients receiving reduced-dose WBRT. Secondary: objective response rate to R-MPV, overall response rate, overall survival, neurocognitive outcome, quality of life, MRI white matter changes (Fazekas scale), apparent diffusion coefficient as a prognostic factor, toxicity R-MPV induction plus rdWBRT and cytarabine consolidation showed high response rates and long-term disease control in this single-arm trial
・PFS: 2-yr 77% (95% CI 63-92%) in 31 pts given rdWBRT (primary endpoint); median 7.7 yr
・OS: Median not reached; 5-yr 80% (rdWBRT cohort; median follow-up 5.9 yr for survivors)
・ORR: 95% (41 of 43 evaluable) after induction; CR 79%
・ITT (n=52): Median PFS 3.3 yr; OS 6.6 yr
・Cognition: Executive function and verbal memory improved after chemotherapy then stable except motor speed decline (n=12 progression-free)
・Biomarker: Post hoc ADC did not predict response, PFS or OS
・Subgroups: Median PFS 7.7 yr if <60 vs 1.4 yr if ≥60 (P = .09)
・Toxicity: Neutropenia main dose-limiting toxicity; new white matter changes in some long-term survivors, none Fazekas grade 4-5; 3 deaths (6%) possibly/probably toxicity-related
・Limitations: Single-arm; R-MPV not tested without WBRT; cognitive data limited to 12 progression-free patients
records.keywords: Morris et al. J Clin Oncol 2013;31:3971-3979  24101038

records.title: MATRix/IELSG43
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Primary CNS LYMPHOMA · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Untreated, immunocompetent B-cell primary CNS lymphoma (first line); randomised only after ≥partial response to 4 MATRix cycles with sufficient stem-cell harvest (≥3×10⁶ CD34+ cells/kg); age 18–65 years regardless of ECOG or 66–70 years with ECOG 0–2; excluded lymphoma outside the CNS, immunodeficiency including HIV, creatinine clearance <60 mL/min, active hepatitis B/C, and isolated ocular lymphoma Ⓐ R-DeVIC: rituximab 375 mg/m² d0; dexamethasone 40 mg/day d1–3; etoposide 100 mg/m²/day d1–3; ifosfamide 1500 mg/m²/day d1–3; carboplatin 300 mg/m² d1; q21d; 2 cycles
Ⓑ HCT-ASCT: carmustine 400 mg/m² d−6, or busulfan 3.2 mg/kg/day d−8,−7 if carmustine unavailable; thiotepa 5 mg/kg twice daily d−5,−4; stem-cell reinfusion d0
・Induction: 4 cycles MATRix (rituximab 375 mg/m² d0,5; methotrexate 3.5 g/m² d1; cytarabine 2 g/m² twice daily d2–3; thiotepa 30 mg/m² d4; q21d)
・Design: Randomised 1:1 after induction Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: complete response rate, overall survival, duration of response, quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30), adverse events, toxicity, neurotoxicity HCT-ASCT improved progression-free and overall survival versus R-DeVIC consolidation after MATRix induction
・3-yr PFS: Ⓐ 51% (95% CI 41–60) vs Ⓑ 78% (69–85); HR 0·43 (0·27–0·68), p=0·0003
・3-yr OS: Ⓐ 71% (95% CI 61–78) vs Ⓑ 86% (78–91); HR 0·46 (0·26–0·81), p=0·0075
・Toxicity: Ⓐ 9·3 vs Ⓑ 14·6 AEs/patient; Ⓑ more febrile neutropenia, stomatitis, diarrhoea; fatal consolidation SAEs Ⓐ 2 (both AML) vs Ⓑ 5 (4 infections, 1 pulmonary embolism)
・Limitations: Applies only to induction responders (229/346); one-third of patients did not reach randomisation

records.title: MARIETTA
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Primary CNS LYMPHOMA · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2021
records.body:
Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with secondary CNS involvement (brain, meninges, cranial nerves, eyes or spinal cord); at presentation with systemic disease or at relapse (isolated or with systemic lymphoma), any prior therapy except high-dose methotrexate or autologous/allogeneic HSCT; age 18–70 years, ECOG-PS ≤3, transformed and double/triple-hit lymphoma eligible; excluded prior organ transplant or other immunosuppression, HIV, primary CNS lymphoma (single-arm) MATRix (rituximab 375 mg/m² IV day 0; methotrexate 3·5 g/m² IV day 1; cytarabine 2 g/m² IV every 12 h days 2 and 3; thiotepa 30 mg/m² IV day 4) for 3 courses → RICE (rituximab 375 mg/m² day 1; etoposide 100 mg/m² per day IV days 1, 2 and 3; ifosfamide 5 g/m² IV day 2; carboplatin AUC 5 IV day 2) for 3 courses, each every 3 weeks, with intrathecal chemotherapy every course → if complete/partial response and adequate stem-cell harvest, carmustine 400 mg/m² day –6 + thiotepa 5 mg/kg every 12 h days –5 and –4 with autologous HSCT; stable/progressive disease on MATRix switched immediately to RICE, with WBRT for subsequent CNS progression before HSCT; chemotherapy-naive patients with life-threatening extra-CNS disease could first receive one or two debulking R-CHOP courses Primary: 1-year progression-free survival. Secondary: overall response rate before autologous HSCT, complete response rate before autologous HSCT, duration of response, overall survival, safety, 2-year progression-free survival MATRix–RICE followed by autologous HSCT showed activity in this very-poor-prognosis population; comparative benefit is unestablished in this single-arm trial
・PFS: 58% at 1 yr (95% CI 55–61); met predefined efficacy threshold (≥41%)
・ORR: 65% (CR 39%) after MATRix–RICE; median duration of response 26 mo
・OS: 2-yr 46% (median follow-up 29 mo)
・PFS (exploratory, 2-yr): 46% overall; 83% in transplanted patients
・PD on treatment: 33% progressed during MATRix–RICE
・Subgroups: Post-hoc 2-yr PFS 71% with CNS involvement at initial diagnosis vs 28% at relapse
・Toxicity: Grade 3–4 neutropenia 61%, thrombocytopenia 60%; serious AEs 56%; 4 deaths (5%) from Gram-negative sepsis, all during MATRix; only 71% of planned courses delivered
・Limitations: Single-arm, no control arm; subgroup and 2-yr PFS findings exploratory/post-hoc

records.title: NCI 89-C-41
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · BURKITT LYMPHOMA · Non-randomised comparison of two successive clinical trial protocols (no phase stated), with randomised GM-CSF allocation in high-risk patients · 1996
records.body:
Small non-cleaved-cell lymphoma (SNCL), histologically diagnosed; previously untreated children (<18 years) and adults <60 years, all HIV-seronegative; 89-C-41 low risk: single extraabdominal mass or completely resected abdominal disease and serum LDH <350 IU/L (NCI) or within institutional normal range; all others high risk Ⓐ Protocol 89-C-41: high risk four alternating cycles A, B, A, B over 12 to 15 weeks; low risk three cycles of modified regimen A
・Cycle A (CODOX-M): CTX 800 mg/m² IV day 1 then 200 mg/m² days 2 to 5, ADR 40 mg/m² IV day 1, VCR 1.5 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8 (cycle 1) and days 1, 8 and 15 (cycle 3), MTX 1,200 mg/m² over 1 hour then 240 mg/m²/hr for 23 hours from day 10 with leucovorin rescue, IT ara-C 70 mg days 1 and 3, IT MTX 12 mg day 15
・Cycle B (IVAC): Ifosfamide 1,500 mg/m² IV days 1 to 5 with mesna, etoposide 60 mg/m² IV days 1 to 5, ara-C 2 g/m² IV every 12 hours days 1 and 2 (four doses), IT MTX day 5
・GM-CSF randomisation (high risk): GM-CSF 7.5 mcgm/kg daily SC from day 13 (cycle A) or day 7 (cycle B) until AGC >1000/cu mm vs no GM-CSF
Ⓑ Protocol 77-04 (historical): CTX 1,200 mg/m² IV, ADR 40 mg/m² IV, VCR 1.4 mg/m² IV (maximum dose 2 mg) day 1, PRED 40 mg/m² days 1 to 5, 42-hour MTX infusion (300 mg/m² first hour, then 60 mg/m² for each of the next 41 hours) with leucovorin, IT therapy in the first six cycles
・Duration: 15 cycles (six for limited disease)
・Design: Non-randomised comparison of two successive protocols Event-free survival, complete response rate, partial response rate, toxicity, myelotoxicity, infectious complications Ⓐ 89-C-41 was associated with higher EFS than historical Ⓑ 77-04; EFS was similar for adults and children on each protocol
・EFS: Ⓐ 92% vs Ⓑ 56% at 2 years and beyond; P < .0001 (non-randomised comparison)
・GM-CSF (other randomisation, high-risk Ⓐ patients): Did not shorten neutropenia; prolonged thrombocytopenia; not beneficial
・Stage IV EFS: Ⓐ 80% vs Ⓑ 19%; P = .003
・CR: Ⓐ 95%
・Subgroups: Children vs adults 2-yr EFS 85% vs 100% with Ⓐ (not significant); 55% vs 56% with Ⓑ
・Toxicity: Neutropenia <500/µL in 97.7% cycle A and 100% cycle B cycles; sepsis 22.1% of cycles; G3–4 stomatitis 58% of cycle A cycles; disabling neuropathy 11/41, mostly with GM-CSF; 1 toxic death (neutropenic enterocolitis)
・Limitations: Historical non-randomised comparison; 77-04 single-centre (NCI) vs multicentre Ⓐ; late effects not yet assessable

records.title: HOVON/SAKK 127
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · BURKITT LYMPHOMA · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2023
records.body:
Adults aged 18–75 with newly diagnosed high-risk Burkitt lymphoma (elevated LDH, WHO PS ≥2, stage III/IV, or mass ≥10 cm) without CNS involvement; HIV-positive allowed; endemic and low-risk disease excluded Ⓐ Two cycles R-CODOX-M/R-IVAC (rituximab 375 mg/m², cyclophosphamide, vincristine 1·5 mg/m², doxorubicin 40 mg/m², methotrexate 3000 mg/m² day 10; R-IVAC: rituximab, ifosfamide 1500 mg/m² d1–5, etoposide, cytarabine; dose-modified if >65 years)
Ⓑ Six cycles DA-EPOCH-R (dose-adjusted etoposide, prednisolone, vincristine 0·4 mg/m², cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, rituximab 375 mg/m²)
・Prophylaxis: Intrathecal cytarabine and methotrexate Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Complete metabolic response rate, Overall survival, Event-free survival, Disease-specific survival, Safety, Hospital stay duration DA-EPOCH-R did not show superior PFS vs R-CODOX-M/R-IVAC in high-risk Burkitt lymphoma but was less toxic
・PFS (2-yr): Ⓐ 76% vs Ⓑ 70%; adjusted HR 1·42 (0·63–3·18; p=0·40)
・OS (2-yr): Ⓐ 76% vs Ⓑ 75%; HR 1·21 (p=0·65)
・Toxicity: Grade 3–5 infections Ⓐ 56% vs Ⓑ 34%; 2 treatment-related deaths (1 infection, 1 COVID-19); more transfusions and hospital nights (43 vs 28) with Ⓐ
・Limitations: Closed early for slow accrual, inconclusive (conditional power 20%); median follow-up 28·5 mo; mITT (n=84 of 89 randomized)

records.title: Ribrag et al. (Rituximab in Burkitt lymphoma)
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · BURKITT LYMPHOMA · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body:
Adults >18 years with previously untreated HIV-negative Burkitt's lymphoma or Burkitt's leukaemia from 45 French centres; first-line therapy; excluded serious comorbidity, creatinine >150 μmol/L, cirrhosis/prior hepatitis B or C, pregnancy, and prior cancer except non-melanoma skin or in-situ cervical carcinoma Ⓐ LMB dose-dense chemotherapy plus rituximab 375 mg/m² IV on days 1 and 6 of the first two COPADM cycles (4 infusions total)
Ⓑ LMB dose-dense chemotherapy alone
・Duration: 14 weeks (group B) or 26 weeks (group C) Primary: 3 year event-free survival. Secondary: 3 year overall survival, Complete response, Toxic effects Rituximab added to LMB chemotherapy improved EFS and OS in adults with Burkitt leukaemia/lymphoma
・EFS: 3-yr, Ⓐ 75% (95% CI 66-82) vs Ⓑ 62% (95% CI 53-70); HR 0.59 (95% CI 0.38-0.94)
・OS: 3-yr, Ⓐ 83% (95% CI 75-88) vs Ⓑ 70% (95% CI 62-78); HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.30-0.86)
・Toxicity: G3-4 infections did not differ, Ⓐ 17% vs Ⓑ 15% of cycles; 26 of 61 deaths non-lymphoma causes
・Limitations: Exploratory multivariate-adjusted analysis showed no significant treatment effect (EFS p=0.23; OS p=0.067)

records.title: Alliance/CALGB 50303
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Attempts to improve on R-CHOP — negative phase 3 trials · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body:
Untreated DLBCL (incl. centroblastic, immunoblastic, T-cell/histiocyte-rich, anaplastic variants), PMBCL or intravascular large B-cell lymphoma confirmed by central pathology review; frontline; stage II to IV DLBCL or stage I PMBCL, ECOG PS 0 to 2, LVEF >45%, fresh frozen tumour biopsy required; excluded underlying indolent lymphoma in marrow or biopsy, known CNS disease or HIV Ⓐ DA-EPOCH-R (96-hour infusional etoposide, prednisone, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin plus rituximab; doses escalated/de-escalated each cycle by nadir ANC and platelet count; mandatory filgrastim)
Ⓑ R-CHOP
・Schedule: Every 21 days for six cycles
・IT methotrexate: 12 mg in cycles 3 through 6 if >1 extranodal site with elevated LDH or marrow involvement
・RT: Consolidative RT prohibited Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: response rate, overall survival, toxicity, CNS relapse Ⓐ DA-EPOCH-R was more toxic and did not improve PFS or OS vs Ⓑ R-CHOP; primary endpoint not met
・PFS (5-yr): Ⓐ 68.0% vs Ⓑ 66.0%; HR 0.93 (95% CI, 0.68 to 1.27; P = .65)
・OS (5-yr): Ⓐ 77.5% vs Ⓑ 78.5%; HR 1.09
・ORR: Ⓐ 86.7% vs Ⓑ 88.0%
・Subgroups: Post hoc, unpowered IPI 3 to 5 subgroup favoured Ⓐ (HR 0.63; unadjusted P = 0.041), not adjusted for multiplicity
・Toxicity: Grade 3-5 treatment-related AEs Ⓐ 98.3% vs Ⓑ 78.2%; febrile neutropenia Ⓐ 35.0% vs Ⓑ 17.7%; neuropathy Ⓐ 18.6% vs Ⓑ 3.3%; five treatment-related deaths per arm
・Limitations: DSMB released data early (167 of 242 planned PFS events); Ⓑ 3-yr PFS of 72% exceeded the assumed 55%, suggesting selection bias limiting generalizability

records.title: GOYA
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Attempts to improve on R-CHOP — negative phase 3 trials · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body:
Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, histologically documented; previously untreated, first-line; CD20-positive by local pathology; IPI ≥2, or IPI 1 and age ≤60 years with or without bulky disease, or IPI 0 with bulky disease (one lesion ≥7.5 cm), ECOG 0-2, LVEF ≥50%, ≥1 bidimensionally measurable lesion >1.5 cm Ⓐ Obinutuzumab 1,000 mg IV days 1, 8 and 15 of cycle 1 and day 1 of cycles 2-8 + CHOP
Ⓑ Rituximab 375 mg/m² IV day 1 of cycles 1-8 + CHOP
・CHOP: Cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m², doxorubicin 50 mg/m², vincristine 1.4 mg/m² (max 2.0 mg) IV day 1; prednisone 100 mg/day orally days 1-5
・Duration: Eight 21-day antibody cycles; CHOP for six or eight cycles, agreed in advance per site, with antibody monotherapy in cycles 7-8 if six CHOP cycles given Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, event-free survival, complete response rate, overall response rate, disease-free survival, duration of response, time to next antilymphoma treatment, safety, progression-free survival by cell-of-origin subtype Obinutuzumab-CHOP did not improve PFS vs rituximab-CHOP in untreated DLBCL; primary endpoint not met
・PFS: 3-yr Ⓐ 69.6% vs Ⓑ 66.9%; stratified HR 0.92 (95% CI 0.76-1.11)
・OS: 3-yr Ⓐ 81.2% vs Ⓑ 81.4%; HR 1.00
・Subgroups: Exploratory GCB subgroup (n=540) HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.51-1.03); COO data available for only 933 patients, possible selection bias
・Toxicity: Grade 3-5 AEs Ⓐ 73.7% vs Ⓑ 64.7%; SAEs Ⓐ 42.6% vs Ⓑ 37.6%; fatal AEs Ⓐ 5.8% vs Ⓑ 4.3%; infusion-related reactions Ⓐ 36.1% vs Ⓑ 23.5%

records.title: REMoDL-B
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Attempts to improve on R-CHOP — negative phase 3 trials · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body:
Previously untreated de novo diffuse large B-cell lymphoma; bulky stage I or stage II–IV disease requiring full-course chemotherapy; sufficient diagnostic biopsy material for gene-expression profiling, with randomisation stratified by cell-of-origin subtype and IPI; ECOG performance status of 2 or less; excluded previous indolent lymphoma, primary mediastinal lymphoma, clinical CNS involvement, HIV/hepatitis B/C seropositivity, active malignancy in the preceding 5 years Ⓐ Five further cycles of R-CHOP-21 (rituximab 375 mg/m², cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m², doxorubicin 50 mg/m², vincristine 1·4 mg/m² [max 2 mg] IV day 1; prednisolone 100 mg orally days 1–5)
Ⓑ Five cycles of R-CHOP plus bortezomib 1·3 mg/m² IV or 1·6 mg/m² SC on days 1 and 8 (RB-CHOP; route changed to SC from Feb 28, 2014)
・Cycle 1: R-CHOP-21 (as above) for all patients before randomisation
・Design: Patients whose gene-expression profiling failed received R-CHOP without randomisation Primary: 30-month progression-free survival (germinal centre and activated B-cell population). Secondary: 30-month progression-free survival by cell-of-origin subgroup, overall survival, event-free survival, disease-free survival, time to progression, duration of response, complete response rate, overall response rate, toxicity, quality of life, peripheral neuropathy up to 30 days after last treatment, safety, progression-free survival in double-hit, double-expressor and NF-κB-mutated subgroups Adding bortezomib to R-CHOP did not improve progression-free survival; real-time molecular stratification for treatment allocation was shown feasible
・PFS (30-mo, ABC+GCB population): Ⓐ 70·1% vs Ⓑ 74·3%; HR 0·86 (95% CI 0·65–1·13; p=0·28)
・OS (30-mo, ABC+GCB population): Ⓐ 82·7% vs Ⓑ 83·6%
・Update (64-mo, overall, 801 classified): PFS HR 0·81 (p=.085); OS HR 0·86 (p=.32); neither improved
・Subgroups (unadjusted for multiplicity, 60-mo): ABC PFS Ⓐ 54·4% vs Ⓑ 69·4% (HR 0·65, 95% CI 0·43–0·98); MHG PFS Ⓐ 29·3% vs Ⓑ 54·9% (HR 0·46, 95% CI 0·26–0·84; n=83); ABC OS Ⓐ 67·4% vs Ⓑ 80·4% (HR 0·58, 95% CI 0·35–0·95); no GCB difference
・Toxicity: Grade≥3 haematological Ⓐ 39·8% vs Ⓑ 42·1%; neuropathy any grade Ⓐ 41·6% vs Ⓑ 56·8%, grade≥3 Ⓐ 1·8% vs Ⓑ 3·8%; serious AEs Ⓐ 42·5% vs Ⓑ 50·2% (5 vs 4 treatment-related deaths); second cancers Ⓐ 2·3% vs Ⓑ 1·4%
・Limitations: Subgroup analyses unadjusted for multiplicity; prospective confirmation of ABC/MHG benefit needed

records.title: PHOENIX
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Attempts to improve on R-CHOP — negative phase 3 trials · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body:
Previously untreated non-GCB DLBCL, confirmed centrally by Hans-based immunohistochemistry (ABC subtype by GEP assessed retrospectively); stage II to IV measurable disease, revised IPI score ≥1, ECOG PS ≤2; excluded known CNS lymphoma, primary mediastinal lymphoma, history of indolent lymphoma or HIV, active hepatitis B or C Ⓐ Ibrutinib 560 mg orally daily + R-CHOP
Ⓑ Placebo + R-CHOP
・R-CHOP: IV rituximab 375 mg/m², cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m², doxorubicin 50 mg/m², vincristine 1.4 mg/m² [max 2 mg]; oral prednisone 100 mg, every 21 days for six or eight cycles per institutional guidelines
・Duration: Study drug given from day 1 of cycle 1 to day 21 of the last cycle
・Design: Double-blind Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, complete response rate, overall survival, overall response rate, safety Adding ibrutinib to R-CHOP did not improve EFS, PFS, or OS in untreated non-GCB DLBCL
・EFS: Primary endpoint not met; HR 0.934 (95% CI 0.726-1.200) ITT, HR 0.949 (95% CI 0.704-1.279) ABC
・PFS: Not improved; HR 0.917
・OS: Not improved; HR 0.991
・Subgroups: Significant preplanned treatment-age interaction; exploratory, <60 yr EFS HR 0.579 and OS HR 0.330; ≥60 yr EFS HR 1.228 and OS HR 1.440
・Toxicity: Ⓐ 53.1% vs Ⓑ 34.0% SAEs (febrile neutropenia, diarrhea, cytopenia, pneumonia); AE deaths Ⓐ 4.3% vs Ⓑ 2.9%; ≥60 yr more SAEs (63.4% vs 38.2%), fewer completing ≥6 R-CHOP cycles (73.7% vs 88.8%)
・Limitations: Age-interaction findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating

records.title: ROBUST
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Attempts to improve on R-CHOP — negative phase 3 trials · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body:
Previously untreated CD20+ ABC-type DLBCL (central gene expression profiling, NanoString Lymphoma Subtyping Test); first line; Ann Arbor stage II-IV, IPI ≥2, age 18-80 (>80 allowed if ECOG PS ≤1 and fit for full-dose R-CHOP), measurable lesion ≥1.5 cm, candidates for six cycles of R-CHOP21; excluded GCB/unclassified subtype, active CNS lymphoma, transformed or composite lymphoma, prior lenalidomide, grade ≥2 peripheral neuropathy, LVEF <45% Ⓐ Lenalidomide 15 mg orally days 1-14 + R-CHOP21 (rituximab 375 mg/m² IV day -1 or 1, cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m², doxorubicin 50 mg/m², vincristine 1.4 mg/m² [max 2.0 mg] IV day 1, prednisone 100 mg orally days 1-5) every 21 days
Ⓑ Double-blind placebo days 1-14 + the same R-CHOP21
・Duration: Six cycles or until intolerability, inadequate response, progression, consent withdrawal or death Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: event-free survival, overall survival, overall response rate, complete response rate, duration of response, time to next lymphoma treatment, safety Adding lenalidomide to R-CHOP did not improve PFS in ABC-type DLBCL, missing the primary endpoint
・PFS: IRAC-assessed HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.63-1.14; P=.29); 2-yr PFS Ⓐ 67% vs Ⓑ 64%; median follow-up 27.1 mo
・EFS: Key secondary endpoint also not met; HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.80-1.34)
・OS: Immature; 2-yr Ⓐ 79% vs Ⓑ 80%
・ORR/CR: ORR 91% in both arms; CR Ⓐ 69% vs Ⓑ 65%
・Subgroups: IPI ≥3 trend favouring Ⓐ, 2-yr PFS 59% vs 50% (P=.09); exploratory only
・Toxicity: Grade 3/4 neutropenia Ⓐ 60% vs Ⓑ 48%; febrile neutropenia Ⓐ 14% vs Ⓑ 9%; serious TEAEs Ⓐ 37% vs Ⓑ 31%; stopped for AEs Ⓐ 17% vs Ⓑ 11%; deaths Ⓐ 20% vs Ⓑ 22%, mainly malignant disease

records.title: SWOG 9704
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · High-risk consolidation — upfront autologous transplant · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2013
records.body:
Diffuse aggressive non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, Working Formulation groups D through H and J; first-line, with randomization requiring at least a partial response after five cycles of CHOP or R-CHOP; age-adjusted IPI high-intermediate or high risk, age 15 to 65 years; lymphoblastic, transformed and mantle-cell histologic types excluded Ⓐ One additional cycle of induction chemotherapy, then autologous stem-cell transplantation after total-body irradiation (12 Gy in eight 1.5-Gy fractions twice daily) or carmustine 300 mg per square meter with etoposide 60 mg/kg and cyclophosphamide 100 mg/kg (carmustine regimen for all patients aged 60 or older)
Ⓑ Three additional cycles of induction chemotherapy (control)
・Induction: CHOP or R-CHOP (R-CHOP for CD20+ disease from April 2003) every 3 weeks for five cycles
・Design: Randomization at ≥partial response after induction Primary: 2-year progression-free survival, 2-year overall survival. Secondary: grade 3 and 4 toxic effects, second primary cancers Early transplantation improved PFS in high-intermediate/high-risk responders to induction but did not improve OS, probably because of effective salvage transplantation
・PFS (2-yr): Ⓐ 69% vs Ⓑ 55%; HR (control vs transplantation) 1.72 (95% CI 1.18-2.51); P=0.005
・OS (2-yr): Ⓐ 74% vs Ⓑ 71%; HR 1.26 (95% CI 0.82-1.94); P=0.30
・Update: Median follow-up 6.3 yr
・Subgroups: Unplanned, no multiplicity adjustment; high-risk PFS Ⓐ 75% vs Ⓑ 41%, OS Ⓐ 82% vs Ⓑ 64%; high-intermediate-risk OS Ⓐ 70% vs Ⓑ 75%; needs prospective validation
・Toxicity: Grade 3-4 infection Ⓐ 50% vs Ⓑ 13%; toxic deaths Ⓐ six (5%) vs Ⓑ three (2%)
・Limitations: 117 of 370 eligible patients not randomized, mostly because of early progression

records.title: POLARIX
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · New frontline standards — ADC, immunomodulation & epigenetics · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body:
Previously untreated CD20-positive DLBCL; first-line; regardless of cell of origin or MYC, BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement; age 18 to 80 years, ECOG 0 to 2, IPI score 2 to 5 (intermediate or high risk); excluded history of indolent lymphoma, contraindication to any R-CHOP component, prior anthracycline, known CNS involvement Ⓐ Polatuzumab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV + vincristine-matched placebo + rituximab 375 mg/m², cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m², doxorubicin 50 mg/m² IV day 1 and prednisone 100 mg orally days 1–5, every 21 days for six cycles (pola-R-CHP) → rituximab 375 mg/m² cycles 7 and 8
Ⓑ Polatuzumab-matched placebo + vincristine 1.4 mg/m² (maximum 2 mg) IV + the same R-CHP for six cycles (R-CHOP) → rituximab 375 mg/m² cycles 7 and 8
・Design: Double-blind Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: event-free survival, PET-CT-based complete response at end of treatment, overall survival, disease-free survival, overall response, safety Pola-R-CHP maintained a durable PFS benefit over R-CHOP, with fewer subsequent therapies
・EFS: Ⓐ 75.6% vs Ⓑ 69.4% at 2 yr; HR 0.75; P=0.02 (primary analysis, 28.2 mo)
・PFS: Ⓐ 64.9% vs Ⓑ 59.1% at 5 yr; HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.62–0.97) (median follow-up 64.1 mo)
・CR: Ⓐ 78.0% vs Ⓑ 74.0% (end-of-treatment, central review); P=0.16; not significant
・OS: HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.63–1.15) at 5 yr; not significant; exploratory competing-risk analysis: fewer lymphoma-related deaths (Ⓐ 46 vs Ⓑ 62, expanded cohort)
・Subgroups: Favoured Ⓐ in ABC-DLBCL (PFS HR 0.38), IPI 3–5 and double expressors; not powered for subgroup analysis
・Toxicity: Grade 3/4 febrile neutropenia Ⓐ 13.8% vs Ⓑ 8.0%; grade 5 AEs Ⓐ 13 (3.0%) vs Ⓑ 10 (2.3%), mainly infections; grade ≥2 peripheral neuropathy Ⓐ 13.8% vs Ⓑ 16.7%; secondary malignancies Ⓐ 5 vs Ⓑ 12
・Limitations: Beyond 5 yr, only treatment-related SAEs were followed, limiting late-toxicity assessment
