records.title: frontMIND
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · New frontline standards — ADC, immunomodulation & epigenetics · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Previously untreated DLBCL or other large B-cell lymphoma (incl. HGBL with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangements, HGBL NOS, grade 3b follicular lymphoma) by local pathology; first-line; high-intermediate/high-risk: IPI 3–5 or aaIPI 2–3 if aged ≤60 years; aged 18–80 years, ECOG PS 0–2, R-CHOP candidates, at least one measurable PET-positive lesion, treatment start within 28 days of diagnostic biopsy Ⓐ Tafasitamab 12 mg/kg IV days 1, 8 and 15 + lenalidomide 25 mg/day orally days 1–10 + R-CHOP
Ⓑ Matching placebos + the same R-CHOP
・R-CHOP: Rituximab 375 mg/m², cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m², doxorubicin 50 mg/m², vincristine 1·4 mg/m² (max 2 mg) IV day 1; prednisone/prednisolone 100 mg/day orally days 1–5
・Duration: Six 21-day cycles
・Design: Double-blind Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: event-free survival, overall survival, 3-year progression-free survival, 3-year event-free survival, 3-year overall survival, complete response rate by PET at end of treatment, ORR at end of treatment, progression-free survival by cell-of-origin subtype, duration of complete response, time to next treatment, safety, quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30, FACT-Lym), 2-year rate of relapse with CNS involvement, serum tafasitamab concentrations, anti-tafasitamab antibody incidence Tafasitamab and lenalidomide added to R-CHOP improved PFS but increased adverse events, including fatal treatment-emergent events; OS immature
・PFS: At median follow-up 35·2 months; 2-yr PFS Ⓐ 71·1% vs Ⓑ 62·9%; HR 0·75 (95% CI 0·59–0·96)
・EFS: HR 0·79 (95% CI 0·64–0·97)
・OS: Interim analysis; HR 0·85 (95% CI 0·63–1·14); not significant
・ORR: End-of-treatment; Ⓐ 80·4% vs Ⓑ 76·1%
・CR: PET-negative; Ⓐ 65% vs Ⓑ 65%
・Subgroups: PFS not powered; HR 0·59 (95% CI 0·36–0·95) ABC-like, 0·69 (95% CI 0·40–1·19) GCB-like
・Toxicity: G≥3 TEAEs Ⓐ 87% vs Ⓑ 76%; serious TEAEs Ⓐ 50% vs Ⓑ 39%; fatal TEAEs Ⓐ 6% vs Ⓑ 4% (COVID-19, sepsis)
・Limitations: OS immature; interim analysis not significant

records.title: DEB
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · New frontline standards — ADC, immunomodulation & epigenetics · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
CD20-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma; previously untreated, first-line; MYC/BCL2 double expression (MYC ≥40%, BCL2 ≥50% by IHC); age 18-80, ≥1 FDG-avid lesion, IPI >1, ECOG 0-2; excluded double-/triple-hit lymphoma by FISH (enrollment allowed before FISH confirmation), planned first-line stem cell transplant consolidation, known CNS or primary mediastinal lymphoma Ⓐ Tucidinostat 20 mg orally on days 1, 4, 8 and 11 of each 21-day cycle + R-CHOP for 6 cycles → tucidinostat maintenance on the same schedule for up to 24 weeks if complete response after 6 cycles
Ⓑ Matching placebo + R-CHOP for 6 cycles → placebo maintenance for up to 24 weeks if complete response
・R-CHOP: Rituximab 375 mg/m² day 1; cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m², doxorubicin 50 mg/m², vincristine 1.4 mg/m² (maximum 2 mg) day 2; oral prednisone 100 mg days 2 through 6
・Design: Double-blind Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: complete response rate, progression-free survival, disease-free survival, overall survival, safety/tolerability, objective response Adding tucidinostat to R-CHOP significantly improved event-free survival in newly diagnosed DEL, with increased toxicity
・EFS: Ⓐ 60.3% vs Ⓑ 50.5% at 2 yr; HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.54-0.96); final analysis (41.3 mo follow-up)
・CR: Ⓐ 73.0% vs Ⓑ 61.8% (difference 11.1 points)
・Other endpoints: PFS HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.56-1.09); DFS HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.51-1.20); OS HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.53-1.13); numerically improved only, hypothesis-generating (no multiplicity adjustment; trial not powered)
・Toxicity: G≥3 AEs during combination Ⓐ 85.8% vs Ⓑ 72.6% (neutropenia Ⓐ 60.7% vs Ⓑ 45.3%; thrombocytopenia Ⓐ 25.6% vs Ⓑ 13.2%; infectious pneumonia Ⓐ 15.6% vs Ⓑ 7.1%); during maintenance Ⓐ 77.4% vs Ⓑ 39.1%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 2.8% vs Ⓑ 3.3%
・Limitations: Single ethnic population; maintenance contribution not isolated

records.title: Lewis et al
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · CNS prophylaxis in high-risk disease · Retrospective cohort study · 2023
records.body:
Aggressive B-cell lymphoma at high CNS risk: DLBCL NOS with CNS-IPI 4-6, HGBL with MYC plus BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangement, primary breast/testicular DLBCL stage I or II, or renal/adrenal involvement irrespective of CNS-IPI; first-line curative-intent anti-CD20 R-CHOP-like or DA-EPOCH-R-like chemoimmunotherapy; age 18-80, diagnosed 2000-2020; excluded CNS involvement at diagnosis, dose-intensive CNS-penetrating antimetabolite regimens or ASCT in first remission Ⓐ R-CHOP-like or DA-EPOCH-R-like anti-CD20 chemoimmunotherapy + HD-MTX prophylaxis (≥1 cycle of IV methotrexate at any dose, during or after frontline therapy; median 2 cycles; ≥3 g/m² for ≥1 cycle in 73.4%)
Ⓑ Same chemoimmunotherapy without HD-MTX (with or without IT-MTX)
・Design: Non-randomised allocation Primary: incidence of CNS progression. Secondary: isolated CNS progression, synchronous CNS/systemic progression, site of CNS progression, progression-free survival, overall survival, post-CNS progression PFS, post-CNS progression OS HD-MTX was not associated with a clinically meaningful reduction in CNS progression risk in this high-risk cohort
・CNS progression (All-pts, 5-yr): Ⓐ 6.9% vs Ⓑ 8.5%; adjusted HR 0.59 (95% CI 0.38 to 0.90); risk difference 1.6% (95% CI –1.5 to 4.4); NNT 63
・CNS progression (CR-pts, 5-yr): Ⓐ 5.0% vs Ⓑ 6.5%; adjusted HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.42 to 1.30); analysed from end of therapy to limit immortal time bias
・Subgroups: Exploratory association with reduced risk in CR-pts with CNS-IPI 4 or HGBL (29 Ⓐ patients); underpowered
・IT-MTX alone: Not associated with reduced CNS progression risk
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: Non-randomised allocation; selection bias; fewer HD-MTX patients enrolled than the 581 targeted (425)
records.keywords: Lewis et al. J Clin Oncol 2023;41:5376-5387  37797284

records.title: Wilson et al. 2026 (HD-MTX as CNS prophylaxis in ultra high-risk large B-cell lymphoma)
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · CNS prophylaxis in high-risk disease · Retrospective cohort study · 2026
records.body:
Large B-cell lymphoma treated with first-line R-CHOP/R-CHOP-like therapy (including DA-EPOCH-R), ultra high risk for CNS relapse (≥1 of: CNS-IPI 5-6; testicular, renal/adrenal or breast involvement; ≥3 extranodal sites); known baseline CNS involvement excluded, but baseline CNS screening not mandated Ⓐ First-line R-CHOP/R-CHOP-like immunochemotherapy with IV HD-MTX CNS prophylaxis (≥1 cycle at any dose; median two cycles, median cumulative dose 6 g/m²)
Ⓑ First-line R-CHOP/R-CHOP-like immunochemotherapy with no HD-MTX
・Design: Non-randomised, non-assigned exposure; intrathecal prophylaxis and HD-MTX timing/dose/cycle number per local policy Primary: CNS relapse rate (isolated or concurrent with systemic relapse) measured from diagnosis. Secondary: Isolated CNS relapse rate, Event-free survival, Overall survival, Overall survival after CNS relapse, CNS relapse by HD-MTX dose, CNS relapse across individual UHR subgroups HD-MTX CNS prophylaxis was not associated with reduced CNS relapse versus no HD-MTX in ultra high-risk LBCL, overall or by subgroup
・CNS relapse (3-yr): Ⓑ 9.3% vs Ⓐ 8.1%; adjusted HR 1.13 (95% CI 0.82-1.57)
・Isolated relapse: Ⓑ 5.9% vs Ⓐ 5.7%; adjusted HR 1.03 (95% CI 0.69-1.53)
・6-mo landmark CNS relapse (responders, progression-free): Ⓑ 6.7% vs Ⓐ 6.6%; adjusted HR 0.95 (95% CI 0.62-1.44)
・Subgroups: No significant difference by cumulative dose (<6 vs ≥6 g/m²) or by ≥3 doses; CNS-IPI 5 isolated-relapse reduction nonsignificant, wide CIs, possibly spurious
・EFS/OS: Crude rates favored HD-MTX but not after landmark propensity matching: EFS 73.7% vs 73.8%; OS 82.7% vs 82.6%
・Post-CNS-relapse OS: 3.8 mo
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: Retrospective, non-randomised; selection/immortal-time bias inherent
records.keywords: Wilson et al. J Clin Oncol 2026;44:2290-2302  42274647

records.title: Alizadeh et al.
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Molecular classification — cell of origin · Observational cohort study · 2000
records.body:
De novo diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not obviously arising from prior low-grade lymphoma such as FL; untreated at biopsy, then given anthracycline-based multi-agent chemotherapy with curative intent at two centres; classified by gene expression as germinal centre B-like or activated B-like; profiled alongside FL, CLL, normal lymphocyte subsets and cell lines Ⓐ Germinal centre B-like DLBCL
Ⓑ Activated B-like DLBCL
・Classification: Lymphochip cDNA microarray gene-expression profiling with hierarchical clustering
・Chemotherapy: Comparable anthracycline-based multi-agent chemotherapy (not assigned by study) Gene expression signatures, DLBCL molecular subgroups, overall survival, event-free survival, overall survival within IPI risk groups Germinal centre B-like DLBCL had significantly better survival than activated B-like DLBCL, suggesting the subtypes represent distinct diseases
・5-yr OS: Ⓐ 76% vs Ⓑ 16%; P<0.01 (all patients 52%); apparently unaffected by chemotherapy regimen used (data not shown)
・Subgroups: IPI 0–2 (low risk): Ⓑ worse OS than Ⓐ; P<0.05; profile adds prognostic value beyond IPI
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: Exploratory two-centre cohort; considerable molecular heterogeneity within subtypes (Ⓐ 5 patients died <2 yr; Ⓑ 3 patients alive at 5 yr)

records.title: PARMA
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — salvage chemoimmunotherapy & autologous transplant · Randomised clinical trial · 1995
records.body:
Intermediate- or high-grade non-Hodgkin's lymphoma; first or second relapse after a doxorubicin-containing regimen; age 18 to 60 years with prior complete response to induction maintained for at least four weeks; chemotherapy-sensitive relapse (complete or partial response after two courses of DHAP) required for randomization; excluded central nervous system or bone marrow involvement at relapse Ⓐ Involved-field radiotherapy if indicated (bulky sites at least 5 cm or extranodal T3/T4; 26 Gy in 1.3 Gy fractions twice daily) → BEAC (carmustine 300 mg/m² day 1; etoposide 200 mg/m²/day, cytarabine 200 mg/m²/day and cyclophosphamide 35 mg/kg/day on days 2 through 5) → autologous bone marrow transplantation
Ⓑ Four additional courses of DHAP at intervals of three to four weeks → involved-field radiotherapy if no progression (bulky sites 5 cm; 35 Gy in 20 fractions of 1.75 Gy)
・Design: Responders to two courses of DHAP randomized to Ⓐ vs Ⓑ Event-free survival, overall survival, response rate, toxic death, morbidity High-dose chemotherapy with ABMT increased event-free and overall survival over conventional salvage chemotherapy in chemosensitive relapsed non-Hodgkin's lymphoma
・Response rate: Ⓐ 84% vs Ⓑ 44%
・5-yr EFS: Ⓐ 46% vs Ⓑ 12%
・5-yr OS: Ⓐ 53% vs Ⓑ 32%; P=0.038, by intention to treat
・Toxicity: Ⓐ 3/49 (6%) died of toxic effects, 1 more died of late toxicity on day 406; Ⓑ no toxic deaths; Ⓐ high morbidity with 30 bacterial infections (septicemia in 17), mucositis grade 3 in 7 and grade 4 in 2
・Limitations: Stopped early (June 1994) for low accrual; 6 of 55 Ⓐ patients did not undergo transplantation; 14 of 18 Ⓑ patients transplanted after relapse died
records.keywords: Philip et al. N Engl J Med 1995;333:1540-1545  7477169

records.title: HOVON 44
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — salvage chemoimmunotherapy & autologous transplant · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2008
records.body:
Aggressive CD20+ B-cell NHL (diffuse large B-cell, mediastinal B-cell or follicle center lymphoma grade 3); relapsed after, or refractory/progressive on, a standard anthracyclin-based (CHOP-like) regimen; aged 18 to 65 years with WHO performance status 0 to 1; excluded CNS involvement, HIV infection, posttransplant lymphoproliferative disorder Ⓐ Rituximab 375 mg/m² (day 5 of DHAP or day 6 of VIM; 3 infusions) + DHAP-VIM-DHAP
Ⓑ DHAP-VIM-DHAP alone
・DHAP: Cisplatin 100 mg/m² day 1, cytarabine 2 g/m² day 2 repeated after 12 hours, dexamethasone 40 mg/day orally or IV for 4 days
・VIM: Etoposide 90 mg/m² IV days 1, 3, 5, ifosfamide 1200 mg/m² IV days 1-5, methotrexate 30 mg/m² IV days 1, 5
・Cycles: Every 4 weeks
・Sequence: CR/PR after 2 cycles → third cycle → BEAM → ASCT, optional involved-area radiotherapy
・BEAM: Carmustine 300 mg/m² day -6, etoposide 200 mg/m² and cytarabine 200 mg/m² day -5 to day -2, melphalan 140 mg/m² day -1
・Discontinuation: <PR or progression after 2 cycles: off protocol Complete response rate, partial response rate, failure-free survival, progression-free survival, overall survival, response after 2 cycles, ASCT rate, infection rate, haematological recovery Rituximab added to DHAP-VIM-DHAP reinduction before ASCT improved FFS and PFS in relapsed/progressive aggressive CD20+ NHL
・Response (2 cycles): Ⓐ 75% vs Ⓑ 54%
・ASCT performed: Ⓐ 63% vs Ⓑ 46%
・FFS (24 mo): Ⓐ 50% vs Ⓑ 24%; P<.001
・PFS (24 mo): Ⓐ 52% vs Ⓑ 31%; P<.002
・OS (24 mo): Ⓐ 59% vs Ⓑ 52%; P=.15; unadjusted HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.52-1.10)
・OS (adjusted): HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.41-0.89) after adjustment for prognostic factors
・Toxicity: No increased infection rate or impaired granulocyte/platelet recovery with rituximab (data not shown)
・Limitations: More DHAP-arm nonresponders received rituximab-containing third-line therapy, confounding OS; patients largely rituximab-naive at entry

records.title: CORAL
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — salvage chemoimmunotherapy & autologous transplant · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2010
records.body:
Aggressive CD20+ B-cell non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, including DLBCL; first relapse or refractory (no CR) after standard anthracycline-based CHOP first-line therapy, with or without prior rituximab, salvage before ASCT; age 18 to 65 years, performance status 0 to 1; excluded CNS involvement, HIV infection, post-transplantation lymphoproliferative disorders Ⓐ R-ICE: rituximab 375 mg/m² before chemotherapy (additional rituximab in first course), etoposide 100 mg/m²/day days 1-3, ifosfamide 5,000 mg/m² continuous infusion day 2, carboplatin AUC 5 (max 800 mg) day 2, every 3 weeks for 3 cycles
Ⓑ R-DHAP: rituximab 375 mg/m², cisplatin 100 mg/m² day 1, cytarabine 2 g/m² twice on day 2, dexamethasone 40 mg/d for 4 days, every 3 weeks for 3 cycles
・Sequence: CR/PR after cycle 3 with adequate stem-cell collection → BEAM (carmustine 300 mg/m², etoposide 200 mg/m², cytarabine 200 mg/m², melphalan 140 mg/m²) → ASCT → second randomization: rituximab 375 mg/m² every 8 weeks for 12 months vs observation Primary: mobilization-adjusted response rate after three cycles of chemotherapy. Secondary: overall response rate, stem-cell mobilization failure, event-free survival, progression-free survival, overall survival, response after transplantation, adverse events R-ICE and R-DHAP gave similar response, EFS, PFS and OS in relapsed/refractory lymphoma after rituximab-based first-line therapy
・Response (primary, mobilization-adjusted): Ⓐ 52.3% vs Ⓑ 54.5%
・ORR (after 3 cycles): Ⓐ 63.5% vs Ⓑ 62.8%
・3-yr EFS: Ⓐ 26% vs Ⓑ 35% (27-mo median follow-up); P=.6
・3-yr PFS: Ⓐ 31% vs Ⓑ 42% (27-mo median follow-up); P=.4
・3-yr OS: Ⓐ 47% vs Ⓑ 51% (27-mo median follow-up); P=.4
・Subgroups: Prior rituximab did not affect EFS in relapse >12 mo after diagnosis; early relapse after rituximab had poor prognosis with either regimen (3-yr PFS 23%); prior rituximab, early relapse, saaIPI 2-3 were adverse Cox factors
・Toxicity: Ⓑ more G3-4 hematologic toxicity (platelet transfusion Ⓐ 35% vs Ⓑ 57%); G4 renal toxicity in 11 patients (Ⓑ); SAEs Ⓐ 90 events/58 patients vs Ⓑ 120 events/68 patients; three toxic deaths after BEAM/ASCT
・Limitations: Only 50% of patients underwent ASCT
records.keywords: Gisselbrecht et al. J Clin Oncol 2010;28:4184-4190  20660832

records.title: NCIC-CTG LY.12
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — salvage chemoimmunotherapy & autologous transplant · Randomised clinical trial · 2014
records.body:
Relapsed or refractory aggressive-histology lymphoma (WHO), including DLBCL and variants, peripheral T-cell and anaplastic large-cell lymphoma; second-line chemotherapy before planned ASCT; one prior anthracycline-containing regimen required (DLBCL transformed from follicular/indolent lymphoma: no more than three previous regimens, at least one with an anthracycline); ECOG 0 to 3; excluded prior cisplatin, cytarabine or gemcitabine, CNS lymphoma or HIV infection Ⓐ GDP: gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8 + cisplatin 75 mg/m² day 1 + dexamethasone 40 mg PO days 1–4, every 21 days for two cycles
Ⓑ DHAP: dexamethasone 40 mg PO days 1–4 + cytarabine 2 g/m² IV every 12 hours for two doses on day 2 + cisplatin 100 mg/m² day 1, every 21 days for two cycles
・CD20-positive lymphoma: Also received rituximab 375 mg/m² IV day 1 of each cycle (amendment November 2005)
・Cycles: Third cycle permitted without CR/PR after two
・Responders: Stem-cell collection → ASCT Primary: response rate after two cycles, transplantation rate. Secondary: event-free survival, overall survival, treatment toxicity, successful stem-cell mobilization rate, adverse events, quality of life, resource usage, hospitalization GDP was non-inferior to DHAP for response after two cycles, with less toxicity, hospitalization and better-preserved QoL
・Response (ITT): Ⓐ 45.1% vs Ⓑ 44.1%; non-inferior (upper one-sided 95.6% CI for difference 5.7%; P=.005; 10% margin)
・Transplantation: Ⓐ 52.1% vs Ⓑ 49.3%; P=.44 (superiority end point not met)
・EFS: HR 0.99 (95% CI 0.82–1.21); 4-yr EFS 26% in each group (53-mo median follow-up)
・OS: HR 1.03 (95% CI 0.83–1.28); 4-yr OS 39% in each group
・QoL: FACT-G mid-cycle 2 improved Ⓐ 18% vs Ⓑ 11%, worse Ⓐ 33% vs Ⓑ 41%
・Toxicity: Grade 3–4 AEs (cycles 1–2) Ⓐ 47% vs Ⓑ 61%; febrile neutropenia Ⓐ 9% vs Ⓑ 23%; hospitalization Ⓐ 47% vs Ⓑ 99%; treatment-related deaths Ⓐ 2 vs Ⓑ 6
・Limitations: Accrual closed early, before planned 637 patients
records.keywords: Crump et al. J Clin Oncol 2014;32:3490-3496  25267740

records.title: SCHOLAR-1
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — outcomes after failed salvage · Retrospective cohort study · 2017
records.body:
Refractory DLBCL, including TFL and PMBCL; salvage setting after an anti-CD20 antibody plus anthracycline as a qualifying regimen, counted at first instance of meeting refractory criteria (MDACC: from second-line onward); refractory defined as PD or SD as best response to chemotherapy (≥4 cycles first-line or 2 cycles later-line) or relapse ≤12 months after ASCT, then a further therapy line; primary CNS lymphoma excluded (single-arm)
・Population: Next line of salvage therapy after refractory status was determined
・Design: Pooled from MDACC and IA/MC observational cohorts and follow-up of the LY.12 and CORAL randomized salvage trials (non-randomised analysis) Objective response rate, complete response rate, partial response rate, overall survival, 1-year and 2-year survival rates Next-line salvage therapy showed poor efficacy in refractory DLBCL, with low response rates and short overall survival
・ORR: 26% (CR 7%)
・OS: Median 6.3 mo (95% CI 5.9-7.0); 1-yr 28%, 2-yr 20% survival
・Subgroups: ORR 20% in primary refractory vs 34% with relapse ≤12 mo post-ASCT; OS similar across refractory subgroups
・Associations: Longer OS with CR (median 14.9 vs 4.6 mo for nonresponders) and with subsequent ASCT (14.4 vs 5.1 mo); non-randomised
・Toxicity: Not reported
・Limitations: Retrospective pooling of heterogeneous trial and observational cohorts; includes effect of treatment period

records.title: RE-MIND2
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — outcomes after failed salvage · Retrospective cohort study · 2022
records.body:
Relapsed/refractory histologically confirmed DLBCL; ASCT-ineligible, index therapy line 2L, 3L or 4L; received ≥2 systemic anti-DLBCL regimens (≥1 anti-CD20), propensity-matched 1:1 on nine covariates to L-MIND patients; excluded CNS involvement, prior allogeneic transplant, first-line CD19-targeted therapy or IMiDs, prior tafasitamab, other malignancy unless disease-free ≥5 years, double-/triple-hit disease; analysis sets required ≥6 months' follow-up Ⓐ Tafasitamab + lenalidomide (L-MIND trial cohort), followed by tafasitamab monotherapy until disease progression
Ⓑ Matched real-world comparator: systemic therapies pooled (primary analysis)
Ⓒ Matched real-world comparator: BR (primary analysis)
Ⓓ Matched real-world comparator: R-GemOx (primary analysis)
Ⓔ Matched real-world comparator: pola-BR (expanded analysis)
Ⓕ Matched real-world comparator: R2 (expanded analysis)
Ⓖ Matched real-world comparator: CD19 CAR-T (expanded analysis)
・Comparators: Given per prescribing information
・Design: Separate matched cohorts Primary: overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, complete response rate, duration of response, event-free survival, progression-free survival, time to next treatment, treatment discontinuation due to adverse events Tafasitamab + lenalidomide improved OS versus matched pooled systemic therapies, BR and R-GemOx, meeting the primary endpoint
・OS: Ⓐ 34.1 vs Ⓑ 11.6 mo; HR 0.553 (95% CI 0.358–0.855); also longer vs Ⓒ BR (HR 0.418) and Ⓓ R-GemOx (HR 0.467)
・PFS: Ⓐ 12.1 vs Ⓑ 5.8; Ⓐ 12.1 vs Ⓒ 7.9; Ⓐ 14.1 vs Ⓓ 5.1 mo (exploratory)
・ORR/CR: Significantly higher Ⓐ vs Ⓑ pooled and Ⓐ vs Ⓓ R-GemOx; not vs Ⓒ BR (ORR Ⓐ 66.7% vs Ⓒ 54.7%; P = 0.181); exploratory
・Expanded analysis: OS longer vs Ⓔ pola-BR (HR 0.441) and Ⓕ R2 (HR 0.435), comparable vs Ⓖ CAR-T (HR 0.953); PFS/ORR better vs Ⓕ R2 only, not vs Ⓔ pola-BR or Ⓖ CAR-T
・Toxicity: Discontinuation for AEs Ⓐ 14.5%–15.1% vs Ⓑ 6.8%, Ⓒ 2.8%, Ⓓ 5.4%; longer Ⓐ exposure and trial-based safety recording
・Limitations: Nonrandomized with potential treatment-selection bias; 11-covariate sensitivity analysis showed OS vs Ⓒ BR not significant; expanded cohorts (Ⓔ/Ⓕ/Ⓖ) small with short follow-up
records.keywords: Nowakowski et al. Clin Cancer Res 2022;28:4003-4017  35674661 Nowakowski et al. Ann Hematol 2023;102:1773-1787  37171597

records.title: ZUMA-1
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — CD19 CAR T-cell therapy, third line and beyond · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2017
records.body:
Histologically confirmed large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL, primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma or transformed follicular lymphoma; 2008 WHO); refractory disease despite recommended prior therapy; refractory defined as progressive or stable disease as best response to the most recent chemotherapy, or progression or relapse within 12 months after autologous stem-cell transplantation (single-arm) Fludarabine 30 mg/m² per day + cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m² per day on days −5, −4 and −3 → single IV infusion of axicabtagene ciloleucel at a target dose of 2×10^6 CAR T cells/kg on day 0; no bridging chemotherapy after leukapheresis Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety, blood CAR T-cell levels, serum cytokine levels, complete response rate Axi-cel showed high response activity in refractory large B-cell lymphoma, evaluated as single-arm evidence against a 20% historical control
・ORR: 82% (95% CI, 72 to 89; P<0.001) in 92 protocol-specified patients; central review 71% in 101 treated
・CR: 54% in 101 treated; 51% by central review
・Update (15.4-mo follow-up, 108 pts): 42% remained in response; 40% in CR
・DoR: Median 11.1 mo
・PFS: Median 5.8 mo
・OS: 52% at 18 mo; median not reached
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 AEs in 95%, including neutropenia 78%; grade ≥3 CRS 13%; grade ≥3 neurologic events 28%; 3 deaths from AEs (grade 5 HLH; cardiac arrest during CRS)
・Limitations: Single-arm design evaluated against a 20% historical control
records.keywords: Neelapu et al. N Engl J Med 2017;377:2531-2544  29226797

records.title: JULIET
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — CD19 CAR T-cell therapy, third line and beyond · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2019
records.body:
Adults with relapsed or refractory DLBCL, including DLBCL transformed from follicular lymphoma and double- or triple-hit high-grade B-cell lymphoma; at least two prior lines including rituximab and an anthracycline; relapsed after or ineligible for autologous transplantation; excluded prior CD19-directed therapy, primary mediastinal DLBCL, prior allogeneic transplant, active CNS involvement (single-arm) Tisagenlecleucel single infusion after one cycle of lymphodepleting chemotherapy (fludarabine 25 mg per square meter plus cyclophosphamide 250 mg per square meter daily for 3 days, or bendamustine 90 mg per square meter daily for 2 days); bridging therapy allowed Primary: best overall response rate. Secondary: duration of response, overall survival, safety, cellular kinetics, complete response rate, progression-free survival, relapse-free survival, biomarkers Tisagenlecleucel showed durable activity in adult relapsed/refractory DLBCL, rejecting the null of ORR ≤20% at the interim analysis; comparative benefit unestablished
・ORR: 52%; CR 40%, PR 12% (efficacy set, interim analysis)
・DoR: Median not reached; 12-mo relapse-free survival 65% among responders, 79% among complete responders
・OS: Median 12 mo among infused patients; 12-mo OS 49%
・ITT: ORR 34% and median OS 8.3 mo among all 165 enrolled
・Subgroups: Response consistent across prognostic subgroups; double-hit lymphoma ORR 50%, CR 25%
・Toxicity: G3/4 CRS 22%, neurologic events 12%, cytopenias >28 days 32%, infections 20%; no deaths attributed to tisagenlecleucel
・Limitations: Single-arm; short follow-up; 30% of enrolled patients not infused (7% manufacturing failure)
records.keywords: Schuster et al. N Engl J Med 2019;380:45-56  30501490

records.title: TRANSCEND NHL 001
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — CD19 CAR T-cell therapy, third line and beyond · Single-arm clinical trial (phase I) · 2020
records.body:
Relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma: DLBCL (de novo or transformed from any indolent lymphoma), HGBCL with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangements, PMBCL or FL grade 3B; PET-positive disease after two or more previous lines of systemic therapy including anti-CD20 and anthracycline chemoimmunotherapy; previous autologous or allogeneic HSCT, creatinine clearance >30 to <60 mL/min, LVEF ≥40% to <50% and secondary CNS involvement allowed (single-arm) Fludarabine 30 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 300 mg/m² IV daily for 3 days → liso-cel 2–7 days later as sequential CD8+ and CD4+ CAR+ T-cell infusions at equal target doses, at one of three target dose levels: 50 × 10⁶ (one or two doses), 100 × 10⁶ (recommended; dose confirmation) or 150 × 10⁶ CAR+ T cells; bridging therapy allowed during manufacture; retreatment allowed for relapse after CR Primary: adverse events, dose-limiting toxicities, objective response rate. Secondary: complete response rate, duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, cellular kinetic variables Liso-cel showed activity in relapsed/refractory LBCL with high ORR and low rates of severe CRS and neurological events in this single-arm trial
・ORR (primary analysis set, dose level 2): 74% (95% CI 66·2–81·6)
・ORR/CR (efficacy-evaluable set): 73% / 53%
・DoR: Not reached (median follow-up 12·0 mo)
・PFS: 6·8 mo
・OS: 21·1 mo
・ORR/CR (ITT set): 61% / 44%
・Toxicity: CRS 42% (G≥3 2%), neurological events 30% (G≥3 10%), no deaths from either; G≥3 neutropenia 60%; prolonged cytopenias at day 29 37%; DLTs 6%, including fatal diffuse alveolar damage at dose level 1; 7 treated patients died of TEAEs
・Limitations: Open-label, single-arm, non-comparative design; follow-up short for later-enrolled patients

records.title: ZUMA-7
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — CD19 CAR T-cell therapy, second line · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body:
Large B-cell lymphoma (WHO 2016); second-line; refractory to first-line therapy (no complete response) or biopsy-proven relapse ≤12 months after completing first-line chemoimmunotherapy with anti-CD20 antibody and anthracycline; intended to proceed to high-dose chemotherapy with ASCT; CD19 staining not required; relapse >12 months after induction not enrolled Ⓐ Axi-cel: leukapheresis → cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m²/day + fludarabine 30 mg/m²/day on days −5, −4 and −3 → single axi-cel infusion (target 2×10^6 CAR T cells/kg); bridging limited to glucocorticoids
Ⓑ Standard care: 2 or 3 cycles of investigator-selected, protocol-defined platinum-based chemoimmunotherapy (R-ICE, R-GDP, R-DHAP/R-DHAX or R-ESHAP) → high-dose chemotherapy with ASCT if complete or partial response Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: response rate, overall survival, investigator-assessed event-free survival, progression-free survival, incidence of adverse events, complete response rate, duration of response, blood CAR T-cell levels, patient-reported outcomes Axi-cel improved event-free survival and response vs standard care; interim OS difference was not statistically significant
・EFS: Ⓐ 8.3 vs Ⓑ 2.0 mo; 24-mo EFS Ⓐ 41% vs Ⓑ 16%; HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.31–0.51)
・ORR: Ⓐ 83% vs Ⓑ 50%; CR Ⓐ 65% vs Ⓑ 32%
・OS: Interim; median Ⓐ not reached vs Ⓑ 35.1 mo; HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.53–1.01); 2-yr OS Ⓐ 61% vs Ⓑ 52%
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 AEs Ⓐ 91% vs Ⓑ 83%; Ⓐ grade ≥3 CRS 6%, neurologic events 21%, no CRS/neurologic deaths; fatal AEs Ⓐ 4% vs Ⓑ 1%
・Limitations: OS immature at interim; 56% of Ⓑ received subsequent cellular immunotherapy, only 36% high-dose chemotherapy with ASCT
records.keywords: Locke et al. N Engl J Med 2022;386:640-654  34891224

records.title: TRANSFORM
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — CD19 CAR T-cell therapy, second line · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body:
Large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL NOS, DLBCL transformed from indolent NHL, HGBCL with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangements, PMBCL, T-cell histiocyte-rich LBCL, FL grade 3B); second-line, refractory to or relapsed within 12 months after initial response to first-line therapy with an anthracycline and anti-CD20 antibody; autologous HSCT candidates aged 18–75 years, ECOG PS ≤1, PET-positive disease per Lugano 2014; secondary CNS lymphoma allowed Ⓐ Fludarabine 30 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 300 mg/m² IV daily for 3 days → liso-cel 100 × 10⁶ CAR+ T cells IV as two sequential CD8+ and CD4+ infusions; optional one cycle of a protocol salvage regimen as bridging during manufacturing
Ⓑ Three cycles of R-DHAP, R-ICE or R-GDP (investigator choice; rituximab 375 mg/m² day 1) → in responders (CR/PR), one cycle of high-dose carmustine 300 mg/m² day 1, etoposide 200 mg/m² and cytarabine 200 mg/m² days 2–5, melphalan 140 mg/m² day 6 → autologous HSCT Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: complete response rate, progression-free survival, overall survival, duration of response, overall response rate, 6-, 12-, 24- and 36-month event-free survival, progression-free survival and overall survival rates, clinical, histological and molecular subgroup analyses including receipt of bridging therapy, rate of completion of high-dose chemotherapy and autologous HSCT, health-related quality of life, progression-free survival on next line of treatment, response 3 months after autologous HSCT, adverse events, laboratory abnormalities, hospital resource use, cellular kinetics, B-cell aplasia Second-line liso-cel (Ⓐ) improved EFS, CR and PFS versus standard of care (Ⓑ) in primary refractory or early relapsed LBCL
・EFS: Ⓐ 10·1 vs Ⓑ 2·3 mo; HR 0·35 (95% CI 0·23–0·53)
・CR: Ⓐ 66% vs Ⓑ 39%
・PFS: Ⓐ 14·8 vs Ⓑ 5·7 mo; HR 0·41
・OS: HR 0·51 (95% CI 0·26–1·00); immature, 50 Ⓑ patients approved for crossover to Ⓐ
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 neutropenia Ⓐ 80% vs Ⓑ 51%; prolonged cytopenia Ⓐ 43% vs Ⓑ 3%; Ⓐ grade 3 CRS 1%, grade 3 neurologic events 4%, no grade 4/5 events; no treatment-related deaths with Ⓐ vs one sepsis death with Ⓑ
・Limitations: Interim analysis (median follow-up 6·2 months); OS immature; only 46% of Ⓑ patients received autologous HSCT

records.title: BELINDA
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — CD19 CAR T-cell therapy, second line · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2022
records.body:
Histologically confirmed aggressive B-cell lymphoma; second line, refractory (lack of complete response) to or relapsed within 12 months after the last dose of first-line anti-CD20 antibody and anthracycline-containing regimen; eligible for autologous HSCT per investigator; ECOG 0 or 1 Ⓐ Tisagenlecleucel: optional bridging (investigator's choice of four prespecified platinum-containing combination chemotherapy regimens) → lymphodepletion with fludarabine 25 and cyclophosphamide 250 mg per square meter per day for 3 days (or bendamustine 90 mg per square meter per day for 2 days) → single IV infusion of 0.6 to 6.0×10⁸ CAR-positive viable T cells
Ⓑ Standard care: investigator's choice of four prespecified salvage chemotherapy regimens (second regimen allowed for inadequate week 6 PET-CT response) → high-dose chemotherapy and autologous HSCT in responders Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, overall response rate, safety, cellular kinetics, response at week 6, modified event-free survival Tisagenlecleucel was not superior to standard care as second-line treatment
・EFS: Ⓐ 3.0 vs Ⓑ 3.0 mo; HR 1.07 (95% CI 0.82–1.40); P=0.61
・OS: Immature at median 10.0 mo follow-up; HR 1.24 (95% CI 0.83–1.85)
・Response (≥wk 12): Ⓐ 46.3% vs Ⓑ 42.5% (not adjusted for multiplicity)
・Progression at wk 6: Ⓐ 25.9% vs Ⓑ 13.8%
・Toxicity: Median leukapheresis-to-infusion time 52 days; grade ≥3 AEs Ⓐ 84.0% vs Ⓑ 90.0%; among infused patients, CRS 61.3% (grade ≥3, 5.2%), neurologic events 10.3% (grade ≥3, 1.9%); deaths from AEs Ⓐ 10 vs Ⓑ 13 (2 each from SARS-CoV-2)
・Limitations: OS immature; only 32.5% of standard-care group received autologous HSCT, 50.6% crossed over to tisagenlecleucel
records.keywords: Bishop et al. N Engl J Med 2022;386:629-639  34904798

records.title: PILOT
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — CD19 CAR T-cell therapy, second line · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2022
records.body:
Relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL de novo or transformed from FL, HGBCL with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangements, or FL grade 3B), PET-positive; second line after one prior anthracycline- and CD20-targeted chemoimmunotherapy; not intended for HSCT and ≥1 TNI criterion: age ≥70 years, ECOG PS 2, DLCO ≤60%, LVEF <50%, CrCl <60 mL/min or AST/ALT >2 × ULN; secondary CNS involvement allowed (single-arm) Lymphodepletion with IV fludarabine 30 mg/m² + IV cyclophosphamide 300 mg/m² daily for 3 days → 2–7 days later lisocabtagene maraleucel as two sequential infusions of equal target doses of CD8+ and CD4+ CAR+ T cells, total target dose 100 × 10⁶ CAR+ T cells; bridging therapy allowed; retreatment allowed for relapse after complete response Primary: overall response rate. Secondary: complete response rate, duration of response, duration of response in complete responders, progression-free survival, event-free survival, overall survival, adverse events, laboratory abnormalities, health-related quality of life, health economics outcomes, cellular kinetic profile Liso-cel produced high response rates, with durable responses in complete responders, as second-line therapy in R/R LBCL not intended for HSCT
・ORR: 80%; CR 54%; p<0·0001 vs external real-world reference rate (50·2%)
・DoR: Median 12·09 mo (21·65 mo in complete responders)
・PFS: Median 9·03 mo
・EFS: Median 7·23 mo
・OS: Not reached; immature at median follow-up of 17·6 mo
・ITT (n=74): ORR 68%; CR 46%
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 neutropenia 48%, leukopenia 21%, thrombocytopenia 20%; prolonged cytopenia (day 28) 30%; CRS 38% (grade 3 in 1); neurological events 31% (grade 3 in 3); no grade 4/5 events; 2 COVID-19 deaths (1 treatment-related)
・Limitations: Single-arm design gives no comparative evidence; OS immature at 17·6 mo follow-up

records.title: ALYCANTE
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — CD19 CAR T-cell therapy, second line · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2023
records.body:
Aggressive B-cell NHL (DLBCL, high-grade B-cell lymphoma or FL grade 3B); second line, refractory to or relapsed ≤12 months after first-line anti-CD20 plus anthracycline chemoimmunotherapy; ineligible for HDCT/ASCT by physician assessment plus ≥1 of age ≥65 years, HCT-CI ≥3 or previous ASCT; excluded >1 prior systemic line, previous CD19-targeted therapy, cardiac involvement, known CNS disease (single-arm) Optional bridging with 1–2 cycles of R-GemOx and/or corticosteroids → lymphodepletion with cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m²/day + fludarabine 30 mg/m²/day for 3 days → single IV axi-cel infusion 2–7 days later, target dose 2 × 10^6 CAR-T cells/kg Primary: complete metabolic response at 3 months. Secondary: objective response rate at 3 months, complete metabolic response at 6 months, best objective response rate, best complete metabolic response, duration of response, event-free survival from leukapheresis, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety, health-related quality of life, cell product characteristics, cellular kinetics Second-line axi-cel showed activity and durable remissions in high-risk R/R LBCL ineligible for HDCT/ASCT (single-arm)
・3-mo CMR: 71.0% (95% CI 58.1–81.8%); primary endpoint met
・Best ORR/CMR: 90.3%/79.0%
・PFS: Median 11.8 mo (95% CI 8.4–not reached); median follow-up 12.0 mo
・OS: Not reached
・Toxicity: Grade 3–4 CRS 8.1%, ICANS 14.5%, no CRS/neurologic deaths; grade ≥3 cytopenias 37.1%; ICU transfer 25.8%; non-relapse mortality 9.7% (all late fatal infections, incl. 2 COVID-19 deaths)
・Limitations: Small sample size; short follow-up; no active control, comparative benefit unestablished

records.title: NP30179
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — bispecific T-cell engagers · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2022
records.body:
Relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma: DLBCL NOS, transformed follicular lymphoma, high-grade B-cell lymphoma or primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma; relapsed after or refractory to at least two previous lines, including at least one anti-CD20 antibody-containing and one anthracycline-containing regimen; ECOG 0 or 1 (single-arm) Obinutuzumab 1000 mg IV 7 days before first glofitamab dose → glofitamab IV step-up 2.5 mg day 8 and 10 mg day 15 of cycle 1, then 30 mg day 1 of cycles 2–12 (21-day cycles)
・Duration: 12 cycles or until progression or unacceptable toxicity
・Design: Open-label Primary: complete response rate. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, duration of complete response, time to first complete response, time to first objective response, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety Fixed-duration glofitamab induced complete responses in 39% of heavily pretreated R/R DLBCL, mostly durable; single-arm evidence
・CR: 39% at median 12.6 mo follow-up; pivotal cohort 35% vs 20% historical control (P<0.001)
・ORR: 52%
・DoCR: Median not reached; 78% of complete responses ongoing at 12 mo; median time to CR 42 days
・PFS: Median 4.9 mo; 12-mo PFS 37%
・OS: 12-mo OS 50%
・Supporting cohort: Lower doses; CR 35%; median DoCR 34.2 mo
・Subgroups: CR 35% with vs 42% without prior CAR T; 34% refractory vs 70% nonrefractory to last therapy; no CR in HGBCL
・Toxicity: CRS 63% (G≥3 4%); G≥3 AEs 62%; G3–4 neutropenia 27%; G≥3 ICANS-like events 3%; G5 AEs 5%, mostly Covid-19, none glofitamab-related
・Limitations: Single-arm, historical-control comparison only; open-label; confidence intervals not adjusted for multiplicity
records.keywords: Dickinson et al. N Engl J Med 2022;387:2220-2231  36507690

records.title: EPCORE NHL-1
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — bispecific T-cell engagers · Single-arm clinical trial (phase I/II) · 2022
records.body:
Relapsed or refractory CD20+ aggressive mature B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL, primary mediastinal LBCL, high-grade B-cell lymphoma or follicular lymphoma grade 3B); at least two prior systemic lines including at least one anti-CD20-containing regimen; prior failure of or ineligibility for ASCT; refractory = progression during or within 6 months of therapy; prior CAR T-cell therapy allowed if ≥30 days since last treatment (single-arm) Subcutaneous epcoritamab in 28-day cycles: cycle 1 step-up 0.16 mg day 1, 0.8 mg day 8, then full 48 mg doses from day 15; once weekly cycles 1-3, every 2 weeks cycles 4-9, every 4 weeks from cycle 10
・Duration: Until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: overall response rate. Secondary: duration of response, complete response rate, duration of complete response, progression-free survival, time to response, overall survival, MRD negativity, adverse events, laboratory abnormalities, quality of life Epcoritamab showed deep and durable responses in highly refractory LBCL, including after prior CAR T-cell therapy, in single-arm evidence with no control group
・ORR: 63.1% (95% CI 55.0-70.6); CR rate 38.9% (95% CI 31.2-46.9) at median follow-up 10.7 mo
・DoR: Median 12.0 mo; not reached in complete responders
・PFS: Median 4.4 mo
・OS: Not reached
・Subgroups: Post-CAR T-cell therapy (n=61): ORR 54.1%; CR rate 34.4%
・Toxicity: CRS 49.7% (grade 3 2.5%, no grade 4/5); ICANS 6.4% with one fatal event; grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs 26.8%; fatal TEAEs 5.7% (2 COVID-19)
・Limitations: Single-arm, no control group
records.keywords: Thieblemont et al. J Clin Oncol 2022;41:2238-2247  36548927

records.title: STARGLO
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — bispecific T-cell engagers · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body:
Relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, NOS; transplant-ineligible, after one or more previous systemic therapies (relapsed: response lasting ≥6 months after last line; refractory: no response or progression within 6 months); after only one previous line, ASCT-ineligible by age ≥70 years, end-organ dysfunction, ECOG PS ≥2, patient refusal or comorbidities; ECOG PS 0–2; excluded transformed indolent lymphoma, double/triple-hit HGBL and HGBL NOS Ⓐ Obinutuzumab 1000 mg IV day 1 of cycle 1, then glofitamab IV step-up (cycle 1 day 8: 2·5 mg; day 15: 10 mg) and 30 mg day 1 of cycles 2–12, plus GemOx; glofitamab up to 12 cycles
Ⓑ Rituximab 375 mg/m² IV day 1 plus identical GemOx
・GemOx: Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² and oxaliplatin 100 mg/m² IV (day 2 of cycle 1, then day 1), 21-day cycles for up to 8 cycles Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, complete response rate, duration of complete response, objective response rate, duration of objective response, safety, time to deterioration in physical functioning, time to deterioration in fatigue, time to deterioration in lymphoma symptoms Glofit-GemOx (Ⓐ) improved overall survival vs R-GemOx (Ⓑ) in transplant-ineligible relapsed or refractory DLBCL after ≥1 prior line
・OS (primary analysis, 11·3-mo follow-up): Ⓐ NE vs Ⓑ 9·0 mo; HR 0·59 (95% CI 0·40–0·89); p=0·011
・PFS (IRC, primary analysis): HR 0·37
・CR (primary analysis): Ⓐ 50·3% vs Ⓑ 22·0%
・DoCR/DoR: Did not differ significantly
・Update (3-yr, OS follow-up 35·1 mo): OS Ⓐ 25·5 vs Ⓑ 12·5 mo; HR 0·60 (95% CI 0·4–0·8); 3-yr OS Ⓐ 47·1% vs Ⓑ 27·4%; PFS (IRC) Ⓐ 14·4 vs Ⓑ 3·3 mo; CR Ⓐ 58·5% vs Ⓑ 25·3%
・Subgroups: 2L 3-yr OS Ⓐ 54·6% vs Ⓑ 30·8% (exploratory); race/region OS subgroup inconsistencies underpowered
・Toxicity (3-yr): G≥3 AEs Ⓐ 77·8% vs Ⓑ 45·5%; CRS in 44·8% of glofitamab-exposed patients (G3 2·3%); fatal AEs Ⓐ 16 (8·9%) vs Ⓑ 4 (4·5%)
・Toxicity (primary analysis): 7 (4%) COVID-19-associated deaths with Ⓐ; drug-related deaths Ⓐ 5 (3%) vs Ⓑ 1 (1%)
・Limitations: Open-label; 2L and race/region subgroup findings exploratory/underpowered

records.title: SUNMO
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — bispecific T-cell engagers · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Refractory/relapsed LBCL (DLBCL NOS, HGBCL NOS or double-/triple-hit, FL grade 3b, transformed FL); refractory or relapsed after ≥1 previous therapy; deemed ineligible for ASCT per treating physician; prior polatuzumab vedotin permitted only if no progression within 12 months of last dose Ⓐ Mosunetuzumab SC 5 mg day 1, 45 mg days 8 and 15 of cycle 1, then 45 mg day 1 of cycles 2-8 + polatuzumab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV day 1 of cycles 1-6 (21-day cycles)
Ⓑ R-GemOx: rituximab 375 mg/m², gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² and oxaliplatin 100 mg/m² IV day 1 of cycles 1-8 (14-day cycles, extended to 21 days if needed for haematologic toxicity) Primary: overall response rate, progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, complete response rate, duration of response, duration of complete response, progression-free survival in prespecified subgroups, quality of life, safety Mosun-Pola improved ORR and PFS vs R-GemOx in transplant-ineligible refractory/relapsed LBCL; interim OS not significant
・ORR: Ⓐ 70% vs Ⓑ 40%; significant at protocol-specified interim analysis (P = .0008)
・PFS: Ⓐ 11.5 vs Ⓑ 3.8 mo; HR 0.41 (95% CI 0.3–0.6)
・CR: Ⓐ 51% vs Ⓑ 24%
・DoR: Median Ⓐ 15.6 vs Ⓑ 6.0 mo
・OS: Interim, not significant; Ⓐ 18.7 vs Ⓑ 13.6 mo; HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.5–1.2)
・QoL: Time to deterioration in physical functioning Ⓐ 17.4 vs Ⓑ 5.3 mo; HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.4–1.1)
・Toxicity: CRS Ⓐ 26% (grade 3 0.7%, no grade 4-5); G≥3 thrombocytopenia Ⓐ 2.2% vs Ⓑ 36%; grade 5 AEs Ⓐ 5.2% vs Ⓑ 6.3%
・Limitations: OS immature; enrolment closed early (208 of 222 planned); prior CAR T-cell therapy (n = 8) not assessable
records.keywords: Budde et al. J Clin Oncol 2025;43:3799-3811  41037766

records.title: ELM-2 (DLBCL cohort)
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — bispecific T-cell engagers · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2025
records.body:
R/R DLBCL (de novo or transformed); refractory to or relapsed after ≥2 prior lines of systemic therapy including an anti-CD20 antibody and an alkylator; double-/triple-hit lymphoma accepted; measurable disease, ECOG 0–1; excluded primary CNS lymphoma, prior CAR T cell therapy or CD20×CD3 bispecific antibody, and prior ASCT (as printed, although 17.3% had prior ASCT) (single-arm) IV odronextamab in 21-day cycles: cycle 1 step-up, either 1→20 mg (1 mg split days 1–2, 20 mg split days 8–9, 160 mg day 15) or optimized 0.7→4→20 mg (0.7 mg days 1–2, 4 mg days 8–9, 20 mg days 15–16) → 160 mg days 1, 8 and 15 of C2–C4 → 320 mg every 2 weeks maintenance until progression or unacceptable toxicity; 320 mg every 4 weeks after CR lasting ≥9 months Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: investigator-assessed objective response rate, complete response rate, duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, quality of life, disease control rate, safety, pharmacokinetics, immunogenicity, ctDNA MRD status Odronextamab showed activity in heavily pretreated relapsed/refractory DLBCL, meeting the prespecified ORR threshold, in single-arm evidence without a comparator
・ORR: 52.0%, above prespecified 35% threshold; CR rate 31.5%
・DOR: Median 10.2 mo; median CR duration 17.9 mo (median efficacy follow-up 29.9 mo)
・PFS: Median 4.4 mo
・OS: Median 9.2 mo
・Subgroups: Undetectable ctDNA MRD at C4D15 associated with longer PFS (HR 0.27; exploratory, 63 evaluable)
・Toxicity: CRS 55.1% (G≥3 4.7%), 53.3% with optimized step-up (G≥3 1.7%); no ICANS; infections 64.6% (G≥3 38.6%, COVID-19 18.1%); fatal TEAEs in 15.7% (3.9% treatment-related), including 15 grade 5 infections (5 COVID-19)
・Limitations: Single-arm, no comparator; MRD association exploratory

records.title: POLARGO
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — ADC & antibody combinations, transplant-ineligible · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body:
Relapsed or refractory DLBCL NOS or DLBCL transformed from indolent lymphoma; ≥1 prior line of systemic treatment; ineligible for autologous or allogeneic stem cell transplantation or CAR T-cell therapy at recruitment; excluded active peripheral neuropathy grade >1 and prior polatuzumab vedotin or gemcitabine plus platinum-based combination Ⓐ Polatuzumab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV + R-GemOx (rituximab 375 mg/m², gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m², oxaliplatin 100 mg/m²) IV
Ⓑ R-GemOx alone IV
・Schedule: Every 21 days for up to eight cycles Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, complete response rate at EOT, overall response rate at EOT, event-free survival, best overall response, duration of response, safety, FACT/GOG-Neurotoxicity-12 Polatuzumab vedotin added to R-GemOx improved OS in transplant-ineligible R/R DLBCL
・OS: Primary and final analysis (24.6 mo median follow-up); Ⓐ 19.5 vs Ⓑ 12.5 mo; HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.43–0.83)
・PFS: Investigator-assessed; HR 0.37; Ⓐ 7.4 vs Ⓑ 2.7 mo
・CR (EOT): IRC-assessed; Ⓐ 40.3% vs Ⓑ 19.0%
・ORR: Ⓐ 52.7% vs Ⓑ 24.6%
・Toxicity: Grade 5 AEs Ⓐ 11.7% vs Ⓑ 4.0% (largely infections, including COVID-19); treatment-related grade 5 Ⓐ 3.1% vs Ⓑ 2.4%; peripheral neuropathy Ⓐ 57.0% vs Ⓑ 28.8% (mostly grade 1; grade 3 in 3.9%, Pola arm only); AE-related discontinuation Ⓐ 23.4% vs Ⓑ 8.0%; grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia Ⓐ 34.4% vs Ⓑ 26.4%
・Limitations: No data for patients given prior first-line polatuzumab-containing therapy
records.keywords: Matasar et al. J Clin Oncol 2026 (online ahead of print)

records.title: GO29365
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — ADC & antibody combinations, transplant-ineligible · Randomised clinical trial (phase Ib/II) · 2019
records.body:
Biopsy-confirmed relapsed/refractory DLBCL, excluding transformed lymphoma; after ≥1 prior line of therapy, transplantation-ineligible per treating physician or after treatment failure with prior ASCT; no biomarker selection, double-/triple-hit lymphomas not excluded; ECOG PS 0-2 and grade ≤1 peripheral neuropathy required Ⓐ Polatuzumab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV day 2 of cycle 1 then day 1 + bendamustine 90 mg/m² IV days 2 and 3 of cycle 1 then days 1 and 2 + rituximab 375 mg/m² IV day 1 (pola-BR)
Ⓑ Bendamustine + rituximab at the same doses (BR)
Ⓒ Separate single-arm cohort: pola-BG with obinutuzumab 1,000 mg IV days 1, 8 and 15 of cycle 1 then day 1 in place of rituximab
・Duration: Each for up to six 21-day cycles Primary: safety and tolerability (phase Ib), complete response rate at end of treatment (phase II). Secondary: objective response rate at end of treatment, best overall response, duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, efficacy by cell of origin, efficacy by MYC/BCL2 double-expressor status, CD79b expression and outcome, safety Pola-BR increased CR rate and prolonged PFS and OS vs BR in transplantation-ineligible R/R DLBCL
・CR (EOT): Ⓐ 40.0% vs Ⓑ 17.5% (P = .026)
・Pola-BG: Single-arm cohort (n = 27); CR 29.6%; median OS 10.8 mo
・PFS: Ⓐ 9.5 vs Ⓑ 3.7 mo; HR 0.36 (95% CI 0.21-0.63); median follow-up 22.3 mo
・OS: Ⓐ 12.4 vs Ⓑ 4.7 mo; HR 0.42 (95% CI 0.24-0.75); exploratory
・DOR: HR 0.47 (95% CI 0.19-1.14); not significant
・Toxicity: G3-4 neutropenia Ⓐ 46.2% vs Ⓑ 33.3%; thrombocytopenia Ⓐ 41% vs Ⓑ 23.1%; anemia Ⓐ 28.2% vs Ⓑ 17.9%; infections Ⓐ 23.1% vs Ⓑ 20.5%; peripheral neuropathy Ⓐ 43.6% (grade 1-2); fatal AEs Ⓐ 9 vs Ⓑ 11 (mostly infection)
・Limitations: OS and between-arm comparisons were exploratory; modest phase II sample
records.keywords: Sehn et al. J Clin Oncol 2019;38:155-165  31693429

records.title: L-MIND
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — ADC & antibody combinations, transplant-ineligible · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2020
records.body:
Relapsed or refractory DLBCL, including transformed indolent lymphoma; after one to three systemic regimens (at least one anti-CD20); not candidates for high-dose chemotherapy and ASCT (eg, age >70 years, comorbidities, failed ASCT, refusal); excluded primary refractory (no response to, or progression during or within 6 months of, frontline therapy; 3 months before June 27, 2016 amendment), known double-/triple-hit, prior anti-CD19 or IMiD, CNS lymphoma (single-arm) Tafasitamab 12 mg/kg IV weekly in cycles 1–3 (days 1, 8, 15, 22; extra loading dose day 4 of cycle 1), then every 14 days (days 1 and 15) + oral lenalidomide 25 mg daily days 1–21 of 28-day cycles, for up to 12 cycles → tafasitamab monotherapy (stable disease or better) until disease progression Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: disease control rate, duration of response, time to next treatment, progression-free survival, overall survival, time to progression, incidence and severity of adverse events, immunogenicity, pharmacokinetics, B-cell, T-cell and natural killer-cell counts over time Tafasitamab plus lenalidomide showed activity in ASCT-ineligible relapsed or refractory DLBCL, with a high complete response rate, in this single-arm trial
・ORR: 60%; CR 43%; median follow-up 13·2 mo
・DoR: Median 21·7 mo
・PFS: Median 12·1 mo (95% CI 5·7–not reached)
・OS: Not reached at 19·6 mo follow-up
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 neutropenia 48%, thrombocytopenia 17%, febrile neutropenia 12%; serious AEs 51%; 4 treatment-emergent deaths, none treatment-related
・Limitations: Open-label single-arm design precludes comparison with other therapies including single-agent lenalidomide; few primary refractory (19%) or double-/triple-hit (2%) patients limit extrapolation to them

records.title: LOTIS-2
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — ADC & antibody combinations, transplant-ineligible · Single-arm clinical trial (phase II) · 2021
records.body:
Relapsed or refractory DLBCL (2016 WHO classification, including DLBCL NOS, HGBCL with MYC and BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangements or with MYC and BCL2 and BCL6 rearrangements, and PMBCL); after two or more multiagent systemic regimens, transformed indolent lymphoma allowed; biopsy-proven CD19 expression required after previous CD19-directed therapy; excluded bulky disease (tumour ≥10 cm in longest dimension, from protocol amendment 2), Burkitt lymphoma, active CNS lymphoma (single-arm) Loncastuximab tesirine IV on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, 150 µg/kg for the first two cycles then 75 µg/kg for subsequent cycles, for up to 1 year or until disease relapse or progression, unacceptable toxicity or death; continuation beyond 1 year allowed with clinical benefit if agreed with the sponsor Primary: overall response rate. Secondary: duration of response, complete response rate, relapse-free survival, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety, concentrations and pharmacokinetic parameters of loncastuximab tesirine, anti-drug antibody titres, health-related quality of life Loncastuximab tesirine showed substantial antitumour activity with durable responses in heavily pretreated relapsed or refractory DLBCL
・ORR: 48.3% (95% CI 39.9–56.7); CR rate 24.1%
・DoR: Median 10.3 mo (13.4 mo with CR, 5.7 mo with PR)
・PFS: Median 4.9 mo
・OS: Median 9.9 mo
・Toxicity: Grade ≥3 TEAEs: neutropenia 26%, thrombocytopenia 18%, increased GGT 17%; serious TEAEs 39%; discontinuation for TEAEs 23%; fatal TEAEs 6%, none treatment-related
・Limitations: Single-arm, no comparator; PFS and OS still maturing (data cutoff April 6, 2020)

records.title: ECHELON-3
records.subtitle: High Grade B-Cell Lymphoma · Relapsed / refractory — ADC & antibody combinations, transplant-ineligible · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body:
Relapsed or refractory DLBCL, including transformed DLBCL; third-line or later after ≥2 previous lines of systemic therapy; CD30 unselected (stratified ≥1% vs <1%); ineligible for hematopoietic SCT or CAR T-cell therapy (prior CAR T-cell therapy or SCT allowed), ECOG PS ≤2 Ⓐ BV 1.2 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks + Lenalidomide 20 mg orally once daily + Rituximab 375 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks
Ⓑ Placebo IV every 3 weeks + Lenalidomide 20 mg orally once daily + Rituximab 375 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks
・Duration: Until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
・Design: Double-blind Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, complete response rate, duration of response, adverse events, overall survival in the CD30-positive subgroup, duration of complete response Ⓐ BV + Len + R improved OS vs Ⓑ placebo + Len + R in heavily pretreated R/R DLBCL
・OS: Prespecified interim analysis; Ⓐ 13.8 vs Ⓑ 8.5 mo; HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.45-0.89)
・PFS: Ⓐ 4.2 vs Ⓑ 2.6 mo; HR 0.53
・ORR: Ⓐ 64% vs Ⓑ 42%
・CR: Ⓐ 40% vs Ⓑ 19%
・Toxicity: G≥3 TEAEs Ⓐ 88% vs Ⓑ 77% (neutropenia 43% vs 28%); fatal TEAEs Ⓐ 12% vs Ⓑ 8% (mostly COVID-19-related); peripheral neuropathy Ⓐ 31% vs Ⓑ 24% (grade 3 6% vs 2%)
・Limitations: PFS and ORR investigator-assessed without independent review; short follow-up; QoL not analysed (low PRO compliance)

records.title: GHSG HD10
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage favorable (stage I-II) — de-escalation & PET-guided RT · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2010
records.body: Untreated Hodgkin lymphoma in clinical stage I or II with none of the trial's risk factors, the GHSG early-stage favourable category; aged 16-75. Nodular lymphocyte-predominant histology was eligible and made up 7.5% of subtyped patients. 1,370 were randomised and 1,190 analysed, after 180 exclusions of which most were incorrect initial staging 4 vs 2 cycles of ABVD, each followed by 30 vs 20 Gy involved-field radiotherapy — a 2x2 factorial randomised 1:1:1:1 to 4 groups Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, PFS, complete response, toxicity. Halving chemotherapy and lowering the radiotherapy dose both held, and less treatment was markedly less toxic; 2 cycles of ABVD plus 20 Gy became the standard for favourable early-stage disease. Against a 7-percentage-point margin on 5-year freedom from treatment failure, 2 cycles gave 91.1% against 93.0% for 4 cycles, a difference of -1.9 points (95% CI -5.2 to 1.4), and 20 Gy gave 92.9% against 93.4% for 30 Gy, -0.5 points (-3.6 to 2.6). The least intensive group, 2 cycles plus 20 Gy, also sat within the margin against 4 cycles plus 30 Gy, -1.6 points (-6.3 to 3.1). 5-year overall survival was about 97% in all 4 groups. Toxicity moved the other way and by more: grade 3 or 4 acute events 33.2% with 2 cycles vs 51.7% with 4, and 2.9% with 20 Gy vs 8.7% with 30 Gy. 6 of the 7 deaths from toxicity of first-line treatment were in patients given 4 cycles, though all 5 deaths from salvage toxicity followed 2 cycles.

records.title: GHSG HD16
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage favorable (stage I-II) — de-escalation & PET-guided RT · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2019
records.body: Untreated classic Hodgkin lymphoma in clinical stage I or II, or nodular lymphocyte-predominant disease in stage IB, IIA or IIB, without a large mediastinal mass, extranodal lesions, raised ESR or 3 or more involved nodal areas; aged 18-75. All 1,150 were randomised before any interim PET existed; the primary comparison rests on 628 PET-2-negative patients analysed per protocol 2 cycles of ABVD then 20 Gy involved-field radiotherapy in all patients vs 2 cycles of ABVD then 20 Gy only where the interim PET after cycle 2 was positive on central review Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, negative interim PET rate, second malignancy, toxicity. Radiotherapy cannot be dropped after a negative interim PET: omitting it cost tumour control and non-inferiority was not met. Among the 628 PET-2-negative patients analysed per protocol, 5-year progression-free survival was 86.1% with ABVD alone against 93.4% with chemotherapy plus 20 Gy, a difference of -7.3 points (95% CI -13.0 to -1.6); the hazard ratio was 1.78 and its interval reached 3.12, above the 3.01 margin, so a 10-point loss could not be excluded. The mechanism was local: in-field recurrence 9% with ABVD alone vs 2%, while out-field recurrence was 5% vs 4%. Survival showed nothing either way on 12 deaths in total, 5-year overall survival 98.4% vs 98.1%, and there were more deaths in the arm with better tumour control, 9 of 328 vs 3 of 300. Interim PET was positive in 34% of the 1,007 scans centrally reviewed.

records.title: GHSG HD13
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage favorable (stage I-II) — de-escalation & PET-guided RT · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2015
records.body: Untreated classic Hodgkin lymphoma in clinical stage I or II, or nodular lymphocyte-predominant disease in stage IB, IIA or IIB only, without a large mediastinal mass, extranodal lesions, raised ESR or 3 or more involved nodal areas. 1,710 were randomised and 1,502 qualified for analysis; stage IA nodular lymphocyte-predominant disease was a named reason for exclusion 2 cycles of ABVD vs 3 reduced-intensity variants — ABV (no dacarbazine), AVD (no bleomycin) or AV (neither) — each followed by 30 Gy involved-field radiotherapy, randomised 1:1:1:1 Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, PFS, complete remission, toxicity. Neither dacarbazine nor bleomycin can be omitted from ABVD. Both dacarbazine-omitted arms were closed early for higher event rates, AV in September 2005 and ABV in February 2006, and each is compared with the ABVD patients recruited alongside it: 5-year freedom from treatment failure 77.1% with AV against 92.3%, hazard ratio 2.57 (95% CI 1.51-4.40), and 81.4% with ABV against 92.9%, 2.06 (1.21-3.52). The bleomycin-omitted variant ran to the end and also fell short: AVD 89.2% against 93.1% for ABVD, hazard ratio 1.50 (95% CI 1.00-2.26), whose upper bound exceeded the 1.72 margin, so non-inferiority was not shown. Overall survival was 94-98% across the 4 groups and did not separate. No death was due to toxicity of first-line treatment in any group, and grade 3 or 4 leucopenia tracked bleomycin, 17-18% with it against 11-12% without. Unmodified ABVD remains the standard; radiotherapy was 30 Gy in every group here, chosen before HD10 established 20 Gy.

records.title: GHSG HD7
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage favorable (stage I-II) — de-escalation & PET-guided RT · Randomised clinical trial · 2007
records.body: Newly diagnosed, previously untreated, histology-proven Hodgkin lymphoma in clinical or pathologic stage IA-IIB without GHSG risk factors (large mediastinal mass, extranodal disease, massive splenic involvement, high ESR); all HL subtypes incl. lymphocyte-predominant; age 16-75, Karnofsky >70%; prior malignancy and composite lymphoma excluded 2 cycles ABVD → 30 Gy extended-field RT (spleen 36 Gy) + 10 Gy involved-field boost vs 30 Gy extended-field RT (spleen 36 Gy) + 10 Gy involved-field boost Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, complete remission, relapse, second malignancy, acute toxicity. Two cycles of ABVD before radiotherapy transformed disease control in favourable early-stage disease and is why chemotherapy became part of the standard: 7-year freedom from treatment failure was 88% with combined-modality treatment against 67% with extended-field radiotherapy alone, a 21-point difference driven almost entirely by relapse, 3.2% against 21.9%. Survival did not separate, 7-year overall survival 94% against 92%, and 51 of 627 patients died in all. Treatment-related deaths ran 2 with chemotherapy added against 7 with radiotherapy alone, most after the salvage those relapses required. Adding ABVD did not increase acute radiotherapy toxicity, grade 3 in a few percent of either arm, though ABVD itself gave grade 3 leukopenia in 11% and hair loss in 9.9%. Second malignancies were 18 against 21, 39 in total, with similar cumulative incidence, though the authors caution that numbers at risk beyond year 9 are small and more events will follow. Median observation 87 months.

records.title: GHSG HD14
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage unfavorable (stage I-II) — intensification & PET-adapted therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2012
records.body: Untreated Hodgkin lymphoma in clinical stage IA, IB or IIA with at least one GHSG risk factor — a large mediastinal mass, extranodal involvement, raised ESR or 3 or more involved nodal areas — and stage IIB with only the last two of those. Median age 32, range 18-60. 1,655 were randomised and 1,528 qualified for the primary analysis 2 cycles of escalated BEACOPP then 2 cycles of ABVD vs 4 cycles of ABVD, each followed by 30 Gy involved-field radiotherapy Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, PFS, response, toxicity. Two cycles of escalated BEACOPP before ABVD improved tumour control decisively, and the price is acute toxicity. 5-year freedom from treatment failure was 94.8% against 87.7% with 4 cycles of ABVD, a difference of 7.2 points (95% CI 3.8 to 10.5), hazard ratio 0.44 (95% CI 0.30 to 0.66); 5-year progression-free survival 95.4% against 89.1%. Superiority was reached at the third of five planned interim analyses and randomisation was stopped early for it. Overall survival was 97.0% at 5 years and did not separate. The cost is in the marrow: at least one grade 3 or 4 event in 87.1% against 50.7%, grade 4 in 56.6% against 5.9%, and grade 3 or 4 leukopenia in 79.0% against 23.5%. All 4 deaths from first-line treatment toxicity were on the intensified arm, though 6 of the 7 salvage-toxicity deaths were on ABVD. Median follow-up was 43 months, short of the 5-year landmarks these figures quote.

records.title: GHSG HD11
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage unfavorable (stage I-II) — intensification & PET-adapted therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2010
records.body: Untreated Hodgkin lymphoma of any histology in clinical stage IA, IB or IIA with at least one GHSG risk factor — a large mediastinal mass, extranodal involvement, raised ESR or 3 or more involved nodal areas — and stage IIB with only the last two of those. 1,570 were randomised and 1,395 qualified for the chemotherapy analysis; 1,351 for the radiotherapy analysis 4 cycles of ABVD vs 4 cycles of baseline BEACOPP, each followed by 30 vs 20 Gy involved-field radiotherapy — a 2x2 factorial in 4 groups Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, PFS, response, toxicity. Neither escalating the chemotherapy nor lowering the radiotherapy dose improved on 4 cycles of ABVD followed by 30 Gy, which the authors concluded should remain the standard. 5-year freedom from treatment failure was 85.0% across the trial. At 30 Gy, baseline BEACOPP and ABVD did not differ, 1.6 points (95% CI -3.6 to 6.9); only at 20 Gy did BEACOPP come out ahead, 5.7 points (0.1 to 11.3). Dropping 30 Gy to 20 Gy after ABVD cost 4.7 points (-10.3 to 0.8), the bound falling outside the 7-point non-inferiority limit, so 20 Gy was not established there; after baseline BEACOPP the loss was 0.8 points (-5.8 to 4.2) and 20 Gy was non-inferior. The interaction between the two questions was not shown, at P=0.16. 5-year overall survival was 94-95% in all 4 groups. Baseline BEACOPP cost more acute toxicity, at least one grade 3 or 4 event in 73.8% against 51.5%, and 30 Gy more than 20 Gy, 12.0% against 5.7%.

records.title: UK RAPID
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage unfavorable (stage I-II) — intensification & PET-adapted therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2015
records.body: Untreated classic Hodgkin lymphoma in clinical stage IA or IIA without mediastinal bulk, aged 16-75. 602 were registered and started ABVD; 571 were scanned after 3 cycles and 426 were PET-negative, of whom 420 were randomised; the 145 who were PET-positive received a fourth cycle with radiotherapy and were followed without randomisation After 3 cycles of ABVD and a negative PET: 30 Gy involved-field radiotherapy vs no further treatment (single-arm follow-up for PET-positive patients, who received a 4th ABVD cycle plus radiotherapy) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: interim PET positivity rate, OS and cause of death, second cancers. Omitting radiotherapy after a negative PET was not shown to be non-inferior, though the absolute loss was small and survival was not harmed. Among the 420 randomised, 3-year progression-free survival was 90.8% without further treatment against 94.6% with radiotherapy, a difference of -3.8 points whose 95% interval ran to -8.8 and so fell outside the 7-point margin. Only 40 of the 46 events the trial was designed around had occurred. Per protocol the gap widened, 90.8% against 97.1%. Survival did not separate: 3-year overall survival 99.0% without radiotherapy against 97.1% with it, and of the 8 deaths in the radiotherapy arm 5 were in patients who never received it. The trade is a few points of tumour control against irradiating everyone, in a group whose 3-year survival exceeds 97% either way.

records.title: EORTC/LYSA/FIL H10
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage unfavorable (stage I-II) — intensification & PET-adapted therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2017
records.body: Untreated classic supradiaphragmatic Hodgkin lymphoma in Ann Arbor stage I or II, aged 15-70, assigned at entry to an EORTC favourable or unfavourable cohort. All 1,950 were randomised before any PET existed; treatment was then adapted to the PET after 2 cycles of ABVD, and the two cohorts were analysed separately PET-negative after 2 cycles of ABVD: 4 cycles of ABVD (favourable) or 6 cycles (unfavourable) with no radiotherapy vs 3 or 4 cycles plus involved-node radiotherapy. PET-positive: 2 cycles of escalated BEACOPP plus involved-node radiotherapy vs continuing ABVD plus radiotherapy Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, second malignancy. Radiotherapy could not be dropped after a negative PET in either cohort, while intensifying after a positive PET improved control. In the favourable cohort 5-year progression-free survival was 87.1% with ABVD alone against 99.0% with ABVD plus involved-node radiotherapy, hazard ratio 15.8 (95% CI 3.79 to 66.07); in the unfavourable cohort 89.6% against 92.1%, 1.45 (0.84 to 2.50). Both upper bounds exceeded their margins, 3.2 and 2.10, so non-inferiority was not shown in either. Where the PET was positive, switching to 2 cycles of escalated BEACOPP raised 5-year progression-free survival to 90.6% from 77.4%, hazard ratio 0.42 (0.23 to 0.74). Survival was not uniform: the PET-positive patients kept on ABVD with radiotherapy had 5-year overall survival of 89.3%, the lowest in the trial, against 96.0% with escalated BEACOPP, hazard ratio 0.45 (95% CI 0.19 to 1.07), which the authors call a trend. The PET-negative strands ran 96.7% to 100.0%.

records.title: GHSG HD17
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage unfavorable (stage I-II) — intensification & PET-adapted therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2021
records.body: Untreated stage IA, IB or IIA classical Hodgkin lymphoma or nodular lymphocyte-predominant disease with at least one GHSG risk factor, or stage IIB with a raised ESR or 3 or more involved nodal areas and neither a bulky mass nor extranodal disease; aged 18-60. All 1,100 were randomised at entry, before the PET after 4 cycles; 905 formed the per-protocol population on which the verdict rests 2 cycles of escalated BEACOPP then 2 cycles of ABVD in both groups, followed by 30 Gy involved-field radiotherapy in all patients vs 30 Gy involved-node radiotherapy only where the PET after cycle 4 was positive Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, complete remission, PET-negative rate, late toxicity, second malignancy. Radiotherapy can be omitted after a negative PET in unfavourable early-stage disease. 5-year progression-free survival was 95.1% with PET-guided treatment against 97.3% when everyone was irradiated, a difference of 2.2 points whose upper bound of 5.3 stayed inside the 8-point margin, so non-inferiority was met; among the PET-negative patients alone it was 95.9% against 97.7%, a difference of 1.7 points with the same bound. The hazard ratio was 0.523 (95% CI 0.226 to 1.211) and crosses 1. 5-year overall survival was 98.8%, with 10 deaths among 1,096 patients and 1 attributed to treatment. Late toxicity, which is the whole reason to omit radiotherapy, is not reported here and is deferred to a later analysis; second malignancies were 7 of 546 against 8 of 550 so far. Median follow-up 46.2 months and 25 progression-free survival events against the 35 the trial was powered for, so the 5-year figures are early.

records.title: GHSG HD8
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Early-stage unfavorable (stage I-II) — intensification & PET-adapted therapy · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2003
records.body: Untreated Hodgkin lymphoma of any histology in clinical stage I or II with one or more risk factors, or in stage IIIA with none — the stage IIIA route is the inverse of the stage I-II one, not a selection within it. Nodular lymphocyte-predominant disease was enrolled. 1,204 were randomised and 1,064 were informative for efficacy 2 cycles of COPP plus ABVD followed by 30 Gy extended-field radiotherapy vs 30 Gy involved-field radiotherapy, each with 10 Gy to initial bulk Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, toxicity, second malignancy. Shrinking the radiotherapy field from extended to involved cost nothing in disease control and spared considerable acute toxicity, which is why involved-field became the standard. 5-year freedom from treatment failure was 84.2% with involved-field against 85.8% with extended-field, a difference of 1.6 points whose upper 95% bound of 5.9 stayed inside the 8-point inferiority limit the trial set; 5-year overall survival was 92.4% against 90.8%. The design tested equivalence rather than non-inferiority and reports no hazard ratio. Acute radiotherapy toxicity was the reason to change practice: nausea 29.1% against 62.5%, leukopenia 33.3% against 49.1% and thrombocytopenia 5.5% against 16.7%, all lower with involved-field. Second malignancies occurred in 2.8% against 4.5% and deaths in 6.4% against 8.1%, neither difference established.

records.title: GHSG HD9
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Advanced-stage frontline (stage III-IV) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2003
records.body: Untreated advanced or unfavourable intermediate-stage Hodgkin lymphoma, ages 15-65: stage IIB or IIIA with a large mediastinal mass alone or with extranodal lesions or massive splenic involvement, stage IIIA with a raised sedimentation rate or 3 or more involved nodal areas, or any stage IIIB-IV; Karnofsky above 70%, HIV-negative. 1,282 were assigned and 1,196 assessable at 10 years (261, 469 and 466 by arm); COPP/ABVD closed early in 1996. 8 cycles COPP/ABVD vs 8 cycles baseline BEACOPP vs 8 cycles escalated BEACOPP (cyclophosphamide 1,200, etoposide 200, doxorubicin 35 mg/m2 with filgrastim from day 8); consolidation radiotherapy to residual or initially bulky disease Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, treatment outcome as complete remission or early progression, second malignancy, causes of death, acute toxicity, survival after relapse. Escalated BEACOPP held its advantage over COPP/ABVD to 10 years, at the price of secondary leukaemia. Freedom from treatment failure was 82% with escalated BEACOPP, 70% with baseline BEACOPP and 64% with COPP/ABVD, and overall survival 86%, 80% and 75% in the same order, at a median 111 months; escalated beat baseline BEACOPP on both (P<.0001 and P=.0053). Secondary leukaemia or myelodysplasia tracked dose - 3.0% with escalated BEACOPP against 1.5% and 0.4%, 10-year cumulative incidence 3.2%, 2.2% and 0.4% (P=.030) - and 13 of the 14 escalated-arm cases arose within 7 years. Second malignancy overall did not separate (cumulative incidence 6.5%, 7.9% and 5.3%, P=.82), non-Hodgkin lymphoma and solid tumours running the other way. COPP/ABVD was closed at the first interim analysis and contributes 261 patients against 469 and 466. This 10-year cut sits outside the trial's prespecified analysis schedule, so none of its comparisons is a protected result.

records.title: GHSG HD15
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Advanced-stage frontline (stage III-IV) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2012
records.body: Untreated, histology-confirmed advanced-stage Hodgkin lymphoma: stage IIB with a large mediastinal mass or extranodal lesions, or any stage III or IV; ages 18-60; ECOG 0-2; HIV-negative and without concurrent disease. Expert-panel reference histology was mandatory and excluded 44 patients from all analyses. 2,182 were randomised and 2,126 analysed. 8 cycles escalated BEACOPP (21-day cycles) vs 6 cycles escalated BEACOPP vs 8 cycles BEACOPP-14 (baseline doses, 14-day cycles); by protocol 30 Gy radiotherapy was planned for residual masses of 2.5 cm or more that remained PET-positive, and withheld otherwise Primary: freedom from treatment failure. Secondary: OS, PFS, complete remission, treatment-related toxicity. Independent endpoint: negative predictive value of PET. Six cycles of escalated BEACOPP were non-inferior to eight and less toxic, and the investigators concluded 6 cycles should be the treatment of choice. 5-year freedom from treatment failure was 89.3% with 6 cycles, 84.4% with 8 cycles and 85.4% with 8 cycles of BEACOPP-14; both reduced-intensity arms met non-inferiority on a hazard-ratio margin of 1.51. Superiority on freedom from treatment failure was not established: 6 cycles separated from 8 there only in the trial's descriptive analysis, not in its protected one. Toxicity favoured 6 cycles: treatment-related death 0.8% vs 2.1%, secondary leukaemia or myelodysplasia 0.3% vs 2.7% (P=0.0001). 5-year overall survival was 95.3% vs 91.9%, a difference of 3.3 points (97.5% CI 0.2 to 6.5). Confining radiotherapy to PET-positive residua cut its use to 11%, with a negative predictive value of 94.1%. Reported at the fourth preplanned interim analysis, median 48 months and 3 years early.

records.title: RATHL
records.subtitle: Hodgkin Lymphoma · Advanced-stage frontline (stage III-IV) · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2016
records.body: Previously untreated advanced classic Hodgkin lymphoma: stage IIB-IV, or stage IIA with bulky disease or 3 or more involved sites; aged 18 or over, no upper limit, fit for full chemotherapy. Of 1,214 registered and 1,203 eligible, 937 were PET-negative after 2 cycles of ABVD and 935 of those were randomised; of the 182 PET-positive, 172 escalated to BEACOPP without randomisation. After 2 cycles of ABVD and a negative central interim PET-CT: continue ABVD for cycles 3-6 vs omit bleomycin (AVD) for cycles 3-6; interim-PET-positive patients escalated to BEACOPP-14 or escalated BEACOPP Primary: 3-year progression-free survival. Secondary: PFS among interim-PET-positive patients given BEACOPP, OS, short- and long-term toxicity, respiratory function. Omitting bleomycin after a negative interim PET fell just short of the prespecified non-inferiority margin, so AVD was not formally established as non-inferior, though efficacy was not significantly lower and pulmonary toxicity was less. 3-year progression-free survival was 85.7% continuing ABVD and 84.4% with AVD; the 1.6-percentage-point difference carried a 95% CI of -3.2 to 5.3, whose upper bound exceeded the 5-point margin, and the hazard ratio was 1.13 (95% CI 0.81-1.57). 3-year overall survival was 97.2% and 97.6%.
