records.body: Colorectal, gastro-oesophageal or pancreatic cancer receiving oxaliplatin-based multiagent chemotherapy with persistent chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia and at least 3 planned further cycles; platelet count 85×10⁹/L or lower on trial day 1 Romiplostim SC weekly, titrated to platelets 100–250×10⁹/L, for up to 3 further chemotherapy cycles vs matched placebo weekly (2:1) Primary: Absence of chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia-driven chemotherapy dose modification in cycles 2 and 3. Secondary: Platelet nadir, Time to platelet response, Grade 2 or higher bleeding, Overall survival, Platelet transfusion, Platelet response by week 4, Safety Romiplostim reduced chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia-driven dose modification: 84% versus 36% had none in cycles 2 and 3 (risk ratio 2.77, 95% CI 1.78–4.30). Platelet nadir was higher and response faster. Grade 2 or higher bleeding did not differ (4.0 versus 7.6 per 100 patient-years; HR 0.53, 0.04–6.77); the fixed sequence stopped there, so overall survival, transfusion and week-4 response were not formally tested. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related AEs were 3% versus 4%; thromboembolism occurred in 2% versus 0% in the safety population. Restricted to gastrointestinal cancers receiving oxaliplatin combinations.

records.title: DESCEND
records.subtitle: Supportive Care · Anti-EMETICS · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Adults with histologically or cytologically confirmed malignant solid tumours; scheduled to receive HEC as defined by NCCN (incl. carboplatin AUC ≥4), or T-DXd- or SG-based regimens; excluded moderately/highly emetogenic radiotherapy within 7 days prior or during days 1-5, benzodiazepine or opioid use within 1 week, severe cardiovascular, diabetic, pulmonary or psychiatric disease, and concurrent antiemetic drugs or CYP3A4 inducers/inhibitors NEPA orally 1 hour before chemotherapy on day 1 + olanzapine 5 mg orally once daily days 1-4 in all arms, with DEX 12 mg day 1 and 8 mg days 2-4 (oral or IV; standard) vs DEX 6 mg day 1 only (DEX-sparing) vs no DEX (DEX-free) Primary: complete response rate (0-120 hours). Secondary: complete response rate (0-24 hours), complete response rate (24-120 hours), complete protection (0-24 hours), complete protection (24-120 hours), complete protection (0-120 hours), total control (0-24 hours), total control (0-168 hours), adverse events, quality of life (FLIE), patient-reported DEX-related side effects NEPA plus olanzapine with DEX reduced to 6 mg day 1 only, or omitted, was noninferior to standard 4-day DEX for CINV prevention in HEC. 0-120 h CR (FAS, stratified): 72.4% standard, 72.2% DEX-sparing (RD –0.2%; 95% CI –8.7 to 8.5) and 70.1% DEX-free (RD –2.2%; 95% CI –10.7 to 6.4); both met the –12% margin, consistent in the per-protocol set. Secondary CR, complete protection and total control did not differ significantly (exploratory tests). DEX-free patients had numerically poorer early nausea (FLIE nausea-domain no impact on daily life ≈51% on days 2-3 vs ≈64%-68%), converging by days 5-7. Open-label; only 5.9% received concurrent immunotherapy, precluding definitive conclusions in that setting. No serious drug-related adverse events; patient-reported DEX-related side-effect severity was lower with DEX-sparing (except facial rash/acne) and with DEX-free.
records.keywords: Meng et al. J Clin Oncol 2026;44:2390-2399  42241642

records.title: Ponsegromab (Groarke)
records.subtitle: Supportive Care · Cancer cachexia · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2024
records.body: NSCLC, pancreatic or colorectal cancer with cachexia, serum GDF-15 at least 1500 pg/mL, ECOG 3 or lower and expected survival at least 4 months Ponsegromab 100, 200 or 400 mg SC every 4 weeks for 3 doses vs placebo Primary: Change in body weight at 12 weeks. Secondary: Appetite, Cachexia symptoms, Physical activity, Safety, Skeletal muscle index Ponsegromab increased body weight dose-dependently, but this short phase 2 trial was not multiplicity-controlled and all reported efficacy estimates were post hoc Bayesian analyses. At 400 mg, the week-12 difference versus placebo was 2.81 kg (95% credible interval 1.55–4.08). Appetite scores and nonsedentary activity favoured 400 mg, but the article reported no consistent difference in other cachexia-symptom or physical-activity measures; only 14/50 versus 12/45 had wearable data at week 12. AEs occurred in 70% versus 80%, serious AEs in 32% versus 24%, and deaths in 21/142 versus 5/45; none was considered treatment related. Results apply only to GDF-15-high cachexia in NSCLC, pancreatic or colorectal cancer.

records.title: API-CAT (Mahé)
records.subtitle: Supportive Care · Cancer-associated thrombosis · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2025
records.body: Active cancer with proximal DVT or pulmonary embolism after at least 6 months of anticoagulation Apixaban 2.5 mg orally twice daily vs 5 mg orally twice daily for 12 months Primary: Recurrent venous thromboembolism. Secondary: Clinically relevant bleeding, Major bleeding, Mortality Reduced-dose apixaban was non-inferior to full-dose apixaban for recurrent VTE (2.1% versus 2.8%; adjusted subdistribution HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.41–1.41) and caused less clinically relevant bleeding (12.1% versus 15.6%; adjusted subdistribution HR 0.75, 0.58–0.97). Mortality was 17.7% versus 19.6%. These results support reduced-dose apixaban for extended anticoagulation in active cancer after the initial 6 months.

records.title: IV Magnesium for Cisplatin-AKI (Gupta)
records.subtitle: Supportive Care · Chemotherapy nephrotoxicity · Observational cohort study · 2025
records.body: Adults with cancer receiving a first IV cisplatin dose at 5 US cancer centres IV magnesium on day 1 of cisplatin vs no IV magnesium (inverse-probability-weighted observational cohort) Primary: Cisplatin-associated acute kidney injury or death within 14 days. Secondary: Alternative acute-kidney-injury definitions, Major adverse kidney events at 90 days IV magnesium was associated with lower cisplatin-associated AKI or death (2.7% versus 5.3%; adjusted OR 0.80, 95% CI 0.66–0.97), with consistency in sensitivity analyses including 90-day major adverse kidney events. This observational association supports randomised evaluation; it does not establish a prophylactic dose, causal renal protection or magnesium safety because direct magnesium adverse events were not reported.

records.title: Dose Adjustments in Renal/Hepatic Impairment (Krens)
records.subtitle: Supportive Care · Dose adjustment / organ impairment · Systematic review · 2019
records.body: Adults with cancer receiving anticancer treatment and renal or hepatic impairment N/A — systematic review and dosing reference, not a treatment comparison N/A Krens 2019 and the 2023 update compile pharmacokinetic evidence, product information and author dose recommendations for anticancer drugs in renal or hepatic impairment. They are historical author syntheses, not current prescribing authority: recommendations vary in evidentiary basis and the 2023 supplementary appendix is not a replacement for contemporary labelling, specialist pharmacy advice or current guidelines. Use the underlying drug-specific source before applying a dose adjustment.

records.title: CaPP3
records.subtitle: Supportive Care · Cancer chemoprevention · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Adults with Lynch syndrome carrying a pathogenic germline mismatch-repair variant Aspirin 100 mg once daily (75 mg in the UK open phase) vs 300 mg once daily vs 600 mg once daily; 2 years blinded then 3 years open-label Primary: Time to first Lynch syndrome cancer, Total Lynch syndrome cancer burden. Secondary: Colorectal cancer, Any cancer excluding non-melanoma skin cancer, Safety Neither 100 mg nor 300 mg formally established non-inferiority to 600 mg because the criterion required both time-to-first-cancer and cancer-burden analyses in both ITT and per-protocol populations. For 100 mg, ITT met both margins (HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.67–1.42; incidence-rate ratio 0.94, 0.65–1.38), but per-protocol time to first cancer did not; 300 mg did not meet non-inferiority. During the blinded phase, any AE was 25.0%, 26.8% and 31.2% and serious bleeding 0%, 0.5% and 1.5% with 100, 300 and 600 mg. Median follow-up was 66.4 months; these are the trial’s first cancer outcomes.
records.keywords: Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2026; published online Jul 9  42425127

records.title: SAKK 96/12 REDUSE
records.subtitle: Supportive Care · SRAE prevention · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2026
records.body: Metastatic breast cancer or castration-resistant prostate cancer with at least 3 bone metastases Denosumab 120 mg every 4 weeks vs denosumab every 4 weeks for 4 loading doses then every 12 weeks Primary: Time to first symptomatic skeletal event. Secondary: Time to first and subsequent symptomatic skeletal events, Hypocalcaemia, Osteonecrosis of the jaw In this ASCO 2026 abstract, denosumab every 12 weeks after loading was non-inferior to every 4 weeks for time to first symptomatic skeletal event (median 56.5 versus 56.6 months; HR 1.023, 90% CI 0.874–1.197). The abstract also reports fewer hypocalcaemia events (30% versus 46%) and osteonecrosis of the jaw (6.9% versus 8.5%). Full-publication confirmation is required before changing practice.

records.title: D-TORCH
records.subtitle: Supportive Care · SKIN toxicity · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2024
records.body: Adults with breast or gastrointestinal malignancy starting capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily on days 1–14 every 21 days; no confounding grade 2 or higher neuropathy or hand-foot dermatosis Diclofenac 1% gel, 1 g per hand twice daily from capecitabine start for 12 weeks or until hand-foot syndrome vs matched placebo Primary: Grade 2–3 hand-foot syndrome by 12 weeks. Secondary: Grade 1–3 hand-foot syndrome, Capecitabine dose changes, Time to hand-foot syndrome, HFS14 quality of life, Adherence, Safety Topical diclofenac reduced grade 2–3 capecitabine-associated hand-foot syndrome at 12 weeks (3.8% versus 15.0%). Secondary grade 1–3 hand-foot syndrome (6.1% versus 18.1%) and capecitabine dose reduction (3.8% versus 13.5%) were descriptive, with unadjusted intervals and no multiplicity control. Grade 3 AEs were 11.5% versus 13.5%; 1 versus 4 patients died during the study, with no death classified as related to topical treatment. No cardiovascular events or AE-related capecitabine discontinuations occurred. This single-centre trial assessed hand application over 12 weeks.

records.title: COCOON
records.subtitle: Supportive Care · SKIN toxicity · Randomised clinical trial (phase II) · 2025
records.body: Histologically or cytologically confirmed NSCLC; locally advanced or metastatic, not amenable to curative therapy, treatment naive (first-line amivantamab-lazertinib); EGFR Ex19del or L858R; brain metastases allowed if asymptomatic or stable after previous localized therapy; excluded history of interstitial lung disease, uncontrolled illness or clinically significant cardiovascular disease All patients: IV amivantamab 1050 mg (1400 mg if ≥80 kg) weekly in cycle 1 then every 2 weeks + oral lazertinib 240 mg once daily in 28-day cycles, with prophylactic anticoagulation for the first 4 months; COCOON DM: oral doxycycline or minocycline 100 mg twice daily weeks 1–12 → topical clindamycin 1% on scalp once daily from week 13, plus daily chlorhexidine 4% nail wash and ceramide-based moisturizer on body and face at least once daily for the study duration vs SoC DM per local practice (no standard preventive regimen) Primary: incidence of grade ≥2 dermatologic adverse events of interest in the first 12 weeks. Secondary: incidence and severity of grade ≥2 dermatologic adverse events of interest in the first 6 months, number of participants with ≥2 different grade ≥2 dermatologic adverse events of interest, time to first grade ≥2 dermatologic adverse event of interest, change from baseline in health-related quality of life (Skindex-16, PGI-S, EORTC QLQ-C30), frequency of amivantamab or lazertinib dose reductions, interruptions and discontinuations due to AEs, frequency and severity of venous thromboembolism, antitumor efficacy endpoints (objective response rate, progression-free survival, duration of response), safety Prophylactic COCOON DM reduced dermatologic AEs of interest (DAEIs) with first-line amivantamab-lazertinib, and their impact on QoL, vs SoC DM. Grade ≥2 DAEIs by week 12: 42% vs 75% (OR 0.24; 95% CI 0.13–0.45; p<0.0001; median follow-up 7.1 mo); grade 3 DAEIs 6% vs 7%. Paronychia was not reduced (21% vs 23% by week 12; 44% vs 37% by 6 mo). Grade ≥2 skin DAEIs excluding paronychia by 6 mo: 41% vs 76%. Secondary p values were nominal. Skindex-16 favoured COCOON DM, but EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status/QoL showed no substantial difference. The design was open-label. ORR 82% vs 75%; median PFS and DoR not reached. No new safety signals and no grade 4/5 dermatologic AEs by week 12. VTE 13% in each arm (grade ≥3: 5% vs 3%) with prophylactic anticoagulation. No difference in infections or liver toxicity.
records.keywords: Cho et al. J Thorac Oncol 2025;20:1517-1530  40923969

records.title: Baseline Fatigue & Toxicity Risk (Unger)
records.subtitle: Supportive Care · Toxicity risk prediction · Observational cohort study · 2026
records.body: Patients receiving systemic therapy in 17 SWOG phase 2–3 trials across prostate, lung, colorectal, lymphoma, breast, melanoma, ovarian and pancreatic cancer Baseline patient-reported fatigue versus none or minimal fatigue (pooled observational analysis) Primary: Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events. Secondary: Grade 4 or higher and grade 5 treatment-related adverse events Baseline fatigue marked higher toxicity risk but did not establish a treatment-modification rule. Some-or-more versus less-than-some fatigue was associated with grade 3 or higher toxicity (OR 2.11, 95% CI 1.59–2.78), grade 4 or higher toxicity (OR 1.98, 1.39–2.82) and fatal toxicity (OR 2.35, 1.07–5.19). Quite-a-lot or very-much versus no fatigue had fatal-toxicity OR 4.99 (1.84–13.51). Associations for grade 3 or higher and grade 4 or higher toxicity were present in advanced-disease trials but not early or adjuvant trials; the grade 5 interaction was null. These pooled observational, exploratory analyses were not multiplicity-adjusted.

records.title: JCOG0504 (Kayama)
records.subtitle: Supportive Care · Brain metastases · Randomised clinical trial (phase III) · 2018
records.body: Adults 20–79 years with ECOG PS 0–2 (PS 3 only from neurologic deficit), 1–4 surgically resected brain metastases and ≤1 lesion >3 cm; eligible primary sites were NSCLC, breast, colon, renal, ovarian, uterine cervix/corpus, gastric or esophageal cancer Surgery then WBRT 37.5 Gy in 15 fractions over 3 weeks, started within 21 days, vs MRI surveillance with SRS for residual disease within 21 days and salvage SRS for eligible recurrent/new lesions (≤3 cm, or >3 cm with GTV ≤10 mL; up to 8 lesions). MRI every 2 months in year 1 then every 3 months; systemic therapy permitted. SRS was 1 day; dose/fractionation was not stated Primary: overall survival. Secondary: intracranial progression-free survival, adverse events, nonworsening performance status and Mini-Mental Status Examination at 6 and 12 months After resection, MRI surveillance with salvage SRS met the OS noninferiority criterion vs WBRT (median 15.6 months in both arms; HR 1.05, 90% CI 0.83–1.33; upper bound 1.33 below margin 1.385), but intracranial PFS was shorter (4.0 vs 10.4 months; HR 1.91). In the surveillance/SRS arm, 37.3% later received WBRT. Grade 2–4 cognitive dysfunction after day 91 was 7.7% vs 16.4% for salvage SRS vs WBRT; grade 3–4 nonhaematologic toxicity through day 30 was 7.6% vs 9.6%, grade 2–3 radiation necrosis was 2.6% vs 1.6%, and 1 WBRT death was deemed treatment related. Noninferiority does not establish equivalent or better intracranial control; unstated late-event denominators limit interpretation
